text: Slept like a log in the blissfully silent room, the bed was pure heaven. The bathroom felt modern and spotless, and the breakfast buffet's fresh pastries and coffee were a perfect start. Zero complaints.
The Wi-Fi held strong all week, and the staff's genuine warmth made check-in a breeze. While not cheap, the stunning harbor view from our room justified every penny for that unforgettable sunrise.

My partner and I spent three nights here for our anniversary, and it was exactly the cozy, historic getaway we hoped for. The room was on the smaller side, but the wood beams, fireplace, and plush bedding made it feel like a warm hideaway rather than a cramped space. We loved that the hotel is right in the heart of the Magnificent Mile, yet our room was remarkably quiet--no street noise at all. The staff genuinely went out of their way, especially the concierge who booked us a last-minute river architecture tour and recommended an off-menu dish at a nearby bistro we still talk about. The complimentary breakfast was simple but well done, and the lobby's afternoon cookies were a lovely touch after a long walk. Sure, the building shows its age in a few nicks, but that's part of its charm. We left feeling rested, spoiled, and already planning a return. Highly recommend for couples who appreciate character over cookie-cutter hotels.
Not worth the steep rates at all. The halls and neighboring rooms were noisy well past midnight, breakfast service was slow and surly, and I barely slept. Won't be returning to the Monaco.
The fresh, understated decor suited the room perfectly, and the skyline view was a bonus. Breakfast had good coffee and pastries, while the Wi-Fi stayed fast enough for work.

This hotel has the worst rooms we have stayed in during the last 10 years. The first room they gave us was a shock. TINY and the bathroom was a joke,, you had to step inside, move out of the way just to shut the door. The furniture is disgusting and all the wood trim was VERY beat up and painted over about 100 times. so they transfered us to the 'executive suite' That room had a tiny bathroom.. I mean TINY! The furniture was hideous and dirty. It was on the 3rd level so you heard every conversation on the street below and traffic was loud. The only impressive part is the lobby.. but don't be fooled. because after that .. the floors above look like they need a major overhaul.. and the rooms were not worth even $100 per night. we stayed there a year ago because we got stuck through Priceline deal. I don't think we want to do Priceline again only because they have the Knickerbocker as a 4 star Hotel and we don't ever want to go back there again. 2 Stars at best for the dumpy Knickerbocker. They should be ashamed of themselves for even allowing guests to stay in those rooms. Boomer. Naperville, IL

My wife and I stayed here for a weekend in Chicago and had an okay experience. The location contrary to other reviews is not very good for a downtown Chicago hotel. Everything is at least a fifteen minute walk which in the winter in Chicago means a taxi ride. The other thing that you should know about this hotel is that they allow smoking everywhere. I don't necessarily mind people smoking but the lobby, the elevator lobbies and any area that was public had tons of people smoking and ashtrays everywhere. The pool/spa/excercise room was not very impressive either. It is accessible by walking through the business center corridor, wondering if you're going the right way and then coming to a pool that is extremely small. There is also no hot tub and the 'spa' is a closet with a massage table. The concierge was helpful but the people that answer the 'sheraton promise' phone told me that there was nothing they could do about ice being out on two floors. The beds were super comfortable. I think that this is probably a nice business hotel with top of the line conference and meeting facilities but for couples or families you can do MUCH better in downtown Chicago.
The location was wonderfully convenient, but the Knickerbocker felt tired rather than stylish. Our room was only passably clean, and the lukewarm, limited breakfast made the stay disappointing.

I expected much more from an Omni stay, especially for the price. Check-in took nearly 30 minutes because only one person was working the desk, and no one acknowledged the line. Our room looked worn, with scuffed furniture, a stained chair, and a bathroom fan that rattled all night. The air conditioning barely cooled the room, so sleeping was uncomfortable. We called twice for extra towels and they arrived hours later, after we had already gone out for dinner. The pool area was crowded and had towels scattered everywhere, with no staff in sight. Breakfast was expensive and surprisingly mediocre. The location was convenient, but that was about the only positive. Overall, it felt more like an aging business hotel than the polished experience advertised.

A far-too-brief stay, but every minute was wonderful. Breakfast had a fantastic made-to-order omelet station, and the location made exploring effortless. The bed was so comfortable I slept better than I have in months.

We booked 2 rooms for 2 nights on Hotwire over Labor Day weekend. We arrived at the Hard Rock at around 10:00 a.m., and they were able to give us our rooms early. Hooray! We were on the 5th floor (Beatles theme). The rooms were very comfortable. One of our rooms was on a corner, and had lots of windows. The other was was a bit larger with fewer windows. Not a great view from our side of the hotel, but we didn't pay for a room with a view. The beds and pillows were EXTREMELY comfortable, the bathroom was full of Aveda products, and there was a bathrobe in the closet. The tv/dvd/stereo combo was nice, but we weren't in the room a lot to use it. We were warned by the front desk not to even touch the snacks/drinks as they were weighted and we'd be charged. No problems there. We did not make use of the free fitness center, because the weather was perfect. My husband was able to go for a run through Grant Park along the waterfront instead. He said it was wonderful. We did use the free internet in our rooms. It was 'wired' internet, but my stepdad said that was better for him anyway. The room was a bit dim at night, but we were able to read just fine using the bedside lamps. There was virtually no hall / elevator noise. The location of the Hard Rock is ideal. It is easy to get breakfast at the Corner Bakery, just blocks to either Grant Park, The Art Institute, State Street Shopping, or Michigan Ave. To sum up, there was absolutely NOTHING to complain about. We would be glad to stay here again any time.

I stayed at the Talbott for four nights in early October and would happily return. The location turned out to be ideal, quiet residential street feel yet only a short walk to Michigan Avenue shopping and plenty of restaurants nearby. My room was spotless when I arrived, and housekeeping kept it that way throughout my stay, right down to the neatly folded towels each afternoon. Despite being in the middle of the city, I never heard noise from the hallway or the street once the windows were closed, and I slept better than I do at home. What really set the place apart, though, was the staff. Everyone from the front desk to the doormen was warm and genuinely attentive without being intrusive. The bellman even gave me walking directions with a hand-drawn map. A solid, comfortable stay all around.

I really wanted to like this place, given the Sheraton name, but our stay left a sour taste. The bathroom was the low point: the caulking around the tub was grimy and peeling, and the showerhead sputtered like it was giving up. The decor felt frozen in the early 2000s, all heavy dark wood and beige wallpaper that made the room feel cramped and dusty, despite the housekeeping attempts. Our two nights here honestly felt like four, dragged out by thin walls and a constant hum from the mini-fridge. The staff were polite enough at check-in, but any request--extra towels, a late checkout--was met with a shrug and a 'we'll see.' It's functional, I suppose, but for the price, I'd expect a fresher, more attentive experience. I left with a headache and a sense that this property has been coasting on its brand for years.

Stayed at the InterContinental for an entire week on business and for the most part a very elegant, convenient visit. Stayed in the historic tower. Very nice rooms, great view, attentive staff, convenient location just north of the Tribune Tower & the river, and nice fitness club at $16 for the entire stay. The only downside is I couldn't get over the feeling that I was being nickle & dimed: $10 a day for Wi-Fi, $6 bottles of water in the room, $26 mini-bottle of wine in the fridge, tipping multiple staff for carrying the same bags, etc. Their in-house restaurant Zest is Zagat rated though I'm not sure why. Within a 5 minute walk there are plenty of great restaurants with much better food than Zest. But, next time I need to be near the Loop I'd stay at the InterContinental again.

I booked this Sheraton for a three-night city break, and honestly, it felt about 48 hours too long. The room itself was clean enough, but the air conditioning wheezed like it was on its last legs, and the walls were thin enough to hear my neighbor's entire phone conversation. Breakfast was the low point--rubbery scrambled eggs, lukewarm coffee, and pastries that tasted like they'd been sitting out since dawn. The staff weren't rude, but they were so brisk and disengaged that I felt like a nuisance just asking for extra towels. At nearly $280 a night, this felt like a rip-off; I've had better service at mid-range chains. The location is convenient, sure, but that doesn't compensate for the sterile atmosphere and the sense that nobody actually cares if you're there or not. I won't be coming back.

I had a very pleasant stay at Hotel Omni and would happily return. The lobby was polished without feeling overly formal, and check-in was quick and friendly, even though I arrived a little earlier than expected. My room was bright, quiet, and genuinely comfortable, with a good bed, plenty of outlets, and a surprisingly spacious bathroom. Everything was clean and well maintained. I also appreciated the small details, like the complimentary water and the helpful recommendations from the front desk when I asked about nearby restaurants. The cafe downstairs served a solid breakfast, though it was a bit busy in the morning. Wi-Fi worked reliably throughout my stay. Overall, the hotel offered a relaxing, convenient experience and felt like good value for the location.

My stay at the Affinia was disappointing from the moment I arrived. The front desk staff were polite enough, but seemed distracted and offered little help when I mentioned problems with the room. The bathroom was cramped, with worn grout, a weak shower, and water that took several minutes to drain. Our view was mostly of a brick wall and a collection of rooftop vents, hardly what I expected for the price. Noise was another issue: conversations in the hallway, slamming doors, and traffic continued well past midnight, and the thin walls made it difficult to sleep. Housekeeping also skipped replacing the towels one day. The convenient location was the only real advantage, but it did not make up for the tired room and lack of attention.

I booked the Conrad expecting refined luxury, but left feeling cheated. The Wi-Fi was a constant battle--it dropped in the middle of a video call and never reconnected without a frustrating lobby visit. Our room faced an inner courtyard, so the 'city view' was really a gray wall and a ventilation shaft humming all night. I slept terribly; the mattress was far too soft, and the air conditioning cycled loudly every twenty minutes. The staff were polite on the surface but utterly unhelpful--housekeeping ignored our request for extra towels twice, and the front desk shrugged when I mentioned the noise. For this price, I've had better service at a mid-range chain. The lobby is pretty, sure, but that's where the charm ends. I won't be back.

The room's fresh, modern decor was a pleasant surprise, and the sweeping harbour view from our window was breathtaking. Perfectly central, though we slept so deeply in those plush beds that we barely noticed the city buzz outside.

I've stayed at the Allegro a couple of times. Like the other Kimpton properties, it's a classic old hotel that's been beautifully updated. I found the staff to be cordial, and I really like their corporate culture. They're pet-friendly (although I wasn't travelling with the dog), I got a recycling bin in my room, Aveda products in the bath and they don't clean with toxic chemicals. The rooms aren't huge and the bathrooms aren't what you're going to get at a Hilton. What the Allegro lacks in square footage it more than makes up for in cool. OK, they may be a little pricey, but I'm willing to pay a bit more considering the higher cost of doing business responsibily.
The Hilton was spotless and welcoming, with a comfy bed and surprisingly quiet room. Breakfast had plenty of options, and the staff made check-in feel effortless.

Disappointing stay at the Monaco. Our room overlooked a dingy alley, the decor felt stuck in the 90s, and hallway noise kept us up both nights. Couldn't wait to check out--two nights felt like a week.

The Allegro turned out to be a quiet gem right in the middle of everything. The lobby had a fun, vintage vibe that made coming back feel special, and the bed was honestly the comfiest I've had in ages.

We've stayed here before but this time around was a marked difference in quality and service - the staff wasn't rude, just incompetent. For example, we ordered wine glasses for the room because the hotel no longer services a mini bar in the room, which seemed like a really cheap way to go for this type of hotel. Nonetheless, the staff brought us 4 coffee mugs... The list of issues goes on unfortunately, including the low grade in-room movie options - our audio and video did not sync on our rental; we eventually had to stop watching after 20 minutes. And the room itself was not clean; the bathroom sink vent holes were black with mold. Clearly the hotel has pulled back on not only amenities, but training or sufficient staff... oh, but the price point for this hotel has stayed the same. Find a newer hotel, there are many in this great city.
Hard Rock's central location made exploring easy, and the breakfast had plenty of fresh options. The sleek bathroom was spotless with a great shower; honestly, our weekend ended too soon.
Genuinely lovely stay. The staff remembered our names, the bed was cloud-soft, and breakfast had fresh pastries worth waking up early for. Pool area is peaceful too. We'll be back for sure.

I had a very pleasant stay at Swissotel and would happily return. The lobby was busy when I arrived, but check-in was handled efficiently and the front desk staff were warm without being overly formal. My room was on a higher floor with a great city view, and it was quiet enough to sleep well despite the central location. Everything felt clean and well maintained, especially the bathroom, which had good water pressure and plenty of counter space. The bed was comfortable, and I appreciated having a proper desk since I needed to catch up on work. Breakfast had a nice range of fresh options, though it got crowded around 9. The location made it easy to walk to restaurants and attractions. Overall, a polished, comfortable hotel with genuinely helpful service.

The staff were lovely, but felt like they were working against the building. Bathroom had a persistent musty smell and the hallways were loud until 3 AM. Not the chic, romantic escape I'd hoped for at this price.

I expected more from a hotel with this location and price point. The lobby looked polished, but that was about where the good impression ended. Our room was not ready at check-in, and after waiting nearly an hour nobody offered an update until I asked. The room itself felt tired: scuffed furniture, a stained chair, and a bathroom fan that rattled all night. The air conditioning barely worked, so it was stuffy despite turning it down several times. We also heard hallway conversations and doors slamming well past midnight. Housekeeping skipped our room one day, then brought towels late in the evening after two calls. Staff were polite when available, but everything seemed understaffed and disorganized. For the rate we paid, I expected a comfortable, dependable stay, not a series of small frustrations.
Expected more from a Hyatt. Room smelled musty, walls were thin, and the front desk took forever to fix our broken AC. Location was fine but honestly won't be rushing back.
Homewood was a disappointment: the room looked tired, housekeeping missed basic details, and the front desk seemed uninterested when we reported the issues. Not worth the price.

I had really hoped for better from the Hotel James, but our stay fell short in almost every way. The bathroom was the biggest letdown -- the shower barely maintained lukewarm pressure, the grout was black with mildew, and the fan rattled loud enough to wake the whole room. Sleep wasn't much better, honestly. The mattress sagged in the middle and street noise poured through a window that refused to seal, so we tossed and turned both nights. Cleanliness was questionable too: sticky rings on the nightstand, a gym towel someone left under the bed, and dust along every skirting board. Honestly, even one more night would have felt too long. The front desk staff was pleasant, but that alone can't rescue a stay this disappointing. We won't be back.

Stayed here in November 2011 on a leisure trip to Chicago. Hotel is very dated, with some rooms that just aren't good enough. Front desk staff was rude. Will not be staying here again - prefer the Swissotel and the Hyatt properties (Regency is similarly priced, and Park Hyatt is 3x more) and a list of boutique hotels in the area as well (Kimpton, etc). Pros: -The only hotel that opens onto Michigan Avenue, very close to all of the excitement -Eno Wine Bar has a great selection of cheeses -Rooms are clean Cons: -Some hotel rooms just make no sense - our first room was tiny and had a window overlooking a ledge (effectively no view), and our second room had two windows that looked out onto a brick wall (actually no view) -You have to pay for everything - internet, gym, and the pool (which was not available due to renovation...) -Entire hotel was very old, not in a classical sense but in a ghost story one -Front desk staff was rude

The James was a pleasant surprise--stylish, quiet, and genuinely comfortable. Location couldn't be better for exploring downtown, and the bed was so good I actually slept in past my alarm. Staff even remembered my coffee order at breakfast. Would happily book again.

Hotel Monaco looked charming online, but the stay was frustrating from the start. Our room faced the street, and traffic, sirens, and late-night voices carried through the windows well past midnight. The air conditioner also clicked on and off loudly, so neither of us slept much. For the rate, I expected better upkeep; the bathroom had worn grout and the shower temperature swung from hot to lukewarm. Breakfast was included but disappointing, with stale pastries, weak coffee, and a small buffet that was nearly empty by 9 a.m. We only stayed one night, thankfully, because a longer visit would have felt exhausting. The staff were polite, but the pleasant lobby could not make the hotel feel worth the price.

I stayed here for 5 nights last summer. I booked the reservation on priceline for $75/night which was the cheapest rate I could find anywhere during a convention week. Anyway, when I arrived at 11 pm from the airport, I was told that they had overbooked the hotel and had no room for me. They booked me at a dumpy 2 star motel by the airport. They gave me $20 for a taxi to get there, and it cost me $35. I was late for a meeting the next morning because of the extra travel and packing/unpacking. The Millennium offered no compensation whatsoever for their foul-up. No free drink, no room upgrade, nothing. Since I booked on the internet, I was chopped liver. Beware.

We stayed three nights for our anniversary, and it was exactly the restful escape we needed. The room facing the inner courtyard was remarkably silent -- we never once heard hallway noise or street traffic, which is rare for a hotel this size. The bathroom was a marble showcase, with a rainfall shower that had fantastic pressure and a deep soaking tub I actually used twice. Every staff member we encountered, from the doorman to housekeeping, greeted us by name after check-in, and the concierge arranged a last-minute dinner reservation at a lovely bistro without any fuss. The decor strikes a nice balance: the public spaces feel grand and freshly updated, while the guest room's classic furnishings have a timeless, elegant charm rather than anything tired. Our only slight quibble was the minibar cost, but that's typical for this tier. We left feeling thoroughly pampered.

I stayed at ICH Chicago for business in November of 2006 and loved it. As a Royal Ambassador member, they upgraded me to a beautiful junior suite with a separate living and working area and 2 bathrooms! My upgrade was in place upon arrival and a beautiful fruit basket was waiting for me on the coffee table. They even had a nice young lady escort me to my room. The suite was beautifully furnished and had an Art Deco feel to it. The only thing I regretted was that I only stayed one night. I will definitely stay here on my next visit.

We loved the Conrad's calm, refined vibe--the room was spotless and the bed genuinely luxurious. Breakfast was excellent, and staff remembered our names all weekend. Probably the best in the city for a quiet, comfortable stay.

Honestly, the ambassador team made everything effortless--they remembered my coffee order by day two and had great local tips. The room was quiet, spotless, and the bed was incredibly comfortable. I left feeling genuinely rested, which rarely happens on work trips.

We booked the Fairmont for a milestone anniversary, expecting the usual flagship-level polish. Instead, we got a room that felt tired and overheated, with a thermostat that might as well have been decorative. The hallway ice machine was out of order, and our request for extra towels took three calls and over an hour. We tried the hotel bar for a nightcap--the bartender was friendly, but the service around him was glacial, and we watched two tables send back drinks. The view was nice, sure, but you don't pay those rates for a view when the bed's pillows are flat and the bathroom caulk is peeling. The gym was fine, but the pool was booked solid with a private event, so guests were locked out. It all felt like a corporate machine running on autopilot. For this price, I expected attentive staff and a room that didn't feel neglected. We left disappointed and questioning the brand's reputation. Definitely not worth it for us.

We stayed at the James for three nights over a long weekend and honestly couldn't have picked a better spot. The location puts you right in the middle of everything, we walked to dinner both nights and barely touched a cab. Our room wasn't huge but it was smartly laid out, and the bed might be the most comfortable I've slept in at any hotel, period. Housekeeping was quick and thorough, and when we asked for an extra blanket it showed up within ten minutes. The front desk staff were genuinely friendly without being overbearing, which is rarer than it should be. Small gripe: the elevator wait got a little long at peak times. That's really my only complaint though. Would absolutely book here again next time we're in town.

Our stay at Hotel Ambassador was genuinely worth the price, especially given the central location and the comfort of the room. We had a higher-floor room with a lovely view over the city rooftops and distant hills, which was especially nice with morning coffee. The staff were warm, professional, and quick to help with restaurant suggestions and a taxi arrangement. Check-in was smooth, and housekeeping kept everything spotless. The Wi-Fi worked reliably throughout our stay, including in the room, so I could handle a short work call without interruption. Breakfast was fresh and varied, although the dining area became a little busy at peak time. Overall, a very pleasant and well-managed hotel.

' Barely Average Hotel at Premium Price' This hotel has a beautiful lobby but fails to fails to maintain its standards beyond the lobby. I have stayed in the Conrad in Dublin, Ireland and in HongKong both of which I loved. I was looking forward to staying at this hotel. I was extremely disappointed. I am very surprised that this hotel is allowed to carry the Conrad name. Pros: Elegant lobby nicely decorated with fresh flowers Location: Located in the Heart of Chicago Disappointments - Stained and worn out carpet in hallway - Room was small - Phone and lightbulb in room were broken - Breakfast was $60 for two people, service was slow and impolite - Hotel rationed soaps and shampoo, one bar of soap to share and one bottle of shampoo which was not replaced for two days, I felt like I was staying at a budget hotel. and to cap off my stay the hotel made a billing error which took three months and more effort than it was worth to correct. I would not stay at this hotel again, It just is not worth the premium price they charge.

My stay at Hotel Amalfi was more disappointing than relaxing. I booked two nights, but by the second morning I was already wishing I had chosen somewhere else; the experience felt far too long for such a short trip. The room looked tidy at first glance, yet there was dust along the bedside table, a smudged mirror, and crumbs near the desk. The bathroom was particularly underwhelming, with worn grout, weak water pressure, and a shower curtain that smelled damp. Staff interactions were polite but noticeably indifferent--questions were answered with minimal effort, and my request for extra towels took several hours. The location was convenient, but that alone did not make up for the tired room and lack of attention to basic cleanliness and service.

Really enjoyed our three-night stay at the Conrad. The location can't be beaten, and while the lobby feels a bit corporate-chic, our room was surprisingly fresh with a lovely modern bathroom. Yes, it's pricey, but the service, the stunning skyline view, and the seamless check-in made it feel worth every pound. Breakfast was a highlight--the made-to-order omelettes were superb, and the pastries were still warm. My only tiny gripe is the hallway carpet looks a little tired, but that's minor. The wifi was fast and reliable in the room and even by the pool, which was perfect for streaming a film at night. Would definitely return.

The hotel definitely doesn't match its 4.5 rating. The receptionist was very unhelpful and dishonest, and I don't feel welcome at all. I booked a non-smoking room, but upon arrival, the receptionist told me that there was no non-smoking room left. Of course he was lying. I argued with him for 5 minutes, before he reluctantly gave me a non-smoking room. At checkout, they tried to charge me $40 upgrade fee each day, because I requested a non-smoking room. This was completely ridiculous. I had to go argue with the receptionist again before they agreed to take away the charges. The room was quite small, the TV was broken, so I had to call someone to fix the TV. Then the wireless network banned my IP address, so I had to talk to their tech-support -- the tech support was quite friendly, knowledgeable and helpful -- I guess this was the only bright point of the stay.

We stayed at the Hotel Talbott for four nights and honestly, it exceeded what we expected. The location is fantastic, quiet side street but just a few blocks from the Magnificent Mile, so easy to walk everywhere without the chaos. Our room was spacious by city standards, and the bed was genuinely comfortable, which mattered because I usually sleep badly in hotels. What really won us over was the staff. The doorman remembered our names by day two, and when we asked the front desk for restaurant suggestions they gave us three spots we ended up loving, none of them touristy. The little touches, like fresh cookies in the afternoon and a real coffee maker in the room, felt thoughtful. Only tiny gripe was slow elevator on checkout day, but that's a minor thing. Would absolutely stay here again on our next Chicago trip.

Despite Sofitel's convenient central location, street noise and thin walls made sleep difficult. Staff were polite but detached, and the overall service felt disappointing for a hotel of this standard.
Swissotel's fresh, understated decor made the room feel calm, the Wi-Fi was reliable for work, and I slept deeply in the quiet bed. It felt well worth the rate.
For nearly $400 a night I expected far more--tired, dated decor, a room that never felt truly clean, and street noise that wrecked my sleep both nights. Disappointing overall.

Upon first entering the hotel, we were greeted by the most friendly and helpful bellmen I have ever encountered. Through our 2 week stay, they told us to 'have a nice day' as we left in the AM and welcomed us back upon our return. Breakfast is served in the AM, and the servers were as delightful as the bellmen. It was a very enjoyable stay.

My stay at Hotel Allegro was far more disappointing than expected. The location is convenient, but the room felt tired and poorly maintained, with scuffed walls, a stained carpet, and a bathroom fan that rattled all night. The bed was reasonably comfortable, although the thin walls meant I could hear conversations and doors slamming in the corridor until after midnight. Breakfast was another letdown: limited choices, lukewarm eggs, and tables that were not cleared promptly. I mentioned the noise and the fan to reception, but the response was polite without offering any practical solution or room change. The staff were not rude, just strangely disengaged. For the price, I expected a cleaner, quieter, more polished experience. I would probably choose somewhere else next time.
Dated, tired decor and a noisy street view that faced a parking lot. Breakfast was a sad cold buffet--stale pastries and watery eggs. Definitely not worth the price.
Hilton made our weekend easy, with a smooth check-in, quiet room, and genuinely friendly staff. The bed was comfortable, and breakfast was better than expected; I'd happily stay here again.

Booked a king room expecting the Conrad standard, but this felt like a budget operation wearing a nice suit. The check-in took twenty minutes because they'd lost the reservation, despite my confirmation email. Room was okay at first glance, but the AC rattled all night, and the bathroom had a lingering musty smell no amount of towels could mask. Housekeeping skipped our room entirely one day, and when I called, they said 'we'll get to it' and never did. The bar served a flat, overpriced cocktail, and the bartender seemed annoyed we existed. Location is decent, sure, but you're paying for the name. I've had better nights in a roadside motel. For the price, this was a letdown. Won't be back.

We stayed at the InterContinental for a long weekend and came away genuinely impressed. The lobby was busy when we arrived, but the front desk handled check-in smoothly and even pointed us toward a quieter elevator bank. Our room felt polished without being stuffy, with a very comfortable bed, good blackout curtains, and enough desk space for me to catch up on work. Housekeeping was consistent and never intrusive. Breakfast was the one splurge we made, and it was worth it for the fresh pastries and attentive service. The location also made it easy to walk to restaurants and nearby sights. Prices are definitely on the higher side, but the level of comfort and care made the stay feel worthwhile.
Absolutely worth the splurge. The skyline view from our room was stunning at sunset, the place was spotless, and the modern decor felt fresh. We couldn't have asked for a better stay.

We booked the Fairmont for a quick anniversary getaway, and I'm genuinely glad we did. The bathroom was a standout--huge marble walk-in shower with excellent water pressure, plus robes that actually fit. Wi-Fi was spotty in the hallway but rock-solid in the room, which mattered since I had to log a few work hours before dinner. Location-wise, you can't beat it; we strolled to the lake, caught a show, and walked back without once needing a cab. If anything, the stay felt too short--I could've happily parked in that bed for another night, but we had to check out and head home. Staff were warm without being fussy. Just wish we'd booked one more day.

Disappointed with the Palmer. Our room smelled musty, the AC barely worked, and housekeeping skipped us one day entirely. Front desk staff were indifferent when we complained. For the price, expected far better. Won't be back.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly, it exceeded expectations for the rate we paid. The location is a major win--you're smack in the middle of everything, with great restaurants and the waterfront just a short, pleasant walk away. I was a bit worried about the decor based on some older photos, but our room felt refreshed and modern, with clean lines and a comfortable, plush bed. We had a corner room facing the city, and the floor-to-ceiling windows gave us a stunning skyline view at sunset, which was a real treat. The staff were friendly without being overbearing, and check-in was a breeze. Considering the prime spot and the quality of the room, it felt like a solid value. We'll definitely book again when we're back in town.

This hotel is very busy and is operating way beyond their means. Incompetent service. Hotel ran out of hot water by 9am saturday. Elevators were very slow, waited 10 minutes on any given event. Red line trains ran every 10 minutes beneath city streets and you can hear the thunder in your room from them but it shouldnt keep you awake at night. Used my stay toward NW airlines bonus points. Bar was ok. One cup coffee service was awful. No free wireless and no free cable channels. Fridge was 25 bucks a day to use. With http://hotels.com res got it for 65 bucks with tax so what can you expect.?.... Location was superb and cab service was convenient but not enough to outweigh the negatives.
Hard Rock felt worn and loud: the room had dusty surfaces, the bathroom was cramped with weak water pressure, and two nights dragged on thanks to hallway noise.
Expected much more from the Talbott. Our room felt dated and the AC barely worked, staff took ages to fix it. Not worth the price at all. Disappointing stay.

Stayed for 3 nights. booked via hotwire, upgraded to historic tower. Got a big room, with a nice view.Service was great. Valet parking was efficient, but you expect it for 53 doller/night. But the location was the best

I expected much more from Conrad, especially for the price. Check-in was slow and the staff seemed distracted rather than welcoming. My room looked polished at first, but the bathroom had hair on the floor, the shower pressure was weak, and the air conditioning rattled all night. I mentioned it to the front desk, but no one followed up. Breakfast was another letdown: lukewarm food, empty coffee urns, and tables left uncleared during a busy morning. The location was convenient, but that was about the only real positive. For a hotel marketed as upscale, the service felt impersonal and the attention to detail was missing. I left feeling like I had paid luxury rates for an average, poorly managed stay.
Loved the Talbott's cozy, classic feel and genuinely helpful staff. Our room was quiet, the bed was great, and the Gold Coast location made walking to dinner easy.

Unfortunately, my stay at the Hyatt was more frustrating than relaxing. Check-in took nearly half an hour, and the room looked worn, with scuffed furniture and a bathroom that needed a deeper cleaning. I booked a city-view room, but the window faced a bland rooftop and a brick wall, so there was little to enjoy. The hallway was quiet during the afternoon, yet doors slammed and voices carried late into the night. The mattress was lumpy, and the constant hum from the air-conditioning made it difficult to sleep; I woke several times. I only stayed two nights, but the visit felt oddly long because of the poor rest and limited comfort. Staff were polite when approached, though they offered no meaningful solution. For the price, I expected much better.

I really wanted to love this Sofitel given the price point, but the stay fell flat in almost every way. Check-in took nearly forty minutes because the front desk was understaffed, and no one apologized for the wait. My room had a strange musty smell, the AC rattled all night, and the 'luxury' bedding felt dated and slightly stained. Housekeeping skipped my room entirely one day and I had to call twice to get fresh towels. Breakfast was the biggest letdown--cold eggs, lukewarm coffee, and a buffet that looked picked over well before closing time. The concierge also gave me blatantly wrong directions twice. For a property charging these rates, the service and upkeep simply don't match. Honestly, I'd expected far more from a brand like this and won't be rushing back.

I stayed at The James for a long weekend and was pleasantly surprised by how comfortable everything felt. The location is excellent, with plenty of restaurants, shops, and the river all within an easy walk, but the room was quiet at night. My king room was a good size, with a very comfortable bed, useful seating area, and a bathroom that was clean and well stocked. I also appreciated the small touches, like the bottled water and the friendly housekeeping service. Check-in was quick, and everyone at the desk was genuinely helpful when I asked for directions and a late dinner recommendation. The decor is modern without feeling cold. It is not the least expensive option downtown, but the service and convenient location made it feel worth the price.

Really enjoyed my stay at the Affinia-the room was huge with a full kitchenette, and the bed was probably the comfiest I've slept in at any hotel. Staff were friendly every time. Would definitely come back next trip to the city.

I had a very comfortable three-night stay at The Knickerbocker. The location is hard to beat, right by Times Square but with surprisingly good soundproofing once you're inside. My room was modern, spotless, and larger than I expected for Manhattan, with a genuinely comfortable bed and plenty of outlets near the desk. The staff were friendly without being overbearing, and they handled an early check-in request quickly after a long flight. I also enjoyed a drink at the rooftop bar; the views were excellent, although it gets busy around sunset, so reservations are worthwhile. The lobby can feel lively and crowded, but that seemed appropriate for the area. Prices aren't low, yet the service, location, and overall comfort made it feel like a worthwhile splurge.

The ocean view from my room was absolutely stunning, and the vibrant decor felt surprisingly fresh and energetic. Being steps from the Boardwalk made exploring a breeze, and honestly, it was worth every penny for the experience.

We were at the Hotel Allegro for an Industry Analyst event. I could not have expected worse. At first glance, you figured it couldn't be too bad as a Kimpton. The unfortunate issue - service and the people were excellent. However, the rooms just sucked. Imagine your normal hotel room and 1/3 that size. Cramp in a king size bed and add a bathroom that's also 1/3 the size. The building has that old hotel smell where things are musky but covered up with some paint smell. The bathroom has showers with modern fixtures but remind you of that nyc studio you rented with 5 other people out of college. The paints peeling on the base boards, the carpet is new, but something is wrong. I would stay at the Marriott, Renaissance, Westin, or any where else.

In the 100 degree heat of a Chicago summer, it sucks if your air conditioner does not work. After 2 maintenance men attempted to rectify the issue I was offered a portable fan which on low speed sound as if a helicopter was hoovering over my room. I requested a room change and a not so polite, unsympathetic night front desk attendant stated that was not possible because the hotel was at capacity. Maybe a manager could help me in the morning. The next day went by and no call was received. At 7pm, I called the front desk. No one was aware of my problem. Approximately 45 minutes later, a manager returned my call and stated a double room was available. I accepted it was glee. Anything was better than a room that does not cool below 78 degrees in the middle of summer. I was paritally correct. The bathroom door of the new room did not close. Thank god my boyfriend and I are past the shy part of the relationship. As for room 1618, I believe I was not the first guest to complain about the air conditioner. What's unfortunate is they continued to place guests into this room. And did not offer any reufunds or perks for my sleepless night in the sauna! This hotel need a major overhaul!!

Stayed three nights at the Hyatt for a conference, and honestly, it exceeded what I expected from a big downtown property. The lobby feels grand without being stuffy, and check-in was painless--the front desk agent actually remembered my name the next morning, which was a nice touch. My room on the 14th floor had a sweeping view of the river, and the bed was firm but cozy, with blackout curtains that worked too well (I nearly missed my alarm). The gym is well-equipped, though it gets busy around 7 a.m., so go early. I didn't try the restaurant, but the bar made a solid old fashioned. One small gripe: the hallway ice machine was out of order, but a quick call to housekeeping fixed that within ten minutes. Overall, a comfortable, polished stay that made the business trip feel almost like a mini-vacation. I'd gladly book here again.

Our stay at the Ambassador East Hotel was extremely relaxing and pleasant. We enjoyed the location. We could easily walk to the Red line or access the bus lines along Michigan Avenue. We felt safe walking along the neighborhood streets and viewing the fabulous architecture that is on N. State Street and Dearborn. We walked to 3rd Coast Cafe, the Chicago History Museum, and Second City from our hotel. Our room was spacious and well-kept, and it was quiet enough for us to take a nap during the afternoon before heading out again in the evening. We would choose to stay there again even if we could afford more expensive locations downtown. We definitely enjoyed the neighborhood feel of the place.

This hotel cannot be beat for location, price, & atmosphere. The location is ideal, at the corner of State & Kinzie. There are fantastic restaurants & bars all around, including House of Blues & Harry Caray's. We stayed in a 'Corner King' room. The room was amazing. Two of the four walls are floor to ceiling windows. Even just being on the 5th floor, we had great views of the surrounding area. The decor and amenities are unmatched. The decor is very clean & simple but luxurious. The hotel is easy to miss from street level, but shouldn't be. The staff were extremely friendly and accommodating. Its a perfect home base if your plans revolve around River North, State Street shopping, or Clark Street nightlife. Even if you'll be on the Mag Mile, this is a short cab ride away. We've officially named this our downtown hotel of choice!

Despite the decent skyline view, our room felt neglected with dust on the sills and a stained carpet. Staff were polite but slow, and hallway noise from neighboring guests kept us awake, making the whole stay honestly underwhelming.

I expected much more from Swissotel given the price and reputation. Check-in took nearly 25 minutes because the desk seemed understaffed, and no one acknowledged the wait. My room looked fine at first, but the carpet had stains, the air conditioning rattled all night, and the bathroom had a lingering damp smell. I called twice about the AC and was told someone would come, but nobody did. Breakfast was crowded, with cold eggs and empty coffee stations, and tables were not cleared quickly. The location was convenient, but that was about the only positive. Staff were polite when approached, yet everything felt impersonal and poorly managed. For this rate, I expected a cleaner room and more attentive service.

I stayed at the Palmer House for @ $150/night on a corporate rate. The bed was excellent, the linens/towels were top of the line. I did not find my room shabby, as other reviewers noted. The Palmer House is over 130 years old. Rooms have older woodwork and classic furniture; I think that lends to the ambience of the place. It is expensive, and I'm not sure I'd stay there if my company weren't picking up the tab. But the hotel itself is still awe-inspiring.

My in-laws booked a one night stay for New Years Eve for the two of us to stay at the James. To be brief there were a few things wrong with our stay which will prevent us from returning and advising our friends not to stay there. 1) Shoddy construction of room fixtures: ceiling light was missing leaving a fist-sized hole with wires exposed, BOTH towel racks fell off the wall without being touched, and bathroom door often came off it's sliding mechanism with gentle use. 2) When we reported these problems, employees simply put the towel racks back on the wall without properly adhering them to the wall. 3) Upon check-out, they did not have record of my in-laws paying for our stay, though it was noted on our reservation that they had made it for us. We had to pay for our ($300) gift and the in-laws were extremely upset. When we wrote a letter to management (as a manager was not available to speak with us when we left) we did not receive an adequate apology.

The wifi was a constant frustration, dropping during video calls. While the staff were polite, they seemed indifferent to my complaints. For this price, the tired, 80s-style decor felt like a rip-off, and the whole stay left me seriously disappointed.

This hotel has a great location, and very friendly staff. However, the physical condition of the property has certainly fallen behind the competition. I use to be a regular at this hotel . . . but have not been back for 15 years. Rooms have not been well maintained (old carpets frayed at doors), wall paper peeling off of the walls, TV's from the 80's. There is currently construction going on in the lobby area, making it impossible to get to the restaurant without leaving the hotel and walking to an outside door.

This is a stylish hotel located right on North Michigan Avenue, a five minute walk from the Orange 'Loop' line that will get you to and from Midway Airport. Forget about taking a taxi: the train is a $2 ride and less than 40 minutes away. Our room (1802) was immaculate and spacious (350 sq ft, we were told). Decorated in grays and white, the room was comfortable and soothing, not jarring. On the other hand, we found the lighting to be very poor and had trouble reading, finding keys, etc. No kidding. The bathroom was also quite dark and it didnt have a heating lamp. On the positive side, however, there were Aveda products in the bathroom, the windows were huge, so during the day there was tons of natural light, and no issues with darkness. The king size bed was very firm, but had a plush pillow top which made it very comfortable and inviting. We had a largish TV with a DVD player. There is a safe and munchies. The gym is perfect, equipped with treadmills, ellipticals, bikes and weights. It is open 24/7 and there is video surveillance for safety. There are towels, water, headphones, disposable ear pads, and complimentary green apples. Suggestion: if you are on a floor below the 22nd, take the elevator up to 22nd, then down to L2 to get to the gym. This way you dont have to traverse the lobby. The front desk staff is amiable, and very attentive. I read some other reviews about nasty personnel, but did not have that experience at all. I got a free newspaper with a smile, a free stamp when I needed it, change and all the coffee I could tolerate in the morning. The Hard Rock is located less than a 20 minute walk from the Water Tower, the Drury Theater, John Hancock, and magnificent mile. For those who like a thrifty breakfast, we recommend Gourmet Pantry at 155 N. Michigan Avenue [--]. This deli made a delicious egg on a toasted roll with butter on a Sunday morning, no less: $1.99. The hotel has a breakfast buffet for $15.00 per person, but we did not partake of it. We would stay at the Hard Rock again, and think it is great for people with 'tweens.' Not sure about the toddler set, though.

We stayed at Hotel Amalfi for four nights and honestly, it exceeded expectations. Our room was spotless, with fresh linens and a bathroom that gleamed--a detail I always appreciate. Despite being near the main road, the double glazing did its job; we slept deeply and undisturbed each night. The staff, especially the front desk gentleman, were wonderfully attentive without hovering, offering excellent local eating suggestions. The location proved ideal, a short, pleasant stroll to the duomo yet removed from the chaos. The breakfast spread was decent, and having a cold bottle of water waiting in the mini-bar was a thoughtful touch. If you value a clean, quiet base that doesn't break the bank, this is a solid pick.

The location couldn't be more convenient, but that's the only highlight. The staff seemed perpetually frazzled and disinterested, our room's view was a brick wall, and breakfast was a sad, lukewarm buffet of rubbery eggs and stale pastries.

We stayed at the Sofitel for four nights and honestly, it felt far too short. From the moment we arrived, the staff went out of their way to make everything easy -- the concierge booked us a last-minute dinner reservation and the front desk remembered our names by day two. Our room on the fourteenth floor looked straight out over the city, and watching the sunset from the window with a glass of wine became our nightly ritual. Breakfast was a proper event: fresh pastries, made-to-order eggs, and a spread of fruit and cheeses that changed slightly every morning. Even the little touches, like turndown service and the doorman hailing cabs within seconds, made the experience feel effortless. We're already planning to return for a full week.

We stayed at the Allegro for four nights in October and it honestly exceeded what I expected from a downtown property at this price. The location is fantastic -- a short walk to the theatres on Randolph and easy access to the L, but the room faced away from the street so we slept without hearing trains or traffic. The bed was genuinely comfortable, and the shower had good water pressure, which I always notice more than people probably should. One small hiccup with our room key deactivating twice, but the front desk fixed it in a minute each time and even apologized with a couple of free drink vouchers. Everything about the place has a fun, slightly jazz-era vibe without feeling gimmicky. Would happily come back next time we're in the city.

Breakfast was fresh and varied, and the central location made exploring easy. My room overlooked the lively street, while the friendly, attentive staff made check-in and every request pleasantly effortless.

I wasn't sure what to expect from a hotel that leans so heavily on being 'homey,' but Homewood genuinely pulled it off without feeling kitschy. Our suite was spotless and way more spacious than I anticipated--the kitchenette actually came stocked with real cookware, so we made breakfast a couple of mornings instead of eating out. The bed was comfortable, and I appreciated the blackout curtains because the hallway light was bright. Staff at the front desk remembered our names by day two, which was a nice touch. The free evening reception on weekdays was a pleasant surprise, and the pool area was clean, even if the water was a bit chilly. Only minor hiccup: the AC unit hummed louder than I'd like. Still, for the price and the location near the interstate, we'd happily book again.

Truly enjoyed our three nights at the Monaco. The location is unbeatable, steps from everything but tucked away enough that the street noise never bothered us. Check-in was smooth, and the front desk staff went out of their way to recommend a couple of local restaurants that ended up being trip highlights. Our room was on the smaller side but beautifully designed, with a super comfortable bed, blackout curtains, and a rainfall shower that had great water pressure. Housekeeping kept everything immaculate, and they even left extra towels without us asking. The complimentary evening wine reception in the lobby was a nice surprise, a lovely way to unwind after a day of walking around. Minor quibble: the elevator is slow during peak morning hours, but honestly that's being picky. Would absolutely stay here again on our next visit.

Loved our stay at Hotel Amalfi -- the sea view from our balcony was worth every penny, breakfast was fresh and generous, and the front desk helped us book a boat day without any fuss. Would come back in a heartbeat.

I really wanted to like this hotel, but between the price we paid and what we got, it fell short. The location is honestly its best feature, just a few minutes' walk from the metro and plenty of restaurants, but that's about where the good news ends. Our room faced the street and the noise was relentless until well past midnight, with doors slamming in the corridor all night too. The wifi barely worked in the room; it kept dropping every few minutes, which was a real problem since I needed to join a couple of video calls during my stay. At over 200 euros a night, I expect reliable internet and some soundproofing, not earplugs and hotspoting from my phone. The staff were polite enough, but politeness doesn't fix a room that feels overpriced. I won't be returning.
Great location, but the room felt worn and noisy, and the front desk was slow to help with a broken thermostat. For the price, I expected a much smoother stay.

We usually stay at the Sofitel but thought we would try the Conrad for a change. I don't think I would rate this hotel over the Sofitel but it was still 1st class. But I do think the service was better at the Conrad. We arrived at the hotel just before the restaurant closed and soon we were the only table left. Normally service goes down hill then but our waiter Eric was the best. Even when I kept ordering my after dinner ports. The meal may not have been The Chop House but it was still very good. The bar was ok, no Crown Reserve. They did have the Cask 16 at $24 a drink, ouch. The room service was very quick. Our room was very clean and the maids replace everything including the ashtrays during their visits. The only fault we could find was the temperature on the 14th floor. It was so hot that we had our window open the whole time with the heat turned completely off. Which wasn't so bad since my wife smokes. The temp on the 5th where the lobby, bar, and restaurant was fine. We enjoyed the hotel enough that we will be back in Sept. One last thing, if you like a cheap fantastic breakfast. Go to the West Egg, only a few blocks away.

The location is ideal. They have very high ceilings so the rooms appear much larger than they are. The views are great. There were fresh flowers in the bathroom. They had all white bedding. You feel like a princess there.

I had a genuinely lovely stay at the Fairmont. Check-in was quick, and the front desk team made us feel welcome without being overly formal. Our room was spotless, quiet, and had a very comfortable bed with great pillows; I slept better than I do at home. The view from the window was a nice bonus, especially in the evening. Breakfast was fresh with plenty of choices, and the coffee was surprisingly good. The lobby and common areas felt elegant but still relaxed, not stuffy. We also appreciated how helpful the concierge was when suggesting nearby restaurants. It is definitely not the cheapest option, but the service, comfort, and overall attention to detail made it feel worth it.

My stay at the Hard Rock was far more disappointing than expected. The room looked stylish in photos, but in person the furniture felt worn and the walls were thin enough to hear conversations in the hallway. Breakfast was especially underwhelming: limited options, lukewarm eggs, and coffee that tasted stale, despite the high room rate. The bathroom was clean but cramped, with weak water pressure and a shower that fluctuated between hot and cold. I was also promised a city view, but my window faced a blank side wall and several air-conditioning units. Staff were polite, though not particularly helpful when I raised these issues. For the price, I expected a more comfortable room, better food, and at least a decent view. It did not feel worth the money.

Just back from a business trip. The Homewood is in a great location just off the Magnificent Mile, includes a great breakfast, heavy hors d'ouevres for dinner with beer and all for a pre-paid rate of $129. Without a doubt the best value in Chicago for a long, long time.

The service at Hotel Amalfi truly exceeded expectations--impeccably warm staff and a spotless room with an incredible sea view. Breakfast was fresh and abundant each morning, making our coastal getaway feel effortless and memorable.
Hotel Monaco looked charming online, but our room was noisy, the shower barely stayed warm, and check-in took forever. For the price, it felt neglected and not very welcoming.

I had really high hopes for the James based on the photos, but my stay last weekend fell flat in almost every way. The room looked chic in the pictures online, but in person it felt dated and the air conditioning rattled all night, keeping me up until I finally gave up around 3am and called the desk. They offered to move me to another floor, but the new room had the same problem. The shower took forever to get hot, and when it did, the water pressure was pathetic. Housekeeping knocked on my door at 8am both mornings even though I asked for late service. The front desk staff seemed annoyed every time I asked for anything, including a simple extra pillow that took four hours to arrive. The location is fine, but honestly that's the only thing going for this place. At this price point I expected far better. Won't be back.
The Omni was exactly what we needed. Breakfast had great variety, and the wifi was solid for work. Staff were genuinely helpful, and our room stayed surprisingly quiet despite the full hotel.

Really impressed with Swissotel. The location is fantastic--you're steps from the lake and a quick walk to all the main sights, yet the rooms feel surprisingly quiet. We booked a corner room and the views over the water were stunning, especially at sunrise. The bed was incredibly comfortable, and I appreciated the blackout curtains after a long flight. Staff were professional without being stuffy; the front desk remembered my name every time we passed, which was a nice touch. Breakfast had a solid spread with fresh pastries and made-to-order eggs, though it got busy around 9. The pool area is small but clean and never overcrowded. Only minor gripe was the hallway carpet showing some wear, but it didn't detract from the stay. Would happily return.

We always stay at the Sheraton Chicago Hotel & Towers when we take our kids to the city. You can't beat the location which is in walking distance of Navy Pier and Michigan Ave. The hotel is also just a couple of blocks from the fabulous Fox & Obel, a high end grocery store with many prepared items available to go and a great cafe that serves a stellar breakfast. The hotel staff are professional and courteous and the rooms are more than adequate with very comfy beds. My kids enjoy the pool with it's windows that overlook the Chicago river.

The Knickerbocker was a great choice for a New York weekend. The location near Times Square is busy, of course, but once we were inside the hotel it felt polished and surprisingly calm. Our room was spotless, comfortable, and well insulated from the street noise; the bed was especially good after long days of walking. Staff at check-in were friendly and gave us helpful subway and restaurant suggestions without being pushy. We also enjoyed a drink at the rooftop bar, where the city views were worth the splurge. Breakfast was a little pricey, but the food and service were both solid. I'd happily stay here again for the convenience, thoughtful service, and classic NYC atmosphere.

The view of the parking garage and neighboring rooftops was a far cry from the advertised skyline, and the flimsy walls made the two-night stay feel like a week. At this price, I expected working Wi-Fi and comfort, not constant disconnections and a stained carpet.

We stayed at Hotel Allegro for three nights and honestly left pretty disappointed. Check-in took nearly forty minutes because only one person was at the desk. Our room overlooked the street and the noise went on until 2am every night - bring earplugs. The air conditioning barely worked, and when we reported it, someone came, jiggled something, and left. Breakfast was the real letdown: thin selection, lukewarm eggs, and coffee from a machine that tasted burnt. Housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely. The location is genuinely convenient, which is why I'm giving two stars instead of one, but for this price I expected much better. We won't be returning, and I'd suggest looking elsewhere if comfort matters to you.

I really wanted to like this place, but our stay at the Affinia was disappointing from start to finish. Check-in took forever because the front desk was understaffed, and when we finally got to our room, it smelled vaguely of smoke despite being non-smoking. The AC unit rattled all night, so neither of us slept well. Housekeeping missed our room entirely one day, and when I called down about it, they promised fresh towels that never showed up. The location is decent, I'll give them that, but for the price we paid I expected much better. Breakfast was cold and the coffee was terrible. The front desk clerk did comp us a parking night, which was nice, but overall I can't recommend this hotel. We won't be returning.
Honestly disappointed with Homewood. My room smelled musty, the AC rattled all night, and the 'hot' breakfast was lukewarm at best. Front desk took forever to answer. Won't be returning.

We've just returned from a two night stay at the Affinia Chicago and our visit was delightful. Thanks to tripadvisor reviews we were prepared for the major construction work on the facade and entrance..it was a mess. And the hotel restaurant and bar remain incomplete and unavailable. Even parts of the lobby had 'wet paint' stickers. All these things could have made for a disappointing stay. Not so!! Although we arrived very early in the day our suite was ready along with a most warm and gracious greeting from the front desk staff. After just a few minutes we felt like we were 'at home.' The suite on the 25th floor, with a fab view along a wall of windows, was sparkling fresh and clean. The bathroom lighting was outstanding and led to my bride of nearly 50 years saying that it made her look younger...she was right! Everything in and about the room was 'like-new' and very stylish. As a visitor we appreciated the very convenient location just a few steps from the Magnificient Mile and all of its ambiance. Thanks to a dedicated and gracious staff, a fantastic location, and chic decorating elements, this hotel can and will be our future hotel of choice in Chicago. The stay was short..but sweet.
Expected much more from a Hyatt at these rates. The room faced a noisy air shaft, the wifi kept dropping every few minutes, and the whole thing felt wildly overpriced for what you get. Won't be back.

The breakfast was a chaotic, lukewarm buffet with stale pastries, and our room faced a brick wall instead of any skyline. Bathroom tiles were grimy, and hallway noise from neighboring doors kept me up until midnight.

Fairmont's got that old-school grandeur done right--my room overlooked the lake and the bed was pure cloud. Staff remembered my name at breakfast, which felt classy without being stuffy. Wish I'd booked one more night.

The breakfast buffet was lukewarm and chaotic, with stale pastries that felt like an afterthought. Wi-Fi kept dropping on the third floor, and our window faced a brick wall--the tired, worn carpet only added to the dated, disappointing vibe.

I wanted to like Hotel Palmer because the location was convenient, but the stay was frustrating from the start. Check-in took nearly twenty minutes even though there was only one person ahead of me, and the front desk staff seemed more distracted than welcoming. My room looked tired: scuffed walls, a stained chair by the window, and a bathroom fan that rattled all night. The shower temperature kept changing between lukewarm and icy, which made getting ready unpleasant. Wi-Fi barely worked on the fifth floor, and calling down for help just resulted in a promise that someone would 'look into it.' Breakfast was picked over by 8:30, with cold coffee and no clean tables. For the price, I expected basic comfort and better service. I would choose somewhere else next time.

We booked the Hotel Amalfi based on the photos, but the reality was a massive letdown. Our 'sea view' room actually overlooked a side alley and a sliver of the harbor, and the constant noise from the street below meant we never got a decent night's sleep. The air conditioning sounded like a lawnmower and barely cooled the room. Breakfast was chaotic--the scrambled eggs were watery and cold, and the coffee tasted burnt. On the second day, the Wi-Fi completely died in our room, and when we called reception, the response was less than helpful. To be fair, the location is central, but for the price we paid, we expected far more comfort and basic maintenance. The only positive was the friendly bartender by the pool. We'll be finding different accommodation for our next trip, that's for sure.

Hotel Monaco was a lovely choice for a weekend in the city. The lobby has a playful, colorful feel without being too loud, and check-in was quick even though we arrived early. Our room was comfortable and surprisingly quiet, with a very good bed, plenty of storage, and a large bathroom. I appreciated the small touches, especially the robes and the complimentary coffee in the morning. The staff were friendly whenever we had a question and gave us a couple of genuinely useful restaurant suggestions nearby. The location made it easy to walk to several attractions, while taxis were readily available for farther trips. My only minor complaint was that the room felt a little dim at night, but overall it was clean, well maintained, and much more personal than a standard chain hotel.

I wasn't sure what to expect with a French luxury brand in the middle of downtown, but Sofitel exceeded every expectation. The room was beautifully quiet, which is rare in this part of the city, and the blackout curtains actually worked, so I slept like a rock. The bed was firm yet plush, with linens that felt crisp and cool. What really stood out was the staff--from the valet who remembered my name every single morning to the front desk agent who helped me rebook a flight without any hesitation. The pool is small but never crowded, and the gym had everything I needed. Breakfast was pricey, but the pastries were legitimately fresh and flaky. I'd absolutely stay here again for the service alone.

My two girlfriends and I arrived at the hotel, and found the hard rock had lost our reservation. I had just called three days before and had confirmed the reservation over the phone. The rude woman at the front desk treated us like we were lying. It wasn't until I started to cause a scene in front of the line of people checking in that she finally decided that she would research the issue. Ten minuets later she found our reservation. Our room wasn't ready, we were told that it would be ready at noon; we came back at 3 and were told it was still dirty! Room was very small. The bathroom shower, sink and floor were filthy. Room service trays sit in the hallways all day. The next morning we called down to get towels, they were never brought to the room, we had to drip dry. The only positive experience at the hotel was the concierge Christopher. He knew everything about the city and sent us to the perfect nightclub.
Honestly underwhelmed for the price. Booked the Conrad expecting luxury but got a room with a broken AC, slow service at breakfast, and street noise all night. Wouldn't return.

The location of the hotel is great, right on the river and Michigan Ave. Almost everything is within walking distance. At the price, though, and given the 4 star hotel, we expected better walls. Our room was connected to other rooms on both sides by locked doors. The sound from both rooms came in loud and clear. We heard our one neighbor making business deals on his phone (he clearly wasn't speaking loudly), and the other neighbors up at midnight yelling and screaming when they came back drunk. We asked them to be quiet (I shouldn't have expected that to work with some young drunks) then called security, but they did nothing. I was completely annoyed with the noise, especially in an expensive business hotel such as this one. Unless you are in Chicago to party, get drunk, and not get any sleep, I wouldn't stay here.

The 'garden view' was really a brick wall, and the thin walls meant I heard every hallway conversation until 3 AM. Staff were polite but unhelpful, and the rock-hard bed left me exhausted; I slept worse here than on the plane.

We just returned from our first trip to Chicago and stayed at the Omni. I read many reviews on trip advisor and picked the Omni based on its wonderful reviews and they were right on. The location, staff, rooms, amenities, etc were all wonderful. Huge thank you to TA members who suggested signing up for the preferred member program. We did that before we left and received complimentary beverages in the morning and newspapers among other perks. I loved being woken up to fresh orange juice and the Chicago Tribune newspaper. We were in room 816 which was perfect. Corner suite with two out of the 3 sides of the rooms being windows with a great view. The room was huge with a gorgeous king bed and great living area with plasma TV. The bathroom amenities were wonderful. I loved soaking in the tub with the mineral salts that were provided. The turn down service was great as well. We would come back to our room with relaxing music playing and our bed ready for us. We ate at their restaurant twice and the breakfast buffet was delicious. The blueberry muffins were the best I have ever had. Everything was so fresh and prepared perfectly. The staff at the Omni is so accomodating. Everyone is always smiling and asking you how your stay is. Have to thank the concierge Melissa and Curtis. They were both so helpful with great dining suggestions and maps for everything we wanted to do. I also used the gym during my stay and it was great. All the machines were top notch and each treadmill has a lcd TV attached. And the gym itself had two plasmas. They also had cold lemon water for you after your workout. I am a stickler for cleanliness and it was sparkling every morning. It really was a fantastic stay at the Omni and we would never stay anywhere else. I also wanted to mention we never heard any construction while we were there. Everything was quiet and we both slept wonderfully on the big comfy bed. Thank you Trip Advisor for another great trip suggestion!

My long weekend at Sofitel felt far too brief--I could have happily lingered another few days just to soak in that skyline view from my room. The floor-to-ceiling windows framed the city beautifully at both sunrise and nightfall. What truly set the stay apart, though, was the staff: every doorman, front desk agent, and housekeeper seemed genuinely invested in my comfort, remembering my name by the second morning. Breakfast was a quiet pleasure--flaky croissants, made-to-order omelets, and fresh-squeezed orange juice served in a serene dining room that never felt rushed. The bed was plush, the bathroom elegant, and the location made evening strolls effortless. I left only wishing I'd booked one more night.

Fantastic stay! The bed was incredibly comfortable, and the staff went above and beyond. Breakfast buffet had so many options, and the location made exploring the city a breeze. Felt genuinely refreshed.
Great stay overall. Rooms were clean and quiet, and the staff went above and beyond when we needed a late checkout. The breakfast had plenty of options. Would definitely return.
Our weekend at Hotel Monaco felt far too long: the Wi‐Fi kept dropping, the cramped bathroom smelled damp, and breakfast was stale pastries with lukewarm coffee.

I was really let down by the Hotel Talbott. The room felt stuffy and dated, and the walls were so thin I could hear every conversation next door. Service was polite but slow, and for the price, I definitely expected a much better night's sleep.

The Intercontinental's marble lobby is stunning, but that's where the glamour ends. My room smelled musty, the AC rattled all night, and housekeeping never replaced our towels. For these prices, I expected far better. Disappointed.

Swisses Chicago: Nice, but lacking in some pretty basic expectations in our modern era in a great spot along the Chicago waterfront. A spacious room is a comfortable respite from the city, but don't plug in your computer or hope for a free donut in the morning. No free WiFi here ,or affordable breakfast, or a free swim in the pool. Just a ten-dollar-a-night charge for internet, an on average $25 plate for breakfast, and another 15 bucks a night for the 'fitness center.' I've stayed in small town no star motels where WiFi is free as part of a 50 dollar room. Get with it - this is 2009! No free breakfast is not so bad as you probably ate too much for dinner and don't need it anyway, but for those of us who aren't charging everything to the company card some basics would be appreciated. Coffee, milk, OJ; stale donuts, ,muffins, maybe some cereal. Throw us a little something besides fruit flavored water in the lobby. With regards to swimming, this is another one wrapped up in a fitness center fee but the pool is only open till 10 pm plan accordingly. This all makes the $6 Fiji bottled water in the room seem like a bargain. Summation: Drop the fees, the nickel dimming of folks, and just charge what you need to charge to compliment what is otherwise a nice hotel.
Loved the stylish room and that rainfall shower--it felt worth every penny. Wi-Fi was flawless for streaming, and the complimentary breakfast with fresh pastries and espresso was a perfect start.

The Hilton exceeded expectations--staff were warm and efficient, and our room stayed blissfully quiet despite full occupancy. I slept like a log, though checkout came far too soon; honestly, one more night would've been perfect.

Great stay at Homewood Suites -- the free breakfast was surprisingly good, and the staff went out of their way to get us a late checkout. Rooms felt homier than most hotels, and it was nice having a kitchenette. Would definitely come back.

We stayed here as an alternative spot for a friend's wedding. The price was about 50% to 65% of what it costs to stay at similar hotels in the area. First the minuses. 1.) The standard rooms are small. if you want a little more space you might want to upgrade. 2.) Since the hotel has been recently rehabbed you can see some of the stuff that the covered or painted. 3.) There really are no views from the hotel. Now the plusses. 1.) The shower is AWESOME. Probably one of the best hotel showers I've seen. Rain shower with wand, great pressure and the enclosure didn't leak like a lot of these shower stalls do. Very nice. 2.) The fixtures and finishes in the rooms were top notch. Very modern and clean. 3.) The bed was great. Better than some hotels that promote their beds. Great nights sleep. Overall. This is a great space for a trip where you are not going to be spending much time in the room. If you were in town for a conference or for work where you will need to spread out your stuff it might not work. Anyone else should really like the experience. All I care about when I travel is having a nice bed and a good shower to relax in after a long day. If you are the same this is a good spot for you.

The bed was lumpy and the duvet felt damp, so I barely slept. The decor is tired and fraying at the edges. My 'city view' was a brick wall, and the bathroom's cracked tile and weak water pressure sealed the disappointing deal.
Swissotel looked polished, but my room was noisy all night, the air conditioning barely worked, and breakfast felt overpriced for the limited, lukewarm selection.

The staff at the Ambassador went above and beyond, remembering my coffee order by the second morning. Room was spotless with a gorgeous view, and the location made exploring effortless. Honestly, it felt like a home away from home--I'm already planning my return trip.

We booked the 'executive suite' for a weekend escape based on the photos, and honestly, we spent the first hour trying to figure out where the executive part was. The room smelled musty, like damp towels left in a gym bag, and the air conditioning unit rattled so loudly we had to turn it off just to hear ourselves think. The bed was one of those springy motel types, and the pillows were flat as pancakes. The bathroom had a cracked sink and the shower pressure was a pathetic trickle. We tried the on-site restaurant for breakfast, but the eggs were cold and the coffee tasted burnt. To make matters worse, the hallway was noisy all night - we could hear every door slam and someone's TV until 2 AM. For the price, this was a huge letdown. The only decent thing was the parking. We won't be returning.

Swissotel was the cleanest hotel I have ever stayed in! The room and bathroom were quite large for downtown Chicago. The pool and hot tub were also very nice. I would definately recommend this hotel. We didn't hear any noise in our room from other guests or from the city. It is in a great location - walking distance to Millenium Park, the Loop and Michigan Ave.

Booked the Fairmont expecting luxury, but everything felt tired and understaffed. Waited 40 minutes for room service, and the 'renovated' room had peeling wallpaper and a broken AC. Definitely not worth the premium rate.

I stayed at the Talbott twice in the last few weeks. I was very pleased with every facet of my stays. The staff, from doormen to front desk, to concierge, to housekeeping, were wonderful. The rooms were nicely sized and clean, and well stocked. I will return to the Talbott anytime!

My stay at the Hilton was much more frustrating than expected. Check-in took nearly 30 minutes, even though there were only two people ahead of me, and the desk agent seemed overwhelmed.
