The room looked fine at first, but the carpet was stained, the air conditioner rattled all night, and the bathroom fan never turned off. Housekeeping also skipped my room on the second day, so I had to call twice just to get fresh towels. Breakfast was expensive for what was offered, with lukewarm eggs and a long wait for coffee. The location was convenient, and one maintenance employee was genuinely helpful, but those positives did not make up for the poor service and tired condition of the room. For the price, I expected a much smoother and cleaner experience.

Stayed for 2 nights at The James, wonderful location 2 mins walk to Michigan Avenue with all the shops. Staff here were all incredibly helpful and genuinely friendly. Nothing was too much trouble. Rooms are huge and the beds the most comfortable I have slept in. Room was very clean, had separate seating area with sofa and chairs with a 42in flat screen tv. There was a bar area with stereo, mini bar and coffee maker. There was another flat screen tv in the bedroom area. Bathroom very good with complimentary shampoo, conditioner, shower gel and body lotion. Hotel is also 'pet friendly'. There was even a large bowl of iced water and a barrel of dog biscuits at the front door of the hotel !!!. Pets even had their own options on the room sevice menu.

I recently stayed at this hotel with my family (10-1 / 10-3). We had a terrific experience. I landed the hotel through Priceline for $80 per night and paid an additional $75 per night for a suite on the 41st floor. My two young boys loved it as the view was unbelieveable and the pool on the 42nd floor was easily accessible. I found all the employees that we interfaced with to be very friendly and accommodating. I would love to stay here again.
This hotel is the perfect location for downtown Chicago shopping. The only thing is the pool is extremely small - it is indoors, but looks much larger on the website.

Stayed here over a long weekend and left feeling thoroughly underwhelmed, especially for the nightly rate. The Wi-Fi was a joke--constantly dropping in the room, so I ended up tethering my laptop to my phone just to get work done. That's not acceptable at these prices. Breakfast was a cramped, chaotic buffet where the scrambled eggs were rubbery and the coffee tasted burnt; we waited fifteen minutes just for a table. Location is decent, right near the strip and easy walking to attractions, but everything else drags it down. The room itself felt worn, with stained carpet and a bathroom that smelled musty. I wasn't expecting luxury, but I was expecting basic competence. For what we paid, this was a rip-off. I won't be back.

Hotel Amalfi was a very pleasant surprise for our weekend stay. The location made it easy to get around, with restaurants and a few interesting shops within walking distance, yet our room was quiet at night. Check-in was quick, and the front desk staff were genuinely friendly without being overbearing. Our room had plenty of space for two, a comfortable bed, good water pressure, and a small sitting area where we could relax after sightseeing. Everything was clean, although the carpet in the hallway looked a little tired. We also appreciated the coffee available in the lobby each morning. It is not an ultra-luxury property, but the service, comfort, and convenient location felt like good value. I would happily stay at Hotel Amalfi again.
Disappointing stay at the Talbott--our room felt dated, the walls were thin, and housekeeping missed basic details. The location was convenient, but the price didn't match the experience.

I had a very pleasant stay at the Hilton and would gladly return. The room was spotless when I arrived, with fresh linens, a tidy bathroom, and no dust or unpleasant odors anywhere. The bed was especially comfortable, and the room stayed quiet at night, so I slept deeply despite being in a busy part of the city. The staff were consistently friendly and professional, from the efficient check-in to the helpful recommendations at the front desk. My room overlooked the river and downtown skyline, and the view was lovely both in the morning and after the city lights came on. Everything felt well maintained and thoughtfully organized. It was a comfortable, relaxing experience with service that made the hotel feel welcoming rather than impersonal.

I arrived and my friends were already there and visiting a nearby art gallery. They put my name on the reservation and told me to get a key from the front desk when I arrived. The front desk staff gave me the key to my room and I put my stuff away and went to meet the group. We returned late that night and I soon realized the room that my friends were in was not the room that I placed my stuff in that afternoon. We went to speak with the front desk. We were met with 'We can't do anything about that right now due to the hour. We will not disrupt the guest staying in the room you say you left your stuff in.' Unacceptable!!! My $1500 laptop and all of the things I brought with me were in that room! Not my mistake! FINALLY, after arguing with the head of security for about 30 minutes, they knocked on the door of the room I had left my belongings in and a lady answered. She was upset and stated she had security take the items from her room in the afternoon. All of my belongings were recovered in the security room; however, all of this hullabaloo could have been avoided had they communicated about the situation! Terrible, terrible customer service. They sent up an apology letter, champagne, and chocolate covered strawberries to the room. Although I was appreciative of the gesture, it still does not excuse the fact that they argued and continued to say 'We can't do anything about it.'

This is a great hotel! The views are fabulous, the service it friendly and the location is superb. We booked a room on an upper floor and had access to the lounge where breakfast and snacks were available with picture perfect views of the Chicago River. The only negative is that the ceilings in the hall and room are low and can make you feel a little cramped. We booked our room for $89 a night for Memorial Day weekend. It was a steal! I highly recommend this hotel to anyone and will be returning!

I recently stayed here for the Chicago triathlon. This was my third stay at this hotel. I have not had any issues until this visit. After the 3rd day of my stay I requested my room to be serviced and returned to what I thought was a clean room. While getting out of bed I was cut by a piece of glass in the carpet. I must not have been the first person to be cut in the room because I found dried blood on the bathroom floor afterwards. I had not noticed it before so I was very disgusted. We notified the staff and asked that the room be vacuumed and the bathroom mopped. We returned to the room after 5pm to find that the dried blood was still on the floor. After making a complaint to the customer service I have gotten no reply from the hotel. Considering the price point of this downtown hotel I would think that they would try to live up the 5 star rating but instead they have failed miserably. Luckily there are many hotels to choose from in downtown Chicago.

Slept wonderfully in the superbly quiet room, and the spotless bathroom made mornings feel effortless. Tucked steps from the seaside promenade, yet breakfast's fresh pastries and strong coffee were the perfect send-off for exploring.
The Palmer exceeded expectations -- the rooftop pool at sunset was pure magic, and the staff remembered my coffee order by day two. Comfy bed, spotless room, brilliant location. Would happily return.

This is best hotel bargin in Chicago if you are not overly unhappy with a small room. Great hotel just redone by Kimpton. This is a great hotel chain that really provides a the sense of escape and fun to all of their hotels. This is a location just off of LaSalle and next to the Cadillac theater. It has a 4 star resturant which we enjoyed in a relaxed atmosphere an amazing Italian meal. The wine list is one of the best in a city of great restaurants. The Kimptons have a social hour 5 to 6 with wine at all of their hotels. You sit in a designer, kind of London circa 1968 couch with a fire place nearby and have that lost art form of relaxation with you fellow guests. They are super animal friendly and provide complete services to your dog if you wish to bring it. The exercise room is great and there is a spa here as well. There are two other Kimptons here but for the money the Allegro is the best value and location. Always consider Kimptons as they never disappoint where ever we have used them.

We had such high hopes for Hotel Amalfi, but honestly the whole stay fell flat. The room was nowhere near as nice as the photos online -- worn carpet, a bathroom door that wouldn't close properly, and the air conditioning barely worked even after we reported it twice. Staff were polite enough but slow to fix anything, and housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely. Breakfast was the real letdown: stale bread, watery coffee, and the same sparse spread every single morning. The location is decent, sure, but you can hear street noise all night through thin windows, which made sleeping miserable. For the price we paid, I expected far more. Definitely won't be returning and can't really recommend this place unless you're just desperate for a bed.

Breakfast had plenty of fresh fruit and made-to-order eggs, and the lobby's mid-century furniture felt pleasantly current. Our room sparkled, and while I could've lingered another day, the weekend was exactly the reset I needed.
The room was surprisingly noisy at night, so I barely slept; the view was mostly a brick wall, and the staff seemed indifferent when I raised the issue.
The Omni looked grand in photos, but our room was dated, with a musty smell and paper-thin walls. Staff were polite but slow, and the overpriced valet was a joke. Left feeling ripped off.

When we were stranded in Chicago for two days since our flight home was canceled, our airline put us in touch with hotels.com who found us the room at the Sheraton Towers. After a long and frustrating day that ended up with us still in Chicago, arriving at the Sheraton was a joy. The entire staff was wonderful. The bell staff was great helping us (finally) let go of the heavy bags, Jonathan at check in was very helpful and had us in a room which he upgraded for us in no time. We enjoyed the location and the facilities of this property during our unexpected stay and would highly recommend this location to others. We can't say enough about the staff. If we are in Chicago in the future we will definitely return here!
Conrad looked polished, but check-in was slow, the room felt dated for the price, and late-night hallway noise made sleep difficult. Definitely not the relaxing stay I expected.

The Conrad felt like a letdown for the price. Check-in was painfully slow, the room had a musty smell, and housekeeping never came despite asking twice. The location is great, but that doesn't fix the dated bathroom or rude front desk.

The only minus for this hotel is they do not provide the free morning coffee at all the other Kimpton hotels. It was a great place to stay for the theater but our rate did say morning coffee. The robes were not in the room and it took a long time (hours) but other than that a great place. The concierge was excellent.

My Husband and I did not enjoy stay at Hotel Allegro! The room was so small. The bathroom was ridiculously stupid, everytime you use the sink you would splash water on yourself. Truly one person at time in the bathroom, it was like being in an airplane's bathroom. The walls are so thin, we heard the people across hall having sex. The some staff were really rude. I did not appreciate it when we had a sign on the door saying do not disturb the day of our check out. Check out time is 11am or 12 and we got a know on the door at 8AM with the sign stating ' do not disturb. ' The hotel did not have any microwaves in their rooms, no mini fridge, and no coffee maker either. NO DRAWERS to put your clothes in and the closet was very very very tiny. We were there for four days and three nights, so we had three suit cases full of clothes and no places to store them at. I also hated the fact that we had to pay almost fifty to park our car. My Husand and I will never stay at Hotel Allegro again!!!

For $800 a night, I expected far more--our room had dust on the nightstands and a bathroom with a broken shower head. Staff were courteous but painfully slow, making the whole experience feel overpriced and underwhelming.

The air-condition has a noisy fan/compressor in each room. It starts every 3 to 5 min and the noise will wake you up. At least the first night. This is an old fashion system that needs to be replaced. The postal service at the hotel is non-working. The hotel messed up our concert tickets that was correctly addressed and transported by UPS. The tickets were at the Hotel General Managers office. The reception denied that they had arrived. We had to spend most of a day travelling to the ticket agent to resolve it. The Hotel did not find any reason to apologize for the inconvenience. The concert was the reason for our travel to Chicago. Else, the Hotel had good standard, free internet in the lobby, not to good view from the rooms, and friendly staff at the restaurants and the bars. We had booked 20 room-nights all together staying at room 612, 425 and 431 from the 23rd June.
Beautiful property, but the staff seemed overwhelmed and indifferent. Waited 20 minutes for basic room service, and the AC never cooled properly. Not the luxury experience I paid for.

The Hard Rock hotel is great for a relaxing getaway. The rooms are quiet, the bed is comfortable and the bathroom is a nice size. We had fabulous service and got a great rate. Other than the fact that there were no bathrobes (it's listed as an amenity) and the Sony radio didn't work, it was perfect. Would definitely stay there again!

We booked the Ambassador specifically for the weekend spa package, and honestly, we should have saved the money. The 'deluxe' room we were given was anything but that - the wallpaper was peeling in the corner by the AC unit, and the bathroom had that lingering smell of damp towels. I'll give them credit for the valet being quick, but that's where the hospitality ended. The front desk staff were polite but dismissive when I asked about the pool closing times, which apparently change daily but aren't posted anywhere. Dinner at the in-house restaurant was a disaster: our reservation was lost, we waited 45 minutes for a table, and my steak came out overcooked and cold. The live jazz band was nice, but we could hear their entire set through the paper-thin walls, making it impossible to sleep before 11 PM. For nearly $400 a night, I expected a lot more than a mediocre breakfast buffet and a stained carpet. We won't be returning.

I wanted to like Hotel Allegro, especially because the theater district location is convenient and the lobby has a lot of character, but the stay was more frustrating than enjoyable. Check-in took nearly half an hour even though the desk did not seem particularly busy, and the room was much smaller and darker than expected. The air conditioner rattled through the night, while the street noise and hallway doors made sleeping difficult. Housekeeping also missed replacing the coffee cups and left only one bath towel for two guests. Staff were polite when I brought these issues up, but nothing was resolved beyond a vague apology. The rates may make sense during a busy downtown weekend, but for what I paid, I expected basic comfort and better attention to detail.
Hotel Allegro felt overpriced: the room had dusty surfaces and stained carpet, the bathroom was cramped with weak water pressure, and our view was just a brick wall.

Spent three nights in Chicago at this property. First of all, I have to say that it would be hard to imagine a better location as it is perfectly situated on the Magnificent Mile close to terrific restaurants, the Art Institute and Orchestra Hall. The hotel has two sides - the historic tower and a new wing. The rooms are larger on the historic side but generally are looking a little tired. This property needs to be renovated. Some observations: The junior suite I had was laid out strangely. A small bedroom and smaller sitting room separated by a corridor off of which was the very large bathroom. The mirror over the sink was not over the sink but skewed to the right - made shaving a challenge and messy. While descending in the elevator one morning, it started shaking so violently that I could barely stand up. It stopped on the 11th floor and I was greeted by an extremely worried looking hotel employee who had a technician shut it down. (This experience was far more powerful than coffee in helping me wake up - an adrenaline rush certainly cures sleepiness!) Reports from my group were of sinks stopped up, exposed bolts in rooms, and generally things not working. Now the good news - the staff is terrific. They make you feel welcome, are personable, have their own personalities, great service in the bar and really went the extra distance to help. I wish they had a better property to work in.

I wanted to like the Talbott because the location is excellent and the lobby has a charming, old Chicago feel, but the stay was frustrating from the start. Our room was not ready at check-in, and no one followed up when they said they would. Once we got in, the room felt worn rather than historic: scuffed furniture, a stained chair, and a bathroom fan that rattled all night. The air conditioning barely cooled the room, so sleeping was difficult. We also could hear doors slamming and conversations in the hallway early in the morning. Staff were polite when approached, but there was little urgency in resolving anything. For the price, I expected better upkeep and a smoother experience. The neighborhood is great, but I would choose another hotel nearby next time.
Staff seemed indifferent, the decor felt stuck in another decade, breakfast was bland and lukewarm, and the cramped bathroom had poor water pressure and peeling grout.

I really wanted to like the Affinia, but the whole stay felt like a bad flashback to the early 2000s. The hallway carpet was that weird, busy pattern that hides stains but looks perpetually grimy, and our room had a bulky, dated entertainment center that screamed for a remodel. The bed was surprisingly firm, but the pillow was so flat it was useless, and I tossed all night. We were on the seventh floor, yet the street noise from below was relentless, punctuated by sirens until 3 a.m. Honestly, three nights felt like an eternity here. The only positive was the convenient location, but that doesn't make up for feeling like I'd wasted a weekend on a tired, noisy relic. I'll pick a different spot next time.

We stayed at the Fairmont for four nights, and by the second morning I was honestly counting down until checkout. The room itself looked impressive at first glance, but the wow factor faded fast. Sleep quality was terrible throughout our stay -- thin walls meant we heard every slammed door in the corridor, and the air conditioning rattled loudly all night no matter what setting we used. I woke up exhausted every single day. Breakfast was the biggest letdown: for the prices they charge, I expected fresh and abundant, but the buffet was lukewarm, the eggs rubbery, and the coffee tasted like it had been sitting for hours. When we mentioned this at the front desk, we got a polite shrug and nothing more. For this kind of money, the value simply isn't there. We won't be back.

Our stay at the Hyatt felt well worth the price, especially considering the spacious room, comfortable bed, and reliable service throughout the weekend. The decor was fresh and modern without being overly trendy; the lobby had warm lighting and tasteful local artwork that made it feel welcoming. We had a higher-floor room overlooking the river and downtown skyline, and the evening view was a highlight. Every staff member we encountered was polite, attentive, and genuinely helpful, from the quick check-in to the concierge's restaurant suggestions. Breakfast was a little pricey, but it was convenient and nicely prepared. I would gladly stay here again for a city visit.
The room was worn and the AC rattled all night, plus the 'city view' was a brick wall. Staff seemed annoyed by basic requests, so I'd skip this place next time.

My stay at the Fairmont was disappointing, especially given the price and the hotel's reputation. The room looked elegant at first, but the walls were surprisingly thin; I could hear doors slamming and conversations in the hallway late into the night. I slept poorly despite the comfortable mattress, waking several times because of the noise and the overly warm room. The Wi‐Fi was another frustration, dropping repeatedly during video calls and taking ages to reconnect. Staff were polite, but resolving these issues felt slow and impersonal. I had booked two nights, which was already enough--rather than wishing I could stay longer, I was relieved to check out. The location is convenient, but the lack of rest and unreliable internet made the experience feel poor value overall.

We stayed at the Talbott for a long weekend and were pleasantly surprised by how much we got for the rate. The location was a dream--steps from the L and a short stroll to a dozen great restaurants, so we barely needed a rideshare. The bathroom, while compact, had excellent water pressure and plenty of hot water for morning showers. Our room's windows faced the side street, so it was quiet at night, which we appreciated. Wifi was reliable and fast enough for streaming a movie before bed without any buffering. Overall, it felt worth every penny, especially compared to pricier chain hotels nearby. Nothing fancy, but clean, comfortable, and in the heart of everything. I'd happily book again.

The room was tired and smelled musty, and the air conditioning rattled all night. The front desk staff were polite but couldn't fix the noise, and breakfast was a chaotic, understocked scramble. Not the Hilton standard I remember.

I had a very pleasant stay at the Hilton and would happily return. My room was spotless when I arrived, from the crisp linens to the sparkling bathroom and well-kept desk area. The bed was exceptionally comfortable, and the blackout curtains kept the room quiet and dark enough for me to sleep through the night, which is rare when I travel. Staff at both check-in and breakfast were warm, efficient, and genuinely helpful with directions and a late checkout request. I also loved the view from my window: the city skyline looked especially nice at sunset, with lights beginning to come on below. Overall, it felt polished, relaxing, and worth the price.

I was honestly impressed with how smoothly everything went at the Hyatt. The front desk team greeted me by name and even remembered I'd mentioned wanting a quiet floor, which was a thoughtful touch. My room was spotless--no stray hairs in the bathroom, crisp sheets, and the carpet actually looked vacuumed. The view faced the city skyline, and at dusk the lights were genuinely beautiful without feeling touristy. I'll admit I braced for tired furniture, but the space felt recently refreshed: the armchair looked new, and the bedside USB ports were a practical bonus. The hallway carpet showed slight wear, but that's inevitable. Staff in the hallways always smiled, and housekeeping restocked my coffee without me asking. Nothing flashy, just well-executed basics with a touch of care. I'd book here again without hesitation.

I stayed at the Fairmont for three nights and honestly can't fault it. My room was spotless, housekeeping kept everything immaculate each day, and the little touches like fresh linens and a properly made bed made a real difference. The bathroom was a highlight, spacious marble finishes, strong water pressure, and those fluffy robes I ended up living in. Sleep quality was excellent too; the bed was firm but comfortable and the blackout curtains blocked out the city light completely. Yes, it's pricey, but for the level of service, the impeccable concierge, and the overall standard, I'd say it's absolutely worth treating yourself. The staff remembered my name by day two, which felt genuinely welcoming. Would book again without hesitation next time I'm in town.

We booked the Hyatt specifically for a quiet anniversary weekend, and left wondering if we'd stumbled into a different hotel than the one in the photos. The air conditioning in our room sounded like a lawnmower having a seizure all night, and the third time we called the front desk, they actually suggested we 'try turning it off and on again.' The hallways smelled like a mix of stale beer and industrial cleaner, which was... memorable. Breakfast was a zoo--cold eggs, lukewarm coffee, and a woman arguing with the staff over the last croissant. On the plus side, the bed was decent and the location was convenient. But for these rates, I expected far more polish and a lot less hassle. It felt like a budget motel wearing a fancy suit. Disappointed feels like an understatement.

I stayed at the Hyatt for a two nights on a business trip. My room was oddly shaped to give a stunning view of the river and NBC Building. Both the room and the bathroom were spotless and the room had an air purifier which ran silently. The hotel was well staffed with individuals who were knowledgeable about both the hotel and the surrounding area. I would not hesitate to stay here again and plan to return with my wife for a weekend.

I stayed at the Affinia for four nights on a work trip and honestly wish it had been longer. The location made getting around easy, and the room was a genuine surprise--much bigger than I expected, with a kitchenette that came in handy more than once. What really stood out was how quiet it was. My room faced an interior side, so even with the windows open I barely heard street noise, and I slept solidly every night on what I'd call one of the more comfortable hotel beds I've encountered. The free wifi was fast and reliable throughout, which mattered since I had video calls most mornings. Staff were friendly without being overbearing, and housekeeping was consistent. If I'm back in the city, this is where I'll book. A few small scuffs on the furniture, but nothing that dented a great stay.

Breakfast at Homewood was a pleasant surprise--hot scrambled eggs, crispy bacon, and fresh waffles that weren't soggy. The bathroom was spotless with a strong shower and plenty of hot water, though the towels could've been plusher. I slept like a log; the mattress was firm but supportive, and the blackout curtains did their job against the morning sun. The Wi‐Fi held up without a single drop, even while streaming a movie on my laptop. Nothing fancy, but everything worked exactly as it should. Staff were friendly at check-in, and the room felt quiet despite being near the elevator. For the price, this was a solid, hassle-free stay--I'd book again without hesitation.
Fairmont made our weekend feel special--beautiful lobby, genuinely warm staff, and a quiet room with a great bed. Breakfast was pricey, but the service and location were worth it.
The James looked polished online, but our room smelled damp and the AC rattled all night. Front desk promised help twice, yet nobody came; definitely not worth the price.

I had a very pleasant two-night stay at the Sheraton for a quick work trip. The front desk team was warm and efficient, and they even held my bag after checkout without making it feel like an inconvenience. My room was quiet, well kept, and had a comfortable bed that made the early meetings easier. From the upper floor, the view stretched over the city skyline and was especially nice around sunset. The restaurant staff were attentive without hovering, and breakfast arrived quickly. It is not the cheapest option in the area, but the dependable service, clean facilities, and convenient location made it feel worth the price. If anything, the stay was too short--I would have happily stayed through the weekend.

Checked in to find the room wasn't ready, then the A/C rattled all night. The 'historic charm' translates to thin walls and dated furniture. Staff was polite but overwhelmed. For the price, I expected much more. Won't be back.

We booked the Conrad for our anniversary weekend and honestly expected it to be lovely, but it still exceeded our expectations, which made the price feel completely worth it. Our room on a high floor was spacious and beautifully maintained, and the bathroom was a genuine highlight -- huge soaking tub, separate rain shower, marble everywhere, and fluffy towels restocked twice a day. The wifi was fast and reliable; I had a video call one morning with zero glitches. Best of all, despite being in the middle of everything, the room was remarkably quiet. We barely heard a sound from the hall or the street, and we slept better than we do at home. Staff remembered our names by day two. We'll absolutely be back for our next special occasion.

This hotel was chosen by my husband's company as the family came along for the business trip. The location was excellent and we had a great view of the lake and aquarium from the 34th floor. My first impressions were that the room was very nice and everything appeared to be clean. The lobby was undergoing renovation at the entrance, but was otherwise ok. Lots of conferences were taking place so the wait for the elevators was long. Seemed like only 2 elevators were working out of the 6 that were there. I had read from another reviewer to join the Fairmont President's club and wi-fi in the room would be free. We signed up for the club, but were puzzled as to why they don't just offer everyone free wi-fi. Parking fees were exorbitant at $58/night, but thankfully the company was paying for this. We were able to walk to Millennium Park and Navy Pier from our hotel. The hotel is NOT kid-friendly in terms of restaurants or amenities. There is no swimming pool, but the concierge arranged for us to swim at the Swissotel next door (there is an underground tunnel that connects the Fairmont there). We loved the Swissotel's pool on the 42nd floor. Fantastic views from the pool! Although the beds were comfortable, my daughter and I were both victims of bed bugs during our stay. Unfortunately we didn't know until the next day after we returned home. Apparently bed bug bites can take up to 7 days to appear. My daughter and I both shared a bed and were bitten on our sides from our necks to our hips. The bites made you want to claw your skin off! My husband and son who shared the other bed were not bitten at all. Beware of room 3405 -- bed nearest the bathroom!!! I will not be fooled by a clean room again and will be checking under mattresses from now on....

My stay at Sofitel was a masterclass in understated luxury. From the moment I stepped into the soaring, light-filled atrium, the atmosphere felt calm and effortlessly chic. The room itself was a sanctuary--the bed was impossibly comfortable, with crisp linens that made it hard to leave each morning. I particularly loved the deep soaking tub and the rainfall shower; it was the perfect way to unwind after a long day of meetings. The staff, without exception, were gracious and attentive, remembering my name and coffee order by the second day. The location on State Street was ideal, putting me within walking distance of the river and Millennium Park. While the lobby bar can get a bit lively in the evenings, it adds to the energy. I left feeling genuinely rested and spoiled. A truly wonderful, refined experience that I would happily repeat.

Disappointing stay at the Affinia. Room was dated with a musty smell, the AC barely worked, and front desk staff seemed indifferent when we complained. Price felt way too high for what we got. Won't return.

I expected a fun, polished stay at Hard Rock, but it felt more like a busy nightclub with rooms attached. Check-in took nearly half an hour because only one desk agent seemed to be working, and nobody acknowledged the line. Our room looked stylish in photos but was worn around the edges: stained carpet, a flickering bathroom light, and an AC unit that rattled all night. The bass from the lobby bar was still noticeable well after midnight, even on a higher floor. Housekeeping skipped our room the first day, then brought towels only after two calls. The location was convenient, but for the price I expected better service, cleaner upkeep, and at least a decent night's sleep.

The Talbott was a quiet refuge--staff remembered my name by day two, and the cozy library lounge felt like a secret gem. Rooms are snug but polished, and the location is unbeatable for strolling to the lake or River North. Thoroughly enjoyed it.

I stayed there on October 6, 2012. When I pulled the covers of my bed, there was a small dark brown insect the size of a grain of rice, which was either a bed bug or cockroach. I trapped it under a glass (see the attached pictures) and called the front desk. The housecleaning person claimed it was a cockroach. Absolutely horrible service by the hotel management to respond to the problem, failing to follow through on promises they made to me. Setting aside the bug problem, I caution that the windows are quite thin. We could hear a lot of the street noise, which made for a hard night's sleep, not to mention worrying about insects even after changing rooms. For $400 a night after tax, I strongly encourage you to check for alternatives.

My stay at Homewood was disappointing and not nearly as comfortable as expected. The decor feels dated, with worn carpets, scuffed furniture, and a generally tired look rather than the fresh, welcoming atmosphere shown in the photos. The bed was reasonably clean, but it was too firm for me, and the thin walls meant I could hear hallway conversations and doors closing late into the night. Breakfast was another letdown: the selection was limited, several items were lukewarm, and the coffee tasted stale when I arrived around 8 a.m. The staff were polite enough, but interactions felt rushed and indifferent when I mentioned the noise. A few basic improvements and better attention to guest concerns would make a big difference. For the price, I expected a much more pleasant stay.

The hotel lost our reservations and then couldin't accommodate what we needed. they gave us a room much smaller than we needed and when we requested something diffrerent they were unable to fulfill our request. we opted to leave the hotel and after there mistake of losing our reservations, they still charged us an early check out fee. If it wasn't for the great location of the hotel, there would be nothing positive to say/

I had high hopes for the Hilton given its reputation, but our three-night stay left us let down at nearly every turn. The 'city view' room we paid extra for mostly looked out onto a grey wall of office buildings and a rooftop of rattling AC units, so we kept the curtains drawn most of the time. Oddly, two nights felt like plenty -- not because we were worn out from sightseeing, but because there was little to enjoy in the room itself. The wifi was a real headache: it dropped constantly in the evenings and made even basic browsing frustrating. Staff interactions were hit or miss. One housekeeper was lovely, but the front desk seemed annoyed by questions, and an early-morning wakeup call we never requested jolted us awake at 5:30. For the price, I expected far more polish and warmth. I won't be rushing back.

Our stay at Hotel Amalfi was more disappointing than expected. We booked a room advertised with a view, but the window looked directly onto a narrow alley and a collection of air-conditioning units; we kept the curtains closed most of the time. The location is convenient for reaching the main sights and public transport, although the surrounding streets became noisy late at night. Staff interactions were inconsistent. One receptionist was pleasant and helpful, while another seemed irritated when we asked about a missing towel and offered no apology. The lobby may once have felt stylish, but the decor now looks tired, with worn carpets, faded upholstery, and dated furniture. Our room was reasonably clean, yet the old-fashioned bathroom and uncomfortable mattress made it hard to relax. I would choose somewhere else next time.

Stayed three nights at Allegro and left genuinely impressed. The bed was firm but supportive, and the blackout curtains worked wonders--I slept straight through until 8am, which never happens at home. Despite being a few blocks from the main square, the room was remarkably hushed; the double-glazed windows completely muffled the street noise. Breakfast was a pleasant surprise, with a made-to-order omelette station and fresh pastries that beat the usual hotel buffet fare. Location-wise, you couldn't ask for more: a five-minute walk to the cathedral and surrounded by cozy cafes and bakeries for afternoon coffee breaks. The only minor hiccup was the shower pressure fluctuating in the morning, but that's nitpicking. Would absolutely book again for the quiet nights and unbeatable convenience.

I booked two nights but left after one, and honestly, that's the only regret I have about my stay at the InterContinental. I slept like a log in the ridiculously comfortable bed, waking only to the soft glow of sunrise over the river. The staff from the doorman to the housekeeping team were unfailingly gracious, never once making me feel rushed or like a bother. Breakfast in the main dining room was a highlight; the made-to-order omelets were perfect, and the fresh pastries were still warm. Between exploring the city and relaxing in my immaculate room, the time simply evaporated. I'm already plotting a return trip with a proper long weekend, because one night here just isn't nearly enough to soak it all in.

I wanted to like the James, especially given the price and the location, but the stay was more frustrating than relaxing. Check-in took nearly half an hour, and the desk agent seemed distracted and never explained the destination fee or how to use the Wi-Fi. Our room looked stylish in the photos, yet the carpet was worn, the bathroom door didn't close properly, and there was a persistent humming noise from the ventilation system all night. Housekeeping also skipped our room on the second day, despite the 'please make up room' sign being out. When I called down, fresh towels arrived much later than promised. The bed was comfortable, and the lobby staff were polite, but those positives didn't justify the expense. I left feeling the hotel's reputation was doing more work than the actual service.

The breakfast was a sad, lukewarm spread of stale pastries, and our room wasn't much better. The walls were so thin we heard every door slam, and I barely slept on the gritty sheets that clearly hadn't been changed.

I expected more from the Ambassador, especially at the rate we paid. Check-in was slow, and the room looked tired rather than charming, with worn carpet, scuffed furniture, and a bathroom that clearly needs updating. Our window faced a wall and a collection of rooftop machinery, so there was hardly any view or daylight. The bed was comfortable enough, but the thin walls made it easy to hear conversations and doors closing in the hallway. We only stayed two nights, which was probably long enough; by the second morning, the little inconveniences had become difficult to overlook. The staff were polite, but not especially attentive when we mentioned the noise. For this price, I expected fresher decor, a better outlook, and a more polished experience. It did not feel worth the money.

The Conrad delivered on every front--stylish, well-maintained interiors that feel current, fast Wi-Fi, and a prime spot steps from great dining and transit. It's not cheap, but the location and comfort justify every penny. I'd happily return.

The Sofitel felt more like a sterile glass box than a Parisian retreat. Our 'upgraded' room had a view of a concrete wall, the air conditioning rattled all night, and housekeeping skipped us entirely until we called twice--truly underwhelming for the price.

This hotel was chosen for me for a business convention. The lobby was pretty cool. But the rooms were tiny and very dark. I had a huge picture of Kiss above my toilet. It was very hard to do my makeup or read because of the lighting. The location is OK. You have to walk a few blocks to get to the best part of Michigan Ave, but its not too bad. Be prepared for some sad sights after dark. Apparently panhandling is permitted in Chicago ( some cities will give you a ticket for begging) because at night, the beggars come out. The saddest thing i saw was an older woman with her two grandkids sitting on a curb in the freezing snow on a -5 temp night. Those kids looked terrible. Unfortunatly its all up and down the wealthiest part of the city. You don't see so many in the daylight. Also the room service at the Hard Rock is pretty good. Its plenty for 2 people. I would not stay here again though. I suggest the Omni Hotel.
The James felt fresh and thoughtfully designed, with a pleasant city view from my room. Breakfast was tasty and well organized, and the Wi-Fi stayed reliable throughout my visit.

I was disappointed by my stay at Hotel Monaco. The lobby and room had a stylish look, but the upkeep did not match the price: worn furniture, a bathroom fan that barely worked, and a mattress that was far too soft. Noise was also a problem, with doors slamming in the hallway and street traffic continuing well past midnight. I had booked two nights, and honestly that felt like more than enough; I was ready to leave after the first evening. Breakfast was another letdown--limited choices, lukewarm eggs, and coffee that tasted like it had been sitting around. The staff were polite, but not especially helpful when I mentioned the noise. With taxes and extra fees, the stay was nowhere near worth what I paid.

The location is fine, right by the park, but that's about all this place has going for it. We booked a 'deluxe' room and got a cramped space with a view of a brick wall, and the AC unit sounded like a lawnmower all night. The hallways smelled like old carpet and stale air freshener. Breakfast was a disaster--cold eggs, dry pastries, and the coffee machine was out of order for the whole three days. The front desk staff weren't rude, just completely indifferent, like we were bothering them by asking for extra towels. We asked for a late checkout and were told no, with zero flexibility. For the price we paid, this felt like a budget motel with a fancy lobby. I honestly don't understand the positive reviews. Maybe they got a different room. I wouldn't recommend it unless you're desperate for the location and don't mind basic, mediocre service. I'm still kicking myself for not booking elsewhere.
A wonderfully quiet stay at Sofitel, with a lovely city view and a price that felt justified. The marble bathroom was spotless, spacious, and stocked with quality toiletries.
Room smelled of stale cigarette smoke despite the no-smoking tag, and the AC rattled all night. Waited 40 minutes for a lukewarm breakfast. Definitely not the Hilton standard I remember.

My wife and I decided to spend three days in Chicago last summer, and booked via Expedia. When we first walked into the lobby we almost fell over at its' beauty. It's like something out of Europe. We were able to get a free room upgrade, even though the rooms are still a bit small, but its' an old hotel in an old city. It's there for sleeping and showering. The restaurants, lounges, and shops were all wonderfull. The next time we travel to Chicago, I'll be affraid to stay anywhere other than the Palmer House Hilton

My stay at the InterContinental was very enjoyable from check-in to departure. The room was spotless, with crisp linens, dust-free surfaces, and housekeeping that kept everything looking fresh each day. It felt well worth the price, especially given the attentive service and the quiet, polished atmosphere. The bathroom was spacious and modern, with excellent water pressure, fluffy towels, and a separate shower that made getting ready easy. I slept exceptionally well on the comfortable bed; the blackout curtains and effective soundproofing meant I barely noticed the city outside. Small touches like complimentary water and a well-stocked coffee station made the stay feel more thoughtful.

I expected more from the Knickerbocker given the rate and its location. My room looked tired, with scuffed furniture and a bed that felt lumpy; I slept poorly because hallway noise and a humming air unit continued well past midnight. The bathroom was especially disappointing: cramped, poorly lit, and the shower pressure barely managed a rinse. Breakfast downstairs was expensive for a limited buffet of lukewarm eggs, dry pastries, and coffee that tasted burned. The only bright spot was the view from the upper floor, which offered a lovely glimpse of the city skyline, though the windows needed cleaning. Staff were polite but did little when I mentioned the noise. I would choose another hotel next time.
I had a really comfortable stay at the Sheraton, with a spacious room, helpful staff, and a great breakfast. The lobby was lively, but everything still felt organized and relaxing.

My husband and I stayed here for three nights while visiting Chicago as tourists. What a beautiful hotel! Our room was lovely, the staff was super helpful and the location was convenient. They don't have an in house gym, but each day you can get a day pass to a cushy gym down the street. The restaurant in the hotel has a very yummy breakfast. The concierge helped us to make dinner reservations at the last minute our first night there. We were able to walk down the Magnificent Mile from our hotel, as well as through the Gold Coast and Old Towne neighborhoods. There are tons of great restaurants in the area (including the famous Gibsons and the Signature Room in the Hancock tower) as well as lots of shopping. There is currently a lot of construction going on near the Talbott (they are building condos right behind it), but regardless we had a wonderful stay and would definitely stay there again when visiting Chicago.

If location is the only thing that matters, stay at the Talbott. However, my wife and I have travelled extensively throughout North America and Europe, and I have never, in my entire life, seen such an inept housekeeping staff. They are unprofessional, noisy, incompetent and better suited for a one star hotel. They were yelling in the halls, slamming doors, and taking far too long to clean each room. They come to your room several times to check the fridge where they sell bottles of water for $3. The hotel was being renovated when we were staying there so we also had to endure the construction work - no discount was offered even after we complained several times. The front desk staff was very polite, but who cares?They're supposed to be nice. I spent a lot of money to stay here and did not feel that I received a fair deal. The room was sub-par for the price, even for an inner city hotel. Stay somewhere else and have a better vacation.

Stayed for a week last month. Can't beat the location - close to the Magnificent Mile, Attractions, Tours, Great Restaurants & Night Life. Have spent a lot of nights in other Homewood suites hotels and other suite hotels. Thought the room was ok, not great. Overpriced in my opinion. Found staff to be uninterested and not very helpful. Had to wait in the lobby on the 6th floor for room to be ready and the front desk staff could care less. Watched during the week as other guests were made to wait as well. Breakfast was the same stuff day after day. As the week went on, they actually started to run out of the more popular food items and these were not replenished (weekly delivery I guess). Also, the room was was so busy that the staff made people wait for a table and treated you as you were waiting for a 5 star restaurant. Travel for work (sales) and frequently stay in hotels. Travel with family every year and also stay in hotels. This is roughing it for me...not a camper. Would come to Chicago again, but would not stay here. There are too many other options worth investigating.
Hyatt looked polished online, but our room smelled stale, the AC rattled all night, and the front desk never followed up after we reported it. Not worth the rate.

My stay at the Conrad was disappointing, especially given the price and reputation. The room looked attractive at first, but the carpet had visible stains and there was dust along the desk and behind the nightstand. The bathroom was spacious, though the grout around the shower needed attention, and the water pressure kept changing. Staff at check-in were polite but distracted, and it took several calls to get extra towels delivered. Noise was another issue: I could clearly hear doors slamming and conversations in the hallway late into the night, while traffic began rumbling outside before sunrise. I mentioned these problems at checkout, but the response felt rehearsed rather than genuinely concerned. The location may be convenient, but the lack of basic upkeep and restful atmosphere made the stay feel overpriced.

I love the Ambassador East, true, she's a little old but she's a classic treasure. The service is wonderful, from the minute you arrive you are greeted warmly and with a nice welcome! I felt the service was good, room was clean and quiet and that all the staff was very accomodating. The biggest gem is the Pump Room bar and restaurant. The best drinks, amazing food, exciting photographs and fun music on the weekends. This is set in the most fabulous location; historical neightborhood, close to walk the lakefront, well known hometown bars, excellent restaurants Chicago has to offer and most of all shopping. There was a nice street market going on over the summer-fall weekends, giving this area a real interesting flavor of Chicago. I can see it needs some updating but I was totally happy and content with my stay. I travel a great deal in my work and have seen all kinds of hotels. I will stay here again in the future.

I wanted to like the James because the location is convenient and the lobby looks polished, but the stay felt overpriced from the start. Check-in took nearly twenty minutes even though there was only one person ahead of me, and no one acknowledged the delay. My room had scuffed furniture, a stained chair, and a shower door that wouldn't close properly, so water pooled across the bathroom floor. The air conditioning clicked loudly all night and the room never really cooled down. I mentioned these issues at the desk the next morning and was told someone would look into it, but nothing changed before checkout. For the rate they charge, I expected better maintenance and more attentive service.

My friend and I stayed for just one night, and loved the hotel. It had an awesome water feature in the hotel, and great large bar. Like all Hyatts it had a very comfortable bed, lot's of pillows, and large bathroom.

Generally speaking, nothing bad about that place if there would not be the cleaning issue. We checked the closed with the mini bar (picture uploaded), so much dust, nobody cleaned here for at least 3 years. We called in housekeeping, giving them the opportunity to check and do something about it. Still the same situation when returning to the room 4 hrs. later. Next day moved to a renovated room, much better but not 5 star clean at all. In addition, there was never a time when there was no waiting line at the reception, no wonder when just 1/3 of the counters is actually open. Please do something about these issues its ruining everything!
Great location near Grand Central and the staff couldn't have been friendlier. Room was spacious with a comfy bed and kitchenette--perfect for my week-long stay. Would definitely return.

The Knickerbocker's tired, dated decor made the price hard to justify, though you can't beat the Mag Mile proximity. My room had dusty corners and a stained carpet, and the cold, rubbery breakfast was a forgettable afterthought.
At Affinia, our room was spotless and quiet, with a pleasant city view. Wi-Fi stayed reliable for work, and the comfortable bed gave us an excellent night's sleep.
The Conrad felt overpriced for the experience: the room was clean but oddly worn, breakfast was bland and chaotic, and the cramped bathroom had weak water pressure.

I had a very comfortable stay at Swissotel and would happily return. The front desk team was friendly and efficient, especially when I needed directions and a late checkout; they handled both requests without making me feel like a bother. My room was quiet, bright, and large enough to work in comfortably, with a particularly good bed after long days exploring the city. The bathroom was spotless and practical, with strong water pressure, plenty of towels, and a spacious walk-in shower, although the fixtures looked slightly dated. I stayed for three nights, which felt far too short because I never had time to enjoy the fitness facilities or relax properly in the lounge. Rates were not cheap, but the location, service, and overall comfort made the price feel justified.

I was really looking forward to our weekend at the Talbott, but the experience left me flat. The front desk staff seemed almost annoyed by our presence, barely looking up from their screens during check-in. The decor is stuck in the early 90s, with tired floral patterns and worn carpet in the hallways that smells faintly of dust. Our room faced the back alley, so the 'city view' was really just a brick wall and a dumpster. The bed was saggy, and the constant humming from the HVAC unit made it impossible to fall asleep until late. I woke up more tired than when I arrived. For this price, I genuinely expect better service and a decent night's rest. I would not return, which is a shame because the location is convenient.

I had a very comfortable two-night stay at the Sheraton while visiting for a conference. The lobby was busy, but check-in moved quickly and the front desk agent was friendly and clear about the hotel facilities. My room was clean, quiet, and larger than expected, with a comfortable bed, plenty of outlets, and a desk that made catching up on email easy. I especially appreciated the strong water pressure and the surprisingly good coffee in the room. The fitness center was well maintained, and the restaurant downstairs was convenient for breakfast when I didn't feel like going out. The location also made it simple to get around, with restaurants and public transportation nearby. Nothing felt overly formal, but everything worked well. I'd gladly stay here again.

My wife and I frequently stay downtown for a night in the city. We have been to many hotels in the downtown Chicago area. My opinion of the Swissotel - spend your money elsewhere and get a much better experience. The Swissotel has a very 'cold' atmosphere and its very difficult to feel comfortable. The room was average at best however the cost per night was far from average. The view from our room faced a construction site which is a soon to be trump building that will block the lake view from the hotel. Other hotels are also a couple blocks closer to the action and again for the cost we would expect more. Our room and the lobby areas had a strange smell and someone was actually vacuuming the hallway floors at 8:00a which woke us up. We called the front desk to complain and were extremely shocked to be treated rudely by the person at the desk. We also had a couple of friends come downtown and they were waiting in the lobby when they were approached by a gentleman asking if they were guests of the hotel. They said no but that they were waiting on us and he actually asked them what our names were and then they looked it up to verify that we were on the guest register. He didnt even apologize to them for the inconvenience and imbarrassment. Overall it was just an unpleasant experience because we were expecting top notch treatment. Spend your money for a nicer hotel just off the lake or off Michigan avenue for real top notch service. Anyone giving this hotel a top review obviously hasnt had the opportunity to stay at a nicer hotel in the area.

Honestly expected much more from a Sofitel. Check-in took forever because the front desk seemed staffed by one overwhelmed employee, and when I finally got to my room the air conditioning barely worked. I called down twice about it and someone said maintenance would come up, but nobody ever showed. The room itself felt tired -- scuffed furniture, a carpet with visible stains near the window, and the 'luxury' bedding was just average at best. Housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely and we had to request towels ourselves. Breakfast was the final letdown: cold eggs, slow service, and an absurd price for what it was. Location is decent, I'll grant that, and the doorman was genuinely kind. But for these rates? Applies nowhere near the standard. Won't be returning.

Fantastic stay at the Hard Rock! The breakfast spread was fresh and generous, staff went out of their way to be helpful, and our room had a gorgeous city view. Honestly felt like great value for the price.

The Omni doesn't just put you in the middle of downtown--it puts you in a genuinely comfortable bubble above the chaos. My corner room had a ridiculous view of the lake, and the bed was so good I actually skipped an early meeting just to stay horizontal. The staff never made me feel like a number; the front desk guy remembered my coffee order by day two. I used the pool when it was quiet, and the towels were huge and warm, not those thin afterthoughts you usually get. Breakfast was pricey, but the omelet station was worth the splurge. Only gripe: the hallway ice machine was on the fritz one night. All in all, I left feeling rested, not frazzled--which is exactly what I want from a business trip. I'd gladly book it again.

We'd been looking forward to staying at the Hard Rock for months, and honestly it fell flat in almost every way. Our room overlooked the loading dock, so instead of any kind of skyline we got dumpsters and delivery trucks rumbling in before dawn each morning. The bathroom was worse: tiny, with a shower that alternated between scalding and freezing, hair in the drain, and water pooling around the toilet because the seal was broken. Sleep was impossible anyway thanks to the thumping bass from the bar drifting up until 2 a.m. Then until nearly 1. The staff, save for one kind housekeeper, seemed genuinely annoyed by requests -- the front desk guy shrugged when I complained about the noise and offered nothing. For what they charge per night, this place is a rip-off. We won't be back.

We booked the Omni for a three-night anniversary getaway, and I'm honestly baffled by the hype. The room we were given - a 'deluxe king' - smelled musty, and the air conditioning unit clanked all night like a trapped bird. We asked for a quiet floor, but we were right above the loading dock, so deliveries started at 6 AM sharp. The bathroom had a cracked tile and the shower pressure was laughable, barely a drizzle. The so-called 'gourmet' breakfast buffet was a sad spread of stale croissants and powdered eggs. I will say the front desk staff were polite, but they couldn't do much about the situation. For the price - nearly $400 a night - this was a massive letdown. We've stayed at far better mid-range chains for a third of the cost. Won't be back.

The view from my 14th-floor room was the only thing that didn't disappoint--a hazy slice of the skyline that felt wasted on a window I barely had time to enjoy. My three-night business stay stretched into an eternity of restless evenings, the bed too firm and the hallway noise relentless until past midnight. I would have traded half that time for functioning internet; the complimentary Wi-Fi dropped every twenty minutes, forcing me to re-login repeatedly while trying to join a video call. The staff, though polite at check-in, vanished when I asked for a late checkout--and the front desk agent who finally appeared seemed annoyed, barely glancing up from her screen. The hallways smelled faintly of stale coffee, and the air conditioning rattled like a loose shutter. For the price, I expected far more than a good view and a lukewarm hello.
Hotel Amalfi looked tired, the room smelled damp, and the air conditioner rattled all night. Staff were polite but couldn't resolve the noise, making the stay frustrating for the price.
Expected more from the Knickerbocker. Tiny room, noisy AC, and the front desk staff acted like we were an inconvenience. For $700 a night, honestly disappointing. Won't be back.
My two-night stay at Hotel Amalfi felt far too short; the quiet room delivered a great night's sleep, and the balcony view was lovely. Excellent value for the price, and I'd happily return.

I expected more from a Hyatt, especially for what we paid over a busy weekend. The lobby looked polished, but everything after check-in felt oddly neglected. Our room had a faint damp smell, the carpet near the window was stained, and the thermostat barely changed the temperature. We called twice about the air conditioning and eventually someone came up, but only suggested opening the window. Breakfast was crowded, with empty trays sitting out for too long and tables not being cleared. Staff members were polite when you could find one, though the front desk line moved painfully slowly each morning. The location was convenient, but that was really the main positive. Nothing was disastrous, just a string of small disappointments that made the stay feel overpriced and not very restful.

I expected more from a property with the Conrad name, honestly. Our room looked fine at first glance, but a closer look told another story: crumbs behind the nightstand, stained upholstery on the chair, and something dry and sticky on the bathroom floor that never quite went away even after we asked housekeeping to redo it. The bathroom itself felt dated for this price bracket, with a shower that fluctuated wildly between lukewarm and scalding. We also underestimated how thin the walls were; every night we heard neighbors' TVs, hallway conversations, and the muffled bass from the bar downstairs until well past midnight. The staff weren't rude exactly, just indifferent. Nobody followed up on anything, requests took hours, and the concierge seemed annoyed to be asked basic questions. For nearly $400 a night, I can't recommend this place. won't return.

I stayed at the Swissotel for a quick weekend break and was sorry to leave so soon. From the moment I arrived, the front desk team were warm, efficient, and genuinely helpful with restaurant suggestions and directions. My room was quiet despite the central location, with a comfortable bed and a great view over the city. The bathroom was particularly impressive: bright, spotless, and well laid out, with a roomy shower, good water pressure, and enough counter space for two people's toiletries. Breakfast was fresh and varied, and the staff kept everything running smoothly without hovering. It is not the cheapest option in the area, but the service, comfort, and location made it feel well worth the price.

Hotel Amalfi was convenient for walking to the river, Michigan Avenue, and several restaurants, but that was about the only real advantage. Our room faced an alley and neighboring office windows, so the 'city view' amounted to brick walls, air-conditioning units, and early-morning delivery noise. The lobby tries for boutique charm, yet the dark carpets, worn furniture, and heavy drapes made the decor feel dated rather than stylish. At check-in, the front desk barely acknowledged us and seemed annoyed when we asked about parking. We also had to request fresh towels twice before they appeared. The room itself was cramped and showed plenty of scuffs and tired fixtures. For the price, I expected warmer service and a better-maintained hotel.

We booked the Allegro based on photos that must have been taken a decade ago. The hallway smelled like a mix of old cigarettes and bleach, and our 'city view' was a brick wall and a flickering neon sign from the laundry across the street. The bed was lumpy, and the pillows were like concrete blocks. After a long day, we just wanted to rest, but the thin walls meant we heard every flush, every TV, and a couple arguing next door until 2 AM.

The breakfast was the final straw. Cold scrambled eggs, watery juice, and a coffee machine that was out of order. The only friendly staff member was the bellman; everyone else acted like we were an inconvenience. For the price, I expect basic comfort and a functioning room. This place missed the mark on everything. I genuinely can't recommend it unless you're desperate and out of other options. Save your money.

The beds were comfortable, I'll give them that, but that's about the only positive thing I can say about my stay. Check-in took forever because there was only one person at the front desk, and she was juggling phone calls and a line of guests. The room itself had a faint, musty smell that no amount of air freshener could cover. Housekeeping never came by on the second day, and I had to ask for fresh towels at the desk, which felt like pulling teeth. The 'hot breakfast' was lukewarm at best, with scrambled eggs that looked like they'd been sitting out for hours. The hallway was noisy until past midnight, and the walls were so thin I could hear the TV in the next room. Honestly, for the price I paid, I expected so much more. I'm disappointed and probably won't be back.
Our weekend at the Knickerbocker went by too quickly. Despite the central location, the room was remarkably quiet, Wi-Fi stayed reliable, and breakfast had fresh pastries, eggs, and good coffee.

We had high hopes for the Monaco based on the photos, but our stay was honestly a letdown. Breakfast was the biggest disappointment: the eggs were cold, the pastries tasted like they'd been sitting out since the previous evening, and they ran out of coffee twice while we waited. The staff seemed indifferent at best--we asked for extra towels at the front desk and got a shrug and a fifteen-minute wait with no apology. As for sleep, forget about it. Our room faced the street and the noise from traffic and late-night revelers went on until nearly 3 a.m., plus the walls are so thin we could hear our neighbor's TV. The bed was decent, but that hardly mattered when we were waking up every couple of hours. For this price, I expected far better.

We booked the Palmer expecting a charming stay, but the reality was a letdown. Breakfast was a sad affair of lukewarm scrambled eggs and stale pastries, with coffee that tasted burnt. The location is undeniably central, which is its only saving grace, but you pay for it with constant street noise--trams clattering until midnight and deliveries starting before dawn. Our room's decor felt frozen in the early 90s, with worn floral drapes and a carpet that smelled faintly of dust. The bed was lumpy, and the bathroom had a persistent mildew smell. While the staff were polite, they couldn't fix the fundamental issues. For the price, I expected so much more. I won't be returning.

I recently returned from a trip to Chicago with my husband and baby and another couple and their baby. While the room at the hotel was quite nice we had a very negative experience with the front desk staff including managers. When we arrived it took over an hour to check in. We had requested two rooms on the same floor, which the hotel staff had confirmed a number of times prior to our arrival. When we arrived they could not accommodate us and offered nothing to us to make up for it. Eventually after we persisted they gave us half off for our room for one of the three nights we were there. We also asked the concierge to make us a reservation for brunch at a restaurant that would accommodate 4 adults and two babies in strollers. When we got to the restaurant they had only a reservation for 4 adults and had to make special arrangements to fit the babies in. We also had asked the hotel to make us an appointment for a personal shopper at Bloomingdales in order for us to save time shopping. We filled out forms in advance to direct the shopper and when we arrived for our appointment Bloomingdales advised us that they had only received the applications moments before and had not pulled together our requests. After complaining again to the manager at the hotel of these disappointments she advised that she would send something up to our room to compensate. This 'something' never arrived. We will not be making a return visit to this hotel. While the housekeeping staff, location and room were quite nice the over all experience was very negative.

My husband, teenage son and myself stayed at this hotel last August. We were transferred there by tour operator who had sent us to a terrible hotel on the other side of Chicago. When I complained I asked for us to be transferred to the Sheraton which they arranged for us. I have stayed at many hotels in my life and this has been the best. The room (although I know it was not the largest) was beautiful and very clean with every amenity you needed. It also had superb views of the river and the lake. The entrance hall to the Sheraton is so imressive as is the leisure centre. In fact all areas are fantastic. The best thing about the hotel though was the staff! From the bellboy, to the receptionists, the dining staff to the concierge - each one was courteous and so very helpful. One of the conciergies spent fifteen minutes on the phone trying to locate a specific pair of trainers for my son! Above and beyond the call I would say! I cannot reccomend this hotel highly enough. The breakfast buffet cost about 10 dollars each but you could eat as much as you like and take as long as you like which we did!! It lasted us all day. If you have the choice of where to stay I think you will enjoy the Sheraton! We did!!

My wife and I just spent the Labor Day weekend in the city, choosing the Hard Rock Hotel as our pad. We've stayed at the HRH in Orlando twice and are blown away by the ambience there. It's not that way here. These may be all ticky tacky things, but they added up to us. First of all, the room. We upgraded our reservation thru the HRH website for a room with 'an Incredible view'. Well, our 9th floor view was of nothing more than the venting on top of the building next to us. That was all we could see. So there was no view. The room was muggy. We had the air turned down all the way and it never got below 74. We woke up sweaty both days. When we opened the window to get a breeze, the noise from the rooftop next to us was overbearing. The room was small and dark, but it didn't bother us that much. The bed may have been the mosr comfortable bed I ever slept in. And we even joked about stealing the pillows! We had the same issue with the honor bar as a previous poster, but they removed the charges no prob. Throughout the entire hotel, I counted a total of 3 pieces of music memorabilia. I thought it was a pretty cheesy attempt to renovate an old hotel, throw a Styx guitar on the wall, and slap a HRH emblem on the outside. The hotel itself was very clean and did not look like a renovation. The location is good, right on the south end of the mag mile, but there are 10-15 better hotels in a better location to shopping, quality eats, and Navy Pier. If you have a car, parking will cost you $38/day, which is prob normal for downtown. The hotel restaurant was a Chinese restaurant. The bar was small and trendy, and I guess the kicker to it all was that my wife tried to order a Pina Colada and they told us they didn't have a blender. WHAAT???? A HRH without a blender? Did they not know that Jimmy Buffet was in town???? Mind blowing! I would never, never, never go back here. Like I said, there are many better hotels in much better locations. I will stay at the HRH in Orlando or elsewhere again.
Sofitel looked elegant, but the room smelled damp, the air conditioning barely worked, and staff took ages to respond. For the price, it felt surprisingly neglected.

The view from our room at Hotel Amalfi was the highlight--waking up to that coastline each morning felt surreal. Staff went out of their way to book us a last-minute boat tour, and the lemon grove breakfast was unforgettable. Wouldn't change a thing.

My stay at the Fairmont was a very pleasant surprise. The room was bright, comfortably sized, and thoughtfully laid out, with a genuinely comfortable bed and plenty of space for my luggage. I slept extremely well; the mattress was supportive, the curtains kept the morning light out, and the hallway stayed quiet throughout the night. I occasionally heard a faint rumble from the street, but it was never disruptive. WiFi connected quickly and remained reliable enough for video calls and streaming, which made working from the room easy. The staff were warm without being overbearing, and check-in was efficient. I only stayed two nights and left wishing I had booked a longer visit, especially since the hotel's location made exploring the area so convenient. I would happily return.

The reviews we read were a bit mixed, but I thought it was excellent. I've stayed in The Splendido, Villa D'Este and others and it doesn't compare, but nor should it. It doesn't claim to be in that space. I expected it to be a notch off the Four Seasons and so it proved. A only a small notch too!. Lovely clean and bright room. Superb views, very quiet, comfy bed etc. Excellent service all round and nice staff. For the money and quality it stacked up very well indeed. Couldn't really fault it any way given it was half the cost of the Four Seasons but pretty close in terms of overall experience. We will go there again when in Chicago. Great location too.
Disappointing Hilton stay: the Wi-Fi kept dropping, staff were polite but unhelpful, and the dated decor made the expensive room feel far from worth the price.

The location is convenient, right off Michigan Avenue, but that's where the positives end for me. Check-in took way too long, and the front desk agent seemed annoyed when I asked about late checkout. The room itself felt tired and stuffy; the AC unit rattled all night, and the carpet had a musty smell that even the generic air freshener couldn't mask. I booked a king, but got a double with a view of a brick wall. Housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely, and when I called down, they said I hadn't put the door tag out--except they'd run out of tags at the front desk. The bar area was overpriced, and the bartender was more interested in chatting with a local than serving me. Honestly, for what this place charges, I expected so much more. I've had better stays at roadside motels. I won't be back.

Great stay at the Hard Rock -- big bathroom with an excellent shower, and breakfast had fresh options beyond the usual buffet fare. Location made getting around easy. Honestly, the weekend flew by and felt too short!

Hotel Palmer was a very pleasant surprise for a weekend stay. The lobby and rooms have a classic style, but it felt thoughtfully maintained rather than dated; the warm lighting, clean upholstery, and small local artwork gave it some character. Everyone we encountered, from the front desk to the breakfast attendant, was genuinely friendly and quick to help with directions and a late checkout request. Breakfast was simple but fresh, with good coffee, eggs, pastries, fruit, and enough seating even during the busy morning period. Our room faced the courtyard, so it was impressively quiet at night, with only occasional hallway noise in the morning. The bed was comfortable, the bathroom spotless, and the overall atmosphere relaxed. I would happily stay here again.

Hotel Amalfi was a pleasant surprise and made our weekend in the city feel easy from the moment we arrived. The staff were warm and efficient, and our room was spotless, with crisp linens, a clean bathroom, and no signs of wear that bothered us. We faced the street but were impressed by how quiet it was at night; we barely heard traffic and slept very well. The Wi-Fi worked reliably for both checking emails and streaming a movie, which was useful after a long day out. Breakfast was simple but fresh, with good coffee, pastries, fruit, and enough savory options to start the day. The location was especially convenient for walking to restaurants and attractions. I would happily stay here again.

I expected more from a Hyatt at this price point. The lobby looked polished, but the room felt dated and was not as clean as it should have been: there was dust on the desk, a stain on the chair, and hair in the bathroom. Breakfast was disappointing too, with lukewarm eggs, limited fruit, and coffee that tasted burnt; items were not replenished promptly. The Wi‐Fi barely worked in my room and repeatedly dropped during video calls, which was especially frustrating on a business trip. Staff were polite when I mentioned it, but no real solution was offered. Overall, the stay did not feel worth the rate, and I would choose another hotel next time.

Booked the Talbott for a three-night business trip based on its prime Mag Mile address, but left seriously underwhelmed. Yes, you can walk to the Apple store and the river in minutes, and the lobby has a certain faded grandeur. That's where the charm ends. My 'king' room was cramped, with a window facing a brick wall, and the bathroom felt like an afterthought--a cracked tile, a showerhead that dribbled sideways, and towels thin as tissue. Sleep was abysmal: the AC rattled all night, and I could hear every door slam and hallway conversation until 2 AM. For the $340 a night they charged, I expected far more. The staff were polite but the whole experience felt like a calculated squeeze for tourists, not a genuine luxury stay. I'd pick a chain next time--at least they'd be honest about what they are. Disappointing value.
For the price, Conrad was a letdown: our room overlooked a noisy service area, the AC rattled all night, and requests for extra towels took nearly an hour.

The Hotel Allegro was a pleasant surprise--quirky yet elegant, with a lively lobby and genuinely comfortable beds. Staff went out of their way to make theater recommendations, and the location made everything walkable. I'd happily book here again for a fun city escape.
Loved the Conrad's prime spot near the river--walkable to everything. Rooms felt fresh and modern, wifi was fast and reliable, and for the quality, the price felt fair. Would return.

We had high hopes for Hotel Amalfi given the price, but honestly it felt overpriced for what you get. The room was technically clean, the sheets looked fresh and the bathroom had no grime, but there was a persistent musty smell near the window that no amount of airing out seemed to fix. Noise was the real dealbreaker for us: the walls are paper thin, and we heard every conversation in the hallway plus what I swear was a vacuum at six each morning. The decor also feels stuck decades ago, with worn carpet, dated furniture, and lighting from another era. For what they charge per night, I expected something far more polished and restful.
