Staff were polite enough, but I probably wouldn't return or recommend it to friends.

I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone wanting accommodation in Chicago. Ideal position, lovely quiet rooms, good facilities, complimentary breakfast well received and the Manager's evening drinks reception excellent; we always tipped the staff who were serving our drinks. The in-house Amalfitini cocktail was very good. The staff were very friendly and helpful. If I ever return to Chicago I would certainly stay there again. Theres nothing bad I can say about this hotel.
My stay at Hotel Allegro felt a little too short, but I slept soundly in the spotless room. The bathroom was compact, though fresh, bright, and perfectly comfortable.

We stayed at the Swissotel over the Thanksgiving weekend and honestly couldn't have picked a better spot. Our room on a higher floor had an amazing view of the river and Lake Michigan, especially at night when everything lit up. The bed was genuinely comfortable, not one of those rock-hard hotel mattresses, and the blackout curtains actually did their job. What really made the trip was the front desk, who arranged a late checkout for us on the last day without any fuss. Location is unbeatable: you can walk to Millennium Park in about five minutes, ladies' number one tip is the Tomato Street restaurant downstairs for breakfast. Only small complaint is the elevators got a bit busy during peak hours. Would absolutely come back.
The Talbott's room was spotless, the Wi-Fi stayed reliable for work, and the Gold Coast location made walking to restaurants easy. For the comfort and convenience, it felt worth the price.
Homewood was a letdown; the room smelled musty, the hallway carpet was worn, and the front desk seemed annoyed whenever we asked for help.

Absolutely lovely stay. The ambassador personally remembered our anniversary and arranged champagne with a handwritten note. Every request was handled lightning fast, and the room's bay view was spectacular. We left feeling truly pampered.
At Hyatt, hallway noise kept me up, and my room faced a dull parking lot. The Wi-Fi repeatedly dropped, making the steep nightly rate feel especially hard to justify.

I had a really pleasant stay at Swissotel and would happily return. Check-in was quick, and the receptionist took the time to explain the breakfast hours and nearby transport options. My room was spotless, quiet at night, and had a comfortable bed with crisp linens. I especially appreciated the city view and the little touches like quality toiletries and plenty of charging points by the desk. Breakfast was busy but well organized, with fresh fruit, eggs, pastries, and good coffee. The gym was also better equipped than I expected for a hotel. A couple of elevators were slow during the morning rush, but that was a minor issue. Overall, the staff were warm, the facilities felt well maintained, and the location made getting around very easy.

I really wanted to like Hotel Monaco, especially given the great location near everything we wanted to see. The check-in process was painfully slow, and the front desk agent barely made eye contact, which set the tone. Our room, while clean, was shockingly small and the much-touted 'signature' decor felt tired and dated, not quirky. The bed was comfortable enough, but the air conditioning unit rattled all night, making sleep nearly impossible. We asked for a quiet room and were given one facing a noisy street. Housekeeping never replaced our coffee, and when we called, we were told it would be brought up but it never arrived. The bar was overpriced and understaffed. For the nightly rate, I expect a certain level of polish and service; this felt more like a budget chain that traded on its name. I wouldn't recommend it, which is a shame because the potential is clearly there, but the execution was a total letdown.

While the parking service was great - the front desk was terrible. We had a huge problem getting ice one night - we had none in our room so we went twice to get some - no one was there to help, called the front desk they promised to deliver some - none arrived so we called again - they said we had to come and get it and would not listen to what we had to say about what had already happened. ...read more

Honestly I expected more from the Omni. We paid a premium rate for a room that turned out to be noticeably tired--scuffed walls, a bathroom fan that rattled all night, and a TV remote with dead batteries that nobody seemed bothered to replace. Check-in took nearly half an hour because the front desk was understaffed on a Friday evening, and nobody apologized for it. Housekeeping skipped our room entirely one day, and when I called down about it, I got a shrug in the form of 'we'll get to it tomorrow.' The location is admittedly convenient, but for this price the walls were thin enough that I heard every hallway conversation at 6am. The gym was decent, sure, but that's not enough. Won't be back.

The Omni was a great base for our city break. The room was spotless and the bed incredibly comfy after long days exploring. Staff were friendly and quick with recommendations, and the location made everything walkable.

Often visit Chicago, but this was my first stay at this location. Was able to secure a good rate through travelzoo. Thought the room was clean and was nicely decorated. Was very disappointed in the service. Stayed on a Saturday night - waited 20 minutes for extra pillows - called for 15 minutes but found out the third shift crew came in 20 minutes late. Also received an incorrect folio under my door(another guests that was staying at this location). I called the front dest to inform them of the error - and they explained that this was made in error and would be corrected. I opened my credit card statement and found that I was charged for three different rooms - one on the date of my visit and two a week later. I called the hotel and guest services took the information and forwarded to their accounting department. Received a message to call the billing department, have called three times - but have not received another reply back.
The air conditioning barely worked and the room was stuffy all night. Staff seemed annoyed when I asked for extra towels. Overpriced for what you get, and the walls are paper thin. Won't return.

We stayed in a king suite at the Hotel Allegro over Memorial Day weekend. We paid $130/night, and it was definitely a bargain. The suite was huge - living room with a couch, two chairs, desk; large bathroom; bedroom; two closets. The room had recently been renovated, and was very clean. Comfortable bed, friendly staff, great location (near the train and bus), evening wine reception and morning coffee provided. While the Allegro isn't a five-star hotel, it is a great place for the money. (Note: a friend stayed in a non-suite room, and reported that it was very small. Upgrade if possible).

Checked in at 3:45 and my room wasn't ready until past 5, even though I'd requested early arrival. No apology, just a blank stare at the front desk. The room itself felt tired--carpet stained near the window, and the AC unit rattled all night like a washing machine. I asked for extra towels twice and never got them. The bar was understaffed, and my cocktail took 20 minutes. Location is fine, sure, but that's about all it has going for it. Breakfast buffet was lukewarm and overpriced at $28. The view was of a brick wall. Honestly, for what they charge, I expected a lot more. Won't be back.

We booked Homewood expecting a decent night's sleep before an early flight, but it was a real letdown. The hallway noise was constant well past midnight--doors slamming, people talking at full volume--and the walls were paper-thin. I could hear the TV from the room next door as if it were on my nightstand. The wifi was practically useless; it kept dropping and was too slow to even load a basic webpage, which I needed for work. Honestly, for what they charged, I felt ripped off. The room itself was shabby, with a stained carpet and a worn-out mattress that sagged in the middle. I tossed and turned all night and woke up more exhausted than when I arrived. Save your money and stay elsewhere.

The Palmer was a letdown despite its convenient location near restaurants and the train station. Getting around was easy, but I barely slept because hallway conversations, slamming doors, and traffic noise carried straight into the room until late at night. The room looked only superficially clean: there was dust on the desk, hair in the bathroom, and a sticky spot beside the bed. When I mentioned this at the front desk, the staff member seemed distracted and offered no real apology or solution. Check-in also took far longer than expected. For the rate, I expected a quieter, better-maintained room and more attentive service.

Breakfast at the Hard Rock hit all the right notes--hot pancakes, strong coffee, and zero rush. My bathroom was spotless with great water pressure, and being steps from the Strip made everything effortless. Honestly, one night wasn't nearly enough to soak it all in.

I had a very comfortable stay at the Hilton and would happily return. My room faced the river, and the evening view of the bridges and city lights was a lovely bonus, especially from the armchair by the window. The room itself was quiet, with a comfortable bed and plenty of space for luggage. The bathroom was spotless and practical, with good water pressure, a bright mirror, and plenty of counter space, although the shower fixtures showed a little wear. The staff made a strong impression: check-in was quick, and everyone I encountered was friendly without being overbearing. The decor felt fresh rather than trendy, with warm colors and updated furnishings, though the hallways were slightly less polished. Overall, it was a dependable, pleasant Hilton experience with thoughtful service.

I had a very pleasant stay at the Sheraton. Check-in was quick, and the front desk team made me feel welcome after a long day of travel. My room was clean, quiet, and surprisingly spacious, with a comfortable bed and a nice view of the city lights. I also appreciated the little things, like plenty of outlets near the desk and good water pressure in the shower. Breakfast had a solid variety, including fresh fruit, eggs, pastries, and decent coffee. The lobby was busy at times but still felt relaxed, and the staff were always helpful when I had questions. The location made it easy to get around, too. I would happily stay here again.

We booked the Talbott for a special weekend, and honestly, it fell flat. The lobby is charming in photos, but the reality is cramped and the staff at check-in seemed rushed, barely making eye contact. Our room was advertised as a 'deluxe king,' but it felt more like a shoebox with a view of a brick wall. The air conditioning was loud and rattled all night, which made sleeping tough. We tried the restaurant for dinner and waited forty-five minutes for overcooked pasta. The bar was better, but they got our order wrong twice. On the plus side, the location on Chestnut can't be beaten, and the bed was comfortable. For the price, though, I expected so much more. It's not terrible, but I'd skip the hype and stay elsewhere next time.
At Sofitel, the bathroom was spotless with a great shower, and the room stayed wonderfully quiet despite the central setting. Its convenient location made the price feel worthwhile.

Our stay at the Fairmont was much more disappointing than expected. The lobby looks impressive, but the room felt tired and under-maintained, with scuffed furniture, a stained carpet, and a bathroom fan that rattled all night. Check-in took nearly 30 minutes even though we arrived after the stated check-in time, and the receptionist seemed rushed and uninterested. We also had to call twice for extra towels, which arrived almost an hour later. Breakfast was crowded, with long waits for coffee and several empty buffet dishes. The bed was comfortable enough, but the room faced a busy street and the windows did little to block the traffic noise. For the price and reputation, the overall service and condition simply did not match expectations.

We stayed at The Palmer for a long weekend and honestly, it exceeded every expectation we had. The location is perfect, tucked away on a quiet street but just a five-minute walk to the harbor and all the best restaurants. Our room was spotless, with a incredibly comfortable bed and a balcony that caught the morning sun beautifully. The staff were the real highlight though--from the cheerful valet who remembered our names to the front desk team that helped us snag a last-minute reservation at a fully booked seafood place. The rooftop bar is a must for sunset drinks, and the cocktails are actually well-poured. Only tiny complaint was the shower pressure was a bit weak, but everything else was so polished it didn't matter. We've already started looking at dates to come back in the fall. Highly recommend this gem to anyone wanting a relaxed, upscale stay without the stuffy vibe.

I'd been looking forward to a special weekend at the Fairmont, but the reality fell far short of the pictures and the price tag. Our room on the eighth floor faced the parking garage and a slice of rooftops; we had to lean out the window to see any skyline, and even then, it was mostly cranes. The hallway noise was relentless--doors slamming and guests talking loudly until past midnight, and thin walls meant we heard every flush from next door. At over four hundred a night, it felt like a robbery for what was essentially a mediocre business hotel. The front desk staff were polite but disinterested, and when I asked about a quieter room, they shrugged and said the hotel was full. Housekeeping skipped our turn-down entirely, and the one call I made to request extra towels rang for ages before someone picked up. I truly wanted to love it, but I left feeling cheated and exhausted.
Disappointing stay at The Knickerbocker: the mattress was uncomfortable, the decor felt tired, and our room overlooked rooftops. The cramped, dated bathroom only added to the frustration.

We stayed at Hotel Amalfi for four nights in early June and honestly could not have asked for a better base for exploring the coast. Our room on the third floor had a small balcony with a view that made getting up early feel like less of a chore. Breakfast was included and the pastries alone were worth it, plus the woman working the coffee machine remembered how I liked my cappuccino by day two, which is the kind of thing that matters. Front desk staff booked us a boat trip to Capri last minute and gave honest advice about which restaurants were tourist traps. The walk up from the beach is steep, but that's Amalfi in general, not the hotel's fault. Would happily return.

I stayed at The Talbott for a long weekend and came away very happy with the experience. The location in the Gold Coast is ideal--quiet enough at night, but close to restaurants, shopping, and the lakefront. My room was comfortable and surprisingly roomy, with a very good bed, plenty of storage, and a bathroom that had clearly been updated. What stood out most was the staff. Everyone I dealt with, from the front desk to housekeeping, was friendly without being overbearing, and they were quick to help with directions and dinner suggestions. The lobby has a relaxed, intimate feel rather than a busy business-hotel atmosphere. Wi-Fi worked well, and I appreciated the in-room coffee each morning. It is not the cheapest option in Chicago, but the service and location made it feel worthwhile.

me (taking a cue from david dancer): 'sup? front desk person: yes? me: so, do I have to wait in the elevator line to get up to my room? front desk person: what room are you in? me: **** front desk person: oh. ...i'm afraid so. OR, you can take the other elevators and take the fire stairs up to the 10th floor. me: oh? wtf! so, we're staying at this hotel, and there is a bar on the 29th floor, but we have to wait 15 minutes in line to get to our fucking hotel room? get bent! we're paying to stay here, not just drinking in your bar!
Hotel Monaco's central location made exploring easy, and our room overlooked a lovely city skyline. Breakfast was fresh and varied, while the staff were consistently warm, attentive, and helpful.

I booked the Hilton expecting the usual standard of comfort, but honestly, it fell flat. The room was fine at first glance, but then I noticed the carpet had a few suspicious stains and the bathroom door didn't close properly, which made for zero privacy. Housekeeping never came by until we called twice, and even then, they only left fresh towels without making the bed properly. The air conditioning unit rattled all night, and the 'city view' I paid extra for was mostly a brick wall and a noisy ventilation shaft. Breakfast was chaotic -- the omelet station ran out of eggs for twenty minutes and the coffee was lukewarm. Front desk staff were polite but seemed overwhelmed, and the checkout line snaked halfway through the lobby. For the price, I'd expect better. Not the worst stay ever, but I won't be rushing back to this particular property.

Hotel Monaco is in a very convenient spot, with shops, restaurants, and the metro only a short walk away, which was the best part of our stay. Unfortunately, the room did not live up to the price. Our window faced a narrow service alley, so the view was basically bins, brick walls, and delivery vans. It was also far noisier than expected, with street traffic early in the morning and doors banging in the hallway late at night. Breakfast looked better than it tasted: lukewarm eggs, stale pastries, and slow coffee refills. Staff were polite but didn't seem able to address the noise complaint. I expected much more comfort for the rate.
Breakfast was sparse and lukewarm, and street noise kept me awake most of the night. The dated decor felt tired, while the room's dusty surfaces and stained carpet made it worse.

Surprisingly quiet for Times Square, and our corner room had skyline views that justified the splurge. Bathroom was sleek marble with a great rain shower--endered every penny for a special occasion stay.

I have stayed in hotels all over the world, and this is probably the worst service that I've ever experienced. The staff was unaccomodating and the hotel did not provide the services that it claimed it would. I decided to try the Monaco because it seemed interesting, was close to the theater, and had what seemed to be a good rate. What a huge mistake. The front desk staff was condescending and not even remotely helpful. The room was not clean, the gold fish we had requested came many hours after we told them we would be arriving, they never bothered to come turn down the beds, and the late check-out 'priviledges' which were guarenteed when I booked the room suddenly became 'upon request' - boy the extra 30 minutes they gave me sure were helpful. Dont' waste your time or your money here. At best, it's nothing special. Personally, I like the Fairmont in Chicago, but anyplace woudl be better than the Monaco.

I'm honestly a little reluctant to leave this review because I want to keep this place a secret. We were on the fourth floor facing the courtyard, and I was braced for hallway noise, but it was almost eerily quiet -- I heard nothing after 10 PM. The blackout curtains did their job, and the bed was firm without being hard; I slept a solid eight hours, which never happens in hotels. The room itself was spotless, right down to the baseboards, and the housekeeper had even folded the toilet paper edge into a neat point. As for the view, it was a pleasant patch of green with a fountain, nothing dramatic, but perfect for morning coffee while watching families wander out to the pool. I'll definitely rebook on my next trip.

We booked the James specifically for a weekend getaway, drawn in by the sleek photos. The reality was a letdown from the moment we hit the lobby--the 'signature scent' was cloying, and the check-in clerk seemed annoyed by our simple request for a quiet floor. The room itself was cramped, with a view of a brick wall and a dusty air conditioning unit. The bed was hard as a rock, and the pillows offered zero support, leaving me with a stiff neck each morning. We tried the rooftop bar, but the cocktails were watered down and cost a fortune for the view we got. Honestly, for these prices, you'd expect at least working Wi-Fi, but ours dropped constantly. The only bright spot was the location, which made it easy to escape the hotel for decent food and drinks. I've stayed in cheaper chain hotels with more character and better service. This was a disappointing, feel-good-but-forgotten experience. I won't be back.

My stay at the Hyatt was much more frustrating than expected. The lobby looked polished, but check-in took nearly half an hour because only one desk was staffed, and the employee seemed overwhelmed. The room was large enough, though it had a tired feel: scuffed furniture, a stained carpet near the window, and fingerprints all over the bathroom mirror. The air conditioner rattled loudly through the night and never really cooled the room, so sleeping was difficult. I also had to call twice before extra towels arrived. Breakfast was expensive for what was offered, with cold eggs and a long wait for coffee. The location was convenient, but that alone did not justify the price. For a Hyatt, the lack of attention to basic details was disappointing, and I would choose another hotel next time.

Ok, I just feel if you're paying well over $200 for a room you should get something to show for it. The location was on Michigan Ave but if I pay just a little more I could have had way better (Peninsula, Park Hyatt, shoot the Omni was 10x better). We ordered a deluxe executive suite, and it was so below sub par. The room was very small (so small the ice bucket was in the closet), the bathroom was just as small, just well lit (a plus). Wallpaper was peeling, outlets barely covered, no view. The only thing appealing was the bed, and that may have been because I was so tired. And we were really excited because this is the Palmer House. The Palmer House does have nice restaurants: the Lockwood (quiet, distinguished) and the Potter's Lounge (grown/sexy)

I have traveled to Chicago many times for business, and so I have expectations of hotels based on reasonable comparisons. There was nothing dramatically wrong the Sheraton, but it was simply overpriced for the quality of the hotel. It almost looked as if an accountant walk through the hotel looking for places to cut costs. The carpets were old, there was only one bar of soap in the bathroom, towels and linens were older than I expected, the rooms were in need of some redecorating, etc. during the week I was paying $349 per night for a room, and it simply was not near the quality I expected for that price. One positive to notice that the fitness room was quite good. Plenty of aerobic machines with TVs, weights, etc. location is also quite good (perhaps the reason for the high price) with close walks to Michigan Avenue and the river. In summary, I think you can find a much nicer hotel in a much better price in downtown Chicago.

I just returned from a 2 night stay at the hotel. I had requested a high floor, quiet room. Neither request was honored. The windows are not well insulated, because the traffic, car horns and sirens continued all night long. On the first night two drunk parties woke us up in the hallway. The safe in our room did not work. Someone had locked it before our arrival. One of the pictures under the tv had been removed, leaving a screw sticking out of the wall. The lights are so dim, that is next to impossible to read. A small alcove with a stained bench had a 'reading light' that was about 50 watts. Our room key cards didn't work, so we returned to the lobby where they recoded them. Upon returning to our room, they didn't work again and we stood there trying over and over again until finally we succeeded with no help from the staff. The bathroom is small and has no fan, so the steam covers the mirrors, and unless you leave the bathroom door open, it does not clear. On Friday night one small cookie was left in our room. What about a second guest. Are we supposed to split a 2 inch diameter cookie???!!!! On Sunday the phone rang with a 7 am wakeup call. We had not requested to be woken up!!!! The concierge did not know the way to get to O'Hare by train, and gave us a longer route than was necessary. I have stayed in much better hotels in Chicago...quieter and more spacious, more elegant and worth the money. This is definitely not worth $400 a month. (By the way, I live in Washington, DC and am used to city noise. This was unacceptable!)

I expected much more from Hard Rock for the price. Check-in was slow, and the room felt tired rather than stylish, with scuffed furniture and noise from the hallway late at night. The bathroom was especially disappointing: the shower pressure was weak, the grout looked stained, and there was barely any counter space for toiletries. Our view overlooked a parking area and construction fencing, not the cityscape shown online. Breakfast was crowded and underwhelming, with lukewarm eggs, limited fruit, and staff struggling to refill coffee. The location was convenient, but the overall stay did not feel remotely worth the premium rate.

The room smelled like stale smoke and the 'rock star' service was a myth--waited 40 minutes at the front desk while staff gossiped. Pool was packed with non-guests, and the bar overcharged for flat drinks. Definitely not worth the hype for this price.

The Hard Rock Hotel was a natural choice for me to book a block of rooms for several colleagues traveling into Chicago.. The location is fantastic - a short walk to top notch city points of interest such as Lake Michigan, Millennium Park, and Art Museum - and several fantastic restaurants nearby to choose from. My co-works LOVED the exterior of the building, views from the rooms, the art on the walls, and crisp, clean & hip feeling of the hotel, but not 'too over the top' for 'business'. By far a better experience than your usual 'chain' hotel where they shuffle you in and out and boring rooms. Here you feel special...for the same price. The lobby and bar have fun & cozy areas to just hang out and watch the people pass on Michigan Ave (or catch a real rock star in the lobby!)

Thirty years ago, we had a tiny 'room' and indifferent service. This time, the service was superb and friendly throughout, with special commendation for the waiters and waitresses at the coffee shop, the door and bell persons, and the hilton honors person at the front desk. They even lowered our price (to moderately high) when we inquired a few days before our stay. When we want to stay south of the river downtown, we will be back

I expected much better from a Hilton. Check-in took nearly 30 minutes because only one person was at the desk, and nobody acknowledged the growing line. The room looked tired, with scuffed furniture, a stained carpet near the window, and an air conditioner that rattled loudly all night. The bathroom was clean enough, but the shower pressure was weak and the hot water kept fluctuating. I also called twice for extra towels and they never arrived. Breakfast was overpriced for cold eggs and limited options, and several tables were left uncleared. The location was convenient, but that was the only real positive. For the rate charged, this stay felt neglected and far below the standard I associate with the brand.

Lovely stay at the Omni -- our corner room had sweeping views of the mountains, and the decor felt fresh and updated. Every staff member we encountered was warm and attentive. Walking distance to everything made it even better.
Hotel Monaco was a lovely base for our weekend, with a cheerful front desk, comfortable bed, and surprisingly quiet room. The downtown location made getting around easy, too.

Location, location, location. What a great find! Excellent, well-run, small boutique-type hotel on a tree-lined street near all the action without being in the oppressive crunch of it. Rooms are good-sized and clean; good bed and shower with tub. The air conditioner, as mentioned in other reviews, is noisy, but it's a minor complaint. The staff is simply wonderful and attentive from housecleaning to concierge. The on site restaurant is great. The red-line El is about 3-4 blocks away which makes getting around the city a breeze. You are footsteps away from Rush Street and North Michigan Avenue and Lake Michigan. I would not have a moment's hesitation booking at this hotel again in the future; in fact, I wouldn't book anywhere else.

I had a very comfortable stay at the InterContinental and was impressed by how smoothly everything went from check-in onward. My room was spotless, with fresh linens, a well-maintained bathroom, and no dust or stray marks anywhere. I especially enjoyed the view over the city; watching the lights come on in the evening was a nice bonus after a busy day. The bed was comfortable, and the room stayed quiet despite the central location. Wi-Fi connected quickly and worked reliably for video calls, streaming, and general browsing, which made the stay easy for both work and relaxation. My only complaint is that I booked just two nights--it felt too short to enjoy the hotel and explore more of the area. I would gladly return for a longer visit.

The walls here are paper-thin. I could hear the couple next door arguing until 2 AM, and the elevator dings all night long, so 'sleep' was a distant memory. The advertised free Wi-Fi was a joke--it disconnected every few minutes, making it impossible to even load a map for dinner plans. The bathroom was the real low point: a cramped, moldy-smelling closet where the showerhead dribbled lukewarm water and the exhaust fan sounded like a dying lawnmower. As for the view, our window faced a brick wall and a row of noisy AC units. I paid extra for a 'superior' room, and this is what I got. The only positive was the location near the beach, but honestly, that's not enough to salvage a stay this disappointing. I expected so much more from an Amalfi hotel. Save your money.

Complete disappointment. Problems: 1. The alarm clock/stereo thing was broken in my room. It was constantly emitting low, changing hissing noises. Sooo annoying. And there was no off switch on the damn thing. I had to move the bed to unplug it (the outlet was wayyy back, buried behind the big bed). I kept hearing it, and didn't realize what it was, until it had kept me awake for a few hours. 2. The shower was ONLY incredibly hot. Turn it all the way cold...very hot. Turn it to hot, and you get boiling hot. Grrrrreat. So how do I get water that won't scald me? This is very inconvenient early in the morning when you need a shower and are in a hurry, and have to dance into and out of painfully hot water. Good job Omni! 3. Hallway carpets are disgusting and old. Walking around, you'd think you're in a motel 6. And my floor had been flooded or something, and they had box fans running in the hallway, 24/7, to try to dry it out. Talk about an overpriced dump.

We stayed at the Sheraton by Navy Pier the first weekend of November and were very pleased with the accommodations and the service. We were upgraded to club level rooms and stayed in 3114 and 3115 adjoining. The view from both rooms was spectacular (as you can tell from the picture attached). They also left a plate of cookies and treats in the kids room upon check-in which made us all feel very special. The hotel is central to both Navy Pier and Michigan Ave. so we walked, trolleyed, and cabbed all around the area. We ate the breakfast buffet both mornings and thought it was pretty good. The eggs were a little runny, but they happily made a different batch for us at the omelet station. Our six year old ate free and our two eleven year olds were $14 (instead of the adult $20) The rooms were clean, the concierge & reception staff were both friendly and helpful...we will definitely visit this Sheraton again when we're in Chicago next time.

I'll be honest--I booked Hotel Monaco mostly for the location, but the stay itself ended up being the highlight of my trip. The room was compact but smartly laid out, with a ridiculously comfortable bed and a window seat I actually used for morning coffee. The staff genuinely seemed to enjoy their jobs, which made check-in and questions feel easy, not transactional. Their restaurant recommendation was spot-on, too. Pet-friendly is a big plus for me, and my dog got more attention than I did. The gym is small but fine for a quick workout. If you're expecting sprawling luxury, this isn't that, but everything was clean, quiet, and thoughtfully done. I'd absolutely stay here again.
At Hard Rock, the room looked tired and wasn't properly clean, while the cramped bathroom had grime around the fixtures. Our stay felt too long, thanks to loud hallway noise all night.

My stay at Homewood was much more disappointing than expected. The location was convenient, but the room felt tired and poorly maintained, with scuffed walls, stained carpet, and a bathroom fan that rattled loudly whenever it was switched on. The bed was uncomfortable, and the heating system kept cycling through the night, so I barely slept. Housekeeping also missed replacing the towels on the second day, and when I called the front desk, the response was slow and not particularly helpful. Breakfast was included, but the selection was limited and several items were lukewarm. I understand that small issues happen, but there were too many of them during a short stay. For the price, Homewood needs better upkeep and more attentive service.

We needed an extra night in Chicago after a gratus stay at The Penninsula and won a SkyAuction bid for The James @ $203. This is one of the nicest hotels that I've ever stayed in. Bathroom aside, we felt it equalled The Penninsula in comfort and level of service. I echo all of the superlatives previously written and would love to stay here anytime I'm in town.

We have stayed here several times and have always found it to be clean with comfortable beds. We were given a choice of breakfast or free cocktails which we thought was a nice touch. Our room was small but adequate. Location was great, close to the L trains and also close to the train station as we always 'walk' from Union Station.
Booked the Intercontinental expecting luxury, but the room felt tired, the AC rattled all night, and housekeeping ignored our do-not-disturb sign. Overpriced and underwhelming for the brand name.

I wrote an email to the sales & reservation team a week ago.........i'm still waiting for a response. All I wanted to do was book a suite for 2 nights but they failed to even reply with an offer. We have now booked another hotel who can be bothered to answer emails. Shame you missed out, coz we tip like rockerfellers!!

Great stay at the Sheraton -- the bed was incredibly comfortable and the front desk staff went out of their way to arrange a late checkout for us. Location was walkable to everything. Would happily return.

I stayed at the Hotel Allegro for three nights over a long weekend and came away really impressed. The room was spotless when I checked in, and housekeeping kept it that way throughout my stay, even restocking the coffee pods without being asked. I'm a light sleeper, but the bed was genuinely comfortable and the street noise was barely noticeable, so I got solid rest every night. The decor has that classic 1920s theater-district character with rich colors and vintage touches, but it felt freshly updated rather than dated, which I appreciated. Wifi was fast and reliable, no dropped connections even while streaming in the evenings. The front desk team was warm and quick with dinner recommendations. Would absolutely book here again next time I'm in Chicago.

Our stay at the InterContinental was genuinely fantastic from start to finish. The room was spotless, with a ridiculously comfortable bed and blackout curtains that made sleeping in way too easy. I loved the little touches, like the Nespresso machine and the fact that the bathroom had both a rain shower and a tub. The staff were the real highlight though--everyone from the doorman to the front desk remembered our names and went out of their way to help with dinner reservations and local tips. The location was perfect for walking to everything we wanted to see, and the lobby bar had a great vibe for a nightcap. We even used the pool, which was surprisingly quiet. For the price, it's hard to beat this level of service and polish. Already planning our return.

Stayed at the Swissotel for a long weekend and honestly couldn't have asked for a smoother visit. The room on the 28th floor had those floor-to-ceiling windows that made the whole city feel like part of the decor--watching the lights come on over the lake at dusk was a highlight every single night. Bed was firm but comfortable, and the blackout curtains actually did their job. Staff were consistently warm, especially the doormen who remembered our names by day two and always had a tip for where to grab a quick bite or skip a line. The indoor pool was a nice escape after long walking days, and the breakfast buffet had enough variety that even our picky eater found something new to enjoy each morning. Location near the river made it easy to get anywhere on foot or via the L. Could've used a bit more drawer space in the room, but that's a minor nit. Would happily book again.
Sheraton made our weekend easy: the room was spotless, beds were wonderfully comfortable, and the front desk team handled a late check-in with genuine warmth.

My stay at the Hyatt was disappointing, especially considering the price. The room looked polished in the photos but felt tired in person, with worn carpet, a small bathroom, and housekeeping that missed replacing the coffee and towels one day. Breakfast was another letdown: the buffet had limited choices, lukewarm eggs, and crowded seating, so it did not feel worth the extra charge. The location was convenient for public transportation and several restaurants, which was the main positive, although the surrounding area became rather quiet after dark. Unfortunately, the hotel itself was not peaceful. Doors slammed late into the night, voices carried clearly from the hallway, and traffic noise came through the window. Staff were courteous when approached, but the overall experience did not match the rates, and I would choose a different hotel next time.
The staff were warm and quick to help, while the Palmer's classic decor felt charming rather than dated. My room overlooked the city, and the clean bathroom had plenty of space.
We had a comfortable stay at the Omni, with a quiet, spotless room and genuinely friendly service. Its central location made it easy to walk to shops, restaurants, and nearby attractions.

For a supposed 4-star hotel, I was not very impressed at akk. The lobby was nice and modern-looking, but there were no bellhops outside to help with bags or open the doors (we didn't arrive that late at night). Additionally, when we walked into the hotel late one night, there was trash and flowers strewn on the lobby floor and, it seemed that there were always water bottles and glasses near the seating area as you walked in. Where was the staff to clean up? That's not a very welcoming sight. The rooms were nice and clean and provided a great view, but the actual location was farther than I would have preferred from Michigan Avenue, andi it was also a little too far south. Area recommendations Rush Street was a lot of fun at night!

We booked the Talbott expecting old-world charm, but the reality felt more like neglect. Our room's carpet had a suspicious sticky patch near the minibar, and the bathroom sink drained so slowly that I ended up brushing my teeth in the shower. The view from our fourth-floor window was a brick wall and a noisy ventilation shaft--hardly the romantic cityscape in the brochure. Staff were polite but indifferent; when I asked for extra towels, the front desk clerk sighed and said housekeeping was 'busy,' then handed me a damp one from a cart. The bed linens were crisp, I'll give them that, but the baseboards were dusty and the window sill had a dead fly. For $340 a night, I expect at least a working hairdryer--mine sparked and cut out. This place trades on its history, but the upkeep is tragic. I won't be returning.

I was expecting a much smoother stay at the James, especially given the rates, but several things were disappointing. Check-in took nearly half an hour even though there were only two people ahead of me, and the front desk seemed more interested in chatting than helping. Our room looked stylish in the photos, but in person it felt worn, with scuffed furniture, a stained armchair, and a bathroom fan that rattled all night. The mattress was also surprisingly uncomfortable, and street noise came through the windows until well after midnight. Housekeeping skipped our room on the second day, then left fresh towels in a heap outside the door. The location is convenient, but it wasn't enough to justify the price. I wouldn't choose this hotel again.

My stay at Hotel Talbott was a pleasant surprise from start to finish. The front desk team greeted me with genuine warmth, even remembering my name when I returned from dinner. My room was spotless--the kind of clean that makes you want to kick off your shoes immediately. Despite being on Dearborn, I heard almost nothing from the street; the windows did wonders, and the hallway noise was minimal, which made for a truly restful night. The location is unbeatable for exploring the Loop or hopping on the riverwalk, and the Mag Mile is just a pleasant stroll away. The bathroom had great water pressure, and the bed was firm but comfortable. It's not a flashy property, but it's efficient, charming, and well-run. I'd gladly book here again for a business trip or a weekend away.

My wife and I stayed two nights at the Talbott at the end of February. This little hotel was the perfect place for us. The lobby is very small but also cozy, and with both fireplaces going it was a welcoming atmosphere coming in from the cold. The staff was very friendly and efficient. The room was pretty spacious, and the king bed was extremely comfortable. We had a seventh floor room facing delaware st, so there was really no view. The bathroom was a good size, including two sinks and a spacious tub/shower. There was also free wireless internet...a big plus for us. Perhaps the best thing about the Talbott is the location. We were only a few steps from State, Rush, and North Michigan. Tons of shopping, bars, and good food are easily within walking distance. This makes the Talbott a great place for tourists who want to walk around and take everything in. We highly recommend the Talbott, and will gladly stay again on return trips.

We had a fantastic long weekend at Hotel James. The location is perfect for exploring the city, but the real highlight was the incredible staff. Everyone from the front desk to the housekeeping team was genuinely friendly and went above and beyond. Our room was a quiet retreat from the busy streets, featuring a wonderfully comfortable bed and a large, bright bathroom. The rainfall shower was a particular luxury. I also appreciated the thoughtful touches, like the complimentary coffee in the lobby each morning that was actually good. The on-site restaurant served a delicious dinner, though it is a bit on the pricey side. We left feeling rested and thoroughly impressed. We are already planning our next visit and wouldn't consider staying anywhere else. Highly recommended for a chic and comfortable base.

Stayed here for a conference and was genuinely impressed. The room was spotless and quiet, the bed super comfy, and the breakfast spread had everything. Staff actually remembered my name at checkout--nice touch that made the whole stay feel personal.

Stayed at Hotel Monaco for a weekend getaway and was genuinely impressed. The room was stylish and quiet, and the staff's little touches--like the evening wine hour--made it feel special. Great spot for exploring the city without the usual tourist chaos.
Loved my stay here -- the rooms are spacious and beautifully done, and the harbor views from the lounge are stunning. Staff was genuinely helpful without being pushy. Would absolutely come back.

The decor felt refreshingly modern, not dated, and the staff were genuinely warm from check-in to checkout. My only wish was that the Wi-Fi held steady in my room, though the stay itself was far too short--I could have lingered for days.

We were greeted by staff with excellent customer service skills. Our room was such a pleasant surprise, from the flat screen TV, the full size shower with rain showerhead & hand held shower wand, the wall attached toilet with flushing options (on the wall), the comfortable bed, the lovely lighting options, etc.. The size of the room was snug, and very comfortable, as would be, in a historic hotel. It was also quiet, and I know that the hotel was sold out. My sister was in the room next door. We did not hear her TV. We also loved walking less than a block, to the shopping and restaurants on North Michigan Avenue.
Skip the Fairmont if you can. Breakfast was lukewarm and overpriced, our room heard every hallway conversation, the bathroom had mildew in the grout, and the 'city view' was mostly a brick wall.

The Omni exceeded expectations--check-in was seamless, the room spotless with a gorgeous view, and every staff member genuinely warm. Breakfast had great options too. I'd happily book again on my next trip downtown.
Disappointing stay at this Hilton -- the room smelled musty, the AC barely worked, and front desk staff were indifferent when I complained. For the price, I expected far better. Won't be returning.

I wanted to like Hotel Allegro because the location was convenient, but the stay was frustrating from check-in onward. Our room wasn't ready at the promised time, and nobody at the desk seemed especially concerned. Once we got in, it looked worn: stained carpet, scuffed furniture, and a bathroom fan that rattled all night. The air conditioning barely worked, so the room felt stuffy despite adjusting the thermostat several times. We also heard hallway noise and doors slamming well past midnight. Breakfast was underwhelming, with lukewarm coffee and very limited options by 8:30. For the price, I expected better upkeep and more attentive service. I wouldn't choose this hotel again unless there were no other options nearby.

Had such high hopes for the Hard Rock, given the brand. What a letdown. Check-in took forever, and the front desk guy barely looked up from his screen, acting like he was doing me a favor. The room itself was tired--carpet stained, a musty smell that the citrus air freshener only made worse, and the 'rock star' view was a brick wall and an AC unit. Paid for a 'premium' room that felt like a budget motel with better guitars on the wall. Housekeeping skipped our room entirely on the second day, so I had to call twice to get towels. The hallways were absurdly noisy all night; we heard every door slam and rowdy group stomping back at 3 a.m. The pool was packed and lukewarm, with a line for chairs. Honestly, for these prices, you're paying for the logo. Location is decent, but that's the only saving grace. Won't be back.

Disappointed with my stay: paper-thin walls meant constant hallway noise, the wifi kept dropping, and I barely slept. The room was ostensibly clean, but stains on the carpet said otherwise. Not worth the price.

I booked a room at the Hyatt through Priceline and was able to get a rate of $45/night! Can't go wrong with that! The rooms are nice, spacious, clean and contain all the amenties a traveler would need. I have to say that I have fallen in love with the Hyatt chain due to their customer service. I have stayed at a few of their hotels in different cities and the staff has always been extremely friendly, which you don't often see at other hotels. I used the self-check in machine, and the customer service person checked in on me to make sure everything was going smoothly. Then, when she saw that my room was not on a high level, she offered to have it changed for me so that I could have a better view. I would highly recommend this hotel!

My stay at Hotel Talbott was much more disappointing than expected. The location is convenient, but the overall experience did not match the price. Check-in took nearly 25 minutes even though the lobby was quiet, and the front desk agent seemed distracted and barely explained anything. The room looked tired, with scuffed furniture, a stained carpet near the window, and a bathroom fan that rattled loudly whenever it was turned on. Housekeeping also missed replacing the coffee supplies after the first night. I mentioned the issues, but the response was a polite apology without any real follow-up. The bed was comfortable enough, and the neighborhood is pleasant, but those positives could not make up for the poor maintenance and lack of attention. I would not choose this hotel again.

We stayed at the swissotel for our 25th anniversary. We got a corner room with both a lake and city view. The room was very clean and spacious. The staff was extremely friendly and helpful. We asked for late checkout, and was told no problem. If you bring your car, park in millinum parking it is just 2 blocks away. The cost there is $14.00 compared to the swissotel which is $41.00.

We stayed at the Palmer for a long weekend and honestly, it exceeded every expectation we had. The location is perfect for exploring the city, but what truly set it apart was the staff--from the doorman who remembered our names to the front desk team who helped us snag a last-minute dinner reservation. Our room faced the garden, which was a quiet oasis after busy days of sightseeing. The bed was wonderfully firm, and the blackout curtains were a lifesaver. We had breakfast included, and the spread was fantastic, with fresh pastries and made-to-order eggs. The only tiny hiccup was a slow drain in the shower, but maintenance fixed it within the hour of us mentioning it. We left feeling genuinely rested and well-cared for. It's rare to find a hotel that balances classic elegance with such modern comfort. We'll definitely be back.

The breakfast buffet was a chaotic free-for-all with empty chafing dishes, and housekeeping never once replenished our towels despite the 'do not disturb' sign we never hung. Save your money for somewhere that actually cares about guests.

I had a really enjoyable stay at The Knickerbocker. The location in Times Square is lively, but the room itself was surprisingly quiet, comfortable, and beautifully designed, with a very good bed and a spacious bathroom. Everything felt polished without being overly formal. The staff were consistently friendly, especially at check-in and when I needed help arranging a car, and requests were handled quickly. I also loved the rooftop bar--the views over Midtown and the Empire State Building were fantastic, particularly around sunset. Breakfast was convenient and well prepared, though the restaurant can get busy. My only minor complaint is that the room lighting was a little dim in the evening. Otherwise, it was an easy, comfortable base for exploring Manhattan, and I would happily stay here again.

The floor-to-ceiling windows offered a stunning city panorama, and the Wi-Fi was impressively fast for uploading photos. Breakfast's fresh pastries were a highlight, while the lobby's modern art and sleek furniture felt anything but dated.

Service at Swissotel felt impersonal from start to finish. Waited 25 minutes at check-in despite a half-empty lobby, and the room had a lingering smoke smell that housekeeping couldn't fix. Shower pressure was weak, plus the AC rattled all night.

Our non-smoking room smelled very badly of stale cigarette smoke. We were not allowed to change rooms. Also, the concierge staff was unprofessional, telling long winded personal stories to uninterested guests while long lines formed. The location was great. Hotel is dated, but would still be a nice place to stay if it weren't for customer service issues.

Booked through Hotwire and consequently was placed in a room where we barely had room to walk around our luggage. The 'view' was of the 'inner courtyard' of nothing but walls of windows of the other rooms. You were unable to determine what the weather was outside except that it was either day or night. They no longer have in-room coffee appliances. You either have to go down to their ostentatious dining room, or go around the corner to Starbucks or McDonald's. Internet access is not free ($12.95/24 hours), the 'Gift Shop' is a joke (tucked away in the corner of the coat check room, Concierge services have limited hours, and the business center is open only during 'business hours' which made it difficult to get work done after 'business hours.' I would not stay there ever again, nor do I recommend it to anyone. I have had better stays at any Holiday Inn Express!

Affinia was a pleasant surprise--great location for exploring the city, and the staff genuinely cared about making sure we had everything we needed. Room was comfy and quiet, and the little kitchenette came in handy for quick breakfasts before heading out each day.

I stayed at Palmer House for one night in early January this year. During the check in, the front desk lady asked me to show my confirmation letter of my reservation. I did not bring the confirmation with me because I had not been asked to present it in other places during check in.So she asked to print out one copy in their business center and bring the confirmation to the bell station to get the room key. I did what she told me and went to the bell station. However, people at the bell station was totally confused and none of them have the key. A bellman was nice enough to help me go ask their staff at the front desk. I finally got checked in after waiting at the lobby for about 15 minutes. As other people pointed out before, the room I got was small and old with a twin bed, and I could hear people next door using the bathroom. This was not a pleasant experience, even though I paid over 100 dollars to the hotel.

My husband and I were there for a conference and had booked the room thru their website, when called to confirm had us down for only 1 night instead of 4, easily changed. First morning cold,cold shower, didn't complain,next day fine. Phone did not work, called every day to complain, and every day said it would be fixed when got back to room, never was. No dial tone, unable to call restaurant, or call for car or call for room service. Finally, on last night someone came to our room while we were there and did fix it. The hotel is beautiful, rooms great and everyone was so nice, even when I was complaining they were nice. Great gym area also, and love the restaurant. BUT, for the money I could easily find another hotel just as nice with a working phone.

Stayed here for a long weekend celebrating our anniversary, and honestly, it exceeded expectations. The location is unbeatable - we walked to the waterfront every evening and it was so easy to hop on the T for exploring. The room itself was spotless and quiet, which we really appreciated after some noisy hotel experiences elsewhere. The bed was ridiculously comfortable, and the blackout curtains were a lifesaver for sleeping in. We had drinks at the rooftop bar one night, and the views over the city were stunning, though the cocktails were a bit pricey. The staff genuinely stood out though - from the warm welcome at check-in to the front desk helping us print last-minute concert tickets. Breakfast buffet was solid with made-to-order omelets. Only tiny gripe: the valet was a little slow on Sunday morning, but they were friendly about it. Would absolutely book again for a city stay.

I was really looking forward to staying here, but the experience left a sour taste. The Wi-Fi was practically useless in my room, dropping constantly and making it impossible to join a video call for work. I had to sit in the lobby, which was far from ideal. The staff, while polite at check-in, seemed overwhelmed and distant whenever I asked for anything, like extra towels or a dinner recommendation--I felt like a bother. Breakfast was a letdown; the scrambled eggs were rubbery and the coffee tasted burnt, sitting in lukewarm chafing dishes. As for the decor, the whole place has a faded 90s vibe with worn carpets and dated floral patterns in the hallways. It's clean, sure, but it feels neglected and tired. For the price we paid, I expected so much more. I won't be back.

I selected the Talbott after 3 hrs comparing hotels online. We have had wonderful experiences with boutiques (Monaco, Allegro) and assumed this would be comparable. Good points: the lobby is beautiful, and one staff member took roses I bought for my wife and arranged them nicely. The many problems: When my wife called with a question on our arrival day, the agent could find no reservation -- 15 mins later she was transferred to another person who found the record instantly. When we arrived, the lobby was stuffed with students; nobody tried to manage the group, several of whom pushed ahead to the check-in desk. We left our bags and went out for 2 hrs so we could check in with less hassle. We finally were checked in, after waiting 15 mins while the confused desk clerk searched for rooms. When we got there, our room had not been made up from the last guest. When we complained, we were given an 'upgrade' to a room that was old and uninspired. Chairs are scuffed, closet shelves are bowed, the air conditioner is noisy, and a wall lamp is loose. The view is of a construction site. Movies-on-demand are dated. We expect this from a budget hotel, not one positioning itself as elegant and upscale. When we returned after an evening out, the card reader to open the main doors did not work. One staff member admonished us (really) for not using the reader, when in fact we had tried. This was embarrassing, as others were standing in the lobby. I tried to access the hotel's wifi network, but was only given a $9.95 upgrade option. I called the desk, and was told to 'click past it', which of course did nothing. It wasn't until 2 hrs later the complimentary access worked. We are pretty easygoing; we love good treatment and tip handsomely. If we had only 1or 2 problems, we wouldn't write. In fact, we would not have written except the hotel did not make things right. The president wrote a letter, and suggested others at the hotel would be in touch...nobody ever was.

I was really looking forward to staying at Hotel Monaco based on the photos and reputation, but the reality fell far short. The room we were assigned had a musty smell that never went away, and the air conditioning unit rattled loudly all night, making it nearly impossible to sleep. I mentioned it to the front desk, and while the clerk was polite, he said the hotel was fully booked and couldn't offer a change. The bathroom was small, with a shower that had poor water pressure and a drain that clogged almost immediately. Breakfast was another letdown--overpriced and lukewarm, with limited options that were gone by 9 AM. On the plus side, the location is convenient, and the lobby looks nice, but that doesn't make up for the uncomfortable stay. Given the nightly rate, I expected much better. I won't be returning.

I expected much more from Conrad, but the stay felt underwhelming from check-in onward. The lobby looks polished in photos, yet much of the room decor felt dated, with worn upholstery and scuffed furniture that didn't match the price. Wi‐Fi technically connected, but it repeatedly dropped during video calls and was too slow in the evening. Staff were polite when approached, though they seemed distracted and no one followed up after I reported the internet problem. Breakfast was especially disappointing: the buffet looked extensive, but several hot items were lukewarm and the coffee tasted burnt. Service at breakfast was slow despite the dining room not being full. Overall, it lacked the attentive, refined experience I expected.

We stay at the Palmer House when we attend conferences in Chicago. It is a stately building. But this year, there were ... problems we have not had before. First, they now have wi-fi available, but it is not free. The cost is $7.50 per hour. On-line it indicated that Hilton hotels charge about $4, but this was almost double. Many hotels have free wi-fi. Wi-fi is wi-fi, so the level of service is not a factor that could justify this exorbitant cost. They also charge for their fitness center, even when you are only going to use the machines. There is no business center in-house for copies, etc. Our bed was against a wall that separated us from the bathroom in the next room. It did not separate us from the bathroom noises. When someone took a shower (at 5:30 a.m.), the pipes 'sung' like old pipes do,but very loudly. An empty wine glass sat outside someone's room door for days without being picked up by housekeeping. The concierge desk had only one person and there was always a line. If you called down, you were put on hold while they dealt with the people in the line. The staff were all very nice, and the location can't be beat, but the luxury prices for normal services felt like a ripoff this year. I doubt we'll return....
Disappointing stay at the Sheraton: the room was noisy late into the night, Wi-Fi kept dropping, and the inconvenient location made our already-too-short visit feel even more rushed.

The location was convenient for sightseeing, but that's the only positive. My room had a stale smell and dusty carpet, the bathroom fixtures were rusty, and the 'view' was just a brick wall. Disappointing overall.

I expected more from Hotel Talbott given the price and location. The room looked tired, with scuffed furniture and a bathroom that never quite felt clean. Our window faced a brick wall and the service alley, so there was no real view beyond dumpsters and delivery trucks. WiFi technically connected, but it dropped repeatedly and was too slow for a video call. Sleep was difficult because of hallway noise, a rattling air conditioner, and early morning deliveries outside. Staff at check-in were curt and seemed inconvenienced when I mentioned the internet issue; no one followed up. The bed was reasonably comfortable, but that was about the only positive. I would choose another hotel next time.

OK, we are back from the Knickerbocker and I would give it the best rating. I can't believe the bad reviews. I got a priceline deal, and I still got a fine room, clean, up-to-date furnishings (OK a little traditional for my taste) and smoke free. Someone said in another thread that some people write prank reviews. I think such people should get a life because people want to read the truth. Here it is from my point of view. Both rooms on 10th floor. Regarding the size of the rooms. We had two rooms. One was a 2 double bed room. It was about 20' x 15'. Each double bed had valences that were kind of mini-canopies. The furniture, bathroom tile, shower (no tub), wall paper and paint had been done in the last few years. A Chinese inspired cabinet held TV, coffeemaker, ice bucket, and mini-bar. Three separate levels (TV, ice/coffee, and minibar) The other room was called 'Queen executive'. This one had queen bed with more of a canopy than valence, sofabed, two TVs and terry bathrobes. Also about the same size but different configerations. One TV faced the bed, other in the three level cabinet, the sofabed. Smoke in the lobby. There is a bar to the right of the entrance. It is an open arrangement so that I am sure the smoke comes from bar to entrance door. No smoke smell in no-smoking rooms. Cost of rooms $75 on priceline plus taxes. Very good value one block from N. Michigan Ave. Only complaint. Concierge said that the free trolley didn't go down Michigan Ave to Field Museum/Museum complex when in fact it does. Was this ignorance? or trying to throw more business to taxi? Either case, not good. He said at this time of year free trolley only goes to Navy Pier during winter....which is clearly incorrect.

i was in chicago from september 17-22 for a convention.. my company booked this hotel for me. the hotel is centrally located , michican ave is less than a block away. perfect location! the suites are huge with comfy beds and a beautiful kitchenette. breakfast is the best... bountiful.. not just muffins and toast... i mean everything you can imagine...waffles, bacon, sausage , hash browns, toast, danishes, omelets, burritos, all freshly made... not artifical... really good. and clean .. also they have a free dinner... buffet.. excellent... mexican night, chinese night, american fare.. all included.. wine and beer also.. well worth the expensive price of $279 a night. a very classy and clean hotel.. i love chicago... will come again!

Our check-in was great, but then we got into our room. The carpet was drenched and stained near the bathroom because the shower (open concept) leaks water onto the floor since there are no doors on it. The mini bar was broken and put an extremely foul scent into the room. Our final hotel bill reflected 2 charges that were incorrect....1 for the mini bar which we did not utilize, and the second was an up charge for a bottle of wine ($69 instead of $50). When my husband went to the front desk to have it corrected, he was met with a very unfriendly and unapologetic employee. It was adjusted, but not without confrontation. There was another guest checking out when my husband was at the front desk who had the same 'mysterious' mini bar charge on her bill as well, and was trying to have it corrected. Overall, the location of the Hard Rock was nice but it will be the last time that we stay in one,

I've stayed at plenty of InterContinentals, so I had high hopes, but this one really missed the mark. The lobby is grand, sure, but that's where the polish ended. Check-in took nearly 25 minutes because the front desk staff seemed more interested in chatting among themselves than helping guests. I finally got my room, only to find the air conditioning sounded like a truck idling and the 'city view' was mostly a brick wall and a sliver of rooftop. The bed was comfortable, I'll give them that, but the bathroom had a lingering damp smell and the towels were threadbare. Breakfast was a chaotic free-for-all--the omelet station had a 15-minute line and the pastries were stale. On my last night, I asked for a late checkout and was told 'not possible,' with zero apology. For the price, this was a letdown. I expected so much more from the brand, and honestly, a mid-range hotel would've treated me better. Won't be back.

They rave about their beds but the beds were average. On surface room seemed clean, however, dropped my pen behind nightstand and discovered at least an inch of dust. It appeared there had been repairs to something where they had to cut away part of the wall. The repair job was covered up with a wallpaper board over the hole but the board did not even completely cover hole. Impossible to have a decent shower or bath. EXTREME water saving devices on both the shower and tub provided basically a trickle of water. I was unable to get the shampoo out of my hair as pressure was so poor. Also be prepared to be nickled and dimed to death. There was even a $10 charge if you used the coffeemaker in the room, really! For room service they tack on a delivery charge and a 20% gratuity. Since the waiter does not stay to serve you how is he earning a gratuity. I have already been charged for him to deliver the food. The parking fees were outrageous at $51 a night but to add insult they charge a hotel patron the same fees as the general public. Upon packing to leave we realized that the dvd set my son had brought was missing. I reported the theft to the hotel. Had to file a report with security who promised me they would investigate and get back to me within 2 days. It has now been over two weeks. No follow up, no apology even given. We will never stay at this hotel again. We have been to Chicago many times and this is the worst hotel we have ever stayed at.

The bathroom had a persistent damp smell and a hair on the towel, and the room itself felt dusty under the bed. For $300 a night, I expected way more--my window faced a brick wall, making the whole stay feel claustrophobic and not worth it.

The fresh, understated decor and spotless marble bathroom made the InterContinental feel polished; it was pricey, but worthwhile for the service and comfort. I only wish our weekend had lasted longer.

I had requested a quiet room several weeks in advance, yet was given a room facing the street from which I could hear traffic noise. I asked to be moved and was told that nothing was available until the next day. The next morning, prior to being moved to a quiet room, the toilet in my original room overflowed creating a large unsanitary flood. About an hour later I was moved to a room which did not face the street. The room was quiet but smaller and darker. The mattresses in each room were very firm, I would even say hard. I asked if any softer mattresses were available and was told that the mattresses were all the same. At checkout I tried to give the hotel a form of payment that differed from the card the room was reserved under, and this process was still not done correctly after 10 minutes, which seemed longer because the van to the airport was waiting right outside, with other passengers. (The cost was not correctly charged until almost a week later.) As recompense for the noise, flood, etc., the hotel offered exactly nothing. Not a great stay.

The location on the strip can't be beaten, but the real highlight was the unexpected calm. We grabbed a spot by the pool early, and the view of the ocean from the higher floors is genuinely stunning at sunrise. Breakfast each morning was a proper spread--think made-to-order omelets and fresh pastries, not just the standard continental fare. While the lobby has a sleek, modern vibe that feels current, the guest rooms lean a bit more traditional with older carpet; it's not shabby, just noticeably dated. That said, the staff were the true stars. From the front desk who remembered our room number to the bartender who mixed a perfect Old Fashioned, everyone was warm and proactive without being pushy. We left feeling genuinely rested, and that's worth a lot.
The Omni looked impressive online, but my room felt dated, the air conditioning was noisy, and service was surprisingly slow. For the price, I expected much more.

Rocked up expecting loud chaos, got pure comfort instead--huge bed, killer soundproofing, and staff who genuinely vibed with me. The pool scene was buzzing but never obnoxious. Already plotting my next stay; the Hard Rock just gets it.

Absolutely loved my stay at the Sheraton! The moment we walked into the lobby, the staff greeted us with such warmth, even offering a late checkout before we asked. Our room was spotless and the bed? Honestly, I've never slept so well in a hotel. The blackout curtains were a lifesaver after a long travel day. I have to give a shoutout to the bar staff--they made the best Old Fashioned I've had in ages, and the bartender remembered my name on the second night. The pool was a bit busy during peak hours, so we went early morning and had it almost to ourselves. Only tiny hiccup was the elevator wait on floor 14 during breakfast rush, but that's a minor thing when everything else was this polished. Will definitely be back for our next city break, and I've already recommended it to my colleagues. Top notch.
The room was spotless, and the bathroom felt fresh with great water pressure. Our stay flew by too quickly, but it was well worth every penny for such comfort and convenience.

Honestly, I almost didn't book here because of a mix-up with my dates, but the front desk agent, Marco, sorted everything out in minutes with a smile. That set the tone for the whole stay. The room was spotless, the bed was like sleeping on a cloud, and the blackout curtains actually worked. I loved that the mini-fridge had real glassware, not just plastic cups. The location is perfect for exploring on foot, but the best part was the quiet courtyard for morning coffee. Breakfast had fresh pastries and made-to-order eggs, which was a pleasant surprise. The only tiny hiccup was the elevator being slow during peak checkout time, but honestly, it gave me a moment to breathe. I left feeling genuinely rested, which is rare for a business trip. Definitely my new home base in the city.

I had a very comfortable stay at Homewood and would happily book again. The suite was clean, quiet, and had enough space to actually relax after a long day. I especially appreciated the small kitchen area, which made it easy to keep drinks and snacks on hand instead of eating out for every meal. The bed was comfortable, the shower had good water pressure, and housekeeping kept everything tidy. Breakfast was better than expected, with hot options as well as fruit, yogurt, and coffee that was ready early. The front desk staff were friendly and gave helpful local recommendations without being overly formal. Parking was straightforward, and the overall property felt well maintained. It was a reliable, welcoming place to stay.

I expected much more from a Sofitel stay, especially for the price. Check-in took nearly 30 minutes because the room apparently wasn't ready, even though we arrived after the stated time. The room looked tired: stained carpet near the window, a loose bathroom fixture, and the air conditioning rattled all night. Housekeeping missed our room on the second day despite us being out for hours. Breakfast was crowded, with lukewarm eggs and empty coffee pots that staff were slow to refill. Everyone was polite when we could get their attention, but the service felt understaffed and indifferent. The location was convenient, yet the overall experience was nowhere near the luxury standard advertised.

I have stayed at this location many times over the past few years and have enjoyed the neighborhood, cost and amenities. The hotel is currently under construction and while they claim to be open, you wouldn't know it. You need to take an elevator to get from the street the lobby and the rooms are bare lacking even an alarm clock. The beds are propped up on a modern bed stand but you might think that you are in a stale mental asylum and not a 'nicer historic hotel.' I will try them again once the construction is through but would recommend staying at any other hotel in the meantime. It was a very frustrating experience.
Slept deeply in the plush bed, waking to a stunning skyline view that justified the premium rate. The rain shower and heated floor made the marble bathroom feel like a private spa retreat.

The view was a dreary wall of the neighboring building, and the noise from the corridor kept me up all night. Staff were indifferent at check-in, while the tired, dusty decor felt stuck in the 90s. Genuinely overpriced.

I'm still scratching my head over how this place earned its stars. The bathroom was the low point--the showerhead dribbled lukewarm water, and the drain gurgled like it was drowning every few minutes. As for sleep, forget it: the mattress sagged into a crater, and the AC unit rattled all night, so I woke up more exhausted than when I checked in. The room itself wasn't filthy, but the carpet had suspicious stains near the baseboard, and the sheets felt damp, like they'd been hung in a closet. Honestly, the stay dragged; by day two, I was counting the hours to checkout, yet the lobby checkout line took forever, making it feel both too short and painfully long. I'd rather have spent the money on a roadside motel--at least that would've been honest about its flaws.

We stay at Hilton for 4 nights last march. It was a pleasant stay. We got a large room with 2 double beds and 2 bathrooms, The TV was Ok, a 27' CRT Flat Screen. The coincierge was very friendly when we need. The room was very cleaned when we arrived, we ordered some pizzas from room service and the pizza was Ok also.The main Hall is beautiful. The breakfast is charged, 20 dollars, kinda expensive. The internet access (WiFi) is charged, 13 dollars/day. Pros: Low rate price, huge rooms, close to attractions at Loop, close to metro station. Cons: Expensive breakfast, Internet access charged. Tip: When leaving the building, always use the Michigan Av exit. Its a great view.
Great stay at Hotel Monaco! The staff were super friendly and the room was perfectly clean. Loved the location--easy walk to everything--and the bed was incredibly comfy. Would definitely book again!

I chose the Hilton for its unbeatable central location, which truly is a stone's throw from everything I needed. That's where the positives end. The lobby's beige-and-brass decor feels like a time capsule from the early 90s, with worn carpets and scuffed furniture that scream neglect. My room's so-called 'city view' was mostly a brick wall and a sliver of a parking garage. The bathroom was the biggest letdown: the showerhead sputtered, the caulking was mildewed and peeling, and the towels were thin as paper. For the price I paid, I expected far better maintenance and a fresher atmosphere. Service was polite but overstretched. I'd only return if every other hotel was booked solid--which, frankly, says it all.

We stayed three nights in a king room with a skyline view, and honestly, it exceeded expectations. The lobby's marble and brass could lean a bit traditional, but our room felt crisp and modern--soft linens, USB ports everywhere, and a bathroom that actually had good water pressure. The staff were the real standout: the front desk clerk remembered our anniversary without us mentioning it and sent up a small dessert plate. Our window faced the river, catching the sunset behind the bridges, which made the higher price tag feel justified. Breakfast buffet was pricey, but the omelet station was worth it. Valet was quick each morning, and the gym had brand-new Pelotons. Yes, the hallways are a little worn near the ice machine, but the overall polish and genuine service made it a solid pick for a special trip. I'd book again.

Great location - right on the Chicago River - away from the other skyscraper hotels - our room was good size, very clean and with a nice river view - Overall, a great staff - in particular I would like to point out Christy Morgan - Chief Experience Officer and Paula Fortney - Concierge for their assistance in making this stay a memorable one - (in the interests of full disclosure, we stayed here on our AMEX - Starwood points)
The Talbott was a lovely stay--comfortable room, genuinely friendly staff, and an unbeatable location for exploring the neighborhood. Everything felt easy and well cared for, and I'd happily return.

The room was spotless, and the morning view of the park from our window was simply lovely. My only regret is that our two nights felt far too short, especially with the hotel's prime spot for strolling to nearby cafes and shops.

I stayed at the Fairmont to attend a conference. I was very pleased with the hotel.
