The doorman offered me an umbrella as I headed out for a walk... and sure enough it started to rain very soon after- I would have been soaked with it. Upon my return, the doorman then asked about my walk, etc. This is reflective of all the staff I encountered. The front desk promptly checked me in. DEFINITELY register for their rewards program before you arrive... The complimentary gym access is excellent, plus you save on internet access fees which are waived for members. The bathroom and separate dressing areas were large and convenient. The only negative- no coffee maker! AND the Starbucks in the adjacent building is closed on weekends since the area corporate offices are closed those days!!! Otherwise my stay was perfect, considering the conference rate was $99 per night!
Disappointing stay at the Sheraton--check-in took forever, the room smelled musty, and the AC barely worked. For the price, I expected much better. Probably won't be back.

I just had a conference there. They have bed bugs--I have all these bug bites and it itches like hell. Food wise, we had chicken BOTH times for lunch (maybe my company was saving some $) but they should at least prepare them differently. It looked like they did the same style chicken but change the underlying 'bed' upon which it is served. For dinner, we had filet mignon and crab cake. Sounds good right? Wrong! The filet mignon seems to be 1/2 the thickness of what I have seen and it was tough. I thought the filet mignon is suppose to be tenderest part of the cow???? Also, the crab cakes was a bit too salty. Finally the portions were tiny and left me lacking. In asking my co-worker, most seem to be blase about the food. However, some seem to like the burger (which they went to substitute) at the Palms, which is a restaurant inside the hotel, just off the lobby. On the positive note, the dessert for dinner was good. Otherwise, I'd recommend another hotel. In the meantime, when I got home, I make sure to bring EVERYTHING straight to the washer/dryer to disinfect (even strip down). But, damn, I'm still itchin'

We stayed at the Homewood Suites for four nights and honestly couldn't have asked for a better value. The rate was noticeably lower than comparable hotels nearby, yet we got far more than we expected. Our room was spotless when we checked in, and housekeeping kept it that way throughout our visit, even restocking coffee supplies without being asked. The bathroom, while not huge, was in great shape with strong water pressure and a shower that heated up in seconds. Best part was the sleep quality: the bed was firm but comfortable, the pillows were fluffy, and despite being near the elevator we never heard a thing once the door closed. With a hot breakfast thrown in every morning, this place easily beats anything else we've stayed at in this price range. We'll definitely be back.

I really wanted to love this Sofitel, given the brand's reputation, but our stay was a letdown from start to finish. We arrived at 3:30 PM, only to be told our room wasn't ready--fine, that happens--but it took another hour and a half of waiting in the lobby before they called. When we finally got upstairs, the 'luxury' room felt dated, with scuffed furniture and a bathroom that had a lingering musty odor. The air conditioning was either freezing or off, and we couldn't find a comfortable middle. I'll give credit to the front desk staff for being polite, but the vibe was pure indifference elsewhere. We tried the bar for a nightcap, and it took ten minutes just to get a menu. For nearly $400 a night, I expect more than a mediocre bed and peeling wallpaper. The location is convenient, sure, but it doesn't make up for the feeling that this property is running on its name alone. I won't be returning.

The Hard Rock Hotel Chicago has become my favorite hotel. I've stayed there at least 5 times now and have never had anything other than a wonderful experience. As you might have guessed - it has a super Rock & Roll theme, with some music paraphanelia in the lobby and on each floor's elevator lobby. The rooms all have large photo murals that are themed to different musicians. You can request being on the floor of your favorite band (like KISS, Aerosmith, etc...) The rooms are GREAT. Well appointed. SUPER Comfortable beds and luxurious sheets and wonderous pillows. The large TV has a cool sound system that ramps up the viewing experience. There's a spacious desk in each room with a mini bar. I've always had a room with big windows and a view down Michigan Ave (the hotel sits right on Michigan - a block from the canal). The bathrooms are furnished with absolutely great fixtures sporting a great design... some of the showers have windows in side of them (you can shower AND enjoy the view down Michigan!) or close the waterproof drapes. I've never had anything but a great experience with the staff here... front desk, doorman, etc are all great. There's a lobby bar that still feels intimate and has nice energy. Big screen TV to catch the latest scores, too. Of course, Rock & Roll music pumps thru the place. You can stay at a 'plain' hotel anywhere... but this is a GREAT, WELL DESIGNED, FUN and MEMORABLE HOTEL that you'll want to return back to. If I had one concern - it would be the rather crazy charge for parking your car overnight. My daily car parking rate was close to $50 per night, which I'm sorry to say is about the going rate in the loop. Stay here. Be cool.

I had high hopes coming here, but Hotel Allegro really let me down. The bathroom was cramped and clearly overdue for a renovation--mildew in the shower grout, a sink that drained painfully slowly, and a wobbly toilet seat that made everything feel grimy. The staff barely acknowledged us; check-in felt like an inconvenience to them, and when I asked a question at the desk, I got a shrug instead of an answer. Noise was the worst part: the walls are paper-thin, and I heard doors slamming and conversations well past midnight. My sleep suffered badly both nights, waking up4 almost hourly. By the time we left, we were exhausted and relieved to go. For the price, it wasn't remotely worth it, and I won't be returning.

We stayed at the Hotel Ambassador for four nights in October and were genuinely impressed. Our room on the sixth floor overlooked the courtyard, so even though the street below gets lively at night, we slept like logs. Beds here deserve a mention -- the mattress was firm but comfortable, and the pillows actually stayed cool. Front desk staff were quick with restaurant suggestions when we asked, sending us to a tiny bistro two blocks away that ended up being the best meal of the trip. Housekeeping was thorough and came when scheduled without us having to chase anyone down. Breakfast had a decent spread, though the coffee could be stronger. Only real hiccup was a slow elevator one morning, minor stuff. Would happily book here again.

I expected more from the Ambassador given the nightly rate and its reputation. Our room faced the back of the building, so the 'view' amounted to a brick wall, rooftop vents, and early-morning delivery trucks. Inside, the furniture looked tired rather than charming: scratched dark wood, a sagging armchair, and an oddly dated patterned carpet. The bathroom was clean enough, but the water pressure was weak and the air conditioning rattled throughout the night. Staff were polite when we spoke to them, though no one seemed especially interested in resolving the noise issue. We only stayed two nights, and honestly that was plenty; by the second morning I was ready to leave. For this price, it did not feel remotely worth it.

I stayed in this hotel during a business trip, and while conducting a business meeting in the hotel bar, a customer grabbed all of the cash out of my wallet. Security was informed, but I was told that I had to wait to talk to them. After about twenty minutes of waiting I was informed that if I did not continue to wait l would never be able to report the incident, despite the fact that I was a hotel guest. Unfortunately I had to go to a business dinner and could no longer wait. Long story short, I no longer felt comfortable in this hotel and wish that someone, anyone would have talked to me about it. I've since been on the phone with a manager, who promised to call me back once she researched the incident, and have yet to hear back, despite the promise that she would call me back two days ago. I expected more from this hotel.

Slept like a log in that ridiculously comfy bed--only wish I'd booked another night. Staff were genuinely warm, not scripted, and the Loop location made everything walkable. Would've stayed longer if my schedule allowed.

Our three-night stay at the Omni was exactly what we needed after months of planning this trip. We were on the fourteenth floor, and the view alone was worth the upgrade I requested at booking--waking up to streetlights and rooftops stretching out toward the mountains each morning felt like a small luxury. Despite being so high up in a busy part of downtown, the room was remarkably quiet; we heard only a faint rumble of an occasional elevator two doors down, and absolutely nothing once we closed the curtains at night. I'm a light sleeper, so this mattered enormously, and I slept eight solid hours every night without waking once. The bathroom pleasantly surprised me too, with a deep tub, strong water pressure, and plush towels replenished daily. The housekeeping staff even folded my daughter's stuffed animal into a little chair one afternoon, which made her whole trip. We'd return here without hesitation.
Disappointing stay at the Sheraton: the room felt dated, housekeeping missed basic details, and the front desk was slow to respond. For the price, I expected much better service and comfort.

My wife and I stayed at this hotel at the end of May, 2009. She came for the weekend for a function and we extended the trip to take in the city. We got a deal on this hotel through TravelZoos. $249/night stay for $99/night plus we got the full buffet breakfast. The room was wonderful. Extremely large King size bed with expansive sitting area. We are used to smaller hotels with little room to move. The bed was extremely comfortable with lots of pillows. No wear or damage in room at all except sink tap dripped a bit (poor taps). We could have upgraded to river view for $20/night but chose not to. We enjoyed the room for what it was. 22nd floor looking south. The buffet breakfast was great. Lots to choose from and very fresh with made to order eggs, non stop coffee and juice and the servers were so eager to please. Great to have breakfast included in night stay. Might be a bit dear to pay at $22/person. It was nice to sit and relax with good breakfast, coffee and newspaper and not have to figure where to catch a morning meal. Concierge desk was most helpful in suggesting places to eat, always informative and ready to provide maps, directions, multiple suggestions and even make the reservations. Cards included to admit without paying cover charges at some jazz clubs. Location was great. Blocks from El and other transportation and easy walking distance to the parks and right on the river. If in Chicago again, would not hesitate to stay here again. A swimming pool would have been nice but we did not miss it.

The Talbott was a lovely stay--quiet, comfortable, and perfectly located for exploring the neighborhood. Staff were genuinely welcoming, and the room had thoughtful touches that made it feel easy and relaxing.

I booked the Talbott expecting charm, but the room felt tired and the walls paper-thin--heard every hallway conversation until 2 a.m. Staff was polite but slow, and breakfast was lukewarm at best. Not worth the price tag.

I really wanted to like this place, but the Omni just didn't deliver for what they charge. The rate felt steep for a room that had a suspicious sticky patch near the nightstand and hair in the bathroom sink upon arrival. Breakfast was the low point: lukewarm scrambled eggs that looked like they'd been sitting out for hours, and the orange juice tasted watered down. The Wi-Fi was technically free, but it dropped every fifteen minutes, making it impossible to stream anything or even load a simple email reliably. I asked the front desk for help, and they just shrugged, saying it was a 'known issue.' Honestly, the only saving grace was the bed, which was comfortable enough. But for these prices, I expect clean surfaces and functioning internet. I left feeling like I'd overpaid for a mediocre stay, and I won't be coming back. There are better options nearby for less money.

We stayed at the Hilton for three nights while visiting family downtown, and the location couldn't have been more convenient--everything we wanted to see was within easy walking distance, and the airport shuttle ran like clockwork. Our room on the fourteenth floor was nicely updated; the decor felt fresh and modern, none of the tired, dated furnishings you sometimes find in big chains. Wi-Fi was fast and reliable the whole time, which mattered since my husband had to join a couple of video calls. Even better, it was remarkably quiet despite being right in the busy part of town--we slept soundly with the blackout curtains closed. Staff at the front desk and breakfast lounge were genuinely friendly. Would happily return on our next trip; it checked every box we cared about.

I booked the Omni specifically for a weekend getaway, expecting the standards their name usually implies. What a letdown. The air conditioning in our room sounded like a cement mixer having a seizure, and maintenance 'fixed' it by leaving a note saying it was 'working as designed' in a heatwave. The bathroom had a faint but constant smell of mildew, and the housekeeping never replaced our coffee pods once. I asked the front desk for a late checkout on Sunday and was met with a curt 'no,' even though the hotel was clearly half-empty. The pool area was packed with unsupervised kids doing cannonballs while the lifeguard scrolled on his phone. The only decent meal we had was at a diner two blocks away. The inflated nightly rate made all of this feel like a personal insult. Save your money.

My stay at the Affinia was more disappointing than I expected. The location is convenient, with restaurants, shops, and public transportation close by, but the central setting did not make up for the condition of the room. The decor feels stuck in another decade: worn furniture, dull carpets, and fixtures that could use a serious update. The bathroom was clean enough at first glance, but cramped, with weak water pressure, chipped tile, and grout that looked tired. Check-in was slow, and the front desk staff seemed distracted rather than welcoming. They answered questions, but offered little help when I mentioned the problems in the room. Noise from the hallway also carried late into the night. This could be a comfortable hotel with some investment, but currently the price feels difficult to justify.

My stay at the InterContinental was much more disappointing than I expected for the price. The lobby looks impressive, but the check-in process was slow and oddly disorganized, even though I arrived well after the usual check-in time. My room was clean enough, but the furniture felt worn, the carpet had visible stains, and the air-conditioning made a loud rattling noise throughout the night. I called twice about it and never received a follow-up. The bathroom was attractive but had very low water pressure, and housekeeping skipped replacing the coffee supplies. Breakfast was also overpriced for a fairly ordinary buffet, with long waits for a table. The location is convenient and some employees were polite, but the service and upkeep did not match the hotel's reputation or rates.

We stayed at the Sheraton for three nights over a long weekend and honestly had zero complaints. Our room on the 14th floor overlooked the river, which was a nice surprise since I hadn't requested a view. The bed was one of those plush ones with tons of pillows, and I actually slept better than I do at home. Housekeeping was consistent every day, and one evening they left extra towels without us even asking. The front desk upgraded us to the club level because of some mix-up with our room type, which normally would've been annoying but turned into a bonus -- free breakfast and snacks all day up there, plus a quiet place to escape the crowds. Location-wise it's an easy walk to basically everything downtown. Pool area got crowded Saturday afternoon but the kids loved it anyway. Would happily book here again next trip back.

My stay at the Fairmont was disappointing, especially given the price. The lobby looked elegant at first, but the guest room decor felt dated, with worn carpeting, heavy furniture, and scuffed surfaces that made the hotel seem overdue for an update. The bathroom was clean enough, but cramped and rather tired; the grout needed attention, water pressure was inconsistent, and the toiletries felt surprisingly basic. I expected a more polished experience for what I paid, but the room offered little value beyond the address and impressive views. Staff members were generally polite, though service felt slow and impersonal, particularly at check-in and when I requested extra towels. A few employees were helpful, but overall the experience did not match the Fairmont's reputation or the premium rate.

Breakfast was a lovely spread of fresh pastries and made-to-order eggs, and the bathroom's rainfall shower felt like pure indulgence. The room was spotless, but honestly, my one-night stay felt far too short to enjoy every comfort.

My husband and I stayed at the Hotel Monaco for 5 days in October, 2007. I cannot begain to tell you how great this place is. The service was impecable and the room was fantastic. Huge window seat to look over Chicago. It was great. The wine reception in the evening was a special treat as was the morning coffee service in the lobby. This was our first trip to Chicago and I hope not our last. I will definately stay at Hotel Monaco again when we return. We booked our room through a safety convention web site.

I stayed in this hotel for a week and I was looking forward to a stay at a top class hotel. I was shocked and disapointed with my stay, Here are some of my gripes - Room had a broken phone and broken lightbulb - Breakfast service was slow and impolite - Hotel rationed shampoo (one bottle for two people sharing and did not refill a bottle that was less than half full). - We also shared a bar of soap. I was so disappointed with this hotel, I paid for a premium hotel and got a very disappointing stay.

My family and I stayed at this hotel during an extended weekend trip in July, 08. We had (3) 1 bedroom suites. Great Location in downtown Chicago. Within walking distance to shopping and most downtown tourist attractions. The service was excellent and the hotel staff was friendly. The breakfast buffet was very good but the eating area can get crowded. I recommend going early. The rooms were quiet and clean. I highly recommend this hotel for families and for travelers staying >2-3 days. We would stay here again. Parking is expensive, about $28/day. It is valet. The cheapest self parking I could find in the area was $24/days so we did valet parking. The valet and bell staff were very helpful and friendly. This is my 3rd experience with Homewood Suites (3 different cities). I have had a great experience each time.

I had a very comfortable stay at the Sheraton and would happily return. My room was spotless, with a supportive bed and good blackout curtains, so I slept through the night without waking up. Despite being close to the elevators, it was surprisingly quiet; I only heard a little hallway traffic in the morning. Breakfast offered plenty of choice, including fresh fruit, pastries, eggs, and decent coffee, and the staff kept everything well stocked. The location was especially convenient for getting around, with shops, restaurants, and public transport within an easy walk. Check-in was friendly and efficient, and the overall atmosphere felt polished but welcoming.

The wifi was useless--kept dropping during work calls--and the location, while central, meant constant street noise that made sleep impossible. I left more exhausted than when I arrived. Definitely not worth the price.

The Hard Rock is glossy and sexy, but an absolutely fantastic hotel.... I was in town for business and stayed here because of it's location, but I absolutely understand why tourists would like it...right on the river, cool art deco building and Millenium Park is just down the street. Regardless- the room was clean, the staff was friendly, but NOT annoying and the bar was fun. I was comfortable having a couple of drinks alone at the end of the day - they were GOOD! I'll definitely try it again!

The Homewood was exactly what I needed--quiet, clean, and the kitchenette saved us on a long trip. Staff were friendly without hovering, and the beds were surprisingly comfortable. Would happily book again next time we're passing through.

We stayed in the Amalfi in July 2010, 4th of July weekend. I was very apprehensive about leaving my Diesel Ford Excursion with the valet at Amalfi. It has a few modifications to the engine and can be damaged if not operated correctly. I explained the procedure to the valet drivers, and felt like it was a complete waste of time. When the vehicle was returned to me the valet driver did not let it idle down and cool the turbo off as I had instructed. When I tried to start it, it wasn't happy, but did finally start. I was so relieved to get it back I just wanted to leave. Driving away I noticed that the top speed recorded on the GPS was 105mph!!! (previous top speed was 95mph, done a few days earlier driving across South Dakota). I could just picture the flying Ferrari scene in Ferris Bueller's Day Off. I couldn't imagine where in the crowded Chicago traffic they found a place to go that fast, though it wouldn't take long to make that happen (see reference to modified engine above). A little while later we stopped for lunch and I noticed a dent in the front bumper. I contacted the hotel and was referred to their claims people. No remedy. Lesson learned. Brett

Upon check in - the lobby was BUSY! I was tired and not feeling well from a tough road show. The Front Desk person I checked in with was so fast and so nice that I walked away from the desk smiling... that alone was such a great feeling. Every time I had any experience with a hotel staff member, I was so pleased! I have to say - service really is everything to me and I have to give this top marks for that. An added bonus was the location... I just think it is perfect for me. On top of that, I had a meeting down in the loop, but not quite sure how to get there - a person approached me in the lobby, asked if he could help me get to my meeting. I thought he was getting me a taxi - but no - he walked me to his SUV and drove me to the meeting, 'just a free service from the hotel' he stated as we drove... really!!!! so cool! I haven't even talked about the Pump Room yet - great dinner, very professional service, and no attitude. I will return - just up date the rooms a little bit, thats all... the curtains need some help.

Booked the Sheraton expecting the usual standard -- walked away genuinely let down. The lobby looks grand in photos, but up close it's tired: scuffed marble, flickering lights, and a front desk that had one person handling a queue of ten. Our room wasn't ready at 4 p.m., and when we finally got in, the 'city view' was a brick wall and an air conditioning unit that rattled all night. The mattress sagged on one side, and the bathroom smelled faintly of mildew. Breakfast cost $28 for rubbery eggs and lukewarm coffee. On the upside, the location is central, and housekeeping did respond quickly to requests for extra towels. But at these rates, I expect more than a courteous apology about 'high occupancy.' Save your money unless you really need the name on the door.
Overpriced for what you get. The bathroom had grime in the corners and the room felt stale. Our window faced a brick wall, and the location was a long walk to the metro.

My stay at the Sofitel was a masterclass in under-delivery. The promise of Parisian elegance faded the moment I stepped off the elevator onto my floor, where the hallway hummed with a persistent, mechanical drone--a sound that followed me into my room, where the air conditioning unit clattered all night. Sleep was fitful; I woke up more exhausted than when I arrived. The two nights stretched on interminably. Staff were polite but maddeningly disengaged; my request for a later checkout was met with a shrug and a curt 'possible, but not guaranteed.' The one saving grace, the panoramic view of the city, was perpetually obscured by a film of grime on the window I couldn't reach. It felt like being trapped in a beautiful, broken spaceship. I finally checked out feeling shortchanged, as if the visit had been a dull, lengthy obligation rather than a brief escape.

Stayed for three nights for a work conference and honestly, the location was the main pull--right by the harbor, a quick stroll to the ferry and some fantastic seafood spots. The room itself was on the higher floors and had a sweeping view that made the morning coffee feel special. Bed was firm but incredibly comfortable, and blackout curtains actually did their job. The bathroom was spotless with great water pressure, which is a win in my book. 

The only hiccup was the Wi-Fi dropping a couple of times during a video call, though it was fine afterwards. Staff at the front desk were efficient and friendly, especially when I asked for restaurant recommendations. The club lounge was a nice perk for evening snacks, though a bit crowded. Would definitely book here again for the convenience and overall comfort. Nothing flashy, but everything done right.

From the moment I walked in, the room was spotless, and the floor-to-ceiling window offered a stunning skyline view. The bathroom was modern with great water pressure, and the complimentary Wi-Fi never dropped once--a smooth, comfortable stay all around.

I want to recognize so many people who were exemplary in their service. 1) Sylvia Rollins, Head Concierge. I wanted a fairly last minute reservation at MK restaurant. I spoke with Sylvia on the phone just a few days prior to arrival and within 15 minutes had the desired reservation. 2) Ryan Lettier, Concierge, provided us detailed information on the architectural cruises. Our morning cruise ended up being cancelled by the tour operator and Ryan provided a late check out time to cover us until we could get back to the Monaco. 3) Turndown service was provided as requested and housekeeping in general seemed to be at a high standard 4) Even the bellman went out of their way to ask if we knew how to get the train etc when leaving the hotel. The rooms are tastfully furnished in that whimiscal Hotel Monaco feel. Beds and bedding both very comfortable. The complimentary happy hour and morning coffee/tea service were both very utililzed by the hotel guests.

Checked in a bit later than planned, around 10 PM, and the front desk had everything ready--even upgraded us to a high floor with a nice view of the river, which was a lovely surprise. The room was spotless, bed super comfy, and the blackout curtains actually worked. Breakfast buffet had a good mix of hot and cold options; the omelet station was a plus, though the coffee could've been stronger. I used the gym in the morning--it's compact but had everything I needed. Location is solid for exploring, with the metro a short walk. Only minor gripe: the hallway ice machine was noisy at night, but it didn't ruin anything. Staff were consistently friendly, from valet to housekeeping. I'd gladly stay here again for the value and reliability.
The staff were lovely, but the room felt dated and smelled musty. The AC was loud all night, and the breakfast buffet was a sad, overpriced spread. Not the Hyatt standard I expected at all.

The Hotel Talbott felt like a hidden gem tucked away from the chaos, and I'm already planning my return. From the moment I walked in, the staff were genuinely warm--not the rehearsed friendliness you often get--and they remembered my name the next morning, which was a lovely touch. Breakfast was a quiet, elegant affair with perfectly flaky croissants and a made-to-order omelet that beat any chain buffet. My room overlooked the leafy street, and watching the city lights flicker on from that window was a real treat. The bed was supremely comfortable, with plush pillows that cradled me into a deep sleep--the kind I rarely get at home. Everything felt thoughtfully curated, and while it's not the flashiest spot, its understated charm won me over completely.

Stayed at Hotel Monaco expecting a boutique treat, but the room felt worn and the AC rattled all night. Staff were polite but indifferent, and breakfast was overpriced for what you got. Not worth the hype or the price tag.

Breakfast was a chaotic scramble of lukewarm eggs and burnt toast, and the hallways buzzed with slamming doors all night. The lobby's tired floral carpet and peeling wallpaper felt straight from the 80s, while our window offered a brick wall.

I really wanted to like the Affinia, but our four nights there were a letdown from start to finish. The breakfast was a joke for the price of the room -- stale pastries, watery coffee, and by 8:30 the fruit bowl was empty and nobody bothered to refill it. The wifi was so unreliable that I gave up trying to work from the room and ended up camping out at a coffee shop down the street. Noise was a constant issue too; our room faced the street and we heard sirens, delivery trucks, and hallway conversations at all hours. The 'city view' advertised on the booking site turned out to be a stare directly into the neighboring building's wall of AC units. Staff were polite enough, but for this price I expected far more. Won't be returning.

Disappointing stay at Swissotel--the room felt dated, the Wi-Fi kept dropping, and housekeeping missed basic details. Staff were polite, but the overall experience didn't match the price or expectations.

Stayed at the Hard Rock for a weekend getaway and honestly left impressed. The rock-and-roll vibe is everywhere--guitars on the walls, a killer playlist in the lobby, even the elevator music is curated. Check-in was quick, and the front desk guy hooked us up with a room on a high floor overlooking the strip. The room itself was clean and comfortable, though a bit on the dark side with all the moody decor. The bed was fantastic, and the blackout curtains did their job. We grabbed drinks at the pool bar one afternoon--overpriced, sure, but the vibe made up for it. Location is unbeatable if you want to be in the middle of everything, and the staff consistently went out of their way to help, from valet to housekeeping. Wouldn't hesitate to book again.

I paid a small fortune for a supposedly upscale stay, yet the carpet looked frayed and the bathroom fixtures felt dated. Breakfast was a bland buffet with lukewarm eggs, and the whole experience left me questioning whether any of it justified the lofty price tag.

I travelled to Illinois from the UK on business, and booked Friday and Saturday night at the Homewood Suites so that I could have a weekend in the city. The location was perfect, walking distance to Michigan Ave for all the shopping and touristy stuff, and literally 100 yards to the L (red line) for getting out to the surrounding areas. The room was great: not exactly 'wow' decor but clean and really well stocked. I was expecting a 'suite' to be a larger than average hotel room with seperate sitting area. It was actually a 3-room mini-apartment, with an open lounge/kitchen, bedroom, and bathroom. Two flatscreen TVs and a huge bed. Breakfast buffet eggs and bacon were great for the hangover(!), and the kitchen meant that I could cook up some lunch rather than eat out if needed.

Disappointing stay at the Hilton. Room wasn't ready at check-in, the air conditioning barely worked, and staff seemed indifferent to my complaints. Expected much more for the price. Won't be returning.

The Hotel Monaco's location was the main advantage: it was easy to walk to restaurants, shops, and public transportation, which made exploring the city convenient. Unfortunately, the stay was far less pleasant than expected. My room faced a busy street, and the traffic, sirens, and late-night voices continued well past midnight despite the windows being closed. The view was also disappointing--mostly a brick wall and a jumble of rooftop equipment rather than anything worth mentioning. Breakfast was another letdown, with a limited selection of lukewarm eggs, dry pastries, and weak coffee, and the small dining area felt crowded. Staff were polite, but service was slow when I asked for help. Given the price, the overall experience felt underwhelming, and I would not rush to stay here again.

I expected more from a Sofitel, especially for the rate we paid. The lobby looks polished, but the experience went downhill quickly. Our room had a strong musty smell, and the air conditioning rattled loudly through the night. Housekeeping missed our room one day despite the sign being removed before noon, and when we called for fresh towels, they arrived nearly an hour later. The mattress was uncomfortable and the bathroom lighting was oddly dim, making it difficult to get ready. Breakfast was expensive and fairly ordinary, with lukewarm coffee and slow service even though the restaurant was not busy. Staff were polite when approached, but nobody seemed empowered to resolve anything. It felt more like a tired business hotel wearing a luxury label.

I had a very comfortable two-night stay at the Conrad and would happily return. The room was spotless when I arrived, including the desk, windows, and the corners that often get overlooked. Decor felt current without trying too hard: warm neutral colors, good lighting, and modern furniture that was actually practical for working. The bathroom was especially nice, with a large walk-in shower, strong water pressure, fluffy towels, and plenty of counter space for toiletries. Breakfast was better than the usual hotel buffet, with fresh fruit, eggs made to order, pastries, and attentive coffee refills. Staff at the restaurant were warm even during the busy morning rush. A polished, relaxing hotel overall.
The Hotel Monaco looked stylish online, but my room was tired, noisy, and not especially clean. Staff were polite, though the overall experience felt overpriced and disappointing for the rate.
Hotel Monaco looked charming online, but the room was tired, the heating rattled all night, and the front desk barely acknowledged our complaints. Definitely not worth the price.

In a very nice location close to shopping and places to eat and also in a beautiful neighborhood. A small hotel with a pleasant place to sit in the lobby, the Pump Room is a classic place to have a drink. We did not have dinner there so I can not comment but we enjoyed people watching while we had an afternoon drink looking out the window at the people in the neighborhood. It is a short walk to very good shopping and eating.

The room's dated furnishings and dusty corners made the hefty price tag feel like a bad joke. Location was central, sure, but the worn carpet and peeling wallpaper overshadowed any convenience--definitely not worth the splurge.

We stayed 6 pleasent days in this not too big and very friendly hotel. the rooms were spotless comfortable and great view too... also nice view from the roof-bar. The area is pleasant nice and clean, minute walk to magnificant mile, easy to walk around to the lake. friendly stuff, very clean, great warm hotel to stay in. it does not have the 'big hotel' factory-like feeling - more like home :)
Really enjoyed my stay at Hyatt: breakfast had plenty of fresh choices, the Wi-Fi was reliable, and the friendly staff were helpful. My room was wonderfully quiet at night.

Hotel James was a really pleasant surprise. The location made it easy to walk to restaurants and shops, but the room itself was quiet enough to get a great night's sleep. Check-in was friendly and quick, and the front desk gave us a couple of useful local recommendations without being pushy. Our room felt clean, modern, and thoughtfully laid out, with a comfortable bed, good water pressure, and plenty of outlets by the desk. I also appreciated the little touches, like decent coffee and enough space to unpack instead of living out of a suitcase. Breakfast was simple but fresh, and the staff kept everything stocked. I'd happily stay here again.

Immaculate room with a stunning city view from the 14th floor, and the location couldn't be more convenient for exploring downtown. Honestly, our weekend felt far too short--we'd happily have stayed another night or two.
Had a really comfortable stay at the Sheraton--the room was quiet, the bed was excellent, and the front desk handled my late check-in without any fuss. I'd happily return.

Really lovely stay at the InterContinental -- the club lounge views over the city were worth every penny, and the concierge sorted our dinner reservations without a hitch. Bed was incredibly comfortable too. Would happily return.

Didn't get the room we were promised. Kind of room we had reserved (2 queens) 'wasn't available. they then squeezed 3 adult ladies into 2 singles and a blow-up bed. Had to pile furniture on top of tables to get it in! Very unsatisfactory!! Will not return, will not recommend. Will tell people going to Chicago to NOT stay in your hotel. When I next visit Paris nextspring, I intend to stop at your world headquarters to tell them what I think of the Chicago facility.
Disappointing stay at Hard Rock: the Wi-Fi kept dropping, and the room felt dusty despite the stylish decor. The cramped bathroom was poorly maintained, though the central location was convenient.

I stayed at the hotel james for three nights last month and honestly wasn't expecting much given the price, but it really exceeded my expectations. My room on the fourth floor was spacious, spotless, and the bed was genuinely comfortable--not one of those rock-hard hotel mattresses. The front desk staff, especially a woman named Priya, went out of her way to help me figure out public transit and even printed my boarding pass. Breakfast was included and while the selection wasn't huge, the coffee was good and the pastries were fresh. Location is a real strong point too: walking distance to several restaurants and maybe ten minutes from the main square. Only minor gripe was some noise from the street early in the morning, but nothing earplugs couldn't fix. Would absolutely come back.

I was really excited about staying at the Amalfi after reading several reviews online. Unfortunately, it was a very disappointing experience. When we arrived, we were told that there was a mistake and the hotel was oversold. So, we had to move to another hotel. Amalfi did take care of the other hotel, cab fare, and after much negotiating...breakfast. We were traveling with 2 children and all of this was very inconvenient. Instead of getting up the next morning and going to the museum as we had planned, we had to get up, pack up our suitcases, check out of the hotel, take a cab, check back into the Amalfi, only then could we head to the museum. We were also told that our first night's stay would be refunded. Well, more than 3 weeks and 3 phone calls later...there still hasn't been a refund. I can't even get a manager to call me back. The Amalfi wasn't all bad, it is centrally located close to train and bus stops and has many restaurants within walking distance. The coctail reception had a nice selection of drinks and appetizers. However, it was in a very small room and there was no place to sit both nights we attended. One reason we picked the Amalfi was that it had 2 queen beds instead of doubles, but they seemed really small for queens. Our view from our room was of the alley. So, overall the best part of staying at the Amalfi was the night that we were sent to another hotel and had a wonderful view of the city from the 22nd floor. Very disappointing indeed!

I expected far more from Sofitel, especially at this price point. My room faced a busy avenue, and traffic noise continued well past midnight despite the windows being closed. The Wi‐Fi was frustratingly unreliable; it dropped repeatedly during a video call and was too slow to work comfortably. The bathroom looked polished at first glance, but the shower drain backed up, leaving water across the floor, and the towels felt worn. The city view from the higher floor was pleasant in daylight, though construction cranes and a neighboring building blocked much of it. Staff were polite but slow to respond when I mentioned the noise and internet issues.

The location is fine, but that's about it. Our room smelled musty, the AC rattled all night, and housekeeping never replaced the towels. Front desk was polite but shrugged off every complaint. For the price, this felt like a basic chain, not a Swissotel. Won't be back.
Staff were indifferent throughout, and the tired decor made the room feel gloomy. The cramped bathroom was poorly maintained; even our two-night stay felt far too long.
Sofitel made our weekend feel special--beautiful room, attentive staff, and a breakfast worth lingering over. The location was perfect for walking around, too.
Hotel Palmer was spotless and surprisingly quiet, with friendly staff who made check-in easy. The location was perfect for walking to dinner, and the bed was wonderfully comfortable.

Despite the prime location just off Michigan Avenue, the Knickerbocker was a huge letdown. Street noise kept me up all night, so I barely slept and the brief stay felt endless. I couldn't check out fast enough.

The dated decor and grimy bathroom tiles made this feel anything but premium, definitely not worth the premium rate. While the bed was decent, dust lined the headboard, and the worn carpet screamed for a renovation.

Room was spotless and the Wi-Fi never dropped once, which made remote work easy. Location put me minutes from everything I needed, and the free breakfast with fresh fruit and hot eggs was a solid start. No complaints.
The Talbott looked charming online, but our room was worn and noisy, with a weak shower and slow front desk service. For the price, it felt more dated than boutique.

Beautifully appointed, professionally staffed, comfortable, well-located, and elegant, with wireless internet access (plus free access in an alcove on the second floor), fitness center (a little small but fine if you use it at the right time), good energy clientele, easy access to Michigan Avenue, next door to 24-hour restaurant, 2 blocks from 2 Starbucks, elevators that are there before you get your finger off the button - they thought of everything. Will definitely return!

This comes a little late as I'm finally catching up on my reviews from the past several months:) A dear friend and I stayed at the Hyatt Regency in late October 2007 for one night while visiting a friend and her husband from out of town. This hotel is perfect, IMO. Easy check in and check out. Lovely, clean, comfortable rooms with great views of the city. I know this area pretty well and it's very convenient to many downtown Chicago attractions. We had dinner and went clubing with our friends around Division St.. We had no problems getting cabs back and forth to the Hyatt and there's even public transportation right near by but we didn't bother since we only needed cabs from and to the hotel. Parking, as is usual for Chicago, was expensive but we were able to get our car out quickly (however, we left on a Sunday morning, not exactly a high traffic time although it was a Bears homegame day, so a bit busier than usual I would think). No problems at all and the best part is that we got a rate of $100 through Hotwire, a downright steal for this area of Chicago and the quality of the hotel.

We booked Hotel Monaco for a weekend getaway based on photos of the lobby, but the reality didn't match the hype. The room was dark and cramped, with a view of a brick wall and an air conditioning unit that rattled all night. The so-called 'boutique' touches felt cheap--peeling wallpaper, stained carpet near the minibar, and a bathroom door that wouldn't close properly. Housekeeping never came until we called twice, and even then they only swapped towels. The front desk staff were polite but genuinely unhelpful when we asked for a late checkout; we got a flat 'no' with no apology. The lobby itself is impressive at first glance, but that's where the charm ends. For the price, you'd expect at least decent soundproofing--we heard every hallway conversation and elevator ding. Location is the only saving grace, but that's not enough to make up for the discomfort. I wouldn't book here again unless they renovate.

I want to issue a travel-warning to folks who might sign up for the weekend deal they offer through travelzoo from time to time: The deal says 'free breakfast' included in the price. However, what they don't tell you, is that the breakfast consists of a cup of coffee and a bisquit (or two)! Moreover, you need to ask for these 'tickets' at the lobby when you check in - they won't give them to you automatically! We stayed there over Christmas '03, and we, and I noticed several guests who bought the same package, had a rather unpleasant experience! The hotel is nice though, if you don't consider their lousy service!
One night at the Hilton was more than enough: the cramped bathroom needed updating, our view was a brick wall, and breakfast was bland and overpriced.
Two nights here felt like a week--the wifi barely loaded anything, the shower dripped all night, and breakfast was cold eggs and stale pastries. Would not stay again.

We just got back from a great weekend in Chicago and have no complaints about the Palmer House. It's very easy to get to from O'hare(the Blue line on the EL train) and then just a 2 block walk from the train station. The hotel itself is beautiful and the staff is super friendly and go out of their way to help. We booked an air/hotel package deal on Expedia. We expected to stay in a room with a full size bed but for only $45 extra per night we upgraded to the Excutive level! Best decision of the trip. We had a beautiful room with a King bed,down comforter,robes,plush towels etc...it also included a nice Continental breakfast each morning,all day snacks and beverages and a great happy hour! We took advantage of this every day. The location was great..lots of shopping along State St. and to get to the Magnificent Mile was a $5 cab ride or a 20 minute walk! We'll be back to Chicago and the Palmer House!

Great building and location, but... staff is indifferent, you have to pay for WiFi (after $300 usd/night I would expect at least free WiFi), no pool in the building and something I found really annoying is that, if you move anything from the minibar, they have sensors that automatically charge you. This is ridicoulus.The iPod dock in the room didn't work. Also, we had to move thenightstand between beds and found dirt all over. Definitely is not value for your money. You're just paying for the Hard Rock brand. I will never go back to a Hard Rock Hotel.
The Hard Rock felt worth the price, with a lively city view, spotless room, and fresh, music-inspired decor that gave the stay a fun, modern feel.

I booked a King Deluxe expecting the loyalty perks I was promised, but the front desk shrugged me off. The room's AC rattled all night, and the hallway smelled like stale smoke. Definitely not worth the $400.

The Knickerbocker was a great base for a long weekend in New York. Its location right by Times Square is busy, obviously, but incredibly convenient for the subway, Broadway, and walking almost anywhere in Midtown. Once inside, the hotel felt much calmer than the surrounding streets. Our room was comfortably sized, stylish without being overdone, and very quiet at night. The bed was excellent, and the bathroom had plenty of counter space and a strong shower. Everyone we dealt with, from the front desk to housekeeping, was friendly and quick to help when we needed restaurant suggestions. We also enjoyed a drink at St. Cloud, where the rooftop views are impressive. Rates can be high, but the service, comfort, and location made the stay feel worthwhile.

Breakfast was the first letdown of the day--cold scrambled eggs that looked like they'd been sitting out since dawn, plus coffee that tasted burnt and watery. I slept terribly, partly because the mattress sagged in the middle and partly because I could hear every footstep in the hallway, as if the walls were made of paper. The staff seemed perpetually annoyed; asking for extra towels earned me a sigh and a slow, grudging walk to the supply closet. The lobby decor hasn't been touched since the mid-2000s--faded floral carpet, wobbly armchairs, and a strange, cloying air freshener. By the second night, I just wanted to leave. For the price, you'd expect at least a decent night's rest and a smile from the front desk. This place delivered neither.

I have stayed at the Palmer a half dozen times in the past and it has been ok. The main drawbacks are the check in desk is always slow and they charge you to use the fitness center, which is truly annoying. In addition, there are so many rooms you often have to walk a hundred years to find your room once you get off the elevator. Other than that, it is a classic old hotel with some yesteryear charm. But, the room they gave me most recently was so small it was laughable. The door to the bathroom could not open as it hit the desk, and the chair to the desk could not be properly pulled out as it hit the bed. There was no room for them to put the TV in front of the bed, so they shoved it off to the side. Room 23242 makes prison cells seem roomy and I promise that no one who works there would ever put someone they know in this hovel. It should not be sold as a hotel room.
Barely slept thanks to a clunky, creaky bed, and the room felt straight out of the 90s. Bathroom had mold in the grout; my 'city view' was mostly a concrete wall. Wouldn't return.

I wanted to like Hotel Talbott because the location is convenient and the lobby looks charming, but the stay was disappointing. Check-in took forever even though there was no line, and the room felt much more worn than the photos suggested. The carpet had stains, the bathroom fan rattled all night, and the shower temperature kept swinging from lukewarm to cold. We also heard doors slamming and conversations in the hallway well past midnight. Staff were polite when we mentioned the noise, but nothing really changed. For the price, I expected cleaner facilities and a more comfortable room. It may work for a quick overnight, but I would choose somewhere else next time.

Booked two nights expecting a boutique escape, but left after one and still felt cheated. At $410 a night, this place is a masterclass in misplaced confidence. Our room's carpet had a sticky patch near the minibar, and the bathroom grout was genuinely grimy--I didn't dare use the glass shower without my flip-flops. The wifi was laughably erratic: perfect in the hallway, dead at the desk where I needed it. When I asked the front desk, they shrugged and blamed the brick walls, as if that excused a premium rate. Frankly, the stay dragged--checkout couldn't come soon enough, yet somehow it still wasn't worth the length. The lobby's nice, sure, but you're not sleeping there. Save your money.

Stunning skyline views from the room made evenings magical, and the location was perfect for exploring downtown on foot. Breakfast offered delicious, fresh options each morning, and while the decor leans classic, it feels well-maintained and elegant rather than dated.

The Sofitel was a seamless blend of French elegance and modern comfort. My room was quiet, the bed heavenly, and the staff anticipated every need--from the perfect welcome drink to the smart turndown service. A truly refined, restful stay.

When making my reservation, I made it for one of the most busiest weekends during the summer Memorial Day. The staff was able to get my family in at an affordable rate. The suites are very spacious, clean, cozy, and comfortable. Upon on arriving staff were friendly, willing to exceed expectations, and serve me with enthusiasm. The Hot Breakfast was delicious each morning. The beds are very comfortable and provided a good nights rest. I would recommend this hotel to my friends and anyone who need additional space when traveling and on a budget compared to other Chicago hotels.

I booked this hotel on Priceline for 4/13, and a week later called the hotel directly to add 4/12 to our stay. The receptionist confirmed my reservation confirmation# and gave me a lower rate for both nights for the same king suite. When we arrived at check-in, there was no record of my 4/12 reservation whatsoever. The hotel was also fully booked, leaving my tired, hungry family and I high and dry with nowhere to go. The only decent thing that happened with this whole debacle was that Lisa at the check-in desk called around to several other hotels close-by to find us a room, and seemed to be the only employee working at a very busy time of evening. We ended up at Embassy Suites for both nights and had a very pleasant experience there.

The view of the parking garage was grim, and the wi-fi dropped every few minutes, making work impossible. I slept terribly on the rock-hard mattress, and despite it being a single night, the stay felt like an eternity.

I expected more from Hotel Ambassador for the rate we paid. The room looked tired, with scuffed furniture and a bathroom that could have been cleaned more carefully. Sleep was difficult because traffic noise and loud conversations in the corridor continued well past midnight; the windows did little to block it out. We stayed only one night, yet it somehow felt longer because there was little chance to properly rest. Staff at check-in were brisk and not unfriendly, but they seemed uninterested when we mentioned the noise, offering no real solution or apology. Breakfast was average and frequently understocked. Overall, the stay did not feel remotely worth the price, and I would choose another hotel next time.
The service was impeccable from check-in to checkout, and the room was spotless with an incredibly comfortable bed. The lobby bar's old-fashioned was a perfect nightcap after a long day.

First, several day s prior to my stay, I called and spoke at length with the concierge and made a breakfast order for room-service Saturday and Sunday. Saturday they didn't bring breakfast - and when I called room-service they stated they never got the advance order from the concierge. When they finally did bring it - they brought the wrong thing.. and then brought the wrong order again on Sunday. I was further inconvenienced by in-room dining staff when we ordered room service Saturday night. The food was limp and uninspired. Further, I ordered soup - which arrived without a spoon. When I called in-room dining to request a spoon, I was told one would be forthcoming. 15 minutes later, a waiter arrived with a menu. When I explained I already had food and I didn't need a menu - I needed a spoon, he had the audacity to argue with me. I respectfully requested he return with a spoon and he agreed to do so. Another 15 minutes (and one bowl of cold soup) later I decided to call in-room dining back to request (again) they send someone with a spoon. They too argued with me and expressed that they'd already sent someone with a spoon. I explained that they had not - that I had received a menu I didn't request, but that no spoon was forthcoming. Another 15 minutes later, a spoon finally arrived. Thanks - for charging me $100+ so that I could argue over cold, flavorless food. In addition to the gross customer service, surly attitude, and sorry food, I found the room woefully lacking. It reeked exhaust fumes so much so that on Saturday night I woke up from the smell. Further, I had specifically requested when I booked the reservation that you keep me away from the elevators... I was right next to the elevators and had the displeasure of listening to them ding all night long as other guests came and went.

I had a very pleasant stay at the Sheraton and would happily return. My room was clean, spacious, and thoughtfully arranged, with a comfortable bed that made it easy to sleep well after a busy day. Despite being in a lively area, the room was surprisingly quiet at night; I only heard a little hallway activity in the morning. Breakfast offered a good variety, including fresh fruit, pastries, eggs, cereal, and made-to-order coffee. Everything was replenished promptly, although the dining area became busy during peak hours. The location was especially convenient, with restaurants, shops, and public transportation just a short walk away. The staff were friendly and efficient throughout my visit, from check-in to checkout, and made the whole experience feel smooth and welcoming.
Disappointing stay at the Fairmont: breakfast was bland and overpriced, hallway noise carried late into the room, the bathroom felt dated, and my window faced a dull service area.

I'm a frequent business traveler and often in Chicago on trips. At times, it's very difficult to even find a hotel in downtown Chicago, and this was one of those times. I recently had to pay almost $400 for one night at the Allegro. It was absolutely not worth it. The hotel was filled to capacity with conventioneers, so check-in and check-out were very slow. There were very few elevators, which were worked beyond capacity with all the guests. The morning I checked out, our elevator stopped at every single floor from the 16th floor down to the lobby, but the elevator was almost completely full when I got on at the 18th floor, so I can only imagine how long it must have taken other guests to get downstairs. The room was extremely small and cramped, even though it had obviously been renovated recently. The TV, bed, and decor were all new and were the high points of the hotel. Still, the rate was way overpriced for such a small room. The best thing about the Allegro was the room service, which was prompt. The food was good, and the prices were very reasonable for room service. From now on, if my regular hotels are booked, I'll just take a cab farther out from the city because it just isn't worth it.

Charming boutique hotel with impeccable service--the staff remembered our names and the rooftop bar had stunning city views. Room was quiet, cozy, and spotless. Breakfast was fresh and delicious. Would absolutely return.

Fairmont is one of those places where everything just works, which sounds simple but is actually rare. The lobby has that grand, old-school elegance without feeling stuffy, and check-in was smooth even though we arrived early. They stored our luggage and texted us the moment our room was ready, which was a nice touch. Our room overlooked the lake, and the bed was genuinely comfortable--not too soft, not too firm. I also have to call out the concierge desk; they booked us a last-minute reservation at a place that was supposedly fully booked, and gave us a walking route that avoided the touristy crowds. The pool area was a bit busy in the afternoon, but it cleared out by evening. Minor gripe: the hallway ice machine on our floor was out of order, but someone brought ice up within ten minutes of us asking. That kind of response makes up for a lot. Already looking forward to coming back.

The room smelled musty and the AC rattled all night, so I barely slept. Staff were polite but shrugged off the issues, and the breakfast was cold and picked over by 8 AM. Really disappointed for what we paid.

This is a wonderful hotel with all the amenities. Everyone was helpful. The breakfast buffet was wonderful. The bed was 'just like home'. We would definitely stay again. A nice touch was the water bottles left in our car for us to enjoy on our way home. It was little touches like this that make this hotel one of the best.

Over-hyped and over-priced. The fact that they have a complimentary wine reception every night at 5 doesnt take away from the fact that they have terrible beds and the place isnt as clean as it should be for a 4 star hotel. The hallways smelled like a dog parlor and the carpets in my room look like they hadn't been cleaned...well, ever. The decorative pillows on my bed were so filthy they were actually stained brown and looked like they had been sitting outside for everyone to use and then put back on my bed. The decor of the hotel was nice and eclectic but it wasnt enough to convince me to ever stay here again. The bed was the most uncomfortable thing I have every tried to sleep on. I couldnt sleep the whole week that I stayed there. It was hard and lumpy and the pillows were tiny. my final say is that it is an over priced Holiday Inn.....

If I didn't have to stay here, I wouldn't. Without exception, I swear I am not lying, every day of my stay brings a new problem. Over the past 3 months, I have stayed here 6 times for 3 nights at a time; problems every time. From the wrong food with room service, to room keys that dont work, unrefreshed bath towels, forgotten and dirty in-room coffee service, unclean ice bucket overnight, forgotten room cleaning, inability to connect to the Internet....I'm too tired to keep writing all the problems. For the price of this chi-chi downtown hotel, I expect more. Finally, their team is certainly not trained in customer service. The front desk teams have attitudes, and Aria's hostesses think they are something else. I'm stuck using this hotel since it is adjoined to Aon, but I would never go back if I had a choice. The only good thing is the food at Aria - outstanding.

I wanted to like Hotel Monaco because the lobby is charming and the location is convenient, but the stay was frustrating from the start. Our room wasn't ready at check-in, and when we finally got keys, the bathroom had hair on the floor and the air conditioner barely worked. The room felt tired, with scuffed furniture and curtains that didn't fully close, so street noise and early morning light were unavoidable. We called twice about the AC and were told someone would come up, but nobody did. Breakfast was overpriced for cold eggs and weak coffee. Staff at the desk were polite, though they seemed overwhelmed and offered little beyond apologies. For the rate we paid, I expected a cleaner room and better follow-through.

We had a wonderful four-night stay at Hotel Amalfi in early September. The location was ideal, tucked on a quiet side street yet just a two-minute stroll to the bustling promenade and beach. Our sea-view room was spotless, with a comfortable bed and a balcony perfect for watching the sunset with a glass of local wine. The staff truly made the difference--everyone from the front desk to the breakfast servers was genuinely warm and helpful, offering great tips for avoiding the crowds. The breakfast spread was ample, with fresh pastries and excellent cappuccino. While the rooms are a bit dated and the walls slightly thin, we slept well. Overall, it offered fantastic value for the area. We would happily return.
The Intercontinental looked impressive online, but my room was tired, the air conditioning barely worked, and staff took ages to respond. For the price, I expected much better.

Wish we'd booked a third night -- two just weren't enough to soak up the Hotel James. Our corner room on the eighth floor gave us a sweeping, postcard-perfect view of the harbor lights twinkling at dusk, which made the short commute to the ferry terminal feel almost like a scenic prologue to our day trips. The staff, from the front desk to the housekeeping crew, were genuinely warm, remembering our names by the second morning and even suggesting a hidden tapas spot that became a highlight. Location-wise, you're smack in the middle of everything -- we walked to the old town in ten minutes and grabbed late-night coffee across the street without hassle. The bed was heavenly, the breakfast spread generous. Honestly, the only downside was having to pack up and leave. We'll be back, longer next time, for sure.

Booked a 'Deluxe King' here based on the historic photos, but the reality fell flat. The room smelled musty, and the carpet had visible stains near the baseboards. The bathroom sink was chipped, and the grout looked like it hadn't been scrubbed in months. For the $340 a night I paid, this felt like a $120 motel experience, only with fancier lobby decor and a lot more noise. My window faced the courtyard, but the ventilation unit clanked all night, and I could hear every footstep from the floor above until after 1 AM. The furniture--orange velvet chair and a laminate desk--felt like a 1990s time capsule, not charmingly vintage. The only modern touch was a cheap tablet on the nightstand with a glaring 'Welcome' screen. Service was pleasant, but honestly, I'd rather have saved my money and stayed somewhere clean. I checked out a day early.

We stayed at the Omni for a long weekend and honestly expected much more for the price. Check-in took forever because they apparently had no record of our reservation, even though I had the confirmation email on my phone. The front desk staff weren't rude exactly, just completely indifferent. Our room smelled vaguely of smoke even though it was supposed to be non-smoking, and the air conditioner rattled all night like it was about to take off. The bed was okay, but the bathroom had visible grime in the corners and hair in the tub, which is just unacceptable. Room service took over an hour and arrived lukewarm. The location is convenient, I'll give it that, but with all the other hotels in the area, I won't be back. Truly disappointing for a place with this reputation.
Great value for the price--the bed was cloud-like, and I slept better than at home. Wi-Fi never dropped, perfect for a work trip. My only regret: a one-night stay felt far too short.

The bathroom had excellent water pressure and plush towels, and the room was spotless when I arrived. Breakfast's fresh pastries hit the spot, and the wifi stayed fast for video calls throughout my stay.

We just returned from a girls shopping /sight-seeing trip.The Palmer House was like home away from home.The hotel is undergoing renovations but we did not notice any inconveniences or hear any noise from the work.The lobby was breathtaking, all dressed up for Christmas.The staff from check-in to housekeeping was very welcoming and friendly.Our room was updated with two beds and two separate baths which was great for everyone to have their own personal space.I would not hesitate to recommend this hotel to anyone.Chicago is a great town.

I had a very pleasant three-night stay at the Ambassador. The building has some old-school character, but the room itself was comfortable, quiet, and well maintained. My bed was especially good, and I appreciated having plenty of outlets and a small desk since I had some work to finish. Everyone I dealt with, from the front desk to housekeeping, was friendly without being overbearing. Check-in was quick, and they happily stored my bags on the final day. The neighborhood was another highlight, with restaurants, coffee shops, and transit all within an easy walk. The only minor issue was that the bathroom felt a little dated, though it was spotless and had good water pressure. Overall, it was a relaxed, convenient stay, and I would gladly book the Ambassador again.

Booked a king room expecting Hilton standards, but the air conditioning rattled all night, the hallway smelled like old carpet, and the front desk seemed annoyed by every question. For the price, I've had better stays at mid-range motels. Won't be returning.

While it was a nice hotel, but i am rather frustrated with them! During our stay our room was cleaned twice by housekeeping. The first day was fine. Second day my diamond earrings came up missing. Noticed they were missing while in the packing up and checking out process. My biggest mistake was not staying there and dealing with this further. But we had a family reunion and funeral to get to. While the front desk was great and said they would handle it, I believe they say these things just to get you to go on about your way! We filed a police report and the GM of the hotel is supposed to be working on it. We have called several times but receive no answers. They keep telling us the cleaning staff have been there 10 + years.....that dosen't matter to me! If they are not held accountable what's to stop them from taking anything. There is a dishwasher in the room, and they found my daughters ring (which was in the same glass with my diamond earrings) in the dishwasher. They say I put the cup in the dishwasher. First, I am on vacation, trust me i'm NOT doing dishes! Second, why would I wash one glass and leave the other dirty dishes in the room? So, while it is a nice hotel....lock up your things of value! They may come up 'missing' and you'll be left frustrated!!

Before booking this hotel, I did read the reviews, and I was concerned. I ended up booking it based on my sisters recommendation. BIG MISTAKE!! The temperature in Chicago was a balmy 99 degrees, and the temp in the room that they gave us was about 85 degrees. When we called to complain at 11:00 am, they told us to turn the temp down to 40degrees. We went back at 7:30pm. it was still humid, the beds were moist & the room very stuffy. Called again, they sent somone to fix it, & he recommended getting a new room, because the room will not cool down. They told us they were booked, yet, after the maintenance man called, they suddenly had a room available, go figure? So they move us to another room, guess what, it is 85 degrees. Again, they told us to turn it down to 40, needless to say, it never cooled down & we should have just slept on the street. We travel a lot, and we stayed here one night, and it was awful!!. At check out, I had to re-tell our entire room issue, they actually ended up not charging us for the night, thank god they did not offer us anothers nights stay, because we would never go back. Also, the room decor is very old and stuffy. If your going to Chicago, don't stay at the Millenium Knickerbocker!!

We stayed two nights. We were registered by a very unfriendly desk attendant. He was very cold. Our room was very, very small and the closet did not even hold the few clothes we packed for two days. The room was stylishly decorated but lacked the nice small touches such as an extra pillow in the closet. We were attracted to this hotel because a bar was on the ground level - however when we went to have a drink, the door to the bar was locked. We called to inquire why the sign said was open when it really wasn't and were told they were short staffed, 'sorry'. WHAT?? are you running here? You are a hotel in the country's third largest city and your amenities are open at whim? This was our first and last visit to a Kimpton hotel.

My stay at Hotel Palmer was disappointing from start to finish. Check-in took nearly 25 minutes even though the lobby was quiet, and the front desk staff seemed more interested in their phones than helping guests. The room looked tired, with stained carpet, scuffed furniture, and a bathroom fan that rattled loudly all night. Housekeeping also forgot to replace the towels on the second day, and I had to call twice before anyone came up. The bed was reasonably comfortable, but the thin walls meant I could hear conversations and doors slamming in the hallway until after midnight. Breakfast was overpriced for the limited, lukewarm options. The location is convenient, but that alone didn't justify the rate. I expected a much better-maintained and more attentive experience.

I had a very comfortable two-night stay at the Omni. My room faced the park, and the view was especially nice in the morning, with plenty of trees and city buildings in the distance. Despite being downtown, it was surprisingly quiet at night; I only heard a little hallway noise once, and the windows seemed to block traffic well. The bed was supportive, the sheets felt fresh, and I slept better than expected after a long day of walking around. The bathroom was clean and roomy enough to get ready without bumping into everything, with good water pressure and plenty of towels. Staff were friendly during check-in and quick to answer a couple of questions. The location made restaurants and shopping easy to reach, so I would happily stay here again.
My stay at The Talbott felt a little too short; breakfast was fresh and satisfying, the central location made exploring easy, and the quiet, comfortable room gave me an excellent night's sleep.

Hotel Allegro made for a very pleasant stay. My room looked out over the river and the surrounding city buildings, especially pretty in the evening when the lights came on. Everything was spotless on arrival, from the bathroom tiles to the fresh linens, and housekeeping kept it that way during my visit. The bed was genuinely comfortable, with good pillows and little noise from the hallway, so I slept deeply each night. Staff members were friendly without being overbearing; the front desk gave useful restaurant suggestions and quickly helped when I needed an extra towel. I would happily stay here again.

The James Hotel met and exceeded our expectations. A haven of cool, uncluttered comfort in a hot, crowded but congenial city. Located within steps of some of the greatest art, architecture, culinary and cultural opportunities anywhere in North America, the staff of the James provided us with a home away from home for the week we visited. The check-in was quick and flawless and the king suite a calm, restorative oasis. It is difficult to over-praise the friendly, attentive staff; this is a hotel that truly has its act together! The day before our visit ended, we experienced problems with the room's air conditioner. When the technician was unable to quickly solve the problem, we were immediately upgraded to a one-bedroom apartment with stunning views of the Chicago skyline. We eagerly await the opening of new James Hotels in other cities.

We stayed at the Swissotel for four nights last month, and while it's not cheap, I genuinely felt we got our money's worth given the location and the quality of everything. Our room was on a higher floor and the view over the city at sunset was absolutely stunning--we found ourselves just sitting by the window with coffee every evening. What really stood out, though, was the staff. Check-in was smooth, and when we asked for a late checkout the front desk handled it graciously without any hassle. The breakfast team remembered our preferences by the second morning, which felt like a nice personal touch. Wifi was fast and reliable throughout, even during a video call I had to take one afternoon. Would happily return.

I had such high hopes for the Fairmont given its reputation, but our stay last week was a real letdown. Check-in took nearly forty minutes because apparently they were short-staffed, and no one apologized. The room itself was worn out - stains on the carpet, a bathroom door that wouldn't close properly, and the air conditioning rattled all night. Housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely, and when we called about it, they brought towels hours later but never actually cleaned. Room service arrived cold twice, and the breakfast buffet was overpriced for what it offered. The concierge gave us wrong directions twice, sending us across town unnecessarily. For a hotel at this price point, staff should be attentive and the rooms spotless. Honestly, it felt like a three-star property charging five-star rates. We won't be back.

My husband and I wanted to spend the weekend in Chicago to celebrate our anniversary, and I had been looking at the James for awhile because it was attached to David Burke's Primehouse. From the moment I called to make my reservation, I knew this hotel understood what customer service means to a consumer and a picky one at that. From the pre-arrival dossier, to the special sweets from the staff to kick off our anniversary weekend and a hand written note thanking us for staying at the James, this staff is well versed in the long lost art of customer service. The rooms were well appointed and the beds comfy and warm on a cool weekend. The walking distance to Michigan Av is a huge plus. From the front desk to the cleaning staff, the staff here is top notch! And David Burke's Primehouse is not to be missed!

We booked this hotel for the second leg of our Chicago stay..it was great!!!! The Lion King package was pricey but reasonable, given the ticket costs and the Suite. Room was great....classical music greeted us when we entered our room after a long day of sightseeing and shopping. NYTimes and Chicago Tribune at your door every morning. One block from the Washington El train station. We never saw the small rooms that every one apparently doesn't like, but the Suite rooms were fun and our kids loved it. Dunkin Doughnuts and Corner Bakery down the block. City Hall, Picasso structure....this was a great place. Book it and also use the Golden Touch Limo service...reasonable. Omar is a super guy.

I loved the vibe at Hotel Monaco--quirky yet polished, with a killer corner room overlooking the park. Staff were genuinely friendly, not fake-cheerful, and the evening wine hour felt like a nice bonus after a long day.

I had a very comfortable three-night stay at the Intercontinental. The building has plenty of character, especially the historic details in the lobby, but the rooms still feel bright and well maintained. My room was quiet, with a genuinely comfortable bed, a useful desk, and a bathroom that had good water pressure and more than enough space for my things. Everyone I dealt with was courteous, from check-in to the concierge, and requests were handled quickly without making me chase anyone. The location was convenient for getting around, with restaurants and shops within easy walking distance. I also appreciated the well-equipped fitness room, which was open early enough for my schedule. It is not the cheapest option, but the service and overall comfort made it feel worthwhile.

Beautiful hotel, but doesn't have a lot to offer for the price. Sheets and pillowcases in the room had stains on them, TV remote would not function properly. Valet service truly needs improvement. We payed quite a bit for overnight parking, and it took them almost an hour to bring our car to us when we needed to leave. When we asked to find out what was taking so long, we got tossed back and forth between bell hop and front desk, with no answers.

Loved how close the Knickerbocker is to everything, yet the rooms stay quiet and cozy. The rooftop bar's a nice bonus after a long day, and the staff actually remembered my coffee order each morning. Would happily book again.
Hyatt's decor felt dated, hallway noise carried late into the night, and despite only staying one evening, it felt longer because I barely slept.

We stayed here because of the enthusiastic positive reviews on Trip Advisor and Yelp.
