We might have had a one in a million experience, but we: - were served a hairy salad (a long black hair held a lettuce leaf hostage); - considered our guest room tiny; - could not submerge a thigh, much less a body, in the tub (we're not obese and we're not Dexter); - endured a broken air conditioner for days (it couldn't be repaired); - experienced the delight of an inexplicably broken toilet (they fixed it that day). On a positive note, the tea from room service tasted delicious, employees were abundant and friendly, the location is great, and it's very easy to get a taxi. In the future, I would reluctantly stay here for business. I would not stay here for pleasure. I think a 20-something who hasn't traveled much would appreciate this hotel more than a seasoned traveler would...as a friend said to me today, 'Oh, the Sofitel? That's the Hilton of France.' I agree.

I was attending a training conference in Chicago and opted to book my own room thru one of the online discount programs rather than stay at the rather sterile and pedestrian hotel where the conference was being held. I booked 4 nights at the Intercontinental and was pleased with the elegance and convenient location (an easy walk to the conference). From the lobby to the rooms, this hotel lives up to it's storied reputation. (The indoor pool seems to be imported from the set of a Busby Berkeley movie!) And even tho' I was there for a conference, the hotel's location on the Mag Mile and a quick jaunt to restaurants and theaters, made for a very pleasant stay at a very affordable price.

Sleek, modern decor and a genuinely comfortable bed made for a great stay at the Swissotel. Wifi was fast and reliable, sleep was solid on the quiet floors, and overall it felt well worth the price. Would happily return.
Had a really comfortable stay at the Talbott--the room was quiet, the bed was excellent, and everyone at the front desk was genuinely helpful. Great location for exploring Chicago on foot.

I really wanted to like the Hotel Ambassador, but our anniversary weekend fell flat. The lobby's plastic plants and stained carpet set the tone; our room followed suit with floral drapes from another decade and a radiator that clanked all night. We paid extra for a 'city view,' which was mostly a brick wall and a sliver of rooftop. The staff were polite but indifferent--at check-in we were handed keys without a smile or a single recommendation, and housekeeping never replaced our empty coffee pods. The bathroom was the worst part: a cracked tub with poor water pressure, a loose faucet, and a hairdryer that died mid-use. The bed was comfortable, I'll give them that, but the peeling wallpaper and gum under the desk made us eager to leave. For these prices, you can do much better.

I really wanted to like this place, but the Omni left me feeling cheated. The location is fine, but the room felt tired and the A/C unit sounded like a lawnmower all night; I got maybe three hours of sleep. The bathroom had a lingering musty smell and the caulking was peeling. I tried to grab a late bite at the bar, but the bartender ignored me for ten minutes and then served a lukewarm, overpriced cocktail. When I mentioned the noise at checkout, the front desk agent just shrugged and said, 'That's how it is.' For the rates they charge, I expected so much more. It's a shame--the lobby is beautiful, but that's where the polish ends. Definitely won't be back.
Disappointing stay overall. Rooms felt tired and dated, the AC barely worked, and staff were indifferent when we raised it. For the price, expected far better from a hotel in such a great location.
Hotel Monaco's spotless bathroom had great water pressure, the room stayed pleasantly quiet, Wi-Fi was reliable, and the cozy bed gave me one of my best hotel sleeps.

We stayed at the Hard Rock for one night to do some intense, day-after-Thanksgiving shopping. It really is a great hotel. The rooms are really cool, and we were just in the basic one. The bed is extremely comfortable, with the softest sheets and great pillows. The technology in the room is great. They have nice upscale tolietries in the bathrooms. For a very modern room, it is still comfortable and homey. The location is perfect for getting wherever you want to go. The staff were very nice and helpful. The bar is really funky with an interesting martini menu. One of the best hotels I have stayed at in Chicago. Really enjoyed it and would highly recommend.

Review's a little late, but... My husband & I first stayed at the Amalfi in 8/06 totally based on reviews I read on this website. We were totally WOWED!! Loved the location, the room, the Aveda bath products, but most of all loved the evening reception & breakfast on our floor. I returned to Chicago with 3 girlfriends in 9/07 and booked us in a suite at the Amalfi. It was great - room was very spacious and my girlfriends were quite pleased! Will stay next time I'm in Chicago too!! P.S. They honor a government rate!!!!

My stay at the Sheraton was much more disappointing than expected. The lobby looked polished, but the room felt tired, with scuffed furniture, stained carpet, and a bathroom fan that rattled all night. Check-in took nearly 25 minutes even though there was only one person ahead of me, and the staff seemed more distracted than welcoming. Wi-Fi was unreliable, cutting out during a work call, and housekeeping skipped my room until late afternoon despite putting out the service sign. Breakfast was overpriced for lukewarm eggs, dry pastries, and slow coffee service. I also had to call twice to get extra towels delivered. The location was convenient, but the high rate simply did not match the condition or level of service. I expected the Sheraton standard to be far better.

My stay at Swissotel was far below what I expected from a hotel of this reputation. The lobby looked impressive, but the room felt tired, with scuffed furniture, a stained carpet, and an air conditioner that rattled through the night. Housekeeping also missed the basics; there were no fresh towels when I returned in the evening, and I had to call twice before someone brought them. Breakfast was crowded and disorganized, with empty serving trays and lukewarm food. Staff were polite enough, but responses were slow and nobody seemed eager to take responsibility when I raised these issues. The location was convenient, which was the main positive, but it did not make up for the poor maintenance and inattentive service. Overall, it felt overpriced and disappointing.

Dispite what other are saying, this was one, if not the best Hotel stay in Chicago I have had. I travel to the Big City about three times a year for pleasure and The James rates up with the best. I was upgraded and the staff made the stay worth my special weekend visit. I don't believe you will be disapointed.

The bathroom was spotless with excellent water pressure, though the dated floral tile felt a bit tired. My room stayed blissfully quiet all night, and the crisp, fresh linens made the clean space feel truly inviting.

We stayed at the Conrad for 2 nights for a friends reunion. The room was clean and new feeling, nice city view, free bottled water in room upon arrival. Check in was a breeze, and our room was ready even though we were several hours early. All staff was friendly and helpful, excellent breakfast.
Our corner room stayed remarkably quiet, with a lovely skyline view at sunset. The clean, well-lit bathroom had a generous shower, and our weekend ended far too soon.

We had a king deluxe room for 2 nights. We reserved the room through the hotel website with AAA discount. We paid $180/nt. We enjoy boutique hotels, as they have so much more personality and personal service. This hotel was no exception. Every employee we encountered was pleasant and helpful. The room was clean, well decorated, spacious and quiet. We were offered at check-in a room with a view, but warned it was across from the elevator, so we decided to take the quiet, large room with no view. The location of the hotel was perfect for us, we saw Wicked while in Chicago and had no problem walking to the theater. We also walked the Magnificient Mile and found the location perfect (we like to walk). We had drinks at the hotel restaurant both nights which was a pleasurable experience. We ate room service for breakfast each morning, and the food was good and the portions were quite large. We would definitely stay here again.

We stayed for a one night getaway with family on a thursday. Triple AAA rate of 173 was a steal. 7th floor room complete with 44in plasma TV bose stereo, voss and evian water, and gorgeous bathroom(no tub but was fine for us) Concierge was very helpful. You cannot beat this location... Only flaw was breakfast was pricey and service was very very slow(2hours for four kids and four adults on a friday morning) even though there were only two other tables in the restaurant. Food was very good so it was worth the wait. I would return in a heartbeat. A gem in chicago...

I had a very pleasant stay at the Talbott and felt the price was justified, especially given the excellent location and attentive service. My room was comfortable, quiet, and noticeably clean, with a cozy design that felt more classic than dated. The furnishings had some traditional touches, but everything was well maintained and still looked fresh. Breakfast was a highlight: the menu had a good range of hot and lighter options, the coffee was reliably strong, and service was quick without feeling rushed. Wi-Fi worked consistently throughout the room and lobby, which made catching up on work easy. The staff were welcoming and helpful with restaurant suggestions and directions. Overall, the Talbott offered a relaxed, polished experience, and I would happily stay there again.
The Knickerbocker looked impressive online, but my room was cramped, street noise never let up, and housekeeping skipped us entirely for two days.
The Sofitel looked impressive online, but my room felt tired, the air-conditioning barely worked, and service was oddly slow. For the price, I expected a far more comfortable stay.

We had a fantastic stay at the Fairmont. The room was beautifully appointed with a super comfortable bed and a stunning view of the mountains. I was a bit worried about it being too formal, but the staff were so warm and welcoming, especially the concierge who helped us plan a last-minute hike. The breakfast buffet was a splurge but worth it for the sheer variety, from fresh pastries to made-to-order omelets. The pool area was a bit crowded in the afternoon, but we found it quiet in the early morning. Our only minor hiccup was a slow drain in the shower, but maintenance fixed it within twenty minutes of us calling. Overall, it was a classy and relaxing getaway that exceeded our expectations. We'd absolutely come back.

Stayed here for 3 nights for a Bridgestone/Firestone convention. No complaints. Room was great with a beautiful view. Staff was very accommodating. Had drinks and appetizers in main bar. Fantastic! Great location. Yes it's a huge hotel as it's used for conventions but that didn't stop it from being a great place.

My boyfriend and I were amazed by the breathtaking view of Lake Michigan! We are from Texas so the view of the city was very important to us. We had no problems at this hotel... rooms, service, location were top notch.
The Palmer turned out to be the perfect base for our weekend--the lobby is grand without feeling stuffy, and our room was spotless with a shockingly comfy bed.

I stayed here 2 nights for a business conference. The food was pretty good. And they had these really good mints that I couldn't resist. The room was very comfortable and the bed was great. But I was annoyed by many issues. First, their internet went down for a couple of hour when I was there on a break from the conference. It wouldn't have been big deal except I needed to do some business while it was down. Second, the internet wasn't available in the conference rooms. I suppose the conference I attended would have had to pay extra for it. Third, The chair in the room was too low for the desk so I was in an awkward position while using my computer which gave me a back ache later. Fourth, on the second night my key didn't work. So I asked for a new one which also didn't work. So I asked for another one and the same thing happened. Thankfully the front desk asked a security guy to meet me up at my room so I didn't have to go back down to the lobby a third time. Then he came back a little later to tell me I was in the wrong room, which I wasn't. Finally, he came back with the right key. Fifth, the TV had one remote control for changing the channels and a different one for the volume. Sixth, they didn't have the comedy channel. Much cheaper hotels do. If this hotel didn't cost so much money all of these things would be minor inconveniences, but I would expect more for what I paid.

The location is unbeatable, but that's where the positives end. The hallways felt musty, the room decor was stuck in the 1980s, and we could hear every door slam until 2 a.m. Staff seemed rushed and utterly indifferent when we asked for a quieter floor change.

Honestly pretty underwhelmed by the Hotel Ambassador. The room smelled musty, the AC rattled all night, and front desk barely acknowledged us at check-in. For what we paid, expected way more. Won't be back.

The sheraton was a wonderful hotel! When me and my mom flew in we were really tired so we decided to take a quick nap. We didnt want to get up! The beds are absolutely to die for. I wanted to take it home with me. The service was great and this was probably one of the biggest if not the biggest hotel ive ever stayed in. They had a really nice restaurant inside with excellent food.

I expected much more from the Conrad, especially given the price, but the stay was a real disappointment. Check-in took nearly 25 minutes, and the receptionist seemed rushed and uninterested. Our room looked tired, with scuffed furniture, a stained armchair, and a bathroom fan that rattled loudly all night. Housekeeping also skipped our room until late afternoon, despite the 'Please make up room' sign being displayed. Breakfast was another letdown: crowded tables, slow service, and food that was barely warm. The pool area was attractive in the photos, but several loungers were broken and the water looked cloudy. Staff did apologize when we complained, but nothing meaningful was offered. The location is convenient, yet it does not justify the high rates. I left feeling the hotel relies on its name rather than delivering a genuinely polished experience.
Loved the stylish rooms and friendly front desk team at the hotel james. The location made exploring easy, and the rooftop drinks were a perfect way to end the day.

We stayed at the Conrad for only one evening but it was such an amazing room we would have liked to stay longer! We were on the newly renovated 9th floor and the room was gorgeous and super clean! There was a flat screen, bose sound system and even an Ihome for our Ipod. Wireless was free and they bring you a free bottle of water at turn down. Everyone was very helpful and so friendly. We can't wait to go back again!

I had a genuinely lovely stay at Sofitel. From the moment I arrived, the staff were warm without being overly formal, and check-in was quick even though the lobby was busy. My room felt polished and comfortable, with a very good bed, crisp linens, and a quiet view that made it easy to unwind after a long day. The bathroom was especially nice, with quality toiletries and strong water pressure. Breakfast had plenty of choice, including fresh pastries, fruit, and made-to-order eggs. I also appreciated how attentive the concierge was when recommending nearby restaurants. The hotel feels elegant but still relaxed, and every interaction left a good impression. I would happily return.

Hotel Monaco was a great choice for a weekend downtown. The lobby has so much character without feeling stuffy, and the front desk team were genuinely warm when we arrived late Friday night. Our room was clean, quiet, and surprisingly spacious, with a comfortable bed and nice little touches like good coffee and plush robes. We walked to restaurants, shops, and the theater, which made the location especially convenient. Breakfast was not included, but the cafe nearby had plenty of options. The only minor issue was that the elevator took a little while during the morning rush. Otherwise, everything felt polished and easy, and I would happily stay here again.

The view from our 14th-floor window overlooked the river and downtown skyline--gorgeous at sunset. The bathroom was spotless with a rainfall shower, and despite being near the elevator, we rarely heard a peep. Wi‐Fi worked flawlessly for streaming and video calls.

The air conditioning barely worked, the hallway smelled like stale smoke, and housekeeping never once replaced our towels. For these prices, I expected far better. Left feeling completely underwhelmed and exhausted.

What a wonderful experience, super great, helpful, friendly staff. Angie at the front desk made sure my husbands birthday would be great. Our room was beautiful. Angie suggested we go to Sullivans for dinner..perfect choice, make the reservation for us.(best seat in the house and a special dessert) wow...Above and beyond what any other hotel or staff has done for us before..Looking forward to staying there again & again. THANKS AGAIN

My husband and i made a reservation for 2sure nights but decided to stay just the second night. I called the hotel and spoke with Eric, he quickly canceled my reservation and i asked if we would be charged for thd cancellation, he said no and that was the end of it. My husband then remembered we needed to cancel from bookit.com as well. I called and they said the hotel wouldnt authorize a cancellation per the terms and agreement. I informed courtney from bookit.com that i specifically asked if we would be charged and i was told no by Eric. She spoke with the mgr Erica and she said Erica would honor that if i could provide a name. I got his name and callex back and he told the bookit consultant that he 'didnt recall' saying that. I was so furious that i called him on 3the way with the bookit consultant and he just lied!!!!!!!!!!! He said, no ma'am i dont remember saying that. I said so since you dont remember thats it??? I said my husband heard him say it b/c he was on speaker phone since we were driving on the way there. I asked to speak to Erica, told her the situation and she said she cant go off of heresay and couldnt honor what her employee screwed up on. I asked him nicely to please tell the truth and he just would not tell thr truth. I have never writte. A review for a hotel before but i am going to go out of my way to make sure corporate sees this. Erica was very unprofessional and cared more about not taking sides than she did about making sure the guests feel welcome. VERY DISAPPOINTED!! WILL NEVER STAY AGAIN!!

I really expected more from a Hilton, honestly. We arrived around 3pm and our room still wasn't ready, then we stood waiting another 40 minutes with no apology or explanation. When we finally got in, the carpet had stains near the window and the AC unit rattled all night, so sleep was basically out of the question. The front desk staff varied wildly -- one woman was pleasant, but the guy on the night shift acted like asking for extra towels was a huge inconvenience. Breakfast cost $28 per person and the eggs were rubbery, the coffee barely lukewarm. Housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely and I had to call twice to get it sorted. The location is convenient, I'll give it that, but for nearly $300 a night I couldn't wait to check out. Won't be rushing back.

i valeted my lexus and it was returned with a smashed side mirror. They admitted it was their fault, and now they won't pay the $500 to fix it because we can't prove it was not broken before!!! the hotel is wonderful, the rooms are new and nice, but we will never stay here again because of this....Be sure to inspect your car before you leave!
Hotel Monaco was a fun surprise--our room was spotless, the bed was wonderfully comfortable, and the front desk gave us great dinner tips. The central location made walking around easy.

My husband and I stayed at the Hotel Allegro in March, 2006. We had a great time! We were upgraded to a suite, and enjoyed the jacuzzi tub with Mr. Bubbles, animal print robes, and a luxurious king- sized bed! THe suite was very nice, and we had no problem with noise from other rooms or from the street. It was very boutiquey, and the lobby was lovely. We enjoyed the complementary wine hour. The staff was attentive, and our stay in this Kimpton hotel made our first-time trip to Chicago memorable! We would return here!

I have stayed in the Talbott a few times and had always liked it. This time was my first visit in 2 years and I was disappointed. The hallways are now looking tired and the carpets need to be replaced. I had asked for a corner room but instead was given a small and very dark room looking out onto a wall 10 feet away with multiple noisy vents immediately outside the window. The lights had to be kept on throughout the day even through the days were bright. The bathroom was tiny and would be difficult to manage with 2 people in the room. The AC unit rumbled on permanently with background white noise even when switched off. Having stayed there before I know there are better rooms but this one was the same price as the others I have been in and the risk is getting it again. Other small things contributed - the lobby brownies are no longer, there were no cup lids for the lobby coffee (so you couldn't walk out with the coffee) and I got a newspaper only on the last morning of a 5-night stay. The construction noise was not too bad but does start at 7.30am and goes on until around 8pm, including weekends.

We stayed at the Affinia for a long weekend and it turned out to be one of the better hotel experiences we've had in the city. Our room was huge for downtown, with a separate seating area and a kitchenette that came in handy for late-night snacks. The bed was genuinely comfortable, which matters a lot to me since I usually sleep badly in hotels. What really stood out was the staff, though. When our heating wasn't working right the first evening, someone came up within ten minutes and fixed it, and the front desk called later just to confirm everything was okay. That kind of follow-through is rare. Location is convenient too, easy walk to Michigan Avenue and plenty of restaurants nearby. Not fancy in a pretentious way, just solid, comfortable, and well run. We'd absolutely come back.

I made reservations with the Chicago Fitzpatrick using their 800 number for two nights in June. I received no written confirmation with cancelation policy, etc. However, when I attempted to cancel my reservation the morning of my first night's reservation, I was told that they would charge me for one nights stay. They have a '3pm THE DAY BEFORE your first nights stay' policy. Even though the hotel was not sold out for the night they would not budge on the policy. This is not a common policy on Michigan Ave. I'd advise making your reservations someplace that offers more flexiblity for emergencies or sends a written confirmation with policy. It was a very expensive mistake on my part to book with this hotel!

As a frequent traveler for work, I stay at many SPG properties. Compared to all the SPG property in Chicago, this is by far the worst. Why? 1) They charge you to use the gym. $12 per day or something like $24 for your entire stay. I can't even begin on what a rip off that is. 2) As a Gold or Platinum member, you always get a complimentary water bottle in your room. They do not offer that option here and you have to make a fuss about it before they give you one. 3) They do not have wireless internet. It is 2010- enough said. To charge you at least over $200 a night, all the above amenities should be built into that cost. I would never stay here again.

The Hard Rock's vibrant, music-filled decor felt refreshingly current, not tired. I slept deeply on the plush bed, and while my two-night stay flew by, the rain shower and sleek vanity made every morning feel like a treat.

I expected much more from the Fairmont given the nightly rate. Our room faced the parking structure and a sliver of downtown, hardly the city view advertised in the booking photos. Worse, the walls seemed paper-thin: elevator chimes, hallway conversations, and traffic below continued well after midnight. The room itself was tidy but dated, with worn furniture and a bathroom that felt surprisingly small. Staff at the desk were polite but distracted; when I mentioned the noise, they offered earplugs rather than trying to move us. Service at breakfast was slow and our coffee arrived lukewarm. For the price, I expected a calmer room and more attentive hospitality.
Hotel Allegro was a lovely surprise--quiet room, comfortable bed, and genuinely helpful staff. The location made it easy to walk to restaurants, and breakfast was a nice start to the day.
The rate felt fair for the location and room quality--the breakfast buffet was fresh with great options, staff were genuinely friendly, and the hallways were wonderfully quiet. I'd gladly book again.

We had an issue with housekeeping and the hotel management did not handle it well. They were subject to a brief staff strike and did not inform guests and in fact failed to tell us about the strike and our room never was cleaned. After 4 calls and several hours we were able to get clean towels. Overall service other than check in was poor for a reportedly 4 star hotel.

My only regret is that I booked just one night at Affinia--I could have happily holed up for a week. The room was a quiet sanctuary despite being on a busy street; I never heard a peep from neighbors or traffic, and the blackout curtains did their job perfectly. I slept like a log on that firm-but-plush bed, waking only to the sun sneaking past the edges. Wi-Fi was fast and stable the whole time, no annoying login drops, which meant I actually finished my emails instead of rage-quitting. Location was ideal for walking everywhere, and the front desk even remembered my name the next morning. It felt less like a chain and more like a well-run boutique. I'm already checking dates for a return trip.
The Talbott felt wonderfully welcoming, with a quiet, comfortable room and staff who remembered our plans and offered great dinner suggestions. The Gold Coast location made walking everywhere easy.

We only stayed one night, which turned out to be our only regret. The room was spotless--not a single speck of dust on the baseboards, and the bathroom smelled of fresh citrus. We slept like rocks on that cloud-like bed, and the blackout curtains meant we woke up naturally, not at the crack of dawn. Breakfast was a pleasant surprise: fluffy scrambled eggs, crispy bacon, and a surprisingly good make-your-own waffle station with real maple syrup. The coffee was strong and hot, exactly what I needed before heading to the airport. Honestly, I've paid twice as much for chain hotels that felt half as nice. The staff even remembered our names at checkout, which was a small touch that felt genuinely thoughtful. We'll definitely book two nights next time.
For a Hilton, this was disappointing: the room smelled stale, the AC rattled all night, and check-in took forever despite barely anyone being in line.

We booked the Sofitel for a anniversary weekend and honestly couldn't have picked better. The room was spacious, with a heavenly bed and a view of the city lights that made us feel like we were in a movie. The staff were professional but warm, especially the concierge who arranged a last-minute dinner reservation for us at a lovely bistro. The pool area was a serene escape from the busy streets, and we spent a lazy afternoon there. Breakfast had everything we could crave, from fresh pastries to made-to-order omelets. While the lobby was a bit busy at check-in, the efficient process made up for it. We left feeling completely relaxed and already planning our return. A truly elegant stay with that special touch you don't find everywhere.

I was a bit skeptical about the WiFi after reading some older comments, but it turned out to be rock-solid--I streamed video and joined a video call without a single drop. The front desk crew genuinely made the stay, though; they remembered my name by the second day and went out of their way to draw a map to a hidden little trattoria that became my favorite meal of the trip. My room was spotless, with that fresh, just-cleaned scent and crisp sheets that made me look forward to crashing each night. The bathroom was compact but thoughtfully arranged, featuring a fantastic rainshower head and fluffy towels that were replaced without me even asking. Everything felt effortless, which is exactly what you want on vacation. I'd happily book here again.
Really enjoyed my stay at Hotel Monaco--the room was stylish and spotless, the bed incredibly comfortable, and the staff made check-in feel effortless. Great location too.

Our room overlooked the little piazza, and honestly, I could have sat on that tiny balcony all day just watching the sea and the lemon trees. The Hotel Amalfi is tucked into the hillside so perfectly that you feel like part of the town itself. Breakfast was simple but plentiful--fresh pastries, local cheese, and the best cappuccino we had on the whole coast. The staff remembered our names by the second morning and helped us book a boat tour that ended up being the highlight of our trip. The room itself was compact but spotless, with a lovely tiled bathroom. The only minor downside was the walk back up from the beach, but the view from the rooftop terrace more than made up for it. A genuinely charming, welcoming place.

We stayed at the Talbott for a long weekend and honestly expected more for the price. The room was smaller than advertised and felt dated, with a wobbly AC unit that rattled all night. Housekeeping skipped our room entirely one day and we had to call twice to get fresh towels. The front desk staff were hit or miss--one person was friendly, another seemed annoyed by every question. Location is decent, but street noise came right through the thin windows. The 'complimentary coffee' in the lobby ran out by 9am both mornings. At these rates, I've had far better experiences elsewhere in the city. Probably won't be back.

If you love Brick Walls and Alleyways, then this view is for you. I asked for a room facing the river, I get a room facing a Brick Wall. That really pissed me off. From all the great reviews, I was expecting better. Before I came here, I stayed in a Hyatt in NYC, and that was awesome. There was nothing about the hotel that blew me away. The wine hour was ok. I was hoping there would be something better food, but I guess that's why it's a wine hour. I ordered room service one night. There wasn't really anywhere to eat it, so I had to eat it on my bed to watch tv. This was my first time coming to Chicago, and I think it will be my last. Just thoroughly disappointed.

Very disappointed in our stay in Chicago Monoco. We have stayed many times elsewhere, primarily in washington DC and are accustomed to great customer service, beverages like water or soda at the wine bar, coffee and papers in the morning, help with bags. Not only did the Chicago monoco do none of these things, the staff was not helpful, either. Requests were not honored and the staff did not seem happy to be there. YOu got the feeling you were 'bothering' people if you asked a question. No bellman, the doorman did not open the door or help with bags. Even though we were traveling with a child, I had to request a fish when they did not bring it. Really baffling.. as we love the Monoco in Washington.
Had a really comfortable stay at the Sheraton; the room was spotless, the bed was excellent, and everyone at the front desk was genuinely helpful. I'd happily return.

Stayed at Hotel James for a long weekend and honestly, it exceeded every expectation I had. The location is perfect--steps from everything but tucked away enough to feel quiet. Check-in was a breeze; the front desk agent actually remembered my name and gave great dinner recommendations. The room itself was spotless, with a ridiculously comfortable bed and blackout curtains that let me sleep in past 9, which never happens. I loved the little touches: the complimentary coffee in the lobby each morning was strong and delicious, and the gym was way better equipped than most hotels I've visited. The only minor hiccup was the shower pressure fluctuating one evening, but it didn't ruin anything. The bar downstairs has a fantastic cocktail list, and the staff there were friendly without being pushy. For the price, this place is a steal. I've already booked my next stay for next month. Can't recommend it enough.

I had a very comfortable stay at the Hyatt while visiting for a long weekend. The check-in desk was busy when I arrived, but the line moved quickly and the staff remained friendly and organized. My room was bright, quiet, and larger than expected, with a genuinely comfortable bed, plenty of outlets, and a good-sized desk for catching up on email. I especially appreciated how spotless the bathroom was and the strong water pressure in the shower. The hotel is also well placed for restaurants, shopping, and public transportation, so I barely needed a taxi. Breakfast in the lobby restaurant was fresh, although service slowed down during the morning rush. Overall, the property felt polished without being stuffy, and I would happily book the Hyatt again.

We really enjoyed our brief stay at the Millennium Knickerbocker! From the front desk personnel and bellmen to the housekeeping staff and bartender, everyone we met was helpful and welcoming. Our 11th-floor room was clean and beautiful, and the view looking north to the Drake Hotel and apartments across the street was nice. The in-room coffee service was appreciated, too. There isn't a lot of room in the bathroom for your toiletries, but I'd still take a room in a beautiful older hotel with character over a spacious-but-cookie-cutter room any day!

The decor felt painfully dated, like stepping back into the 90s, and breakfast was a bland, overpriced buffet. Room Wi-Fi dropped constantly, and our bathroom had a clogged drain and a musty towel smell that sealed the disappointing stay.
The Ambassador looked promising online, but the room was tired, the hallway smelled faintly of smoke, and front desk requests went unanswered. Not worth the price.
Affinia felt welcoming from check-in onward, with a spacious, spotless room and surprisingly quiet nights. The staff gave great neighborhood tips, and the location made getting around easy.

This was a refreshing change from the ordinary. I loved the location, the service and the amenities offered by this hotel. The room was charming with a window seat and a water view. The decor was unique but cheerful. Free wireless internet services were a plus here. The staff was helpful and attentive. We loved having goldfish share our room! I would definitely stay here again.
I barely slept due to hallway noise, and our two-night stay dragged on. The view was a drab parking lot, while the Wi-Fi repeatedly dropped out.

We had a fantastic stay at the Hilton. The location was perfect for exploring, and the staff truly went above and beyond. From the moment we checked in, everyone was incredibly welcoming, and they even arranged a late checkout without us having to ask. The room was spotless and the bed was wonderfully comfortable; I haven't slept that well in ages. We also loved the breakfast buffet--tons of fresh options, and the coffee was actually good, which is rare in hotels.

The only minor hiccup was the pool being a bit busy on Saturday afternoon, but that's not really on them. Overall, it was a seamless, relaxing experience, and we wouldn't hesitate to book here again. A big thank you to the front desk team for making our anniversary feel so special! Highly recommended for both couples and families.

I booked the Ambassador expecting a bit of a splurge, but honestly, I left feeling like I'd thrown money away. The room rate was steep, and for that price, I expected something more than a worn carpet and furniture that looked like it hadn't been updated since the early 2000s. The mustard-yellow armchair had a suspicious stain, and the curtains smelled faintly of dust. Our window faced a brick wall, so 'view' was a generous term--we had to keep the blinds shut for any privacy, which made the room feel like a cave. The staff were polite but overwhelmed, and the breakfast buffet was a sad spread of stale pastries. I was only there for one night, yet that was more than enough. Two nights would have felt like a punishment. Not worth the premium, not by a long shot.
Stayed two nights at the Hilton for a conference and was pleasantly impressed--quiet room, comfortable bed, fast elevators, and the front desk handled a late checkout without any fuss.
Great stay at the Sheraton--the bed was incredibly comfy and the pool area was spotless. Staff went out of their way to help with directions. Would definitely book again.

Booked here expecting the iconic rock-and-roll vibe and Sunset Strip energy, but left feeling totally flat. Check-in was a mess--waited 45 minutes behind a huge tour group while only two front desk agents worked. The room itself looked nothing like the photos: the 'signature' Panasonic sound system was outdated, the decor felt cheap and borrowed from a mid-range chain, and the window faced a brick wall. Housekeeping knocked three times before noon even though our 'Do Not Disturb' sign was up, and the hallway smelled like stale perfume mixed with cleaning chemicals. Worst part? The pool area was overcrowded with non-guests from a private event, so we couldn't even grab a chair. The minibar was overpriced and the staff seemed overwhelmed and unbothered. For these prices, you'd think the legend would live up to the hype. It didn't. Save your money for a boutique spot with actual character.

Stayed at Hard Rock for a long weekend and honestly came away impressed. The room was spotless--crisp white linens, no stray hairs in the bathroom, and the surfaces actually looked wiped down. Given the prime location and the way the place is styled, I expected to pay a tourist tax, but the rate felt fair for what you got. I'm a light sleeper, yet the blackout curtains and quiet hallway meant I slept through the night both evenings, which never happens for me in hotels. Staff stood out, too. The front desk clerk remembered my name at checkout, and housekeeping proactively restocked the coffee pods without me asking. Minor quibble: the elevator wait got long at peak hours, but that's a small price. I'd book again without hesitation.

The grime on the windows completely obscured the so-called skyline, and the bed felt like a damp sponge, leaving me exhausted. Despite the tired, musty decor from decades past, the two nights here somehow stretched into an eternity too long.

Hotel Allegro was a really pleasant surprise. The location made it easy to walk to restaurants and shops, yet the room was quiet once the windows were closed. Check-in was friendly and efficient, and the front desk gave us a few genuinely useful local recommendations instead of a generic map. Our room was spotless, with a comfortable bed, strong shower pressure, and enough space to unpack without feeling cramped. Breakfast had a nice mix of fresh fruit, pastries, eggs, and good coffee, and the dining area never felt chaotic. We also appreciated being able to leave our bags after checkout. A couple of furnishings showed minor wear, but nothing that affected our stay. I'd happily return for another city break.

I really expected more from a Hyatt, honestly. Checked in around 4pm only to wait nearly 40 minutes because they were 'short on housekeeping staff,' and the room I finally got still smelled faintly of cigarettes despite being labeled non-smoking. The AC rattled all night like it was about to take off, so I barely slept. Bathroom had hair on the floor when I arrived, and the shower took a solid five minutes to get warm. Breakfast was a disappointment too -- cold eggs, coffee machine empty for over half an hour with nobody refilling it. Front desk staff were polite enough, but that doesn't make up for a $300-plus night that felt more like a budget motel. I won't be rushing back to this location anytime soon.

I had a very pleasant stay at Hotel Amalfi. The location was convenient, with restaurants, small shops, and public transportation all within an easy walk, yet the street was quiet enough at night. My room was clean, bright, and comfortably furnished, with a surprisingly good mattress and plenty of storage for a longer visit. The bathroom looked recently refreshed, and the water pressure was excellent. Staff at reception were welcoming and helpful, especially when I needed directions and a late taxi. Breakfast offered a nice variety of fresh fruit, pastries, eggs, and good coffee, although the room became busy around 9 a.m. Wi-Fi worked reliably throughout my stay. It is not a luxury property, but it felt well cared for and offered very good value.

We stayed for just one night ,but the hotel staff was extremely friendly and polite. The rooms were clean and large. The decor had just been redone. The best perks were the complimentary continental breakfast on each floor in the morning and the free cocktail hour with premium drinks and great appetizers at night. We got a great rate and would go back. Great location for walking around.

The Omni was chosen for it's location whichworked out perfectly. The bedding was wondeful and everything seemed fairly clean ...until...I sat down in the tub...there was BLACK MOLD in the soap holder, in the cracks on the walls between the tile, all under the tile overhang above the tub and completely around the toilet bowl. Needless to say I drained the tub and took a shower...I really don't care for showers. Oh yes...the toilet leaked as well...The staff were very helpful but I was disappointed. I travel extensively and don't think I will return. we needed color copies for a business meeting and their printer was broken, so the man in the business center took the jump drive to another part of the hotel, printed the presentation and delivered it to our room. They try! We booked online for a weekend package and got a room on the 10th floor with a view of the windows of another building...but we weren't there too much.

Check ins went smoothly. But be advised.... Walls are super thin, the building is old and the rooms are very very very small. The downside of them allowing pets was that we could hear the poor dog barking in the morning probably because it needed to go out. For the price it wasn't bad. It was walking distance to most major attractions. Overall ... it's ok at best. Another plus is the CTA is close by.

I stayed at the Omni with a Band that what in town. The room was amazing. Just walking in, the hotel was gorgeous. I have no complaints. Prompt Room service, Friendly front desk. Many shops, beautiful fountin. Just an all around great hotel in a great City.

Really enjoyed my stay at the Talbott. Rooms were cozy and spotless, and the location off Rush Street made walking to dinner and shopping easy. Staff remembered my name after one day. Would happily return.

We had a very pleasant stay at the Sofitel and would happily return. The lobby felt elegant without being overly formal, and check-in was quick, friendly, and well organized. Our room was spacious, quiet, and exceptionally comfortable, with crisp bedding and a lovely city view. I especially appreciated the thoughtful touches, including the quality toiletries, good lighting, and plenty of outlets near the bed. Breakfast offered a wide selection, from fresh fruit and pastries to cooked options, and the coffee was surprisingly good. The staff throughout the hotel were attentive but never intrusive, always greeting us warmly and helping with directions or restaurant suggestions. The only minor issue was that the Wi-Fi slowed down in the evening, but it did not affect our overall experience. A polished, relaxing stay with genuinely excellent service.

I'm not sure if the walls are paper-thin or if my neighbors were just having a full-blown party, but I heard every thump and laugh until nearly 2 a.m. For nearly $300 a night, I expected better soundproofing. The room itself was clean and stylish, but that didn't make up for the constant noise, nor the lukewarm breakfast where the scrambled eggs were dry and the coffee tasted burnt. The location is convenient, but I felt the whole experience was wildly overpriced, almost like paying for a luxury brand without the substance. My two nights felt like an eternity, and by the second morning I was counting the hours until checkout. If you crave peace and value, look elsewhere.

Checked in after midnight to find the hallway reeked of stale cigarette smoke, and the smell crept right under the door into our room. The bathroom was the worst part--the showerhead sprayed sideways, the caulk around the tub was peeling and gray, and the hairdryer sounded like a dying lawnmower. Housekeeping clearly missed this one: there was a sticky patch near the minibar and what looked like crumbs under the desk. Location is decent if you want the Loop, but you're paying for that address alone. I could hear every door slam and the elevator ding until 2 a.m., plus the HVAC rattled on and off all night. Bed was firm, sheets were clean, but that's the only positive. For Hyatt's name, this was a letdown--dirty, dated, and far from restful. I won't be back.

I expected more from the Knickerbocker given the rates and its Times Square location. The lobby is impressive, but that was about the only part of the stay that felt polished. Check-in took nearly half an hour because our room was apparently not ready, even though we arrived after 4. When we finally got upstairs, the room was smaller than the photos suggested and had a persistent stale smell. The air conditioner rattled loudly all night, and the blackout shade didn't fully close, which is not ideal with city lights outside. We also called twice for extra towels and they never arrived. The rooftop view is nice, but drinks were overpriced and service was slow. Convenient location, yes, but I left feeling like I paid luxury prices for a fairly average, frustrating experience.

My stay at the Sheraton was much more disappointing than I expected. The lobby looked polished, but check-in took nearly 30 minutes even though there were only two people ahead of me, and the desk agent seemed rushed and uninterested. The room was reasonably large, but it felt tired: scuffed furniture, stained carpet near the window, and a bathroom fan that rattled all night. Housekeeping also skipped my room on the second day, so I had to call twice for fresh towels. Wi-Fi was unreliable during a work video call, which was especially frustrating given the hotel's business-oriented setup. The location was convenient, and the bed itself was comfortable, but those positives did not make up for the poor service and lack of upkeep. I would choose somewhere else next time.

I had a really pleasant stay at the Omni and would happily return. Check-in was quick, and the front desk staff were warm without being overly formal. My room was clean, quiet, and had a comfortable bed with plenty of pillows; I also appreciated the blackout curtains after a long travel day. The bathroom was spotless and the water pressure was better than expected. The lobby and common areas felt polished but still welcoming, and the location made it easy to walk to nearby restaurants and attractions. Breakfast was a little pricey, but the food was fresh and service was attentive. Overall, it felt like a well-run hotel with thoughtful details and genuinely friendly staff.

I expected much more from an InterContinental stay, especially for the price. Check-in took nearly 30 minutes because the desk seemed understaffed, and nobody acknowledged the wait. The room looked polished at first, but the carpet was stained, the air conditioning rattled all night, and the bathroom had a lingering damp smell. Housekeeping missed our room one day and only brought fresh towels after two calls. Breakfast was crowded, with cold items sitting out too long and empty coffee stations. The location was convenient, but that was the main positive. Staff were polite when approached, yet there was no sense of proactive service or attention to detail. Overall, it felt like a tired business hotel trading on its name rather than delivering a luxury experience.

Stayed at the Monaco on my way skiing at Easter & loved it. Staff were helpful & friendly, room was huge with fantastic view of the river. Central location, 5 min walk to the EL. Adjoining Restaurant/Bar, great food & service. I have stayed in more expensive, supposedly better, hotels in Chicago, but this is the best. Thanks Monaco, I'll be back.

I'd heard great things about the Intercontinental brand, so I was genuinely excited for our anniversary weekend. Unfortunately, the experience fell far short of the reputation. Check-in took nearly 25 minutes despite arriving at 3 PM sharp, and the front desk agent seemed more interested in a phone call than greeting us. Our room, when we finally got the key card, smelled faintly of damp carpet and the air conditioning sounded like a small tractor every time it cycled on. The 'city view' turned out to be a roof and a ventilation shaft.

We tried the hotel restaurant for dinner and were sorely disappointed. My steak arrived overcooked, and the waiter disappeared for so long we nearly walked out. The crowning issue, though, was the noise--paper-thin walls meant we heard every conversation from the room next door until almost midnight. For these prices, I expected polish, not a lesson in patience. Won't be back.

Will not stay here again. We were here pre-construction so didn't have the noise problems that others are now experiencing. But room and service quality were so poor that we will not return. Our suite was large enough, but it was dirty, dated and worn. The bed linens were stained and the bathroom did not appear to have been cleaned properly. Public hall areas had room service trays sitting for two days, disgusting. We (politely) requested housekeeping to touch up our room and pick up trays and they never showed. We had paid for the King Tut Package, which was supposed to include tickets to the exhibit. They had no record of this and didn't honor it. Of course, the exhibit was sold out, so our main reason for visiting Chicago was ruined as we weren't able to see this part of the Field museum. My (also polite) letter to Hilton and the manager was never acknowledged. Very very disappointed in this property and am now avoiding Hilton in general when possible.

Stayed at Hotel Palmer last weekend and was genuinely impressed--the room was spotless, the bed super comfortable, and the front desk even remembered my name at breakfast. Great value for the area, and I'd happily book again.
Hotel Palmer looked promising online, but the room was noisy, the AC barely worked, and the front desk seemed uninterested when we mentioned it.

We stayed three nights at the Conrad and honestly it exceeded expectations. The check-in was smooth, and we were upgraded to a partial ocean view room on the 28th floor, which made my wife's day. The bed was genuinely comfortable, blackout curtains worked perfectly, and the bathroom with the soaking tub was a nice touch after long days walking the city. Breakfast at the restaurant downstairs was excellent, though pricey, fresh pastries and made-to-order eggs, worth it once or twice. Housekeeping was prompt and they remembered we'd asked for extra pillows. Location is great too, easy walk to plenty of restaurants. Only tiny gripe: the lobby elevator wait at peak hours could be a bit long. Would absolutely return next trip.

I booked the Amalfi expecting a charming coastal hideaway based on the photos, but the reality was a letdown from the moment I walked in. The front desk clerk barely looked up from his phone, and our 'sea view' turned out to be a sliver of water wedged between two construction cranes. The room itself was stuffy, with a musty smell that the overworked air conditioning unit couldn't fix. Housekeeping was inconsistent--towels were replaced one day, forgotten the next, and the bathroom sink drained slowly the entire stay. The breakfast, supposedly included, was lukewarm scrambled eggs and stale pastries served in a cramped dining area. I'll admit the location is convenient for the ferry, but for the price, I expected comfort and basic attentiveness. This felt more like a budget hostel wearing a fancy name. I really wanted to like it, but I left feeling cheated and exhausted. Won't be back.
The Hard Rock delivered on every level. Staff were incredibly friendly, the room was spotless and quiet, and that pool area is a total vibe. Would happily book again for a city escape.
The room felt worn and noisy, with a rattling air conditioner that kept me awake. For the price, I expected cleaner hallways and a much more responsive front desk.

After reading so many great reviews I booked the Hotel Monaco and was not disappointed. I booked through their web site about 2 1/2 months prior to arrival for $170/night plus tax for a room with 2 queens. The location was perfect - right by the river near Michigan Ave. - minutes walk to the El, Millenium Park, the Theater District and Shopping. The room was clean, a little larger than standard and nicely decorated. We had window seats in the room with a view of the river. There was Starbucks coffee in the lobby in the morning and a wine reception in the evening. To top it off, the staff was very friendly and knowledgable about the area.

Just returned from a 3 night stay at the Talbott. This was our first visit there, and I can honestly say that I wouldn't stay at any other hotel in Chicago. From when we first were greated by the bell captain until our final departure, the staff was nothing less than amazing, always greeting with a smile and can I help you attitute. The room we had (1508) was very spacious and comfortable. The bed was probably the most comfortable that my wife and I have ever slept in (including the Four Seasons). Had great breakfasts and drinks at Basil's. You would be missing a fantastic experience, if you didn't stay at the Talbott.

Rooms are so dark we had to insist they bring lamps so we could see. The room we had at almost $400 a night was dingy and small. Don't mistakingly think the Hard Rock Cafe is there, it isn't. They have a Chinese restaurant that is overpriced and limited on items. The room service menu is broken down in terms of times you can order certain foods. When my wife wanted a milk shake we had to call the Manager to have it made since the kitchen staff said it wasn't a choice. The Rolled Roast beef sandwich was listed under the 2 am choice and they refused to make it untill again, we called the Manager who did get it to us. The staff did appear friendly, although housekeeping totally disregarded our 'do not disturb' sign and would call us on the phone. Don't make the mistake of staying here but if you do, walk across the street and buy snacks you want because even a soda is $3 plus 19% gratuity. We ended up having to order delivery food brought to us. This is the most overpriced, over rated and dingy hotel we've ever stayed in. Taxi to airport is $40.

The room was wonderfully quiet despite the busy street below, and the skyline view from the window was a lovely bonus. I slept deeply on the comfortable bed, and the decor felt modern and fresh without being too trendy. A genuinely pleasant stay.

Great location and quality place to stay. Lovely large clean room with a queen size bed it was great. Staff were very helpful and put us onto some great restaurants and then some music bars. Coleman on the front desk was a great guy to meet as a first impression he sold the hotel to us with his personality. The hotel delivered an anniversary cake to us in our room (compliments of the hotel) for me this showed that they care about their guests Many thanks to all it was a great place to stay.
The room was clean enough, but the tired decor and dull parking-lot view felt uninspired. The cramped bathroom had worn grout and weak water pressure, making the stay disappointing.

Checked in Thursday and, honestly, I could have stayed another three days. The bed was that perfect middle ground between cloud-soft and supportive--I slept like I hadn't in months, only waking because the sunrise streamed through the blackout curtains' edges. The hallway was whisper-quiet all night; the only interruption was the faint hum of the AC, which I actually found soothing. The wifi was flawless, streaming a movie on my laptop in bed with zero buffering, which is rare for a hotel this size. My only complaint is that the shower pressure was slightly weak, but the lobby coffee made up for it. It felt like a quick retreat, and I left genuinely refreshed.

Rude, rude, rude! We stayed here on July 4th weekend. We drove from Michigan, we called customer service to get directions from I-95 w/c is a major highway to Chicago-- calling them from a cellphone, telling them we're in a middle of a storm and that we're lost....we were put on hold, forwarded to another person who did not know how to get to the hotel and we were on hold again. Giving up we decided to just exit the highway and try our luck at a 7-11 store. When we finally arrived at the hotel at 2 am no one was there to take care of our car so we looked for parking ourselves. Checking in we were not greeted by anyone, even the receptionist did not greet us!! no welcome to the knickerbocker, nothing! The man at the reception was rude, which makes me think what kind of customer service training this hotel has. The guy could not find our reservation and he seemed frustrated that we are checking-in at 2 am!! Well if they were able to give us directions maybe we would have been there 2 hours earlier. The room is not even spectacular, very small, probably a little bigger than a walk-in closet. Stay here at your own risk.

The walls were paper-thin--I heard every door slam and hallway conversation until 2 AM. Our bathroom had a persistent mildew smell, and the lukewarm, bland breakfast buffet was barely edible. I slept terribly and left more exhausted than when I arrived.

I expected more from a Fairmont, especially at the rate we paid. The lobby looks impressive, but the experience fell apart after check-in. Our room was dated, with scuffed furniture, a noisy air conditioner, and a bathroom fan that rattled all night. Housekeeping missed our room the first afternoon, and when we called for fresh towels, they arrived nearly an hour later. The bed was comfortable enough, but the hallway noise started early and the walls seemed very thin. Breakfast was expensive and surprisingly mediocre; cold coffee and dry pastries are not what I associate with this brand. Staff were polite when available, though the front desk always seemed understaffed. It wasn't a terrible stay, but it certainly didn't feel luxurious or worth the price.

Having booked the hotel directly with the hotel on its website, I arrived tired from Ireland, to find that they had mislaid my booking and had no room on that night, but did have rooms for the rest of the week. They booked me in to another (not as nice) downtown hotel and paid for my taxi to that hotel and for that nights accommodation. On my return to the hotel next day, I was upgraded to the Club level. What really impressed me was that the hotel did everything they could to make up for their earlier mistake...unprompted. Of course, the hotel itself (particularly on the 32nd floor) is excellent. I will definitely be back.
My stay at The Knickerbocker felt a little too short; the room was surprisingly quiet, Wi-Fi worked reliably, and breakfast was fresh with plenty of satisfying choices.

Staff barely acknowledged us at check-in, and the lobby furniture looks straight out of the 90s. Breakfast was stale pastries and weak coffee, plus the bathroom had mold in the shower grout. Won't return.

Stayed here for a conference and the location was perfect--right by everything. Room was quiet, bed super comfy, and the front desk genuinely friendly. Breakfast was a bit pricey, but overall a smooth, hassle-free stay. Would gladly book again.

I had a very comfortable three-night stay at the Affinia. The room was larger than expected, with enough space for a small sitting area and a desk, and the bed was genuinely comfortable. My window looked out over the neighboring buildings and a slice of the city skyline--not a dramatic view, but enjoyable at night when the lights came on. Despite being in a busy part of town, the room was surprisingly quiet, aside from an occasional hallway sound. The bathroom was spotless and practical, with good water pressure and plenty of counter space, although the fixtures showed a little age. Overall, the decor felt more classic than trendy; some pieces were dated, but everything was well maintained and gave the room a warm, lived-in character. I would happily return.

Stayed here for a conference and honestly left wondering if I'd booked the wrong hotel. The lobby looks great in photos but the reality is worn carpets and a constant hum from the AC that never quite went away. Check-in took twenty minutes because the front desk seemed understaffed and the person helping me kept disappearing. My room smelled faintly of damp, and the 'city view' was mostly a brick wall with a sliver of sky. The bed was firm enough, but the pillows were flat as pancakes, and housekeeping didn't show up until after 4 PM each day, even with the do-not-disturb sign off. I tried room service once--the burger arrived cold and the fries were soggy. The gym had two broken treadmills and no water refill station. For the price, I expected far more polish. Location is convenient, sure, but that's the only thing that worked. I won't be back.

I expected the Hard Rock to be lively and polished, but the stay was more frustrating than fun. Check-in took nearly 25 minutes, and the receptionist seemed distracted, offering little explanation about the facilities or local area. Our room overlooked a flat rooftop crowded with vents and service equipment, so keeping the curtains open was hardly appealing. The bathroom was cramped, with tired grout, weak water pressure, and a shower that took several minutes to warm up. The bed looked comfortable, but the constant hallway noise and loud music from somewhere downstairs made sleep difficult; I woke repeatedly both nights. Staff were more pleasant when we complained, but no practical solution was offered. The music theme is entertaining, yet the overall experience felt overpriced and poorly maintained.
Expected way more from the Monaco. The room smelled stale, the AC rattled all night, and front desk took forever to answer. For the price, honestly a letdown.
Gorgeous property with beautiful views of the city. The concierge went out of her way to book us a hard-to-get dinner reservation, and the room was immaculate. Would happily return.

Used this hotel the first time I was in Chicago. For the prices and for being classified an intercontinental...I wouldn't consider it that good. The rooms were solid. The view was ok (but so is it virtually everywhere else on Michigan Ave.) The service was ok. The prices were ridiculous for everything from wifi to well everything else. We came here for a Jewish/Hindi wedding. Appetizer was fine. Main entree was a small portion of meat with forgettable everything else. Dessert was inedible. I have been to some other expensive hotels with similar ratings but they had more or just better rooms to an extent that it would be worth it. I personally preferred the Conrad. Better prices and better service.

Had to bring my new puppy with me on a business trip and stayed at the Palmer House. The service was wonderful, staff was very friendly towards dog owners, even stopped to tell me how nice my dog was. Easy access to red line from Midway. Valets were prompt at retrieving car (they recommended calling down in advance we did and the car was there waiting).

We booked the Swissotel based on its reputation, but the whole experience felt tired. The hallway carpet was worn, and our room's decor looked like it hadn't been updated since the early 2000s - beige, scuffed, and with a lampshade that was crooked. I slept poorly, partly because the mattress sagged in the middle and partly because the air conditioning hummed loudly every ten minutes. On the bright side, the windows were well-insulated, so street noise wasn't the issue. What really got me was how long the stay felt; we had booked for three nights but checked out after two because there was simply nothing enjoyable to linger over. The staff was polite but overstretched, and the breakfast buffet ran out of everything by 9 a.m. I can't call it a disaster, just a persistent, drab disappointment that made me wish we'd picked another property.
Swissotel made our weekend feel effortless--lovely river view, spotless room, and genuinely warm staff. Breakfast was fresh and varied, though the lobby got busy in the evening.
I slept deeply in the quiet room, and the Wi-Fi stayed reliable for work. The city skyline view was lovely at dusk; my only complaint is that the weekend at Fairmont went by too quickly.

I expected much more from a Conrad, especially for the rate. The room looked nice at first glance, but the carpet had visible stains, dust sat along the window ledge, and there were hairs in the bedding. The bathroom was cramped and oddly worn, with weak water pressure, a loose faucet handle, and grout that needed serious attention. Staff at check-in barely acknowledged me and seemed annoyed when I asked whether another room was available. Service requests took far too long as well. Noise was another problem: I could hear doors slamming, conversations in the hallway, and traffic well past midnight. The bed was comfortable, but I left feeling disappointed rather than rested.

I live in Chicago and have frequent occasion to recommend hotels to friends and business acquaintances. We recently put up a candidate (and his family) we were recruiting for our company at the Conrad. We had had good luck with this hotel when it was a Le Meridien. It was a disappointment for all concerned as a Conrad. On the plus side, our guests were able to check in early with no problem and they generally liked their room. On the downside... They learned after the fact that all rooms with two beds have no bath tub (only a shower). Our guests moved to a room with a bath tub and found hairs in it, which they had to clean themselves. When the coffee bar had no caffeinated coffee and our guests asked for some, they were told it would be delivered immediately. When they called 30 minutes later the front desk admitted that they had 'forgotten.' While the concierge and doorman were quite helpful, our guests told us that the front desk personnel were sullen and unresponsive. Our guests were generally under whelmed by one of the 'five best hotels in Chicago.' Conrad has a long way to go to compete with the Four Seasons, Peninsula and Park Hyatt.

I stayed for just one nite at the Sheraton Hotel and Towers and was a little nervous after reading a few negative reviews from other TA posters but I was not let down. I got the room via PL @ $70 and was first placed in a room on the 8th floor with a fabulous view of the roof of the lobby and a parking lot. Since I had nothing to lose, I asked to be moved to a 'room with a view'. The front desk attendant( Rasheeda) wanted to make sure that the room I had at first was clean and was in order and I assured her that it was. She then moved me up to the 24th floor with ease and it took about 1 minute. I was quite surprised as I have heard that they treat PL and Hotwire folks with a little less love than full price customers. The new room was very clean and spacious and overlooked the Navy Pier, a few other skyrise condos and the beautiful infinity of Lake Michigan. All this for $70? Yep! I skipped room service and walked to the local gourmet market as suggested by others and it was pricey but all food there was delicious! The room was comfy, had an ample closet and room to breathe as well as a convenient internet connection location. I didnt use it since I wasnt staying that long but at least it was on the desk. The bed and pillows were very comfy, but I awoke at about 330 in the morning sweating from the comfy but VERY WARM and somewhat weighty duvet on the bed. This was a great deal for the price and I would absolutely stay here again.

this is my new favorite place to stay in downtown chicago, and I've been to this hotel at least 4 times. the rooms are clean, wonderfully designed and comfortable. The staff is friendly, service focused - and the restuarant is great, especially for the breakfast fruit crepes. Love this hotel. It's a great location, very good and consistent service and quality .

Affinia felt overpriced for a tired, poorly cleaned room, with dust on the surfaces and a cramped, grimy bathroom. Staff were polite enough, but distant and slow to respond, making the stay disappointing.

I stayed at the Sofitel for three nights on a work trip and honestly couldn't fault it. The check-in was smooth, and the concierge went out of his way to book me a last-minute dinner reservation when everything nearby seemed full. My room on the eighth floor was spacious, spotless, and the bed was genuinely one of the most comfortable I've slept in at any hotel -- the pillows especially. Housekeeping respected my do-not-disturb mornings without issue. Breakfast had a great spread, the fresh pastries were worth getting up for, and the coffee was much better than the usual hotel machine stuff. The location is also super convenient, walking distance to the metro and plenty of restaurants. Only tiny gripe was a slight wait for the elevator at peak times, but that's minor. Would definitely return next trip.

I booked the Knickerbocker expecting old-world charm, but the reality felt more like neglect. Our room faced the interior airshaft, so the 'city view' was a brick wall and a humming vent, which also meant we heard every conversation from neighboring rooms and the clatter of housekeeping carts from 7 AM. At nearly $400 a night, it was a real gut punch. The carpet was stained, the furniture had that dusty, faded look from the 90s, and the single elevator was perpetually packed. The lobby is grand, sure, but the rooms don't match the facade. The location on the Mag Mile is the only saving grace, but it doesn't excuse the noise, the dated decor, or the feeling that the staff couldn't care less. I'd skip it unless you're desperate for the address.

This is a great hotel! From the doorman who greeted us as we arrived, to the young man at the reservation desk to the young woman serving complimentarily wine, everyone was very friendly and helpful. We were 'strangers but for a minute!' The room was extremely clean, well appointed and we had a pretty view of the Chicago River, especially enjoyed from the large window seats. Loved the purple polka-dot paper on the toilet paper roll! Hallways were large and quiet. The restaurant next door, South Water Kitchen is very nice too. The location is in walking distance of the theatres, parks, the river (take a cruise), Michigan Ave. It's ideal. The only negative is that the concierges were not nearly as friendly or inviting as the rest of the staff nor were they very helpful. For a self-sufficient traveler, you wouldn't really need their services (although it is nice) but for someone coming to Chicago for the first time, a concierge can be very helpful. I would definately stay at this hotel again and would recommend it.

I expected more from a Sheraton, especially for the rate we paid. Check-in took nearly half an hour because only one desk agent was working, and no one acknowledged the line. The room looked tired: scuffed furniture, a stained chair, and a bathroom fan that rattled all night. The air conditioning barely cooled the room, so sleeping was uncomfortable despite calling the front desk twice. Housekeeping also skipped our room on the second day, leaving us to hunt down fresh towels ourselves. Breakfast was expensive and pretty ordinary, with lukewarm eggs and empty coffee dispensers. The location was convenient, but that was about the only positive. This property feels overdue for maintenance and better staffing.
Hotel Palmer was a lovely surprise--quiet rooms, comfortable beds, and genuinely friendly staff. The location made walking to dinner easy, and breakfast was fresh and well stocked.

We had a really great stay here for our anniversary. The staff genuinely seemed to care and made us feel special -- the front desk even remembered our reason for visiting and sent up a small dessert plate. The room was clean and quiet, with a super comfortable bed and blackout curtains that actually worked, which is rare. We loved the lazy river and pool area, even on a busy Saturday afternoon. Service at the pool bar was quick, and the cocktails were strong. Drinks at the lobby bar one night were a bit pricey, but that's expected. The location is unbeatable for the Boulevard, and we walked everywhere. Would definitely book again for a fun, easy getaway.

Great hotel in heart of Chicago for business or pleasure. Rooms are recently upgraded and very modern and large. Flat screen TVs, marble baths, all rooms are suites, great desk, kitchenette, comfortable bed, free wireless internet... everything you could ask for. Location is easy walk to Magnificient Mile and lots of great restaurants. Staff is friendly and helpful. Short cab ride to Loop.

Slept terribly on a rock-hard mattress, and the room smelled musty with dusty corners. At these prices, I expected far better. Breakfast was a sad spread of cold eggs and stale pastries--definitely not worth the money.

After reading all the lukewarm reviews for this hotel, I went ahead and got an Ambassador membership just to hedge off any unpleasantness. I normally have a good experience with Intercontinental hotels, particularly the Mark Hopkins in SF. I called the hotel directly to confirm that my reservation was designated as Ambassador Club. When I arrived at the hotel, there was no separate check-in line (as advertised) and the manager on duty basically ignored me when I told him I was an ambassador club member and stuck me with a regular tiny room. I was nearly half an hour checking in the room and had to deal with the arrogant attitude of the manager on duty. They gave me a room in the 'modern' tower, (built in the 60's) which was about 2/3 the size of a regular room at the Mark Hopkins (built in '29). I had to deal with torn sheets, cracked marble sinks, and the spare roll of toilet paper being located OUTSIDE the bathroom inside the closet - how convenient is that? The closet door, if you are not careful, may break the full length mirror attached to the bathroom door. I was not provided with a key to the minibar and I called for turndown service, which never happened. The next day, they finally got around to the fact that I was an Ambassador Club member and entitled to an upgraded room, but since I travel with a medical device which I already set up in the tiny room, I declined. To their credit, they did send some of the amenities I would otherwise be entitled to as an Ambassador Club member. I would not stay at this hotel next time I go to Chicago. There are other better places for the money including, the Omni, The James, The Fairmont, Hyatt, Sheraton, Monaco, Crowne Plaza, even the Holiday Inn and Marriotts located in the same general area.

The Affinia was a real letdown, especially for the price tag. Our room felt tired and stuffy, with a view of a brick wall and a heating system that clanked all night. The 'modern' amenities were a joke--the iPad controlling the room kept disconnecting, and the so-called blackout curtains had a gap that let in a glaring streetlight. The bathroom had a persistent moldy smell, no matter how often we asked for extra towels to mask it. I get that it's an older building, but the lobby's slick photos don't match the threadbare carpet and chipped furniture in the actual rooms. Staff were polite but overwhelmed whenever we needed anything, like an extra blanket, which took over an hour. For this money, I'd expect far better. We left more exhausted than we arrived, and I can't recommend it. Shop elsewhere.

Very disapointed in the service and quality of this hotel. I travel quite frequently to chicago and have never had this happen at any other 4 star hotel. I reserved a king bed. At checkin I was informed they were out of kings and basically offered no type of compensation or upgrade. When i arrived at the room the air conditioner door was open and rattled all night. The TV did not work. Had to call for service. The following day returned from work at 6pm and found the room had not even been serviced. Stay somewhere else.

The view from our room was a stunning slice of the harbor, and the staff's genuine warmth made every request effortless. Despite the central location, it was blissfully quiet, and I felt every penny was justified for that restful escape.

I booked the Fairmont expecting a touch of elegance, but what I got was a masterclass in indifference. Breakfast was a chaotic, overpriced buffet where the scrambled eggs were cold and the coffee tasted burnt; getting a server's attention felt like a minor miracle. The staff, when they weren't avoiding eye contact, were curt to the point of rudeness, especially at the front desk during check-in. The location is admittedly convenient for sightseeing, but that's the only positive. My bathroom had peeling caulk around the tub and a hair dryer that barely worked, plus the water pressure in the shower was laughably weak. For the nightly rate, I expected polished service and clean details. Instead, I left with a bitter aftertaste and a lighter wallet. I won't be returning.

My anniversary dinner reservation was lost, and the front desk shrugged it off. The room's air conditioning rattled all night, and housekeeping forgot our turn-down service. For this price, I expected polish, not problems.

I really expected more from this Homewood, especially at the rates they charge. The room itself was fine, but sleep was nearly impossible both nights. There's a highway right behind the property, and even with the window shut I could hear trucks rumbling past well after midnight. The HVAC unit also cycled loudly every twenty minutes like it was struggling. The wifi was the bigger frustration, though -- it dropped constantly and the 'premium' network I was apparently paying for in my rate barely loaded a Youtube video. When I called the front desk about it, I got a shrug and a suggestion to 'try standing closer to the door.' For nearly $180 a night, that's not acceptable. The breakfast was the one bright spot, but it doesn't make up for two rough nights. I won't be back.
