Stunning views from the upper floors and the bed was incredibly comfortable. The breakfast buffet had plenty of options, and the location near the waterfront made evening strolls perfect.

I had a very pleasant stay at the Hyatt and felt the rate was fair for the level of comfort and service. My room was clean, bright, and had a comfortable bed that made it easy to relax after a long day. The bathroom was especially nice: modern fixtures, strong water pressure, plenty of towels, and a spacious shower with good lighting around the mirror. Wi-Fi connected quickly and stayed reliable for both video calls and streaming. Despite being near the elevator, the room was surprisingly quiet at night, with little hallway or street noise. Staff at check-in were warm and efficient, and the lobby felt polished without being overly formal. I would gladly stay here again.

For the price, this felt like a major letdown--the dated floral carpet and worn fixtures screamed 1990s. My room had dust on the nightstand and a suspicious stain by the window, and the thin pillows made for a restless, aching night.
Expected much better from Hyatt: the room smelled musty, the AC rattled all night, and staff seemed indifferent when I mentioned it at checkout.

We had a wonderful three-night stay at the Omni. The location was perfect for exploring the city, but honestly, we could have just stayed in the hotel the whole time. The pool area was a real highlight--clean, well-heated, and the towels were always stocked. Our room was spotless and the bed was incredibly comfortable; I slept better than I do at home. The staff were all so welcoming, from the valet to the front desk. We had one small issue with the TV remote and someone was up to fix it within minutes. Breakfast on the terrace was a lovely way to start the day. We're already looking at dates to come back next year.

My first trip back to Chicago in about 7 years was perfect! I chose the Knickerbocker as I had read that their rooms were recently renovated on top of being a great location to Michigan Avenue, Rush Street and downtown Chicago. I must say I was very impressed with the guestrooms! I had not stayed there prior but it definitely is a refresh from what I've seen in photo's posted on the reviews. The guestrooms are nicely decorated with a modern feel and they are good sized for a historical hotel! The beds are wonderful -- I need to get a pillow top mattress at home! I used the Internet access with no issue and I LOVED the larger screen TV's. The shower is fun with the different types of shower heads you can choose. And the bathrooms are fresh with all new granite and tile. I'm anxious to get back to Chicago and it won't be 7 years from now! I would highly recommend this hotel -- fantastic guestrooms, location and staff! I've added some digital pictures of my room as they are completely different from the one's I saw on previous reviews with the new renovation.

Hotel Talbott was a great choice for a weekend in Chicago. The location made it easy to walk to Michigan Avenue, restaurants, and the lake, yet the room was surprisingly quiet at night. Our king room was comfortable and spotlessly clean, with decor that felt classic and well cared for rather than dated--warm colors, nice furnishings, and a modern bathroom. Breakfast in the restaurant was fresh and filling, especially the eggs and pastries, though it was a little pricey. The Wi‐Fi worked reliably in both the room and lobby, which mattered since I had to check in with work. Overall, the stay felt worth the price for the service, comfort, and excellent location.

Stayed for a long weekend and honestly couldn't fault it. The room was spotless, with a ridiculously comfortable bed and a view that made me just sit and stare for an hour. Staff were attentive without hovering--the concierge remembered my name after one interaction and gave great dinner tips. Breakfast buffet had everything, though the eggs benedict was the standout. Pool area was calm even on a busy Saturday, and the loungers were actually spaced out, which never happens. Minor hiccup with the Wi-Fi in the room, but they sorted it within minutes. Location is perfect if you want to be close to the river but away from the tourist crush. Would happily book again, and I'm picky about hotels. Great value for what you get.

Booked a king room expecting a four-star experience but got stained carpets, a broken coffeemaker, and noise from the hallway all night. The front desk shrugged off my complaints and the breakfast pastries were stale. Definitely not worth the price--I'd skip this one.

Our stay at Hotel Amalfi was disappointing, especially considering the price. The location was convenient for reaching the main sights and restaurants on foot, but that was the main advantage. Our room faced a narrow alley, so the 'view' consisted mostly of a wall, bins, and occasional delivery noise. The bathroom was cramped and tired, with peeling grout, weak water pressure, and a shower curtain that let water spread across the floor. Breakfast was another letdown: limited choices, stale pastries, watery coffee, and no fresh fruit on either morning. Staff were polite but seemed rushed and offered little help when we mentioned the problems. The bed was reasonably comfortable, yet the overall condition and lack of attention to detail made the hotel feel overpriced. I would not choose it again.

I'd been searching for a cool, non-chain hotel for a weekend getaway with my boyfriend. I thought I'd found a winner in the Affinia... SOO disappointed!! In spite of the fact that our reservation was for two adults, we arrived to find our room had a DOUBLE bed. What?! I was floored, but after a delayed flight and a 2 hour cab ride, was too tired to make a fuss. We were hungry after all the delays and planned on attending an event that night, so we called for room service hoping to keep it simple. I was told that room service would call ME back to take my order...and nothing happened. I didn't want to be late to our event so we ended up going to the restaurant downstairs. Nothing special; entree, dessert and NAB for two still came out to $*...I am no hayseed, I'm WELL aware that everything costs more in Chicago, but this just wasn't worth it. Our room was by the elevator w/ parking garage view...the bathroom was tiny, shower curtain was stained, funky toilet seat/lid, and the vanity featured that 'rude awakening' lighting normally found in low-rent dressing rooms, i.e., 'Holy crap, have I looked that bad this whole time?!' If you're a traveler who likes using the in-room coffeemaker, they charge for their chintzy coffees (I don't use these, but... come on). Nice enough ambience in the upstairs bar, but weak drinks... That night, our bed was so tiny and uncomfortable that I almost asked to switch rooms. But the Marathon was that weekend; the hotel was so busy I didn't want to be a pest. I can't believe I was so impressed with this place online. Next time I'll happily pay more to stay someplace that's actually a treat.

From the moment we arrived, the service was impeccable, and our room offered stunning views of the city. The breakfast spread was fantastic, and the pool area was a perfect retreat after a day of exploring.

I booked the Sofitel expecting the Parisian polish everyone raves about, but honestly, my stay fell flat. The lobby looks stunning in photos, but the reality is worn edges and a strange musty smell near the elevators. My room was supposedly upgraded, yet the carpet had visible stains and the air conditioning rattled all night, making sleep nearly impossible. I asked for an extra blanket twice and it never arrived. The bathroom amenities were half-empty, which is just embarrassing for this price point. Breakfast was chaotic--the buffet ran out of basic items like yogurt and pastries, and staff seemed more interested in chatting than clearing tables. Location is convenient, sure, but for the nightly rate I expected service and upkeep that matched the brand. I left feeling like I'd stayed at a mediocre business hotel, not a Sofitel. Disappointing, especially since I'd been looking forward to it for weeks. Won't return.

The room was fine but the air conditioner rattled all night and the front desk brushed me off when I asked to switch. Overpriced for what you get, and the hallway smelled like stale food. Won't be back.

The Affinia was a letdown from the start--the lobby smelled like stale fries, and the room's 'upgraded' view was a brick wall. The air conditioner rattled all night, and housekeeping never replaced the towels. Not worth the price, honestly.

My husband and I stayed here for New Years eve weekend. This is an excellent hotel in an excellent location. Hotel is very tastefully decorated and warmly welcoming. The rooms had the best electronics I've ever seen. Loved that they had a soaking tub and a spacious shower stall. The hotel restaurant seemed to be empty everytime we walked by, so we avoided it too. Ate at Joe's across the street - excellent seafood. And you can shop til you drop without going outside! Nordstroms and four story mall is attached. Lots of good 'food on the run' places in there. Loved Chicago - loved the Conrad. I will go back!

THE ROOM I booked a room here and was told I'd be getting a king bed. When I check in, they say they only have a queen bed room available. I protested to no avail. When I got to the room, it was really only a full size bed. So I went from from a king bed at home to a full size bed in a tiny broom closet of a room in Chicago. For the pleasure, I paid the same price as a normal king bed room. The full size bed we had was also extremely uncomfortable. I think it was lop sided because they never rotate the mattresses. We would wake up with body aches and headaches. My wife even said she lost feeling in her arms some nights. Not good. Also, the internet in the room is hard to set-up, slow to use, and inconsistent. I generally had to restart my computer at least once to get the internet to work. The internet worked one day on my iPhone and then would not log me in. It's not really worth it. ROOM SERVICE Room service was very inconsistent and nonsensical. Some mornings they would take our towels (even the ones we hung up to use again) and not replace them, other times they would replace some towels and not others. They would also come at vastly different times. HOTEL SERVICE This hotel LOVES to nickel and dime. I asked for a fridge in the room and they told me it'd be $25. No other hotel I've ever stayed in (regardless of how many stars it had) has ever charged me for a fridge in the room. Late checkout? charge. Shuttle from the airport? - nonexistent. The front deck 'gold passport' people can't even figure out how to get you points. In the end I will have to call corporate and get my points for my stay (not that i plan on staying at a Hyatt property again). By the way, apparently the hotel is still undergoing changes because my mini-bar was missing. I was thinking of using it as a fridge instead of paying $25. THE HOTEL The hotel has some cool bars and a beautiful lobby area in the east tower. The west tower has some underground amenities no one uses. The bars are extremely expensive, but the drinks are tasty. The food is edible too, but I wouldn't brag about it. The hotel is not directly on the main street (Michigan), but it's not too far from it. It's right next to the boat tours and, in some rooms, has a view of the Navy Pier. Our room faced another hotel, but we could see a sliver of the pier. The hotel is walking distance from Millennium Park. It's a bit of a walk to any of the L stations though. If you want a wonderful breakfast place, go to Wildberry on Randolph st. It'll have you waiting to eat for a long time, but it's yummy! CONCLUSION I get better rooms, better beds, better service, and better amenities at a Holiday Inn Express or a Best Western. Save the money and stay elsewhere.

The room was big and luxurious, befitting the price tag ($299). Bed was very comfortable. However, my bed was against the wall abutting the elevator shaft, and I heard the elevators running all night. Also held a one-day conference there for 25 people. They stuck us in a long, narrow room that was cramped. Also, the night before we had a pre-conference dinner at the Palm restaurant in the hotel. Service was so slow that some of our party left before entrees were served. And the steaks were only so-so, a far cry from my experience with other Palms.

Pleasantly surprised by the James--rooms feel fresh and modern, and my floor-to-ceiling window overlooked the city nicely. WiFi was fast, breakfast had solid options despite the small cafe space. Would return.
The James looked stylish online, but my room felt worn and oddly cramped, with thin walls and slow service. For the price, I expected a much more comfortable, polished stay.

My stay at the Conrad was a real disappointment, especially given the price and reputation. The Wi‐Fi was unreliable throughout the visit, repeatedly dropping during video calls and requiring me to reconnect. Staff were polite enough at the front desk, but interactions felt rushed and unhelpful when I reported the issue; no one followed up. Breakfast was another letdown, with lukewarm eggs, dry pastries, and very slow service despite the restaurant not being especially busy. The room was clean, but the decor felt tired rather than luxurious, with worn-looking furniture and dated carpeting that didn't match the polished images online. The bed was comfortable, and the location was convenient, but those positives couldn't make up for the poor value and lack of attention to basic details.

The location is amazing, right across from Nordstrom's on Michigan Avenue. The hotel is beautiful and the rooms are clean. But... We are Intercontinental Ambassadors (the rewards club) and to get to the Ambassador suite level, we have to ride a private 'express' elevator. The elevator took three minutes to get to the thirtieth floor. When we checked in, the person behind the counter was rude and acted as if we were lucky to get checked-in. Also, there was a language barrier becuase she was Russian. The pool and spa were both beautiful, but we had to pay an extra fee because of 'upkeep'. If you want a nice hotel all the way around...go to the Omni.

Not worth the steep rate at all--the wifi barely connected and dropped constantly. My room faced a blank wall of the building next door, and honestly even one night there felt too long. Won't be back.
Stayed at the Sheraton for a quick weekend and was pleasantly surprised by the quiet room, comfy bed, and genuinely friendly front desk. Breakfast was a nice bonus too.

Thank god I got this hotel through priceline. I can't imagine paying full price for this place. The tub was moldy and dingy. The toilet didn't flush. Their selection of TV channels was limited to say the least. Unless you wanted to pay $5 for a rerun of an NBC show. Oh, and internet? Why that will set you back about $15 for the day. And breakfast? That's about $16 for a cup of coffee, a croissant and two slices of honeydew. This hotel is the pits. The customer service is....absent! When you walk in to the ridiculous lobby (decked out like some bad late 80's prom) there's no one to direct you upstairs to the check in. And once you're there, check in is very fast, i'll grant them that. This hotel is a big, crummy rip-off. I will never stay here (and will steer clear of Hyatts in general I believe).

I stayed at the Chicago Fairmont for four nights for a conference. My fiance' accompanied me. When we checked in, we were given a room with two full size beds despite the fact that our reservation was for one king size bed. So instead of relaxing on the large luxurious bed we had imagined, we were forced to either sleep in separate beds like Ward and June Cleaver or either cuddle up on a small full size like two college kids in a fraternity house! We discovered that the coffee maker wasn't working and called down to the desk to have someone look at it, and waited two and half hours. We had issues with the plumbing, including extremely slow hot water tap in the bathtub which took 45 minutes to fill. The toilet stopped working twice. We returned one afternoon from the art museum to find the maid in our room, sitting on the bed, watching the tv and talking on her cell phone. They bellman were rude, and wouldn't let my fiance unload our own car which was packed with some of his very expensive camera equipment. There were errors on our bill. Last but not least, we saw a ROACH in the drawers. Alive. The restaurant downstairs was decent, and the location is fairly good since my conference was in the Hyatt next door but for the price you can find someplace better. I will never ever stay here again under any circumstances.

I wasn't expecting much from a mid-range property, but the Palmer genuinely surprised me. The decor does lean traditional--think rich wood and classic patterned carpets--yet it's been maintained so well that it feels charming rather than tired. The staff were the real highlight: the front desk remembered my name by the second day, and the bellman gave me a fantastic local eatery tip that wasn't in any guidebook. Breakfast was a pleasant affair, with made-to-order omelets and proper strong coffee, all served without a chaotic rush. Despite being near a busy avenue, my room was remarkably quiet--the double-paned windows did their job perfectly, and I slept soundly both nights. For the rate I paid, this felt like a genuine bargain, and I'd happily book here again on my next visit.

The bathroom was spotless with excellent water pressure, and the view over the harbor made every morning feel special. Despite the central location, my room was impressively quiet, though I honestly could have stayed another night without getting bored.

The concierge was so helpful. Without hesitation they had the best recommendations for restaurants and attractions all turning out to be wonderful. They even gave us business cards for restaurants that did not take reservations so we could obtain preferential or immediate seating's. Loved the health club at the back of the hotel. By joining the presidents club, it only cost ten dollars a day to use the facilities. The rooms were large, updated and had views looking out in 3 directions. The coffee maker in the room was exceptional. Location is great for getting mostly anywhere. Parking is overpriced so we took our cart to the underground Millennium Garage that was only $25.00 per 24 hours and a few blocks walk from the hotel.

I had a very pleasant stay at Hotel James and would happily return. The location was convenient for getting around, with restaurants and shops close enough to reach on foot, but the room itself was surprisingly quiet at night. My room was clean, comfortable, and thoughtfully laid out, with a good bed, plenty of outlets, and a surprisingly nice shower. The front desk staff were consistently warm and helpful, especially when I needed directions and a late checkout. I also enjoyed the relaxed atmosphere in the lobby and the coffee available in the morning. My only minor complaint is that the room felt a little small for two suitcases, but it was still perfectly manageable. Overall, the service, cleanliness, and comfortable atmosphere made this a very easy place to recommend.

I expected more from Hotel Amalfi given the price and central location. Our room looked tired, with scuffed furniture, a stained carpet near the window, and an air conditioner that rattled loudly through the night. The bathroom was tiny and the shower pressure kept dropping to a trickle. We mentioned the noise at the desk, but were told the hotel was full and nothing could be done. Breakfast was another letdown: lukewarm coffee, limited pastries, and very few tables available. The staff were not rude, just distracted and slow to respond. Location was convenient for walking around, but that was about the only positive. I would choose somewhere better maintained next time.
The view from our room was spectacular, and the linens were so crisp I slept like a log. The space felt fresh and modern, not dated at all, which was a pleasant surprise for such a classic property.
Disappointing stay at the Omni: the bathroom was cramped and dated, hallway noise kept waking me, breakfast was bland and overpriced, and I barely slept.

Stayed at Hotel James for a long weekend and honestly couldn't have asked for a better base. The location is fantastic--steps from the park and easy walking to everything we wanted to see, though we also used the bikes they lend out, which was a nice touch. Room was quiet and dark at night, which I always appreciate, and the bed was genuinely comfortable, not just hotel-speak. The coffee in the lobby each morning was a lifesaver before heading out. Staff surprised me most, though--they remembered our names at breakfast and gave spot-on tips for a neighborhood spot we ended up loving. Valet was quick every time, even on Saturday night. Minor nitpick: the shower pressure could be stronger, but that's about it. Already planning a return.

Checking in was seamless--the front desk team even remembered my name the next morning, which felt personal without being overbearing. The bathroom was a genuine highlight: a rain shower with strong pressure, plus a deep soaking tub that I actually used twice. I'd booked three nights but left wishing for one more, though that's more a compliment than a complaint. The location made exploring easy, yet the rooms insulated me from street noise entirely. For the rate I paid, considering the breakfast spread and the evening turndown service with chocolates, I felt the value was solid--not a steal, but fair for the quality. Staff everywhere, from housekeeping to the concierge, were attentive without hovering. I'd gladly return, and likely will on my next trip.

The room was dated and smelled musty, and the 'sea view' was mostly a parking lot. Breakfast felt like an afterthought with cold eggs, and the staff seemed annoyed by every request. Not worth the price for what you get.

Disappointing stay at the Swissotel. Room was dated with a stained carpet, check-in took forever, and the 'luxury' breakfast was cold and overpriced. Staff seemed indifferent throughout. Expected far more for this price.

I really wanted to love the Fairmont, but the experience fell flat. The room felt dated and the air conditioning was painfully loud. Service was slow everywhere, and we waited over an hour for room service that arrived cold.

We had a great weekend at the Hard Rock. The room was spotless, comfortable, and had a fun music-inspired style without feeling overdone. Staff at the front desk were genuinely welcoming and quickly helped us arrange a late checkout. Breakfast was better than expected: plenty of hot choices, fresh fruit, pastries, and good coffee, with servers who kept things moving even during the busy morning rush. Our room faced the street, so there was a little city noise early in the evening, but once the windows were closed it was quiet enough to sleep well. It is not the cheapest option, but the central location, attentive service, and overall atmosphere made it feel worth the price.
The WiFi dropped constantly, and breakfast was cold scrambled eggs with stale pastries. Location was central, but the view faced a brick wall. Disappointing stay overall, especially for the price.

I LOVED this hotel. The room was so chic and trendy, the bed was comfortable, great slippers and robes. I love the Keihl's bath products in the bathroom. We went during my birthday weekend, and they had a card and plate with pastries waiting in the room. We got a great deal on a junior suite from Travelzoo, but when we tried to take another trip to Chicago, the deal was gone. I really recommend the hotel. I LOVED it. The ONLY problem we had was with the David Burke Steakhouse. The service was horrible, they switched our order with the table next to our's and the only compensation was they took off a $7 side dish we ordered (and they were nice enough to NOT charge us for the other side dish we DIDN'T get). DON'T go there. Go to the Lawry's accross the street. But stay at the James. (BTW- its not a 3-star hotel like the website lists- its at least 4-star)

We stayed 2 nights at the Knickerbocker and could not have had a better stay. The hotel has recently renovated there rooms. The staff could not have been more friendly and helpful from Dave and Cora at the martini bar to Julie at the front desk who help out with an upgrade for us. The hotel has everything you need for your stay and is close to all the fun that Chicago offers. Our pick for THE CITY is the Knickerbocker. JOHN and JUDY.

The Hilton's Wi‐Fi dropped constantly during my three‐night stay, and our room overlooked a grimy rooftop with no hint of skyline. The decor felt tired, with peeling wallpaper and dated furniture, making the visit drag on far longer than it should have.

The room's floor-to-ceiling window faced the bay, and I'll admit I spent at least an hour just watching the ferries slide past at dusk--lights flickering on one by one. Wi‐Fi was rock solid throughout, even from the balcony, which surprised me given how many devices I had connected. The bed was the real highlight: firm but plush, and I slept straight through until my alarm, which never happens in hotels. The bathroom mirrored the rest of the space, all cool marble and a rain shower with real pressure; the soaps smelled of cedar and citrus, a nice switch from the usual generic bottles. Staff checked me in quickly and even remembered my coffee order at breakfast the next morning. If you want a dependable, quietly luxurious escape without any fuss, this place earns its name--I'd book again without hesitating.

Honestly, I expected a lot more from a Hyatt at this price point. We were there three nights and it felt like a week in the worst way. The room overlooked the loading dock, so every morning around 5:30 the delivery trucks started backing up with that relentless beeping. Even with earplugs I barely slept -- the walls are paper-thin too, and I could hear the neighbors' TV until well past midnight. When I called the front desk about the noise, they promised someone would look into it, and unsurprisingly nobody ever did. The view was a gray shaft between two buildings, nothing you'd want to linger on. Housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely. Two good things: the bed itself was comfortable, and the lobby coffee was decent. That's about all I can praise. Won't be returning.

We travel to Chicago frequently and have stayed in many of the hotels downtown. We were excited to try the Swissotel, but left disappointed. The actual hotel and rooms were very nice with amazing views, the staff was extremely rude. The man that checked us in was on the phone and did not acknowledge us until he was done with his phone call. He then did not say more than five words, which were 'I need a credit card'. The lobby bar had fireplaces and was very cozy. The hotel information said it closed at 2am so we came back to hotel at 1230am for a 'night cap', that was last call. That was fine for us, but the bar was full and many people were coming back from their night wanting a 'night cap' but did not make last call. Our night ended listening to many unhappy people complaining and receiving no sympathy from the employees. There are many places to stay in the area that are just as nice or nicer, no need to stay at the Swissotel again. Definitely don't stay if you're looking for a romantic weekend away, the employees will ruin your experience from the second you walk in the door.

We booked the Intercontinental expecting their signature standard, but our stay fell far short. The room itself felt tired; the carpet had visible stains near the armchair, and the duvet cover was wrinkled with what looked like a dried spill. Our 'city view' was mostly a brick wall and a sliver of a parking garage, which made the space feel claustrophobic. The bathroom was the biggest letdown--the grout was discolored, the shower pressure dribbled, and the tiny bottle of shampoo was nearly empty. To make matters worse, the walls were paper-thin. We heard the neighboring guests' TV until nearly midnight, and then the elevator bell chimed every few minutes from the corridor. All of this for nearly $400 a night. I've had better sleep in a roadside motel. The staff were polite but offered no apology or adjustment when we mentioned the noise at checkout. Disappointing, especially for the brand's reputation.

We stayed for five nights at the Ambassador, and honestly, it exceeded what we expected from a city-center hotel. The moment we walked in, the doorman remembered our names from the second day on--that little personal touch meant a lot. Our room on the seventh floor was quiet, spotless, and had a brilliant view of the old town's rooftops, though the bathroom could've used a slightly stronger shower head. The breakfast spread was generous, with made-to-order omelets and pastries that stayed fresh. We had a minor issue with the air conditioning on the first evening, but the front desk sent a technician within ten minutes and followed up the next morning to make sure everything was fine. The pool area is small but pleasant, and the bar staff mix a solid negroni. If you want a comfortable, attentive stay without any fuss, this is it. We'd gladly return.

The heating in our room didn't work and wasn't repaired depite numerous requests, the rooms were very small, the litter in the bin remained in the bin for the whole stay, the cleaner made the bed but nothing else, when we returned home my credit card statement showed that the hotel had charged me for the 5 night stay despite my having pre-paid through a travel agent, it took the hotel 2 months to re-credit my card without an apology or offer to pay for my numerous trans-Atlantic phone calls to them.

The location was good. Check-in was ok. Asked for non smoking room, given floor with half smoking half non smoking. We could smell the smoke as soon as the elevator doors opened. We asked for and recieved a room on a non-smoking floor. They did not bring up the key, we had to go down to the lobby to get it. Breakfast could have had some healthy choices, the sweet rolls and danish were not fresh. Bananas not ripe. Room only had ONE wash cloth, had to call down for more. Housekeeping NEVER showed up at our room. Not for turndown service , not for the morning clean -up. Called down upon our arrival back to our room after being gone all day and we were accused of putting our the Do Not Disturb sign. They said they would come up and they never came when they said they would. We finally told them not to come because of the time. We wanted to get ready to go out for dinner. Never greeted by anyone as we came and went. I have stayed at the Peninsula and the Burnham. The Burnham was booked during our stay or I would have stayed there.I will NEVER stay at this hotel again, Not worth 300.00 a night
Disappointing stay at Hotel James: the room felt tired, housekeeping missed the basics, and street noise made sleeping difficult. For the price, I expected much better.

We paid Sofitel prices expecting a proper luxury stay and left genuinely let down. The first night was a write-off: the room overlooked the mechanical units on the roof, and even with the windows sealed the droning kept me up until nearly three. When I asked to move, the second room was better for noise but the air conditioning rattled constantly, so sleep was a struggle either way. Housekeeping was hit and miss too -- a makeup-stained hand towel stayed in the bathroom our whole stay, and one afternoon the bed wasn't made at all. The decor hasn't been refreshed in years, honestly; the purple-and-gold accent scheme and scuffed armchair felt very early 2000s, nothing like the sleek lobby photos online. Staff were polite enough, but politeness doesn't fix a worn-out, noisy hotel. I won't be back.

I booked the Hyatt expecting more, but the noise from the hallway kept me up all night and the AC unit rattled constantly. Staff were polite but unhelpful about the issues, and honestly, the room felt worn down for what they charge.

The hotel was undergoing renovations so it was dirty and noisy. The entrance was really scary since it was covered with scaffolding, making it dark. They charge a lot for internet hook up, wifi is not included. The staff was very slow, I am assuming they were all new. They could not say where anything was or what attractions were nearby. The room was set up weird, the bathroom opened facing the bed, rather than the hall as most do. Room temp was hard to control, even though they had a digital thermostat. Overall I was very disappointed, had I been staying more than one night I would have switched hotels.

The location is genuinely unbeatable--steps from everything you'd want to see--but that's where the positives end for me. I paid a premium expecting a boutique experience, yet the room felt tired, with scuffed furniture and a bathroom that smelled faintly of damp towels. The wifi was an absolute joke; it dropped constantly, forcing me to hotspot my phone for basic work. Despite the central address, I barely slept--the street noise filtered through the supposedly soundproofed windows like they were open, and the thin walls meant I heard my neighbor's TV until 2 AM. For the nightly rate, which rivaled four-star chains, I expected better insulation and reliable connectivity. The staff were polite during check-in, but no one offered a solution when I mentioned the noise. I left feeling robbed and exhausted. If you value sleep or stable internet, look elsewhere--this place trades on its address alone.

The elevator system was impossible. It seems they were trying to improve it but only made it worse. Many people waited 15+ minutes and some bailed out to the stair wells. It happened several times. I had read about it before booking but guess I didn't take it seriously. It'd be a deal breaker for any future return unless I heard clearly it was improved. Also, I always think it's lame that you have to pay extra for WiFi. Area recommendations North Michigan Avenue and Lake front areas are best.

Stayed at the Knickerbocker for a weekend escape and honestly couldn't have asked for smoother. The location is perfect for wandering, but the real win was the cozy room with a great view and the friendliest front desk crew I've met in ages. Would happily return.

We stayed at the Hotel Palmer for three nights over a long weekend and honestly couldn't have asked for better. The location is ideal -- a short walk to the river and plenty of restaurants nearby without being in the middle of the noisy tourist strip. Our room was on the sixth floor, quiet, with a really comfortable bed that made sleeping in dangerously easy. The front desk staff went out of their way twice for us, once to print our train tickets and again when we asked where to find a good bakery in the morning (they pointed us to one two blocks over that was excellent). Breakfast buffet had a decent spread, nothing wild, but the coffee was actually good which matters more to me than it probably should. Small things: fast wifi, plenty of outlets by the bed, housekeeping was thorough. Would happily book again.
Hotel Palmer was a letdown: the Wi-Fi kept dropping, the room overlooked a grim alley, and hallway noise lasted late into the night. The bathroom floor and sheets also felt poorly cleaned.
Hard Rock looked lively online, but our room was noisy all night, the AC barely cooled, and check-in took forever. For the price, it felt worn down and frustrating.

The bathroom was the first crack in the facade. The caulking around the tub was black with mildew, and the provided 'premium' toiletries were empty, cheaply refilled bottles. I get that midtown isn't cheap, but for this price, I expected more than a lukewarm dribble from the showerhead. Location-wise, you can't beat it for Bryant Park, but that's the sole saving grace. My room faced a brick wall, so the view was a depressing expanse of soot. Breakfast was a chaotic, overpriced buffet where the scrambled eggs were rubbery and the coffee tasted burnt. The staff were polite but overwhelmed, clearly stretched thin. I've stayed at far better Hiltons for less. This one felt like a faded, tired husk of a hotel, relying entirely on its address. I was genuinely relieved to check out.

Went there for business and the Hard Rock Hotel on Wacker Drive was recommended. I was to meet my girlfriend there who had arrived 1 hour before me. When she go there at 6PM, the room wasn't ready, the phone didn't work, the shower didn't work. When I got there she was already very upset. I called the manager to complain, but was put on hold for 30 min. I could hear everything in the room next to me as if there wasn't any wall separating us. I asked for a wake up call, but nobody called me the next morning. When I called to complain the next day, the told me the phone system was down. Ordered room service and got the wrong order... The building is very old and the elevator sounds like it is on its last breath... I would not recommend it to anyone Patrick

The location was the only saving grace. Room was tired, the AC rattled all night, and housekeeping ignored our do-not-disturb sign twice. Front desk shrugged off the noise complaint. Paid way too much for what felt like a budget stay. Won't be back.

Stayed here for a long weekend and was genuinely impressed. The location is unbeatable--we walked to the harbour and the old town in under ten minutes, which made sightseeing effortless. I'll admit I was a little worried the interiors might feel tired, but the lobby and our room struck a nice balance between classic elegance and modern touches; the carpet was spotless and the furniture felt well-maintained. Our corner room offered a sweeping view over the marina, and watching the boats come in at sunset was a real highlight. The Wi-Fi was reliable throughout, which let me catch up on emails without any frustrating drops, and even streaming a film at night worked without buffering. Breakfast had plenty of variety, and the staff were attentive without hovering. Minor quibble: the gym could use a few more free weights, but that's nitpicking. I'd happily return.

I am a fan of Kimpton Hotels, however I have never experienced top service as I did at the Hotel Allegro. Even before my visit, concierge Mark Kraemer advised us on things to see, and booked tickets in advance to Second City. We were welcomed warmly on arrival, and the bellman checked up on us as we came and went from the hotel. All the staff have a personal interest in making your stay a great experience. The hotel is next to City Hall, where I had some business. We had a large quiet room, and used room service-the meal came quickly, and included a a bonus fruit cup. Enjoyed the pasta night (20 dollars for a three course meal) at the 312 restaurant-the starter and the dessert were wonderful, the main pasta a bit too salty. And that is the only complaint I can make-from start to finish, if you want attentive service, this is the place to be. Thank you, Hotel Allegro, for a great stay. I can't wait to return.

We booked the Fairmont for a milestone anniversary, expecting the usual level of polish you associate with the name. Instead, we got a masterclass in indifference. Check-in took over twenty minutes because only one agent was on duty, and she seemed genuinely annoyed that we had questions about parking. The room itself was tired--carpet stains near the window, a lampshade with a visible scorch mark, and a bathroom door that wouldn't close without a firm shove. Housekeeping skipped our turndown service entirely, and when I called to ask about it, they said 'maybe tomorrow' and hung up. The bar was the one bright spot, but even there, the cocktail list was half out of stock. For nearly $600 a night, I expect better than a sad, worn-out room and staff who treat you like an inconvenience. We won't be back.

Great location near midtown, but that's the only plus. The bathroom was grimy with mold in the shower, the room dusty, and constant street noise made sleeping nearly impossible. Disappointing overall.

The Conrad looked impressive online, but the room felt tired and noisy, housekeeping missed basic requests, and breakfast was overcrowded and overpriced. I expected a much smoother experience for the rate.

The Fairmont was exactly what we needed after a long trip--room was spotless and quiet, and the staff remembered our name at breakfast. The lobby felt grand without being stuffy, and the location made everything walkable. Would happily book again.
Disappointing stay at the Sofitel: the room looked tired, housekeeping missed several basics, and the street noise made sleeping difficult. For the price, I expected far better service and upkeep.
The Sheraton was worth the price, with a spotless, modern bathroom and a generous breakfast spread. Staff were consistently warm and helpful, making the whole stay easy and comfortable.
Booked for the location, but the room felt worn and noisy, the shower barely had pressure, and staff seemed indifferent when we mentioned the broken AC.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly couldn't have picked a better spot. The lobby has this warm, moody vibe that immediately felt like a escape from the city noise, even though you're right in the middle of everything. Our room was on the quieter side, which was a pleasant surprise--the blackout curtains actually worked, and the bed was that perfect level of firm with soft sheets. I'm still thinking about the breakfast spread; the fresh pastries and made-to-order omelets were a step above typical hotel fare. The staff genuinely seemed happy to help, from the doorman who remembered our name to the front desk arranging a last-minute spa slot. Only tiny hiccup was the elevator wait during checkout rush, but that's hardly worth complaining about. Great value for the location and vibe--I'd definitely book again.

I stayed at the Sheraton for a conference last week and left genuinely impressed. The location is unbeatable if you need to be in the heart of the city, but what really stood out was how smoothly everything ran. The front desk staff were warm and efficient, even with a long line at check-in. My room was on a higher floor and surprisingly quiet, with a comfy bed and blackout curtains that actually worked. I'm a light sleeper, so that mattered. The club lounge had a solid breakfast spread, and the espresso machine was a lifesaver each morning. I also used the pool one evening--it was clean and not overcrowded. The only minor hiccup was slow elevator service during peak hours, but it didn't ruin anything. For the price and the level of service, I'd absolutely book here again.

I believe I can not describe how amazing was our stay at The James. Service was impecable, from the door man to the front desk. Location could not be better. Yes, you can hear the ambulances in the street from the 14th floor, but, come on, you are downtown, what do you expect....Overall noise was not in a level to bother us. The only minor incident was a cleaner that tried to open our room to clean at 9 pm...PM not AM? Go figure...

The Knickerbocker had so much potential, but our anniversary stay felt like a disappointment wrapped in faded grandeur. The room's carpet was visibly stained near the minibar, and the bathroom grout had a suspicious, dark film that made me keep my slippers on. Honestly, two nights felt like an eternity because the noise was relentless--every door slam in the hallway echoed, and we could hear the couple next door arguing until 2 AM. The decor was a strange time capsule: brass fixtures and floral wallpaper that might've been chic in 1989, but now just felt tired and dusty. Even the lobby's chandelier seemed dimmed by neglect. We checked out a day early, but the front desk still charged us fully, citing a policy we never saw. For the price, I'd expect fresh linens, not a pre-owned vibe. Skip it unless you're desperate for a retro-themed nap.

Don't stay here if you take peace in knowing you have a reservation. About 3 months ago, we booked a room here for our wedding night (which is in less than 2 weeks). My fiance called last week to confirm the room and everything was great until today when they called to bump us to another hotel - no upgrades, no discounts. Apparently it is my problem that their manager can't manage the convention schedule. I don't even want to stay at another Kimpton Hotel because I don't find their reservation system reliable. Unfortunately, due to the conference, there isn't any other place to stay.

I really wanted to love the Monaco based on the photos, but our stay was a letdown from start to finish. Check-in took almost forty minutes because they were understaffed, and no one apologized. Our room faced the alley, so we heard garbage trucks at 5am both mornings despite requesting a quiet room weeks in advance. The air conditioning barely worked and the front desk just shrugged, offering nothing. Housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely. Breakfast was cold and the buffet ran out of most items by 9am. For the price, I expected far better service and basic comfort. Location is decent, but honestly that was the only redeeming thing. Won't be returning.

Absolutely loved my stay at Hotel Allegro. The location is unbeatable--steps from the theater district and a quick walk to the Loop, yet the rooms are surprisingly quiet. I was a little worried the historic building might feel dated, but the mix of vintage charm and modern updates is spot on. My king room was cozy but well laid out, with a plush bed and excellent blackout curtains that made sleeping in a breeze. The staff genuinely stood out: the front desk remembered my name by my second morning and even texted me a dinner reservation suggestion that turned out to be fantastic. Housekeeping was thorough without being intrusive. The lobby bar has a great buzz in the evenings, and the breakfast service was efficient, though nothing extraordinary. For the price, especially on a weekend rate, this is a steal. I'd happily return and already recommended it to colleagues visiting for shows.

Triple A rate with upgrade to view room was less than $200 which also included breakfast vouchers. Had a great view of river, lake, Wrigley Bldg. & Tribune Bldg. Most major restaurants, Shopping, Sightseeing attractions within walking distance. Large room with a very comfortable bed.
The Sheraton looked impressive online, but the stay was disappointing: a long check-in, tired room furnishings, and thin walls made it hard to relax, especially for the price.
The Talbott looked charming online, but our room was worn and noisy, and the front desk seemed indifferent when we mentioned the broken thermostat.

This review has two parts. . .I advise reading both. Chapter One: The actual hotel and staff I found the in house staff to be very friendly and accommodating. The room was nice and clean as well. I have no disagreement with any of the other reviews regarding the hotel room or the staff. This is a great location where you can walk three blocks to to the South to reach the riverfront, or a few blocks to reach the water tower to the North. Very easy (one block) walk from the subway (Red line). The morning complimentary breakfast is substantial. Not just muffins and coffee. You can have a complete breakfast here if you want. And, even the breakfast servers were really nice and efficient. I would recommend this hotel IF based solely on the physical location, the room, and the staff. Chapter Two: The nightmare I booked this room through central reservations in July for a mid-September arrival. The rate was quoted to me as $159 per night for four nights. When the confirmation was emailed to me, it was incorrect by over $300. I immediately called the hotel. They said they made the correction and emailed a new confirmation with the correct amount. I did receive the corrected confirmation email. . .All done? NO. One week later, my credit card statement arrives with the old higher amount having been charged. I called the hotel and was transferred to central reservations to resolve. When I explained the error, I was literally called a liar by the person in reservations, and told 'That's not my problem. I can't help you'. . . and then told that I have to pay the higher amount. Excuse ME? Now, I go back to calling the hotel manager to get some assistance. After a few left messages, I get the general manager to call me back, and discuss the issue. After taking down all of the names of people I spoke with, he assures me that he will credit the account immediately. I even get a call from someone in his accounting dept to confirm my credit card etc. . . One week later, still no credit. So, I call the general manager again. Oh, this might take up to 72 hours to process, I am told. So, please give it another week. Another week passes, still no credit. So another call to the manager. I am told now that the credit HAS been processed, and he even sends me an email confirming our 'agreement' for the credit, just to appease me. Another week passes. Still, not seeing that credit that was 'definitely processed' a week ago. Yet another call to the general manager on the day before I am to leave on my trip to Chicago. I told him I will be arriving, and at this point, I want to see him personally, and he can physically use my credit card to process the credit while I am there. Remember, we are now talking SIX WEEKS and this is still not resolved. I arrive at the hotel, and to make a long story short, the general manager was NEVER available to see me, nor did he make any attempts to schedule any time to see or talk with me. The only person I spoke face to face with, was the assistant general manager. He was completely unconcerned with my situation, and made the completely inappropriate statement to me of 'you realize this boils down to a matter of 'he said she said''. . . WHAT???? Today, my trip is over, and I have flown back home. I STILL HAVE NOT RECEIVED THE CREDIT TO MY ACCOUNT!!! I will absolutely be reporting all of this to Hilton Corporate Customer Service, and will absolutely be disputing the entire amount at this point. Take this little adventure into consideration when dealing with this hotel.
My room at Affinia overlooked a lively avenue, but it was quiet enough for deep sleep. Everything was spotless, and the Wi-Fi stayed reliable throughout my visit.

The Sofitel was a lovely stay, with a beautifully quiet room, exceptionally comfortable bed, and genuinely attentive staff. Breakfast was fresh and varied, making it easy to relax from the moment we arrived.

I had a very pleasant stay at the Hyatt and would happily return. Check-in was quick and friendly, even though I arrived later than expected, and the front desk staff gave me a few useful local recommendations. My room was clean, quiet, and more spacious than I anticipated, with a comfortable bed, plenty of outlets, and a surprisingly nice city view. I also appreciated the strong Wi-Fi and the small coffee setup in the morning. Breakfast had a good variety, and everything I tried was fresh, though the restaurant got busy around 9 a.m. The fitness center was well maintained, and housekeeping kept the room tidy without being intrusive. The location made it easy to walk to restaurants and nearby attractions. Overall, it was a comfortable, polished experience with genuinely helpful service.

Breakfast at the Hard Rock was surprisingly solid for a hotel--think made-to-order omelets and a decent spread of fresh fruit and pastries, not just the usual sad continental slap. The staff genuinely set the tone though; the front desk crew remembered my name by day two and the bellman flagged me down with a spare umbrella when a freak storm rolled in. Honestly, for what you get--the location, the pool, the little rock-and-roll touches in the room--it felt like a fair deal, even if the weekend rate stings a bit. I was braced for thin walls and party noise, but my floor was quiet after 11, and the blackout curtains did the heavy lifting for sleep. A couple of minor wear marks in the hallway kept it from a perfect score, but I'd book again without hesitation.

Let me first start by saying I have always been pleased with the Conrad hotels and that is why I chose the Conrad Chicago. I was very disappointed in the level of service. 3 phone calls to get maintenance to fix the bathroom sink, unpleasant experience in the Terrace resturant, front desk not aware of room eminities, and a very uncaring MOD! All the Conrad hotels I have stayed at have been 5 STAR but not this one. I have to give it 2 stars!!!:(

This hotel is rather stupid to be frank. It's a horrible attempt to be retro-sheek but ends up looking similar to that Saturday Night live skit where things are so sheek that they are not functional. The rooms are about the size of a shoe box and there isn't much in them. I actually like the Pedestal in the bathroom but there is no sink. I had to put my make-up on using the toliet for 5-days. It also took me 10-minutes to figure out how to turn on the shower and the bathroom is more like a closet then anything. I had guests over one evening and everyone could hear everyone pee b/c the bathroom doors aren't doors at all and there is no bathroom fan! It was just over the top for me and lots of costruction nearby to keep you up at night. On a good note, the staff are really friendly and the place is really clean. That's about the only good thing I can say about this place. I would not go back.

Hotel Amalfi made our weekend in Rome feel wonderfully easy. Our room was spotless and comfortable, with a supportive bed and blackout curtains that helped us sleep deeply every night. Despite being close to Termini, the room was surprisingly quiet; we only noticed faint hallway sounds in the morning. The staff were warm, efficient, and happy to suggest nearby trattorias. Wi‐Fi worked reliably for maps, messages, and a short video call, which was a relief. Breakfast was simple but fresh, with good coffee and pastries. We stayed three nights, and honestly it felt too short--we would gladly return for a longer visit.

The room's 'clean' look faded fast--sticky floors and a dusty nightstand. Our so-called city view was a brick wall, breakfast was cold scrambled eggs, and the hallway noise kept us up until midnight. Definitely not worth the price.

My stay at Hotel Talbott was exactly what I needed--charming without trying too hard. The building has that old-school character you don't find in chain hotels, with creaky floors and a cozy lobby that smells faintly of wood polish. I booked a standard king, but the room felt generous, with a window seat overlooking the quiet side street and a bed I actually sank into. The front desk clerk remembered my name when I asked for extra towels, which was a small touch that went a long way. Breakfast was simple--pastries, fruit, decent coffee--but served in a sunlit nook that felt more like a friend's dining room than a hotel. Location-wise, it's a short walk to the river and a bunch of good restaurants, though the walls are a bit thin; I heard my neighbor's TV one night, but it faded by 10. All in all, a warm, unpretentious place I'd happily return to.

We choose to stay at the hotel due to the high rooftop ratings at the hotel. Not only is the rooftop terrace on the 5th floor, but it was occuppied with private corporate events for the entire duration of our stay. We did - as recommended - have a drink indoors only to be highly insulted by their bartender there. There is no breakfast buffet - you order a la carte. Keep that in mind when paying extra for breakfast and internet. Also note that the minibar is empty on arrival - we were only told on departure that we would have needed to call reception to order. We have stayed at the Omni before and it as a much better experience. I dont recommend spending so much for a mediocre hotel.

We stayed at the Hotel Knickerbocker for a long weekend in the city and honestly it exceeded what I was expecting. The location near Times Square could have meant chaos, but the hotel itself feels like a quiet pocket of calm once you step inside. Our room was compact but thoughtfully designed, with a really comfortable bed and blackout curtains that made sleeping through the noise outside a non-issue. The bathroom had great water pressure and nice toiletries too. The staff were genuinely warm, not the fake-polite kind, and the concierge gave us two dinner recommendations that ended up being highlights of the trip. St. Cloud, the rooftop bar, is expensive but worth one drink for the view. Small knocks: elevators got busy at peak times and the AC ran a bit loud. Still, we'd absolutely return.
The Fairmont room was spotless, with a bright bathroom and excellent shower. The bed was wonderfully comfortable, I slept soundly, and the courteous staff made everything feel effortless.

I stayed at the Sheraton as it was where a conference I was attending was being held. On the plus side, the hotel is reasonably well located, within a few minutes walk of Michigan Avenue. My room had a superb view out over the river. However, for the price I must say that the room look decidedly shabby and worn and is in need of refurbishment. The decor was dated, and my bathroom unit was cracked and the shower rail rusty. The wifi is ridiculously expensive, and frustratingly as a conference delegate I was unable to use the service downstairs in the venue despite having paid for 24 hours access. There was no wifi in the conference rooms, although it was free in the lobby area should you wish to sit there and do your emails. I know Chicago is expensive, but for that price I feel the experience should have been better.

Expected more from the Conrad. Room felt dated for the price, and housekeeping skipped our floor twice. Front desk was polite but slow. GREAT location though--sadly that's the only highlight of our stay.

The Omni left me feeling genuinely underwhelmed. The bathroom was cramped, with a showerhead that dribbled water sideways and a towel rack that fell off the wall when I reached for a fresh one. My 'city view' turned out to be a direct line into an office building's HVAC units, so I kept the curtains drawn the entire time. The wifi was a sore spot--connection dropped constantly, making it impossible to stream anything or even hold a simple video call for work. Oddly, my two-night stay felt both too short and too long: too short to offset the travel hassle, but too long after the third cold shower and the fourth hour of internet frustration. The bed was comfortable, I'll grant that, but this was not the relaxing retreat I'd booked. I left more stressed than when I arrived, and I won't be returning.

Booked a king room and got a double with a view of the parking garage. The hallway smelled like stale smoke, and housekeeping never showed up despite asking twice. Breakfast was cold scrambled eggs and watery juice. Definitely not worth the price.
Hotel Allegro looked stylish online, but our room was cramped, the air conditioning rattled all night, and the front desk never followed up on our complaint.

The Sofitel's quiet luxury was exactly what I needed--slept like a log in blissful silence. Spotless room, plush bedding, and a marble bathroom with a rain shower that felt spa-level. Wouldn't hesitate to return.
Hotel Amalfi was a pleasant stay: the room was spotless, the sea view was lovely, and the modern bathroom had good water pressure. Wi-Fi worked reliably throughout.
My room had stained carpets and a musty smell, while hallway noise kept me awake most of the night. Breakfast was lukewarm and sparse, making the stay even more disappointing.

Wish our weekend at the Knickerbocker had been longer--two nights flew by. Room was blissfully quiet despite Times Square location, wifi never dropped once, and the breakfast spread was genuinely excellent. Would return in a heartbeat.
The Knickerbocker made our weekend in New York feel effortless--stylish room, genuinely helpful staff, and an excellent rooftop bar with unforgettable Times Square views. I'd happily stay here again.
Swissotel's decor is a little dated but still comfortable, and the Wi-Fi worked reliably throughout my stay. For the price, it felt like good value, and the bed made for excellent sleep.

Disappointing for the price. My room had dust on the sill and a stained armchair, the wifi kept dropping every few minutes, and breakfast was a sad buffet with rubbery eggs and cold coffee. Won't be returning to the Talbott.
Great stay at the Hilton -- comfy bed, spotless room, and the executive lounge breakfast was a nice bonus. Front desk sorted a late checkout without any fuss. Would happily return.

Our two-night stay at the InterContinental felt far too long, which is not what I expected at this price point. The lobby is impressive, but the room was dated, with worn furniture and a loud air-conditioning unit that cycled on all night. I barely slept because of the noise from both the unit and the hallway. Service was polite but slow; we waited nearly 40 minutes for extra towels. Breakfast looked plentiful, yet the hot items were lukewarm and the coffee was weak. For the premium rate, I expected a more comfortable room, better attention to detail, and a genuinely restful experience.

We stayed at the Sheraton for a long weekend and honestly expected better for the price. Check-in took almost forty minutes because the front desk seemed understaffed, and when we finally got to our room the air conditioning barely worked. We called twice about it and nobody came up until the next morning. The bed itself was fine, but the bathroom had hair in the tub and stale towels that I had to exchange myself at the housekeeping cart. Breakfast was the biggest letdown. Over $30 per person for cold eggs, watery oatmeal, and a coffee machine that kept jamming. The lobby looks impressive, sure, but the service behind it falls flat. Location is convenient, I'll give it that, yet with so many other hotels nearby, I won't be back here. Disappointing overall.

We stayed at the Fairmont two Saturday's in a row, and both stays were disappointing. We had to call the hotel prior to each stay and both times it took the hotel 30-40 minutes to answer their phone. For the price, we expected nicer decor (it looked cheaply done); more comfortable beds-the mattresses were too soft and the sheets too hard-pillows weren't comfortable either; a more accomodating front desk staff. Our friends who were also there on the same dates will undoubtably add similar comments.

The Intercontinental looked impressive, but the room felt tired, check-in was painfully slow, and housekeeping missed basic details. For the price, I expected polished service and left feeling genuinely disappointed.

I had a really pleasant stay at Hotel Talbott. The location in the Gold Coast was ideal--quiet enough to sleep well, but close to great restaurants, shopping, and the lakefront. My room was spacious, spotless, and surprisingly quiet for being in the city, with a very comfortable bed and a good-sized bathroom. The staff made the experience especially enjoyable; everyone I spoke with was welcoming, efficient, and happy to offer recommendations. I also appreciated the small touches, like the lobby atmosphere and the easy access to coffee in the morning. Check-in was quick, and checkout was just as smooth. The only minor issue was that the Wi-Fi slowed down briefly one evening, but it didn't affect my stay. I would happily return on my next Chicago trip.
Overpriced for a tired, poorly cleaned room with dusty surfaces; the cramped bathroom had weak water pressure, and staff seemed indifferent when we raised concerns.

My wife & I celebrated our anniversary at the Knickerbocker & could not have been treated better. Before we were out of our cab, our bags had been loaded on a cart & we were walked into the hotel by a doorman. The rooms were well appointed & the entire hotel staff was very friendly. This is a prime location for shopping, sightseeing or nightlife.
Homewood's location was convenient for getting around, but our stay felt too short to justify the steep price; staff were polite yet distant, making the experience disappointing.

Beautiful historic hotel -- and since I'm in historic building business, was looking forward to stay. Moved rooms on second night because of loud party in adjacent suite, they escorted me to a room that was completely torn up -- duct work torn apart in bathroom, lamp fixtures literally falling off wall, mirror torn off wall, etc. Ended up in a room on 20th floor -- much nicer, but yesterday waited 10 minutes for elevator on two separate occasions. Only two of three elevators to top floors work -- and these two elevators skip floors, so you can be stuck waiting for ever. When I raised this to hotel staff, was told this was an old hotel and basically to stuff it. Umm, no. This is not an old building problem, this is a fixable elevator problem if anyone cared enough to fix it. Thumbs way down, stay away. Go to the Drake or Knickerbocker if you're looking for old world charm, sans hassle.

We reserved a room with a sleeper couch a few weeks before our stay. After checking in and unpacking, we discovered that the sleeper sofa had been removed (supposedly during renovation). The front desk clerk and bellman never mentioned that there was no sleeper sofa even though they saw all 4 of us check into the room. Colleen, one of the managers, was argumentative and did nothing to resolve the problem. We ended up having one of our children sleep on the couch and the other slept on an antiquated rollaway bed. We never spoke to the general manager who was conveniently 'absent from the hotel' during most of our stay. We stayed here on more than one occasion over the past decade and had never encountered such incompetence. We had to make several phone calls to receive a miserly discount and we never received an apology. The lack of training of the staff was clearly evident, as was the cavalier attitude of the management.
Disappointing stay at the Fairmont: the room felt dated, housekeeping missed basic details, and the service was strangely indifferent for a hotel at this price. I expected far more.

I had a really pleasant stay at the Hyatt and would happily return. Check-in was quick, and the front desk team was warm without being overly formal. My room was spotless, quiet at night, and had a comfortable bed with plenty of pillows. I also appreciated the small details, like good water pressure in the shower, blackout curtains, and enough outlets near the desk to work easily. Breakfast had a nice range of fresh fruit, pastries, eggs, and coffee that was actually decent. The location made it simple to get around, and staff gave helpful restaurant suggestions nearby. The lobby felt busy but relaxed, and overall the hotel was well maintained. It was not the cheapest option, but the service and comfort made it feel worth it.

We booked a standard room for a quick weekend getaway, and honestly, the spotless condition of it blew me away. The white linens were crisp, and the bathroom smelled like fresh citrus, which was a lovely touch after a long drive. Our window faced the inner courtyard, so instead of a grand vista, we got a peaceful view of the small fountain and the late afternoon sun hitting the ivy. It was calming, not flashy. The front desk team, especially a gentleman named Marco, was incredibly attentive, even calling up to check if we needed extra pillows after seeing us check in with a toddler. Though we had planned for two nights, the time flew by--we barely had a chance to use the pool. It felt far too short, and we left with that familiar, wistful feeling of wanting just one more lazy morning in the big, soft bed.

I expected more from a Hyatt, especially for the price. Check-in took nearly 25 minutes because only one person was working the desk, and nobody acknowledged the line. The room looked clean at first, but the carpet had stains, the bathroom fan rattled all night, and the air conditioning barely cooled the room. I also had to call twice for extra towels, which arrived late in the evening. Breakfast was disappointing: lukewarm coffee, sparse options, and several empty trays that were never refilled. The location was convenient, but that was about the only positive. Staff were polite when available, yet the hotel felt understaffed and poorly maintained. I would choose another property next time.

I have been 4 times in Chicago, and I have stayed in 4 different Hotels: This has been for much the very best option. The lobby, the warm of the receptionist, the room, the hotel is very good. It is walking distance to the Magnificent Mile and there's no chance for you to get lost from this hotel. If you like to travel with style this could be a very good option.

Hotel Palmer was a really pleasant surprise for our weekend stay. The lobby has a relaxed, slightly old-school charm, and the front desk team made check-in quick even though we arrived later than planned. Our room was spotless, quiet, and had a comfortable bed with great pillows, which honestly made a difference after a long day out. I also appreciated the little touches like good coffee in the room and plenty of outlets near the desk. The location worked well for walking to restaurants and shops, and we never needed to move the car. Breakfast was simple but fresh, with enough options to start the day. Only minor issue was that the hallway could be a bit warm, but overall we left very satisfied and would happily stay again.

Stayed at the Omni Chicago for a long weekend and was pleasantly surprised by how comfortable the suite felt after busy days downtown. Our room had a separate sitting area, plenty of outlets, and windows overlooking Michigan Avenue, so it was easy to relax before heading back out. The bed was excellent, and housekeeping kept everything spotless without ever being intrusive. Front desk staff were friendly and efficient, even when we arrived earlier than expected, and the concierge pointed us toward a couple of nearby restaurants we genuinely enjoyed. The location is hard to beat for shopping, walking to the lake, and catching a cab when the weather turned. The lobby can get lively in the evening, but our room stayed quiet. I'd happily book here again.
Such a letdown for a Sofitel--the bathroom had cracked tiles and weak water pressure, the decor felt stuck in the 90s, and the location wasn't walkable to anything. One night honestly felt too long.

My significant other and I recently spent 3 nights at The James and on the last day I said, 'I wish we could stay longer'. That good! The room was immaculate and a very pleasant surprise from the moment you open the door. Everything is high tech. Plasma TV, CD/Radio, Projection alarm clock (love that so much bought one today). If you wanted room service you got it from David Burke and the mini bar and liquor selection was plentiful. They even have a four legged friend menu. The bathroom was pleasant with bathrobes/slippers and upscale products provided. The bed was the best in a hotel ever. Linens were crip, white and fresh. Maid service twice daily with turn down service. Safe in room, ice delivered, iron, hairdryer all top of the line. The filtered window shades blacked out the light and matched the modern decor. Mid-century style with funky chair/ottman, cubes and a table with nightstands gave us plenty of room and felt like comforts of home. The staff was courteous and accommodating. The library, free internet access, in room wifi were extras we didn't expect . Bar/lounge areas seems to be frequented by locals enjoying cocktails and appetizers in the lobby. Funky artwork. Location, location, location. The best place we've ever stayed not only in Chicago. Highly recommend.

Arrived on 06/04/05, greeted by friendly doorman, and zipped up to the 5th Floor Lobby. Very open lobby area with friendly reception staff. Room was on the 12th Floor and very nice. Everything was in order and very clean! The king size bed was nice and each night I had a restful sleep. Bathroom was large with separate glass shower stall. The room was furnished with everything I needed including internet hook-up access. Also, you can walk thru on the 5th Fl to the Westfield North Bridge Shopping Mall, where you will enjoy Nordstrom and other stores. Of course, you're steps from Michigan Ave. too. The central location of the hotel was great, as I could walk to most places. The CTA Subway stop (Grand Ave. on Red Line) was an easy 2 block walk. I will stay here again on my next trip to Chicago!

Our stay at Hotel James was more disappointing than expected. The room looked tired rather than stylish, with scuffed furniture, faded upholstery, and decor that clearly needs refreshing. The bathroom was clean enough, but cramped and poorly lit, with low water pressure and grout that was beginning to discolor around the shower. We only stayed two nights, which was probably fortunate; by the second morning we were already wishing we had booked somewhere else. Staff interactions were polite but noticeably indifferent. Check-in felt rushed, and when we mentioned the shower issue, the receptionist acknowledged it without offering a solution or even sending anyone to inspect it. The location was convenient, but that alone did not justify the price. Overall, the hotel needs better maintenance and a more welcoming approach.

Stained carpet and a sour smell made the room feel grubby, and the patchy Wi-Fi kept dropping calls. The sleepless night stretched forever, yet checkout came cruelly early, leaving me cheated of rest and value.

I've been here for 4 days. Great location right off of miracle mile, near all major hotels, best shopping and theatres. Rooms very large. Hotel staff very friendly and helpful, and respond immediately. Problems: there frequently are homeless people (even during daylight) on Superior between St. Clair and Michigan Avenue (the main route you walk for or all activities, and just about everything is in walking distance from here). At night, the street on the north side of Superior is dark, and it usually smells strongly of several unpleasant odors. The street people do not approach you, although they may stare as you go by. Usually 2 or more along the way, where they sleep on the window sills of Neiman Marcus. I would not think a woman would feel safe by herself. (I am from a large city and do not have a street people phobia.) There are homeless up and down Michigan Street, but this is different as it's a lonely stretch and no open business is along either side of the street. The entire hotel needs a lot of cosmetic work, and apparently will soon undergo a major renovation. For now, expect two extremely small, warm, slow elevators with long waits serving 17 floors and warm, cramped hallways! All the walls throughout the hotel need painting, and the wallpaper is peeling in places. In the room, several electrical outlets were hanging out of the connection, the carpets were stained, the bathrooms needed new grout (some mold visible), the TV is very small (16 Inch?) and the windows very, very dirty. You won't get your room serviced unless you ask for it, sometimes more than once. The 'pub ' downstairs is run down, dark and kind of creepy. Food and room service are very expensive, as is parking ($34/day public and $38/day valet). On the plus side, the bed was very comfortable, there was ample comfortable furniture in the sitting area, plenty of space and a decent view as the hotels spans St. Clair street toward the north and south. You can see a sliver of Lake Michigan. Pool small, but clean. All in all, it was clean and quiet and provides lots of space for sitting around in the room, but I think it is overpriced, and I would not stay here again.

My daughter and I were in Chicago for one night after having attended a three-day conference elsewhere in Illinois. We were only in Chicago on our way home. We didn't know where to stay in Chicago, but booked one night at the Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers based on their ad in the Chicago Visitors Guide. We're glad we did! We enjoyed our stay very much. Our room was very comfortable and well appointed and had a wonderful view of the city. That's what we wanted--a great view, and we got it. Also, the hotel is within walking distance of many attractions and is accessible from the bus stop (we took the train and bus from the airport into the city and it wasn't bad--saved us a lot of money). The elevators to our room were fast and quick and there was one always available. We found the front desk staff to be friendly and accommodating. The only downside for us is that we had only booked one night in Chicago. We wish we could have stayed there at the Sheraton for at least another night. We would definitely stay there again.

We chose the Hotel Knickerbocker for a mix of sightseeing and a little R&R, and it hit the right notes. Our room on the ninth floor was surprisingly quiet given the hustle below, and the blackout curtains were a lifesaver after long days. I really appreciated the little things: a proper coffee maker, not one of those pod machines, and a bathroom with excellent water pressure. The location was unbeatable for wandering to Navy Pier or hopping on the L. We didn't eat at the restaurant, but the bar's old-school vibe was perfect for a nightcap. Staff at the front desk were friendly and quick to help with directions. Sure, the decor leans toward classic, and the carpets could use a refresh, but it felt clean and well-cared-for. I'd absolutely stay here again for the blend of history and convenience. The complimentary bottle of wine upon arrival was a pleasant, unexpected touch that set the tone for our whole weekend.

The Knickerbocker turned out to be a surprisingly restful hideaway despite its central location. Our room faced the inner courtyard, so street noise was virtually nonexistent--just the faint, pleasant hum of the city far below. The view, while not skyline-facing, had a quiet charm: rooftops and leafy terraces that felt private and calm. As for cleanliness, I'm particular, and I found zero faults; the white linens were crisp, the bathroom gleamed, and the carpets looked freshly vacuumed. The staff genuinely elevated the stay. From the doorman who remembered our name to the front desk agent who patiently rebooked our dinner reservation after a mix-up, everyone seemed to anticipate needs before we voiced them. Even the housekeeping team left a handwritten note about the weather forecast. It's rare to find that blend of efficiency and warmth. I left feeling genuinely refreshed, not just tolerated. I would absolutely return.

Booked the Allegro for a weekend getaway and left pretty let down. Room was worn, the AC rattled all night, and the 'helpful' front desk seemed annoyed every time I asked a basic question. Not worth the hype or the price.

I gave the Conrad a second try at impressing me and it failed miserably. The hotel will not honor room requests. I expressed this was for a special occasion and would love a room with a view on my reservation. I got there and my 'view' was of the adjacent office building windows.
