I didn't pay nearly $400 a night for that. I called down and the manager was absolutely rude. 'That would've required you to pay at least $40 more..' Rude. Lots and lots of mistakes happened. Requested pillows were never sent up, the television sound was not functioning (i.e. NO sound), when telling the manager of the problems he was horribly condescending and cared very little. I've had better service at a Hampon Inn! When they screwed up our breakfast vouchers I had to physically go down and question it.. they said 'we will send them right up'.. No, that never happened. Absolutely ridiculous. The bathroom has always been nice, and the room had been renovated since I was there last year (thank the lord!)... It had a nice ambiance to it. The bed was quite nice as well. The valet guys were fantastic, probably the nicest men within that entire hotel. Also the bellman, and housekeepers were wonderfully sweet and always said 'hi' or 'hope you have a wonderful day'.. I appreciated that. Perhaps the management team needs to go back to training school to learn about customer service. Breakfast at the Conrad restaurant is to be avoided completely. The service was abysmally inept, and not to mention slow. We had two different watresses and it took upward of 15 minutes just to get our juice. They looked like they hated their jobs, and treated us with the same attitude. We were never checked on after the food came. The food is overpriced and the quality is severely lacking. I got a continental breakfast and it included a muffin (burnt), a small croissant, and a tiny cinnamon roll. 14 dollars for that. Laughable. Or if you choose, for 14 dollars you can get some toast and juice! Spare yourself and choose to eat elsewhere where you can get an actual tasty meal for your money. Overall, the managers need to learn what customer service means, and how to bend over backwards for a customer. Otherwise your business will crumble. And the Conrad has crumbled for me. I spent way too much money on terrible service. I've already sent my opinions to Hilton headquarters. I'll be looking at other hotels the next time im in Chicago.
Disappointing stay at the Omni. Our room smelled musty, the AC rattled all night, and housekeeping skipped us entirely one day. For the price, I expected far more--probably won't be back.

Deeply disappointing stay at the Hotel Palmer. The wifi barely worked, my room smelled musty and wasn't properly cleaned, and the street noise kept me up half the night. The 'view' was a brick wall. Won't be returning.
The Knickerbocker looks impressive, but the room felt tired, service was oddly slow, and street noise kept me awake most of the night.

The thing that makes this such an enjoyable place to stay is the staff who were all excellent and polite and the service was impeccable. The room was very clean, the beds were comfortable but it was a little small and the water in the bathroom was not very hot. Other than that it was a great place to stay.
I slept soundly in the plush bed, woke to a lovely skyline view, and appreciated the spotless, spacious bathroom. The Fairmont felt well worth the price for the comfort and service.

We spent four nights at the Knickerbocker and were genuinely impressed. Even though the hotel sits right on Broadway, our room on a higher floor was remarkably quiet--I honestly never heard street noise once, which is rare in midtown. The view from our window looked out over the rooftops toward Times Square, and watching the city light up at dusk never got old. Housekeeping kept everything spotless; the bathroom gleamed and the linens smelled fresh every day. The staff went out of their way for us too--doormen greeted us by name by the second day, and the front desk arranged a late checkout without any fuss when our flight changed. One small note: the elevator can get a bit crowded at peak hours, but that's a minor quibble. Would absolutely stay again.
Affinia's location was handy for getting around, but the tired decor and dusty, poorly cleaned room made the steep rate feel like a real disappointment.

On a recent trip to Chicago to attend a major trade show I had the pleasure of staying with the Sofitel Chicago Water Tower. I say stay with as that is how they make you feel, from check in to check out they go above and beyond to ensure your stay is perfect and you want to return. The rooms are clean, chic and roomy, the beds - the best I have slept in, bathrooms large and super clean. What can I say, my new home when in Chicago...
Hotel Palmer was a pleasant surprise--quiet room, comfortable bed, and staff who happily pointed us toward a great nearby breakfast spot. The lobby felt welcoming, and everything was spotless.
The outdated room smelled musty, and the air conditioning sounded like a lawnmower all night. The staff at check-in seemed annoyed by my questions. You'd expect more for these prices.

My husband and I and our 10 month old took a quick trip to Chicago. We stayed one night at The Palmer house after reading that they were a four star hotel. I guess I am just confused as to why they are a four star hotel. Yes the lounge area is nice but the rooms were so small I couldn't set up a pack and play for my son. I had to call and 'upgrade' my room just so my son could have someplace to sleep. The lower levels have been updated which makes them slightly better than a Holiday Inn. The wall paper is peeling away from the walls and the shower was dirty. I will NEVER stay there again.

I booked the Hotel Allegro hoping for a charming boutique stay, but the reality was a letdown from the moment I checked in. The front desk agent barely acknowledged me, handing over the key card with a curt nod and zero information about the property. My room, while visually okay at first glance, had a suspicious stain on the carpet near the window and a layer of dust on the headboard. The bathroom was the worst part: the shower pressure was a pathetic trickle, and the grout between the tiles was black with mold. I couldn't even enjoy the much-talked-about view--all I saw was a brick wall and a noisy ventilation unit grumbling outside. The location is convenient, but the apathetic staff and tired, dirty rooms made it feel like a glorified hostel. I would not return.
Affinia's location was convenient for getting around, but the Wi-Fi kept dropping, the cramped bathroom felt worn, and the breakfast was bland and overpriced.

I only stayed out with my boyfriend for one night, however enjoyed my stay. The staff was friendly, the room was nice and clean, the hallways and ballrooms etc were elegant. Room service was quick and had good options to choose from that actually tasted great. The staff was able to extend our check out time for an extra 1-2 hours without an extra charge to the room. Great location too! Walking distance from the Art Museum, Millennium Park, Grant Park (right across the street) and a quick cab ride to McCormick Place. If I were in the city again I would love to stay there again.

I booked the Hotel Palmer based on photos that promised charm, but the reality was a letdown from the start. The bed was rock hard, and the thin pillows left me tossing until 3 AM; I woke up with a stiff neck and a headache. The Wi-Fi was essentially a rumor--it dropped every few minutes, making it impossible to even load a simple email. While the hallway was quiet, the walls were paper-thin, and I heard every flush and conversation from the neighboring room until midnight. The bathroom was the worst offender: the showerhead sputtered with uneven pressure, and the sink had a stubborn clog that left water standing for hours. I'm not one to complain, but for the price, this stay felt like a complete waste of money. I won't be back.

I had a lovely stay at the Talbott during a quick weekend in Chicago. The location is hard to beat--quiet enough at night but only a short walk from Michigan Avenue, restaurants, and the lake. My room felt more like a comfortable apartment than a typical city hotel room, with plenty of space to unpack and a very good bed. Everyone at the front desk was warm and efficient, especially when I asked for a late checkout and a nearby breakfast recommendation. The building has an older, classic feel, but it was clean and well maintained rather than dated. I also appreciated that the elevators were quick and the room was surprisingly quiet despite the central location. I would happily stay here again.

I had a really enjoyable stay at the Hard Rock Hotel. The whole place has a lively atmosphere without feeling chaotic, and the music-themed details give it much more personality than a typical chain hotel. My room was clean, comfortable, and surprisingly quiet at night, with a very good bed and plenty of space for my bags. Check-in was quick, and everyone I dealt with was friendly, especially the front desk staff, who pointed me toward a couple of nearby restaurants. I also liked being able to grab coffee and a quick breakfast downstairs before heading out. The location made getting around easy, and there was always something interesting to look at in the lobby. It is not the cheapest option, but the service and overall experience made it feel worthwhile.

Stayed at the Hilton for a conference and honestly came away impressed. Location is unbeatable--walkable to everything, and the staff from bellmen to front desk were genuinely friendly without being over the top. Room was spotless, bed comfy, and the blackout curtains actually worked, which is rare. The executive lounge had a solid breakfast spread and the evening snacks were a nice perk after long days. Only minor hiccup was the elevator wait during checkout rush, but that's about it. The gym could use more free weights, but cardio machines were plentiful and new. Pool area got busy around noon but that's expected. Overall, a solid, dependable stay that made the trip easy. I'd book here again without hesitation.
Absolutely loved my stay at Hotel James! The staff went above and beyond, and the room was spotless with a killer view. Breakfast had tons of options, too. I'm already planning my next visit.

The Knickerbocker's Times Square location made getting around effortless, and the staff were welcoming and efficient. Our bathroom was spotless with a great shower, while the room stayed surprisingly quiet at night.

Quiet room, spotless bathroom, and solid wifi for work calls--all things I appreciated at the Talbott. The location near the Magnificent Mile made getting around easy, and it felt like fair value for downtown pricing.

Loved every minute at the Hilton--the staff were genuinely friendly and sorted a late checkout without fuss. Room was spotless, bed super comfy, and the breakfast buffet had plenty of fresh options. Would happily book again next time I'm in town.

I had a very pleasant stay at the hotel james. My room was spotless when I arrived, with crisp linens, clean floors, and no dust on the furniture. The Wi-Fi worked reliably throughout my visit, including in the room, which made catching up on emails easy. The bathroom was modern and well maintained, with good water pressure in the shower, plenty of hot water, and fresh towels replaced daily. Despite being close to busy streets, the room was impressively quiet at night; I barely heard any outside traffic or neighboring guests. Staff were welcoming and efficient at check-in, and the overall atmosphere felt relaxed and comfortable. I would happily stay here again.
The room was tired and smelled like old cigarettes, and the breakfast eggs were cold rubber. Tried to get extra towels and waited an hour. For this price, I expected so much more.

Stayed here with friends for a long weekend in August and loved the hotel. Enjoyed the free nightly wine happy hour, and the accomodations were quite nice (our beds were very soft and comfortable). We had excellent views of the river from our rooms. The location was wonderful for seeing the sights around town, with easy access to public transportation nearby. My friends actually received the goldfish upon request, which they enjoyed. Some noise could be heard from rooms nearby or above, but it was minimal. Price seemed very resonable to us for the location. Will certainly return to the Windy City and plan on staying here again.

The room was spotless and the bed incredibly comfortable--slept like a log after using the fantastic gym. Staff at the front desk were genuinely helpful, and the breakfast spread had everything I craved. Would happily return.

Booked a King Executive for a weekend getaway and left scratching my head at the hype. The lobby is gorgeous, sure, but that's where the polish ended for me. Check-in took nearly twenty minutes despite being a priority member--the agent kept disappearing into the back office. Finally got to the room and found the mini-bar half-stocked and the bathroom trash can unemptied from the previous guest. Gross. The bed was comfortable enough, but the duvet had a suspicious brown stain on the corner that housekeeping never addressed even after I called twice.

The pool area was overcrowded and the water felt lukewarm, not refreshing. Breakfast was a chaotic free-for-all, with scrambled eggs sitting lukewarm in a chafing dish that was clearly past its prime. For the price we paid, I expected much better service and attention to detail. Won't be returning, which is a shame because the location is genuinely convenient.

My stay at the Hilton was more frustrating than relaxing. I had requested a room with a city view, but the window faced a rooftop crowded with vents and maintenance equipment; there was barely any skyline visible. The room itself was clean enough, though tired-looking, with scuffed furniture and a bathroom that needed better ventilation. Wi-Fi connected repeatedly but dropped every few minutes, making it difficult to join a work call, and the premium access offered at checkout felt like an unnecessary extra charge. The staff were polite but distant, and resolving a billing question took two calls and most of an afternoon. I only stayed two nights, yet the experience felt oddly long. The location was convenient, but the service and overall value were disappointing.

The Intercontinental's tired decor and a musty, poorly cleaned room made our three-night stay drag on far too long, plus constant hallway noise meant we barely slept. Expected much better at this price.

I really wanted to love this place, but the Swissotel felt like a relic from a bygone era. The decor in the hallways and our room was desperately dated--think muddy browns and heavy, tired furniture that screamed 1990s corporate retreat. While the location near the river was undeniably convenient for sightseeing, the noise was relentless; the street-facing room picked up every tram, siren, and late-night reveller until past 2 AM. We asked for a quieter room, but were told the hotel was full. For the premium price we paid, I expected better soundproofing and at least a hint of modern chic. The bed was comfortable enough, but that's hardly a consolation when you're exhausted from poor sleep and staring at worn carpets. It simply wasn't worth the money, and I left feeling cheated of a proper rest.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly, the location is unbeatable--steps from the Magnificent Mile but tucked away enough to feel like an escape. The room was on the smaller side, but the floor-to-ceiling windows made up for it with killer city views, especially at sunset. I loved the vintage vibe in the lobby; it's got that old-school Chicago charm without feeling stuffy. The staff were genuinely warm, not that fake hospitality energy. Someone at the front desk recommended a deep-dish spot two blocks over that was incredible. The bar upstairs was a nice bonus for a nightcap, though drinks were pricey. Bed was plush, blackout curtains worked perfectly. Only minor gripe--hallway noise carried a bit, but it quieted down early. Would definitely book again for the charm and convenience.

The location was stunning, but that's where the magic ended. Our room smelled musty, the air conditioning barely worked, and the breakfast buffet was lukewarm and chaotic every single morning. Expected so much more for the price.

As a regular visitor to Chicago and a freuent guest at the Ambassador East, I was exceptionally disappointed during our last visit. Room service has been eliminated despite the renowned Pump Room being located in the hotel, there was no in-room directory, the carpet was torn and stained, no phone book, the refigerator and honor bar had been removed, and the room was so small I had to turn sideays to get past the bed and the armoire. I asked the desk clerk about larger rooms, and he said they were all the same except for corner rooms - which is untrue, as there are several larger room types. He didn't even offer to check availablity of other rooms! In talking with the consierge, she blamed everything on upcoming renovations - which the hotel has been promising for more than two years. All in all, a very disappointing, and expensive, experience.

The hotel itself was beautiful and wonderful staff but the bottom line for me was that it was impossible to sleep through the night because the noise of the ambulance sirens continued throughout the night. For THREE consecutive nights. There was simply inadequate soundproofing - even 14 floors above the street (OK - 13 floors as there is no 13th floor). I hesitate to write this review but I rely on Trip Advisor reviews when traveling, and had I been warned about the ambulance sirens, I would have chosen to stay elsewhere. If you are a sound sleeper and noise is not an issue then it is a lovely hotel and excellent value. Conveniently located. Wonderful staff. But quiet is a key priority for me so I would not stay here again. :(
Had a really easy stay at the Hyatt--the room was quiet, the bed comfortable, and everyone I dealt with was genuinely helpful. Great location too, with plenty nearby.

My stay at Homewood was disappointing overall. The location was convenient for getting around, with restaurants and public transportation nearby, but that was the main advantage. The room looked tired and could have been cleaner, especially around the bathroom fixtures. Wi‐Fi was technically available, but it kept dropping and became so slow in the evening that I gave up trying to work. Noise was another problem: I could hear doors slamming and conversations in the hallway late into the night, and the thin walls did little to block it. For the price, I expected a more comfortable room, reliable internet, and better maintenance. Staff were polite when I raised the issues, but nothing was really resolved. I would not choose this hotel again unless the rates dropped considerably.

A friend highly recommended this hotel and we couldn't have been happier! It was wonderful ~ my husband and kids were already planning our next trip there before we had even left the hotel. The kids loved the goldfish in the room and thought the window seats were the best.

We loved this hotel and would definitely come back. Initially we weren't given a goldfish, which was disappointing, but then we left a tip for the housekeeper, and she rewarded us with one. We had fun sipping wine and playing Wii in the lobby every afternoon. The staff were quite friendly and helpful, even printing our boarding passes for us. Our room was very comfortable, with a cozy little alcove at the window where we read the paper. At first we were worried about noise, since our room was next to the elevator, but we hardly heard it, and didn't notice any street noise either. The hotel is colorfully and tastefully decorated, well-lit, and ideally located.

Truly a tattered run down facility that you should avoid . Rooms are small, dirty, and in no way represents the web sites representations. Staff is poorly trained and a very big disappointment. At best it is a 3 star facility ands with so many options in Chicago, 'please' avoid this one. I had no choice to stay here as a client booked the rooms.

The service was reasonably well...they seemed to have my reservation and checked me in fairly easily. The location was fine being that it was central to the city but I found out that it was also a tremendous drawback. It was interesting that the survey I took at the hotel in order to obtain internet access at the hotel asked what my most important quality was in a hotel visit and my response 'Quiet'. My visit was anything but, mainly attributed to the fact that they put me on the second floor, facing the street. I awoke at 4 a.m. and never did return to sleep because of the constant street noise and screeching of the L train that sounded as though it was just outside my window. Not the most conducive for a restful sleep prior to an important meeting. At check-out when I informed the hotel clerk of my dissatisfation he chuckled and said, ' Ah, city noise.'

I really wanted to love this hotel given the price, but the Intercontinental fell short in ways I didn't expect. Check-in took nearly 40 minutes because apparently they were short-staffed, and no one apologized. My room had a musty smell that never fully went away, even after I called housekeeping twice. The air conditioning rattled all night, which made sleeping miserable before an important meeting. Breakfast was the biggest letdown--cold eggs, a shortage of coffee cups, and a line out the door with only two staff working. The concierge gave us wrong directions twice. For a property branding itself as luxury, the service felt more like a budget chain. The location is decent and the lobby is beautiful, but that's where the good ends. Probably won't be back.
Loved my stay here--the room was spotless and the bed incredibly comfy. Staff went out of their way to help when my flight got delayed. Great location too, would definitely come back.

The Conrad Hilton recently took over this property from the failed Meridian Hotel. It seems that the Conrad has inherited a hotel property that just doesn't work. The entrance is very difficult to find. There are only two elevators to take you up to the lobby. As a result, there was often a line waiting for them. The same problem affects the guest room elevators located beyond the registration area. If you go in and out of the hotel more than a couple of times during your stay, you will find the poor elevator layout annoying. The King room is what I would consider small compared to other Chicago hotels. Although I like modern design, the room was quite stark and cold. It was also showing quite a bit of wear and tear. The bathroom was the best part. Has anyone from management tried to sit in the chair and work at the desk? It was the most uncomfortable set-up I've experienced. The views are non-existent for most of the rooms. In a city with amazing vistas, this was disappointing. I saw a couple walking the halls with management trying to find a room that was acceptable to them. Room service breakfast was a highlight of our stay. Excellent food and high quality presentation. Sorry I couldn't write a better review. Would I stay here again? No. Chicago has some incredible hotels and this is not one of them.

I expected more from the Sheraton given the nightly rate and its reputation. My room looked worn, with a stained chair and an air conditioner that rattled loudly whenever it started. The Wi-Fi technically connected, but it kept dropping during video calls and was too slow to be useful in the evening. At check-in, the front desk agent barely acknowledged me and seemed irritated when I asked about breakfast hours. Housekeeping was polite, but they missed replacing towels one day. I was only there for two nights, yet the stay somehow felt much longer because every small inconvenience added up. For what I paid, I expected a cleaner room, dependable internet, and warmer service.
I barely slept through hallway noise; the decor felt dated, the view was a brick wall, and the cramped bathroom had weak water pressure.
The Omni looked dated, and our room smelled musty despite the high rate. Slow check-in, thin walls, and an unhelpful response to the noisy neighbors made the stay disappointing.

The service from check-in to checkout was excellent - timely and efficient. The room was more then I has expected. It was spacious and laid out very well. I particularly enjoyed the living room area as well as the double closets and separate bath and shower. The bed abd pillows were extremely comfortable. I believe it's the first time I stayed in a hotel that provided a toothbrush and toothpaste in the room. The location was perfect for us as we were able to walk to everywhere we needed to go. I particularly enjoyed the excellent food at theChina Grill which is attached to the Hard Rock hotel. The service was very good and the staff very friendly.

We had a very pleasant weekend at the Talbott. The front desk team was genuinely welcoming and had us checked in quickly, even offering a few neighborhood restaurant suggestions that turned out to be excellent. Our room felt spotless, from the fresh linens to the well-kept bathroom, and housekeeping was attentive without being intrusive. For such a central location, it was impressively quiet at night; we barely heard hallway traffic and slept well both nights. Being just a short walk from Michigan Avenue, Oak Street, and plenty of cafes made it easy to explore without constantly calling a car. The hotel has a warm, classic feel rather than a generic chain atmosphere. We would happily stay here again on our next Chicago trip.
Hardrock's location near the Strip was convenient, but the Wi-Fi barely connected. Our room had dusty surfaces, and the cramped bathroom smelled damp with a weak shower--far below expectations.

Hi,Stayed here for three nights recently,From check in to check out all Staff members went out of their way to make sure everything was ok and if there was anything they could do to help us,directions,restaurants, transport,nothing was too much trouble,The dinner from monday to thursday 5-7 was a wonderful surprise,also the breakfast was more than adequet,Stayed on the 15th floor and slept soundly,Hotel close to everything for the tourist or business traveller.Restaurants and shopping all within 5-10 mins.

Check-in was fast, the room was perfect, and there were no problems. This is a standard big-city business hotel with every amenity imaginable. I got a very good deal for a one-night stay, but they made the money back from the exorbitant parking rate and the absurd access fee for wireless internet. If you are bored of the routine hotel fare, walk two blocks to Gourmet Pantry (155 N. Michigan) for a refreshing change.
Swissotel looked impressive online, but my room felt tired and the service was surprisingly slow. Breakfast was crowded, and the overall experience didn't justify the high price.

Checked in after a long flight and was met by a front desk agent who barely looked up, muttering through the process as if I were interrupting something. The room itself felt tired--carpet stained near the window, a layer of dust on the nightstand, and the bathroom grout looked like it hadn't seen a scrub brush in weeks. The Wi-Fi dropped three times during a single video call, forcing me to restart the whole session. Location is decent if you want to be near the convention center, but it's a hike to any decent restaurant or bar. Honestly, for the price, I expected far more polish. I've stayed at better-run Hiltons in smaller cities. I won't be returning to this one.

Hotel Palmer was a pleasant surprise from check-in to departure. The staff were genuinely welcoming, quick to answer questions, and even gave us a helpful recommendation for dinner nearby. Our room was quiet, comfortable, and well maintained, with a bathroom that felt especially fresh: good water pressure in the shower, plenty of clean towels, bright lighting, and enough counter space for toiletries. The bed was comfortable, and the location made it easy to walk around the area. We only stayed two nights, which honestly felt too short because we settled in so easily. Considering the service, cleanliness, and convenience, the rate felt fair and definitely worth the price.

I love the free breakfast and dinners on weeknights. The hotel is clean and nice rooms The pool needs some updating(but kids don't care) My friend and I took our granddaughters for a grandma grandaughter outing and this hotel was perfect

I asked for a high floor away from the elevator and that is what I got. The room was pleasantly decorated, functional and very clean. I didn't need a whole lot of service but when I did they were pleasant and prompt. I used the fitness center which was well equipped and everything was in working order. It is in a great location at one end of the Michigan Avenue shopping district.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly, the location is unbeatable. You're right in the middle of everything, steps from the river walk, and the views from the upper floors are stunning at sunset. The room itself was a bit on the compact side, but the bed was incredibly comfortable and the blackout curtains worked wonders. What really impressed me was the staff--every single person, from the doorman to the front desk, was genuinely friendly and helpful without being overbearing. The rooftop bar is a must-visit, even if you're not a guest, though the cocktails are pricey. My only minor gripe was the hallway noise in the mornings, but it wasn't a dealbreaker. I'd absolutely book again for the charm and convenience.
Swissotel was a great value: the Wi‐Fi worked flawlessly, staff were warm and efficient, and our room's sweeping city-and-river view made the stay feel special.

I stayed at this Hotel for 1 night. We just wanted to stay in downtown Chicago. This hotel is right next to John Hancock building. Walking distance to many shopping, restaurant, and everything else. From valet people to front desk people, they were all very friendly and helpful. The best thing about this hotel (other than the awesome location) is that all rooms are suites. You can choose 1 king or 2 double which will be inside the room and you get another sofa bed in the living room area. You get 2 TVs also. The roof top pool over looking Michigan lake was lovely also.
Street noise kept me awake most of the night, and the Wi‐Fi dropped constantly. The room looked neglected, with dusty surfaces and hair in the bathroom.

What can I say... this USED to be our FAVORITE hotel in Chicago because of its location, its historic and gorgeous pool, it amazing Sunday brunch, it's relatively low price compared to comparable hotels, its exclusive benefits of the ambassador membership... All of the above has fallen disappointingly by the wayside with a resounding THUD. Let's break it down: Location: I'll concede that it's still great. Get a corner room in the Historic tower higher than the 20th floor with a view of Michigan Ave and/or the river. Its historic and gorgeous pool: Closed indefinitely! When asked when it will re-open, the hotel staff actually said, 'Maybe never.' Its amazing Sunday brunch: Zest is gone, and his been replaced by a very dark Michael Jordan restaurant that takes up much of the lobby and second entrance. (The lobby, by the way, used to be beautiful and open with lots of places to sit. Also no longer...). The food is very bad. Very. Bad. There are so many restaurants in this city. Do yourself a favor and go somewhere else to eat. Its relatively low price compared to comparable hotels: Based on my review of everything else. Go to the Drake, or the Peninsula. Completely worth the extra money... That, or downgrade to the Hilton and get what you expect and pay for... The InterContinental has fallen so low that you pay a higher price than the Hilton, but you get a worse experience! Its exclusive benefits of the ambassador membership: I canceled our membership after this disaster. Part of the membership includes early check-in (granted, when available)... but our room wasn't ready until 6pm. This is obviously after normal check-in. The staff was overwhelmed, and not effective or helpful. I tried to speak with the manager about our room, waited in long line to speak with someone, only to be told that my husband needed to be with me because the membership was in his name. In a nutshell. Go somewhere else. ps: Go to Argo tea next door instead of the Starbucks in the hotel. Way better food and coffee.

We stayed at the Hard Rock for three nights during a concert weekend and honestly it exceeded what I expected for the rate. Check-in took a few minutes and the front desk guy even gave us a tip about avoiding the elevator crowds after shows, which saved us time twice. Our room faced away from the street so it was remarkably quiet given how lively the lobby gets at night -- we slept fine even with a party happening downstairs. The music memorabilia everywhere gets a bit touristy, but that's part of the charm. Breakfast was included in our package: solid buffet with fresh fruit, made-to-order omelets, and decent coffee that got refilled without asking. The staff overall seemed genuinely happy to help, not just going through the motions. For the location and quality, I'd call it worth the money. Would book again.

Great stay at the Allegro -- the room was comfy and quiet despite being downtown, and the breakfast guy remembered my coffee order. Location made walking everywhere easy. Would book again without hesitating.

I had a very pleasant stay at Homewood. My room was spotless when I arrived, including the bathroom and kitchenette, and housekeeping kept everything tidy throughout the visit. The staff were consistently warm and helpful, from the quick check-in to answering a question about nearby restaurants. The decor isn't ultra-modern, but it felt clean, comfortable, and thoughtfully maintained rather than dated. I especially appreciated the roomy layout and the quiet nights, which made it easy to relax after a busy day. Breakfast was convenient and had enough variety to get me started each morning. Considering the space, service, and overall cleanliness, I felt the price was fair and definitely worth it.
WiFi barely worked in my room, and staff seemed indifferent when I asked for help. The dated decor and tired furnishings made this Hilton feel far too expensive for what we received.

For the price, Hotel Amalfi felt like a genuine steal--the bathroom was spotless with excellent water pressure, and breakfast offered fresh pastries and proper espresso. The room itself was immaculately clean, making the whole stay effortlessly comfortable.

I travel a lot for business and quite frankly, my expectations were starting to reach new lows. I usually always choose W Hotels just for the consistency (of average hotels). The Affinia in Chicago has raised my expectations and W Hotels are going to suffer in comparison. This hotel is one of the cleanest I have stayed at in some time. Service was impeccable. Friendly front-desk staff and the extra towels I ordered arrived literally within minutes. The gym has new equipment with plenty of space. And such a fun vibe - without dark hallways and loud music. I have to thank the other reviewers - their reviews led me to the Affinia and I was so pleased. My new 'Chicago Hotel'. It will even lead me to try the Manhattan hotels.

The Ambassador's rooftop pool was the highlight of my trip--sunset views over the skyline while the staff brought fresh towels without being asked. Rooms felt spotless and quiet, and the front desk even remembered my name at checkout. I'm already planning a return.

After reading good reviews about I booked a 5 night stay. Checked in late bit called early in the day to assure we'd have a roll away as well as the pull out sofa for 2 teens. They somehow had us booked for two rooms instead. Got that sorted out and arrived around 10 pm. Checked in and waited for our luggage... Finally went down and got it ourselves. The room was a little grungy, furniture shabby, and discovered a suspicious stain on the duvet cover. Ewww. Called for a new duvet cover which was delivered and unceremoniously handed to me. FYI it's kinda gross to have to change the duvet cover in a hotel. Next day tried to iron a dress for dinner and the iron didn't work. Called for a replacement, waited a while, called again and was brought another iron which also didn't work. Third time was a charm. Oh boy. Too bad we paid in advance. Won't be staying here again.

I stayed at the Affinia for a four-night business trip and was genuinely pleased with the experience. The location is hard to beat--just a couple of blocks from the subway and walking distance to plenty of restaurants, which made getting around effortless. I'd read mixed things about the rooms online, but mine felt fresh and well maintained, with updated furnishings and a comfortable bed rather than anything dated. The view wasn't anything dramatic since I faced a side street, but it was quiet and bright during the day, which I appreciated. Wifi worked reliably the whole time, even during video calls, with no annoying dropouts or login hassles. Staff were friendly and check-in took two minutes. Would absolutely book again for my next visit.

We had a lovely two-night stay at the Sofitel and it felt like a real treat without being stuffy. The lobby was busy when we arrived, but check-in was warm and efficient, and the receptionist made sure we had a quiet room away from the elevators. Our room was spotless, with an extremely comfortable bed, blackout curtains, and a surprisingly good view over the city. I also appreciated the little things: proper coffee, plenty of outlets by the desk, and robes that were actually soft. Breakfast was excellent, especially the pastries and fresh fruit, though it gets crowded after 9. The concierge pointed us toward a nearby bistro we never would have found ourselves. Service was consistently friendly. I'd happily return.

I got a Sunday night stay for only $50 off of Priceline.com, so it would be hard to complain...but this was truly a great hotel, even if I paid double. The first impression you get when you walk through the sliding doors of the Hyatt Regency Chicago is WOW. The lobby is beautiful with a upscale mall type of look to it with an open area that has a restaurant, plenty of couches,seats etc to people watch and a lake with water fountains. You take the escalator to the concierge/directory/check in area. The hotel let me check in at 12pm (I had a 3pm check in time). I suggest you call ahead like I did so they know you are coming early.The women at the desk was friendly and when I requested a higher level floor she was more than happy to look it up and even told me 'I have a room on the 18th floor with a veiw of the river or you can go higher with no view'. I thought it was pretty nice to give me that information so that I wouldnt get stuck with a room with a view of a wall. The rooms are big (I had a doubles room) The beds were beautiful with great pillows,blankets,headboards etc. An Ipod alarm clock was a nice 21st century touch to the room. Great to plug in your ipod, listen to some music and get ready for a night out or when relaxing after a long day of touring Chicago. The view was very nice and the bathroom was spotless and had great toiletries. Another great feature is the concierge area's computers that gives you access to printing your boarding pass before you get to the airport. You simply look at the screen, click on your airline icon and following the instructions. I had my boarding passes in about a minute. Came in handy when I got to OHare and was able to skip a long line of frustrated passengers. I was only in the hotel for 1 day, but it was by far one of the better hotel experiences I have had and I travel alot. It is a business hotel, but definitely a great choice for families and couples. Definitely would stay here again when Im passing through Chicago.
My weekend at the Fairmont felt too short; the bed was exceptionally comfortable, Wi-Fi worked reliably, and the room's view over the city was a lovely bonus.

a great hotel, we used the CTA the 2 days we were in Chicago and it is great, that the Line 6 stops nearly in front of the hotel. So we did not need any taxi and traveled from Midway to the city and to Ohare for 9$ and we used the buses alot (freezing cold). The hotel itself is great, very clean rooms, realy on of the best bathrooms i ever had. Staff very friendly, they even found me out were i can get Timerland shoes.... and she was right i got them in one place she told me... thats service...I also was having a look to the gym room and the swimming pool area, did not use it and I do not know if it would have been included in the room price....but realy a nice view makes running easyer....

I had a great time here! It is centerally located in Chicago so walking around is so easy and pleasent. The staff was amazing and very helpful! Parking was a bit steep, but to be expected. The room was very nice and the bed and linens were very confortable. The yoga mat rental was wonderful as well! Wonderful and relaxing experience overall.

Disappointing stay--the room was dated and smelled musty, and housekeeping never restocked our towels. Check-in was slow despite booking directly, and the AC barely worked. For the price, I expected far more polish. Probably won't return.

The tired, beige decor felt straight out of the 80s, and the hallway noise seeped into our room all night. Found dust on the nightstand, and honestly, two nights here dragged on far longer than my patience could handle.

I had a very pleasant stay at the Ambassador. The welcome was friendly and check-in was quick, and my room was clean, comfortable, and larger than expected. The decor has a classic feel rather than a completely new, modern look, but it was well maintained and gave the hotel some character. My bed was especially comfortable, and the room was quiet at night, so I slept better than I usually do in a city hotel. Breakfast offered a good range of choices, including fresh fruit, pastries, eggs, and decent coffee, with the buffet replenished regularly. The Wi-Fi worked reliably throughout my stay, including for video calls, although it slowed slightly in the evening. The location was convenient for restaurants and transport, and I would happily return.

I stayed at the Hilton for three nights on a work trip and came away genuinely impressed, which I wasn't expecting at this price point. My room was on the fourteenth floor, and the view looking out over the city at dusk was the kind of thing you stop unpacking to stare at. The bathroom was spotless and bigger than I'd anticipated, with strong water pressure and fluffy towels restocked without my even asking. Every staff member I crossed paths with, from the front desk to the breakfast crew, seemed to actually enjoy their jobs and greeted me by name after the first day. The lobby and rooms have been recently refreshed, so nothing felt tired or dated the way some older chains do. Only tiny gripe was slow elevator waits at checkout time, but that's a crowd problem, not a quality problem. I'd happily return.

We honestly expected more from a place with such a big name. The moment we walked in, the decor felt dated -- the so-called rock memorabilia looked tired, the carpets were stained, and everything had a worn 2005 vibe that no amount of neon could hide. Our room was no better: scuffed furniture, a wobbly bed frame, and a bathroom that smelled vaguely of mildew. The shower dripped constantly, the grout was black in places, and the towels were thin and gray. The staff didn't help much either; check-in took forever, and when we asked for extra pillows, the front desk seemed annoyed rather than accommodating. Housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely. Honestly, two nights here already felt too long. We won't be back, and we'd think twice before recommending it to anyone.

Arrived at 1:30am only to find that sleep was not in my future because of the dance club connected to the hotel. If you party and stay out all night anyway, this hotel would be fine. But don't plan to get any rest if the club is open! Front desk lady was extremely rude to people calling in to inquire about the hotel while I was checking in. She was fine with me and gave me a corner room, but sure wouldn't want to be on her bad side.
Loved the old-school charm and surprisingly quiet room despite being right by Times Square. Staff were warm, the bed was excellent, and the rooftop view made our weekend feel special.

Stayed here for 5 nights while visiting Chicago for the first time. The location is great, the hotel has been recently renovated and our room was very spacious with two bathrooms. The lobby is a great place to chill and have a drink. Didn't eat in the restaurant but there are a few good ones nearby and we were beside The Art Institute, Cultural Centre & Macys. Staff were friendly. Would recommend it as a base to tour the city.

Great location and the staff genuinely seemed happy to help with dinner spots and local tips. Room was comfortable and quiet, though the AC ran a bit loud at night. Overall a solid, hassle-free stay that hit the mark for a quick city trip.

No excuse for a hotel like this to have cold showers on three consecutive days and then to tell customer that engineering will look at it and that we should have told them sooner. I wouldn't expect a cold shower at a budget hotel, let alone an Omni. Great location and the bar is nice.

My two-night stay at the Hilton was frustrating from the start. The room overlooked the loading dock and a row of dumpsters, so the advertised city view was really just delivery trucks idling before dawn. Wi-Fi technically connected, but it dropped every few minutes and was unusable for a video call. The room also felt tired, with a noisy air conditioner and stains on the carpet near the desk. I expected the short stay to pass quickly, yet each evening seemed to drag because there was little comfort in returning to the room. Staff at the front desk were polite but dismissive when I mentioned the internet and noise, offering no real solution beyond 'we'll note it.' For the price and Hilton name, this was a disappointing experience.

Stayed at the Fitzpatrick before, about 4 years ago, it was ok. The management was great, staff was so kind, and rooms were clean. ** But this time I promised my self NEVER to go back!! The new staff was so rude!! I made a reservation for my Anniversary on the internet, and the day of check in I was told by the hotel staff that they do not have my reservation!** 1) I was transferred around back and forth from the hotel staff to the reservations hotline. 2) Staff was extremely rude! Not arrogant, but rude! Like they hated thier job. 3) They offered check in at 1pm but the room wasn't ready till 3pm! 4) There were stains everywhere! 5) Because of the high sales of rooms due to popularity on this site, they must have hired a cheap unfriendly staff.

Stayed here for a long weekend and was genuinely impressed. The room was spotless - the kind of clean that makes you want to kick off your shoes immediately. Staff were warm without being fussy, and the front desk actually remembered my name when I asked for extra towels, which felt like a small, thoughtful touch. The decor leans traditional, but it's been kept up so well that it reads as elegant rather than tired - think rich wood, crisp linens, and soft lighting that doesn't scream 'renovation needed.' For the rate I paid, I'd call it a fair deal, especially given the central location and the quiet at night. Breakfast was solid, and the bar had a nice, unhurried vibe. Would happily book again, though I might splurge on a corner room next time for the extra light. A comfortable, dependable choice that doesn't try too hard and gets it right.

We booked the Affinia for a three-night city break, and honestly, we left feeling let down. The location is excellent--right by the park and within easy walking distance of restaurants--but that's where the positives end. Our room on the sixth floor was anything but quiet; we could hear constant street noise and doors slamming well past midnight. The carpet looked stained, and I found a hair in the bathroom sink on arrival. The staff seemed indifferent, more interested in chatting behind the desk than helping us with a broken TV remote. It was a disappointing stay for the price, and I wouldn't recommend it unless you're desperate for the address.

I really wanted to like Hotel Palmer, but this stay was a letdown from start to finish. The bathroom had mold creeping along the grout lines, and the shower drain backed up on our second morning, leaving standing water with nowhere to go. We'd booked a room with a view we were promised would be scenic -- instead we stared directly at a grimy brick wall and the kitchen's ventilation ducts, humming day and night. The noise wandered in from the street until nearly 2 a.m., plus hallway conversations echoed like the walls were paper. As for the staff, they barely acknowledged us; the front desk guy was glued to his phone and gave a shrug when we mentioned the drain. For these prices, I expected basic competence. Won't be back.
The room was spotless and quiet, so I slept wonderfully in the comfortable bed. Fresh, modern decor made it inviting, and the bathroom was roomy with a great shower.

I had a very pleasant stay at the Ambassador and would happily return. My room was spotless when I arrived, including the desk, windows, and the areas that often get overlooked around the bed. The bathroom was compact but thoughtfully arranged, with strong water pressure, plenty of fresh towels, and a shower that warmed up quickly. The hotel has character without feeling worn out; the decor mixes classic details with newer furnishings, so it felt welcoming rather than dated. Despite being in a busy area, the room was quiet at night. The mattress was comfortable, the pillows had just the right amount of support, and I slept through the night both evenings. Staff were friendly and efficient, which made the whole visit easy.

I really wanted to love the Fairmont, but our anniversary stay fell flat. The room felt dated, the air conditioning was noisy all night, and the staff seemed rushed and indifferent when we asked for a quiet floor. For the price, I expected far more polish.
Shower barely had hot water and the bathroom felt grimy. Street noise kept me up half the night, so I slept terribly, and breakfast was cold and stale. Not worth the price at all.

We booked the Palmer based on photos that made it look like a charming boutique escape. The reality was a letdown. Our room, while spacious, had a musty smell that air freshener couldn't mask, and the window looked directly onto a brick wall. The advertised 'rain shower' was a weak dribble. Service was polite but painfully slow; we waited over forty minutes for two coffees at breakfast, and the pastries were stale. The pool area was overcrowded, with no available loungers by 9 AM. Loud construction noise started promptly at 8 AM on Saturday, making a lie-in impossible. For the price, I genuinely expected a relaxing stay. Instead, we paid a premium for damp, noisy mediocrity and left feeling underwhelmed. There are far better options in the area for less money. We won't be returning.

In from Minneapolis and was hoping to stay on Michigan Ave at hotel. When we arrived we were told a previous guest had extended their stay so we did not have a room. The hotel moved us to another hotel 2 miles away in a less than desireable location. Management on duty was unfriendly and even stated they would call security if we did not leave. They gave us $15 for cab fare. Will never stay there again. Happened to numerous guests the same weekend.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly couldn't have picked a better spot. The location is perfect--right by the waterfront, and everything we wanted to see was a short walk or quick cab away. Check-in was smooth, and they even let us into our room early, which was a huge win after a red-eye. The room itself was spotless, with a super comfortable bed and a great view of the harbor. The blackout curtains were a lifesaver for sleeping in. We hit the pool one afternoon, and it was surprisingly quiet and well-maintained. Only tiny hiccup was the hallway noise on Saturday night, but it died down quickly. The breakfast spread had plenty of options, and the staff were all genuinely friendly, from the valets to the front desk. Would absolutely book here again for a city escape.

I called on December 6th, 2010 at 3 p.m. to book a room for an upcoming weekend getaway, and was taken aback when the phone was picked up and promptly hung up without a word. Thinking this might have been a simple mistake, I gave it another try. A woman introducing herself as 'Toni' answered the phone, rushed through her introduction, sounding incredibly bored and annoyed that she had to answer the phone. Barely letting a second go by after her introduction, she gave a snotty 'Hello?!' before I could open my mouth and tell her 'Never mind.' Never has a hotel answered my call so rudely. I'd like to give the hotel the benefit of the doubt and pin this unpleasant experience to 'Toni'; however I will not be calling back again in hopes to stay at this hotel during this trip.

Stayed at The Knickerbocker for a long weekend and it was a great base for the city. The location just off Times Square is obviously busy, but once we were inside the hotel it felt surprisingly calm and polished. Our room was comfortable, very clean, and quiet enough to get real sleep, which I did not expect in this part of Manhattan. The staff at the desk were warm without being overly formal and helped us arrange a late checkout when our train was delayed. We also had drinks at the rooftop bar one evening; the views and atmosphere were worth it, even if prices were typical for the area. Elevators were a little slow during the morning rush, but that was the only small annoyance. I'd gladly stay here again.

I expected much more from the Omni, especially given the price and its reputation. Check-in took nearly half an hour, and the front desk seemed overwhelmed even though the lobby wasn't particularly busy. Our room was a decent size, but it felt tired: scuffed furniture, a stained carpet near the window, and a bathroom fan that rattled all night. Housekeeping also skipped our room on the second day, so we had to call for towels and toilet paper. The location is convenient, but the street noise was surprisingly loud, and the windows didn't seem to block much of it. Staff were polite when we reached them, yet nothing about the stay felt attentive or worth the premium. I left disappointed and would choose another hotel next time.

Was there recently for one night for a conference. Tried to check-in at 5:30pm (the published check-in was 3pm), they said my room wasn't ready, where as others coming after me were assigned rooms. Was given a dummy door key card and asked to chill in the lounge on the 32nd floor and that they would call on may cell as soon as the room was ready. I chilled there until 8pm, no call, so went out for dinner. Came back at 9:30pm and asked if my room was ready. The gal said of course yes and give me a key. When asked why no one called me, she just shrugged. No, my troubles did not end there. I went to the room and opened the door only to find someone else in the room. Came back to the lobby, then they apologized and gave me another room. I said I was not going to walk-in on somebody else again, so they sent someone with me to open the new room. For all my 'trouble' they reduced my bill by about 40%. It was definitely not worth the trouble they put me thru. Very bad experience.

I'd heard the Amalfi's location was unbeatable, and that much is true--you're steps from the old town. But that's where the positives end. The 'sea view' we paid extra for was mostly a rooftop and a sliver of water, and the window hadn't been cleaned in months. Check-in took forever, and the front desk clerk seemed annoyed by every question. The room itself felt trapped in 1985, with mustard-toned carpet, a tiny tube TV, and a showerhead that dribbled. Housekeeping never replaced the coffee pods, and the hair dryer died on day two. When I asked for a late checkout, I got a flat 'no' without apology. Honestly, the building's location is the only thing working in its favor. For the price, you could do much better a few blocks over. I left feeling tired, dusty, and thoroughly unimpressed.
Our room overlooked a noisy parking garage, the carpet and bathroom felt grimy, and the Wi-Fi kept dropping. For the steep Omni rate, this stay was a real letdown.

I booked this via Priceline, and was not sure I'd like it, as some Sheratons have fallen off the cliff. This hotel absolutely surpassed my expectations. Despite booking with Priceline, I was treated like a king. They let me check in early, gave me a beautiful room, and even went so far as to look up my Starwood number so I could get some credit for the stay. The staff was unfailingly pleasant, the property immaculate, and the room very comfortable. I highly recommend this hotel.

Recently returned from a two-night stay at Ambassador East Hotel. Was looking for a comfortable hotel to stay at while visiting family now located in Chicago. Mission was accomplished. If you would like a quiet, comfortable hotel in a great area - this is it. While some of the furnishings show some signs of their age, it does not detract from the elegant style of the rooms and adds to the comfortable and home-like feeling. Found staff to be friendly and helpful. We will be return guests many times in the future for sure.

Striking architecture is only the beginning of what can only be described as one of the best hotel experiences of my professional life. The attention to detail in the room and the bathroom is remarkable and the bed is the best night's sleep I've ever experienced in a hotel. Gorgeous LCD tv and Bose wave machine added to my enjoyment. Sofitel is worth the extra $'s.

I stayed at the Hotel Palmer for three nights in early October and was genuinely impressed. The bed was incredibly comfortable--firm mattress, plush pillows--and I slept soundly every night despite the central location. The bathroom was spotless and recently renovated, with a rain shower that had excellent water pressure and plenty of hot water, plus nice toiletries. Breakfast exceeded my expectations: fresh pastries, real fruit, good coffee, and made-to-order eggs rather than the usual sad buffet fare. Staff were friendly without being intrusive. Considering how central it is and the quality of everything, the price felt very reasonable. I'd happily book again on my next visit and would recommend it to anyone wanting solid comfort without paying boutique-hotel prices. Overall a very satisfying stay.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly couldn't have asked for a smoother experience. The front desk team was warm and efficient even with a packed lobby on Friday afternoon--we were in our room within ten minutes. The room itself was spotless, the bed was genuinely comfortable, and I loved that the blackout curtains actually did their job. Location is a huge plus: walked to the riverwalk, the Bean, and several great restaurants without ever needing a rideshare. The breakfast buffet had solid variety, though it does get busy around 9 a.m., so go early if you want a quiet corner. Also appreciated the gym being open 24 hours--managed a quick workout before checkout. Only tiny gripe: the hallway ice machine on our floor was out of order, but the front desk had someone bring up a bucket promptly. Would happily return here for business or a city trip.

Great stay at the Sheraton--fast wifi, blissfully quiet room even with a wedding going on downstairs. I only booked two nights and honestly wished it had been longer. A bit pricey, but worth every penny.
Hotel Monaco felt overpriced for a restless night: hallway noise carried through the door, and the bed was uncomfortable. Staff were polite enough, but not especially helpful.

Stunning views from the upper floors and a super comfy bed made my stay memorable. The breakfast spread was fresh and varied, and the staff genuinely cared about our comfort. A solid pick for a hassle-free, relaxing city break.

Not impressed at ALL. The hotel itself looks really nice, especially in the big foyer area. Our room was small, and the bathroom needed some major upgrades. It had the green tile, like at your grandmother's house, all over the walls, and 2 people couldn't fit in it if you tried. We could hear the people beside us in the early morning every morning, so obvioulsy the walls aren't so thick. Our room looked directly on to a brick building outside, VERY close, we couldn't even tell if it was nice outside or not. We are assuming we were not in a renovated room from the looks of it, and I felt yucky the whole time in it. I just wouldn't pay lots of money to stay here, there is nothing exceptional about it at all.

The view from our high floor over the bay was simply breathtaking, and the staff genuinely anticipated every need without hovering. Breakfast offered fantastic local options, though I could have easily spent another day soaking in that serene atmosphere.

While overall a decent property, the incident I had with this hotel has been like none other in my history of travel. I recently stayed at the Hotel Monaco for five nights, checking out on Monday, March 19th. Shortly after leaving the hotel and retrieving my car from the valet, my partner and I noticed a large scrape on the bumper of the car that wasn't present upon checking in. We had not requested use of the car for the duration of our stay. I called the hotel approximately two hours after checking out and was directed to speak with the garage manager at Park One (their valet company) who stated that he would review video of the car and call me back within 48 hours to verify that the car was unblemished upon arrival, and was scraped upon departure from the garage. The garage manager, Mike Yunan, didn't call back until I had an email exchange with the general manager of the hotel, Marco Scherer. When he finally got back to me, the garage manager stated that he would file an 'incident report' and claim with his insurance company, Travelers, which would eventually deny the claim because garage staff wouldn't admit fault or liability, nor did they supply the video they stated they had of the car entering or exiting the garage, which could have verified that the damage wasn't present upon check-in, but was at check-out. Their insurance representative even told me that the garage does not have surveillance at that location, contradicting the garage manager. In the end, this Kimpton InTouch guest got stuck with a $1,000 bill for parking at this Kimpton property: an almost $500 paint scrape on top of a $48/per day parking fee, rental car expenses, several hours of lost time in dealing with the issue, and one gigantic headache. In the end, do NOT trust the valets or staff at this hotel, and take your business elsewhere if at all possible.

The Hotel Talbot exceeded my expectations, though I wish I'd booked one more night. The staff were the real highlight--from the cheerful doorman who remembered my name to the front desk clerk who patiently mapped out a running route along the river. My room faced the courtyard, which meant a leafy, tranquil view instead of street noise. The decor felt pleasantly vintage, with brass fixtures and floral drapes that seemed intentional rather than tired. It's a charming throwback, not a museum piece. Breakfast was generous, and the evening turn-down service with homemade cookies was a lovely touch. The only reason I'm not giving five stars is the slightly soft mattress, but honestly, given how welcoming everything felt, I'd still return in a heartbeat.

A peaceful haven--the room was whisper-quiet despite the bustling streets below, and the bathroom's rainfall shower felt indulgent. Staff greeted me by name each morning, warm and efficient. My only regret? A stay that ended far too soon.
For Sheraton rates, the stay felt poor value: Wi‐Fi barely connected, the room faced a parking lot, and my two-night visit somehow dragged on far too long.

I stayed at this hotel over the weekend of the Chicago Bears Fan Convention (Feb 27- March 1). The hotel is beautiful. I had a Towers room. I had a decent view of the city (Sears Tower). The room was a little small but had two bathrooms (1 King bed). The Tower room has it's own registration area and comes with a free continental breakfast, evening snacks and free sodas throughout the day. The registration/ lounge is on the 24th floor and overlooks Lake Michigan. The hotel was full but service was excellent. The location is convenient but there are a number of homeless people within a block or two (especially toward the El train). We loved our stay at this hotel and never had to take a cab or rent a car. I will stay here again. Hilton offered a Sunday night free on their website with a 3 day stay. This made the cost reasonable (for Chicago). However, the Pavilion restaurant left a lot to be desired. The pub on the first floor was a good place to hang out and have a drink.

Checked in late after a long drive, and the front desk clerk barely looked up from her phone. The room itself was clean enough, but the walls were paper-thin--I heard the neighbor's TV until 2 AM and every flush from the floor above. For the price, I expected at least a decent night's sleep, but instead I felt like I was paying to camp in a hallway. The bed was lumpy, and the AC rattled all night, which made the stay feel endless. I'd booked for two nights but cut it to one because I couldn't face another evening of that noise. Staff on checkout were equally indifferent, no apology, no follow-up. I've stayed at cheaper motels with more character and better quiet. Not worth it, and I won't be back.
Disappointing stay at the InterContinental: the room was clean enough, but the tired decor felt overdue for renovation. My view was mostly rooftops, and the cramped bathroom had worn fixtures.

Here are some pros and cons: Pros: -Good location -Nice staff -Clean room Cons: -Lack of bathroom amenities (I get better items at a Holiday Inn) -Housekeeping wasn't so great... 1. A bathroom rug was taken out of my room (no idea why) and never returned it. The marble floor in the bathroom was very dangerous when slippery...I had to throw towels on the ground to make sure I did not fall. 2. I was charged for items I did not take out of the minibar.
Swissotel looked polished, but check-in took forever, the room smelled stale, and the air conditioning barely worked. For the price, it felt far below expectations.
Booked a king suite for a weekend getaway. Air conditioner rattled all night, and housekeeping never came despite the do not disturb sign being off. Hit or miss at this price.

We had reservations (guaranteed by credit card) for 2 nights this past weekend. When we checked in the clerk told us that they could not accommodate us for both nights because they were overbooked due to a conference in town. I asked them to relocate us for both nights so that we would not have to move in the morning. They sent us over to another location that they assured could accommodate us. The night manager gave us the address to a different hotel and sent us on our way. Eventually we arrived at the correct second hotel where the staff were expecting a letter from the Sheraton for the transfer - something we were never given. Eventually we checked into this second property and the next afternoon when our keys didn't work we found out that the night manager of the Sheraton had not assured that we could stay both nights at the second hotel. So once again we had no place to stay despite having a guaranteed reservation with the Sheraton. In addition to all of this, we had to pay $24 for parking at the Sheraton to find out that they would not accommodate us despite a guaranteed reservation. I am still shocked by this bad experience.
Stayed at the Omni for a weekend and was pleasantly surprised by how quiet the room was. The bed was comfortable, staff friendly, and being near the shops made everything easy.

The room was freezing and the AC unit rattled all night, so sleep was impossible. Service felt robotic and distant, and housekeeping never replaced the towels. For these rates, I expected far more polish. Sadly, left disappointed.

I stayed for four nights while attending a conference. The hotel is in a great spot - easy walk to Michigan Ave shopping or Rush St., but just off the busy streets. The room I had was spacious, and very well-appointed. The staff was friendly, and the fitness center, while not huge, was well-equipped and clean. I've stayed at a number of hotels in Chicago, and this one is my favorite. Internet wasn't free, but at $10 for 24 hours is cheaper than most business hotels, and it worked very well.

Stayed here for three nights and honestly left impressed. The location was a dream for exploring--we could walk to the harbor in about ten minutes and grab a cab to the old town without any hassle. Yes, it's pricey, but given the plush bedding, the incredibly quiet room, and the genuinely warm service, I felt the splurge was justified. Breakfast was a highlight: the made-to-order omelets were fluffy, and the fresh pastries and tropical fruit selection felt far above the typical hotel buffet. I slept like a log both nights--the blackout curtains and the soft, supportive mattress were perfect after long walking days. Even the hallway ice machine was silent. If you can manage the cost, this is a solid, comfortable base that won't disappoint.

We stayed here for four nights and honestly, it exceeded what I was expecting. The front desk staff, especially a guy named Marcus, went out of his way to make our check-in smooth even though we arrived way past midnight due to a delayed flight. Our room was clean, spacious, and the bed was genuinely comfortable -- I haven't slept that well in a hotel in ages. The music theme is everywhere, and even as someone who isn't a die-hard rock fan, I thought it was fun rather than cheesy. Breakfast had a solid spread of options and the coffee was actually good, which matters to me. The location was convenient for getting around, and the pool area was never too crowded. Minor nitpick: the elevator situation got a bit slow during peak times. Would definitely come back.

We visited for my 40th birthday. We had never been to Chicago so was not sure where to stay. Found the deal on this hotel from Travelzoo. Great rate, staff was awesome, very helpful and nice, location was great. Enjoyed our stay but still like NYC better. Great, great hotel. Would stay again.

I booked the Conrad expecting a premium experience, but the reality fell far short of the price tag. The location is genuinely excellent, right in the heart of things, which is the only reason I'd rate it two stars instead of one. However, the value for money is poor; our 'deluxe' room felt tired, with dated furniture and a musty smell despite the inflated rate. The noise was a constant issue all night long--thin walls meant I could hear the neighboring guest's television and every hallway conversation, and the street traffic below kept my windows vibrating. Staff interactions felt transactional and cold. At check-in, I was handed a key without a smile or any acknowledgment of our anniversary, and when I asked for a quiet room or a later checkout, I was brushed off without empathy. It's a shame, because the property has potential, but this wasn't worth the splurge.

The room faced a bustling street, so traffic noise kept me up most of the night--I barely slept. Wi-Fi kept dropping, and while the location near downtown was handy, the constant din and poor connection made my stay genuinely frustrating.

Wished we could have stretched our time here into a second night, but even one evening at Hotel Amalfi felt wonderfully complete. The room was spotless, with crisp white linens and a bathroom that gleamed like it had just been sanitized. Breakfast was a pleasant surprise--fresh pastries, creamy cappuccino, and ripe fruit that didn't taste like it came from a can. Location-wise, you couldn't ask for better; we strolled to the marina in under five minutes and stumbled upon a quiet piazza for dinner. The staff even remembered our names at checkout, which added a personal touch. Only regret? Not booking longer. For a quick coastal stop, this place nails the essentials without fuss.
Expected far more from a Sofitel. Room felt tired, AC barely worked, and staff were indifferent at best. The so-called luxury price bought us noise until 2am and a mediocre breakfast. Won't be back.
Hotel Amalfi looked promising, but the room was tired, the air-conditioning barely worked, and street noise kept us awake. Staff seemed uninterested when we asked for help.

I expected more from Homewood given the nightly rate. The room looked tired, with scuffed furniture and a bathroom that never seemed quite clean despite being recently serviced. Noise was the biggest issue: doors slammed along the hallway late into the evening, and I could clearly hear the television and conversations from the room next door. Sleep was difficult even with earplugs, and the lumpy mattress did not help. Wi-Fi technically connected, but it dropped repeatedly and was too slow for a video call. Breakfast was crowded and picked over by 8 a.m. Staff were polite when asked for help, but no real solution was offered. For the price, this stay felt disappointing and not worth repeating.

We booked the Knickerbocker based on its reputation, but honestly, it missed the mark. Our room was dated, with scuffed furniture and a finicky thermostat that kept the place either sweltering or freezing. The bathroom had a lingering musty odor we couldn't shake no matter how long we ran the fan. We asked for extra towels twice and waited over an hour both times, only to receive them after we'd already given up. The bar was overpriced, and the bartender seemed annoyed that we wanted simple cocktails. Even the so-called 'lake view' was mostly a parking garage. For the nightly rate, I expected far more polish and attention to detail. I'm not sure what the hype is about, but I left feeling like we wasted our money on a faded, understaffed establishment that coasts on its history.

This hotel was great - In a great area right downtown and close to everything. The daily happy hour had great food, wine and premium liquors. The free breakfast was even better! Actually I believe everything was included breakfast/happy hour/business center/WiFi. Our room was a king size facing the back of the building. Really clean new and comfortable. Small touches such as books and cds to enjoy made the room feel less like a hotel - Would highly recommend.

Really enjoyed my stay at Hotel Allegro--the room was spotless, the bed surprisingly comfortable, and the staff were warm without being overbearing. The location also made exploring the city wonderfully easy.
The view was mostly parking lots, and the dated decor made the room feel tired. Our two-night stay dragged on thanks to constant hallway noise and thin walls.
Loved the old-school glamour at the Knickerbocker, especially the rooftop views after dinner. Our room was quiet, spotless, and surprisingly roomy, and the front desk made everything easy.

Staying at this hotel was one of the high points of a last minute, budget Valentines weekend trip for my husband and me. We got a great rate -- $70 -- on Priceline. Close to the subway (red line) and we got from O'Hare to the hotel in less than an hour for $3.50 for both of us. We were able to check in more than 4 hours early. Room was great -- very clean, good closet space and fantastic bedding. Had one expensive drink at the Irish bar, but the bartender's advice on restaurants and clubs to check out made it worth the price. Concierge was helpful, too. Overall, service was terrific, room was great and staying there was a treat. I would stay there again any time, especially at that price.
Desk staff acted like we were an inconvenience, and our 'city view' window faced a brick wall. Worse, the street noise kept me up all night despite earplugs--barely slept at all. Won't return.

The rooftop view of the skyline was the only saving grace, but the worn carpet and dusty corners made the room feel far from clean. For the price we paid, the painfully slow wifi and dated furnishings left us regretting the booking entirely.

Our stay at the Fairmont was excellent from check-in to departure. Our room overlooked the river and skyline, and the evening lights made it especially relaxing to sit by the window with a drink. The bed was wonderfully comfortable, with good pillows and effective blackout curtains, so we slept deeply despite being in the city. Breakfast offered plenty of choice, including fresh fruit, pastries, eggs made to order, and strong coffee; the staff kept everything replenished without being intrusive. The location was also ideal--close enough to walk to shops, restaurants, and major attractions, while still feeling calm once back at the hotel. Service throughout was warm and polished.

I wasn't expecting much from a mid-range hotel, but the Allegro genuinely surprised me. I slept like a log--the blackout curtains did their job, and the mattress had that perfect firm-but-plush balance. The WiFi held up even when I was streaming late at night, which is more than I can say for most places. My room was spotless: no dust on the baseboards, fresh-smelling linens, and a bathroom that looked like it had been scrubbed that morning. As for the decor, it's a bit of a time capsule--think early 2000s business chic with dark wood and geometric patterns--but it's well-maintained and has its own quiet charm. The location was ideal for walking to dinner and the staff at the front desk were genuinely warm. I'd book again without hesitation.

I really wanted to love the Conrad, but our stay fell far short of the price tag. The much-touted city view from our room was mostly obscured by a massive, grimy window that hadn't been cleaned in what looked like months. Smudges and water stains blurred the skyline into a depressing haze. Worse, the room itself felt stale. While the bed was made, I found a long, dark hair on the pillowcase and a sticky patch on the nightstand that clearly hadn't been wiped down. The wifi was a joke--constantly dropping during a video call, forcing me to tether my phone. As for sleeping, the air conditioning cycled on and off with a loud, rattling thump every twenty minutes. Add in the thin walls, and I barely got a wink. For these prices, I expected far more attention to detail; instead, I left feeling grimy and exhausted. We won't be back.

My stay at Hotel Amalfi was, frankly, a letdown from the moment I walked in. The 'boutique charm' advertised online translates to dark, cramped hallways and a lobby that smelled like stale cooking oil. My room faced the main road, and the noise was relentless--scooters revving and car horns blaring through the flimsy windows until past midnight. I barely slept. What little rest I got was on a mattress that sagged in the middle, and the pillow was as flat as a pancake. Breakfast the next morning was the final straw: lukewarm scrambled eggs, rubbery croissants, and coffee that tasted burnt.
