I found myself counting the hours until checkout, yet the check-in process was so slow I felt my vacation slipping away before it began. Given the price, I expected far more. Certainly not a stay I'd recommend.

Booked the Sofitel expecting Parisian elegance, but got worn carpets, a broken mini-bar, and staff who seemed annoyed by every request. The 'quiet' room faced a jackhammer. Not worth the premium--I'd pick a clean mid-range hotel next time.

This hotel was wonderful! I am a college student who went with my mom for the weekend and we both liked it! Pros: THE FRONT DESK and THE STAFF!!! -Helpful: Knew great places to eat and HOW to get there Breakfast: Pastries, coffee, tea, muffins, etc: Fresh Drinks + hors d'oeuvres: Yummy!! Rooms -Clean -Well decorated Lots of people of different ages stayed there Cons: Very very very far from the museums

The hotel is very impressive upon entering and the staff was very friendly, however we felt our room was very dated and worn looking. Our air conditioning didn't seem to be working well, but we turned it down and thought that it would eventually... cool off. Our first night was interrupted by a phone call at one A.M. That was a fax, it happened 4 times. By this time we realized that the air was not working again, so after fussing with the controls it did kick on. The next morning I mentioned to the concierge the issues with the phone, but didn't think to mention the issues with the air because it appeared to be working. After being out seeing the sites of Chicago for several hours and being very hot we were looking forward to resting in a cool room before going to a show . Our room was 78 degrees, I called and maintenience did come to check. After determining that the unit needed a motor it was another hour so we did not get to rest in a cool room before going out. I feel an offer should have been made to us by the hotel. Also was very surprised that WiFi was not a free service !! We will not be staying at the Hilton on our next trip to Chicago.

I travel to chicago quite often, and have stayed at a bunch of hotels. I stayed at Conrad a couple of times. My impression was not too good. Both times the receptionist was quite cold and I didn't feel welcome at all. The room was noisy. Thin walls, and you could hear exactly what the next room is talking about. One time the tv was broken too, and a guy came in and took like an hour to fix it... Anyway, given that this is a 4.5 star hotel, it really didnt live up to my expectations. After the 1st time at this hotel, I thought I might give it a second try. After the 2nd time, I decided I am really not coming back, especially given that there are so many other hotels close by. The other attendees of our conferences were also complaining about the hotel. So I guess I am not alone in this...

The room looked like a country club prison cell. Flat paint on all walls, doors, trims, not especially clean. A platform bed and a long shelf/desk with an iron chair. No amenities, no homey touches, nothing on the walls. No room service, no gym, no concierge. The air conditioner clunked off and on all night. On the plus side, the bedding was nice and there was a large screen TV. Don't waste your money.

This hotel does not belong in the same league as The Peninsula, Four Seasons, or Ritz Carlton. It was more like staying at an overpriced W Hotel. Staff was very nice and attentive, but the lobby is cramped, and only two small elevators for 17 floors!! Several times the elevator was full by the time it reached our floor, and we were forced to take the stairs. The hotel must be flooding the travel websites itself with high reviews.

We just got back from 3 nights at the Sofitel. We really have nothing bad or negative to say about it. We've stayed at other higher end hotels in Chicago such as the Park Hyatt, The Peninsula, and The Four Seasons - and the Sofitel tops them all. It's a 4 star hotel with 3 star prices. It's a beautiful hotel all the way around. Staff is uniformly friendly without being patronizing. They were helpful with the one small problem we had and solved it quickly. The common areas are fresh and modern in appearance. The room was very clean with comfortable beds and well-appointed marble-accented baths. My wife loved the huge tub. We had breakfast via roomservice every morning and it was always hot and delicious. The robes and Evian at turndown was always appreciated. The property is ideally situated in the middle of the Gold Coast and all the best shopping and eating is within a short walk. Want a Bentley or latte? They're all close by. This was our second stay since it opened and I'm sure it's to be our home away from home when we are in Chicago.

I really wanted to like Hotel Allegro, but the experience left me feeling cheated. I barely slept a wink; the air conditioning unit rattled like a trapped wasp all night, and the mattress was so lumpy I might as well have been on a park bench. The much-touted breakfast was a sad affair of lukewarm powdered eggs and stale pastries, with coffee that tasted burnt. The staff, while polite, were utterly indifferent, barely glancing up from their phones when I asked for a late checkout--they just shrugged. For the premium price we paid, this felt like a highway robbery. The location is decent, but that's the only saving grace. I've stayed in far better hostels for half the cost. Save your money and find somewhere else.

Mostly great with a few islands of relatively minor problems. First the good: Outside of the hotel and lobby were decorated like a winter wonderland, as befitted the season. The restaurant service was absolutely flawless ( servers who don't write orders because they are expected to remember them, remember clients clearly from one day to the other, and go above and beyond consistently). Rooms are comfortable: yes the beds are great! The gym is well equipped. Second the slightly off putting: mmmhh...we got the 'I love chocolate package' which advertized: bfast every day, dinner once, snack once and...a gift. And we have an A-Club favorite guest membership, which also advertized ' a gift'. So, no gift...either for the chocolate package or the favorite guest membership. Upon enquiry, 'the snack was the gift'. Not at all what the package suggested. That said, bfast was sublime and the chocolate dinner outstanding as well. Some problems at checkout though: we got charged for all dining despite having booked the package and it took quite a while for a polite but seemingly less than informed front desk staff to correct the problem. Would absolutely go back, but probably not on a special package.

This a great property, excellent location and wonderful staff. Everyone was very accommodating and polite. The room I had was on the 23rd floor and was like a suite, with a living area and a bedroom. The living room was spacious, with a plasma TV, a desk and a couch. The beds were very comfortable and the toiletries of very good quality. In the closed they placed an umbrella, which came in handy, it rained the whole time I was in Chicago. The internet connection is $9.95/24hrs. Great place, I will return for sure.

If you asked me two years ago, I would have recommended the Talbott Hotel without hesitation to anyone who asked. Now, I have definitely changed my mind. While this hotel is located in a nice area of Chicago, surrounded by great restaurants, shops and affluent people, it has really begun to slowly downgrade. As noted by my reviews, I am incredibly serious about customer service. If you're in the hospitality industry, there is really no excuse for falling short in this category--- but alas, the Talbott really has. The door staff don't say a word, the desk people acknowledge you only when they are not doing a million other things (which they always are) and the staff have an air of snobbishness. Inexcusable since we, the customers, are paying to stay at their over-priced hotel. Perhaps the most annoying aspect of my latest stay was that I had to walk down 11 flights of stairs to get to the lobby of the hotel because I waited a solid 15 minutes for the elevator, which, when it arrived, was packed to the brim. I get that it's an old hotel, but it is incredibly annoying that they only have two elevators for the entire place and when one is down for construction, the other one overflows with people and I am forced to walk ELEVEN flights to simply get to my dinner reservation on time (which I didn't.) I will not continue giving this hotel my business and have other better recommendations to give to friends who plan on visiting.

We booked a superior room with a sea view, but got a cramped box facing a brick wall. The front desk shrugged and said 'full occupancy.' Breakfast was cold scrambled eggs and stale pastries, not worth the €25. For these prices, absolutely not.

Our stay at the Omni was far more disappointing than expected. The lobby looked impressive, but the room felt tired, with scuffed furniture, dusty corners, and a bathroom fan that rattled all night. Check-in took nearly 25 minutes even though there was hardly anyone waiting, and the receptionist seemed more interested in chatting with a colleague than helping us. We also had to call twice for extra towels, which finally arrived late in the evening. The bed was comfortable enough, but the air conditioner kept cycling loudly and never seemed to reach the temperature we set. Breakfast was overpriced for lukewarm eggs and slow service. For the rate, I expected a polished, relaxing experience; instead, nearly every detail felt slightly neglected. I would probably choose another hotel next time.

Great stay at the Hyatt--worth every penny for the rate. Breakfast had fresh options beyond the usual, front desk staff were warm and quick with requests, and my room stayed impressively quiet despite the busy street. Would happily return.

It has been a couple of years since I stayed here, and got it for a night last weekend on Hotwire. I paid only $100 and stayed a Saturday night. I was very impressed with the redecorating done to the hotel. The lobby has always been great, but the rooms were a little shabby in the past. Not any more, as the hotel has been redecorated in the last few years. The location is still amazing, and with the Berghoff open again, there is a great restaurant within walking distance.

My stay at Hotel Omni was disappointing, especially considering the price. The location was convenient for getting around, with restaurants and public transportation nearby, but that was the main advantage. The room looked acceptable at first, yet the bathroom felt tired and poorly maintained, with cloudy fixtures, weak water pressure, and grout that clearly needed a deep clean. The bed was also a letdown; the mattress was too firm, and noise from the hallway kept waking me throughout the night. Staff were polite but not particularly helpful when I mentioned the problems. For what I paid, I expected a cleaner room, better soundproofing, and a more comfortable sleep. The convenient location does not make up for the worn facilities and lack of value, so I would not choose this hotel again.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly, it exceeded expectations. The room was spotless, with an incredibly comfortable bed and blackout curtains that made sleeping in feel glorious. The view of the river at sunset was a real highlight--I could have sat by the window all evening. Staff were professional without being stuffy; the concierge booked us a last-minute dinner spot that was fantastic. Breakfast had a good variety, though the coffee could have been stronger. The pool area was a bit crowded on Saturday afternoon, but that's my only minor gripe. Overall, a polished, relaxing stay that felt worth every penny. I'd happily return.

I stayed at the Omni for one night following a business meeting at another downtown Chicago hotel. I was completely impressed by the service; all personnel during my stay were absolutely outstanding. I checked in quite early (no problem) and was efficiently checked in. My room had a somewhat heavy scent of air freshener (the ONLY negative from the entire stay), which was managed reasonably well by opening the windows. I don't generally require much during my hotel stays, but suffice to say the doorman, housekeeping, the night manager and bartender at 676, the day waiter at 676, and the concierge were amazing - I never waited more than about 30 seconds for anything. The room was very comfy and the amenities were superior. One very tiny complaint - there was no wastebasket near the sink or near the wet bar - had to walk to the other end of the bathroom or sitting room to dispose of kleenex/coffee paraphernalia. One wastebasket would make all the difference. All that said - what a great hotel!! Thanks, Omni - I had a great stay!
Disappointing stay at the Fairmont. Our room wasn't ready at check-in, the AC barely worked, and housekeeping skipped our floor one day entirely. For the price, expected far better service.
Dusty surfaces and a stained carpet set the tone, and street noise kept me up half the night. Breakfast was sparse and lukewarm. Barely slept two solid hours--would not stay again.

Booked a room w/ a queen bed for 2 nights for a wonderful NYE, and was rather disappointed. Bed was either the world's smallest queen, or was actually a double, not to mention it was uncomfortably springy. Some of the things in the bathroom had been previously opened and used (q-tips). Lots of noise seemed to carry through the vents as we could hear other rooms rather clearly. When the tv was off, there was a very audible high-pitched humming noise that we could not get rid of unless we unplugged the tv. Hot water was very inconsistent in the shower. It is in a great location, however, next time I will try one of the other hotels in the area like the Intercontinental or Marriott. This might not be too bad if you are passing though quickly on business, but I wouldn't recommend it for a romantic night or two.

We spent three nights at the Swissotel and honestly wished it could have been longer. The staff stood out most to me -- the front desk upgraded our room without being asked, and the concierge was never pushy, just genuinely helpful when we asked about dinner spots nearby. The room itself was sleek and considerably more generous than I expected from a big chain tower, and the bathroom was a real highlight: granite counter, deep soaking tub, and water pressure that actually deserves the word 'powerful.' Given the river views and the location right near the Loop, the price felt fair, maybe even a bargain compared to some competitors. Sunday checkout was smooth and unhurried. If we get back to Chicago, this is where we'll stay again.

We were checked into a room with empty beer bottles, dirty underwear in the closet and unclean bathroom. There was no manager available for an hour to take any complaints. We missed our show because of the extra time it took in moving into another room etc. Finally when I got to talk to the manager and complained about beer bottles especially when I had a child and a teenager with me she offered to send me wine and cheese to make up for the inconvenience!!! Staff was somewhat reluctant to take request of extra blankets at night. They kept telling me to look into the closet for extra blankets. I asked for two blanket , but they delivered one. I had to keep calling to get settled. I saw a comment form from the prior guest in our room on the study desk, who had taken the trouble of filling it out, but no one collected it or cared for it. ht. Noisy rooms. Can hear the doors all night. Thebreakfast items kept running out and had to make calls to get them replenished. I will not recommend this hotel to any one even at discounted rates!!

Hotel Monaco was a great base for a weekend in the city. The location made it easy to walk to restaurants, shops, and several attractions, and we rarely needed a taxi. Our room was comfortable, quiet at night, and nicely maintained, with a bed that made it hard to get up in the morning. WiFi worked reliably for checking emails and streaming without interruptions. The front desk team was genuinely welcoming and quick to help with directions and dinner suggestions. It is not the cheapest option nearby, but the convenient location, polished atmosphere, and attentive service made it feel worth the price.

I have just returned from a lovely shopping trip to Chicago. It is a very nice hotel, and I will love to stay there if I visit Chicago again! There is a lot of positive to say about the hotel; staff is excellent, never experienced such an excellent service -- that alone is worth coming back for. Was pleasantly surprised that the room rate was including breakfast. A few things that could make this hotel even better... A hand shower in the bathroom. The hairdryer to be placed in the bedroom, instead of the bathroom, when the bathroom is all damp after a shower I prefer leaving the bathroom to dry my hair. Free internet access in the lobby. I was surprised I had to pay 6 or 7 USD (for 15 minutes) to log-on and check-in with my airline (only with a few airlines you can check-in without paying?!?!?!?)

I just left the Conrad Chicago and have nothing but good things to say. We used Hilton points to stay there but paid $35/night to upgrade to a junior suite. We were in room 1519. I would reccomend people ask for an odd numbered room so that they will have a view looking north on Michigan Ave. Our room was very modern with 2 large HD/flat panel tv and Bose 3 speaker sound system. 4 big windows that actually open. The bed lineds were very nice, the towels were OK. The room was clean and the bath room had a seperate shower and tub. Marble everywhere. Robes, slippers, etc. The work out room was good with different machines and some free weights. There are clean towels in the workout room too. We never ate in the hotel so I can't comment on the food or the prices. There is a Starbucks across the street (Michigan) and an Espresso bar attached to the Nordstrom that is on the ground floor of the hotel. It was very nice to have the little mall right under the hotel. The location of the hotel could not be better. We were walking distance to everything. Every kind of shopping or dinning experience you could possibly want was within 2 miles. Over all the hotel had a boutique feel to it even though it is part of the hilton chain.

My stay at the InterContinental was more disappointing than expected for a hotel at this price point. The lobby still has an impressive entrance, but the room decor felt dated, with worn-looking furniture, dull carpeting, and scuffed walls rather than the fresh, polished atmosphere I expected. Housekeeping had done a basic job, though I found dust along the desk and a few crumbs near the bedside table. The bed was comfortable enough, but street noise made it difficult to sleep. I only stayed two nights, which was probably long enough; by the second morning I was ready to leave. The bathroom was clean overall, but cramped, with weak water pressure, limited counter space, and fixtures that looked overdue for replacement. Staff were courteous, yet the experience never felt especially welcoming or worth the cost.

I expected much more from Swissotel for the price. Check-in took nearly 30 minutes because the desk seemed understaffed, and nobody explained the facilities or breakfast hours. The room looked polished at first, but the carpet had stains, the air conditioning rattled all night, and the bathroom smelled faintly of damp towels. I called twice about the noise from the room next door and was told someone would 'look into it,' but nothing changed. Breakfast was crowded, with empty trays and cold coffee by 9 a.m. The location was convenient, but that was about the only positive. For a supposedly upscale hotel, the service and maintenance felt surprisingly careless.

My stay at Swissotel was a real disappointment, especially considering the price. Check-in took nearly 30 minutes, and the front desk staff seemed distracted and never explained the hotel facilities or Wi-Fi properly. The room looked tired, with scuffed furniture, stained carpet, and a bathroom fan that rattled loudly throughout the night. Our supposedly quiet room faced a busy road, so sleep was difficult even with the windows closed. Housekeeping also forgot to replace the towels one day, and calling reception took several attempts before anyone answered. Breakfast had a decent selection, but most of the hot food was lukewarm and the dining area was crowded and chaotic. The location is convenient, but that alone does not justify the rates. I expected a polished, comfortable experience and left feeling that Swissotel offered neither.
Affinia looked dated, the room smelled musty, and the air conditioner rattled all night. Staff were polite, but the overpriced stay was far from relaxing.

We booked this hotel using points on our credit card. When we arrived, we were immediately greeted by a friendly face. We arrived several hours before check-in. However, they let us check-in early. They also gave us a free room upgrade. The hotel is absolutely stunning! In addition, it is off of State Street. There are many things to do - shopping, dinning, theater. It is also close to public transportation if you would like to go to the United Center or the airport. The hotel also allowed us to have a late check-out at no additional charge. The room was so dark and quiet we slept in.

Not a good start when the front desk isn't willing to tell their customers that they have a problem with your room! We reserved a King Suite, and the hotel put us in a Queen Suite without telling us up front. Only after we confronted the Manager did they come clean about the switch, he offered us a free breakfast, but would not up-grade our room. The whole problem could have been avoided if they would have told us the truth and let us decide if we still were willing to stay at the Omni. We will not be retuning to this Hotel again.
Our room overlooked noisy construction, the AC rattled all night, and the front desk brushed off our concerns. For the price, the worn furniture and slow elevators were a real letdown.

The Wi-Fi dropped constantly during my work calls, and the hallway noise from neighboring guests kept me up until 2 AM. I barely slept, and my room's view looked straight into a concrete wall--utterly grim for the price.

We absolutely loved the Knickerbocker. Now, if you expect your hotels to be cookie cutter comfortable, forget this place. If Holiday Inns are like the rows of housing developments in the suburbs, the Knickerbocker is like those beautiful old houses in the center of the city. The location is great, the hotel bar is cozy and classy, and the rooms feel like guest bedrooms in Victorian mansions. For the price, you simply can't do any better than this in downtown Chicago.

The staff remembered our name every morning at breakfast, which made the whole stay feel personal. The room was spotless and the beds were incredibly comfy, plus the location is perfect for hitting the Strip. We'll definitely be back.

Stayed at the Talbott for a quick business trip and was genuinely impressed--the location is unbeatable, steps from the river. My room was spotless, quiet, and the bed was superb. Staff even remembered my coffee order by day two. Would happily return.
Hotel Amalfi was a lovely surprise--our room was clean and comfortable, the staff genuinely welcoming, and breakfast had plenty of fresh choices. The location made exploring everything easy.

The location of this hotel was excellent as it is just beside the subway and the bus stop for the free trolley bus to Navy Pier is just beside the hotel. The room was very spacious. Kind of too big for a solo traveler. The view from the room was excellent and it was a great view to sleep at night. The bathroom was spacious too and the room has a big wardrobe. The kitchen has microwave oven and cooking utensils. Some of the cooking utensils were a bit dirty, probably because they had not been used for sometime. However, the microwave oven was very useful as I can heat up food to eat at night. You can easily walk to the magnificent mile by cutting across the shopping mall across the road. Do check out Pizzeria Uno which is near the hotel that serves the delicious deep dish pizza. For cheaper food, do check out the foodcourt at the shopping mall. The hotel also serves breakfast and dinner from Mon to Thur. I did not find the food that fantastic but it was pretty decent. I will strongly recommend this hotel to everyone going to Chicago.

Genuinely lovely stay at the Knickerbocker--the room was sleek and quiet despite Times Square being right outside, and the rooftop bar view alone was worth it. Staff treated us like regulars from day one.

I expected far more from a property carrying the Swissotel name. We arrived for a three-night stay and were put in a room facing the service alley, so the 'city view' I'd requested never materialized -- just bins, deliveries and a brick wall. It was also noisier than I'd imagined: constant beeping from trucks in the morning and hallway chatter late at night despite the do-not-disturb sign. The bathroom was the real letdown. Water pressure barely trickled, the shower temperature swung from cold to scalding, and the grout in the corners was stained with mildew. The decor felt frozen around 2009, with a faded brown carpet, scratched cabinetry and that beige-on-beige look that just reads tired now. Staff were polite when we flagged issues, but nothing much changed. For the price, I won't be returning.
Despite the friendly lobby staff, the room smelled damp, the AC rattled all night, and housekeeping skipped our towels. Definitely not the relaxing stay we expected.

staff was very courteous. desk clerk gave only one coupon for the free breakfast instead of two. second desk clerk gave the wrong time for the breakfast on the second day, causing us to miss the free period. room was very clean, with a nice view of the river. bed was very comfortable. toilet looked like it belonged in a public restroom (no tank; instead it had a stainless steel valve) instead of a 4-star hotel. no dresser to store clothes. no wastebasket in the room, and there was a cover for the icebucket, but no icebucket. folding luggage stand had a broken strap. location was good, close to the river. several american-style eating places nearby. overall, a disappointment for a four-star hotel. i expected more for a hyatt regency.

I had a very pleasant stay at the Conrad and would happily return. The lobby felt polished without being stuffy, and the front desk team made check-in easy even though I arrived later than planned. My room was quiet, beautifully kept, and had a comfortable bed that made it difficult to get up for an early meeting. I also appreciated the small details: plenty of outlets by the desk, good water pressure, and blackout curtains that actually worked. Breakfast was fresh and the staff remembered my coffee order on the second morning, which was a nice touch. The location made it simple to walk to restaurants and nearby attractions. It is definitely a higher-end hotel, but the service and overall comfort made the price feel justified.

Reservation was for a King size bed, instead I was given a double-bed room. Check-in person must had a bad hair day, because she was unfriendly. Wall St Journal or USA Today is not complimentary. Requested a room that is away from the noisy elevator, but given a room next to a service elevator which is more noisy. I didn't bother to file a formal complain because I was very tire. I travel often to Chicago for business and the first will be the last at Intercontinental.

My husband and I were very excited to be staying at the Conrad, unfortunately, we would never stay in this hotel again. The rooms looked nice, but the closer you look there was mold in the bathroom and red stains that looked like dried blood near the sink. The room service cost was super high - costing us over $100 for 1 burger, 1 order of french toast, 2 pops and 2 desserts. In the middle of the night the pipes in our room made a very loud vibrating noise which kept us awake. We called the front desk and it took almost 40 minutes for someone to walk over to our room (we were on the 5th floor, same as the reception desk). They did nothing to fix it and the same thing continued the following night and anytime the room above us or to the right used their shower. The staff was friendly enough, but NOT helpful and they did nothing to try and make our stay better with all of the problems. There was not even a coffee pot in the room. Definitely would NOT stay here again for the price. NOT worth it!

For a hotel at this price point, the Talbott was a letdown. The room felt tired and dated, the noise from the street kept us up half the night, and staff service was indifferent at best. Probably won't be back.
Fresh, stylish decor and a bright city view made our stay at Hotel Palmer feel special. The central location was wonderfully convenient, though our two-night visit ended far too soon.

Booked a 'Rock Star Suite' expecting the legendary Hard Rock vibe, but honestly, it felt like paying a premium for faded glamour. The room was dark and dated, with scuffed headboards and a bathroom that had seen better decades. Housekeeping was inconsistent--towels were missing one day, and the mini-fridge was warm on arrival. The air conditioning rattled all night, so I got maybe four hours of sleep.

The lobby is flashy, sure, but the actual service is where the polish stops. Front desk staff were polite but indifferent, and when I asked for a late checkout, I got a curt 'we're fully booked' that clearly wasn't true. The pool area was packed with non-guests from a private event, making it unusable. For these prices, I expected the rock-and-roll energy, not a tired conference hotel with a guitar mural.

Honestly, I'd look elsewhere next time. The brand's reputation outpaced the reality here.
Disappointing for the price: the bathroom felt dated and cramped, street noise disturbed sleep, and although the InterContinental's location was convenient, it didn't justify the expensive stay.

Stayed at the Knickerbocker for a long weekend and honestly couldn't have picked a better spot. The lobby is gorgeous without feeling stuffy--that old-school glamour mixed with a laid-back vibe. Check-in was a breeze, and the guy at the desk even remembered my name the next morning when I asked for coffee directions, which I thought was a nice touch. Room was on the smaller side, but the bed was insanely comfortable and the blackout curtains actually worked, so I slept like a rock. Location is unbeatable for walking to the river or catching an Uber up north. The rooftop bar gets busy, but we snagged a seat at sunset and the view of the city was worth every penny of the overpriced cocktail. Only minor hiccup was the hallway noise one night, but it died down quickly. Would absolutely book here again for a city escape.
The bathroom felt dated and grimy, hallway noise kept waking me, and the lumpy bed offered little rest. Breakfast was cold, sparse, and not worth the price.

I actually booked this reservation with the hotel over the phone and got a great rate -- much lower than the usual price! It was a lovely hotel, beautifully appointed, walking distance from the places we wanted to go. We would highly recommend the Fairmont.

Months prior to my 5-night reservation with the Hilton Chicago I requested a room that allowed in a lot of natural light, facing an open view, not a close building. (The reservation was made through a conference travel agency.) I confirmed my request by telephone a few days in advance directly with the hotel and at check-in the clerk noted it in my record. She told me it would be difficult to find, but consulted a chart and appeared to be satisfied with the room she assigned me. I was very surprised to open the door onto a room on the inside of one of the towers, tucked into a very dark corner, facing a wall of rooms. I called the desk immediately and was told that the hotel was sold out and it was hard to tell what rooms were still available that suited my request, but to 'sit tight' and someone would call me. No one did. Further calls yielded similar results. At one point I was told I could have a 'parlor room,' with a sofa bed, at a reduced rate, but I could not go see the room before committing to moving. That's real hospitality for you. Worried that a bad sofa bed could be worse than rooming in a cave, I ended up staying in the dreadfully dark room. (I had asked for a bright room with one bed and got a dark room with two beds.) The only redeeming feature of the room was that it had 2 bathrooms. Other than that, it was tight quarters with a tiny closet, two uncomfortably low chairs, at the desk and in a (dark) corner. Light fixtures didn't do much to brighten things up. Since I was here at a conference, I really wanted a bright environment to wake up early and start the workday in and to have as a cheerful office for mid-day calls and e-mail, but instead I got a cave. Consequently, I spent as little time as possible in the room and next time I am in Chicago, conference or not, I will absolutely stay at another hotel. There are much better locations that the Hilton Chicago and looking at the percentage of 'inside tower' rooms, places with a much better chance of having a bright room as well as better customer service. Shame on the Chicago Hilton.

The Knickerbocker's location is hard to beat, right by Times Square yet surprisingly quiet inside. Bed was incredibly comfortable and the rooftop bar views alone were worth it. Staff went out of their way to help with dinner reservations. Would happily return.

My stay at the Hyatt was disappointing, especially considering the price. Check-in took nearly 30 minutes because only one person was working the desk, and she seemed overwhelmed. The room looked tired rather than polished: scuffed furniture, stained carpet near the window, and a bathroom fan that rattled loudly all night. Housekeeping also skipped my room on the second day, even though I had left the sign off the door. I called twice for extra towels and finally had to collect them from the front desk myself. Breakfast was crowded, with several empty stations and lukewarm food. The location was convenient, and the bed was reasonably comfortable, but those positives did not make up for the poor maintenance and inattentive service. I expected a much smoother experience from Hyatt.

Stayed at Hotel James for three nights and honestly couldn't have asked for a better base. The location is fantastic for exploring, but what really sold me was the value. For the quality of the room, the amenities, and the service, I felt like I got a steal. Breakfast each morning was a genuine highlight--fresh pastries, proper coffee, and made-to-order eggs that beat any continental buffet I've tried. The room faced the courtyard, so street noise was never an issue, and the blackout curtains were a lifesaver. I slept like a log every single night, which almost never happens in hotels. The bed was firm but supportive, and the pillows were perfect. If you're weighing options, choose this one--you won't regret it. I'm already planning my return trip.

I was a bit wary about the carpet in the hallways, but honestly, the room itself felt fresh and modern, with clean lines and a comfortable, neutral palette. The Wi-Fi was flawless--I streamed a movie without a single hiccup, which is rarer than you'd think. And the bed? I slept like a log, truly. The blackout curtains did their job, and the mattress had that perfect balance of firm and plush. Surprisingly, it was also dead quiet at night; I heard nothing beyond the soft hum of the AC. I will say the bathroom fixtures looked a little dated, but everything was spotless and functional. Overall, a solid, restful stay. For the price, this location is a steal, and I'd happily book again next time I'm in the area.

We didn't stay in the hotel a lot because we went for the sites not the room. Saying that, we picked this hotel because it was the cheapest but the hotel not having any parking we spent money on parking our car than what we could have spent on a better more expensive hotel with parking. Hotel is great for guys getaway weekend that won't have a car. Not a family frienly hotel. Dining tip: Long walk from hotel Gino's pizza is a must have!! Worth the walk. Many things in between hotel and Gino's to do so you can break up the walk.
The room had dusty surfaces and a stained carpet, Wi-Fi kept dropping, and the sparse, lukewarm breakfast was forgettable. For the price, Hotel Talbott was a real disappointment.

I was honestly bracing for a lackluster stay given some older photos I'd seen online, but the Hyatt surprised me. Our room faced the courtyard, and the silence was remarkable--I slept through the night without a single hallway squeak or street rumble, which almost never happens for me. The bedding was crisp and the blackout curtains did their job perfectly. While the lobby has a classic, slightly traditional feel, the room itself felt freshly updated with clean lines and modern fixtures, nothing tired or worn. For the rate we paid, especially with the breakfast included, it felt like solid value--not a steal, but fair for the comfort and service. I'd happily book again for a quiet, stress-free weekend.

Really pleasant stay at the Homewood. Room was spotless, bathroom had good water pressure and plenty of towels, and the free breakfast offered a nice variety. Staff were warm and quick to help with everything. Would happily return.

The room was fine at first glance, but the air conditioning rattled all night and the hallway noise made sleep impossible. Staff seemed overwhelmed at check-in, and the breakfast buffet ran out of everything by 8 AM. Not the Hilton standard I expected.

My stay at Hotel Palmer was exactly what I needed--a comfortable, no-fuss base that made exploring feel effortless. The room wasn't huge, but it was smartly laid out, with a surprisingly plush bed and blackout curtains that actually worked. I slept like a log.

The real standout, though, was the breakfast. Fresh pastries, good coffee, and eggs cooked to order, all served in a bright little nook off the lobby. It beat any chain buffet I've tried. The front desk team also went out of their way to book a last-minute dinner reservation for me when everywhere seemed full.

Sure, the decor is a bit dated, and you'll hear hallway noise now and then. But for the price, the friendly service, and the quiet street location, I'd happily return. It's not flashy, but it's genuinely solid.

The location was lovely, but the hotel itself feels tired and dated. The air conditioning barely worked, breakfast was chaotic, and our room smelled musty. Definitely not worth the premium price we paid.
Expected more from Swissotel. The room felt tired and the AC rattled all night, and housekeeping barely showed up. Location is fine, but for this price I won't be returning.

We stayed at the Affinia for a long weekend and honestly had a great time. Check-in was quick despite us arriving early, and the front desk guy even mentioned they'd try to get us into a room right away, which they did. The room itself was bigger than expected for a city hotel, with a little kitchenette that came in handy for leftover pizza and morning coffee. Beds were comfortable, though the pillows were a bit soft for my taste, so I asked for a firmer one and housekeeping brought it up within ten minutes. Location was solid, plenty of food options nearby and easy access to the subway. One tiny thing: the hallway elevator wait could stretch a bit at peak times, but nothing that ruined anything. Would happily come back next trip.
Homewood was a great fit for our family--quiet room, comfortable beds, and the little kitchen made mornings easy. Breakfast stayed stocked, and the front desk was genuinely helpful.

I had really high hopes for the InterContinental given its reputation, but my three-night stay left me honestly underwhelmed. The location is undeniably convenient, right in the heart of everything and steps from the metro, so I'll give it that. Unfortunately, that central position meant constant traffic noise filtering into my room even on the fourteenth floor, andInforma I barely slept. Housekeeping also seemed to miss my room one day entirely -- used glasses sat out until evening, and I found hairs on the bathroom floor on arrival. The front desk staff were polite enough but slow to resolve anything; requesting a room change took two phone calls and a visit in person. For the price point, the service and upkeep simply don't match. I expected far more from a property calling itself a luxury hotel.

I stayed in a Deluxe King Suite. No desk to work at or to sit at to eat room service meals. The only table was coffee table height and the couch was some strange futon that was lower than the coffee table (!) and canted forward. Incredibly uncomfortable to sit at and ridiculous for room service meals or to work at computer. Since my room was configured like all the other Deluxe King Suites depicted in on line photos, I have to assume this design flaw with the couch/futon runs throughout the property. Bed was fine and bath was fine but I can't imagine why business travelers would rate this property well. The couch/futon seating is the worst I've encountered in a modern hotel.

I'm sitting in the hotel as I right this review and am not impressed with the room. The hotel is not modern in the least - it feels like you're staying in your grandmother's attic. Wallpaper is peeling off the wall, not well lit, very few outlets in the room -- especially convenient ones (none next to the bed or built into lamps), terrible views and loud construction noises woke me up at 7am. Even the location is off the beaten path - closest L stop is on the Red Line -- so not accessible via the loop stops on the blue line from the airport without transferring. Health club is not on site either. There are hundreds of other hotels I would stay in over this one.
Expected far more from a hotel at this price. The room was musty with stains on the carpet, the wifi barely loaded anything, and my 'city view' mostly faced a brick wall. Not worth the money at all.

From the moment I checked in, the Omni felt like a calm retreat tucked right in the middle of the city's energy. My room on the 14th floor faced the lake, and I caught a spectacular sunset over the water that I didn't expect to see from a business trip. What impressed me most was how genuinely quiet it was--I heard none of the typical street noise or hallway chatter, and I slept deeply both nights, waking up refreshed before my meetings. The bathroom was a real highlight: a spacious walk-in shower with excellent water pressure, thick towels, and plenty of counter space for my toiletries. Everything felt thoughtfully designed for comfort rather than just style. The staff were warm without being intrusive, and location-wise, I could walk to dinner easily. I'd gladly book here again for a stay that balances work and relaxation effortlessly.

I'd heard great things about Hotel Monaco, but my stay left me scratching my head. The lobby's gold-and-maroon palette felt frozen in the late nineties, with worn velvet armchairs and a dusty chandelier that screamed for an update. My room's decor was equally tired--peeling wallpaper near the window and a carpet with mysterious stains I avoided stepping on. Sleep was elusive; the mattress sagged in the middle, and the air conditioner rattled like a dying lawnmower all night, cycling on and off every twenty minutes. Breakfast was a letdown: lukewarm scrambled eggs, stale croissants, and coffee that tasted burnt, served in a cramped, noisy dining area. The staff, though, were polite but utterly indifferent--no smiles, no proactive help, just mechanical yes/no answers to my questions about local transport. For the price, I expected charm and care, not this faded, forgettable experience. I won't be returning.
Disappointing stay at Hotel Talbott: the room looked clean at first but had dusty corners, breakfast was mediocre, and the Wi-Fi kept dropping, making the high price feel unjustified.

I really wanted to like the Hotel Palmer, but our stay was a letdown from start to finish. Check-in took nearly forty minutes because the front desk was understaffed and the clerk seemed completely lost. Our room smelled faintly of mildew, the air conditioning rattled all night, and the 'city view' was basically a wall three feet from the window. The hairdryer didn't work, and housekeeping skipped our room entirely on the second day. Breakfast was the real low point--cold eggs, stale pastries, and the coffee machine broke down while we were standing there. Worse, nobody apologized or offered any kind of accommodation when we complained; we just got shrugs. For the price they charge, this place is seriously overrated. I won't be back, and I'd suggest looking elsewhere.

Three nights at the Intercontinental left me genuinely puzzled about the reputation. We booked a 'premium' room and got a view of a brick wall, with windows that hadn't been properly cleaned in weeks. The air conditioning rattled all night, and when I mentioned it at the desk, they promised to send engineering--nobody ever came. Housekeeping skipped our room entirely one day, and when we called for towels, it took an hour and a half. The lobby is grand, sure, but the hallways smell like stale carpet and the elevator wait is absurd during checkout. The pool was overcrowded, the sauna lukewarm, and the breakfast buffet is overpriced for rubber eggs and stale pastries. Honestly, the only bright spot was the bartender on the 14th floor, who genuinely tried to make up for the chaos. For the nightly rate, this is a hard pass. I've had better service at a mid-tier chain.

We spent three nights at The Talbott and honestly, it was the perfect home base. The location can't be beat--we walked everywhere, and coming back to that quiet, tucked-away entrance on Delaware felt like a small escape from the street bustle. Our room was on the smaller side, but it was so thoughtfully laid out that it never felt cramped. The bed was exceptionally comfortable, and I slept better than I do at home. The staff genuinely stood out; from the doorman who remembered our names to the front desk team that booked us a last-minute dinner reservation. The little touches, like fresh flowers in the lobby and the cozy bar, gave it that old-world charm without feeling stuffy. We even appreciated the filtered water station on our floor. It's not the fanciest or flashiest, but it's warm, efficient, and incredibly well-run. We wouldn't hesitate to return.

Stayed for a conference and was genuinely impressed. The suite was spotless, bed super comfy, and the evening reception with hot food was a nice surprise. Staff went out of their way to help with directions. Would absolutely book again.

Let me start by saying we are seasoned travelers who take 5-6 trips for pleasure on a yearly basis (not including our business travel). We've traveled all over the world and often stay at older hotels because of their charm and attention to detail. We were not at all impressed by this hotel. At $220/night we were expecting a decent, clean hotel but obviously not a 5*. We were highly disappointed by the state of the room we were given (1546). The paint/wallpaper/tub were peeling, there was hair in both the tub/toilet when we got to the room, the internet service was extremely slow, the toilet ran throughout the night, and quite frankly we were not convinced the bedding was changed from the previous guests as it was wrinkled and look slept in. We told the gentleman working at the front desk about the state of our room and his response was 'I know, we can't wait for our renovations.' If it hadn't been for the fact we were meeting up with our relatives who were traveling from the UK & booked into this hotel by a travel agent, we would have checked out as soon as we checked in. Let me also add that the front desk seemed short-staffed as the check-in/check-out process was painfully slow. All we can credit the hotel with is a great location and very friendly/responsive door staff. In its day this was likely a lovely hotel & but it is in dire need of a renovation. Despite its location I cannot understand how travelers continue to pay those rates for such a sub-par experience. We would never book at this hotel again.

My stay at the Hotel Amalfi was genuinely relaxing, and it's rare I find a city hotel that hits this many notes so well. I was a bit worried about street noise given the location, but our room faced the inner courtyard and it was wonderfully quiet--I slept through all eight hours without a single interruption. The Wi-Fi was solid too, which mattered since I had to answer a few work emails; no dropped connections, and the speed was plenty for video calls. Breakfast was a pleasant surprise: fresh pastries, decent coffee, eggs made to order, and a nice spread of local cheeses. The room itself was spotless, with crisp white linens and a bathroom that looked like it had just been deep-cleaned. Honestly, the whole stay felt effortless, and I'd happily return.

I have stayed at the Omni off an on over the years. On business, for personal trips. This trip started off quite rocky, and left me very un-impressed. 1) Be aware, they have a new policy where they charge debit card $55 per day for 'incidentals' which you *may* incur. They do this if you elect not to use a standard credit card. Even if you have booked and paid for your room in advance. The desk clerk claimed 'all the hotels do this now'...funny how when I put a remote employee at the O'Hare hilton on my business debit card, I was never asked for additional funds. Having a policy is one thing, spreading blame for it is another. While not a problem for me, someone who plans trips down to the dollar and dime might encounter a problem with this 'policy' of theirs. To my knowledge, they never did this sort of thing before. (I don't use Credit Cards, its why I have money in a recession. =)) 2) Rooms were clean, but their in room accoutrements and mini bar items had no price list. The only thing labelled with a price was a bottle of water (about 600 ML) for $7.50. As such, be careful with the tray of goodies. If the water is $7.50, imagine what the snickers bar might cost. 3) Our suite had a bathroom sliding door between the bedroom and bathroom which appeared broken, and would not move. Calling the front desk resulted in ... nothing. Finally about 9:00 PM I elected to have another look at it, and it seemed to be off its track. I was able to successfully 'fix' it, but the lack of response from maintenance, considering the rate for a suite, is sad. I remember this hotel being much more attentive and responsive. 4) The seem to cut a lot of corners on room stocking now. Overall, I think I will be skipping the Omni, and they will get no more of my business. It seems Hilton treats people better overall. It's quite sad, as I have a lot of good memories with Omni. I will not be back.
The room was spotless and comfortable, with a lovely skyline view. Omni's central location made exploring easy, though our relaxing weekend getaway felt far too short.
For Conrad prices, the dusty room and stained bathroom were unacceptable. Breakfast was lukewarm and sparse, making the whole stay feel like poor value rather than a luxury experience.
Spotless room with fresh, modern decor and a bathroom that felt genuinely upscale. The bed was so comfortable I slept straight through the night. Would happily return!

Just returned to Seattle after a visit home to Chicago and I loved The James!!! Recently stayed at the Ritz at Water Tower and the Dana around the corner--both of which were great but The James was perfect. Secured the room through a package w/ American Express for a great deal so though the view wasn't great the space, decor and location can't be beat. Staff was friendly, courteous and very helpful, the gym was substantial and though I didn't try the restaurants/room service, the menus looked yummy. I've stayed in Chgo in that area on avg 1-2s/mo over the past three years and the James is at the top my list now. If you can get a good deal, I highly recommend!!
Homewood felt worth the price, with a clean bathroom, reliable Wi-Fi, and a tasty breakfast with plenty of choices. A comfortable, convenient stay overall.
The bathroom was spotless with strong water pressure, breakfast had plenty of fresh options, and the staff were genuinely helpful. For the comfort and service, Sheraton felt worth the price.
My window faced a drab parking structure, and traffic noise kept me awake most of the night. The room had dusty surfaces and stained carpet, making the steep rate feel unjustified.

We wrapped up a conference downtown and decided to stretch the trip into a long weekend at the Hilton. Honestly, the location was the first win--steps from the river walk and maybe ten minutes to Grant Park. But the real surprise was how quiet the room stayed despite the busy streets below. I'm a light sleeper, and I didn't hear a single siren all three nights. The bed was firm in that just-right way, and the blackout curtains actually did their job. Breakfast at the lobby cafe was pricey, so we grabbed pastries elsewhere, but the in-room coffee was drinkable--a bigger compliment than most hotels get. The front desk clerk remembered my name on day two and offered a late checkout without me even asking. Small touches like that make the difference. I'd book here again for work or play.

Our weekend at the Conrad felt far too brief--we were just getting comfortable when checkout arrived. The staff, from the valet to the front desk, anticipated our needs with genuine warmth; the concierge even remembered our coffee preference on the second morning. Our room was immaculate, with crisp linens and a sparkling bathroom that smelled faintly of eucalyptus. I'm picky about WiFi, but the connection here was seamless, streaming video without a single drop. The only reason I hesitate to give five stars is that the breakfast buffet, while delicious, ran out of fresh pastries by 9 AM. Still, the housekeeping team refreshed our towels twice daily and left our space spotless. A memorable, cozy escape--I only wish we'd booked one more night.
Stayed for a weekend escape and was blown away. The room was stylish, quiet, and spotless, while the staff's friendly, genuine service made us feel truly pampered. Highly recommend.
Hotel Monaco had a great downtown location, and the staff made us feel welcome right away. Our room was quiet, comfortable, and nicely decorated; I'd happily stay here again.

The Omni is in a fabulous location on Michigan Avenue. Within just blocks are all types of stores, including Saks, Nordstroms, H&M, Filenes Basement, Macys, La Perla, Apple, Bloomingdates.....I could go on and on! The room itself was fabulous. Comfortable, nice big flat screen tvs, nice sized bathroom. They charge for Wi-Fi, but we found if we clicked yes on joining their guest program we could then go from the sign-on screen right to our email without actually completing the registration. We got this hotel for $214/night through Priceline and felt it was a terrific deal!
Disappointing stay at Swissotel: the room felt dated, housekeeping missed basic details, and check-in dragged on. For the price, I expected far better service and comfort.

We have just returned from a week at the James Chicago. The hotel is fabulous, very chic and chilled. The service is beyond compare. Check in and out were swift and painless. The Concierge service is also super efficient having located an excellent hair salon and a couple of fab restaurants for us during our stay. The hotel restaurant itself is rated 5 in the top 10 in Chicago - voted by Chicago residents. We stayed on the 14th floor with great views of the city. The room (a deluxe king) was equipped with a great selection of cocktail making lovelies, hairdryer, safe, tv, robes & slippers, a very interesting selection of minibar items (one of which was a real surprise!) including crisps/snacks a first aid kit and an umbrella! We also had a spotless and elegant bathroom with Kiehls products and a cosy little dining area. The ipod dock/CD/radio and complimentary chillout CD were a nice touch and husband liked the enormous plasma tv. The super comfy bed ensured a good snooze and complimentary WiFi allowed us to plan our next day's activities from our bedroom. We were so busy touring around the city we didn't get an opportunity to use the gym or the spa - both of which looked fab. The bar/lobby area is a haven of civilised tranquility with smooth music playing in the background to help you chillout that bit more. Staff are attentive without being fussy and a good selection of drinks and bar snacks are available. The barman mixes a mean mohito ! This hotel is full of nice little thoughtful touches to make people feel welcomed and cared for e.g. The Virtual Tuck In service - basically a couple of PCs with webcams to allow people to say goodnight to their children when they're away from home on business. Also the dog biscuits and water outside the front door for our furry friends. Next visit to Chicago I'll definitely be staying here and wouldn't even consider an alternative if The James can maintain these standards.

I really expected more from a hotel with this reputation. The room itself was decent, but the noise was relentless -- I could hear the elevator shaft all night, plus doors slamming in the hallway until well past midnight. I'd booked four nights and honestly by night two I was counting down. The staff were polite enough at check-in, but every request afterward seemed to be someone else's job; housekeeping was never called back and my wake-up call never came on the last morning. For nearly 300 euros a night, this felt poor value -- I've stayed in far cheaper places that delivered more comfort and actual service. The location is convenient, I'll grant that. But overall a disappointing, restless stay that I wouldn't repeat at these prices.

Room smelled musty, and we found a hair on the pillow--hardly Hilton standards. Location was handy for downtown, but the dated decor and a cold, soggy breakfast buffet made the stay feel like a letdown.

We stayed at the Ritz Carlton two weeks prior, and in comparison the Sofitel does not come close. With the deal the Ritz Carlton is putting on right now, stay two nights...get one free, choose the nicer option! Pros: Room Service: Quick! 15 minutes tops. Bathroom: Large bathroom with a separate shower and tub. Lobby: Very impressive, and the doormen are on top of opening the doors and hailing a cab for you. Location: Close to the train station and MI Ave. Cons: NO TOP SHEET! We asked the others at the conference, they confirmed...there is no top sheet. You just sleep with the duvet cover over you. Room: -Small, and not a fan of the modern decor. -Broken closet door, the bottom track was bent. By the last day my husband removed the closet door completely so I could get to my things. -Barely any storage: closet was teeny tiny anyways, almost no bigger than a tall locker, only the top drawers of the nightstands open. -Shower: Horrible water pressure. -The cleaning staff did not replace shampoo, soap, etc. Had to call the front desk, and they delivered within 10 mins. -The cleaning staff did not replace our duvet cover during the three nights we were there, realized this as I still noticed a stain we made the first night. I made sure not to leave the 'save the water' card out. They changed our towels, but not the bedding??? -Our room was at the end of the hall across from where the staff enter, and you could heard that door slam shut all hours of the day. -They charge for Wi-Fi! -You can change the settings on the tv...brightness, etc.

Our stay at the Hard Rock Hotel was much more disappointing than expected. The lobby looks impressive, but the room felt tired, with scuffed furniture, thin walls, and a bathroom that clearly needed better cleaning. We could hear music and people talking in the hallway well past midnight, so neither of us slept properly. Check-in took nearly 30 minutes even though the hotel did not seem especially busy, and the staff member we spoke with was polite but not very helpful. Breakfast was overpriced for the limited, lukewarm options, and getting fresh towels required two phone calls. I expected a lively, stylish experience, but the noise, poor maintenance, and slow service made the hotel feel more chaotic than fun. For the price, I would definitely choose somewhere else.

I booked the Sofitel expecting Parisian elegance, but left feeling thoroughly underwhelmed. The hallway carpet looked tired, and our room's decor felt stuck in the early 2000s--stiff beige fabrics, a bulky armoire, and lighting so dim it was hard to read. Worse, the air conditioner rattled all night, and I barely slept; the thin walls let every hallway conversation seep through. Housekeeping was inconsistent: the bathroom floor had a stray hair on arrival, and the glass shower door was smeared with fingerprints. I asked for a quiet floor at check-in, yet we faced a busy street where sirens blared until 3 a.m. The bed itself was comfortable enough, but that's the only positive. For this price point, I expect freshness, soundproofing, and meticulous cleaning--none of which were delivered. I won't be returning.

I expected a much smoother stay at the Fairmont, especially given the price and reputation, but several things felt surprisingly tired. Check-in took nearly 30 minutes, and the agent seemed more interested in explaining fees than welcoming us. Our room was comfortable in size, yet the carpet had visible stains and the bathroom fan made a loud rattling sound all night. Housekeeping also skipped our room despite the 'please service' sign being out, so we had to call twice for towels and coffee. The lobby is impressive, but the restaurant was expensive and my dinner arrived lukewarm. Staff were polite when contacted, though nobody seemed particularly attentive. It wasn't a disaster, but the overall experience felt ordinary and poorly managed for a hotel charging luxury rates.
The decor felt dated, and hallway noise kept waking us; despite the stay feeling far too short, indifferent staff made the experience disappointing and not worth repeating.

We booked a corner king for our anniversary and were honestly blown away by the view--the Empire State Building was perfectly framed, glowing across the city at night. Morning coffee on the windowsill was a highlight. Breakfast downstairs was a solid, generous spread with good coffee and made-to-order omelets, though nothing wildly gourmet. Our room was exceptionally quiet at night, a real feat given the location, though you could hear faint traffic if you listened. Being a five-minute walk from Bryant Park, the subway, and a handful of excellent bakeries made it ideal for a weekend. Staff were warm and attentive at check-in. We'd absolutely recommend it for a city stay, and it's priced fairly for what you get. Just don't skip the rooftop bar at sunset.

I expected much more from Hotel Monaco given the price and the photos online. The lobby looks stylish, but the room felt tired: scuffed furniture, a stained chair, and a bathroom fan that rattled loudly all night. Our air conditioning barely worked, so the room stayed stuffy despite several calls to the front desk. Staff were polite but never really resolved anything, just said someone would 'look into it.' Breakfast was disappointing too, with lukewarm coffee and several empty trays that were not refilled. The location was convenient, but that was about the only positive. For what we paid, I expected a clean, comfortable stay and basic service, not constant little frustrations.

I expected more from a Hilton, but this stay was disappointing from the start. The location is undeniably convenient, just a short walk from the station and several restaurants, yet that was the main advantage. Check-in took far too long, and the staff seemed distracted rather than apologetic when I asked about my room. Breakfast was crowded and underwhelming: lukewarm eggs, stale pastries, and empty coffee containers that were not refilled promptly. My one-night stay somehow felt longer because the room was noisy and the air conditioning rattled all night. When I mentioned it at checkout, the response was polite but indifferent. I would choose a different hotel next time.

Expected much more from the Omni. Our room smelled stale, the air conditioning barely worked, and front desk staff seemed annoyed every time we asked for anything. For the price, honestly a real letdown.

I wanted to like Hotel Monaco, especially given the central location and attractive lobby, but the stay was more frustrating than relaxing. Check-in took nearly half an hour even though I had already provided my details online, and the desk seemed disorganized when I asked about parking. My room looked tired, with scuffed furniture, a stained armchair, and a bathroom fan that rattled loudly whenever the light was on. Housekeeping also skipped my room one day, and calling down for fresh towels took two requests. The bed was comfortable enough, but hallway noise continued well past midnight, so sleep was difficult. Staff were generally polite, yet nobody seemed particularly concerned about the problems. For the price, I expected a much better-maintained property and more dependable service.

The beds were rock hard and the walls paper-thin; I heard every elevator ding and hallway conversation. Service felt indifferent and our room wasn't ready until past check-in. Disappointing for the price.

We stayed at the James hotel for a 40th birthday. The location was excellent for shopping and restaurants, but also very loud. The room was horrible. VERY SMALL. We had a double/double and it was the size of a college dorm room, plus completely white walls and linens. Absolutely no color except for one accent pillow. It was very sterile and uninviting. We were on the 11th floor and the lobby for the elevator was dark and done in red and balck with minimal lighting. It looked like the entrance to hell, if not a haunted house. Staff was very nice and accomodating. I would not return to this hotel.
Disappointing stay: hallway noise kept me awake, Wi‐Fi dropped constantly, and the room was only superficially clean, with dust on the desk and grime in the bathroom.

I left the Talbott feeling more frustrated than rested. The room looked pleasant at first, but the street noise and a humming air unit made sleep difficult; I woke several times and never felt properly refreshed. At check-in, the front desk was distracted and offered little acknowledgment beyond handing over keys. When I asked about the noise the next morning, the response was polite but noticeably uninterested, with no real solution. For the rate, I expected a quieter room and more attentive service, especially given the hotel's upscale reputation. I only stayed one night, yet it somehow felt longer because I was tired and waiting around for basic assistance. The location is convenient, but that alone did not make the price feel justified.

We booked this hotel for an adult weekend away on Priceline, paid $85 which thought was good price for a 4* in downtown Chicago. The location is great. The hotel minimally OK> Unsure how it gets a 4* rating. It is old and though clean the decor is definitely jaded and needing a face lift. Staff were pleasant and overall it was a good stay. However I would NOT recommend this hotel. I would rather have paid $100 and got something more updated - trouble with old it tends to look somewhat seedy and this was true in this case. My suggestion DO NOT BOOK PRICELINE FOR CHICAGO IL AND ASK FOR 4 * BECAUSE THIS IS WHAT YOU ARE ALMOST SURE TO GET.....NOT GOOD ENOUGH PRICELINE.!! IN MY OPINION.

I had high hopes for the Palmer given its history and location, but my stay last weekend was a letdown from start to finish. Check-in took nearly 45 minutes because they claimed my reservation had 'disappeared' from the system, even though I had a confirmation email right there on my phone. When I finally got to my room, the air conditioning barely worked and the room felt stuffy and dated -- worn carpet, a bathroom with a sink that drained painfully slowly, and hair in the tub when I arrived. I called the front desk twice about maintenance and no one ever came up. Breakfast in the lobby restaurant was another low point; cold eggs and a 20-minute wait for coffee. The location honestly saved this from being a total disaster, but at these prices I expected far more. Won't be back.

We stayed at The Knickerbocker for a long weekend and were genuinely impressed. The location is hard to beat--close enough to walk to Times Square, Broadway, and the subway, but the room itself was surprisingly quiet once the door was closed. Our king room was comfortable, spotless, and had a great city view, with a very good bed and plenty of space for luggage. Everyone we encountered, from the front desk to the doormen, was warm and efficient without being overly formal. The rooftop bar was a highlight; it is busy, but the views made an evening drink worthwhile. Breakfast downstairs was also better than expected, especially the coffee. It is definitely a lively Midtown hotel, but it felt polished and relaxing after a full day out.
Swissotel was a great base for our weekend--the room was quiet and spotless, breakfast had plenty of choices, and the front desk helped us find a late-night restaurant nearby.

Just got back from three nights at the Knickerbocker. Went up to Chicago for some last minute Christmas shopping. Hotel is in a great location. North end of Michigan Ave. about half a block away. Staff was very nice and professional. Everyone we came in contact with was very helpful. Granted this is a older hotel and some of the rooms are no bigger than closets. We were booked into a standard room and when we arrived we upgraded to a deluxe room. Good size room, with nice furnishings and a comfortable bed. Bathroom was somewhat small. Housekeeping did a great job cleaning the room every day. Did not eat at the restaurant Nix, but saw several people getting orders delivered to the bar. Overheard comments saying the food was very good. Drink service at the Martini Bar can be slow. Martinis run $9 and up. Very good drinks and they don't shy away from the liquor. Valet parking was $35 a day with in/out priviliges. Overall a great stay. Would definately stay at this hotel in the future.

I have been meaning to write a review of the Omni but wasn't sure if people would believe it as most of the reviews are quite high. We stayed here for 5 nights. The room was fine when I walked in. But about five minutes or so I was all congested. Thought it might have been from the flight. I then noticed there was dust everywhere. The TV, the Minibar, and worst of all the air vent. It was literally hanging off the vent. I called down to front desk they said they would send housekeeping up. After 30 minutes of waiting and noticing other things. A bathroom door that wouldn't close, broken light fixtures, a toe or fingernail on the bed. broken bathroom fixtures. This place was a dump. Hopefully the pictures will show some of it. I could go on and on. Almost 90 minutes later the hotel manager came up to look at the room, Both he and head of housekeeping were 'shocked' at the room. We were moved to another room, not as large as this one was because the hotel was completely booked, or so I was told. I stayed at the Omni once prior and have to say was very impressed. But this will be the last time. Sad to say. The hotel did cut the rate of our 5 day stay, but doesn't explain how a hotel of this caliber let a room like this pass any inspection.

This is a great hotel, in a great location, in a great city !!! There's a cool bar area to the left of the main door when you can hang out and all of the staff are quite funky and look the part. The rooms are spacious and well thought out with a picture of some old rocker(s) in the bathroom ... I had the Beatles and although they're not my cup of tea, I was happy enough with George staring back @ me! The hotel itself is on the corner of Michigan Ave and a short walk will take you to the fabulous shops and restaurants ... try the 'Cheesecake Factory' or have a meal / cocktail on the top floor of the 'John Hancock Centre'. A slighty longer walk (or a short cab ride) and you're at the 'Navy Pier' - take a ride on the 'Seadog' then enjoy all the fun of the fair ... or maybe a drink or two whilst listening to some great live music. This hotel (& city) is WELL worth checking out.

Stayed for 3 nights for our anniversary. The desk clerk was great and since it was our anniversary, he gave us an upgrade...imagine our surprise when we got off on a floor with only 3 other rooms! Corner tower suite with a view of the river and Michigan ave. Beautiful! Cabs available right outside the lobby... Never paid more than $7 for a cab ride. If you go in Dec. you must go to the ChrisKindl Festival for strudel!

A disappointment to say the least. I have heard rave after rave about Hotel Allegro and was super excited when our brother-in-law gave us an American Express gift card that we decided to use for a night out! I called Hotel Allegro and made the reservation for a Saturday night. The person who took the reservation was very sweet and assured me that there would be no problem using the gift card, since they do indeed take American Express. I couldn't wait to get there! We arrive at Hotel Allegro at about 3:00 on Saturday afternoon. Me, the tourist, I am already taking pics of the sign out front and trying to get a sneek peak of the ballroom set up for a wedding. We get in the line to check in. I give them the gift card and my check card. They tell me that neither one will work because they are charging the cards for not only the room rate, but for incidentals as well. We give them a credit card instead. While in line checking in, we hear complaint after complaint from other guests and I start to wonder what our experience is going to be like. The guy at the front desk is on the radio with the bell-man. Someone's luggage has been lost. He desk clerk snaps at the bell-man for the entire line to see. Not impressed. We get to our little shoebox of a room that I was so disappointed to see. The rooms on the website looked glorious! My bedroom at home is nicer than this tiny room. The sink is too small - water splashes everywhere even as evident by the water all over the floor when we got into our room. Yuck. We stay the night and go to check out in the morning. Again, I give them the American Express gift card. The clerk says 'their system usually doesn't take them'. I tell him that I called to confirm that their system would take it on Friday. He swipes the card and bam! it works! What do you know?? He was so rude. I will not stay at Hotel Allegro again, nor would I recommend it to anyone. Such a disappointment!

Really enjoyed my stay--the hotel ambassador was warm, attentive, and genuinely helpful with local recommendations. Check-in was smooth, the room was comfortable, and everything felt welcoming without being overdone.
Fairmont made our weekend easy: quick check-in, a quiet room with a great bed, and staff who actually remembered our breakfast order. The lobby bar was a nice bonus.

Friendly staff at the Palmer made check-in a breeze, and our room's fresh, updated decor was a pleasant surprise. Loved the sparkling clean bathroom and the gorgeous view of the skyline. Would happily return!

Our stay at Hotel Monaco was far more disappointing than expected. The lobby looks stylish, but our room felt tired and poorly maintained, with scuffed furniture, a stained carpet, and a bathroom fan that rattled all night. The bed was comfortable enough, although the pillows were unusually flat. Housekeeping also missed replacing the coffee supplies and left a damp towel hanging behind the door. When we mentioned the issues at reception, the response was polite but offered no real solution beyond saying they were 'aware' of the maintenance problems. The location is convenient, and the building has plenty of character, but the price does not match the condition or service. We left feeling that the hotel relies too heavily on its reputation and attractive public spaces.

We booked our room at the Swissotel on Hotwire for $88 (unbelievable rate!) and were extremely impressed with the Swissotel. The staff was so polite and catered to our every need. The room was oversized, clean, and had a large bathroom. We had a partial view of Lake Michigan, which was an added bonus. On the 42nd floor, they have a spotless workout room and pool with a view of the city and lake from 3 sides. Spectacular! We sat in the hot tub and looked down on Navy Pier. We can't wait to go to the Swissotel again!
The rooms feel freshly updated and the harbor view from our floor was stunning. Location is unbeatable, steps from everything, and honestly three nights felt far too short--we'll be back.

I booked this hotel for a business trip since I was able to get a $129 rate on Travelzoo and figured I'd save my company some money. I had also read excellent reviews on TripAdvisor. I had a guaranteed and confirmed room reservation for two nights in November. When I arrived in Chicago at 7:30pm I decided to go to dinner prior to checking in so called the hotel to request a late check in and was told 'no problem.' When I arrived at the hotel at 11:45pm I was told they didn't have a room for me and that I'd have to move to the Four Points Sheraton which they paid for. It was a major inconvenience to have to move and completely unacceptable that my confirmed room was given away. I was told that they overbooked and didn't get as many cancellations as they expected. I did check into the hotel the next day and once there did have a good experience. I would recommend staying here but do ensure that your reservation is indeed confirmed and avoid any late check-ins or you might not have a room! The 'experience designers' were great and very helpful. The rooms were very nice and comfortable (felt like home). The breakfast could stand to add on some bagels for the 'healthy factor.' It was nice that they did have fruit. I think that once the kinks are worked out that this will be a great hotel--they just need to get the basics down!

The Fairmont felt tired--worn carpets and dated drapes made the halls feel stuck in another decade. Breakfast was bland and overpriced, while staff seemed disinterested whenever we asked for help. Location was convenient, but that couldn't salvage a disappointing stay.
Loved the Omni's roomy suite and easy walk to shops and restaurants. Everyone at the front desk was cheerful, and the bed was so comfortable after a long day downtown.
For the price, the InterContinental felt tired: my room smelled musty, the shower barely drained, and front desk took ages to answer a simple request.
Hotel Amalfi felt tired, with dated decor and a cramped bathroom with weak water pressure. Staff were curt when we asked for help, and even our brief stay felt longer than it should have.
