Conrad was a great base for our weekend--quiet room, comfortable bed, and staff who remembered our dinner reservation question later that evening. The lobby bar was lively without being overwhelming.

Swissotel Chicago turned out to be a genuinely pleasant surprise. The location is unbeatable--steps from the riverwalk and a short stroll to Navy Pier, which made evening exploring effortless. I was half-expecting tired, corporate decor, but the lobby feels crisp and contemporary, with warm wood accents that haven't aged badly at all. The front desk team was exceptionally warm, even helping me rebook a dinner reservation when my plans shifted at the last minute. My room had a lovely lake view, and the bed was so comfortable I nearly missed my morning meeting. If anything, my two nights felt far too brief--I could have easily settled in for a lazy weekend. The only minor quibble is the elevator wait during peak check-in, but that hardly dampened an otherwise flawless stay. I'd absolutely return.

We booked our hotel stay thru Yahoo and requested a room for 4 with 2 beds. When we got to the hotel, not only did they not have a room for us (we pre-paid!), but they said they could not guarantee what we had requested online, they could only give us what was available. The hotel staff was rude and condescending and only after I got upset did they finally tell me they did have a room for us. If you book online - beware! You may not get what you paid for. They did not stand by their promise they advertise in each room.

The Sheraton is a fantastic hotel. My wife and I stayed on the 29th floor overlooking the Chicago River and Lake Michigan. The view was great. We got a corner room that also had a couch in. The hotel was just a short walk to the Navy Pier and the Magnificant Mile Shopping area. Food at the hotel was great. Service from checking in to maid service was first class. Great Hotel, Great Town, Highly recommend it.

My wife and I had to stay downtown for event that we were attending at the Drake Hotel. I have stayed at the Drake before and while it is nice, it is bit stuffy and a little outdated for the price. We opted to walk across the street and stay at the Millenium instead. I know this property has under gone many renovations in past year and I have to say they have done a great job. This place used to be the hotel you would crash in when you came to Chicago on a college roadtrip (I did). But that is not the case any more. This property is directly across from the Drake Hotel and for 1/2 the price you get their great location with a newer (albeit smaller) room and every ammenity you would expect from a 4* hotel. The rooms are tastefully decorated (Asian influence w/flat screen tv) and the bed is very comfortable. The bath is small (no tub), but very clean and the shower is great. You are not going to be spending a bunch of time in your room when visting Chicago, so the room's size is not a big deal. (It works well with a couple, but a family of four may be a bit cramped.) The service was attentive and friendly and the location can't be beat. I would definitely stay here again, but the next time I would leave the car at home ($49/night parking is a bit steep).

We stayed at the Palmer House Hilton in early December, we stay there that weekend every December and we think it is the best location in the city for us. We like State Street better than Michigan Avenue and the Palmer House is right there. We stayed in the Towers, in a room with two double beds and 2 baths. The room was not huge, but very comfortable. The towers area was recently refurbished and it shows, the lobby is beautiful with plasma screen TVs on the walls, comfortable chairs and tables and a seperate room for the food/drinks. There is a continental breakfast in the morning, appetizers during cocktail hour and cookies are laid out until the room closes. There is a fridge stocked with soft drinks, water and juice that are yours for the taking. We were very pleased with the upgraded Towers, everyone should check it out!

Booked a two-night stay expecting the classic Hard Rock energy, but honestly, it fell flat from check-in. The front desk staff were polite but painfully slow, and we waited over 40 minutes just to get our keys. The room itself was tired--scuffed furniture, a frayed carpet, and a bathroom that smelled faintly of mildew no matter how much we ran the fan. Soundproofing is a joke; we heard every hallway conversation and the elevator ding all night. The mini-fridge was warm, and housekeeping never replenished our coffee after the first day. I tried the pool, but it was overcrowded with no available loungers, and the bar service took 25 minutes for a simple drink. Location is convenient, sure, but for the price, I expected far more polish. Won't be returning.

Stayed three nights for a conference and was genuinely impressed. Check-in was seamless, with the front desk staff proactively offering a late checkout when they saw my evening flight, which I appreciated. The lobby and my room felt recently updated--sleek lines, warm woods, no worn carpet or faded drapes. My corner room had a panoramic view of the city skyline, and watching sunset from the floor-to-ceiling window was a real highlight. Room service was prompt, and the bed was exactly the firmness I needed. For the nightly rate, especially given the location and the quality of service, it felt like fair value. Not a luxury palace, but a solid, comfortable stay that exceeded expectations. I'd happily book here again for a work trip.

I was really looking forward to a weekend getaway, but the Knickerbocker left me feeling more tired than when I arrived. The bed was rock hard, and the constant hum from the street traffic meant I was up half the night. Breakfast was a sad affair of lukewarm, rubbery eggs and stale pastries, served by a staff that seemed completely indifferent. The bathroom had a perpetually clogged drain that left the floor wet, and the water pressure in the shower was pathetically weak. We paid extra for a city view, but our window looked directly over a noisy construction site and a grim airshaft, offering just a sliver of the skyline. Overall, it was a disappointing stay that felt far overpriced for the quality. I wouldn't recommend it.

We booked Hotel Allegro for a long weekend and honestly I can't figure out how it has the rating it does. First off, we arrived at 3pm, close to check-in, but the room wasn't ready until nearly 5. No apology, just 'come back later.' When we finally got in, the air conditioning was barely working and the room overlooked the alley, so we got delivery trucks beeping at 5am both mornings. The elevator situation is a disaster too -- two elevators for the whole building means long waits every single time. Breakfast at the restaurant downstairs cost way more than it should for cold eggs and slow service. Ask the front desk a simple question and you get a shrug._LOCATION_ I wanted to like this place, the lobby is pretty, but pretty doesn't make up for everything else. We won't be back.

We stayed at the Sheraton for three nights and were genuinely impressed. Our room on the twelfth floor had a gorgeous view of the harbor, and watching the sunset from the window each evening became the highlight of our day. The room itself was spotless--housekeeping even left fresh towels twice a day without being asked. The bed was wonderfully comfortable with plush pillows, and the blackout curtains meant I slept straight through the night, which almost never happens for me when traveling. Every staff member we encountered, from the front desk to the breakfast team, was warm and attentive; when I mentioned I preferred extra coffee packets, they appeared the next morning without a reminder. Location was convenient too, just a short walk from the metro. Would absolutely return next time we're in the city.

Just got back from a 10 day visit to Chicago. For the rate of $219 per night, it was extremely good value. Reception staff were efficient, courteous and very friendly. I was given a room on the top floor (32nd floor) facing the lake and the John Hancock Tower. The rooms were large and very comfortable. Housekeeping/Turn Down Service were efficient and thorough. Bathroom amenities were very good and replaced daily. This is definitely my first choice for a Hotel in Chicago. It is also very close to all the shops, restaurants and the subway.

Stayed at this hotel with 3 friends or 4 nights. The hotel was clean and tidy, throughout. The Concierge Christopher was excellent and helped as with all our needs, gave us discount vouchers etc. Hotel was in excellent position. 3 blocks from John Hancok Building and more importantly The Cheesecake Factory , Bloomingdales 3 blocks away and the Water Tower Shopping Centre 2 blocks away. We went to the huge I Max cinema which is about ten minutes away. Cant wait to go back to Chicago and The Affinia
Hotel Amalfi was pleasantly quiet at night, and I slept soundly. The Wi-Fi stayed reliable throughout my visit, while my room offered a lovely view of the city.

I wanted to like Hotel Allegro because the lobby has character and the location was convenient for the theater district, but the stay was frustrating from the start. Our room wasn't ready at the stated check-in time, and nobody followed up when they said they would. Once we got in, the room felt cramped and worn, with scuffed furniture, a noisy air conditioner, and a bathroom door that would not stay shut. The hallway noise carried straight through the walls, so sleep was difficult both nights. We also had to ask twice for fresh towels after housekeeping skipped our room. Staff at the desk were polite but seemed overwhelmed and offered little more than apologies. For the rate, I expected a cleaner, calmer, better-maintained experience.

My husband and I had a wonderful stay at the Omni Chicago Hotel. I had contacted the customer service representative prior to our stay to request a quiet suite. When we arrived, she greeted us and confirmed that we were getting exactly what I had requested--and more. Our suite had a partial view of the lake!!! And, we were able to check in early. The service at this hotel is incredible. Everyone made us feel welcome and took care to respond to any question or request that we had. The suite was very quiet even though we were on the east side of the hotel, very near to Michigan Avenue. Housekeeping was prompt and thorough. We really couldn't have asked for a better hotel. We will definitely stay there on future trips to Chicago and will recommend this hotel to anyone who travels there.
Lovely harbor view from our room, and the fresh, modern decor made it feel welcoming. Breakfast had plenty of hot and cold choices, and the stay was well worth the price.

My boyfriend and I decided to stay at the Conrad Chicago for our anniversary. The second we walked in, we were immediately won over by the look and feel of the room. White luxurous bedding on the King bed, plasma t.v./ subroofer/ surround sound speakers (my boyfriend was more impressed than me, as I reminded him that we didn't come to Chicago for the hotel room) very large bathroom w/ tub and separate stand-in shower, granite countertops, his/ her robes and slippers. The view wasn't great, but we were on the 6th floor and not really high enough to see anything but the side of the building next to us. Not a large room by any means, but again . . . we didn't go to the city for the hotel room. It was the prefect size for the amount of time we were actually in the room. We got a great rate on it ($140 at hotels.com) but I think the going rate is usually closer to mid $200's. I've stayed in quite a few hotels in the downtown area and none have ever impressed me more than this one. We will definitely be staying there again on our next trip into the city.

The Hotel Monaco looked great online, but the reality was a letdown. The room was stuffy and the hallways noisy all night, and the front desk seemed annoyed by every question I asked. Not worth the hype or the price.

Great stay at Hotel Knickerbocker! The rooftop bar with those city views was a real highlight, and the room was surprisingly quiet for being so central. Staff were friendly and quick with recommendations. Would happily book again.

I booked the Hyatt expecting more, honestly. The lobby looked impressive in photos but felt dated and slightly grimy in person, with scuffed floors and a weird smell near the elevators. Check-in took over twenty minutes because only one person staffed the desk, and they seemed frazzled, barely making eye contact. My room on the seventh floor had a cracked bathroom tile, a sticky patch on the carpet near the mini-fridge, and the air conditioner rattled all night unless I turned it off completely. The window faced a brick wall, so the 'city view' I paid extra for was a joke. Breakfast was overpriced and underwhelming--cold scrambled eggs and stale pastries. Housekeeping skipped my room one day entirely, and when I called, they said I'd missed their window. The location is decent for walking, but that's about all this place has going for it. For the price, I'd pick a solid mid-range chain next time. Disappointing.

I stayed at the Swissotel for a business trip the first week of Aug 2007. I arrived late the first night and got shoved into a hospitality room the first night. However, this was more than made up when after a strong talk they assigned me a corner room on the 28th floor. EXCELLENT view of the city, river and Lake Michigan. In fact, I would say the corner room of the Swissotel has a better view than any other hotel in the vicinity. The room was huge, and everything was clean and the bathroom was nice. The hotel is very convieniently located to the Magnificient Mile and Millenium Park. Would very much recommend this hotel, and would suggest trying every method possible to get a corner room in a higher floor.
The view was mostly rooftops and a sliver of river, my mattress sagged enough to ruin two nights of sleep, and there was a sticky patch on the bathroom floor. For this price, it was a letdown.
Really enjoyed my stay at the InterContinental--my room was quiet, the bed was excellent, and everyone at reception was genuinely helpful. The central location made getting around effortless, too.
The city view was mostly blocked by rooftops, and thin walls made sleep difficult. The room looked clean at first, but the high rate felt unjustified.

A very nice hotel with small but adequate rooms. The decor was lovely. My daughter and I spent 5-nights here, saw Wicked just down the street and used the public transportation to get all around town. Was a bit disappointed with the bar/restaurant which opened and closed it's kitchen at will without regard to posted hours. The room description boasted of safe's large enough to accomodate a laptop, so I brought mine. I was informed after check-in that the safes are not in every room (and not in mine). As a side note, I was surprised that nearly all the shops many restaurants closed at 6pm in that area... even the 7-11.

We really wanted to love this place, but it just missed the mark in so many ways. The location is fantastic, but that's about the only positive. Check-in took forever because there was only one person at the desk, and she seemed completely overwhelmed. Our room on the third floor was noisy--we could hear every conversation in the hallway and the plumbing was ridiculous. Also, the air conditioning barely worked, so we slept terribly. The breakfast buffet was a disaster: lukewarm scrambled eggs, empty bread baskets, and coffee that tasted burnt. I asked the front desk for a wake-up call and it never came, which almost made us miss our ferry. The curtains wouldn't fully close either, so we were up with the sunrise. Honestly, for the price we paid, I expected far better. We've had much nicer stays at cheaper hotels. I wouldn't bother revisiting.
Disappointing stay at the Hard Rock. Rooms felt dated and the AC barely worked, plus check-in took forever. For the price, I expected way better music-themed fun than a noisy, tired hotel.

I had a very pleasant stay at Hotel Allegro and would happily return. The location was especially convenient, with restaurants, shops, and public transport all within an easy walk, yet my room was surprisingly quiet at night. It was not huge, but it was bright, clean, and thoughtfully arranged, with a comfortable bed, good shower pressure, and plenty of outlets. The staff were friendly without being overbearing, and check-in took only a few minutes. I also appreciated the small touches, such as the fresh water in the room and the well-maintained common areas. Breakfast offered a decent variety of fresh pastries, fruit, eggs, and coffee. Wi-Fi worked reliably throughout my stay. Overall, it felt welcoming, efficient, and good value for the price.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly, the location can't be beat--right in the thick of the Loop, steps from the river walk and a million transit options. The lobby is a stunner, all old-school grandeur with a modern twist, and check-in was painless. Our room was on the quieter side, which was a relief, and the bed was seriously comfortable. The blackout curtains did their job, and the bathroom was spotless, though the shower pressure was just okay. We grabbed drinks at the rooftop bar one night; the views of the city skyline were worth the slightly steep prices. Staff were friendly and quick with recommendations for dinner spots. Only minor gripe: the hallway was a bit noisy early morning, but it didn't ruin anything. Would absolutely book again for the convenience and comfort.
Woke up to a stunning skyline view and slept like a log on the comfy bed. Breakfast had fresh pastries and great coffee, and for the price, this place genuinely felt like a steal. I'd book again.

My stay at the Conrad was a very comfortable one from start to finish. The front desk team was welcoming without being overbearing, and check-in was quick even though I arrived a little early. My room was modern, spotless, and thoughtfully laid out, with a particularly comfortable bed and plenty of space to work. Breakfast had a good mix of options, including fresh fruit, pastries, eggs made to order, and strong coffee; service in the restaurant was attentive and efficient. Despite being in a busy area, the hotel was surprisingly quiet at night, and I slept well without hearing hallway or street noise. The Wi-Fi connected immediately and remained reliable for video calls and streaming. Overall, the Conrad felt polished, calm, and worth the price.
Hotel Palmer's dated decor and dusty room made the stay feel longer than it was. Street noise carried well past midnight, so getting any decent sleep was difficult.
Unfortunately, I barely slept through the noisy night, and although the one-night stay felt too short, the gloomy alley view and unreliable Wi-Fi made leaving feel like a relief.

I had a very pleasant stay at the Sheraton and would happily return. Check-in was quick and friendly, even though I arrived a little earlier than expected. My room was spacious, quiet, and clean, with a comfortable bed and plenty of outlets for charging devices. I especially appreciated the large desk since I had some work to finish in the evenings. The lobby felt modern without being overly formal, and the staff were consistently helpful whenever I needed directions or extra towels. Breakfast had a good variety, including fresh fruit, eggs, and decent coffee. The fitness center was also better equipped than I expected. The only minor issue was that the Wi-Fi slowed down at busy times, but overall the hotel offered a comfortable, reliable experience and good value.

The Fairmont was an excellent base for our weekend in the city. Its location made everything easy: we walked to restaurants, shops, and the waterfront, and taxis were always available right outside when we went farther afield. The lobby and room decor felt classic rather than dated, with polished wood, comfortable seating, and a few modern touches that kept it from feeling stuffy. From our upper-floor room, we had a beautiful view of the skyline at sunset, which was a real highlight. Wi-Fi worked reliably throughout our stay, including during a video call and while streaming in the evening. Staff were warm and efficient, and the room was quiet, clean, and very comfortable.

The room was far more stylish than I expected, with a sleek, modern palette that felt fresh rather than the tired beige I've seen in so many other chains. The staff genuinely impressed me--from the cheerful valet who remembered my name to the front desk agent who proactively recommended a quieter floor when she heard I had early meetings. Wi-Fi was rock solid throughout, even during peak evening hours in the lobby bar, which is where I camped out with my laptop. My only real complaint? The stay felt criminally short. I booked two nights for a conference and wished I'd tacked on a third to explore the rooftop pool and that incredible breakfast spread. The bed was so plush I almost missed my alarm, and the blackout curtains worked like a charm. If you're weighing between here and the generic spot across the street, do yourself a favor--choose this one. I left feeling genuinely rested, not just tolerated.

My expectations were not high because I booked this hotel through priceline for $58 / night. An amazing deal if not for the fact that you had to wait 15 - 20 minutes for hot water. I called the front desk to tell them that there was no hot water - to which they nonchalantly replied: 'try running it for 15 to 20 minutes.' They forgot to tell me to keep the water running after my shower, if anyone else expected to use the shower. My boyfriend, who showered after me, had to wait another 10 minutes to get the shower warm again. To make matters worse, after room service was delivered, we called and said we needed another fork. They told us it would cost $3 ($1 for the fork, $2 for delivey charge). Absolutely ridiculous!! At least with a 1 star hotel, you get hot water. This is supposed to be a 4 star hotel. I guess you do get what you paid for - I just feel bad for the people who actually paid full price.

I had a very pleasant stay at the Hilton and would happily return. My room was bright, clean, and comfortable, with a lovely view over the city skyline and the river in the distance. The bed was excellent, and despite being in a central area, the room was surprisingly quiet at night; I only heard occasional hallway noise. Breakfast offered a generous selection, including fresh fruit, pastries, eggs made to order, and good coffee, with plenty of seating even during the busy morning period. The location was especially convenient, within an easy walk of restaurants, shops, and public transportation, which made getting around simple. Staff were friendly and professional throughout, quickly helping with check-in and providing useful local recommendations. Overall, it was a comfortable and well-managed stay.

I really wanted to love this place after reading the reviews, but our four nights felt like two weeks. The room itself was decent-sized, yet whoever cleaned it clearly rushed--crumbs under the desk, a sticky ring on the nightstand, and hair trailing one of the pillows. The bathroom was the real letdown: the shower head sputtered between scalding and lukewarm, the drain gurgled all night, and the grout had visible mildew along the tub edges. Staff interactions were cool at best. Front desk barely looked up during check-in, and when we asked for extra towels we waited nearly two hours. The concierge did help with a dinner reservation, I'll give him that. For what this costs, I expected thoroughness and warmth, and got neither. Won't be back.
Disappointing stay at Hotel James: breakfast was bland and overpriced, hallway noise carried late, and the tired decor needs updating. My room overlooked a brick wall instead of anything scenic.

My wife and I travelled to Chicago and really were treated like royalty by the hotel staff! (My brother and his wife also stayed during this period.) The front desk staff, the concierge, the Star Bucks server, the restaurant, the lounge servers . . . all were wonderful! The rooms were spacious and the flat screen tv was really great! The bath room was a real plus ... it was huge and had everything one desires. Great view from 20th floor to Michigan Avenue below! Overall, great stay and highly recommended!

We had a very comfortable weekend at The Knickerbocker. Our room was spotless when we arrived, including the bathroom and the often-overlooked corners around the desk and windows. We were high enough to have a terrific view of Times Square and the surrounding towers, especially after dark, yet the room itself was surprisingly quiet. With the curtains closed, we barely noticed the crowds and traffic below and slept well both nights. Everyone we encountered was pleasant and capable, from the quick check-in team to the concierge who helped us choose a nearby dinner reservation. The location is undeniably busy, but the hotel feels like a calm retreat once you step inside. I would gladly stay here again for a New York visit.

My husband and I were in the Fairmont Chicago recently for a conference. We stayed in a spacious suite. All amenities appeared recently updated and in excellent shape. The bed was very comfortable. Views were great. I love their products in the bathroom and used them in the pristine tub two out of three nights. The room was so quiet, it was very relaxing. We ate in the restaurant downstairs (Aria) and although pricey, it was excellent. The staff were consistently attentive and responsive. It is evident that everyone is very well-trained. I would love to stay here again.
My Hyatt stay was disappointing: the room looked worn, housekeeping missed basic details, and the front desk took ages to respond when the air conditioning stopped working.

We booked our room on Priceline, and got a good deal at around $100 per night. We stayed for the first 2 nights of our US trip so didnt use too many of the hotel's facilities The hotel is centrally located, just over the Chicago River from the shops at North Michigan Avenue, and around a mile from Navy Pier Our room was clean and comfortable, and on the 29th floor we had a good view of the city, and could just about see Lake Michigan (though the weather was very bad). The layout of the room is a little peculiar, with the bed facing away from the window, but over all we have no complaints about this hotel, and unlike some other reviews we were not disturbed at all by noise from other guests So, pros and cons: Pros: Helpful and friendly staff Clean and comfortable throughout Spacious rooms Large and airy public areas Starbucks and gift shop in lobby Cons A large hotel, so a long walk from the elevators to the front desk / lobby area

The Hard Rock delivered the perfect quick escape--wifi was lightning fast for streaming, and the room stayed blissfully quiet despite the lively lobby. It felt like a fleeting weekend, but at that rate, every minute was worth it.

My only regret is that our stay at the Conrad was far too brief--the room was immaculately clean, the staff anticipated every need with genuine warmth, and the wifi was lightning-fast. Pure perfection from check-in to checkout.

Maybe it was because we booked thru priceline that we were treated like second rate guest - couldn't get a room thru Fairmont website as busy weekend with Ryder Cup.....but never have had this experience in using priceline before. The night time check in girl was rude and unhelpful. We were told no options to pay for upgrade or king bed and that we were stuck with two tiny beds and a ugly room. We had comforter with dirt in several places - and a bathroom for handicap with no counter space - had to use ironing board for toiletries. This hotel is huge and not at capacity - may have had a renovation but the good look of this hotel stops at the lobby. Hallways, rooms, carpet run down - just not what you come to expect of a fairmont. I have stayed in many all over the world and this is by far the worst. Maybe because we were on a low floor it was not updated...we paid as much as other guest and I'm a Fairmont Gold member. Positives - great location, daytime staff helpful at desk - they have two bikes to borrow which is handy. Views could be great if you get a higher room. Checked out the Raddison Blu across street - looked much nicer!!!

The hotel is almost always very helpful. This stay caused me to re-think if I like the Palmer House. I had dirty covers for the bed. It was also the smallest room in the hotel I am sure. My husband and I usually come 8 times each year. He is there doing Business and CTA work. We are not pleased with the size of the room at all now. Rooms have always had two chairs, desk, and usually 22 by 25 feet. Not this room on the 11th floor. It was only 15 X 17 approx. The service men at the doors have always said a welcome but not this time. In the past we had a bell man steal a $300. pair of sun glasses and the hotel did nothing about our loss financially.

My stay at the Hilton was disappointing overall, especially considering the price. The room was clean enough, but it felt dated, with thin walls and a mattress that was far too firm. Breakfast was another letdown: the buffet was crowded, hot items were lukewarm, and the coffee tasted stale. I only stayed two nights, which was probably long enough, although the poor sleep made even that feel excessive. Staff interactions were polite but distant; when I reported a noisy air conditioner, the response was simply to turn it off rather than offer a real solution. The location was convenient for public transport and nearby restaurants, but that was the main advantage. I expected the usual Hilton standard and left feeling that the experience was overpriced and underwhelming.

The Sheraton's modern, airy lobby felt freshly renovated, and my room's floor-to-ceiling window offered a stunning skyline view. The reliable WiFi made work a breeze, and for the prime location and comfort, it was definitely worth every penny.

We stayed at Hotel Allegro for three nights in October and honestly it exceeded our expectations. Location is great, just a short walk from the main square but on a quiet side street, so no noise at night. Our room was spacious, spotlessly clean, and the bed was genuinely comfortable, which is rare in my experience. Breakfast was the highlight really: fresh pastries, good coffee, eggs made to order, and the staff kept everything stocked even when it got busy. Speaking of staff, everyone we interacted with was warm and helpful, and reception arranged us a taxi on the last day without any fuss. Minor quibble: the elevator is small and a bit slow, but nothing that would put me off returning. Good value overall. Highly recommended.

I enjoyed my stay at the Affinia and would happily return. The location made it easy to walk to restaurants, shops, and nearby attractions, while the front desk staff were friendly and quick to help with directions. My room was comfortable and surprisingly spacious, with a useful sitting area and a bed that was genuinely easy to sleep in. The stay felt a little too short, since I only had two nights and barely had time to settle in. Despite being in a busy part of the city, the room was mostly quiet at night; I heard some hallway noise one evening, but nothing disruptive. WiFi worked reliably for email, streaming, and a video call. Housekeeping kept everything tidy, and the overall atmosphere felt relaxed and welcoming.

Visiting during a busy 2day conference in Chicago. Most hotels booked solid. The full hotel allows you to meet a wide array of customers. Everyone is complaining about service, cleanliness, and overall experience. Location is good. Hotel is tired. Employees surly. Too many cool properties to choose from in this town, will never stay here again and will re-think Hilton in general

Attended a conference at the Palmer House and it truly surpassed my expectations. I had no idea it would be so large, so nice and with so many amenities. I also didn't realize that it is just around the corner from Milenium Park and the Art Institute. We were met at the door by the friendliest staff. Even with a long line at check-in, the entire process was about 10 minutes. We enjoyed the room with the up-to-date TV, decent size bathroom and comfortable bed. Had a fantastic breakfast buffet as well as a delicious take-out lunch at the main restaurant. Paid $200/night through the conference which seemed quite fair considering downtown Chicago. We have stayed at the Sofital which is much more upscale, but we also paid over $300/night there.

My stay at Hotel Allegro was more disappointing than expected. The lobby has a dramatic look, but the rooms feel stuck in another decade, with worn carpeting, scuffed furniture, and heavy curtains that made the space seem gloomy. My mattress was too firm, and noise from the hallway continued well past midnight, so I slept poorly both nights. Breakfast was another letdown: the buffet was small, lukewarm, and slow to be replenished, with limited fresh options for the price. A few staff members were polite, but service at the front desk felt distracted and impersonal when I asked about the noise. The location is convenient, but that alone did not make up for the tired decor, uncomfortable sleep, and lackluster morning service.

We booked our stay through Priceline.com and got a great deal. We were only staying one night and we had our 2 year old with us. At check-in, we were upgraded to a suite with a lake view of Lake Michigan. It was beautiful. The suite had a king bed with a living room and a bar and mini-fridge which we didn't need, but if we were staying longer, it would have been a godsend. This hotel is in close proximity with Grant Park which has the beautiful Buckingham Fountain. We walked around the park and even saw a movie being filmed....but if you are looking for a hotel with a lot of restaurants around it, this isn't the one. We ended up eating at the Irish Pub inside the hotel (Kitty O'Shea's) which has great food. (We have stayed here before and always end up eating here.) There are a lot of attractions within a mile including the Field Museum, Shedd Aquarium, Soldier Field, and Navy Pier. They may not be walking distance but we could see them from our hotel window. Overall, we had another wonderful stay at the Chicago Hilton. (Our 4th stay) The only downside is the expensive parking within the hotel.....41 dollars a night is kind of ridiculous.

I expected more from the Affinia given the rate and its reputation. Check-in took nearly half an hour because only one person was working the desk, and nobody acknowledged the line. The room itself looked worn: scuffed furniture, a stained chair, and a bathroom fan that rattled loudly whenever the light was on. I could also hear hallway conversations and doors slamming well past midnight, so sleep was difficult. The air conditioning barely cooled the room, despite maintenance being called. They never followed up, and I didn't want to spend another evening waiting around. Location was convenient, but that was really the only positive. For the price, the service and upkeep felt disappointing.

We stayed at the Amalfi for a quick two-nighter, and honestly, I could have used one more day just to soak in the atmosphere. The location was a quiet goldmine--steps from the harbor restaurants but tucked away enough that our room felt like a peaceful retreat. I slept like a log both nights; the blackout curtains did serious work, and the bed had that just-right firmness without any of that annoying sag in the middle. The decor leans traditional rather than trend-forward, think warm wood and soft cream tones, but it felt well-maintained and cozy rather than tired. Our only regret was not booking a longer stay to try the pool and breakfast spread. A genuinely comfortable, convenient stop worth repeating.

I really wanted to love the Hotel Ambassador given everything I'd read beforehand, but our three-night stay left me underwhelmed, especially for what we paid. At nearly $300 a night, I expected more than a room where the carpet was worn at the edges and the light fixtures looked like they hadn't been updated since the nineties. The decor is trying hard for classic elegance but mostly reads as tired and dated, not timeless. Our window faced an air shaft and a brick wall rather than any kind of view, which was a real letdown considering I'd specifically requested something nicer. The front desk staff were around, but asking for an extra pillow felt like an inconvenience to them. Honestly, one night here would have been plenty--by night three I was ready to check out early. Disappointing overall.

I had a very comfortable three-night stay at the Hyatt while visiting for a conference. The location made getting around easy, and the front desk was friendly without making check-in feel slow or formal. My room was quiet despite being near the elevators, with a genuinely comfortable mattress, blackout curtains, and enough outlets around the desk. I slept better than expected, which is not always the case in city hotels. The bathroom was spotless and a good size, with strong water pressure and plenty of counter space, although the shower fixtures showed a little wear. The decor felt fresh and understated rather than trendy, with warm lighting and practical furniture. Rates were not cheap, but considering the location, cleanliness, and quality of sleep, I felt the stay was worth the price.

Honestly disappointed with the Sofitel. Paid for a premium room and got a view of the air shaft, air conditioning that rattled all night, and front desk staff who couldn't care less when I complained. Won't be back.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly couldn't have asked for a smoother visit. The suite was spotless and the kitchenette came in handy for late-night snacks, though the pull-out sofa was a touch firmer than I'd prefer. Breakfast had solid options--the make-your-own waffle station was a hit with the kids, and the scrambled eggs were actually fluffy, not rubbery. The indoor pool was warm, and the staff at the front desk remembered our room number every time we walked by, which felt personal. Location is convenient, about ten minutes from the interstate and a quick drive to a few decent restaurants. Only minor hiccup was the ice machine on our floor being out of order, but the guy at the desk offered to fill our cooler from the lobby without hesitation. I'd book here again for the value and the quiet, comfortable sleep.
Loved the city skyline view from our room; the decor felt fresh and stylish, the rate seemed fair, and breakfast had plenty of tasty hot and continental choices.

The Omni exceeded expectations. The bed was ridiculously comfortable, and the staff remembered our names at breakfast. Great downtown location, too. We'll definitely book again for our next city escape.
Hard Rock was a letdown: stains on the carpet, a grimy bathroom with a dripping faucet, and bass from the lobby thudding through the walls until 2am. Two nights honestly felt too long.

I was disappointed by my stay at Swissotel. The room looked modern in the photos, but mine felt worn, with scuffed furniture and a bathroom that needed better cleaning. Breakfast had a decent selection, including eggs, fruit, and pastries, yet much of it was lukewarm and the coffee tasted surprisingly weak. The staff were polite at the front desk, but not especially welcoming, and requests took several reminders before anyone followed up. Sleep was difficult because the walls seemed thin; I could hear conversations, doors slamming, and elevator noise well past midnight. The bed itself was comfortable, but that hardly mattered with the constant disturbance. For the price, I expected a quieter room, more attentive service, and a noticeably better breakfast. I would consider other hotels before returning.

WARNING: FOOD POISONING ALERT!!! The room was dirty, the shower had mold and the handle in the shower my daughter cracked her head open on. The elevators were absolutly terrible they made me dizzy every time i went on it. They hade pasta night and they put out a bowl of noodles and sauce and i couple of rolls well you get what you pay for. What was worse is the sauce must of had bad meat in it because my family got so sick. The one thing that was nice was the location which was right by michigan avenue. The second night we left and went to another hotel which was 80 bucks cheaper and 100 times nicer. DO NOT STAY HERE
Conrad felt overpriced: the decor was dated, the room had dusty surfaces and a stained carpet, and traffic noise plus a lumpy bed made sleep nearly impossible.

I had a very pleasant stay at Hotel Ambassador and felt it offered good value for the price. My room was clean, comfortable, and larger than expected, with a lovely view over the city rooftops, especially at sunset. The bed was supportive, and the room stayed quiet despite the central location. Every staff member I encountered was friendly and professional; they gave useful local recommendations and handled check-in quickly without making us feel rushed. The Wi-Fi worked reliably throughout the stay, including during a couple of video calls, which was important for me. Breakfast was fresh and varied, though the dining area became busy around 9 a.m. Overall, the hotel is not luxurious, but it is well maintained, welcoming, and a worthwhile choice for a convenient visit.

The front desk staff seemed irked by every request, and the lobby's worn carpets screamed 1980s. Breakfast featured soggy pastries and lukewarm coffee, while our bathroom had a cracked tile and a showerhead that sprayed sideways. Disappointing.

I have stayed at the Amalfi Hotel before and it has always been excellent. This time was no different. Usually I book direct with the hotel, however, I found a slightly better deal booking through Expedia, which saved about $100. The staff were great. I arrived early and they had a room waiting. I was placed on the 6th (top) floor and it was quiet and comfortable. Overall, it was as good as it gets! I will definitely continue to stay here when I'm in Chicago. Remember, the hotel is close to everything - downtown, the Magnificent Mile, lots of restaurants, etc. Everything is within walking distance!

The bathroom had a persistent odd smell and the shower pressure was pathetic. I slept terribly on a lumpy mattress, and the staff seemed indifferent at checkout. Honestly, it felt like a waste of money for what we got.

Stayed for a weekend getaway and was genuinely impressed. The room was spotless with a super comfy bed, and the location made exploring the city effortless. Staff were friendly and quick with recommendations. Wouldn't hesitate to book Swissotel again.
Our room was spotless, with a lovely view over the city rooftops. The bathroom felt modern and well stocked, and the Wi‐Fi worked reliably throughout our stay.

I expected more from the InterContinental given the rate and location. The lobby looks polished, but the guest room felt stuck in another decade, with worn carpet, dark wood furniture, and lamps that barely lit the space. Cleanliness was also disappointing: there were crumbs beside the chair, fingerprints on the minibar, and hair in the shower when we arrived. The bathroom was cramped, with chipped tile around the tub and weak water pressure; the extractor fan rattled all night. We only stayed one night, yet it somehow felt much longer because of the noisy hallway and uncomfortable mattress. Staff were polite at checkout, but no one seemed interested when I mentioned the room issues.

We stayed three nights over a weekend and, honestly, I was bracing for chaos given the Hard Rock reputation. Instead, it was one of the smoother hotel experiences we've had in a while. The room was spotless--no stray hairs in the bathroom, crisp linens, and the carpet actually smelled fresh. Wi-Fi held up flawlessly for streaming and video calls, which was a pleasant surprise for a property this size. We were on a higher floor facing the pool, and while there was some ambient bass from the bar until about 11 PM, it faded quickly and never disturbed our sleep. Considering the location and the free breakfast buffet, it felt worth every penny--especially compared to nearby options. Staff were genuinely friendly, not robotic. I'd book again without hesitation.

The Fairmont felt worth every penny--the lobby's classic elegance still charms, not dated at all. Breakfast croissants were flaky perfection, and the marble bathroom with a rain shower made mornings feel like a spa ritual. A refreshing, polished stay.

We traveled to Chicago to visit with our daughter who lives in the city. To our suprise what once was a lovely older hotel is now under major renovations. Gone is the lobby and gusts are required to walk down to the basement to get the one... elevator that is working to the second floor to register. Our first room was recently renovated.....stark white walls, no amenities at all. Guests had to enter the room and find their way to the bed to turn on the light to the room. Modern furniture includes a bed that is close to the groud, a cold blck slab functioning a a desh and metal chair. No fride, coffee maker, iron, or even a picture on the stark white walls. We asked to change our room and then were put in one of the older suites on the 15th floor. While this room was attractive, we were greeted to jack hammers at 8 every morning. The staff were all very nice but the accommodations were lacking. lake shore drive

I loved the Ambassador! What a great hotel. It's really beautiful, and the room was absolutely striking, very classic and elegant. Everything was done really well: the staff treated me like a regular. This is a top-notch hotel, the best place I've stayed in a long time. My only complaint is that I wish it was on the Mile, but that's it.

We stayed at the AE for two nights for a three generation 'girls weekend' (Grandma, mom and daughter). I looked at their website for an idea of rates and looked at any packages that might interest us. Then I called the property directly and was assisted by a very gracious man named Reece. Rates were a bit high for the Saturday night portion of our stay but when I requested the American Girl Package, he was more than happy to honor the advertised rate. The American Girl package was perfect for us. My 8 year old daughter was thrilled. They give you a doll bed, a backpack and a travel kit to keep. They have matching bathrobes for girl and doll (you don't get to keep those). She also got a special welcome letter and a complimentary room service snack from a specially printed menu. Our room, 1334, was large and clean. It had two double beds with nice linens, two chairs, a desk and a clean bathroom. The employees are all very friendly and helpful. We had a drink in the Pump Room but did not eat there. We ate breakfast nearby at a great place called the 3rd Coast. This hotel is north of Michigan Ave. But it is just a short, pleasant walk to the Mag. Mile. I would definately stay here again in Chicago.

The Sofitel's prestige is skin-deep. From check-in, the staff seemed to be doing me a favor by acknowledging my reservation, and the welcome drink was a watered-down juice. The room itself was tired: scuffed furniture, stained carpet near the window, and the 'signature' bed was lumpy in the middle. I got zero sleep hearing plumbing from the adjacent room and hallway chatter late into the night. The bathroom looked grand at first glance, but the shower door wouldn't seal and leaked all over the floor. For what they charge, you'd expect at least a functioning wardrobe--the doors kept sliding off their tracks. Breakfast was hectic and the pastries were stale. The only nice touch was the pool views, but I couldn't enjoy them with the maintenance crew power-washing the deck at 8 AM. I expected far more polish and attention. This felt like a standard business hotel coasting on a luxury label. I won't be back.

Affinia was a comfortable base for a long weekend in the city. My room was quiet despite facing a busy street, and the bed was genuinely excellent--firm enough for support, with soft linens that made it easy to sleep through the night. The bathroom was spotless and more spacious than expected, with good water pressure, plenty of towels, and useful counter space for toiletries. Breakfast was simple but fresh: eggs, fruit, pastries, coffee, and a few hot options, all replenished quickly by attentive staff. The location and friendly service added a lot to the stay. It is not the cheapest hotel nearby, but the comfort, cleanliness, and restful sleep made it feel worth the price.

After reading some of the most recent reviews I'm really perplexed. I didn't know what to expect, but I was most pleasantly surprised. Just as all the past reviews, both negative and positive, have stated, you can't beat the location of this hotel. It's perfect. We had a big spacious room in the old tower. We avoided the expensive pitfalls of the hotel extras such as bottled water and items in the room fridge. The beds were great, the rooms were kept clean and the staff was very friendly. Great martinis in the hotel bar. I really can't understand the negative reviews. I know you can't please everyone, but in some cases I simply don't believe their claims. I've traveled a lot and have stayed in plenty of hotels. This is a great hotel!

The location is fantastic, but that's where the positives end. Our room felt tired, the air conditioning was broken, and housekeeping never replaced the towels. A truly disappointing stay for the price.

Affinia's location was the one real advantage: I could walk to nearby restaurants and catch the subway without much trouble. Unfortunately, the hotel itself felt tired and overpriced. The lobby and room decor looked like it had not been updated in years, with scuffed furniture, dull carpeting, and dated artwork. My bathroom was especially disappointing--tiny, poorly lit, and fitted with an old tub whose drain backed up during showers. There were water stains around the sink and the towels felt rough. When I mentioned the drainage issue, the front desk was polite but dismissive and never followed up. Housekeeping also knocked repeatedly before checkout time. For the rate, I expected a cleaner room and staff who seemed more interested in resolving problems.
Hilton's central location made getting around easy, and the reliable Wi-Fi was great for work. The bathroom was spotless with a roomy shower, while breakfast offered fresh fruit and hot options.

I had a very pleasant stay at the Hilton and would happily return. My room was on a higher floor, with a lovely view over the city lights and nearby rooftops, especially nice at sunset. Despite being close to busy streets, the room was surprisingly quiet at night; I barely heard any traffic or hallway noise. Breakfast offered plenty of choice, including fresh fruit, pastries, eggs, hot dishes, and good coffee, with staff keeping everything well stocked. The location was one of the best parts--restaurants, shops, and public transport were all within an easy walk, so getting around was effortless. The room was clean, comfortable, and well maintained, and the team at reception were welcoming and efficient.

Good location and looks like a good property but did not seem to be managed well. Front desk staff was inattentive to customers and slow. Nice large suite for a room but plumbing fixtures were in disrepair (housekeeping staff could/should have reported each day) - partially clogged shower head, dripping sink, etc. Clean and OK, but neglected - we expected more from an Intercontinental Hotel. Many hotels to choose from in this area of Chicago - can get more for the price from almost any other.
The Sheraton felt tired and overpriced: our room smelled musty, the AC rattled all night, and requests for extra towels went unanswered until checkout.

I really wanted to like this Homewood Suites, and the location is honestly its one saving grace -- right off the highway with quick access to restaurants and the business park, which made my morning commute painless. Unfortunately, everything else fell flat. Despite paying for an upper-floor room, I faced a parking lot and a strip mall, so the 'view' was a joke. Worse, the walls are paper-thin; I heard my neighbor's TV until midnight and doors slamming at 6 a.m. both nights. The breakfast, usually the highlight of this chain, was a letdown: cold eggs, watery oatmeal, and the waffle iron ran out of mix both mornings with no staff restocking. The front desk did offer points as compensation, but between the noise and the sad hot plate, I won't be returning.

We stayed at Hotel Monaco and upgraded to a suite. I was disappointed with the room layout, and shabby furniture. I bumped into the coffee table and the top almost crashed to the ground. The make up mirror in the bathroom didnt work, the TV reception was very poor and overall the room just wasnt worth the $450 we spent there. Next time, we will go back to Trump Tower across the street, which is far superior to Hotel Monaco.

I stayed at the Omni for four nights over a long weekend and have zero complaints. The location is honestly hard to beat--everything I wanted to see was either walkable or a short rideshare away. Check-in was painless, and the bellman went out of his way to point out a fewlocal restaurants he personally liked, one of which turned out to be the best meal of the trip. My room was quiet despite being downtown, and the bed might be the most comfortable hotel bed I've slept in. Housekeeping kept everything spotless, and when I asked for extra coffee pods they were at my door within ten minutes. Breakfast in the restaurant one morning was solid, if a little pricey, but that's expected at this level. Would absolutely book here again next time I'm in town.

When you check into a hotel after being stuck in a airport, you areusually not in the best of mood. I, working in a upscale hotel, do encounter many guests checking in who this has happened to. All they want is a friendly face and a smooth check in. The desk clerk who checked me in at this property, did neither. She was short, rude, handed me my keys and walked away. I would never go back to this property due to this.

I was honestly a bit skeptical booking Affinia on a budget, but it turned out to be a solid value. The bed was the highlight--firm enough for support but with a plush topper that had me sleeping like a log until 9 AM, which never happens on business trips. The room's decor is a mix of clean contemporary and a few quirky touches that feel intentional, not tired, though the hallway carpet shows some wear. I only had one night, and I did wish I could stay another just to use the pool and lounge area; it felt like two days would be perfect. For the price I paid, especially given the location near everything, I'd call it a fair deal. The staff were genuine, and the blackout curtains were a godsend. I'd return without hesitation.

I booked the Intercontinental expecting the grandeur its name implies, but what I found was a faded echo of a bygone era. The lobby is impressive, sure, but my room felt stuck in the 90s, with worn carpet and furniture that looked tired rather than classic. The staff were courteous but overwhelmed; a simple request for extra towels took three calls and nearly an hour. While the location is undeniably convenient, just steps from the Magnificent Mile, that's its only saving grace. My window faced a brick wall and an air conditioning unit, offering a view that was frankly depressing. For the premium price, this felt like a letdown. I honestly expected far more polish for a property of this stature. I left feeling I'd overpaid for a name, not an experience, and I would think twice before returning.
Swissotel made our weekend easy: the room was spotless, the skyline view was lovely, and breakfast had plenty of choice. Staff were warm without being overbearing.

I spent two nights at Affinia and honestly wished the visit had been longer. The room was comfortable and thoughtfully laid out, with enough space to unpack and a small desk that was useful for catching up on email. Despite being close to busy streets, it was surprisingly quiet at night; I heard only faint city noise from time to time. The bed and pillows were excellent, and I slept through both nights without waking up, which is unusual for me in a hotel. WiFi connected quickly and stayed reliable for video calls and streaming. The front desk staff were friendly without being overly formal, and check-in was easy. It felt like a calm, convenient base for exploring the city.
At Homewood, street noise and a lumpy bed ruined sleep, the cramped bathroom had weak water pressure, WiFi kept dropping, and even one night felt far too long.

I am staying here now and actually am compelled to write this review before I fall asleep. The front desk staff were brief and one of them was chatting with her friend (gossiping) as I checked in (VERY unprofessional). The room she offered me was on a 'high' floor (5th.... HA) and when I checked in there was a big bag of grapes left behind by the previous guest on the window sill and some of the previous guests hair in the bathtub....I was DONE. Called down and had them re-clean the room; they made no offer to compensate or upgrade...not even a bottle of wine. The front desk clerk suggested I come down and get a key to another room (like I have time for that). Disappointing as I do like Kimpton hotels and am a Kimpton In Touch member (btw they've done away with the amenities...you just get a free item from the mini bar).

We stayed at the Hard Rock for three nights and honestly it exceeded our expectations. The room was spotless when we arrived and housekeeping kept it that way throughout our stay, even replacing towels before we asked. The wifi was fast and reliable, which mattered since I had to join a couple of video calls from the room with no buffering at all. The bathroom was a pleasant surprise, actually spacious, with good water pressure and plenty of counter space for two people getting ready in the morning. Despite being right in the middle of everything, our room was impressively quiet at night, we never heard noise from the hallway or the street below. The rock-and-roll decor is fun without being gimmicky. Would absolutely book again on our next trip.

From the moment I walked into the lobby with its golden guitars and rock memorabilia, I knew this wasn't going to be your standard cookie-cutter stay. The front desk crew were absolute legends--charming, fast, and genuinely funny, offering tips on the best local taco spots without any of that stiff corporate politeness. My room on the tenth floor was spotless, with crisp white linens and a killer view of the strip, and I never heard a peep from the hallway or neighboring rooms despite the hotel being fully booked. The Wi-Fi was surprisingly solid too; I streamed a movie without a single buffering wheel, which is more than I can say for most places I've crashed. Sure, the pool gets lively and the bar hums at night, but if you're after quiet, the room seals it off beautifully. Solid, rock-and-roll hospitality that actually delivers. I'd come back in a heartbeat.
Hotel Monaco looked charming online, but our room was worn and noisy, the air conditioner barely worked, and the front desk seemed indifferent when we mentioned it.

HI HO HI HO, off to Chicago we go. Here's the skinny, if you're hoping to run into a washed up rock star (CeCe Deville for us, and no the teenagers had no idea who he was) you may want to spend your hard earned money here. I took my younger sister and a couple of her friends (teenagers) for an overnighter in Chicago on our way to Wisconsin. I chose the Hard Rock for the ambiance. I mean come on it is supposed to be 'COOL'. Well it wasn't. The Positives: *It is in the Carbon & Carbide Building, which is beautiful. *The location: it sits in the middle of everything *The lobby has two computers for guest use. *The fitness center is very nice. Cardio machines have individual TV's and there are head phones in case you forgot yours. They have protein bars for those that like them for a post workout snack. *Check-in and out was quick and Valet was very courteous. The Negatives: *The rooms were small and ours wasn't clean (pistachio shells on the floor). The rooms were painted purplish gray (we were on the Prince floor) with a picture of Bob Marley hanging on one of the walls. The girls thought the coolest part about the hotel was the fuzzy throw pillows. *Bathroom had only a shower and not a full tub. *The cable reception was poor; I kept looking for the bunny ears to fix the picture. *It isn't anywhere near the Hard Rock Cafe. *There was very little memorabilia. *There is no pool, and yes I knew this when I made the reservation. To wrap it up, I won't be staying here again. If I am going to drop almost 4 Benjamins on a hotel room, I will stay at the Palmer House Hilton. But that is a whole different review.

Stayed three nights for a conference and was genuinely impressed. The location is perfect, tucked a block from the river but still close to the old town's busy lanes. My room on the sixth floor had a small balcony overlooking the rooftops--quiet in the morning, just the church bells. The bed was firm but comfortable, and the blackout curtains actually worked, which is rare.

Breakfast was the real highlight: fresh pastries, proper cappuccinos made to order, and scrambled eggs that weren't rubbery. The staff remembered my name by the second day, which felt thoughtful, not forced. Only minor gripe--the gym is tiny with just two treadmills, and the elevator can be slow during check-out rush. But the rooftop bar at sunset made up for it entirely. Would happily return for a leisure stay.

I was very happy with my stay at the Knickerbocker. The room were nice, and the staff was excellent. I was able to stay here for $80 per night thru Priceline. That was an incredible bargain in my opinion .. this hotel is very nice. It has an excellent location ... just off of Michigan Ave. All of the best shopping in Chicago can be found right around the corner. It's a great location ... very close to many great attractions. If there is any negative it would be that there is no swimming pool, but I think that is common with a lot of the older hotels in Chicago, I would definately recommend this place ... hopefully I will be able to stay there again in the future.

We just arrived from a 3 nights stay at the Sofitel Chicago Water Tower. It was faboulous. Fine Linen, nice room with bigs windows, bathroom with a shower, flat TV. Check for the deals on the Sofitel website, we had 3 nights for the price of two !

We stayed at the James for three nights in mid-October and left genuinely impressed. The location is hard to beat -- a short walk to the Magnificent Mile, but tucked on a quiet side street so you don't get the constant street noise. Our room was spotless when we arrived, and housekeeping kept it that way throughout the stay, restocking towels and coffee without being asked. The bathroom was a highlight: generous counter space, a deep soaking tub, and those Kiehl's products my wife kept raving about. What really made the stay, though, was the staff. The front desk teammate who checked us in remembered our names after the first night, and the concierge sorted out dinner reservations twice with zero attitude. Would absolutely return next time we're in Chicago.
Conrad's central location was handy, but the cramped bathroom felt dated and street noise kept me awake. My two-night stay somehow dragged on, with little comfort to offset the disappointment.

Booked this place expecting the Hyatt standard, but honestly, it fell flat. The hallways had that faint, musty smell of old carpet, and our room's decor felt straight out of the early 2000s - heavy drapes, worn wooden headboard, and a lampshade with a suspicious brown stain. Cleanliness was a gamble: the sheets were fresh, but the baseboards had a fuzzy layer of dust, and there were stray hairs in the shower drain. The bathroom was the worst part - the caulking around the tub was peeling and gray, and the water pressure vacillated between a trickle and a violent spray. At $280 a night, it felt like a $140 motel. The cracked tile floor and sticky closet handle just sealed the deal. I've had better stays at mid-range chains for half the price. Disappointing, especially since the staff were polite. I won't be back.

We stayed at Hotel Ambassador for four nights and left thoroughly pleased. Our room faced the courtyard side, so despite the central location we heard almost nothing at night -- genuinely quiet, and we slept well every evening. From the small balcony on the upper floors you can catch a glimpse of the rooftops toward the old town, nothing dramatic, but charming at sunset. The location really is the hotel's trump card: the metro stop is a two-minute walk, and restaurants and a pharmacy are right around the corner. Staff were consistently warm without being overbearing -- the front desk arranged an early check-in without fuss, and the breakfast team remembered our coffee order by the second morning. Small touches like the fresh fruit in the room made it feel cared for. Would happily return.

Stayed at Swissotel for a city break and was thoroughly impressed. The wifi was fast and reliable, breakfast offered a generous spread with fresh pastries, and our spotless room boasted breathtaking lake views. A truly comfortable, stress-free stay.

We planned to stay for 5 nights on a family trip. I booked this hotel because of the expected value for a suite as well as the free breakfast - get a quick bite, then head out for the day to do normal tourist stuff. Well, our stay here lasted 1 night and we quickly, and thankfully, switched to a different hotel for our last 4 nights. The room was dirty. When we opened the sofabed, the sheets were filthy and there was a mess of dirt and crumbs that fell out. Ridiculous considering this is a suite hotel where the sofabeds are likely used, and theoretically cleaned, a lot. Extra blankets were also dirty and bathrooms weren't much better. Temperature control in the room was imprecise - minor inconvenience but without clean blankets on our only night, it made for a cold stay. If you like to eat for free (they have free breakfasts and dinner on certain nights) and don't care to eat the great food Chicago has to offer, I guess some may find this place tolerable. But we found the buffet no better than average and felt like we were at a Golden Corral. The only thing this hotel really has going for it is location but there are other options in this area (we switched to The James and had a great experience). I couldn't be paid to stay here again. I'm shocked by the high overall rating given our experience.
Hotel Amalfi was charming and spotless, with a wonderfully central location. The staff gave great dinner tips, and our room was quiet despite being near all the action.

Checked in expecting a premium stay, but the cracked ceiling and dingy carpet made the price feel absurd. Wi-Fi dropped every few minutes, and the 'city view' was mostly a brick wall. Two nights here felt like five.
Perfectly located steps from the waterfront, this hotel exceeded expectations. Staff were warm and attentive, the room spotless. Two nights felt far too short--we'll definitely be back.

This hotel must have originally been an ordinary downtown hotel in a not very nice neighborhood. The owners have painted it over and fixed up the lobby to make it an 'upscale' overpriced boutique hotel. But it's still just an ordinary hotel with a paint job. Stay here if you want to experience staying in a flophouse, but with all the sleaze removed. Definitely stay at the chain's other location, the Burnham, for a much, much nicer hotel.

I expected much better from a Sheraton. Check-in took nearly 30 minutes even though there was no obvious queue, and the receptionist barely acknowledged the delay. The room looked tired, with scuffed furniture, a stained carpet near the desk, and an air conditioner that rattled all night. Wi-Fi kept dropping, which made it difficult to work. Breakfast was disappointing too: lukewarm eggs, empty coffee dispensers, and tables left uncleared for far too long. I mentioned the noise and internet issue at checkout, but was simply told they would 'make a note.' The location was convenient, but it did not make up for the lack of comfort or service.
Hotel Amalfi was a lovely surprise--quiet room, comfortable bed, and genuinely friendly staff who helped us find dinner nearby. The location made walking around the city incredibly easy.

What a quaint, warm and friendly place to stay! Very accomodating ..had 2 dble beds and bathroom was fine....a bit small compared to USA hotels....but compared to european travel...the place was palatial! Would def. stay here again. Location is great too!

My 3 nieces and I stayed here for a long weekend, we had a wonderful time. We arrived early around 8:30am and they let us into our room. This was very nice otherwise we would have had to store our luggage and register later Room was very clean as was the bathroom. With 4 women we needed extra towels, they brought them up right away and then we got a call to make sure they were delivered. Room was also quiet, construction going on behind us and we never heard anything. Beds comfy and so were the quilts... Good location for Michigan Ave. All in all a wonderful stay. Would return.

I stayed at the Grand Hyatt for four nights on a work trip and came away genuinely impressed. My room on the 22nd floor was quiet enough that I slept through the night every single time, which almost never happens for me in hotels -- the bed was firm but comfortable and the blackout curtains actually did their job. The bathroom was a highlight: large walk-in shower with strong water pressure, plenty of counter space, and they restocked towels without my even having to ask. Decor-wise, everything felt fresh and recently updated, with warm lighting and modern fixtures rather than the tired gold-and-maroon look some older Hyatts still have. It isn't cheap, but between the location next to the transit stop, the helpful front desk, and the quality of the room itself, I felt the price was fair and would happily return.

My stay at the The James was perfect. My room was thoughtfully designed: the lighting, the storage space, the bar area, the eating nook and everything else in the room was purposeful and pretty to look at. The staff was friendly and and genuinely accomadating. The restaurant (Primehouse) echoed the above. Great service and one of the best steaks I've had in a very long time.

While the James was once considered an elegant, chic establishment, it has lost its luster. The small rooms are filled with cheap Ikea type furnishings, Our tiny bathroom flooded with water that escaped the shower curtain. Showers and flushings from neighboring rooms sounded more like protective levies collapsing. The 2 small elevators could not handle the guests, and many of us were forced to walk down several flights of stairs rather then wait for extended periods of time. The thin windows could not contain street noise and sidewalk conversations were heard throughout the night. It was rather provocative to listen to the couple next door carousing, but also rather tacky & unsettling. It took more then 30 minutes for the valet to bring our car after we checked out. This hotel has lost it and the James sysndicate will have a difficult time competing in New York's Soho when they try to open in September. New Yorkers will not tolerate shabby incompetence.

Our stay at the Hotel Ambassador was a real disappointment. The lobby looked impressive, but the room felt tired and poorly maintained, with scuffed walls, a stained carpet, and a bathroom fan that rattled all night. The bed was uncomfortable, and despite asking twice, housekeeping never brought the extra towels we requested. Breakfast was another letdown: the buffet was crowded, several dishes were lukewarm, and staff seemed overwhelmed rather than welcoming. We also had trouble with the Wi-Fi, which repeatedly disconnected during a work call. When we mentioned these issues at checkout, the receptionist listened politely but offered no meaningful apology or compensation. Perhaps we were unlucky, but for the price and reputation, the Ambassador did not deliver the comfortable, attentive experience we expected.

Really pleasant stay at the Hotel Ambassador -- spacious room with a comfy bed, friendly staff who upgraded us on arrival, and a proper good breakfast. Location was spot on too, walking distance to everything.
The decor felt fresh and modern, and the city view from our window was stunning. Being steps from the metro made exploring effortless, though our two-night stay flew by way too quickly.

Avoid The Talbot, especially for group functions. My in-laws spent a great deal of time trying to find just the right hotel to use for our wedding party and several out of town guests. They were lured in by promises from The Talbot, that since they were a small boutique hotel that they could provide 'special, personal treatment'. Nothing could have been further from the truth. They failed to honor two requests to keep the bar open after our reception, they persistently confused reservation requests, they front desk failed to contact the valet despite multiple requests and nearly caused of my guests, his wife, and his two year old daughter to miss their departing flight. Now the worse part. Mistakes are made, even hotel managers are human, but where a hotel, which is supposed to be in the hospitality service, can distinguish itself is in how they handle and correct the error. Case in point: I had requested on several occasions when I made the reservations for my family that they all be placed under my credit card, all expenses, they assurred me that this would be no problem. Of course, when my brother, his wife, and asthmatic five year old arrived to searing hot and humid Chicago after six hours of travel they wouldn't let them check in until they physically saw my card... again despite them having my card on record, and despite my explaining this to them over the phone. My brother recalls the 'indignation' of the desk clerk when he mentioned that the charges were to be put on my card. Then Another guest, in this case my older brother, came by and put the charges onto his card so that the five year old could escape the heat and the prolonged waiting in the lobby. When I finally was able to get across town, leaving a Cubs game early, I again spoke to them about putting all the charges on my account. Again they agreed, but never did anything about it. In the end when my older brother checked out on Sunday he was told everything was alright, but when he went to his ATM his account was frozen from 'unathorized overuse'. The hotel kept billing his debit card automatically for multiple charges ubtil his account was essentially drained. When he got home he had to take an entire day off to discuss with his bank how to rectify these events. I spent Sunday afternoon for an hour and three hours on Monday, the first two days of my honeymoon on the phone, calling The Talbot, the credit card fraud division, my brother, etc trying to solve this situation. The most aggregious insults continued to come form the covering manager, who at one point suggested that 'I was mistaken about coming back down to talk with the desk clerk about these matters'.... this was a witnessed event, and her insinuation was that I was lying, and that there was no way her clerk could have made a mistake. In the end, there is no one running this place... managers from one department refer you to the manager of another departments voice mail. When I was finally able to get the name of the general manager (after two days)m neither he nor his assistant would ever call back. The communication between the staff and mangement is non-existant. Fortuneatly the staff at the Signature Room (where we had the reception) was beyond excellent so the day was not lost, but the The Talbot went out of its way to insult and poorly serve my family and many of our wedding guests. Try The Ambassador East (same neighborhood) cheaper, much more professional staff.

I wanted to like the Palmer, especially because the location is so convenient, but the stay was more frustrating than enjoyable. Check-in took nearly 30 minutes, and the front desk agent seemed overwhelmed and barely explained the resort fee or Wi-Fi charges. Our room looked tired, with scuffed furniture, a stained lampshade, and a bathroom fan that rattled loudly all night. Housekeeping also skipped us on the second day, despite our leaving the room for several hours. The historic lobby is impressive, but the crowds and long elevator waits made the hotel feel chaotic rather than special. Staff did apologize when we complained, though nothing was really done beyond offering a vague assurance. For the price, I expected better maintenance and smoother service, and I would probably choose another downtown hotel next time.

I expected more from Hotel Amalfi, especially for the rate. The room looked as though it had only been tidied in a hurry: dust sat on the bedside table, there were marks on the mirror, and I found a stray hair on the sheets. The bathroom was the biggest letdown, with cracked grout around the tub, weak water pressure, and a lingering damp smell that never went away. Staff at the desk were polite enough but distracted; when I mentioned the bathroom issue, I was told someone would look into it, but nobody did. I had booked three nights and by the second evening the stay already felt much too long. The location was convenient, but it did not make up for the uncomfortable, poorly maintained room.
Fairmont's central location was convenient, but the room felt poorly cleaned, the bathroom was cramped and dated, and hallway noise kept me awake most of the night.

We have just returned from 4 nights at the Conrad Chicago, everthing about the hotel was excellent. Wonderful room and service from all the staff was first class. Great view from our room. The hotels location is great, right in the centre of the magnificent mile. A wonderful stay in an amazing city was made perfect by our stay at the Conrad.

The room itself was fine and comfortable(very peaceful), but the customer service by the so-called, concierge or 'experience something or the others' left much to be desired. First, I arrived and the doorman walked me to the desk. I was not greeted with the usual 'Hello, welcome to...'. Instead, I got, 'Your name? ID?' No, 'hello', no 'welcome to the Amalfi Hotel,' just plain old poor customer service from the very beginning! That left a very bad taste in my mouth, but I decided to let it go and see how the rest of my stay was.

We stayed at the Talbott for four nights in October and were genuinely impressed. Our room on the fourteenth floor was beautifully refreshed -- the furnishings, bedding, and bathroom all felt recently renovated, nothing dated about it at all.
