Sleep quality was excellent; the bed was plush but supportive, blackout curtains worked perfectly, and despite being so close to Rush Street we barely heard any street noise, just the occasional distant siren. The wifi was free and fast enough for video calls I had to take for work, with no drops during my stay. Housekeeping was prompt and thorough. Location is unbeatable for shopping and dining, and the staff remembered my coffee order by day two. Would happily return for our next Chicago trip without hesitation.

Stayed at the James for a long weekend and came away really impressed. The location made it easy to walk to restaurants, shops, and the lake, but the room was quiet once we were upstairs. Our king room felt thoughtfully laid out, with a comfortable chair by the window, a useful desk, and plenty of outlets for phones and laptops. The bed was excellent--firm enough for me, with soft sheets and great pillows. I also appreciated the rainfall shower and the quality toiletries, which felt like a small upgrade over most city hotels. Everyone at the front desk was warm without being overly formal, and they helped us find a late-night dinner spot nearby. The lobby has a polished, relaxed feel. I'd gladly stay here again.
The wifi dropped constantly, forcing me to work in the lobby. My room had dust on the baseboards and the bathroom smelled musty, though the location near the metro was undeniably handy.

My stay at Sofitel was a very pleasant one, although two nights felt far too short to properly enjoy the hotel and the city. The welcome was warm without being overdone, and every staff member I dealt with was polite, efficient, and happy to help with directions or a late dinner recommendation. My room was quiet, comfortable, and thoughtfully arranged, with a remarkably good bed and plenty of space for luggage. Breakfast offered a nice mix of fresh fruit, pastries, eggs, yogurt, and better-than-expected coffee, so I never felt rushed in the morning. From the higher floor, the view over the surrounding streets and rooftops was especially attractive at sunset. Everything felt polished but still relaxed, and I would gladly return for a longer visit.

I booked the Intercontinental based on its reputation, but my stay left me scratching my head. The lobby is grand, sure, but the room I was given felt dated, with a musty smell and a view of a brick wall and air conditioning units. The carpet had visible stains near the bed, and the bathroom looked like it hadn't seen a remodel since the 90s. Service was oddly inconsistent: the front desk was courteous at check-in, but housekeeping ignored my 'Do Not Disturb' sign twice, and room service took over an hour for a simple salad. The pool area was overcrowded, and the water was lukewarm at best. For the price I paid, I expected far more polish. The location is convenient, but honestly, this felt like a mid-tier business hotel charging a luxury premium. I won't be back, and I'd advise others to look elsewhere for their stay in this city. Disappointing is the kindest word I can find.

I booked the Talbott based on photos that made it look charming and intimate. What a letdown. The room was incredibly cramped, with a musty smell that no amount of airing out could fix. The 'courtyard view' was essentially a brick wall and a dumpster. The Wi-Fi kept dropping every few minutes, making it impossible to get any work done. Breakfast was a sad, lukewarm buffet with scrambled eggs that looked like rubber. The staff seemed overwhelmed and indifferent. For the price we paid, this felt like a roadside motel dressed in fancy packaging. The only positive was a decent shower, though the hot water ran out after five minutes. Save your money and look elsewhere.

My stay at Swissotel was far more disappointing than I expected for the price. The lobby looks impressive, but the room felt tired, with scuffed furniture, worn carpet, and a bathroom that needed better cleaning around the fixtures. The air conditioning was noisy and never seemed to reach the temperature I set, so I barely slept. Wi-Fi also kept dropping during a work call, which was especially frustrating. Staff at check-in were polite enough, but the queue moved slowly and nobody explained the various charges on my bill. Breakfast was expensive for what was offered, and several items were lukewarm when I arrived. The location is convenient, but that alone does not justify the rates. I left feeling that the hotel relies too much on its name and views rather than delivering a consistently comfortable stay.

I was apprehensive after reading some of the more negative reviews of the Hotel Allegro. However, our stay there was without problems and the staff could not have been more friendly and helpful. The room was not huge but there was plenty of room to move around without bumping into one another. The bathroom was small but well appointed. Overall, it was a clean and interestingly decorated room and we were pleased. Others have complained about being able to clearly hear people in adjacent rooms but we must have lucked out in that way and did not experience that although we could occasionaly hear people talking in the hallway. One other reviewer complained rather bitterly about the area and said that it was dangerous and I can't even begin to understand that as we found it to be extremely safe. The area is also very close to public transportation (we used the trains exclusively) and got around quite well without a car. We would most definetly stay here again and recommend it to others.

Our room was on the third floor so there was some street noise - but it certainly didn't spoil our 4 nights in this lovely hotel. Wine tasting evening went down extremely well after a day seeing the sights of the city!! Our goldish was called Oliver - nobody could believe we had our very own goldfish in our room!! All the staff were really helpful and welcoming, making our stay here very relaxing and comfortable. Would certainly recommend this hotel.

Very pleasant front staff, wine in the evening in the lobby, large rooms, great rates, and free Internet for those that are members of the loyalty program. Overall an excellent value. Close to the El for those coming in from either Midway or O'Hare airports.

Do you imagine getting there for the first time and overlooking the room, that was supposed to be ready, with used towels and the mouthwash opened and used? what about when they left the towel for the floor (the foot towel) to dry my face? what about the slippers that, although being still in the bag, had all the sole broken and left tiny plastic parts over the way to the garbage (all over the room, de facto). i didn't realise that would happen to me until i saw paris hilton on tv and then i knew god is great and he did it to us for being such an idiots to go to a company that has been able to create her. shame on us, actually!

The Swissotel is totally understaffed and lacking any charm or atmosphere. It was clean, comfortable and had great views but if you wanted to check-in, use the concierge, check-out, or report a problem to the front desk, forget about it. I booked this place through Priceline.COM so I can't complain too much as I didn't pay a lot for the room but I have stayed at 4 star hotels in the past as well as another Swissotel. It left a lot to be desired. The minibar fridge in my room didn't work so forget about a cold beer. Also, the internet/movie/guest services console didn't work so I had to go to the business office to access the internet. When it was time to checkout the console still wasn't working. It's better than the Holiday Inn but way below expectations for a 4 star hotel

We booked the Homewood expecting the usual Homewood Suites standard, but this felt like a cheap imitation. The room we were given had a sticky patch on the carpet near the mini-fridge, and the sofa bed mattress was so thin I could feel every spring through the sheet. We asked for extra towels at the front desk and were told they'd be sent up; after an hour and a second call, we gave up and used the bath mat. The 'hot breakfast' was lukewarm at best, with scrambled eggs that looked and tasted like they'd been sitting out since dawn. The hallway smelled strongly of stale frying oil the whole stay. Worst part? The air conditioner rattled so loudly all night I got maybe four hours of sleep. For the price, I expected a lot more. Definitely won't be back.
My stay at the Hilton was more frustrating than relaxing: the room felt dated, housekeeping missed basic details, and check-in took nearly an hour despite arriving after the posted time.

Booked a suite for a weekend getaway, but the room smelled musty and the A/C sounded like a jet engine all night. The front desk was indifferent when I complained, and breakfast ran out by 9 AM. Overpriced for the wear and tear.

Great location right in the heart of the city, but our four nights felt like twice that long. The room had sticky floors and dusty corners, and the staff barely acknowledged us at check-in. Disappointing for the price.

I stay at this hotel 2 times a year on business and LOVE it! The staff are great, the rooms are spacious and clean, and the location is perfect for shopping and dining on Michigan Ave. Plus if you sign up for Omni Select Membership (for free) you get free wireless internet access.

We stayed at the Grand Hyatt for four nights over a long weekend and honestly can't find much to complain about. Check-in was quick, and the front desk agent actually took time to point out a few good restaurants nearby, which was a nice touch. Our room on the 14th floor was huge by city standards, with a super comfortable bed I kept 'testing' far too long each morning. Housekeeping was thorough without being intrusive. The breakfast buffet is worth it even if it feels a little pricey at first--fresh fruit, made-to-order omelets, and the coffee is decent. Pool and gym are clean and never crowded when we went. Only minor gripe is the elevator wait times during peak hours. Would book this place again without hesitation.

Stayed three nights here and honestly couldn't have asked for a smoother trip. The lobby is elegant without being stuffy, and the front desk agent remembered my name each time I walked by--a small touch that made the stay feel personal. Room was spotless and quiet, with a bed that had me sleeping better than I do at home. The blackout curtains actually worked, and the bathroom had great water pressure plus those thick towels you only seem to get at nicer places. Location was perfect for walking to dinner and catching a show, but I also appreciated the hotel bar for a nightcap. The bartender mixed a solid Old Fashioned and chatted without hovering. Only minor gripe: the elevator took a while during checkout rush. Would book again without hesitation.

I visited Chicago with my two teenage daughters. Homewood Suites is amazing. The complimentary breakfast and receptions offer so much variety. The hotel was within walking distance to many places to eat and shop. We got caught in a thunderstorm, and got soaking wet. I dried all our clothes in the dryer right in the hotel! The Homewood Suites was so much like home. The suite was very spacious and had everything we needed. The hotel had lots of brochures and suggestions for dining and activities. The staff was so friendly and helpful. Chicago is an amazing place and the Homewood Suites is the place to stay. I would definitely stay there again.

I expected more from Affinia given the rate and photos online. Our room looked tired, with scuffed furniture, a stained chair by the window, and a bathroom fan that rattled all night. The bed was fine, but the walls were so thin we heard a neighboring TV and people coming back from the elevator after midnight. Check-in took nearly 20 minutes because only one person was at the desk, and when I mentioned the noise the next morning, the response was basically a shrug. The location was convenient for our plans, but that was the only real positive. Housekeeping also skipped our room despite the sign being removed early in the day. It did not feel like a hotel charging these prices.

The Conrad has all the right stuff - great bedding, fancy decorations, beautiful lobby, etc. However, they are seriously missing the boat when it comes to customer service and attention to detail. When I checked in, I went to get a glass of wine from the minibar, only to discover that everything in the fridge was warm. I called for help and was cheerfully told that they would send an engineer right away to fix it. In the meantime, I said, great, but what about a cold drink? They proceeded to send me 1 glass of wine via room service, without asking me if this would be okay. I paid $25 for 1 glass of wine. The minibar bottle would've given me 2 glasses for about $33. Nothing was said to me about this obvious difference. When I called to complain, I was made to feel cheap. To me, it was not the money, it was the principle. The next morning, my bill showed that I had eaten something out of the minibar. I had not. I called, and they said that the automatic sensors in the minibar must have triggered something (duh - when the engineer came and took the entire fridge out of its compartment to fix it), and they took the charge off. They also took $10 off my room service bill, but I was still annoyed that nobody bothered to apologize or acknowledge the fact that I was overcharged. Also, when they fixed the minibar fridge, they did not replace anything in it. The guy said, it'll take a while for things to cool down. Oh, really? How about the warm beer, that was once cold, that will now taste disgusting? I guess they're saving that for the next person who checks into my room and has no idea. Another annoyance was that the lighted mirror in our bathroom did not work. When I plugged it in, it made 2 other lights in the bathroom go off, and then it never would come on. It seems that the Conrad thinks it can spend a lot of money to make itself look beautiful, without worrying about each customer's experience. I don't think they go into the rooms and check them out. And their sta

Got a good deal on a weekend pacage in this Hotel and have to say it is the nicest stay I have had in more than a dozen business trips to Chicago. All rooms are Suites, staff is friendly and professional, Restaurant is out of this world and all the extras like a great health club, turn down service, complimentary morning beverages delivered to room and on and on. Room was very clean and every need was attended to without feeling intruded on. Will definately stay here again.

We stayed here for one night, and found it a hotel that concentrates on conferences rather than your normal guest. We found it hard to get a room in the city for that particular night and so we paid above the odds for this - @ $200 for the night. We felt when we checked in that if you weren't with the conference, then why were we staying in the hotel. The guy at the main door didn't even hold it open when you are trying to lug your bags into the lobby, we then had to que for 15-20 minutes just to check in. We were not given any information about the hotel and when I rang down to reception at one stage to find out if there was a business centre in the hotel that I could access the Internet through, I was just short of being asked why didn't I bring my lap-top with me so I could use the Internet access in the room.... !! I found the staff very rude and not helpful at all and would not recommend this hotel for a tourist.

I had a very pleasant stay at the Conrad and would happily return. The lobby felt elegant without being overly formal, and check-in was quick, friendly, and well organized. My room was spacious, quiet, and exceptionally clean, with a comfortable bed and a great city view. I especially appreciated the thoughtful details, including the quality toiletries, plenty of outlets, and the coffee setup for early mornings. Breakfast had a good variety, though the restaurant was busy one day, so service took a little longer than expected. The staff throughout the hotel were warm and attentive, always greeting me with a smile and helping with directions or transport suggestions. The location also made it easy to explore nearby attractions. Overall, it was a polished, relaxing experience and good value for the level of service.

our stay was absolutely perfect. its a cool hotel to look at, the design and feel is very trendy and hip. all the staff are terrific, especially the consierge staff-great info and attitude. our room was on the top floor, with great views. super comfy bed, and neat bathroom. fantastic, choose this with no hesitation!
The James was a lovely stay--our room was quiet and thoughtfully designed, the bed incredibly comfortable, and the staff genuinely welcoming. The location made it easy to explore everything nearby.

My wife and I stayed at the Ambassador East Hotel for the first 3 days of our honeymoon in mid-October. We decided to split our honeymoon up and stay in two different hotels so that we could experience different aspects and areas of Chicago in a week. I'll start out by saying that this was a great experience. At check-in, I indicated that we were on our honeymoon and were upgraded to a suite. The Ambassador East is probably a 10 to 15 minute walk from the North end of the Magnificent Mile. It is also just a 2 or 3 minute walk to a lot of great restaurants and bars on Rush. Our room itself was incredibly spacious and well appointed. Our suite (on the 3rd floor) had two very large closets, a large 'living room' and a large bedroom. The bed was incredibly comfortable and the bathroom was nice enough. If I would have payed full price for this suite, I probably would have given it a rating of 4, but because the staff was so kind and because my wife and I had such a great time here, I decided to give it a five. It is also worth mentioning that the concierge was very helpful. My wife and I decided to eat at The Pump Room restaurant, but we were not very impressed. We found the food and service mediocre. The atmosphere was probably pretty neat when Sinatra used to eat there back in the day, but not anymore. Although we were unimpressed by the Pump Room, the staff were kind enough to seat us in the 'Sinatra Booth' which was back in a corner and enclosed by curtains. That neat experience was really the only redeeming value of our meal here. The Ambassador East is an older hotel, but it is in a charming older neighborhood. The staff's kindness and overall charm of the hotel itself really impressed my wife and me. When we are in Chicago again, we will definitely consider staying at the Ambassador East again.

Stayed 5 nights at this great hotel. Updated rooms. Clean. Used Tim to book theater and dinning reservations. Provided excellent service. Close to subway, shopping and dinning. Excellent value. Free wireless internet and access to nearby health club very nice perks. Highly recommend it. Future concern is adjacent construction of condos. Not a problem while we were there but something to ask front desk about in the future.

I stayed at the Sheraton for four nights for a work trip and honestly it exceeded my expectations. The front desk sorted out my early check-in without any fuss, which was great after a red-eye flight. My room on the 14th floor was spacious, spotless, and the bed--oh that bed, the Signature bedding thing they advertise is legit, I slept better than I do at home. Housekeeping was consistent every day, always restocking water and towels. The club lounge had a decent breakfast spread with fresh fruit and good coffee, though it got a bit crowded around 8:30. Location was perfect, walking distance to the metro and plenty of restaurants nearby. Only small gripe was the gym had a couple of broken machines, but there was plenty of equipment anyway. Staff overall were warm and genuinely helpful. Would absolutely stay here again.

I really wanted to like this place based on the photos, but the reality was a letdown from the moment I walked in. The lobby smelled like stale fryer oil, and the front desk agent barely looked up from her phone to hand me my key card. My room, supposedly a 'deluxe,' faced a brick wall and a rattling AC unit that sounded like a lawnmower all night. The carpet had mysterious stains, and the bathroom mirror was smudged with toothpaste from a previous guest. I paid extra for the 'city view' which turned out to be a sliver of roof. The breakfast buffet was an absolute joke--cold eggs, stale pastries, and coffee that tasted burnt. The only positive was the housekeeping staff, who were polite, but they couldn't fix the noise from the hallway or the paper-thin walls. For the price, I'd rather sleep in my car honestly. Won't be back.
Disappointing stay at Hotel Allegro: the room felt dated, the walls were thin, and breakfast was poorly stocked. Staff were polite, but the overall experience wasn't worth the price.
Disappointing stay at the Omni: my room overlooked a bland wall, the rate felt excessive, Wi-Fi kept dropping, and the supposedly clean room had dust and a stale smell.

I stayed here for business and loved it. Got it for $93 inc tax on Priceline, an incredible deal for this hotel. If I wasn't on priceline I would expect to pay $200 per night (maybe more) for this location/level of service. It's in the heart of downtown Chicago, walkable to many locations. The lobby is very impressive, the room was very nice. No complaints at all, from check-in to check-out. I was alone so didn't go to the bar but it looked like people were really enjoying themselves. It was full of people all the time. I want to stay here when I come back with my husband for a fun weekend in the city.

I had a very pleasant stay at the InterContinental. The room was spotless when I arrived, with fresh linens, dust-free surfaces, and plenty of space to unpack comfortably. The bed was the highlight--firm enough for support but still cozy, and I slept deeply both nights despite being in a busy part of the city. The bathroom was equally well maintained, with good water pressure, a spacious walk-in shower, fluffy towels, and quality toiletries. Service was warm and professional without feeling overly formal. The rate was not cheap, but considering the location, comfort, and consistently high standards, it felt worthwhile, especially for a special trip. A quiet room and thoughtful details made the experience feel polished from start to finish.
Hotel Amalfi's location made sightseeing easy, but the stay felt far too long: the cramped bathroom had weak water pressure, and the worn, dated decor made the room feel gloomy.

A bunch of us got together and we had a great time in this hotel we asked for limes and they gave us like a punch bowl of them the rooms were so awesome you really have to see it to believe how extradionary this hotel is i love the decorations on every floor and being surrounded by such elegance. Will definitely stay here again

We stayed at Amalfi for 2 nights and i have to say after reading all the reviews here i expected a little bit more. It's a fine place with clean bathrooms and comfy beds but it's just not worth the money. It does have comfy beds and free continental breakfast. The sheets though, made us itch for some reason and we are normally not sensitive to these things. The breakfast could really benefit from some bagels or yougurt. Otherwise, it's just an early morning sugar attach of muffins, danishes, sweet breads, and croissants. There are plenty of restaurants around but they are all of the big chain variety, if you are into that sort of thing. Also, the windows do not open and there is a climate control device in the room. The problem with it that it keeps blowing air all the time, alternating between cold and warm, right over the bed. There is a sign not to turn it off but we did once just to see what happens and the air in the room got uncomfortably stale. They do have a business center where you can send fax and use internet for free. The problem is it is only one tiny room with one computer in there. One person at a time... All and all, we will not stay there again. If we feel like luxury, we have to find some other place. But if we feel like a regular hotel in the heart of the city, maybe we will try Red Roof Inn or something like that. At least we'll know what we are paying for.

I stayed at the InterContinental for a long weekend and came away genuinely impressed. The lobby is busy but elegant, and the front desk team made check-in easy even though we arrived earlier than expected. Our room was quiet, very clean, and had a comfortable bed with excellent blackout curtains--always a plus in the city. I also appreciated the little things, like plenty of outlets near the desk and fresh water replaced each day. The location made it simple to walk to restaurants, shopping, and a few museums without relying on taxis. Breakfast was a bit pricey, but the service was attentive and the coffee was good. The concierge gave us a useful dinner recommendation that ended up being the highlight of our trip. I would happily stay here again.

The bathroom had a constant musty smell and peeling caulk, which set the tone. Staff ignored my requests for fresh towels, though the location near the metro was the only plus, drowned out by nonstop hallway noise until 2 AM.

I had a very comfortable two-night stay at the James. The room was spotless when I arrived, including the desk, bedding, and even the corners that often get overlooked. It felt polished without being overly formal. The bathroom was a particular highlight: roomy, well lit, and equipped with a large walk-in shower, thick towels, and quality toiletries. Everyone at the front desk was friendly and efficient, and the concierge gave us useful dinner suggestions without pushing the obvious tourist spots. The location made the trip especially easy; we could walk to Michigan Avenue, several restaurants, and the river in minutes, while cabs were always nearby. Noise was minimal despite being downtown. I'd happily stay here again for either business or a weekend in Chicago.

The view from our 18th-floor room was genuinely spectacular--a sweeping panorama of the city skyline that shifted from glittering night lights to a soft, golden sunrise. We barely wanted to close the curtains. Breakfast downstairs was a cut above the typical hotel buffet: the made-to-order omelets were fluffy, the pastries were still warm, and the fresh-squeezed orange juice was a small luxury I didn't expect. Location-wise, you couldn't ask for more; we walked to the historic district in under ten minutes, and the metro station was basically at the corner. As for sleep, the bed was firm but comfortable, and the blackout shades did their job perfectly--I slept straight through until my alarm, which never happens at home. A few minor quirks with the Wi-Fi speed, but honestly, the stay felt worth every penny.

We had a lovely weekend at the Fairmont and were impressed from the moment the doorman helped with our bags in the rain. Our room was quiet, beautifully maintained, and had a comfortable bed that made it difficult to get moving in the morning. I especially appreciated the blackout curtains and the good water pressure--small things, but they matter after a long day out. The lobby felt polished without being stuffy, and the concierge gave us a few genuinely useful restaurant suggestions rather than the usual tourist list. Breakfast was a little pricey, though the service was prompt and the coffee excellent. The location also made it easy to walk almost everywhere we wanted to go. We would happily return.

We had a really enjoyable stay at the Hard Rock Hotel. The whole place has a lively atmosphere without feeling chaotic, and the music-themed decor gives it much more personality than a typical chain hotel. Our room was clean, comfortable, and surprisingly quiet at night, with a very good bed and plenty of storage. Check-in was quick, and the staff were friendly whenever we needed anything. We especially liked the pool area, which was well maintained and a great place to relax in the afternoon. The restaurant was convenient for breakfast, although service was a little slow during the busiest period. It is not the cheapest option, but the location, entertainment, and overall experience made it feel worth the price. We would happily stay here again.

I'll be honest--I booked the Conrad mostly for its location, but the stay turned out to be the highlight of the trip. The lobby feels understated and classy without trying too hard, and the check-in was smooth even though we arrived early. They stored our bags, texted us the moment the room was ready, and even added a small welcome note for our anniversary. The room itself was quiet, which I never take for granted in a city hotel, and the bed was genuinely comfortable. Breakfast was a bit pricey, but the coffee was excellent and the staff remembered our order on the second morning. The gym is compact but has everything you need. We didn't use the pool, but the view from the lounge at sunset was worth it alone. I'd happily stay here again.

My husband & I stayed at the Fitzpatrick in early June 2004 for my birthday-great hotel! Location provides easy walking to Navy Pier, Marshall Field, Michigan Avenue & John Hancock. Room seemed spacious even though its only about 300 sq ft. Lots of room in bathroom; comfortable bed; very quiet, upscale hotel. We would definitely stay here again!

I had purchased this deal of off groupon. Lets just say we found a bunch of hidden treasures. when We layed down to sleep in our bed. We lifted our blanket and found very distubing spotting on our bed (attached in photos), we immediatly called the front desk. The only thing they offered was a new set of sheets. when the room service men came to change the sheets he brought us another one with a big red stain on it and quickly/hid changed it before we seen it and he apologized and offered to bring us new ones once again. we denied since it was so late and just slept on the sheets the appeared to be clean. Then next day i eagerly showed the fronk desk and manager the photos, and they offered me a ($68) refund. I was very dissapointed,and dirty sheets that made us very uncomfortable and sleepless and I broke out on my face with ACNE (i never had a acne or skin issues) im positive something in those dirtyy sheets. We drove 4.5 hours to enjoy Chicago and we stayed @ the hard rock based on reputatuion, and unfortunitly we were very disspointed. it was DISGUSTING! I then wrote a Email to management and HEARD NOTHING BACK. NOT even a response or apology. I just really expected alot more.
Immaculate room with a stunning view of the river, and the marble bathroom was a real treat. WiFi worked flawlessly the whole stay. Would happily return.

The room was stuffy and the bed sagged, giving me a restless night. My cramped bathroom had a constant drip, and the patchy wifi kept cutting out during work. The stay felt far too long for what little comfort was offered.

Three nights there on business. Hadn't realized that the place was under construction and therefore the bar and restaurant are in the basement, very bleak. Told the front desk that I hadn't realized about the construction, so I'd have to switch hotels, they said they were still going to charge me for 3 nights. So I stayed. TV didn't work. Tried to get them to fix it and they ignored me...eventually after I called again, a few hours later, a couple grumpy maintanance guys came and fixed it. Long and complicated experience at the business center (which doesn't open until 9am, BTW), where I ended up paying $45 to print 55 pages. Had to buy these cards, and then the woman behind the desk ended up printing them herself anyway, (and charging me for them). I was left with $22 on a card for use at the business center in the basement of the Swissotel in Chicago, 2000 miles from where I live. I asked for a refund on the card and -- no surprise -- she declined to help me with that. Nice room, nice view, but the hotel is sterile and the service was incredibly bad. Worst experience I've ever had at a hotel when traveling for business.
Disappointing stay at Hotel Amalfi: the bathroom was cramped and tired, the dated decor needed attention, and although the location was convenient, even one night felt too long.

I haven't actually stayed at this hotel- yet- but am already disappointed in their customer service. I visit Chicago quite often and usually stay at the InterContinental, but yesterday I read some online articles advertising The James Hotel's 'Cyber Monday Special'. The promo states that if you buy a gift certificate from their website, the hotel will match that amount in 'James Credits' that can be used toward your stay. None of the articles gave an expiration date for these credits. My next trip to Chicago is in April, so I thought I'd give The James a try. I travel frequently with my pet and I've heard they have a very liberal pet-policy. So today I went online and bought a $500 certificate. Me, having the one track mind that I do, somehow missed the part about the credits expiring March 31, 2010. I realized my mistake immediately and called the hotel front desk to explain my predicament. I said I couldn't be in Chicago until April (I'm overseas on business until then), and asked if they could extend my credits an extra month, or it not, refund my gift certificate purchase. I had only just made the purchase minutes before and hadn't even recieved my email confirmation yet. Most businesses offer a 24 hr grace period. The girl at the front dest was extremely rude to me- basically saying 'too bad, it's your problem now'. She didn't even bother to act polite or pretend to be sympathetic about my situation at all. So now that I know this is the kind of service I can expect from The James, I might just call it a wash and stay at my usual hotel, or try Hotel Monaco. I hear they have great service and are good with pets too.

The James hotel is located close to everything in Chicago, the miracle mile, Pizza House Uno,Rush street, The Water Tower everything. We walked everywhere because everything was close by. The rooms are very modern and a little on the small side. But the bed was very comfortable, Very! The service is very good and the calls are answered professionally and nicely. All service was very fast and through. The lobby is a liitle small but that keeps the riff raff from hanging out in it, the bar service was good. The drink prices were high but what do you expect in a hotel bar. I got a great deal from leading hotels of the world for my stay of 3 days was just over $400.00 for a 5 star hotel that's cheap. Due to the location, price and service I may stay there again. But I think my next trip may take me to Trump's hotel in Chi Town. The James is a good stay . The doorman at the hotel are Great! Always pleasent, with a smile and very good service.

My girlfriends and I stayed 4 nights at the Talbott returning home on Saturday 9/29. We all had a wonderful time and thoroughly enjoyed the hotel. The staff from top to bottom were excellent, accommodating. The room was roomy...with our only complaint being not being able to cool the room fast enough after a day on the town. The construction next door was obstructing the sidewalk, but being on a oneway street limited that difficulty. The doorman, Andrew was an excellent source at this hotel. He arranged all our transportation at night to restaurants. We enjoyed everything about the hotel and the city. The hotel was expensive but met expectations.
Our two-night stay at Hilton felt too long in a dated, poorly cleaned room with dusty surfaces and stained carpet. Definitely not worth the high rate.

I really wanted to like the Affinia, but the whole stay felt like a series of small letdowns that added up. The room was advertised as spacious, but the layout was awkward--a giant column right in the middle of the floor made it impossible to move around the bed without stubbing your toe. The air conditioning unit sounded like a lawnmower and kicked on every fifteen minutes, so I got maybe three hours of sleep total. Housekeeping never came by even though I left the sign out, and when I called down, they just said they'd 'try again tomorrow.' The lobby looks nice in photos, but the hallways smelled like stale cigarette smoke, and the elevator took forever. Honestly, the location is the only saving grace, but for these prices, I expected way better. I won't be back.

I had a very comfortable three-night stay at the Omni Chicago. The location on Michigan Avenue made it easy to walk to restaurants, shops, and the river, and we hardly needed a taxi. Our room was surprisingly roomy, with a small sitting area that gave us space to relax without feeling like we were sitting on the bed. Everything was clean and in good condition, and the bed was excellent after long days exploring the city. Check-in was quick, while the front desk staff remained friendly and useful whenever we had a question. We also appreciated how quiet the room was at night despite being downtown. The lobby cafe was convenient for morning coffee, although breakfast there was a little pricey. Overall, it was a polished, comfortable base, and I would happily return.

We booked the Amalfi looking for a great boutique hotel in Chicago. The hotel is a nice property with clean rooms and nice amenities in a good location. However, when i booked the hotel I was offered an upgraded room from a king room to a corner king room for only $10 more. That was great until I checked in. The corner room looked at two brick walls and an alley. During the night there were several homeless individuals fighting in the alley. It would seem that this is a place for them to congregate. On top of this, the dumpsters in the alley were being emptied by the waste department between 5 and 6 am in the morning. The noise was crazy loud. I think this is a nice hotel with some unfortunate aspects due to its location. The staff is extremely friendly and very helpful.

Stayed three nights at the Palmer and left feeling thoroughly underwhelmed. The lobby looks grand in photos, but in person it's tired, with scuffed marble and wilted flowers that nobody bothered to refresh. Our room faced the courtyard, which sounded nice until we realized it meant zero natural light and a view of the ventilation units humming all night. The bed was okay, but the pillows were flat as pancakes, and housekeeping skipped our room entirely on the second day until we called twice. Breakfast was a disaster: lukewarm eggs, stale pastries, and coffee that tasted burnt. The staff at the front desk were polite but useless when we asked for a late checkout--they just shrugged and said the system was full. For the rate we paid, I expected so much more. I left feeling cheated, honestly. Won't be back, and I'd warn anyone else to look elsewhere in the area.

This was a weekend trip for my friends and I. We booked a couple of rooms and asked in advanced for the reservations to be connected in some way. Our rooms were right next to one another as requested. As it was almost everyone's first time to Chicago, we had to do a bit of cold-searching for a hotel. And, our choice was next to perfect. I had an amazing time during my first visit to Chicago and it was largely due to this hotel. The customer service was AMAZING. Everyone was extremely nice and helpful. One of our rooms ordered late night room service and raved about how they felt they had ordered a 5 star lunch because it was as fresh as having ordered food at 2 pm, and delicious. My friend suggested they had a full-staff at 3 am because the food came up quickly too. In another of our rooms, housekeeping had accidentally discarded a CD when replacing the CD player with an iPod dock. The concierge had the exact CD purchased and ready at check-out from the neighboring record store. Our rate included complimentary breakfast which was fantastic! Everything was freshly made in their kitchen too. An added bonus was that the hotel is attached to a mall. Therefore, you don't need to leave the building to get a pair of shoes, a coffee, or a some other type of trinket. I was beyond pleased with this hotel and would stay here again without hesitation.

I was really disappointed by my stay at The Knickerbocker. I booked it expecting a memorable experience, but the room felt much less polished than the price suggested. The view was mostly of nearby rooftops and a brick wall, with only a narrow glimpse of Times Square, so keeping the curtains open was hardly worthwhile. The room itself was generally clean, though I found dust along the window ledge and a few water marks on the bathroom fixtures. Staff were polite at check-in but seemed distracted, and getting a simple request for extra towels took two calls. I stayed for three nights, which felt too long given the lack of atmosphere and comfort. The location was convenient, but it did not make up for the disappointing service and poor value.

I had a very pleasant stay at Hotel Ambassador. The location made it easy to walk to nearby shops and restaurants, yet the room was quiet at night. Check-in was quick, and the front desk staff were genuinely friendly when I asked for directions and a late checkout. My room was clean, comfortable, and had a surprisingly good amount of space for a city hotel. The bed was excellent, with crisp linens and plenty of pillows, so I slept better than expected. Breakfast had enough variety to start the day well, including fresh fruit, pastries, eggs, and good coffee. A few parts of the decor feel slightly dated, but everything was well maintained. I would happily stay here again.

I had a very comfortable stay at Homewood and felt the room was a good value for the price, especially with the extra space and small kitchenette. Everything was clean when I arrived, including the floors, bedding, and counters, and the room had a fresh, well-kept feel without being overly fancy. The bathroom was simple but nicely maintained, with good water pressure, plenty of towels, and a shower that heated up quickly. My bed was comfortable, and the room stayed quiet enough at night that I slept soundly throughout my visit. The staff were friendly at check-in and answered my questions without making me wait. It is not a luxury property, but it was practical, comfortable, and reliable, which is exactly what I needed.
Our stay at the Hyatt was genuinely comfortable, with a spotless room, helpful staff, and a surprisingly good breakfast. The location made getting around easy, and we'd happily return.
Our stay at the Conrad was wonderfully easy, with a quiet, comfortable room, quick check-in, and genuinely friendly staff. The location made getting around simple, and we'd happily return.

Spent two nights at the InterContinental on a business trip. This is a tremendous, towering hotel in one of the best locations in Chicago -- right on the Magnificent Mile and superbly convenient for shopping and well placed for the business area. My room was in the Historic Tower -- a 1920s Masonic Club which has been converted at enormous expense. The effort has been worthwhile. My room was very large and well furnished, with a beautiful bathroom which contained a separate shower cubicle. It had breathtaking views down Michigan Avenue. There is a superb recreation centre (with an impressive swimming pool) beautiful bars and a good restaurant, Zest, that serves a great breakfast. There is wifi in the rooms ($9.95 per day) and tea and coffee making facilities. No trouser press, but there is an ironing board and iron. The staff is friendly and anxious to please. I recommend this hotel in the strongest possible terms. It's expensive, but it will be difficult to find a better one in Chicago.

I expected more from Affinia for the price. The bathroom looked dated, with stained grout around the tub and a weak shower that took ages to warm up. Our window faced a brick wall and the service alley, so there was no real view beyond delivery trucks and overflowing bins. Sleep was difficult because hallway doors slammed late into the night and traffic noise came through the old windows. Staff at check-in were polite but rushed, and when I mentioned the noise, the response was simply that the hotel was 'in a busy area.' Housekeeping also skipped our room one day. Overall, it felt worn down and poorly managed rather than comfortable.

We stayed at the Talbott in January and honestly left disappointed. The lobby and location are nice, I'll give them that, but the room we got felt tired and worn. Scratches on the furniture, a bathroom fan that rattled all night, and the heater could not keep up -- we woke up freezing twice. Housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely and we had to call down to get towels. The front desk staff were polite but slow; checking in took almost twenty minutes even though there was no line. Parking valet took forty minutes to bring our car when we checked out. For the price, I expected much better comfort and service. There are plenty of other options in the Gold Coast, and next time we'll try one of them. Probably won't be back.

We booked the Homewood expecting a decent value for a city break, but honestly, it felt like we overpaid for what we got. The location is walkable to the main sights, which was a plus, but that's where the positives end. Staff were polite yet appeared overwhelmed at the front desk; check-in took ages, and requests for extra towels were met with a curt 'we'll see.' I barely slept--the air conditioning rattled like a loose fan all night, and the mattress felt like a lumpy sack of potatoes. The hallways echoed with noise from neighboring rooms until well past midnight. For what we paid, I'd expected a properly functional room, not a tired, neglected one. Disappointing overall.

Affinia felt reasonably priced for its prime midtown spot--easy walk to Grand Central and Times Square. The decor leaned modern enough, not tired, and our corner room's skyline view was a pleasant surprise. Solid, hassle-free stay.

The 'city view' was mostly a wall of neighboring windows, and breakfast felt like a rushed cafeteria. The bathroom's shower drain clogged nightly, making the three nights drag on far too long for such a letdown.

I had a really pleasant stay at Hotel Palmer. The location made it easy to walk to restaurants, shops, and the waterfront, but the hotel itself was quiet and relaxing at night. My room was bright, clean, and thoughtfully arranged, with a comfortable bed, plenty of outlets, and a surprisingly good shower. I also appreciated the small touches, like the quality toiletries and the coffee available in the morning. Everyone I encountered at the front desk was friendly and genuinely helpful, especially when I asked for local dining suggestions. Check-in was quick, and the common areas had a warm, modern feel without being overly fancy. It wasn't the largest room I've stayed in, but it was more than adequate and felt well cared for. I'd happily return to the Palmer.

Very Very noisy - Constant water running through pipes. It was terrible!! There are much better hotels to stay at in Chicago. Thier parking rate is obnoxious ($42.00 a night) and way too far out to walk to much. If you must stay here, try to park for free on dead end street (feed meter on weekdays) and take the stairs down to the next street level and you will find a Jewel grocery store for sodas/snacks. (A can of soda at the hotel was $4.50 plus 18% restocking fee!!)

I had a very pleasant stay at the InterContinental. The lobby was elegant without feeling overly formal, and check-in was quick, friendly, and well organized. My room was spacious, quiet, and exceptionally clean, with a comfortable bed and a great view of the city from the higher floor. I especially appreciated the thoughtful touches, including plenty of outlets, good water pressure, and a coffee machine that was easy to use. Breakfast had a generous selection, from fresh fruit and pastries to hot local dishes, although it became busy around 9 a.m. The staff throughout the hotel were consistently professional and genuinely helpful, particularly when arranging a late taxi. Prices are not the lowest, but the service, location, and overall comfort made the stay feel worthwhile. I would gladly return.

We spent a week in this hotel and were very pleased with the experience. As described in previous reviews. the room was very comfortable with the huge televison and bathroom being particularly outstanding. Service was excellent overall (I especially liked the bottle of water at my bedside with the turn down service). The door and bellmen/women were particularly pleasant and helpful and the concierge was friendly and knowledgeable. We had completely satisfactory (though overpriced) drinks in the bar but didn't eat at the restaurant. The health club was fine and the equipment was well maintained. While there were only three treadmills and two elipitical steppers, I never had to wait for a machine although it might be a different story in the dead of a Chicago winter! One minor quibble--I like to have coffee first thing in the morning and there was no in-room coffee maker. The restaurant offered free coffee 'to-go' but only before eight AM. This is a very, very comfortable, attractive hotel in a wonderful location. Chicago is an expensive city but we felt that we got a reasonable value for our money.
Two nights at the Hotel Talbott simply flew by. Spotless room, an immaculate bathroom with great water pressure, and staff who anticipated our needs. Would happily have stayed longer.

My wife and I stayed here in the middle of February 2005. We took the (EL) subway to the hotel from O'Hare. It was very convenient. The lobby was nice and the room was clean and comfortable. I've stayed in many a hotel room, this bed was the most comfortable I've ever slept in. The hotel is located in a great area and close to everything. Walking distance to almost all the interesting sites Chicago has. Would definetly recommend this hotel to anyone visiting this great city.

We were encouraged to stay at the Affinia as part of a group in town for a Chicago wedding. We booked our rooms 6 months in advance, with the promise of a brand-new, full service hotel in a great locaiton in Chicago. The lobby was non-existant (under construction). The front desk staff was incredibly rude and unhelpful. The hallways and elevators are small, cramped and uncomfortable. The rooms are great - great beds, great television set. NO ROOM SERVICE - the kitchen is under construction. The bottom line is that during our stay, this was NOT a full-service hotel and should not have charged what they did. We were totally disappointed, hope it will improve, but vow to never stay there and will recommend to anyone to check out one of Chicago's truly amazing hotels. It is not worth the risk with this unproven dress rehearsal.

My wife and I spent several nights here on a getaway excursion. I didn't choose it -- Priceline gave it to me for $70. If I'd paid the book rate, $175, I'd have been less pleased. No troubles with checkin. Very small room but bed was clean and comfortable. Starbucks in the lobby was a godsend. I'd read horror stories about the staff but they seemed friendly enough. For $70, it's a steal. For its online face value, not so much. Will definitely return if can get similar price.

My husband and I decided to take a trip to Chicago at the last minute and quickly chose the Conrad, not really knowing it's location. We were pleasantly surprised to find it was almost right on Michigan Ave. (It's connect to Nordstroms right in the heart of downtown. ) Great for shopping. The hotel itself was fabulous. The staff was extremely helpful in giving suggestions for shows and restaurants. I recommend going to Joe's that's right across the street from the hotel. Everyone was raving about it . . .but we couldn't get a reservation. The room was wonderful and the bed and pillows were very comfortable. It had a very warm and inviting atmosphere. My husband loved the workout room. I highly recommend the Conrad!!

To start with, this hotel had the worst customer service. They were impossible to work with on EVERYTHING! Now, the problems we had in chronological order. First, we arrive at 8 PM Sat. to check in. They did not have the room with 2 beds we had reserved available, so they offered us a room with one bed and a rollaway (free of charge). However, the room was not ready yet. Finally at 10.30! (2.5 hrs later) we were able to get our room keys. But, there was no rollaway. Another 30 mins and 3 phone calls later, we had a rollaway, but had to get the charge waived a second time. Now we go to check out on Mon. and they couldn't print us a bill or give us a total. We stop 3 hrs down the road to get gas only to find out that our bank card had been overdrawn $2,127.00! We called the bank and found out the hotel had ran our card through 3 TIMES, for $709 each, when our bill was supposed to be $450. After sitting at the gas station on the phone for 1.5hrs, the money was finally put back in our account so we could continue our trip home. I would recommend a Holiday Inn over the Intercontinental any day.

We booked the Conrad specifically for a luxurious weekend away, and I'm genuinely baffled by the hype. The check-in process was painfully slow, and when we finally got to our room, the air conditioning was louder than a lawnmower. We reported it twice, but it was never fixed, just shrugged off. The 'city view' we paid extra for was mostly a brick wall and a sliver of the adjacent rooftop's ugly ventilation units. The bathroom felt dated, with grout that looked like it had seen better decades. Honestly, the only saving grace was the breakfast buffet, which was decent. But for this price point, I expect better than a moody staff member who rolled their eyes when we asked for extra towels. It felt less like a five-star hotel and more like an overpriced conference center. I won't be back.
Really pleasant stay at the Homewood. The room was spacious and spotless, and the free breakfast actually had decent variety. Front desk staff were friendly. Would gladly come back on my next trip.

The Good - excellent location, neighborhood is pretty and quiet, close to shops, restaurants, the waterfront, close to train/subway station, etc The Bad - Very old decor, which isn't a big deal, but the tv was smaller than my PC monitor. We were supposed to have a king bed (anniversary trip) we were given two double beds and told we would be switched - that never happened. The shower/tub was stopped up so bad that after I showered my husband waited over one hour for the tub to drain before he could shower. Who wants to shower in someone else's dirty water even if it is your wife. The indifferent - room was a decent size, bed linens were okay, staff was mediocre to marginally rude
Our room overlooked the city skyline, and the central location made sightseeing easy. The decor felt fresh, and the quiet bed and blackout curtains helped me sleep wonderfully.
The Talbott's location is convenient, but the room felt tired and poorly maintained, with thin walls and a shower that never got properly hot. For the price, I expected much more.

The historic feel of the hotel really had a strong influence on my choice to book this hotel. Unfortunately, the ambiance of the hotel could not make up for the rest of its shortcomings. The front desk staff was rude, the doormen were usually busy chatting or playing on their cell phones instead of greeting us or opening the door. There are three elevators but good luck with them all working. They are very very small and when only one is up and running...you end up waiting a long time for one. Not fun when you are on the 12th floor. The room was TINY and the air conditioning did not work at all...the room felt damp and miserable. We put the thermostat as low as it would let us (65) and the room never went below 78. (and it was 107 outside the whole trip!!!). There really are no amenities inside the hotel other than an ice machine and a slightly overpriced restaurant. Internet is not free either... Overall, I would never stay here again.

I expected more from a hotel with this reputation, but the stay felt overpriced and oddly impersonal. Check-in took nearly 30 minutes even though there was no obvious crowd, and the room looked tired: scuffed furniture, a stained chair, and a bathroom fan that rattled all night. Street noise was much louder than advertised, so sleep was difficult despite being on a higher floor. The thermostat barely responded, leaving the room uncomfortably warm. Staff were polite when I finally reached someone, but requests for extra towels and a late housekeeping visit were forgotten. The location is convenient, and the lobby is attractive, but that did not make up for the lack of comfort and attention. For the rate, I expected a much smoother experience.
Had a lovely stay at Sofitel--the room was stylish and quiet, the bed incredibly comfortable, and the staff genuinely welcoming. Breakfast was excellent too, making the whole visit feel effortless.

Our three-night stay at the Sheraton flew by far too quickly--the kind of visit where you find yourself lingering over coffee in the lobby just to soak up the atmosphere a little longer. The front desk team was genuinely warm, remembering our names by day two and offering a fantastic local bakery tip that became our morning ritual. We booked a high-floor room with a skyline view, and watching the city lights flicker on each evening felt like a private show. Given the plush bedding, spotless bathroom, and the surprisingly robust breakfast buffet, I'd say the rate was absolutely fair for what you get. I honestly wouldn't change a thing, except maybe steal one more night on that balcony.

Stayed in a Junior Suite which was beautiful and spacious. It had the largest flat screen tv I have ever seen in a hotel (great excuse to catch up on some movies) The breakfast buffet was great and was served in the hotels huge atrium which was nice. The service was top notch. Stayed in a lower floor in the East tower which was great as there was no waits for an elevator and they were always empty. The Shed aquarium was a complete waste of time and money but the Field musium was amazing. Chicago remains tied with London as my favourite city.

We got a spanking deal at this hotel for $99 a night. It's in a good location to the Loop. Excellent transportation options abound. My gripe comes from the fact that we were obviously put in a 'crappy' room. It overlooked the back of the building and the roof of a building next to us. The toilet in the room was not bolted to the floor. Other than that, if I needed to stay in the Loop again for something and I knew I wasn't going to be put in a undesirable room, I would stay here again.

I've stayed at plenty of Sheratons over the years and usually know what to expect, but this visit was a real letdown. The check-in process took nearly 30 minutes because only one person was at the front desk, and when we finally got our keys, the room smelled musty--like the AC filter hadn't been changed in months. The bed was comfortable enough, but the pillows were flat and lumpy. Housekeeping never came by during our two-night stay, even after we hung the 'service please' sign. Breakfast was chaotic, with empty buffet trays and coffee that tasted burnt. On top of that, the pool had a weird green tint and was closed for 'maintenance' without prior notice. For the price we paid, I expected better. The staff were polite but seemed overwhelmed, which made everything feel disorganized. I'd probably look elsewhere next time.

Stayed for three nights to celebrate an anniversary, and honestly, they made it feel special without being fussy. The room was spotless with a ridiculously comfortable bed. I loved that the blackout curtains actually worked--slept past nine, which never happens. The pool area gets busy by late morning, so go early. Breakfast had a great mix of local and western options; the made-to-order omelet was a hit. Staff were attentive but not hovering. The location is perfect for walking to the old city, and the concierge gave us a fantastic, less-crowded route to the market. Only tiny gripe: the elevator wait during checkout was a bit long. Otherwise, a genuinely relaxing stay. Worth the splurge.
Thin walls meant I heard every hallway conversation til 2am, and the 'suite' felt tired and musty. Front desk was polite but slow. For the price, I expected way more. Not staying here again.

The Palmer completely exceeded expectations for a city stay. Our room was spotless, the bed was incredibly comfortable, and the staff went out of their way to make us feel welcome. I'd happily book here again.

We stayed at the Fairmont two nights for the SOFA art fair at the Navy Pier. I was impressed that the bellman called us by name when he met the taxi and pronounced it correctly, which is quite unusual. Everyone smiled and welcomed us. The lobby looks clean and friendly, not ultramodern, but not at all tired or worn. Our room, also clean and comfortably furnished, was larger than we expected, with a clean, modern bath and a lovely view of the Navy Pier and the lake. We did not eat at the restaurant, but it looked attractive. Our only problem was that we had asked for non-feather pillows, upon reserving the room, upon checking in, and calling housekeeping. After waiting an hour, we went to bed. The next day the check-in desk person was extremely apologetic and by the time we returned, all the feathers were replaced with foam and non-allergenic materials. The hotel is convenient to Millenium Park and Michigan Ave. We would stay there again, assuming we could get good rates.
Lovely stay at the Allegro--the breakfast spread was fresh and generous, wifi never let me down once, and honestly the whole visit felt too short. Great value for what we paid. Would happily return!

We booked directly with the Intercontinental--a special room for our wedding night. After our wedding, we went to the Hotel excited and happy. When we got there, the night changed. We were treated rudely and with no respect. They told us there was 'no room' even though we had a confirmation number. Instead of showing any empathy, they told us to go sit down while they figured out 'what to do with us'. My husband was in his tux and I was in my wedding gown! No apology! No concern! We were given $20 and told to go find a cab and take it to a hotel where they'd 'found' a room. The Intercontinental RUINED our wedding night. We are telling anyone and everyone of our experience. This place was supposed to be elegant. We've never been treated so poorly. We will never stay in another Intercontinental Hotel and highly recommend you do not contribute to a place that would do this to a newly married couple!!! STEER clear of this place.

My family and I have just had a two week holiday in Chicago, and we stayed for a week at the Hilton Towers. We had a fantastic time and enjoyed every minute of our stay at this incredible hotel. The sheer size of the place is breathtaking and the atmosphere is very friendly and hospitable. If you prefer discreet modern boutiquey-type hotels, maybe this wouldn't be your thing. However if you enjoy old style glamour and glitz, you will be bowled over by this hotel. The place literally sparkles thanks to the enormous chandeliers that are everywhere in the lobby. Tons of celebs have stayed here over the decades and the history of the hotel and past guests etc is fascinating. We got a very reasonable rate for our stay and could not fault anything about this very special place!

Will start by saying the employees were wonderful, especially in the restaurant / bar employees, could not have been nicer.....what appeared to be the hotel manager went above and beyond....Unfortunately, that's where it ends! The rooms, in my opinion, appeared different then pictures and were worn and ratty...you know, uninviting sofa and crappy coffee table and desk area... the first room I was given had bright construction lights shining in my room and men working on the next building that were looking directly into my window!!I kid you not; they seemed as if they were about 15-20 ft from my window!! And this was after I specifically had asked for a room that might have a decent view..I was then switched to a room that had virtually no light and was truly, again... just worn out!!!NOT a 4 star hotel, this seemed to be closer to a 2, perhaps being extremely kind 3 star...I travel on business so I know the difference...I merely touched the cabinet door on the bar unit and it literally fell off in my hand! I complained to a very nice woman from housekeeping and to her credit, she made sure the door was fixed ASAP. They gave me a bottle of wine to compensate..which I utilized to dull my senses as to my surroundings for the next 2 days....I wanted to give Omni a shot...big mistake... Unfortunately, brought a friend with me to show her how great Chicago was and I was soooo embarrassed, as I had chosen the hotel...She was extremely disappointed as well...should have gone with my first instinct which was the Conrad!! Lesson learned!

My son & I joined my husband on a work trip. We planned to swim while he was working. We overheard a lady asking when the pool would open as as we were checking in. Though my son was eager to swim as soon as we checked in the pool was still closed at 630 pm. We gave up & went out for the evening. We had a very noisy sleepless night. We weren't facing MI ave, but still heard sirens and I'm not sure what the other noise was, but it sounded like a malfunctioning hand dryer in our ceiling that would sound off about 20x an hour throughout the entire night. I called the front desk the next morning and was told the pool was open, so my (very excited) son got his bathing suit on and we got to the fitness center only to be told by housekeeping that the pool was closed for construction. Upon calling the front desk again the lady claimed she was unaware of the maintenance crew's actions & on my insistence she said she'd look into it. A gentleman called back an hour later & said the pool should open at 5pm...it was 9am. It is now 6pm & we still haven't even seen the pool. We check out tomorrow. We passed up time with grandparents who are in for the holiday to 'swim in Chicago.' Needless to say we are VERY disappointed.

The staff seemed bothered by every request, and the lobby's peeling wallpaper made the whole place feel stuck in the 80s. Our bathroom had a grimy shower curtain, and honestly, our two-night booking felt about a day too long.

I expected more from the Ambassador given the rate and its reputation. The lobby has a few attractive details, but the overall decor felt tired, with worn carpeting and dark furniture that made the room seem smaller than it was. Our window faced a narrow alley and the air-conditioning units, so there was little natural light and certainly no pleasant view. At check-in, the staff seemed distracted; requests for extra towels and a restaurant recommendation were handled slowly and without much interest. The bathroom was the biggest disappointment: cramped, poorly ventilated, and showing mildew around the tub caulking. The shower pressure was weak, and the sink drained very slowly. The location was convenient, but it did not make up for an uncomfortable, underwhelming stay.

We loved our stay at the Talbott. The location is just perfect for exploring the Magnificent Mile, but what really sold us was the old-school charm--the lobby feels like stepping back into a more elegant era, without being stuffy. Our room was on the smaller side, but it was spotless and the bed was ridiculously comfortable after long walking days. The staff at the front desk were genuinely warm, remembered our names, and gave fantastic dinner recommendations. The complimentary coffee in the morning was a nice touch, though I wish the hours were a bit longer. The bathroom was tight, but the rainfall shower pressure was great. It's not a flashy modern high-rise, but if you appreciate polished, boutique-style service and a classic Chicago vibe, book here. We'd absolutely return.

Having had a great stay at the Monaco last Fall with friends, I was disappointed (initially) to arrive on Saturday with husband and find that they didn't have our Quikbook made reservation in their system and they had no rooms available for Sat. eve. BUT they immediately took responsibility for their mistake by doing the following: found us a nice room at the neighboring Swissotel and paid for it! Gave us cab fare to get the 4 blocks over there. Paid for our valet parking $33 that eve. So naturally when they asked if we were interested in returning for Sunday eve (when they did have room), we said yes. When we returned, they gave us a corner suite with jacuzzi tub for our $139 quikbook rate! Now that's what I call a recovery!!

Stayed here for a conference and left feeling genuinely let down. The lobby looks grand in photos, but the reality is worn carpets and a front desk that seemed perpetually understaffed. Check-in took over half an hour, and when we finally got to the room, the air conditioning sounded like a lawnmower and never actually cooled the space below 78 degrees. I asked for a fix twice; maintenance eventually showed up, shrugged, and said it was 'normal for summer.' The bathroom had a cracked sink basin and only two towels for a double-occupancy reservation. The rooftop bar, which we were excited about, was closed for a private event both nights--no advance notice, no comp. Breakfast was a chaotic, overpriced buffet with lukewarm eggs and stale pastries. Honestly, for this price point, you're paying for the address, not the experience. I'd skip it and book somewhere with actual service.

The bed was advertised as plush, but it felt like a lumpy sack of potatoes, and I woke up every hour with a stiff back. The whole place has a sad, early-2000s vibe, with worn carpet in the hallways and furniture that looks like it survived a frat party. At nearly two hundred a night, I expected better; this felt more like a budget motel with a fancy lobby. Our window faced the parking garage and a dumpster, so we kept the curtains shut the entire time. The noise from the HVAC unit rattled all night, too. Honestly, the only positive was the front desk clerk, who was friendly but couldn't fix the fundamental issues. I left more exhausted than when I arrived, and I definitely won't be back. Save your money.

I had a very pleasant stay at the Hyatt and felt it offered good value for the price, especially given the central location and comfortable facilities. The lobby and room decor felt fresh and modern without being overly trendy, with thoughtful lighting, a comfortable bed, and a spotless bathroom. Every staff member I encountered was welcoming and professional, from check-in to the breakfast team, and they handled a small room request quickly and cheerfully. My room faced the city, with a wide view of the skyline and plenty of light during the day; it was especially attractive after sunset when the buildings lit up. The hotel was quiet at night despite its busy surroundings. I would gladly stay here again and would recommend it for both business and leisure trips.

The Hotel Monaco exceeded expectations in nearly every way. Breakfast was a highlight--the made-to-order omelets were fluffy, and their fresh pastries paired perfectly with strong coffee. Given the prime location and thoughtful touches like the evening wine reception, it absolutely felt worth the splurge. My only regret is that I booked just two nights; I could have easily spent four, unwinding in the cozy yet stylish room. The view over the historic district was charming, especially at dusk when the streetlights flickered on, though rooms facing the courtyard are quieter if you're a light sleeper. Staff were genuinely warm, offering great local dining tips without being pushy. I left refreshed and already planning a return--just a bit longer next time.

My sister and I went to Chicago for a weekend and decided to stay at this hotel because I have a friend who works at Homewood Suites here in Cleveland so we got a discount. The valets were really friendly, you get in and out service when you pay for parking with the hotel. Check-in is on the 6th floor because there are restaurants beneath the hotel at street level. That also made finding the hotel tricky because I expected a groove to pull into and it turned out that I just had to pull over to the right side of the street. The lady at the front desk was friendly and informative. Our room was very clean. The fact that it is an extented stay hotel was nice when it came to bringing home leftovers from restaurants, storing and reheating food. The complimentary breakfast was great! They have real food such as eggs, bacon, french toast, cereal, bagels, juice, milk, and yogurt. The hotel is in walking distance from everything and there is a trolley that goes to Navy Pier and passes by Michigan Avenue. They also have free WiFi. Overall, I would definately stay here again and I would recommend it to others.

I stayed at Affinia for a long weekend and came away pleasantly surprised by how comfortable it felt for a city hotel. My room was quiet, especially at night, with a good-sized sitting area, a useful desk, and a kitchenette that made morning coffee and snacks much easier. The bed was excellent and the housekeeping staff kept everything spotless without being intrusive. Front desk staff were friendly when I arrived early and held my bags until the room was ready, then pointed me toward a couple of nearby restaurants that turned out to be great choices. The location made getting around simple, whether I was walking to meetings or hopping in a cab. The decor is a little dated in spots, but it was warm, clean, and well maintained. I'd happily stay again.

The Affinia left me genuinely puzzled. The location was undeniably its only saving grace--steps from the El and a short cab ride to the Loop made sightseeing easy. Inside, though, the decor felt frozen in the mid-2000s, with tired floral patterns on the bedding and a hallway carpet that had seen better decades. My bathroom was the low point: the showerhead had only two settings (dribble or scalding blast), and the grout looked like it hadn't seen a scrub brush in months. The staff were polite but perpetually overstretched; the front desk gave clipped answers to my questions about dining, and housekeeping knocked at 8:30 AM despite my 'Do Not Disturb' sign. For what they charge, I expected polish, not this faded, disengaged experience. I won't be back.

We booked the Knickerbocker expecting old-world charm, but the reality fell far short. Our one-night anniversary stay felt painfully long, largely because the air conditioning clanked all night and the walls were thin enough to hear every hallway conversation. Breakfast was a rushed, lukewarm buffet of powdered eggs and stale pastries, with coffee that tasted burnt. Staff seemed indifferent; the front desk barely acknowledged our early check-in request and the valet was gruff when we asked for directions. The location near the Magnificent Mile was convenient for shopping, but that's the only saving grace. For the price, we expected so much more--genuine hospitality, a quiet room, and a meal worth waking up for. Instead, we left exhausted and relieved to be gone, vowing never to return.
Great location, but the room felt worn and oddly cramped for the price. We also waited forever for towels, and the front desk seemed uninterested.

I'll admit I booked the James mostly for its address, but the stay itself turned out to be the highlight of my trip. The room wasn't huge, but it was spotless--fresh linens, no stray hairs in the bathroom, and the walk-in shower had excellent water pressure. What really stood out was the staff: from the front desk who remembered my name to the concierge who circled three under-the-radar restaurants on a map, everyone seemed genuinely happy to help. Location-wise, you're steps from the river and a short stroll to Michigan Avenue, yet the street itself felt calm at night. I slept better than I have in months. Minor quibble: the hallway ice machine was out on my floor, but that's hardly a dealbreaker. I'd return in a heartbeat, and I've already recommended it to two coworkers.

I had high hopes for the Conrad, but honestly, the experience left me frustrated. The bathroom was the first letdown--a single, shallow sink that splashed water everywhere and a showerhead with only two settings, one of which dribbled. The room itself wasn't truly dirty, but there were dust bunnies under the desk and a suspicious stain on the armchair I didn't want to examine closely. Staff were polite at check-in but completely dismissive when I asked for extra towels, telling me to call housekeeping myself; when I did, no one ever answered. Despite the 'city view' promise, I heard constant hallway chatter, slamming doors, and what sounded like furniture being dragged upstairs until nearly 2 AM. For these rates, I expected polish and attention--instead I got a mediocre stay that felt more like a mid-tier business hotel. I won't be returning.

Booked a deluxe room expecting the Swissotel standard, but this felt like a tired, overpriced version of it. Check-in was painfully slow--one person at the front desk for a line of fifteen. Our room had a lingering smell of damp carpet, and the 'city view' was basically a brick wall and a sliver of rooftops. The AC rattled all night, kept cutting out, and the thin walls meant we heard every door slam and hallway conversation. Breakfast was chaos: cold scrambled eggs, empty coffee carafes, and staff who looked annoyed when we asked for a refill. The pool area was packed and the water was lukewarm, not refreshing. To their credit, the bed was comfortable and the shower pressure was decent. But for the price, I've had better stays at a three-star. Maybe it's just getting run down, but I won't be back.

This place is a dump. I booked on Priceline, because the last time I booked a Priceline hotel in Chicago, I got the Westin and loved it. Despite having paid for Priceline, I ate the money I had already spent and called for a reservation at the Westin and went there for the weekend, instead. I didn't regret it for a second. You will be disappointed if you stay at the Millenium Knickerbocker because you are paying for a Holiday Inn at the price of a Westin when you could have the real deal for just a little more. The location is not worth the place being old and so unimpressive. There are enough hotels near the loop (and near a train/bus stop if you need to move around the city inexpensively) that you should not spend the money on the Millenium. Do not waste your time and stay here--this is a trap because of its location, but it's not worth it. Really.

The Chicago Hyatt Regency deceptively alters the cancellation policy by charging the full room rate upon cancellation--ie the room cannot be cancelled. I recently booked over the phone a one night stay directly with the hotel. The reservation specialist mentioned over the phone there was a 72-hour cancellation policy.
