However, when I tried to cancel the reservation within that timeframe, Robert, the reservation supervisor, said that the room could not be cancelled at any time without charging full price for the room. He said that I should refer to the confirmation e-mail that states at the bottom that prepayment is required at time of booking / non-refunable. This clearly was not what was agreed to over the phone. I told him to cancel without being charged. In response, he threatened to cancel and charge me for the full stay. Why would someone cancel if they are going to be charged full price? The bottom line is the hotel deceptively changed the terms of the agreement, and Robert should go back to customer service school!

My stay at the Sheraton was much more disappointing than expected. The lobby looked polished, but the room felt tired, with scuffed furniture, stained carpet, and a bathroom that clearly needed better maintenance. Check-in took nearly 25 minutes even though there was hardly anyone waiting, and the front desk staff seemed more distracted than welcoming. The bed was comfortable enough, but the air conditioner rattled throughout the night and the walls were so thin that I could hear conversations and doors slamming in the hallway. Breakfast was overpriced for lukewarm food and slow service. I also had to call twice before extra towels arrived. This may once have been a reliable business hotel, but the property currently feels neglected and not worth the rate.

I left Hotel Allegro feeling let down, especially for the rate. The room looked as though it had only been quickly checked: dust sat along the desk edge, there were marks on the mirror, and the carpet had a sticky patch near the bed. The bathroom was cramped and dated, with weak water pressure, a loose shower fixture, and mildew around the tub caulking. Our window faced an alley and a row of service vents, so there was no real view and plenty of early-morning noise. Staff at the desk were curt when I mentioned the cleanliness issues and offered no solution beyond saying housekeeping was busy. The location is convenient, but the room and service did not justify the price.

I wanted to like the hotel james because the location is convenient and the lobby looks stylish, but the stay was frustrating from check-in onward. Our room wasn't ready at the promised time, and nobody offered an apology or even an update until I asked twice. The room itself felt tired: stained carpeting, a flickering bedside lamp, and a shower that took several minutes to get warm. Street noise came through the windows all night, so sleep was not great. Housekeeping also skipped our room despite the sign being removed early in the morning. For the rate we paid, I expected cleaner facilities and more attentive service. It may work for a quick overnight stay, but I wouldn't choose it again.

We connected to Affinia Chicago thorugh a city websight. The deal was fair for a downtown hotel on the main drag with an attractiion included. There was information out there that the hotel was being overhauled although we did not pay much attention to that. They are currently under major construction. They will be a little late of their projections in the finish date. I must say that the staff tried very hard to make our stay comfortable under very difficult circumstances. The room was complete and was good. It had a very nice bathroom. The main lobbie and all hotel amenities are totally unfinished drywall with no food, drink, or rest room opportunities. The construction guys did their best to limit activity and noise to after 9:00am. I think this will be a good one once they are done. As of the end of May, they have a way yet to go.

Checked in around 4pm and the front desk agent barely looked up from her screen, handing over the key card without a single question about our stay. The room itself was a letdown--dust bunnies in the corners, a sticky spot on the nightstand, and the bathroom mirror had smudges that looked like they hadn't been wiped in days. Breakfast the next morning was borderline sad: lukewarm scrambled eggs, stale pastries, and coffee that tasted burnt, all served in a dining area that felt cramped and grimy. The decor throughout felt trapped in the early 2000s--beige carpets, dated floral patterns, and worn furniture that desperately needed replacing. Even the hallway smelled faintly of old carpet cleaner. For the price we paid, I expected far more polish and attention. Disappointing overall, and I'm honestly not sure I'd return even if the location is convenient.

The room was grimy, with sticky spots on the floor, and the thin walls meant constant hallway noise. The Wi-Fi dropped every few minutes, making work impossible, and I barely slept on the lumpy mattress. Waste of money.

Ok, so first trip to chicago and I was a litlle worried about the hotel and the location, finally I decided on the CONRAD and wath a good experience i had, I booked a king deluxe room on the 6th floor, view was not amazing but that was the only coplaint i could had, room is nice, bath was all appliances and good size, good plasma tv, free internet, we asked one day for breaksfast and amazing food! so overall and for the price aroufn 220 It was a great surprise, the locating was very good a few blocks from everything and very quiet hotel

We brought our giant rottweiler and she had a great time. Small rooms, but this is normal for the chicago hotel scene. Lots of interesting amenities in the room. Convenient to theatres and downtown restaurants and shopping. Really loved the lobby -- a great place to hang around or wait for someone. Lots of nooks and crannies and little tables and sofas everywhere. Watch out: The concierge (like all concierges at big hotels) will direct you to mediocre, large restaurants where they get kickbacks. We have stayed here several times and I always check for rooms here when I travel to Chicago. However, the hotel is often full so book early.

From the moment we pulled up, the doorman's warm greeting set the tone. Check-in was swift, and the room--a Prestige suite--was absolutely spotless. The bed felt like a cloud, and the blackout curtains worked wonders for jet lag. We grabbed cocktails at the bar each evening; the mixologist actually remembered our order on the second night, which was a lovely touch. Breakfast had plenty of variety, though the coffee could be stronger. The only hiccup was a slightly noisy AC unit that hummed all night, but honestly, it faded into background noise. Location-wise, you're steps from the river and a short stroll to the Louvre. Staff went out of their way to print our museum tickets and even recommended a hidden bistro that became our favorite meal of the trip. If you want understated luxury without any snobbery, this is it. We're already eyeing a return visit in the fall.

We booked the Affinia at a reasonable rate, and frankly, it felt like a steal for what we got. The bathroom was a pleasant surprise--spacious, with excellent water pressure and plenty of fluffy towels, plus a nice rainfall showerhead that made mornings feel luxurious. The wifi was solid the entire stay, no dropped calls during a video conference from the room, which is always a gamble. My only minor caveat is that we could hear hallway chatter now and then, but the room itself was quiet enough, and the bed was so comfortable that I slept like a log anyway. For the location and amenities, I'd absolutely choose this place again. A genuinely smooth, hassle-free experience that exceeded expectations without breaking the bank.
Our stay felt too short to recover from the high price, especially with the dated decor. The room was clean, but the overall experience didn't feel worth what we paid.
My room had a pleasant city view, and the Affinia's central location made exploring easy. The decor felt fresh and inviting, while the quiet room and comfortable bed made for excellent sleep.
Hotel Palmer looked promising, but the room smelled stale, the walls were thin, and the front desk barely acknowledged us. Not worth the price for such an uncomfortable stay.

I called the reservations line to book a room at the beginning of December 2012 for a rate with a local corporation. When I first made the reservation I did not get an e-mail confirmation. I had to call again to get the e-mail and then saw that I was booked in a handicapped accessible room which i did not need as there was me, my wife and three year old. I called the reservation line and asked for a regular room which they said was impossible at the rate I was at, however for ten dollars more I can upgrade to a regular room. I then asked what if a disabled person needs the room and he said he could not help me. i told them to cancel the room. based on the reservation experience, I did not want to run into anymore trouble at this hotel.

We stayed at the Swissotel for a special birthday weekend for my wife from Aug 25 to 29. I had called ahead to ask for a nice room and to order flowers for my wife. Jaymes Ballard, the Concierge, made arrange for flowers, early check-in and we had a great room. Our room was the 33rd floor with a view facing the city. Room was large, everything looked like new, great bed, large bathroom with separate shower, great ammenities. A beautiful bouquet of flowers arrived upon our arrival. The hotel is about 10 mins from everything, not close but not far from anything. Has a great restaurant, 2 patios outside where I had a cigar. A really nice pool and hot tub on the 42nd floor. I would recommend this hotel to anyone and thanks to Jaymes for making our trip very special.
Disappointing stay at the Sheraton: the room felt worn, the AC rattled all night, and staff seemed uninterested when I mentioned it at checkout.

I wanted to love the Fairmont given its reputation, but our stay fell flat in nearly every way. We paid a premium for a 'city view' room, and what we got was mostly a glimpse of a rooftop ventilation system and an unobstructed look at the neighboring building's wall--maybe ten percent sky if we pressed our faces to the corner of the window. The neighbors weren't the problem, though; the hallway was. Housekeeping started their carts rattling past our door at 6:40 each morning, and the walls seemed to conduct every conversation next door. For this rate, I expected genuine care from the staff, but requests for extra towels took hours, and my question about late checkout was answered with a shrug and a flat 'that'll be a fee.' Dollars to donuts, this is not the luxury experience the price promises. We won't be back.

We booked the Hilton expecting more from the name. The hallways smelled musty, our room's AC rattled all night, and housekeeping ignored our request for extra towels twice. Overpriced for what felt like a dated, understaffed experience.

I expected more from the Knickerbocker given the price and location. Our room faced a neighboring office building, so the 'city view' amounted to windows and construction scaffolding rather than anything memorable. The room itself looked tired, with dust along the baseboards, a sticky spot on the desk, and hair in the bathroom sink when we arrived. Staff at check-in were polite but distracted, and requests for extra towels took nearly an hour. The stay also felt oddly long for just two nights because every small issue required follow-up. The bed was comfortable, but that was about the only real positive. For a hotel positioned as upscale, the service and cleanliness were disappointing.

Stayed at Hotel Amalfi for four nights and honestly couldn't have asked for a better base. The location is perfect--close enough to walk to the main sights but tucked away on a quiet street, so you actually get decent sleep. Our room faced the courtyard, which was a lovely bonus; you could hear the fountain at night, which was surprisingly calming. The staff were the real highlight, though. Every single person we interacted with, from the front desk to the breakfast team, was genuinely warm and helpful without being overbearing. They pointed us to a tiny trattoria two blocks away that ended up being our favorite meal of the trip. Breakfast was simple but fresh--good coffee, pastries, eggs made to order. The room itself was clean and comfortable, maybe a bit dated in the bathroom, but spotless and the bed was fantastic. Would happily return.

I wanted to like the Talbott, but the stay was more disappointing than expected. The room looked tired, with scuffed furniture and a bathroom that could have used a deeper cleaning. Wi-Fi was technically available, but it repeatedly dropped during video calls and was painfully slow in the evening. My window faced an alley and a brick wall, so the 'view' was essentially a reminder to keep the curtains closed. Sleep was also difficult: the mattress was lumpy, the pillows were flat, and hallway noise continued well past midnight. The staff were polite enough at check-in, but not especially welcoming, and my request for extra towels took two calls and nearly an hour. For the price, I expected a much more comfortable and attentive experience.

The Fairmont exceeded my expectations in nearly every way. I slept like a log in the incredibly plush bed, with blackout curtains that made the morning feel like midnight until I chose to rise. The bathroom was a marble sanctuary, complete with a rainfall shower that had fantastic pressure and Le Labo toiletries that felt like a real treat. Breakfast in the main restaurant was a highlight--the made-to-order omelets were fluffy and perfect, and the fresh pastries were still warm. While it's undeniably pricey, the level of service, the spotless room, and that serene night's sleep made me feel like I genuinely got what I paid for. I'd happily book again for a special occasion.

I expected much more from Sofitel given the rate and reputation. The lobby looks elegant, but the experience quickly fell apart. Check-in took nearly 30 minutes because the room was apparently not ready, despite arriving well after the stated check-in time. When we finally got in, the air conditioning barely worked and the bathroom had a lingering drain smell. I called reception twice and no one followed up until the next morning. The bed was comfortable, but noise from the corridor and neighboring room made sleep difficult. Breakfast was crowded, with empty trays and slow coffee service. Staff were polite when approached, yet everything felt understaffed and disorganized. For the price, this was very disappointing.

We went to Chicago to see an exhibit at the Art Institute and selected the Fairmont because it was so close. Although the lobby is still being renovated, our experience at the hotel was uniformly positive. The room was nicely sized and newly remodeled and immaculate. The only glitch involved getting the room coffee replenished. The maid does not do that, and by bedtime on the first night, we still didn't have coffee. We called the front desk and they immediately delivered a fresh supply. The restaurant is a little underwhelming, but with so many other places to go within a very few blocks, we probably wouldn't have eaten there any more than we did. After having stayed in close to a dozen different Chicago hotels, this may be the hotel we return to whenever we return.
Great location for walking downtown, and the front desk handled our late arrival without any fuss. Room was quiet, clean, and surprisingly roomy; breakfast staff were especially kind.

The staff recognizes you by name with excellent eye contact. The 'welcome back' sets the tone for your stay. Flowers in the lobby and reception area beautiful. The house-keeping staff is terrific, helpful and prompt. Room service food was served hot and that makes a big difference too. Pump Room food was surprising tasty and impressed my clients. Well done!

I booked the Hyatt expecting the usual level of polish, but left genuinely frustrated. Our room faced a construction site, so the 'city view' was mostly a crane and a lot of dust. The noise was relentless--jackhammering started before 7 AM, and the thin windows did nothing to muffle it. I barely slept; by the second night, I was counting the hours until checkout, and honestly, the three nights felt like a week. The hallways weren't much better, with slamming doors echoing until midnight. I'll give credit to the front desk clerk who moved us to a higher floor, but it still didn't help. The bed itself was decent, but that's about all. For the price, I expected far more. I won't be back.

Stayed there three nights from 4/17/09 through 4/20/09. Chechecked in about 9:15 AM. Had to wait about 15 minutes because of specials requests I had made. Room was quiet, and comfortable. Marked improvement over last time I stayed there (about 5 years ago). The renovations were great, and maintained the old time charm of the hotel.

Despite the prime location, this Sofitel felt like a costly mistake. The bathroom was dated with a finicky shower, and breakfast was a chaotic, lukewarm buffet. Definitely not worth the premium price for such a tired room.

The room was spotless, and the cloud-soft bed gave me the best sleep in weeks. Breakfast offered everything from fresh pastries to made-to-order omelets, while my window framed a stunning skyline view. Truly a refreshing, worry-free stay.

It's so frustrating when a hotel posts a deal prominently on its website, claiming said deal is available on certain dates. But, when you call to make a reservation based on that deal, they tell you it's not available. There are rooms available, but not the deal. Then they try to condescendingly tell you they can only sell so many rooms at such a deal. I get that. Then just SAY that on the website. 'Here's a great deal . . . but only a small number of people will actually get it.' So much for the great reviews about service . . . I couldn't even get past the first phone call without being frustrated and annoyed. Bad form, Conrad, bad form.

We recently stayed at the hotel allegro in chicago illinois, while the hotel was nice please take my advice and do not stay here. I payed cash for the room and handed over my credit card for incedentals ($50.00) the next day my debit card was charged $200 clearly this had to be a mistake...i called the hotel manager who was the rudest person i have ever spoken with about the charge and was told that it was my fault i paid cash and that i could give him my bank account, routing, SS # and authorization code and he could call my bank and take care of it. Clearly i am smart enough not to give this information to anyone yet alone someone who had already taken more then should have been charged. I then called corporate to complain and let them know about the situation the only thing corporate could tell me is that they had already credited my account and that they were sorry and it was clearly my mistake. I then questioned them about the manager asking for all my information if they had already credited my account and they told me they didnt have an answer for me. So for your bank accounts sake do not stay here they are many other options in chicago
Had a really comfortable stay at the Intercontinental--our room was quiet, the bed was excellent, and everyone at reception was genuinely helpful. The lobby bar was a nice bonus.

I expected far more from Swissotel for the price. Check-in felt cold and rushed, and when I mentioned the noise from the corridor and nearby traffic, the staff simply suggested using earplugs rather than offering another room. Sleep was difficult: doors slammed well past midnight, and the air-conditioning rattled on and off. Breakfast looked extensive, but much of it was lukewarm; the eggs were dry, pastries stale, and tables were not cleared promptly. Coffee took several minutes to arrive despite the restaurant being only moderately busy. The room itself was clean, but the overall atmosphere felt impersonal and poorly managed. It was a disappointing stay, especially for a hotel that presents itself as upscale.

I stayed at the Ambassador for a long weekend and came away pleasantly surprised by how easy everything felt. The front desk team was friendly without being overly formal, and they had us checked in quickly even though we arrived earlier than expected. Our room was quiet, very clean, and had enough space to spread out rather than living out of a suitcase. I especially appreciated the comfortable bed and the strong water pressure in the shower after a full day walking around town. Breakfast was simple but fresh, with good coffee and plenty of options before heading out. The location made it easy to get to restaurants and nearby attractions on foot. A couple of areas show the building's age, but it was well maintained and added some character. I would happily stay here again.
Room smelled like stale smoke and the AC rattled all night. Front desk shrugged when I asked to switch. Paid way too much for a broken shower head and paper-thin walls. Won't be back.

Simply a nice place to stay... I had a great deal for the room, and was impressed with the quality. Hotel staff was very helpful; they were able to let me check out and helped me print boarding passes. Negative: It is frustrating that nowadays you do not have free internet in most hotels and it's the same here; you have to pay for the internet. Negative: Loud on the phone you may hear your neighbors on the phone, or them shower.
Sofitel's central location was convenient, but our brief stay felt longer thanks to a dusty room and curt staff who seemed irritated by every request.
Disappointing stay at Hotel Allegro: my room overlooked a blank wall, the Wi-Fi kept dropping, and even one night felt too long. Definitely not worth the price.

Absolutely gorgeous property with impeccable service from check-in to checkout. The room was spotless and the bed heavenly. We loved the luxurious pool area and the staff's thoughtful touches made our anniversary truly special.

I booked the James for a special weekend, and honestly, it fell flat. The location is decent--you can walk to the river and a few good spots--but that's the only saving grace. Our bathroom was the real letdown: a cracked tile in the shower, lukewarm water pressure that sputtered, and a sink that drained so slowly I had to brush my teeth in the tub. The room itself looked tidy at first, but the carpet had visible stains near the window, and I found a stray hair on the duvet. Staff were polite enough, yet when I mentioned the bathroom issue at the front desk, the response was a shrug and a promise to 'note it' that never materialized. For the price, I expected more polish. It wasn't a disaster--just a list of small disappointments that added up to a stay I won't be repeating.

Stayed here for two days in the first week in January, when hotel was very quiet. Got a big corner room. Staff are friendly, decor is modern, and there's a huge choice of pastries and cakes and breads for breakfast, which you take back to your room. The free hors d'oevres with the drinks are great antipasti - olives, breads, cheeses and meats, marinated vegetables. This was a really easy hotel to stay in, fairly central - a couple of blocks away from the 'L', and quiet, despite the building work opposite. If you're in Chicago, stay here.

WOW!! Where do I start? Booked this hotel through Hotels.com for less than I paid for the Travellodge Downtown. Check in was a breeze, the entire staff was friendly and helpful. Our room was huge. The king bed was very comfortable. Our room also had 2 nightstands, 2 chairs with a small table, a desk, and walk-in closet. Even with all the furniture, the room was very spacious. The room did show some signs of wear, but I think this adds to the charm and the rich history of this hotel. The hotel is located in a neighborhood, so it felt like we were staying in a condo or a home rather than a hotel. There is very little noise, however, you are only about 2 blocks from Rush and Division streets, with all the nightlife, and the Red Line at Clark and Division is only 3 blocks away. We decided to walk to Michigan Ave and the next thing we knew, we were at the Hancock building. By staying here, you are away from the noise, but not away from the action. Had breakfast at the Pump Room, which is a story in itself. We had our photo taken in booth 1. Take some time and research who has sat in this booth. It is impressive. Some 1400 photos of celebrity guests adorn the walls of the Pump Room. Didn't have a chance to have dinner here, but I will return for dinner someday. Breakfast was not anything fancy, and a bit pricy, but the history and experience was worth it in my opinion. The waitstaff was friendly as was everyone who worked at this hotel was. I can't wait to return here!
Swissotel was a really comfortable stay, with a spotless room, helpful staff, and a great city view. The location made getting around easy, and I'd happily come back next time.

My wife and I stayed here for a long weekend and it was great. The check-in staff changed our room to a single bed without question, and the bar served the best martini I have had in a while. The rooms were well decorated and spacious, although it did get a little tight through the bathroom door. The bell staff was very accomodating and walked my wife up to our room when she arrived late. I would definitely stay here again!

Two main issues: (1) understaffed from the street to the front desk. Unfortunately I had to drive into the city, when I arrived there was an excessively long wait for parking. Then inside, there was a huge queue line with just one clerk working in a big city hotel. Not good (I will say friendly however) (2) I know this is a big city, but, $49 a night to park my car when I'm staying at that hotel? Really?? That's unreasonable and a bit gouging in my opinion. Again, I realize this is Chicago, but, I'm already paying a hefty price for this outdated hotel.
Our stay at Conrad felt far too short; the room was spotless, staff were warmly attentive, and the sleek bathroom had a great rain shower and plush towels.

I had a very enjoyable stay at Hotel Allegro for a long weekend. The location made it easy to walk to the theater district, restaurants, and the river, and the front desk staff were friendly without being overbearing. My room faced the street, with a pleasant view of the surrounding downtown buildings and plenty of daylight in the morning. The decor has a colorful, slightly theatrical style that feels intentionally retro rather than worn, and everything was clean and well maintained. WiFi connected quickly and stayed reliable for video calls and streaming. The room itself was comfortable, though the bathroom was a little compact. Three nights went by far too quickly; I easily could have stayed another day or two and would happily book here again.

The bathroom was spotless with excellent water pressure, and the room's double glazing kept the street noise out completely. Wi-Fi never dropped during my video calls, and I slept like a log on the plush bed.

I stayed @ Affinia for one night on a purpose not to drive all the way from NW suburbs to Women's hospital oir my surgery. Few things I really didn't enjoy - I could hear noise from outside all night long as well as inside noise from slamming doors.No noise insulation at all! Very dusty between window frames(I understand - cars,pollution) but it looked like it wasn't cleaned for a very long time.One more thing really made me upset - broken blinds on a right side. I was unable to pull them down to enjoy my sleep time...We didn't notice the problem until very-very late.The Affinia hotel serving tourists and guests of Chicago as well as Northwestern Hospital patients and their families - which really need extra privacy and comfort ! Strange but every hotel I stayed @ was supplied with the SEALED roll of toilet paper.Affinia didn't even offer that.Looked like someone used a bathroom right after it was taking care of by a cleaning lady! Neither toilet paper nor toilet seat were sealed for us to use!!!!!!!!!!!! Hopefully,no more surgeries for me...Won't stay @ this place for leisure - even with discount!

If you're in Chicago and want to stay in The Loop, The Allegro Hotel is perfect for you. It's centrally located, stylish rooms and attentive staff. I stayed at the hotel for 3 nights and was very pleased with everything. The bed was very comfy and had plenty of fluffy pillows, large flat screen tv, radio with ipod docking station and bathroom was hip and clean. Everyone that I came in contact with was very friendly and helpful. My last day there, I ordered room service and not only was my meal perfect and delivered on time, the kitchen called to see if everything was alright. I have never had that kind of follow up service. I've stayed at the Palomar in DC, another Kimpton hotel and received exceptional service there too. I will definitely see if Kimpton has a hotel at my next destination.

The Homewood was a solid pick--clean suite, comfy bed, and the free breakfast actually had decent options. Staff were friendly and quick at check-in, and the location made it easy to grab dinner nearby. Would happily return.
Our weekend at Hotel Amalfi felt too short; I slept deeply in the quiet room, woke to a lovely city view, and found the attentive service well worth the price.
Hotel Palmer looked tired, the room smelled faintly of smoke, and the AC rattled all night. Staff were polite but slow to respond, so the stay felt overpriced and frustrating.

We stayed at the Hard Rock on January 27th, 2009 for $125/night. It is located on Michigan Ave, just two blocks from the Mag Mile, two blocks from Millenium Park, and five blocks from the Chicago Art Institute. Our hotel room was very nice with views of Michigan Ave and a unusually comfy bed. The hotel even offered free coffee in the lobby every morning and free wifi in the rooms. Parking was $45 for valet and $30 for self parking. The staff was very helpful with all of our request.

We stayed at the Omni for a long weekend and were pleasantly surprised by how easy everything felt. The front desk had us checked in quickly, even with a busy lobby, and pointed us toward a great breakfast spot a few blocks away. Our room was quiet, very clean, and larger than expected, with a comfortable sitting area where we could unwind after walking around the city all day. The bed was excellent and the blackout curtains actually kept the morning light out. Housekeeping was attentive without being intrusive. The location made it simple to get to shops, restaurants, and transit on foot. The lobby can get lively in the evening, but it never affected our room. Would happily return.

I booked the Conrad for a work trip and came away genuinely impressed. The staff were the standout--from the doorman remembering my name by day two to the front-desk agent who proactively rebooked my taxi when a meeting ran long. Breakfast was a cut above the usual hotel buffet: the made-to-order omelets were perfect, and the fresh pastries disappeared fast, which tells you everything. My room faced the street, yet I heard next to nothing once the window was shut; even the hallway noise was minimal. The Wi-Fi held up flawlessly through two video calls and a late-night streaming session without a single drop. It's not the flashiest property, but the consistency and care made it a restful, productive stay. I'd happily return.

We had a blast at Hard Rock. The location is killer, right in the middle of everything, and the whole vibe is just fun from the second you walk in--guitars everywhere, music playing in the lobby, you can't help but tap your foot. Check-in was quick, and the lady at the front desk was super friendly, even upgraded us to a higher floor with a nice view. The room itself was clean and modern, with a comfy bed and a cool rock-and-roll theme without feeling cheesy. The pool area was lively but not overcrowded, and the drinks were strong. We ate at the restaurant one night and the burgers were actually really good. Only tiny downside was the hallway noise from other guests, but that's pretty standard for a busy hotel. Overall, a solid, energetic stay and we'd definitely come back.

We booked this hotel as a last minute vacation planned on doing a little shopping and nightlife downtown. We where woken up at 6:00 in the morning with our bathroom flooded, this water was brown and all the clothing and our belongings left in the bathroom were dirty and sopping wet. We where moved to another room, but it was smaller then the orginal room we had gotten and paid for. The next day the housekeeping service never even came to change our sheets, coffee or towels, which is just horrible service. The service along with the orginal room where perfect, but we do not plan on ever spending another weekend in that flooding hotel.

I expected much more from Sofitel, especially given the price and the brand's reputation. The lobby looked polished, but the welcome at reception was oddly cold and check-in took nearly half an hour, despite there being only one guest ahead of me. My room was attractive at first glance, although the carpet had visible stains and the chair by the desk was worn. The air-conditioning made a loud clicking sound throughout the night, and the mattress was far too firm for my liking. Housekeeping also skipped my room on the second day, so I had to call twice for fresh towels. Breakfast was another disappointment: limited choices, lukewarm coffee, and slow service. The location was convenient, but the overall experience felt careless rather than luxurious.

The rooftop bar was the perfect end to our anniversary night, and the staff genuinely cared about us, not just our reservation. Our room was quiet and classically stylish, with a view that made the city feel magical. We're already planning our return trip.

Booked the Allegro expecting a boutique classic; got a box of missed opportunities instead. The lobby is all moody lighting and peeling velvet, which would be charming if the front desk actually acknowledged you. Waited fifteen minutes while two staff argued about a shift swap. Room 812 was a shoebox with a view of a brick wall, the A/C rattled like a dying lawnmower all night, and the 'signature' rain shower dribbled lukewarm water. Housekeeping skipped us entirely one day, and when I called, they said 'we're understaffed, sorry.' The bar downstairs charges $19 for a cocktail that tastes like melted popsicle. Location is the only saving grace--you can walk to the river and theaters--but honestly, for this price, I'd rather sleep in a hostel with better service. Left with a stiff neck and zero interest in returning.
Loved the historic charm and surprisingly quiet room; staff made check-in effortless, and the rooftop views over Times Square were worth lingering over after dinner.

We have been for the first time in Chicago and stayed in the Swissotel for five nights,a wonderful place.Room was on the 29th floor,absolutely clean and nice and a breathtaking lakeview.Breakfast perfect and service really good.People were always helpful.It's a little bit far from Magnificent mile and the loop,but in front of the hotel there are buses (number6)waiting there next turn,not a real bus stop,but drivers are frindly and you can get on the bus.Next time going to Chicago we will again stay in the Swissotel.

My daughter and I woke in the morning wanting to go swimming. When we arrived at the pool the water was covered by a white scum. I then attempted to use both of the phones at the pool, one white phone and one emergency red phone, to call the desk. Both were out of service!!!! I am glad there wasn't an emergency. As we were exited the pool area I ran into a hotel employee and told her about the problems and then asked her to call us when the pool was clean.... never heard back. One more thing, in our room the furniture was mostly child friendly except for a large metal and glass outdated coffee table. Within 30 minutes my 5 year old fell and hit her mouth and began bleeding. They need to update this piece of furniture.

We stayed at the InterContinental for four nights over a long weekend and honestly have very few complaints. Our room on a high floor had a great view of the river, and the bed was probably the most comfortable I've slept in at any hotel -- the pillows alone deserve a mention. Housekeeping kept everything spotless and even remembered our extra coffee request after the first morning. The club lounge was worth the upgrade, with decent snacks in the evening and a quiet place to work. Location is hard to beat too; we walked to most of what we wanted to see. Only minor gripe: the elevator wait could get long around breakfast hours. Front desk called up on our last day to confirm our late checkout without us even asking, which was a nice touch. Would happily return.

I was very disappointed with the hotel this time. They seem to be coming down in quality quite a bit. The clientele also seem to be of a lower quality. The lobby was quite a rambunctious scene with no one on staff seeming to notice. The house keeper only did the bare minimum in the room each day and did not replace the used toiletries or the coffee; she also left the dirty coffee cups in the room. I think I will have to stay with the InterContinental next time.

I stayed at the Hilton Chicago last week and was very disappointed. The highlight of the stay was waiting 20 minutes for a bellman to come and get our luggage. Finally, my 72 year old mother, 8 year old son, and myself gave up and dragged it all down to valet parking ourselves - no easy task. The security guard was kind enough to hold the door for me. The valet parking attendants looked over and then ignored us. As far as I could tell, he was just standing there doing nothing. I couldn't let go of the bags without everything falling so I gave my son the parking receipt. The attendant pointed to where our car was parked - no short distance away. My 8 year old had to tell him to pull it up. They should have been ashamed. Less significant, but irritating issues. The pool is part of the Hilton Athletic club. Two lanes are reserved for adults wanting to lap swim. Basically, two adults can take up 2/3rds of the pool while everyone else is consigned to the leftover 1/3rd. This is ridiculous and very family unfriendly. In addition, the pool closes at 9 p.m. What pool closes at 9? We stayed for 3 nights. Not one single additional bar of soap, bottle of shampoo, or coffee stirrers.

We stayed at the Sheraton over a long weekend and honestly I wish it had been longer. From the moment we arrived, the staff went out of their way to make things easy -- the front desk upgraded us when they could, and the concierge spent twenty minutes marking up a map with restaurant suggestions that turned out to be spot on. Our room on the fourteenth floor looked straight out over the river, and watching the boats go by at night with the city lights up was worth the price of the room on its own. The bed was genuinely comfortable, housekeeping was prompt and thorough, and everything felt well maintained without being stuffy. It's not the cheapest hotel in town, but given the location and the little touches, we felt we got real value. Already looking at dates to come back.

So...the location to the Clark/Lake train stop is great...and that is the only thing that is great with the hotel. The wall are very thin...so much you can hear giggling and early morning housekeeping conversations in the hallway. There is no coffee maker in the room, however; free coffee is available in the lobby...becuase everyone wants to go to the lobby first thing in the morning??? Finally, the 'business center' is a pay for use set-up...no courtesty internet usage or printing. Lastly...they bathroom is micro-tiny and lacks in counterspace and comfort.
The location near the train station was the only perk of my stay. Wifi barely worked, the bathroom had mold around the tub, and breakfast was stale pastries and weak coffee--totally underwhelming.

I expected more from a Sofitel, especially at this rate. The room looked polished in photos, but in person the decor felt tired: scuffed furniture, a worn carpet edge, and heavy curtains that made everything seem dark. Cleanliness was also below standard; there were dust marks on the bedside table and hair in the bathroom when I arrived. Sleep was difficult because traffic noise carried up late into the night, followed by hallway doors slamming early in the morning. The bed itself was comfortable enough, but that hardly mattered after a restless night. Staff were courteous when I mentioned the noise, though no practical solution was offered. The location was convenient, but the room did not feel like the refined, relaxing stay the Sofitel name suggests.

Beautiful hotel, but very dated--threadbare carpets and faded furniture. We didn't sleep well with the noisy AC. Paid a premium, felt overpriced. Two nights was one too many; I was honestly relieved to leave.

I stayed at the hotel for 5 nights in mid-March and was so disappointed with everything. The room was small, the carpets in the looby were smelly, no bathtub in the washroom and view of brick walls from the windows. Not even free internet which even the cheapest hotels offer these days. It costs $10/day to connect to internet. If you want to use internet in the lobby, minimum charge is $5 per use. To use the phone in the rooms for local calls, it is $1.25/15mins and then 10 cents every min. Even the local calls are charged, what a rip off!!! Every hotel I have stayed at offers free intercontinetal breakfast, of course no such thing at this hotel. No indoor pool, go figure. I won this from bidding process at priceline, I will be reluctant to use this service and this hotel in future.
Disappointing stay at Sofitel: the room felt tired, housekeeping missed basic details, and the service was strangely indifferent. For the price, I expected a much more polished experience.

I had a very comfortable two-night stay at the Conrad. The front desk team was warm and efficient, and they took time to point me toward a nearby coffee shop when I arrived early for a meeting. My room was spotless, with a great bed and enough desk space to work without feeling boxed in. Despite being in a busy area, it was remarkably quiet at night; I never heard hallway traffic or neighboring rooms. Wi-Fi connected immediately and stayed reliable for video calls and streaming. Breakfast was a pleasant surprise, with fresh fruit, eggs made to order, good pastries, and attentive servers who kept coffee topped up. I would happily return.
The room wasn't dirty, but the decor felt stuck in the 90s, and the view was just a gray rooftop. The bathroom had a cracked tile and weak water pressure, which sealed the disappointment.

I booked the Sofitel expecting the usual French polish, but honestly, it fell flat. The lobby is stunning--that's where the magic ends. Check-in took forever because the clerk kept apologizing for a system glitch, and I stood there with my jet lag and a heavy suitcase. My room, while spacious, had a stale cigarette smell that lingered despite the 'purified air' card on the desk. The bathroom faucet dripped all night, and the minibar was stocked with warm sodas. Breakfast was chaos: cold eggs, empty bread baskets, and staff who ignored me until I flagged someone down. For the price, I expected better service and attention to detail. The location is convenient, but next time I'll pay half as much at a boutique hotel down the street. Disappointing, Sofitel. I expected more.

I booked the Sofitel expecting a lot more than what I got, and honestly, I left feeling pretty let down. The room itself was spacious, but 'clean' felt like a stretch--there was a suspicious stain on the armchair and a layer of dust on the bedside lamps that I noticed right away. The staff were polite enough at check-in, but that was it. When I asked for extra towels and a quiet room away from the elevator, I got a shrug and a 'we're fully booked,' which made me feel like an inconvenience rather than a guest. The view was a dreary, direct look at a concrete parking structure, not the city skyline I'd pictured. For the premium price I paid, this was nowhere near worth it. I've had better service and upkeep at a three-star, honestly. It's disappointing because you expect a certain standard, but the Sofitel just missed the mark on almost everything that matters. I won't be returning.
Even our short stay at Hotel Monaco felt too long: Wi-Fi kept dropping, the bathroom was cramped and tired, and breakfast was bland and overpriced.

My family of four went to a convention and stayed here in early August. We were promised a room with two double beds. When we arrived (earlier than most) we were told they were 45 double beds short. We reluctantly agreed to take a room with a king bed and a promise of a roll away bed. We had a to sleep very uncomfortably with a 12 year old in our bed and our other child in the roll away. Little did we know we were being CHARGED a daily fee for this bed. The managment could not handle the large group that was at this hotel. The bellhops and bartenders were visibly stressed and we did not have towels one day until very late at night. The managers would not take off the roll away bed charge and were not the least bit accomodating. We were so disappointed in this hotel. Also, they do not have a pool here. If you want to use a pool there is a health club next to the hotel but you have to pay $20 a day to use it. $80 for a family to take a little swim was a bit ridiculous. Do yourself a favor, if you want to be accomodated and are thinking of booking this hotel for a convention or otherwise, go elsewhere. Chicago has too many hotels to choose from to pick this one. I never heard back from managment on this issue when I called and emailed so obviously they don't care, even when I told them I'd write a review on this website. Chicago is an awesome city though. We loved it!

I really wanted to love the Hard Rock, especially after paying what I did, but the whole stay felt like a letdown. Check-in took almost half an hour because they were short-staffed, and nobody apologized even once. The room itself looked tired -- scuffed walls, a lamp that didn't work, and the AC rattled all night no matter what I set it to. I called the front desk twice about it and got a different answer each time, and maintenance never actually showed up. The 'rock and roll' theme is everywhere, but it mostly means loud music blasting in the lobby at 11pm right outside the rooms. Breakfast was overpriced for what it was, and the coffee tasted like it had been sitting for hours. Honestly the location was the only saving grace. I won't be back.
Slept soundly in a comfortable bed, with barely any hallway noise. The Wi-Fi was reliable for work, and the sunrise view over the river from my room was a lovely bonus.

I stayed here for a conference and got the conference rate of $149. I was worried that I wouldn't get a nice room, since it was the weekend before the election and the hotel is across the street from Grant Park, so it could easily have gotten a lot more for the nicer rooms. I requested a quiet room away from elevators and foot traffic, and that is exactly what I was assigned (perhaps because I am also a 'silver' member?). It was a beautiful room with windows on two sides, a king sized bed. The room was quiet, comfortable and immaculate. The maid even left a thank you note for the tip I had left. All the staff were helpful, polite and cheerful. I appreciated the fact that I could actually purchase a breakfast for under $15 (oatmeal, coffee, and juice)--something not possible at a lot of big hotels, like the Hyatt I stayed at last year.

I expected a much more polished experience from Sofitel, but the stay was disappointing from the start. Check-in took nearly 25 minutes, even though there was no obvious queue, and the receptionist seemed distracted rather than welcoming. Our room looked tired, with scuffed furniture, marks on the carpet, and a bathroom fan that rattled loudly through the night. The bed was comfortable, but the air conditioning was difficult to regulate and the room became uncomfortably warm. Breakfast was another letdown: several dishes were lukewarm, tables were not cleared promptly, and staff seemed overwhelmed. We also had to call twice for extra towels. The location is convenient, but the service and upkeep did not match the Sofitel name or the price. I would not rush back.
Disappointing stay at the Conrad: check-in dragged on, the room felt tired for the price, and hallway noise kept us awake. Staff were polite, but it never felt worth the expense.

We loved the hotel. When I see other posts about it being shabby I can't for the life of me figure out what they are talking about. Rooms were large with TWO bathrooms, lobby was fabulous, pool was large with two hot tubs and huge gym, staff was courteous. For us, the location was great--across the street from Grant Park with a great view of Buckingham Fountain and close to all the museums and theatres. I'm sure others would rather be north of the river closer to the Magnificent Mile but we enjoyed the quieter and more scenic location. Got it for $105 on Hotwire. What a bargain for such a nice hotel.

Our three-night booking felt like a week, mainly because the cramped bathroom flooded every shower. The view of a concrete wall matched the stale, lukewarm breakfast buffet, making each morning a chore.

I chose this hotel for a nice weekend getaway and was nothing but disappointed. The previous weekend, I stayed at a 2.5 star hotel a few blocks away, and was much more impressed there. The Hard Rock had a number of issues including: very dark room - not much light (artificial or natural); lots of street noise; very cheap decor and furniture; broken cabinet door; very warm room - said they would send maintenance, but they never arrived; had bar charges on account that were not ours. Overall, I was very surprised that this was a 4 star hotel. I expected a much better experience!

I booked the Conrad expecting the usual five-star polish, but the experience felt off from the moment I walked in. The lobby is stunning, sure, but the front desk staff seemed frazzled and barely acknowledged me until I coughed twice. My room wasn't ready at 4 PM, and when I finally got in, the 'upgraded' view was a brick wall and a noisy AC unit that rattled all night. Housekeeping forgot to restock the coffee pods, and when I called, they said they'd send some up--they never did. The bathroom fixtures looked great in photos but felt cheap, with a shower head that sprayed sideways. Breakfast was a disaster: cold eggs, dry pastries, and a server who rolled her eyes when I asked for more juice. For $400 a night, I expected better. The location is convenient, but that's the only saving grace. I've had more attentive service at a roadside motel. Won't be back.

The bathroom's constant drain gurgle grated through paper-thin walls, and the hallway noise never let up. Location is handy, but that's it--the cramped room made the night feel far too long in the worst way.

I was scheduled to stay at the Hard Rock in June, but had to cancel. I had booked the hotel back in January. When I called six days before my arrival date to cancel, I was told that I would be charged for my stay because I did not cancel seven days in advance. I told the customer service rep that I had never heard of such a practice, but she said, in a very smug manner, that I was told back in January. I honestly don't remember being told of the cancellation policy, but think it is a unprofessional practice to capture some additional dollars since it is not an industry standard to require a seven day cancellation policy when you book directly with the hotel. I, for one, will never stay at a Hard Rock hotel and will make sure that my friends and business associaties know of this unfair practice.

We had our hotel reservations at another hotel set and after we were reading all of the negative reviews we cancelled and made out reservation at the Hilton - I am so glad we did the hotel was clean, hotel staff was pleasant and helpful and the beds were amazing. We knew we were paying a little more than some other hotels but it was well worth every penny.

My experiences at the Fairmont Chicago were less than desirable. I try to be fair when I write my reviews, but fair is not in the Fairmont Chicago language. From pulling up to check in I felt the gouging start. $54 a night for parking is terrible for this area $30-$35 is the average and that is not affordable as it is but $54 is just disgusting to put on your guests. The parking was more than my car rental. In the room the internet is not complementary it is $16 for standard and $25 for some sort of ultra upgraded internet service. Gouge gouge gouge, who charges for internet anymore and even worse upgraded services. I didn't go online every day of my 8 day stay because of the cost. One update on the internet that they don't tell you upon check in is that if you sign up for the free premiere Fairmont club you will receive free in room internet service, I found that out on the last day of my stay. Other issues with this property is the shower pressure is not very good. The bed was hard and uncomfortable. And I would say there are many other properties that have a better location and price in the city. On a good note the Aria resturant in the Fairmont has a tremendous staff and serves up the best burger and fries I have ever had, loved the complimentary naan and dips to start, and the complimentary orange bark to finish.

My stay at the Hard Rock was disappointing and did not feel worth the price. The room looked stylish in photos, but it was worn in person, with scuffed furniture and a bathroom that needed attention. The grout around the shower was discolored, the water pressure was weak, and the sink drained very slowly. Staff were polite enough at check-in, but they seemed rushed and not particularly interested when I reported the plumbing issue. Noise was another problem: loud music and voices from the hallway continued well past midnight, followed by doors slamming early in the morning. The bed itself was comfortable, but I barely slept because of the noise. Overall, the atmosphere felt more like a busy entertainment venue than a relaxing hotel, and I would choose somewhere quieter next time.

We stayed here three nights for a family visit and honestly expected better from Homewood. The first room they put us in smelled strongly of cigarette smoke even though it's supposed to be non-smoking, and it took over an hour to get moved. The new room was okay but the AC unit rattled all night and the pull-out sofa bed had stains on the mattress. Breakfast was a letdown too--eggs were watery, some items ran out and weren't replaced, and the seating area was always a mess. Housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely and we had to ask for towels at the front desk. The location is convenient, I'll give it that, and a couple of staff members were friendly, but for the price I can't recommend it. We won't be back.

The Sofitel was a dream--staff anticipated every need, the bed was pure cloud, and that view of the city from the pool bar made happy hour unforgettable. Check-in was swift, evening turn-down flawless. A perfect, restorative escape.

I was disappointed with my stay at Hotel Amalfi. The location is convenient, but the property feels tired and badly in need of maintenance. Our room had scuffed walls, a stained carpet near the bed, and a bathroom fan that rattled loudly whenever it was turned on. The air conditioning struggled to cool the room, so sleeping was uncomfortable even though the weather was mild. At check-in, the front desk clerk seemed rushed and gave us almost no information about the facilities or nearby restaurants. Housekeeping also skipped our room one day, and getting fresh towels took two calls. Breakfast was expensive for what was offered, with limited choices and coffee that tasted stale. Nothing was disastrous on its own, but the overall experience was poor for the price, and I would not choose this hotel again.

I expected more from Homewood, especially for the rate. The suite looked worn the minute we walked in: stained carpet near the sofa, a sticky spot on the kitchen counter, and one of the lamps flickered all night. The refrigerator made a loud rattling sound and the air conditioner barely cooled the room, so sleeping was uncomfortable. Breakfast was disappointing too; by 8:30 there were empty trays, watered-down coffee, and no staff around to restock anything. We mentioned the AC and cleanliness to the front desk, but were told maintenance would 'take a look' and nobody came before checkout. The location was convenient, but that was about the only positive. It did not feel like a well-maintained property, and I would choose somewhere else next time.

I loved it here! My boyfriend and I booked this hotel online and were a little worried what it would be like since we paid next to nothing for our 3 nights here. (I've paid more to stay at the Santa Barbara Motel 6!!) Gorgeous hotel, great staff, fun bar/lounge area and we were most impressed with the room. The large windows in the bathroom were the best--I took a bubble bath one night while looking at the views of Navy Pier and the skyline. I remember thinking, 'This is really living...' The room was comfortable and quiet, again with great views just like in the bathroom. Chicago is a wonderful town--I have nothing but good things to say about it. CAn't wait to come back!

I had a very pleasant stay at the Sofitel and would happily return. From the moment I arrived, the staff were warm, professional, and genuinely helpful without being overbearing. My room was elegant, quiet, and thoughtfully arranged, with a very comfortable bed and excellent bathroom amenities. I especially appreciated how spotless everything was and the small touches that made the space feel more personal. Breakfast offered a good variety, including fresh pastries, fruit, and properly prepared coffee, although the restaurant became busy later in the morning. The location was convenient for getting around, and the hotel's atmosphere felt refined but still relaxed. A couple of minor details, such as a slightly slow check-in, kept it from being perfect, but overall the service, comfort, and attention to detail made this a satisfying stay.
Lovely stay at Hotel Ambassador--our room was spotless, breakfast had plenty of choice, and the front desk team were genuinely helpful with local restaurant tips.

The Hyatt turned out to be a solid choice for my three-night stay. I was initially worried the common areas might feel tired, but the lobby and hallways have a clean, contemporary vibe that hasn't aged poorly. The room itself was quiet, and the bed was the real standout--I slept better here than I have at home in weeks, thanks to the firm mattress and blackout curtains that actually did their job. The bathroom was a pleasant surprise: a rainfall shower with strong water pressure and plenty of hot water, plus generous counter space that didn't get cluttered. Given the location and the level of comfort, I felt the rate was fair, especially compared to nearby options with less to offer. The only minor quibble was the slightly worn carpet near the door, but it didn't detract from an otherwise restful and worthwhile stay. I'd happily book here again.
Hotel Amalfi was pleasantly quiet at night, and I slept soundly in the comfortable bed. WiFi was reliable, and the room's city view over the rooftops made mornings especially nice.

Booked this on priceline for an insanely low price of $65 a night. The BF and I were amazed when we got there--the person checking us in was friendly and helpful to suggest some local nightspots and the room was gorgeous! A nice upscale, downtown feel and super comfy beds. We had a fabulous view from the 25th floor that inlcluded a sliver of Lake Michigan, a sliver of the Taste of Chicago crowds, and some friendly office workers in the builiding next door who waved to us a few times. Seriously. We had a pretty anonymous experience the rest of our stay--which was fine with us. The hotel consists mainly of 2 towers and is like a huge, sprawling city inside. But we weren't there to stay in the hotel room the entire time...we like to get out and explore as much as possible. The location was fantastic. Easy walking distance to Michigan Avenue and the rest of downtown. We walked for blocks well into the night and never felt like we needed a cab. I also highly recommend the Urban Cruise on the river (the entrance is right across from the hotel)--we saw some amazing architecture from the boat and got to cruise Lake Michigan a bit too. Don't park your car here if you don't need to--it's very expensive. Park downtown or ditch the rental car--you won't need it anyway, you can walk to tons of stuff or grab a cab. Love Chicago and totally recommend this hotel!

I really wanted to love my stay here, but the experience left me feeling deflated and counting the hours until checkout. The biggest issue was sleep: the mattress was lumpy and sagged in the middle, and the street-facing window offered zero soundproofing, so I was awake until 2 AM listening to traffic. The shower in the bathroom was a torrential mess, with weak pressure and a curtain that clung to my skin. Everything felt tired--the carpets were stained, and the floral bedspread looked like it was from the 1980s. Even the promised high-speed wifi was a joke; it dropped constantly in my room, making it impossible to stream a movie. I can't shake the feeling that they're coasting on the building's old reputation, and I'd advise anyone to look elsewhere first.

I vacationed at the Fairmont Chicago for 3 nights in July 2009. The room, the bathroom, the view, and the staff were all wonderful. I just wish the hotel were a few blocks North (on MI Ave). Sometimes, when you're tired, that extra couple of blocks seem like miles!

I disliked the Sofitel so much we changed our week stay to the Grand Hyatt after the first night. We checked into our suite and was blasted by the smell of body odor immediately. We were tired from our flight, but went downstairs to change rooms. The second suite smelled just as bad, but stayed anyway. I disliked the hotel lobby, the staff, the decorating, and especially the bed. HORRIBLE. Soft, flimsy mattress. We come to Chicago frequently. We have always stayed at the Grand Hyatt and never been disappointed. We just thought we'd try some place new. Never again. Back to the Hyatt or Four Season we go!

I had a genuinely relaxing stay at the Sheraton. Check-in was quick, and the front desk team was warm and helpful when I asked about nearby restaurants. My room was spotless, with a very comfortable bed, strong water pressure in the shower, and enough workspace to catch up on emails without feeling cramped. I also appreciated how quiet the floor was at night despite the hotel being busy. Breakfast had plenty of choices, including fresh fruit, pastries, and made-to-order eggs. The lobby bar was a nice spot for a late drink after a long day. The location made getting around easy, too. A few furnishings showed minor wear, but nothing that affected the experience. I would happily stay here again.

I recently stayed at the Sheraton for an onsite conference, and had problems from the getgo. I had problems with the check-in even though I had made arrangements beforehand to pay by company check and they have a credit card on file. The front desk clerks were kind of rude. The room was okay, not worth what I paid for. The sheets were kind of messed up and the room didn't feel very clean. They also charge for internet access, which is ridiculous. Most hotels provide free wi-fi. The conference food, which I assume is catered by the hotel, was not good at all. On the day of the check out, I had arranged for a late check-out, but in the morning before check-out time, someone else got assigned to my room and was attempting to get in! Then they locked me out of my room with my luggage still in there before my check out time. All in all, I would recommend staying somewhere else.

Stayed in old tower. Room was nice and room service was very good. Room Wi-Fi was expensive as was the bottled water. For the price of the room, at least there should at least have been water. I would rate the value as sub-par. The restaurant menu was not great, food mediocre by comparison to other downtown Chicago restaurants and the service was below average especially since there were only three tables in use in the entire restaurant.. In summary, I will go to the M... or H... next time. Some of the above comments are based on a previous week resort stay on the outer banks of North Carolina and earlier this year in Northern California. P.S. If you are a fitness room user, the $16 per stay per person is a good deal at this hotel.

We stayed here through Hotwire and got an amazingly low rate- $60 some odd dollars nightly for a 2 night stay last May. The room they had us in was small and had no view of anything except the wall of the other part of the hotel, but it was very clean, tastefully decorated and cozy. We had a great vacation, walking all over town until we ended up near the Planetarium which was where we then turned around and saw the skyline of Chicago and were just wow. So anyway, the hotel is great, the service was great, the room was very nice- I would recommend this hotel to anyone though I work at the front desk of a hotel myself and the previous person's comment about how she wasn't able to get adjoining rooms, well, internet sites don't guarantee things like that anyway- you've got to call the hotel direct and verify things like that. There's a note about that on internet sites as well- no room type/location is guaranteed. 5 stars out of 5 for this hotel.
Disappointing stay at the Omni--the room looked tired, housekeeping missed our floor twice, and hallway noise continued past midnight. For the price, I expected much better.

I booked two nights at Affinia as a weekend escape, and honestly, I'm relieved it wasn't a week. The room's window faced an interior air shaft, offering a grim view of concrete and a humming exhaust fan, which I stared at more than I'd like because the Wi-Fi kept dropping every few minutes on my laptop. Traffic noise from the street seeped through the glass all night, so rest was elusive--I heard every siren and motorcycle until 3 a.m. The stay felt both cramped and overlong, as the tiny bathroom and worn carpet made me eager to leave by checkout. Front desk staff were polite but couldn't fix the connectivity or offer a quieter room. For the price, this was a letdown; I'd look elsewhere next time.

Stayed at the Sheraton for a conference and honestly, it exceeded what I expected from a big chain. Check-in was a breeze, even with a long line, because the front desk moved people through with real efficiency. My room on the 14th floor was quiet, which is rare, and the bed was genuinely comfortable--I slept like a rock. The bathroom was spotless and the water pressure in the shower was fantastic after a long travel day. I grabbed dinner at the hotel bar and the service was attentive without hovering, and the food was surprisingly good for hotel fare. Location wise, it's central enough to walk to a few good spots, and the staff gave me solid recommendations. The gym was decent, with working treadmills and free weights, nothing fancy but functional. Only minor hiccup was slow Wi-Fi in the evening, but morning speed was fine. I'd gladly book here again for a business trip or a weekend getaway.
Sofitel made our weekend feel special: the room was quiet and beautifully styled, staff were warm without hovering, and breakfast had plenty of fresh options.

The room's fresh, modern decor felt effortlessly stylish, and the skyline view from bed was a treat. Slept like a log on the plush linens, and for the price, it's genuinely hard to beat--already planning my return.

I expected more from Hotel Amalfi based on the photos and location. The room was much smaller than advertised, with worn furniture, a stained carpet, and an air conditioner that rattled loudly all night. The bathroom looked clean at first glance, but the shower drain was slow and left water pooling around my feet. Wi-Fi barely worked in the room, which was frustrating after a long day out. Breakfast was basic and several items were already gone when I arrived, with no one refilling them. Staff at reception were polite but seemed uninterested when I mentioned the noise and poor Wi-Fi. The central location is convenient, but it did not make up for the uncomfortable stay.

The hotel is well located, but the service is poor. They seem to cater to large conventioneers, with service more like a moderate chain hotel - not your typical Fairmont. There are too many specifics to outline here, let's just say that from the front desk, to the spa, room service which only got my order correct one-day, to housekeeping which didn't even clean my room one day (although they sent a manager to inspect the room because the housekeeper said she did clean the room. Yep, that's just what you want to come home to after 10 hrs of meetings! They did offer me a complimentary breakfast for my inconvenience! The hotel is large and many times between 5-7 pm there would literally be a long line of guests waiting for an elevator. I've stayed at this Fairmont twice. The 1st time I attended a conference nearby and the last time l chose it for the price. But it's not worth enduring such poor service. That was the last time for me.

The Talbotts antique charm wore thin fast--our 'deluxe' room was cramped, the AC rattled all night, and the front desk shrugged off our noise complaints. Overpriced and underwhelming; we cut our stay short.

I stayed at the James for a quick Chicago weekend and was pleasantly surprised by how relaxed it felt despite being right in the middle of everything. Check-in was friendly and efficient, and the front desk gave us a couple of solid dinner suggestions that were actually nearby. Our room was quiet, nicely designed, and had a very comfortable bed; the blackout curtains were especially appreciated after a late night out. The bathroom was spotless with a great shower and plenty of counter space, which is not always a given in city hotels. We walked to Michigan Avenue, the river, and several restaurants without needing a cab. The lobby can get busy in the evening, but it never felt chaotic. I'd happily stay here again.

I had a very pleasant stay at The James and would happily return. My room was spotless when I arrived, with fresh linens, dust-free surfaces, and a comfortable bed that made it easy to settle in. The Wi-Fi connected quickly and stayed reliable for both video calls and casual streaming. The bathroom was modern and exceptionally clean, with good water pressure, plenty of towels, and quality toiletries. I also appreciated how quiet the room was, especially at night; I rarely heard hallway traffic or outside noise, which made sleeping easy. The staff were welcoming without being intrusive, and check-in was smooth. The location was convenient for getting around, and the overall atmosphere felt polished but relaxed. It was a comfortable, well-managed stay from start to finish.

This hotel has a great location and nice infrastructure. The river north area is full of great restaurants and the north bridge area is great for out of towners. The decor is lovely and a nice hold-over from when this was a Le Meridian. While the Conrad aspires to be in the top tier along with the Peninsula, the Four Seasons, the Ritz and Park Hyatt, it falls short. We and dinner at the Terrace Restarant outside the other day and were initially impressed with the setting and the selection. While the prices were similar to the Peninsula, we figured that it was a nice day and worth a try. Wow, were we ever disappointed. First off, we were told that we could have a seat but only stay until 7. OK, thats fine and we sat down. The waitress made a point to ask if anything was wrong, so that she could make it right. When we indicated that our glasses of champagne were not very full ($20 per glass), she consulted with the manager and then another manager (a heavier fellow in a dark suit). She came back and said that was the standard puor and that she would be glad to bring us additional glasses. What bothers me is not the outcome, but the fact that the management is not service focused. At a Four Seasons or the Peninsula, this would never happen and if we expressed any displeasure, it would be made right. At the Conrad, the Terrace manager just ignored it.
The 'Ambassador' promised much but delivered little. Our room had a broken AC and the pool was drained all weekend. Staff were indifferent, and the breakfast was borderline inedible. Save your money.
The Omni made our weekend easy and comfortable, with a spotless room, quiet nights, and genuinely friendly staff. I especially appreciated the quick check-in and excellent downtown location.

I booked the James expecting a stylish boutique stay, but the reality fell flat. The lobby is nice in photos, but the room I got had a broken AC unit that rattled all night, and the hallway smelled like old carpet and mildew. I asked for a quiet floor, yet I heard every door slam and the elevator dinging until 2 AM. Staff were polite but unhelpful when I requested a late checkout--they said no without even checking. The bar downstairs was overcrowded with non-guests, and one drink took 20 minutes. Breakfast was a joke: lukewarm eggs, stale pastries, and coffee that tasted burnt. For the price, I've had far better at a standard chain. The location is decent for downtown, but honestly, I wouldn't return unless they fix the noise and maintenance issues. Disappointing.

We stayed at the Affinia for four nights and honestly couldn't wait to check out. The room faced the street, and the noise was relentless -- garbage trucks at 5am, sirens throughout the night, and thin walls that let us hear every conversation in the hallway. Sleep was basically impossible without earplugs, which we didn't have the first two nights. The wifi was another letdown; it dropped constantly and was so slow in the evenings that streaming anything was a gamble. For the price, I expected far better. The staff were pleasant enough, but that doesn't make up for exhaustion every morning. By the last day, the stay felt way too long, even though friends had told us it would fly by. Disappointing overall, and we won't be returning.

I stayed at the Hilton Chicago because I was attending a conference at the hotel. The room was sufficient - had a coffee maker, bed, hangers, tv, etc. That's about where my compliments end: *restaurant rates are outrageous. $21 for a breakfast buffet? $25 to use the gym? $7.50/hr for WiFi!?!?! This is unacceptable when I'm paying $249 per night. Thank goodness the ice was free. *servers in the restaurant and bar were surly, not well-versed in English, and just rude. *computer monitors in rooms are silly and turn on at random times during the night *conference was incredibly cold...everybody was wearing their overcoats the entire time, despite our complaints to management. *fridge in room was not usable. had to store cold items in the ice bucket. *Cable channels just flat out SUCKED. I was soooo bored when I had to spend an hour in my room. If I'm paying that much, at least provide the full 70 channels.

The two nights here stretched into an eternity, yet somehow the time I actually wanted to enjoy slipped away. The air conditioning rattled like a dying lawnmower, and the hallway noise from a wedding party seeped under the door until past 1 AM. Our room's decor felt trapped in the late 90s--scuffed beige headboards, a worn floral armchair, and a bathroom with grout that had seen better decades. The staff, though polite, moved with a distracted air. Twice I asked for extra towels, and the request was met with a cheerful nod that took forty minutes to fulfill. The lobby's fresh flowers and chic lighting were a cruel contrast to our tired quarters. Breakfast was competent but forgettable, and checkout felt rushed. For the price, I expected the Sofitel sparkle. Instead, I got a faded ghost of it.

We were so excited to stay here for my husband's birthday weekend, but honestly the whole thing was a letdown from start to finish. Check-in took nearly an hour because the line barely moved and there were only two people working. Our room had a broken AC that blew warm air the entire first night, and when we called the front desk they said someone would come up but nobody ever did. The 'rock star' atmosphere they advertise just feels like a garish gift shop attached to a mediocre hotel. Pool was packed with kids until closing and getting a lounge chair was basically impossible. Breakfast at the cafe cost almost $60 for two people and the food was lukewarm at best. Location-wise it's far from the beach unless you drive. For the price we paid, I expected so much more. We won't be back.
The room looked tired, the AC barely worked, and check-in took forever despite a nearly empty lobby. For the price, Sofitel felt far less polished than expected.

I booked the Fairmont for a three-night anniversary trip, and honestly, I'm struggling to see where the five-star reputation comes from. The lobby is grand, sure, but that's where the polish ended. Our room faced an interior courtyard with a constant humming ventilation noise, and the curtains didn't fully block the light from the corridor. More frustrating was the service: we waited over an hour for a simple extra pillow request, and when I called again, the front desk put me on hold and then forgot about me. The housekeeping also skipped our turndown entirely one night without explanation. Breakfast at the restaurant felt overpriced for lukewarm eggs and slow coffee refills. I've stayed at far better hotels for less money. The location is convenient, but that doesn't excuse the apathy. I won't be returning, and I can't recommend it for a special occasion--it felt like a standard business stopover at best.

The Hard Rock's reputation and that iconic guitar sign had me hyped, but my stay was a total letdown. Check-in took forever; the line snaked around the lobby with only two agents working. Finally getting a key, I walked into a room that smelled like stale smoke and old carpet. The much-talked-about rock memorabilia was scarce, just a couple of framed prints. The bed was lumpy, and the pillows were flat as pancakes. I could hear every footstep and conversation from the hallway, so sleep was a joke. The bathroom had rust spots around the drain. I tried the restaurant for breakfast, but the service was glacial and the food was overpriced and mediocre. For these rates, I expected at least a spotless, quiet room. This place runs on its name, not on quality. I'm genuinely disappointed and wouldn't recommend it.
Homewood's location was convenient for getting around, but our two-night stay felt dragged out by indifferent staff and repeated issues. For the price, it was far from worth it.

Overall the hotel is very nice. The rooms are spacious and well-appointed, but they tend to be aging or dated.
