My bathroom was particularly below average, with old wallpaper and a dingy tub with a crummy showerhead. The toilet paper roll holder was pulling out of the wall and its screws were exposed. The conceirge recommended an expensive and mediocre restaurant. I hate it when they do that- it makes me suspect they're getting kickbacks from places that otherwise don't get enough business on their own. Breakfast was very good. It's a relatively large european-style spread.

The room smelled musty, the air conditioning clanked all night, and housekeeping never replaced our towels despite calling twice. The lobby looks great in photos, but the hallways are dingy and the hallway noise is relentless. Not worth the price.

I was completely blown away by this hotel. It was magnificent. I got a great deal and I am so happy that I stayed here. Before arriving I was nervous as I had read a few bad reviews about the impact the renovation was having on peoples stay, for example very noisy. However, whilst the renovation was still going on and the gym was not open nor the restaurant, it made no difference to me. My room was huge, bathroom was spacious with excellent water pressure, bed was perfect and the view was amazing. Hotel is so close to the great shops of Magnificent Mile, plus a comfortable walking distance to Hancock tower and Millennium Park.

Our three-night escape at the Intercontinental felt like a single, blissful afternoon--I actually found myself wishing we'd booked one more day just to linger over that skyline view from the 22nd floor. The room was immaculate, with crisp white linens and a bathroom so spotless it gleamed under the soft lighting. Housekeeping even folded my stray charging cable into a neat coil, a small touch that spoke volumes. The Wi-Fi was flawless from check-in to checkout, handling both work calls and late-night streaming without a hiccup. I'm not one to gush, but the floor-to-ceiling windows framed Lake Michigan so perfectly that I caught myself staring out more than watching TV. Genuinely, a stay that felt both too short and exactly right.

Comfortable bed, quiet room even with the station nearby, and the breakfast spread was worth getting up for. Staff fixed a charger issue within minutes. Would happily book the Swissotel again next trip.
Had a great stay at Hard Rock--the room was stylish and comfortable, the staff were genuinely welcoming, and the live music and lively atmosphere made the whole visit feel special.

I chose the Affinia because the location looked convenient, but the stay was more frustrating than expected. Check-in took nearly half an hour, even though there were only two guests ahead of me, and the desk agent seemed rushed and uninterested. Our room was large, but it felt tired: scuffed walls, stained carpet near the window, and a bathroom fan that rattled loudly whenever the light was on. Housekeeping also skipped us one day, so we had to call down for clean towels and more toilet paper. The bed was comfortable enough, although the pillows were flat, and street noise made sleeping difficult. Wi-Fi was inconsistent and the extra daily fees were not explained clearly at booking. The staff eventually helped, but overall the property did not feel worth the price.

We booked the Ambassador expecting a nice anniversary getaway, but it fell flat. The room was stifling hot, the AC barely worked, and housekeeping never showed up until we called twice. The bar was understaffed and drinks took forever. Not worth the hype or the price.

Disappointing given the price--our room faced a brick wall, and street noise kept us up past midnight. The location near the Loop is convenient, but that can't excuse the dated furniture and overpriced minibar. I expected far more for what we paid.

I expected more from a Hilton, especially for the rate we paid. Check-in took nearly half an hour because only one person was at the desk, and no one acknowledged the line. Our room looked tired: scuffed furniture, a stained chair, and a bathroom fan that rattled all night. The air conditioning barely worked, so the room stayed stuffy despite repeated adjustments. We called down about it and were told someone would come by, but nobody did. Breakfast was expensive and picked over by 8:30, with cold coffee and empty trays left sitting out. The location was convenient, but that was about the only positive. This felt more like a neglected airport hotel than the dependable Hilton experience I was expecting.
The Hyatt felt worth the rate for its comfortable room and calm nights. Breakfast had plenty of fresh options, and every staff member was friendly, attentive, and quick to help.

We experienced bed bugs in our room while staying at the Omni Chicago Hotel on the Magnificent Mile. We never received a return call from General Manager Sanjay Mahajan after several voicemails. We will never return to the hotel and will work to spread the word. We also heard from several employees from the cleaning staff that this is common in the hotel.

This was our second time staying here. We were very much looking forward to our weekend at the Amalfi (based on how well the first stay was). It turned out better than our anticipation. The beds are very comfortable. 2 headed showers with a large bathroom. The hotel is also pleasantly quiet and easy to check-in and out. Our room was near the exercise room which helped motivate us to get in an hour morning workout. Then we were able to grab some complimentary fruit, pastries, juice and coffee on our floor (breakfast is on every floor). No great view from our room, but I don't think there are great views from most any room since it is only 5 floors. We didn't need to drive, take a cab or jump on the L the whole weekend since the hotel is centrally located. We easily walked to bars, blues clubs, restaurants, the hancock tower, the loop and the waterfront all from our hotel. The highlight of the hotel was the complimentary happy hour. Free top-shelf drinks and wonderful meats, cheeses, peppers, and breads. This ran from 5:30 to 7:00, and was a great warm-up to a nice dinner. This alone saved us a bundle in money that would of been spent eating and drinking out in the evening. And an extra money-saving tip...park at the self-park lot 2 blocks west of the hotel on Kinzie. Its $24 per night during the week and only $6 per night on the weekends. I think the hotel charges $30 to $40 per night to park.

Got a great deal through Hotwire for $70 a night but if I ever return to Chicago I would definitely stay again, even at full price. We really liked the rooms muted modern decor, we had John Lennon and Bono for company. Comfortable bed, mini coffe maker, plenty storage space and a lovely, clean bathroom stocked full of Aveda products (so I was sold straight away...it doesn't take much, I know!). If you're a product junkie, tip the maid and request some extra bottles and you will leave with lots of goodies :) We liked the location and had a great view down N Michigan Ave, found the staff to be really friendly and relaxed (reception, gift shop and bar). The bar area is very trendy, I liked the chilled atmosphere which surprised me cause I normally find these types of bars a bit too pretentious for my liking...the lack of memorabilia didn't bother me but I was more interested in the art deco features of the building itself anyway. The only fault was that the speakers in the room were crackling a bit oh, and my boyfriend thinks he was propositioned by a 'friendly lady looking for business' when he was at the bar. I think it's a place you will either love or hate, if you like laid back, contemporary hotels without the intimidating factor then this is the place for you!
The InterContinental's decor felt fresh without being flashy, and the price seemed fair for the comfort. The spotless bathroom was excellent, though my two-night stay passed far too quickly.

I stayed at the hotel one night. The hotel is excellent, comparable quality than Marriott and Sheraton, perhaps superior, but the location is definitely much better. Whatever your trip purpose is, business or leisure, you can drop your bags and take a walk on the Magnificent mile. Loved it!

I had high hopes for the Swissotel given its reputation, but my stay last week was honestly a letdown. Check-in took nearly forty minutes because apparently they were short-staffed, and nobody apologized or offered anything for the wait. My room had a decent view but the air conditioning rattled all night and freezing water came out of the 'hot' tap every morning. Housekeeping skipped my room entirely one day, and when I called the front desk about it they said someone would come by, which never happened. The gym equipment looked tired and half the treadmills were out of order. Breakfast in the restaurant was overpriced for what you got, and service there was slow even though it wasn't crowded. For the money, I expected far better. Probably won't be back.
Disappointing stay at the Hyatt. Room wasn't ready at check-in, AC barely worked, and staff seemed indifferent when we mentioned it. Expected way more for the price.

Very quaint and romantic, yet masculine. I've noticed that at most Chicago hotel bars it's hard to get a drink much less a seat but I guess because it's a small hotel that was not a problem at the Talbott - plus people take their drinks out to the seating in the lobby because it's so inviting - cozy and comfortable - love that! Would love to stay again but I must say that I was surprised by all the comments on the comfortable beds - ours was too firm. Also note there is no gym on the premises - but walking and shopping is enough of a workout!

Hotel Allegro was a great base for a long weekend downtown. The lobby has a fun, contemporary feel without trying too hard, and the room carried that through with colorful accents and updated furnishings rather than the tired decor I sometimes expect in older city hotels. Everything was spotless when I arrived, including the bathroom and the desk area, which I appreciated since I had some work to finish. The Wi-Fi connected immediately and stayed reliable enough for video calls and streaming in the evening. Best of all, I slept remarkably well: the bed was comfortable, the curtains blocked the morning light, and I heard very little hallway noise. Staff at the front desk were warm and efficient. I'd happily stay here again.

My sister and I stayed on the 22nd floor, there was a refrigerator in the hallway for the first three nights, beat up and old dorm style. It was not until we told the concierge that we were going to post the picture we took of it on Tripadvisor did the thing get removed. Breakfast dishes left outside rooms will stay on the floor for a day or two routinely. All night there are chimes that make noise, that are supposed to be comformting or relaxing and rather they are just annoying. There is no wifi - no matter what they tell you, I paid for the wifi, and still we were unable to get on. Lastly, my sister and I split the bill, I had already paid for the first night in form of a deposit and they gave her the credit. Room cost with city taxes etc. was 313.69 a night. I know the Comfort Inn just a few blocks away is significantly cheaper! So while the View was wonderful, it is NOT worth the money.

As we pulled away in a taxi heading to the airport for our trip home my wife turned to me and said 'We picked the right place.' Having chosen the Talbott from other Trip Advisor reviews I found myself thinking in terms of a Trip Advisor review when we arrived. Nice entrance, friendly reception, I noticed everything and immediately knew the Talbott was a non-corporate warm hotel with touches not typically seen in big name hotel chains. The smell of the elevator and attention to decorative details strongly reminded me of Europe, simple, not overstated but elegant. The location is great, there was light snow but we walked to the Art Institute, Rush Street, the Theater District, and we're from California where anything below 50 degrees keeps us inside! All I can say is if you are the kind of traveler that wants comfort, class and somewhere unique, stay at the Talbott. Oh yeah, we were in a room that looked down at the construction, we were on the 15th floor and could not hear a sound, it was very quiet.
Disappointing stay at the Hyatt--the room was dated, housekeeping missed obvious details, and the hallway was noisy all night. For the price, I expected much better service and comfort.

Stayed at the Omni for three nights during a work conference and honestly had a lovely time. My room on the 14th floor was spacious, spotless, and the bed was genuinely comfortable--rare for a hotel, I usually struggle to sleep somewhere new. The staff went out of their way constantly; the concierge gave me excellent dinner recommendations downtown and the front desk fixed a keycard glitch within two minutes. Room service was a bit slow one night, but the food arrived hot and the carbonara was surprisingly good. Loved the lobby smell (I asked what scent it was, no shame). Checking out was quick and they stored my luggage after checkout without any fuss. Would absolutely stay here again next time I'm in town for business--maybe even bring the family for a weekend.

Stayed here for a business conference and was pleasantly surprised by the whole experience. The room was spotless, with fresh linens and a carpet that actually looked vacuumed, which is rarer than it should be. The Wi-Fi was fast and reliable--I streamed a video call without a single drop, which made working from the room a breeze. The bathroom had excellent water pressure and the rainfall showerhead was a treat after long days, though the glass door did let a bit of light in early morning. Street noise was minimal thanks to the double-paned windows; I only heard distant sirens twice all week. The bed was firm but comfortable, and housekeeping was prompt each day. Minor quibbles aside, this was a solid, hassle-free stay that met all my needs. I'd happily book again for future trips.

The Hyatt was exactly what I needed after a long travel day. Check-in was smooth, and the front desk actually remembered my name the next morning, which was a nice touch. My room had a fantastic view of the skyline, and the bed was the kind that makes you want to skip your morning plans just to stay in it. The shower pressure was perfect, and the blackout curtains worked wonders for jet lag. I visited the restaurant for breakfast, and the avocado toast with poached eggs was surprisingly good, not your typical hotel fare. The gym was well-equipped, and the pool area was quiet even on a weekend. Location-wise, it was easy to walk to the waterfront, and the staff gave me a great tip for a less touristy dinner spot nearby. I really have no complaints. It's a solid, comfortable place that got everything right, and I wouldn't hesitate to book it again next time I'm in town.

Excellent location, about a block from Michigan Ave. and two blocks from Water Tower Place and John Hancock Tower. Beautiful hotel, felt very luxurious and high-class for being a moderate priced hotel. Staff was excellent -- friendly and accommodating.

We stayed at the Palmer for a long weekend, and honestly, it exceeded expectations. Our room on the seventh floor faced the garden side, which meant we woke up to a serene canopy of trees instead of the usual city clamor--a truly lovely surprise. The location was a dream for exploring; we walked to the High Line and Chelsea Market in under ten minutes, and grabbing the subway was effortless. I was a bit worried about street noise, but the double-glazed windows worked wonders. I slept like a log each night, the bed was firm yet plush, and the blackout curtains kept the morning light at bay. It's rare to find a hotel this central that feels this peaceful. The staff were friendly without being intrusive, and the lobby's coffee bar became our daily ritual. For a traveler who values both convenience and quiet, this was just right--we'll definitely book again.

The location was the one real advantage: it is an easy walk to restaurants, shopping, and the train, so getting around downtown was simple. Unfortunately, the stay itself did not match the price. My room looked only superficially cleaned; there were crumbs by the window, dust on the desk, and a questionable stain on the chair. The bathroom was especially disappointing, with poor lighting, a slow-draining sink, and mildew around the shower seal. When I mentioned the drain and asked for extra towels, the front desk acted as though I was inconveniencing them and nothing was addressed until the next day. The bed was comfortable enough, but the worn room and indifferent service made this feel far from a polished hotel experience.

What a fabulous hotel! From its location directly on the Magnificant Mile and surrounded by the finest shopping, to the curtious staff and excellent restaurants and bars, this hotel is one of the best in Chicago. Our room was very clean and fresh, the public areas comfortable and the staff at the concierge and front desk very extremely helpful. This is the only place to stay to be in the cnetre of the action in Chicago. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!

We arrived and thought for $350 a night, it would be a decent place. Good reviews,etc... We arrived to find that the website pictures were misleading. The hotel lounge was a 'room', it was really odd and very dark. The first night there I noticed that the blanket on the bed was nasty looking. Resembled something you'd find on a street. To top it all off we woke up after night #2 to find that bed bugs had attacked us. My husband and I were both bitten. I was bitten WAY more than my husband. My legs were covered with bites. I was on ointments and Benadryl for over a week. I immediately came home and scalded all our clothes. There was also mold around the tub both inside it and on the floor by it. The bathroom floor was also curling up by the tub. The view in room #607 is of a roof. Not good. The stay was VERY disappointing. The only good thing there is the free breakfast on every floor.

Honestly, I expected way more from a hotel with this name on it. Check-in took almost forty minutes because they'd somehow lost my reservation, and by the time I got to my room around 6pm, the tech I'd requested still wasn't set up. The room itself looked tired--scuffed baseboards, a stained armchair in the corner, and the air conditioning rattled all night no matter what I did with the thermostat. Housekeeping skipped my room entirely on the second day even after I called twice about it. Breakfast was the real letdown though: cold eggs, no decaf available, and a hostess who seemed annoyed anyone showed up before 8. The location is genuinely convenient, which is the only nice thing I can say. For nearly $400 a night, this was a disappointing stay and I won't be returning.

The Fairmont turned out to be exactly what I needed after a messy travel day. Check-in was smooth and the front desk agent noticed my exhaustion and offered a late checkout without me even asking--that little gesture set the tone. The room itself was classic and quiet, with a genuinely comfortable bed and blackout curtains that worked. I slept like a log. The lobby feels grand without being stuffy, and the location is perfect for wandering down to the waterfront or grabbing a cab. I had breakfast at the restaurant one morning and the eggs benedict was properly done, not the usual hotel mush. Housekeeping was unobtrusive and thorough. My only minor gripe is that the hallway ice machine was out of order, but that's a blip. I'd happily book here again for a city stay.
Great stay overall -- spotless bathroom with strong water pressure, wifi was fast and reliable, and the room was blissfully quiet. Slept like a rock both nights. Would happily return.

I stayed here with a dozen of my friends, and more than half of us got eaten alive by bed bugs! We stayed there from September 28 - September 30th, but the symptoms (i.e. the crazy itchiness) didn't come until Sunday night when we all got home. I complained to the hotel and basically all they're gonna do is cover the cost of our dry cleaning bills. Honestly, they should reimburse us, because it was not worth it at all. DO NOT STAY AT THIS HOTEL!!!

I reserved the 'Rock star' suite for my boyfriend's birthday months and months in advanced. When we arrived at the Hotel Monaco, they told us that they doubled booked the room. This was after many emails to the hotel inquiring about the room and if it was available. They tried to make up for it by providing us with a room with a wonderful view of the river and giving us a ten dollar gift certificate to their resturant - which we didn't even use. I felt we were taken advantage of because we were young. The doorman didn't make us feel any better when he told us that it wasn't the first time they did this for the 'rock star' suite. However, the conceirge was incredible with providing us with a bottle of champagne for his birthday and delivered the birthday cake I ordered. If it wasn't for the room confusion - It would have been a wonderful stay.

Hotel Amalfi was a lovely base for our weekend. The location made it easy to walk to cafes, shops, and the waterfront, yet our room was surprisingly quiet at night. We had a bright, spotless room with a very comfortable bed and good air conditioning, which was appreciated after long days out. Breakfast was simple but fresh, with pastries, fruit, eggs, and decent coffee. The front desk team really made the stay: they were warm, efficient, and gave us excellent restaurant suggestions without being pushy. The bathroom was a little compact, and the elevator can be slow during busy morning hours, but neither issue affected our overall experience. I'd happily stay here again.

I had a very comfortable three-night stay at the Talbott. The front desk team was warm and efficient, and they happily arranged a taxi and suggested a couple of nearby restaurants without making the conversation feel rehearsed. My room was spotless when I arrived, with fresh linens, a well-kept bathroom, and plenty of space to unpack. I was pleasantly surprised by how quiet it stayed at night; despite being in a busy part of the city, I rarely heard hallway or street noise. The location in the Gold Coast was especially convenient, with shops, cafes, and the lakefront all within an easy walk. The decor felt a little traditional, but everything was comfortable and in good condition. I would gladly stay here again on my next Chicago visit.

I expected more from the Omni given the rate and reputation. The location was convenient for walking to restaurants and downtown meetings, which was the one real advantage. Unfortunately, the room felt dated, and the bathroom was especially disappointing: dim lighting, worn grout around the tub, and weak water pressure made getting ready unpleasant. I also barely slept because the hallway noise carried straight through the door and the air-conditioning rattled on and off all night. Staff were polite, but a polite greeting does not make up for a tired room and poor rest. For the price, I expected cleaner finishes, better soundproofing, and a more comfortable stay.

I stayed at Hotel Allegro for a long weekend and came away very happy with the choice. The lobby has a lively, old-school theater feel without being too formal, and the front desk staff were friendly whenever I had a question. My room was on the smaller side, but it was comfortable, quiet, and nicely laid out, with a surprisingly good bed and plenty of outlets near the desk. Everything was clean, including the bathroom, and housekeeping did a thorough job each day. The location is excellent for exploring downtown, with restaurants, the river, and several theaters within an easy walk. I also appreciated being able to leave my bags after checkout. It is not the newest hotel in Chicago, but the character, service, and convenient location made it a very enjoyable stay.

Stayed here for a conference and was genuinely impressed. The staff were warm and efficient, and the location made getting around town a breeze. My room had a lovely skyline view, and I slept like a log on that comfy bed.

We got a great deal on this hotel, just $91 found through travelzoo. We only stayed one night, but were very impressed. The sevice was fantastic from the moment we stepped up to the property. The hotel smelled wonderful and was immaculate. Our room, while not enormous was perfect. We had a great view of the city and lake. The bed was extremely comfortable. We never heard any noise outside of our room. The bathroom was nice sized considering we must have had one of the smaller rooms in the hotel, two could get ready very comfortably. Location was perfect, just off Michigan Ave and steps away from Millenium Park. We would definetly stay here again, especially if we could get this great deal!
The room was tired and the AC sounded like a jet engine all night. Staff were indifferent when I complained, and the pool felt more like a crowded public bath. Left with a sour taste for the price.

Swissotel continues to be a *yawn* As previous posters state, punching in your floor is ridiculous. On the other hand, technology wise it could be helpful in routing ppl to different elevators (but if idiots like to cram into one elevator and leave the others free for me, why change)? In any case, I want to take a nice hot soak and--guess what--they are having water problems... SOOOOO disappointed. Hopefully I don't get bug bitten this time (checked under the sheets). Sadly, due to my company's deal, I think I have to stay here again next year *sigh*...but so far they are batting 1 star.... -------------- Oh boy, it must be my luck...or rather this hotel is just run down. I had to swap room FOUR TIMES. And that's for a Thurs nite-Sunday morning stay. My first room had no hot water so I had to switch rooms. They gave me the key to the 2nd room, which happened to be occupied. Luckily the occupants had their security latch on, so there wasn't any embarrassing moment. My third room was fine for 2 nights but then today (just now) I had to move because of water leakage (above my room and below my room). BOY, talk about an awful hotel (or my just awful luck???? Maybe it's karma since I wrote a bad review last year, and continue to write one...but it's the TRUTH). Oh, also last year may not have been bed bugs. I have checked the room and it looks bug free but I STILL get these itchy patches on my leg. Perhaps it is something in the sheets...or the air/HVAC.... in any case, despite the decent staff, it is a ONE at best (0 for hotel, 1 for the still nice service--since it's not their fault....) All I can say is ...THANK GOODNESS MY COMPANY WON'T HOLD THE CONFERENCE IN CHICAGO NEXT YEAR, or AT LEAST AT THIS HOTEL!!!!!!!!

I had a very pleasant stay at Swissotel and would happily return. The check-in process was quick and friendly, even though I arrived a little earlier than the official time. My room was spacious, clean, and nicely quiet, with a comfortable bed and a great city view. I especially appreciated the practical touches, including plenty of outlets, good water pressure, and a small area where I could work. Breakfast offered a wide variety, from fresh fruit and pastries to hot local dishes, and the staff kept everything well stocked. The location was also convenient for getting around, with restaurants and public transport nearby. The only minor issue was that the Wi-Fi slowed down in the evening, but overall the service, comfort, and atmosphere made this a very satisfying stay.
The staff were lovely, but the room felt tired and the AC barely worked. The hallway noise kept me up all night, and breakfast was a sad, overpriced buffet. Not the Sheraton standard I remembered.

I really wanted to like this place, but too many small issues added up to a frustrating stay. The room itself was clean and decently sized, but the air conditioning was nearly useless--it just barely took the edge off, even after maintenance fiddled with it. I tried calling the front desk twice after 10 PM about some hallway noise, and nobody picked up. When I walked down, there was a single frazzled employee who said he'd 'make a note,' but nothing ever changed. The breakfast buffet was genuinely disappointing for the price; the eggs were rubbery and the coffee tasted burnt. Check-in also took over twenty minutes because they insisted on verifying my reservation through some offline system that kept lagging. On a positive note, the location was convenient and the lobby was lovely. But for over $250 a night, I expect a working thermostat and responsive staff. I'll likely look elsewhere next time.
Swissotel looked polished, but our room was noisy all night and the air conditioning barely worked. Staff apologized, yet no real solution came, making the stay feel overpriced.

Genuinely lovely stay--the concierge sorted our dinner reservations in minutes, and the king suite was spotless with a gorgeous harbour view. Breakfast spread was top-notch too. Will absolutely be back.

Booked the Conrad expecting the usual five-star polish, but this stay left a sour taste. Check-in was painfully slow, and the front desk seemed more interested in their phones than acknowledging me. The room itself was tired--stained carpet, a bathroom door that wouldn't close properly, and a view of a concrete wall. Housekeeping never came until I called twice, and even then they only swapped towels. The restaurant at breakfast served lukewarm eggs and coffee that tasted burnt; I ended up eating out. On top of that, the air conditioning rattled all night, so I barely slept. For the price, I've had better experiences at boutique hotels. Honestly, the staff's indifference was the biggest letdown--nobody asked about my stay or offered a solution when I mentioned the noise at checkout. Just a flat 'sorry' and a receipt. Won't be back.

Our corner room at the Knickerbocker was a pleasant surprise. The view stretched from the glittering Magnificent Mile down to the lake, and I found myself just watching the city lights at dusk, which felt like a free show. Given the prime location, I'd say the rate was fair--not a bargain, but you're paying for that postcard scenery and the easy stroll to everything. The front desk crew were genuinely warm, even when we asked for extra towels twice, and the doorman remembered our names by the second day. The bathroom, though compact, had a rainfall shower with strong pressure and fluffy robes that made it feel indulgent. The bed was plush, and the blackout curtains worked perfectly. Only minor hiccup: the elevator wait during checkout rush. Still, I left rested, impressed, and already planning a return.

Having stayed at the excellent Affinia chain in NY, I had very high expectations. When I saw the Trip Advisor rating, I immediately booked. What a huge disappointment: -- The quality Simmons pillow top mattress is covered with very cheap, foam pillows -- the kind they sell in the store for $4. You cannot sleep on these -- The windows are so thin, you can hear the buzzing from walk/don't walk sign on Superior below. -- The walls are so thin that when my neighbor smoked, I was awaken around midnight, my room engulfed in smoke odor. A call downstairs yielded no results -- There are nice furnishings but many are chipped showing bare wood; the desk chair was full of loose threads -- The water flow is very weak, but the towels are nice -- There are unpainted floorboards, the kind you find in Day's Inn -- They charge for internet service The tiny lobby has materials and pictures of what the hotel will eventually look like. The sign outside is also a banner. Having stayed all over the U.S., you are better off at Red Roof -- this is really an embarassment for the Affinia chain. Wait until they complete the renovations in 2008. I did supply this feedback at my checkout and the front desk apologized by shaking my hand. Good heart, but the problems are not fixable.

Stayed three nights for a business trip and was genuinely impressed. The room was spotless--fresh linens, no dust on the baseboards, and the housekeeping even folded my loose charger cord neatly. For the rate I paid, it felt like a steal compared to the chain hotels nearby. The bathroom was compact but modern, with a rainfall showerhead that had strong, hot pressure and those thick towels that actually absorb. I slept like a log both nights; the blackout curtains did their job, and the mattress was firm but supportive, no springs poking through. Only minor gripe: hallway noise bled through around 7 a.m. on the last morning. Still, I'd book again without hesitation--clean, quiet enough, and honestly a great value for the location.
The Amalfi made me wish I'd booked one more night--I slept like a log in the plush bed, woke to a stunning bay view, and felt every euro was justified. A rare, restorative gem.

I booked the InterContinental expecting a touch of grandeur, but the reality felt like a faded postcard. The lobby's marble gleams, sure, but the hallway carpets are worn, and the room's furniture looks straight out of the late '90s, with scuffed edges and a tired floral armchair. The bed was comfortable enough, but the cleanliness was spotty--I found a stale receipt under the desk and dust bunnies lurking by the baseboards. Our one-night stop felt both rushed and interminable; the paper-thin walls let me hear every door slam and hallway conversation, so I got little rest. The bathroom was the low point: a cracked tile, a showerhead with uneven pressure, and a faint musty smell that no amount of ventilation could fix. For this price, I expected polish, not patina. I won't return.

This was our third trip to Chicago this year (we LOVE the city!) - every time we stay at a different downtown hotel. Swissotel was definitely our favourite. When we come back in July to see the play ' Wicked' for the second time, we will be again at Swissotel. No more need to try other hotels! The location is good because it is between the financial district and the Magnificent Mile. The room was spotless and quiet, the view amazing and those elevators were so fast. Comfortable beds, friendly service, not as many noisy sirens! We even watched the Navy Pier fireworks from our bed! This was the best anniversary ever. We would recommend Swissotel to everyone!

We stayed at the Hard Rock for a long weekend celebrating our anniversary, and the whole experience exceeded our hopes. The view from our room, which faced the lagoon, turned out to be a real highlight. Watching the sunsets reflect off the pool area was a subtle, beautiful touch we didn't expect. The room itself was spotless, from the gleaming bathroom to the crisp, white linens; housekeeping clearly takes pride in their work. I slept better than I have in months, honestly. The blackout curtains truly blocked every sliver of light, and the bed was that perfect mix of firm and plush. Every staff member we encountered, from the valet to the baristas, was genuinely warm and helpful without being intrusive. They even left a handwritten note and a small dessert for our anniversary, which felt personal, not manufactured. We'll definitely be back for another escape. The convenience and energy were remarkable.

Great location, but that's where the positives end. The front desk staff were polite enough, but check-in took forever because they seemed to be juggling three tasks at once. Got to our room and it was stuffy, with a lingering musty smell like the AC filter hadn't been changed in months. The 'city view' was mostly a brick wall and a sliver of the neighboring rooftop. Housekeeping only came by when we called, and even then, they forgot to replace the towels. The breakfast buffet was a nightmare--cold scrambled eggs, stale pastries, and coffee that tasted burnt. On our last night, the hallway was noisy until 2 AM with what sounded like a party, and the walls were thin enough to hear every word. I really wanted to like this place, but for the price, I expected a lot more. Won't be back.

Lovely stay at the Sofitel--spotless marble bathroom with a great rainfall shower, and despite the central location the room was impressively quiet at night. Not cheap, but the walkability made it worth every penny. Would gladly return.

We stayed 2 nights over spring break in what was called a Jr Suite but resembled a wide hallway with a window at one end. Bad cheap furniture, carpet that stops short of reaching the wall, a TV that sticks out into the middle of the room and a window that whistled when the wind blew. BAD BAD experience. Find aother hotel plenty in the area.

Checked in at 3 PM, but the room wasn't ready until nearly 5, and no one offered so much as a complimentary drink while we waited in the crowded lobby. The wifi was practically useless in our room--kept dropping every few minutes, making any work impossible. Staff were polite but visibly overwhelmed, and my request for extra towels took three calls and an hour. For the premium rate we paid, the carpet looked stained and the bathroom had a lingering musty smell. We booked three nights, but by the second morning, we were already counting the hours to checkout. The location is convenient, sure, but this felt like a $120 motel experience dressed up with a fancy lobby. I'd rather have skipped the last night entirely than paid what they charged. Genuinely disappointing for a brand I once trusted.
Disappointing stay at the Hotel Palmer. Room smelled musty, the AC barely worked, and front desk staff seemed annoyed every time we asked a question. Definitely not worth the price.

Stunning property with impeccable service. The room was luxurious and quiet, and the staff anticipated our every need. The breakfast buffet was outstanding, a perfect start to exploring the city. We can't wait to return.

This was the 2nd time that we have stayed at the Hyatt Regency Chicago. The first time was far above our expectations for a $69/per night room. The rooms are very nice, and the beds are comfortable. This time we got a great rate through travelzoo @ $104/ night for a room with a view. We were aware of the $41 parking per night. The first night we got there the valet was yelling at us and said that we couldn't park they were full. We had no clue where to park at this point and had to drive around for over 45 minutes looking at closed parking garages. (It was a Saturday evening) Finally found a spot and were told that it would be $38. This was 6 blocks from the hotel. Mind you its -6 outside and we have luggage to carry too. Not very good service for a 5-star hotel. We got inside and apparently they were running a nightclub out of thier lobby, its called the harddrive. That's cool and all, yes it was very noisy but once we got to our room, it wasn't an issue. The HVAC controls to our room were broken. The first night we were ok, but by the second night it was blazing hot in there, 86 degrees. So hot we couldn't sleep. It was miserable. They sent up the 'engineer' and he determined that there was definately a problem and opened our window, 24 floors up. It never did cool down enough in there we kept that window open all night. It was 5 below that night and the window being open 8' didn't help. They would not put us in another room either. At checkout, Monday morning, our bill came to $240.43 after taxes for the room. We then had a second bill in which our internet and parking was billed on for $56.65. Cool, I got my reciepts and went on our way. On Wednesday I was on my online banking checking my account, to find that Hyatt charged me $289.03 and another charge of $103.63!!! That is almost $100 more than what the reciepts from checkout say. I was furious, so I called the hotel. Nothing was resolved by my phone call, they treated me as if $100 isn't but something you wipe with. She said give it another day or two and see if the additional authorization falls off. That didn't settle well with me, but what could I do. I waited. Its Friday now. I check on my account again and the charges cleared as they should have with the correct original amounts, and they still have 'authorizations' on the two incorrect amounts as well. They have charged me an additional $300!!!!!! Im so furious! and guess what... Hyatt doesn't care. They gave me the same [--] line as they did Wednesday. SAVE YOURSELF SOME HASSLE AND DON'T STAY AT THIS HOTEL UNLESS YOU HAVE EXTRA MONEY FOR THEM TO PLAY WITH.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly, it exceeded expectations. The location is unbeatable--steps from all the action but the rooms are surprisingly quiet, so you get the best of both worlds. Loved the quirky, colorful decor; it's not your typical boring chain hotel. The staff were genuinely friendly, especially the bartender in the lobby who recommended a great local spot for brunch. My room was spotless, bed super comfy, and the blackout curtains worked wonders. Only tiny hiccup was the elevator wait Saturday morning, but it cleared up fast. Would absolutely book again for a city escape.

I had high hopes for the Hyatt based on the brand name, but this stay was a letdown from start to finish. The check-in line moved at a snail's pace, and when I finally got to the desk, they'd lost my reservation details even though I had the confirmation email right on my phone. The room itself felt tired and musty, with a scratchy carpet and a bathroom that smelled faintly of mildew. The bed was lumpy, and the pillows were flat as pancakes. I tried to order room service for a quick dinner, and the food arrived cold and undercooked, with the wrong side dish. The gym was cramped, with two broken treadmills and no water refill station. I expected more from a property with this name, and honestly, I left feeling like I wasted my money. I won't be back.

The staff seemed bothered by every request, and the bathroom had a lingering mildew smell. For the price, the stained carpet and dusty surfaces made it feel like a budget hostel, not a four-star hotel.

It is always interesting going to a high quality Hotel. I cannot help but think about the service and the value. Maybe I have too high expectations. Certaintly the location is great and the swimming pool is really nice and the room was generally well appointed oh and the bed was great. But, the room was not well cleaned, a little smelly truthfully and they stole a watch that I left in the room. The hotel where immediately worried about there financial situation and not the service. I noticed here others on this site have lost stuff from this hotel. I know that this is always a possibility but really did not expect it at a hotel like this. Overall, Chicago exceeded my expectations but the intercontinental did not. Stay else where.

We were disappointed with this hotel. The staff seems hurried and unhelpful. Our room was not made up until after 5 PM despite several requests. The blower in the hallway blew freezing air, but the staff told us that there was nothing that could be done about it. The lobby is not inviting and there is no where comfortable to sit. The room and bed was comfortable, but the cream and and modern art work are not our style. The room lacked many of the amenities other hotels in this price range offer. Certainly not worth the rate compared to other hotels I have stayed at in Chicago.

Lovely stay at Hotel Allegro. The bathroom was spotless with a strong shower, and breakfast offered fresh pastries and good coffee. Staff were welcoming and efficient, making the fair price feel like excellent value for a comfortable, hassle-free visit.
Sofitel looked polished online, but our room smelled damp, the air conditioning rattled all night, and reception barely acknowledged the complaint. Not worth the price.
Disappointing stay at Hotel Palmer--the room was dated, the hallway smelled musty, and staff seemed indifferent when we asked for help. Definitely not worth the price.
The Conrad felt worth the rate, with fresh, understated decor, dependable Wi-Fi, and a very convenient location near restaurants and transit. I'd gladly book it again.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly, it exceeded expectations for the rate we booked. The room was spotless, with a bed that made it hard to get up in the morning--those blackout curtains actually work. Bathroom was a highlight: rainfall shower with strong pressure and plenty of hot water, plus the towels were thick and plush, not those scratchy hospital ones. Wi-Fi was surprisingly reliable; I streamed a movie without a single buffering pause. I was worried about street noise, but the double-glazed windows kept everything silent--we heard nothing but the AC hum at night. The location is convenient too, a short walk to tourist spots but far enough to escape the crowds. Sure, the lobby gets busy, but for the comfort level, I'd definitely book again. Worth every penny.

Great stay at the Swissotel--spacious room with a stunning city view, comfortable beds, and the staff couldn't have been friendlier. Location is walking distance to everything. Would definitely return.

Stayed here for a corporate event and left genuinely puzzled by the hype. The lobby looks impressive in photos, but the reality is worn edges, scuffed hallways, and an elevator system that felt like a daily puzzle. Check-in took over twenty minutes despite booking weeks ahead, and the front desk seemed more interested in chatting among themselves than acknowledging a queue. My room faced an interior courtyard, so natural light was basically a rumor. The carpet had visible stains near the window, and the bathroom sink drained so slowly I had to brush my teeth in shifts. Housekeeping skipped two of my four nights entirely. Breakfast buffet was a sad parade of lukewarm eggs and dry pastries, priced like a fine dining experience. I've stayed at far cheaper properties with better mattresses and actual soundproofing--the hallway noise at 2 AM was relentless. It's not awful, but for this price point and brand name, it's a letdown.
My stay at the Conrad felt too short, but I slept wonderfully in the quiet, comfortable bed. The fresh, polished decor and spotless marble bathroom made it easy to relax.

The Omni Chicago really delivers on all fronts, from the spaciousness of the rooms to the helpful staff to the prized location on Michigan Avenue. While this address in Chicago requires a high level of quality, the Omni delivers. Check in for myself and a whole group of people with me was under 3 minutes, the staff had plentiful recommendations for dining and events, and the rooms are some of the largest you'll find at this price range in Chicago. Even the 'standard' room has a separate living area and work desk. The fitness center has free weights, weight machines, and two rows of cardio equipment. I shared the room with 7 others and did not feel cramped in any way! All in all, a great property!

The Talbott was a really pleasant surprise for our weekend in Chicago. The location is hard to beat--quiet enough to sleep well, but only a few minutes from Michigan Avenue, restaurants, and the lake. Our room felt classic rather than overly trendy, with a comfortable bed, plenty of space, and a spotless bathroom. I especially appreciated the little touches, like good water pressure and enough outlets near the bed. Everyone at the front desk was warm and helpful, offering directions and storing our bags after checkout without making it feel like a hassle. We also enjoyed coffee in the lobby before heading out each morning. It's not a flashy mega-hotel, which was honestly part of the charm. I'd happily stay here again.

After reading the reviews on this hotel, I decided to book my stay for July 4th weekend here and I am glad I did, this hotel is absolutely beautiful. Our suite was gorgeous it is a very romantic hotel with big sit in picture windows. I do have 1 complaint. The bar is very boring and the resturant is not that great, but other than that I loved it. I would definitely stay there again.
Hard Rock felt worth the price: our spotless room had a lively, fresh design and a great city view that made mornings especially enjoyable.

We recently stayed at the Intercontinental Hotel for a week. The hotel was in a wonderful location and the service was great. We found all of the staff very helpful and prompt. We highly recommend the Intercontinental for any travel needs whether it be for business or pleasure.
Hyatt delivered a pleasant stay: breakfast had fresh pastries and hot options, Wi‐Fi was reliable, staff were warmly attentive, and the room stayed impressively quiet at night.
Hotel Amalfi looked promising, but the room was cramped, the air conditioning barely worked, and breakfast felt stale. Staff seemed indifferent when we mentioned the noise.

I expected more from Homewood for the rate we paid. The location was convenient for our meetings and close to restaurants, which was the best part of the stay. Unfortunately, the room felt worn, with stained carpet and a bathroom that needed better cleaning. WiFi technically worked, but it was painfully slow in the evening and kept dropping during a video call. Noise was another issue: we could hear hallway conversations, doors slamming, and traffic well past midnight. Breakfast was picked over by 8:30 and staff seemed overwhelmed. For the price, this stay was disappointing and I would likely choose another nearby hotel next time.

I really wanted to like this place, but our stay at the Hotel Monaco fell flat on almost every count. Check-in took nearly half an hour because they claimed they couldn't find our reservation, even though I had the confirmation email right on my phone. The room itself was smaller than the photos suggested, and the air conditioning rattled all night like it was about to give up. Housekeeping skipped our room completely one day, and when we called the front desk about it, we got a shrug and a promise that never materialized. The location is decent and the lobby is pretty, sure, but that doesn't make up for lukewarm breakfast, hallway noise, and the overall sense that the money we spent went straight into the interior design rather than the service. Won't be back.

Very centrally located in the Loop directly south of the 7th Day Adventist Church (my room looked down upon Wacker Drive, the aforementioned church and the Chicago River. Small room, virtually no storage space. Attended a conference with the Monaco as venue. They provided adequate service, with no problems. This was the first time I spent with a Kimpton Hotel and I registered for their Frequent Stay program. I never felt comfortable in this hotel. I'm 60 yrs old and it appears the clientele they target is half my age. Rude front deskperson of unidentifiable gender. The young people can have at it. I'll stay at the Marriott Michigan Ave next time.

Stayed here for a conference and left underwhelmed. The room smelled musty, housekeeping skipped our floor until late afternoon, and the air conditioning rattled all night. Overpriced for what feels like a dated property coasting on its name.

As a frequent traveler to Chicago, I generally stay at the Sutton Court, but thought I would try a different boutique hotel. I will never stay at this hotel again. The first room they brought me to -- their standard room -- was a glorified closet, leaving me absolutely claustrophobic! Actually the smallest hotel room I've been in in the U.S! I complained to the front desk, who then moved me to a 'premium' room -- still quite small, but manageably so. The bathroom was tiny, without a vanity, making it difficult to put your toiletries in the room. The location leaves much to be desired, as my room looked out directly onto the El (elevated subway - background noise), and the street was pretty deserted on a Sunday evening. I will say that the free wi-fi was great. If you can find a chain or other hotel closer to Michigan Avene, I'd highly recommend you take that. If you want a nice room in a great location, check out Sutton Place hotel instead.

I expected a much better experience from the InterContinental, but several things fell short. Check-in took nearly 25 minutes, even though the lobby was not particularly busy, and the staff member seemed distracted and uninformed about basic questions regarding breakfast and the pool. Our room looked tired, with scuffed furniture, a stained carpet near the window, and a bathroom fan that rattled loudly throughout the night. Housekeeping also forgot to replace the coffee and bottled water on the second day. The bed was comfortable, and the location was convenient, but those positives did not justify the high rate. For a hotel carrying the InterContinental name, the service and upkeep felt surprisingly ordinary. I left disappointed and would probably choose another property next time.

This is an older hotel, and the age shows. Rooms are small, and a bit drab. Bathroom in my room was in urgent need of upgrade. Bed was comfortable, though, and the room was quiet, Hotel staff was polite, but not really interested in the guest. Even the concierge was disinterested. Check-in was irritatingly slow for the few number of people in line. Really, a hotel tjhat promises so much in its promotional material should deliver better. The hotel really didnt seem to be trying.

Beautiful hotel, but the Wi-Fi kept dropping, making work impossible. I slept poorly on the rock-hard mattress. For this price, it felt like a total rip-off, and thankfully my one night was mercifully brief.

My stay was quick but awesome. After a long day, seeing a substantial line at check-in was a bit of a groaner, but then i saw the self-serve kiosks. i was checked in with keys in hand in under 3 minutes. in the morning i was able to check out on the TV in my room. the hotel is a beautiful historic landmark with all the amenities of a modern hotel and all the charm of its 1927 origins. The bed was FABULOUSLY comfortable. i wish i could live there. they have many rooms wtih 2 bathrooms. i stayed in a room like that once with a friend and we didn't know ahead of time that we had two bathrooms. talk about squeals of delight. that was about 7 years ago in virginia beach. i was by myself at the hilton and had no need for a room with two bathrooms, but it's the first time i've seen this since. what a great feature!

I had a very comfortable three-night stay at Hotel Monaco. The room was bright, nicely decorated, and larger than I expected, with a comfortable bed and a useful sitting area by the window. Wi‐Fi worked reliably throughout the stay, including for video calls, and connecting was quick. The bathroom was spotless and well stocked, although the counter space was a little limited; the shower had good water pressure and plenty of hot water. Despite being downtown, the hotel was surprisingly quiet at night. I occasionally heard hallway doors, but street noise never disturbed me. The location made everything easy, with restaurants, shops, and major attractions within a short walk, plus public transportation nearby. Staff were friendly and responsive whenever I needed anything. I would gladly stay here again.

I booked the Monaco for a two-night romantic getaway, and frankly, it felt about two nights too long. We checked in with high hopes, but the magic evaporated quickly. The bed was impossibly hard, like sleeping on a concrete slab wrapped in a sheet, and I woke up each morning with a stiff back and a foul mood. Our room faced a brick wall and a noisy ventilation shaft, so the 'city view' was a literal brick joke. The promised high-speed Wi-Fi was a cruel myth; it dropped constantly, making it impossible to stream anything or even scroll social media without frustration. The whole experience felt soulless and overpriced. I'd rather sleep in my car than spend another restless, disconnected night here. Save your money.

My first stay at this hotel and was expecting good things based on reviews. For some reason, I kept being disappointed at every turn. Noisy room on the 4th floor. Could not get the room to cool down - it was stifling. BE WARNED - No water, no mini-bar no vending machine, no nothing once you get in your room. You might as well be in prison. They have coffee in the morning, but it starts at 6 so I had to wait both days. I guess that is convenient for them, but what about me? Workout facility - pretty small but not the smallest. The only treadmill I could get on was broken. Guess what a cooler with water in it! Oh no - it was only stocked for one day. After that nothing. Way to set expectations and then fail to deliver. Same with towels - one day they have them - next day they don't. They essentially forced me to sign up for their loyalty program to avoid a riduculous $10 charge for wireless (go a few doors down to Starbucks where it is free). They should fire the marketing moron who came up with that approach. I have stayed at much better for less. Won't be coming back.

The Intercontinental surprised me--fresh, updated decor and a spotless bathroom with great water pressure. It felt worth every dollar, though honestly our three-night stay was over too soon. We'll be back for longer next time.
Loved the playful decor and welcoming staff at Hotel Monaco. Our room was spotless, the bed incredibly comfortable, and the downtown location made exploring restaurants and shops easy.
Despite the convenient downtown location, our view was a dull parking garage, traffic noise lasted all night, and staff seemed dismissive when we asked for help.

We booked Affinia expecting a polished stay, but it felt more like a faded chain trying too hard. Breakfast was a cramped buffet of lukewarm scrambled eggs and stale pastries, and the coffee tasted burnt. The wifi dropped constantly, making it impossible to stream anything or even load a basic map without frustration. Our room faced an interior airshaft, so the 'view' was just a brick wall and a humming vent. Noise was the worst part--thin walls meant every hallway conversation and door slam echoed through the night, and we got little sleep. The bed was decent, but that's about the only compliment. Staff were polite but couldn't resolve the internet or offer a quieter floor. For the price they charge, this was a letdown. I'd look elsewhere unless you're desperate and don't mind feeling like you're in a budget hostel with nicer curtains.

My stay at Hotel Palmer was disappointing overall. The location is convenient, with restaurants and public transportation close by, but that was the main advantage. The room was not as clean as expected: there was dust on the bedside table, hair in the bathroom, and the carpet looked overdue for a deep cleaning. Noise was another problem. I could hear doors slamming and conversations in the hallway late into the night, so sleeping was difficult. The front desk staff were polite enough, but they seemed distracted and did not show much urgency when I reported the issue. The room also felt dated, with worn furniture and weak water pressure. Given the price, I expected a more comfortable and better-maintained stay.

The staff genuinely made our anniversary unforgettable, upgrading our room and charming us with a thoughtful dessert. The bed was pure cloud, and that harbor-view breakfast beat any tourist spot. We didn't want to leave.

We stayed at the Omni between Christmas and New Year's in 2008 just to get away for a few days. We found it through web deals and got a penthouse suite very cheap. So this year we checked online just a day or so after Christmas and the deal was there again. It also included parking at the great price. Huge suite overlooking downtown Chicago. Best location to walk EVERYWHERE. My 12 and 11 yr olds loved swimming at night and the chocolate cookies on their pillows. Can't wait to go back.

Booked the Swissotel for a weekend getaway, and honestly, I should have trusted the mixed reviews. The lobby looks impressive, but that's where the polish ends. Our room faced the inner courtyard, so all we saw was a concrete wall, and the window wouldn't open more than a crack. The air conditioning sounded like a freight train and cycled all night, so sleep was nearly impossible. Housekeeping knocked at 8:30 a.m. on Saturday, then again at 9, even though we had the do-not-disturb sign up. The bathroom had a nice shower, but the grout was stained and the drain was slow. Breakfast was a crowded, overpriced buffet with lukewarm eggs and watery coffee. Check-out took forever with only one person at the desk while three guests waited. For the price, this was a real letdown--location is convenient, but the service and room basics feel neglected.

The bathroom was spotless with a rainfall shower that made the stay feel indulgent. Despite being near the busy Opera district, our room stayed wonderfully quiet. It's pricey, but the central location and comfort justify it; I'd happily return.

Stayed here on business a few nights and really liked it. Very attractive, classy and comfortable hotel that's got an element of sexy and sharp. Public spaces are very nice, with an open area bar in the front lobby and nice sitting areas. Rooms are lovely as well, with handsome fixtures and furniture, a terrific desk work space and comfortable bed. Bathroom amenities and fixtures are sleek and attractive as well. Best of all, the hotel has breathtaking views of the city and the water - both the river and the lake. If you're working in the area, it's the best choice for that part of town, and I prefer it to the nearby Hyatt and Monaco.
Two nights here felt like a week. The decor is stuck in the 80s, the bathroom wasn't properly cleaned, and for what we paid it was a complete rip-off. Won't be back.

We recently completed our second stay at the Fairmont Chicago. The check-in process was quick and painless but the front desk staff was almost disinterested in the whole procedure. That is fine when I am traveling on business, but on leisure trips I would appreciate a warmer greeting. The hotel was hosting a convention at the same time as our stay, but other than seeing some signage/attendees in the lobby, we wouldn't have noticed. This is probably due to the separation of the conference areas from the guest rooms and the 8 speedy elevators. We stayed in a Parkview Suite so we had a large room with a great view of Millenium Park. The anteroom was well appointed with a sofa, coffee table, desk, mini-bar with sink and coffee maker, and dining area. The bedroom appeared to be the same as a standard Fairmont room, but maybe slightly larger. The bathroom also appeared to be similar to a standard Fairmont room, and once again, possibly slightly larger. The upscale modern decor is pleasing but not overtly luxurious, and several small touches such as a shoe shine station (with extra collar tabs), are peppered throughout. We booked a few evening activities through the concierge and everything was perfectly handled. The hotel restaurant, Aria, couldn't find our reservation but they oddly new my name and remembered that the hotel had called to make a reservation for us. They had no problem seating us and the dinner (both food and service) was lovely. Minor complaints: The pillows could be better. I'm not sure if they remembered our preference for non-down bedding from our last visit, but seriously, these things barely felt like pillows. I'll suffer through some congestion if I can get better neck support. Also, the valet parking attendants seem overly eager to take your car (and charge you $49). And as I mentioned above, the front desk experience could be improved. Best feature: After our first stay, I gave a brief review in the comments section of the Fairmont President's Club (membership is free) website. I received a phone call from the Director of Rooms the same day asking to discuss our experience. After this stay, I left a comment essentially thanking the hotel staff for a great stay, but still received a warm, friendly phone call from the Director of Rooms asking if he could do anything to improve our next stay. Kudos to the Fairmont for taking its customers seriously, and for that, they've won my loyalty.

The location is unbeatable for sightseeing, right by the river and a short stroll to the Old Town. We booked a standard room and were pleasantly surprised by the space, plus the soundproofing was perfect--slept like a baby despite the bustling city outside. The breakfast spread deserves a special mention: fresh pastries, made-to-order eggs, and a great selection of local cheeses. Staff were professional and friendly, quickly sorting out an extra pillow request and recommending a fantastic restaurant for dinner. My only minor gripe was the slightly slow Wi-Fi in the evenings, but it didn't ruin anything. The gym is small but well-equipped, and the pool area is a nice bonus after a long day of walking. For the price and quality, I would definitely stay here again on my next trip.

We stayed at the Homewood for three nights while visiting family and honestly it exceeded what I expected for the price. Check-in was quick and the front desk guy (Jamal, I think?) actually gave us a list of local places to eat instead of just handing us a map. The room was spacious with a proper kitchenette, which came in handy more than we thought it would. Bed was comfortable, AC worked well, and the free breakfast had real options, eggs, waffles, fresh fruit, not just sad pastries. One small note: the elevator was a bit slow during peak morning hours, but that's a minor gripe. The evening social on Wednesday with snacks was a nice touch we weren't expecting. Would definitely book here again if we're back in the area. Solid value and genuinely friendly staff.

I expected much more from an InterContinental, especially at the rate we paid. Check-in took nearly half an hour because the room apparently was not ready, despite arriving after 4 p.m. The lobby looked polished, but the room felt tired: stained carpet near the window, a loose bathroom fixture, and a thermostat that either blasted cold air or shut off completely. We called twice about the noisy air conditioner and never received a follow-up. Breakfast was expensive and disappointingly lukewarm, with tables left uncleared for far too long. The location was convenient, but that was really the only positive. Staff were polite when we could get their attention, though the overall service felt understaffed and indifferent. For a supposedly upscale hotel, it was a frustrating and overpriced stay.

Great location near everything downtown, I'll give it that, but two nights here felt more than enough. The front desk was indifferent at check-in, and for what we paid the room felt tired and dated. Not worth the rate.

The view from our room was stunning, and the breakfast spread offered fresh pastries and made-to-order eggs each morning. The location put us steps from the old town, and while the lobby decor feels slightly dated, the overall stay was comfortable and worthwhile.

Other reviews complain about the small rooms. For a major city, we found our room quite comfortable with a king bed and really nice furnishings. One feature we liked is the ability to open the window. The Knikerbocker is a small boutique hotel right off Michigan Avenue in the best area of Chicago. The staff was friendly and helpful. For the $116 we paid on Hotwire, we could not have found a better room in downtown Chicago.

Booked the Hotel Amalfi based on the photos online, but the reality was a letdown from the moment we walked in. The lobby smelled musty, like old carpet and damp towels, and the front desk staff barely acknowledged us while they finished a personal phone call. Our room, supposedly upgraded, faced a brick wall and a clanking air conditioner that sounded like a lawnmower. The bed was lumpy, and the pillows were so thin they were useless. Breakfast was chaotic--empty chafing dishes, stale croissants, and coffee that tasted burnt. To top it off, the pool was closed for 'maintenance' the entire stay, which we only learned about after we'd unpacked. The only positive was the location, but that didn't make up for the dingy room or the indifferent service. For the price, I expected far more. Save your money and book elsewhere.

I really wanted to like the Affinia, given the photos online, but the reality fell far short. The room was stuffy, and the A/C unit sounded like a lawnmower every time it kicked on, making sleep nearly impossible. The carpet had a faint, sour smell that no amount of air freshener could mask. Housekeeping was also spotty--we came back one afternoon to find our coffee cups not replaced and the trash bin only half emptied. The bathroom was cramped, with a showerhead that sprayed in every direction but down. On the plus side, the front desk staff were polite, but they couldn't do much about the noise from the hallway or the paper-thin walls. For the price we paid, I expected a lot more. I genuinely wanted to like this place, but it felt more like a worn-out roadside motel than a boutique hotel. I wouldn't book here again.

What's not to like? --> Problems getting the room you actually reserved: I had to call this hotel three times and email four times in order to insure that we actually got the room we had reserved. --> Overcharging. They charge for everything here. Wireless. The Fitness Center. The Business Center. I've only run into one other hotel that ever charged for use of the fitness center. Note to the Intercontinental: If you're going to charge for something that is commonly included, you should advertise that fact. What's next? Charging for sheets on the bed? --> Very poor customer service. The staff does not communicate in full sentences, or wait to hear your answer. This is Chicago, not New York. How about a little Midwestern patience?

I really wanted to love the Conrad given its reputation, but our stay was a letdown. At nearly $500 a night, I expected far more than what we got. The room looked fine at first glance, but on closer inspection there were coffee stains on the desk, hairs in the bathroom, and a dusty vent. Housekeeping barely refreshed anything during our three nights. Wifi was spotty at best -- it dropped constantly, which made working from the room frustrating. Breakfast was the biggest disappointment: the buffet looked tired, eggs were lukewarm, fruit was soggy, and one morning we waited almost twenty minutes for coffee before giving up. The location is convenient and the lobby is impressive, but honestly the service and details don't justify the price. I'd stay elsewhere next time.

I can easily say this is one of the worst hotels I've stayed at the. The receptionist up front was a snooty, sarcastic teenager or post teenager. You can get better service from a waiter or waitress at a diner. The room was dirty, stains on the carpet, the showerhead was moldy and rusted, the doors of the bathroom and main door all had dents and scratches. The towels had a horrible aroma. The hotel is very narrow, so we were near a construction zone so, I would plan on waking up at 6:am if you choose the Talbott. The next day, I asked for another room and the concierge who was a decent guy moved us to a larger more comfortable room. That room though was right by the elevator and it was torture hearing the sounds of the elevator which just would never stop. I asked for late checkout at 1pm and the receptionist refused stating that we would be charged for a half day, if were not out by noon. I had to speak to the manager who gave us till 1pm. Please stay away from this hotel, I think a Holiday Inn would be better. Andrew F. Gulli
The Affinia's location was convenient, but the room felt tired and wasn't very clean, with a slow check-in and noisy hallway traffic making the stay more frustrating than relaxing.

I expected much more from an InterContinental, especially at the rate we paid. The lobby looks polished, but the experience fell apart quickly. Our room was not ready at the advertised check-in time, and nobody offered an explanation beyond 'housekeeping is busy.' When we finally got in, there was dust on the desk, a stained chair by the window, and the air conditioning rattled loudly all night. The bed was comfortable enough, but the hallway noise started early and the walls seemed very thin. Breakfast was overpriced and lukewarm, with several empty trays left unattended. Staff members were polite when approached, though it often felt like there were too few people working. The location was convenient, but that alone did not justify such a disappointing stay.

We booked the Hotel Palmer on a bit of a whim for a long weekend, and honestly, it turned out to be the perfect home base. The location is fantastic--you can walk to so many places, and the train station is right there, which made exploring effortless. The staff were genuinely friendly, from the doorman who remembered our name to the front desk helping us map out a rainy-day itinerary on their tablet. Our room was quiet, which was a blessing, and the bed was incredibly comfortable with soft, high-quality sheets. The blackout curtains actually worked, and we slept in later than we have in months. The little touches, like a proper Nespresso machine and a handwritten welcome note, didn't go unnoticed. We didn't try the restaurant, but the bar made a mean old fashioned. We left feeling rested and would absolutely book again for a city trip.

My wife and I stayed at the Amalfi on a trip to visit our son and some friends from Norway who were vacationing in the City. We were excited about staying at the Amalfi after reading the reviews here, but really disappointed in the accommodations. The web site has a photo of the 18 story building that houses the hotel. It doesn't state that the hotel only occupies the first 6 floors of the building. The rest are offices. Our room was on the 4th floor with a view of a blank brick wall about 16 feet distant. The room itself was unremarkable, with standard furnishings equivalent to a Holiday Inn. Although it is close to the best part of the City, it is tucked behind the new Trump Tower and opens on a surprisingly sketchy stretch of road/sidewalk. Our Norwegian friends, by contrast, stayed on the 33rd floor of Swissotel and had views of the Lake and Navy Pier.

Even though the reviews of this hotel are very good, the only good thing about it is the Location, which is excelent. aside from that, there are only 2 elevators, so there is ALWAYS a wait to get in. they also seem to have insufficient staff so getting your luggage, room service, etc takes forever. even if you arrive in a cab, there is no space to load/unload so you have to block the street while you arrive/depart, the rooms seem a bit dated and in need of a refresh. all in all, there are much better options in Chicago

We stayed at the Knickerbocker for three nights over the holidays and I'm still thinking about it. The location is hard to beat -- Times Square is right there but somehow once you step inside the lobby you can't hear any of the madness. Our room was on a higher floor with a view down toward the intersection, which kept us entertained for longer than I'd like to admit. The bed was genuinely one of the most comfortable I've slept in at a hotel, and the shower had great water pressure, which I always appreciate. Breakfast at the restaurant downstairs was excellent -- the avocado toast and cappuccinos were worth getting up for. The staff went out of their way for us when we needed extra towels and a late checkout. Not a huge gym, but perfectly adequate. Would absolutely book this place again on our next trip to the city.

This place had character I'll give it that. But it wasn't really my style. Arrived late in the evening. The first room they gave me the TV didn't work. Maintenance took a look at it, and couldn't figure it out. Told me I'd have to wait until the morning for the electrician. He then passed some gas and left. Real professional. I phoned the front desk on account of the tv, and was able to get another room The second room was much like the first. Horrible striped wall paper, dingy, and old worn carpet. Bathroom was incredibly small. Hard to use the toliet without banging into the door, or the sink. Very cramped. The beds weren't very comfortable either. Room temp hard to regulate and the AC somewhat noisy. Location seem very convenient. I was there for a training session about 8 blocks away. But all of the theatres seemed to be near by, if thats what you were there for this place may be tolerable for a night or two. And don't make a long distance phone call from your room without a calling card. It was about $2/minute. I knew it would be expensive but wasn't expecting that type of rate.
Loved the view of the harbor from our room, and the bed was so comfy I slept straight through the night. Breakfast had fresh pastries and good coffee. Honestly felt like solid value for the price.

I had a very pleasant stay at Homewood and would gladly return. My suite was surprisingly quiet, even in the evening, and I barely heard hallway traffic or neighboring rooms. The window overlooked a small park and the downtown skyline beyond it, which was especially nice with morning coffee. The location made getting around easy; restaurants, a grocery store, and several shops were within a short walk, and downtown was only a quick drive away. Everyone on the staff was warm and helpful, from the efficient check-in to the front desk team offering directions and local recommendations. The room was clean, spacious, and comfortable, making the trip feel relaxed from start to finish.

We stayed at the Conrad for our anniversary and honestly left feeling let down. The lobby is gorgeous, no argument there, but that's where the good impressions ended. Check-in took nearly 40 minutes even though we'd booked weeks in advance. Our room had a musty smell and the AC rattled all night. Housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely and never came back after we called. Breakfast was chaotic both mornings -- waiting 25 minutes for coffee, cold eggs, staff who seemed overwhelmed. For a hotel that charges this much, the service simply didn't match the price tag. The executive lounge ran out of food before 8pm. Would not stay here again, especially not for a special occasion. Plenty of other options in the area that deliver better.
The Hilton felt fresh and thoughtfully decorated, making the rate seem worthwhile. Staff were warm and efficient, and our high-floor room offered a lovely city view, especially at sunset.
Swissotel was a comfortable base for our trip, with a bright, spotless room, quick check-in, and genuinely helpful staff. The city views from breakfast were a lovely bonus.
The location was handy for Times Square, but the decor felt tired, the room had dusty surfaces, and the overpriced breakfast was lukewarm and forgettable.

I booked the Knickerbocker expecting old-world charm, but what I got was a tired room and a lot of noise. The hallway carpet was stained, and the air conditioner in our room sounded like a lawnmower all night, which made it impossible to sleep. I called the front desk twice about it, and they just said they'd 'send someone up,' but no one ever came. The bathroom had a broken showerhead that sprayed sideways, and the grout was frankly gross. Location is the only saving grace, but that doesn't excuse the peeling wallpaper in the elevator. For nearly $400 a night, you'd think they could afford a basic repair crew. I'll be staying elsewhere next time and I'd advise you to do the same.
