I chose Homewood because the photos made it look comfortable and convenient, but the actual stay was a letdown. Check-in took nearly half an hour, and the desk agent seemed distracted and offered no useful information about parking or breakfast. Our room was large, but it smelled faintly musty, the carpet had several stains, and the sofa bed looked as if it had seen better days. The kitchenette was a nice idea, although there were only two plates and no dish towel. Housekeeping skipped our room one day, and when I called for fresh towels, they arrived several hours later. Breakfast was crowded and most of the hot food was gone by 8:30. Nothing was terrible individually, but the overall experience felt poorly managed and not worth the price.

Checked in late and found crumbs on the carpet and a sticky bedside table; the bathroom had a lingering musty smell. Between thin walls and slamming doors, I barely slept, which made the three nights feel far too long.

I expected more from the Hard Rock name, but this stay felt tired and overpriced. Check-in took nearly 30 minutes even though there were only two people ahead of us, and no one acknowledged the delay. Our room had a strong stale smoke smell, despite being listed as non-smoking, and the bathroom fan rattled all night. The bed was comfortable enough, but the walls were so thin we could hear conversations and doors slamming in the hallway until after 2 a.m. Breakfast was mediocre and lukewarm, with empty trays sitting unfilled for a while. Staff at the bar were friendly, which was probably the best part, but it didn't make up for the overall lack of care. For the price, I would definitely choose somewhere else next time.

I stayed at the Allegro Hotel while interviewing for a position in Chicago. I read the reviews and they were mixed, but since the property was suggested by the organization (due to location), I booked a room. True to the reviews, the room was extremely small, was cold (the heater blew in cold air in -2 degree weather), and just generally uncomfortable. There was no closet so I hung my suit on the doorknob of the door of the adjoining room. The bathroom was extremely small and although tidy, not especially clean (it was dusty). The bed (which was supposed to be a queen but was really a full) was quite low and the sheets were hard. Because I arrived late, I ordered room service. There was so little space in the room that the wait staff had to approach the desk/table sideways. Although there is free wireless (a plus), I kept getting kicked out of the system and had to, no lie, reconnect on-line a record 16 times. Finally, to top it all off, the television stopped working just a little before midnight. I was only there for one evening (not even 12 hours) but that was enough for me. This is supposed to be a 4 star boutique hotel but I've stayed at better 2 star properties. On the positive side, the staff is nice and friendly, the food is reasonably good, and the lobby is really vibrant. There is a martini bar (although as I was coming in, a hotel guest was complaining about it being unsually smokey) that looked interesting. Overall though, not the best stay I've had. I won't be staying again.

I had a very pleasant stay at the Affinia and would happily return. My room was spacious, quiet, and thoughtfully arranged, with a comfortable bed that made it easy to sleep well after long days exploring the city. The bathroom was clean and modern, with good water pressure and plenty of towels, although the lighting could have been a little brighter. Breakfast offered a solid variety, including fresh fruit, yogurt, eggs, pastries, and good coffee; it was convenient and satisfying rather than especially memorable. The staff were welcoming and quick to help with directions and a late request for extra towels. Considering the room size, central location, and overall comfort, I felt the price was fair and definitely worth it.

Our stay at Hotel Palmer was much more disappointing than expected. The lobby looks stylish, but our room felt tired and poorly maintained, with scuffed walls, stained carpet, and a bathroom fan that rattled all night. The bed was surprisingly uncomfortable, and the thin walls meant we could hear doors slamming and conversations in the hallway until well past midnight. Housekeeping also skipped our room despite the 'please service' sign, and when we called the front desk, the response was basically an apology with no real solution. Breakfast was overpriced for a limited, lukewarm selection. The location is convenient, but that was the only clear advantage. For the price, I expected a cleaner, quieter, more attentive experience and would not choose this hotel again.

Booked a 'Strip view' room and got a gorgeous vista of the parking garage and the Hard Rock Cafe's neon sign that buzzed all night. The blackout curtains couldn't block the hum. Breakfast was a chaotic free-for-all, with lukewarm scrambled eggs and bacon so rubbery it bounced. The waffle station had a twenty-minute line. As for sleep, I don't think I got more than three consecutive hours--the walls are paper-thin, and I heard the guests next door arguing until 2 AM, followed by their kid crying. The hallway was noisier than the casino floor below. I paid premium prices for a subpar stay, and the front desk shrugged when I mentioned the noise. Save your money and book elsewhere. This was a major letdown.
Disappointing stay at the Conrad. The bathroom tile was grimy and the shower barely drained, plus street noise kept us up all night. Location was decent, but even a one-night visit felt too long.
Sadly not worth the price at all. Our room had dusty surfaces and a grimy bathroom with moldy grout, and the staff were dismissive whenever we raised issues. Won't be returning.

The James was exactly what we needed - stylish and quiet, with a bed so comfy I actually slept past my alarm. The rooftop bar had fantastic views, and the staff made check-in feel effortless. Would happily return.

We stayed at this Hotel in February 2010. The room was great we had purchased it at a raffel at work for a fund raiser for United Way. So we probably paid more then we needed but it was for charity. We were woke up at 3:00am in the morning by a group of at least 25 young people that were so loud coming off the elevators and down the hall ways they must of woke everyone up on our floor. Of course one of the rooms they rented was right next to ours. They were so loud shouting profanities and banging on the walls that we thought there was maybe a fight going on. We called the front desk who sent security up immediately. Security tried to get the people that were not registered guests to leave. We called down to the front desk two more times to send security back up again since nothing changed this went on for over an hour until it finally quieted down. Because of this we ended up over sleeping in the morning since we were so exhausted. When we complained about it in the morning managemnet would do nothing for us because as they stated we used a gift certificate. Well we still paid for it!!. They would not give us one thing free for the trouble that we had. We would never stay at this hotel again, obviously they really don't care about their guests.

I had a very comfortable stay at the Sheraton and would gladly return. The front desk team was friendly and efficient, especially when I arrived late and needed a quick recommendation for dinner. My room was clean, quiet, and spacious enough for a small work area, with a very comfortable bed. I was on an upper floor overlooking the river and downtown buildings, and the evening view was surprisingly nice when the lights came on. The lobby was busy but well organized, and the fitness center had everything I needed for a short workout. I only stayed two nights, which felt far too short; I easily could have added another day to enjoy the hotel and city. Considering the location, service, and room quality, the rate felt reasonable and worth paying.

I booked the Omni based on pictures that must have been taken years ago. The hallway carpet was stained, and our room smelled musty, like old air conditioning. The 'renovated' bathroom had a chipped sink and a showerhead that dribbled, not sprayed. We asked for extra towels twice and waited over an hour both times, only to get a call saying they were out and would bring them later--they never came. The air conditioning unit rattled all night, and the blackout curtains had gaps, so we were up with the sunrise. Location is decent, but that's about it. The front desk staff were polite but clearly overwhelmed, and the breakfast buffet was cold and overpriced. For the rate we paid, I expected far better. I'm genuinely disappointed, and I won't return.

For the price, I expected far more. The room wasn't dirty, but the constant hallway noise made sleep impossible, and the staff's indifference to my complaint felt dismissive. Overpriced for what you get.

While this is a good location for shopping and sightseeing, I would not recommend this hotel to anyone. The rooms are small and bathrooms are tiny, all of which is to be expected in an old urban hotel, but apparently care has not been given to updating the hotel (ever!). The crown molding and base boards are cracked and it appears to only have been painted over and over again. The newer tub liner in the bathroom is merely floating above the old tub and when you stand in the shower it bubbles under your feet. The shower tiles are old and the grout is not clean. This hotel has not been restored the updating that has been done are merely band-aides. There is no fan exhaust in the bathroom and the carpet is ontop of a very hard surface, probaly concrete with no pad in between. The lobby is smokey because of the large open bar in the small space. We were in town on business and supposed to stay 4 nights, we left after 2 and went to another hotel.

As others have said, once all the construction works are completed I suspect that the prices this hotel can (legitimately) charge will put it out of our price range. Which will be a pity because it is an excellent hotel, & the location couldn't be better. The room was very spacious, with separate sitting & study areas & a nice bathroom. Only 3 minor points: downstairs they were serving a free basic breakfast (coffee & pastries), but we only knew of it on our last morning - nobody had mentioned this; the cost of internet - $9.99 - is a bit dear especially when lots of motels now offer it free; there was only powered milk in the rooms, which wasn't that nice. But none of these really spolied a really enjoyable stay.

The hotel is beautiful. It is an excellent location. There was a few minor issues. The hotel is clearly geared toward the convention and business crowd. There were charges for almost everything, although I did not incur any of these. Our room was a little small for the class of hotel, but not overwhelmingly small. Not a true complaint, but the elevators were very slow. My comparison was that we stayed in an equally aged hotel in a different city during our trip, and the Intercontinental's were significantly slower. That's it, no more little nit picks. The staff was excellent, the doormen being the highlight. The hotel bar was also very nice. The hotel was immaculately clean. I would definitely travel to this hotel again.

We became an Ambassador member just before spending Mother's day at the Chicago Intercontinental, and received a room upgrade to an exceptional room. Our Saturday night stay was the BEST $99 we ever spent (Mother's day special). The welcoming chocolate covered strawberries began the weekend on a high note; the concierge continued it by arranging a wonderful dinner (moderately priced) , and the great Sunday breakfast topped it all off. All in all, Mother's day in Chicago was Super. We loved it enough to be back for Labor Day weekend (another 'package').

I had hopes for the Talbott based on its reputation, but our three-night stay was a letdown from start to finish. The wifi barely functioned -- it dropped constantly in the evenings and took ages to load anything, which made working from the room impossible. Staff ranged from indifferent to outright curt; when we mentioned the thermostat wasn't working, nobody ever came to check it. Breakfast was the biggest disappointment: cold eggs, lukewarm coffee, and a sad pastry selection that looked like it had been sitting out since the day before. The rooms themselves are part of the problem, too -- the decor feels straight out of the early 2000s, with worn carpet, scuffed furniture, and heavy drapes that didn't quite close. For the price point, I expected far more. We won't be back.
Bathroom was grungy with hair in the tub, and the street noise kept me up half the night. Staff barely acknowledged us. Not worth $300 a night--won't be back.

The location was perfect for our Amalfi Coast day trips, and the sea-view balcony made every morning feel special. Staff sorted our ferry tickets without fuss, and the breakfast spread had fresh pastries and local fruit. A lovely, hassle-free stay I'd happily repeat.

We loved the Talbott. The location was fabulous...very close to the shopping. The hotel is smaller, but the rooms are very nice. They are very spacious and are able to be darkened to sleep well. Also, the beds are some of the most comfortable I have ever slept in. I might also add that our room at queen beds. The staff is all friendly and puts them themselves out for you. The hotel has a cute outdoor eating area on the sidewalk that has flowers, etc. It looks like a scene out of Europe. I would highly recommend the hotel. We were there with our daughters; ages 10 and 13.

Seriously overpriced The room was clean and comfortable but did not stand out from any other mid priced hotel. The 'amenities' were a smoke screen, nothing was offered that you would not get at a much lesser quality motel but they did not have the basics that you would expect from a Holiday Inn. I would gladly have forgone the scale in the bathroom for a cup of hot coffee that I did not have to get dressed and go down to the lobby to purchase. Being charged $15/day for Internet on top of a $250/night rate was a bit over the top. The bathroom was not well lit which was inconvenient. The shower was a nice size with a fantastic over-sized shower head, unfortunately twice the water pressure was low so the effect was lost. The staff were friendly and helpful, actually the best part of the stay were the staff. All in all I found it overpriced for the quality of the room.

The breakfast buffet was watery scrambled eggs and stale pastries, nothing worth waking up for. I barely slept--the bed sagged and the AC rattled all night. Worn carpets and faded floral drapes screamed 1980s, and crumbs on the nightstand proved housekeeping skipped us.

The skyline view from my room was absolutely stunning, especially at sunset, and the wifi never dropped once. Being right on Michigan Avenue made exploring effortless--I honestly wish I could have stayed a few more nights instead of my quick weekend.
Disappointing stay at the Conrad: the high price didn't feel justified, the decor looked tired, and while the room was clean, street noise made for a poor night's sleep.

This hotel was not worth it. From the moment we walked into the hotel lobby through check out, the staff were rude and contemptuous. Rooms were only serviceable, and certainly did not live up to the pompous self-descriptions on the website. The bathroom porthole and sliding door were odd and inconvenient. The 'fitness centre' was tiny and poor. We would not come here again.

I can't recall another time I've had to deal with such rude front desk help. While pleasant initially, as soon as I demonstrated the slightest bit of frustration that I was still waiting to claim my luggage for check-in (I arrived prior to check-in time, so they were holding a few bags), the true quality of this establishment surfaced. Never mind that the luggage wasn't sent up to our room in the afternoon or that i waited in the lobby for 15 minutes at 7:30pm still looking for my luggage or at least a bellhop. While that was a bit annoying, the worst part was witnessing the poor attitude of Donna, the very attractive but aloof front desk employee. Her lack of initiative was only matched by her pettiness, as I noticed she refused to make eye contact with me for the remainder of my stay, including when my family came down to the lobby the following morning. I also booked a rate that included parking, which Donna acknowledged at check-in but at check out billed me separately; I assume after I got on her bad side. Even with my last polite good bye to the front desk, I felt a phony, uppity attitude from Donna, and I really can't convey the extent of how insulting it felt. I can honestly say it was the worst part of my first trip to Chicago. The hotel is well appointed and the lobby was small but cozy. Great location as well. To be fair, most of the staff seemed very friendly, and I am not so obtuse as to not recognize my rating of this hotel is a statistical outlier. But I think most travelers, like me, would trade a few amenities for consistent and reliable service, so as to not have a 'situation' that could single-handedly ruin a travel experience. Unfortunately, that was the case here.

no bell boys there when you need them, sully staff, no smiles at all in this place. had to wait 30 min for my luggage and was never greeted by any of the staff. boy, sure is a lousy fairmont compared to the one in SF. never here again!

The Hyatt exceeded expectations. The bed was perfect, the staff remembered our name each morning, and the rooftop pool at sunset was serene. We left feeling genuinely refreshed. Already planning our return trip.

I was honestly prepared for downtown noise, but my room on the eighth floor was remarkably peaceful--just the faint hum of the city below. The staff felt genuinely attentive without hovering, especially the front desk agent who remembered I mentioned an early flight and had coffee ready at 6 a.m. The decor surprised me: sleek and crisp, with warm wood accents that still felt current, not like a hotel stuck in 2015. My corner room faced the river, and watching the lights flicker on the skyscrapers at dusk was a quiet thrill. Bathroom was spotless, rainfall shower had real pressure, and the bed was firm enough to sleep like a rock. A few scuffs on the hallway baseboards, but nothing that dampened the experience. I'd absolutely book again next time I'm in town.

I expected much more from the Conrad given the price and reputation. Check-in took nearly half an hour because the room supposedly was not ready, even though we arrived well after the stated check-in time. When we finally got upstairs, the room had a strong musty smell and the bathroom counter still had hair and water marks on it. The view was nice, but the air conditioning rattled all night and made sleep difficult. I called down twice about it and never received a response. Breakfast was also disappointingly slow, with cold coffee and a long wait for eggs despite the dining room being only half full. Staff were polite when available, but the whole stay felt understaffed and poorly managed. Not worth the premium rate.

The Talbott Hotel itself is a bit worn around the edges. No - not a bit worn - very much so I'm sorry to say. Although the location a block and a half from the best part of Michigan Ave. can't be beat, and the level of service is on par with many Four Seasons, there were quite a few bumps in the road. Number one, the rooms are quite dreary - brown on brown is just so not pleasing. The desk chair was so badly worn that the 'lift' button simply swirled down when you sat in it and no we're not grossly obese. The back of the chair leaned so much it was uncomfortable. My husband had to use 2 couch pillows to use it - one to get him up to desk heighth, one up against his back to scoot him up to the desk. The bathroom was oddly arranged so that the door swung up right next to the sink, so if you were using the far sink and someone needed to enter the bathroom you got hit with the door. The towels were very well worn and thin, although bath sized, which was a plus. The restaurant downstairs is practically another posting - suffice to say, it was horrific. We had some appetizers outside on the nice streetside tables, and they (appetizers) were awful and looked as though a child had tossed them together in the kitchen. A room service sandwich ordered later in our visit was totally wet on the side, served on a large white plate, and was one slice of meat and one slice of plastic American cheese on a grocery store-like roll - very very sad. Even the menu, as limited as it was, looked as though someone's child had written it out. The good news is that Chicago is a fairly well-read restaurant town so there are plenty of other places to go. Unfortunately for us, the 3 days we stayed there was a large convention and jazz festival in town so we paid $325/nt for our disappointments. The good news is that the mini bars' wares were incredibly well-priced - when's the last time you had a $4 beer anywhere in a hotel? (even if it was Bud and Bud lite - lol!~) The front desk and curbside staff could not have been more accommodating. The water out of the shower was hot and plentiful, and the bed comfortable. The A/C was not noisy nor uncomfortable whatsoever, and we had it going the entire time as it was in the 90's our entire stay. Free wi-fi - YES! And it wasn't horribly grindingly slow! No need for the advertised 'upgrade' for faster wi-fi. Talbott - please update your rooms and get a new restaurant concept and you will be ahead of the game. Apparently there are enough folks getting deals on rooms here so they are pleased, but we were sadly not.

I expected a much smoother stay at the Intercontinental, especially given the price and the reputation of the brand. The lobby is impressive, but the room felt tired, with scuffed furniture, a stained carpet near the window, and a bathroom fan that rattled all night. Check-in took nearly half an hour even though there were only two people ahead of me, and the receptionist seemed more interested in answering messages than helping guests. Housekeeping also skipped my room on the second day, so I had to call twice for fresh towels. The location was convenient and the bed was reasonably comfortable, but those positives did not make up for the general lack of attention. It felt more like an expensive, aging business hotel than a memorable luxury stay.

The Wi-Fi dropped every few minutes, making work impossible, and the bathroom had a persistent mildew smell. Breakfast was overpriced instant eggs, though I'll grant the location near the subway was the only saving grace.

My weekend at the Sofitel went by far too quickly. From the moment I arrived, the team was warm without being overly formal, and the concierge patiently helped us sort out dinner reservations when our original plan fell through. Our room was quiet, beautifully maintained, and had a wonderful view over the city lights; I found myself lingering by the window with coffee each morning. Breakfast was a highlight, with fresh pastries, fruit, made-to-order eggs, and attentive servers who kept everything moving despite a busy dining room. The bed was exceptionally comfortable, and housekeeping was discreet and thorough. It felt like a proper escape while still being close to everything we wanted to see. I would happily return.

I had a very pleasant stay at the Affinia. The location made getting around easy, with restaurants, shops, and public transportation all close by, yet my room was quiet at night. I appreciated having more space than in a typical city hotel, including a comfortable sitting area and a small kitchen setup that was handy for keeping drinks and snacks. The bed was cozy, and everything was clean when I arrived. What really stood out was the staff: check-in was quick, and everyone I dealt with was friendly without being overbearing. The decor is a little dated in places, but that was a minor issue compared with the overall comfort and convenience. I would happily stay here again, especially for a longer visit.

Rocked up expecting just a music-themed room, but the vibe was next level--staff hooked us up with late check-out and the pool scene felt like a mini Vegas escape. Cranking tunes in the shower sealed it; definitely booking again for a proper weekend.

The room's cleanliness was questionable--stains on the carpet and a dusty bathroom--while the promised city view was mostly a brick wall. Wi-Fi dropped constantly, and street noise seeped in all night, making sleep nearly impossible. Definitely not worth the price.
The Sheraton looked tired, check-in took forever, and the room smelled musty. For the price, I expected cleaner bathrooms and staff who seemed more interested in helping.

The Omni's location made exploring effortless, and the staff's warm greetings set a great tone each morning. Though our spotless room made it tempting to linger, the weekend felt far too brief for all there was to enjoy.

I spent two nights at Hotel Allegro for a quick Chicago getaway and left wishing I had booked one more. Our room looked out over the surrounding downtown buildings, and at night the lit windows and traffic below made the view surprisingly enjoyable. The decor has personality--bold colors, patterned details, and a slightly theatrical lobby--but it felt fresh and well cared for rather than dated. The room was comfortable, quiet enough for sleeping, and the bed was excellent. Wi-Fi worked reliably for checking maps, streaming a show, and answering a few work emails without any frustrating dropouts. Staff at the front desk were warm and efficient, too. It was a short stay, but a very satisfying one.

The James looked promising online, but the stay was a real disappointment. Check-in took nearly 25 minutes even though there was no line, and the receptionist seemed distracted and barely explained anything. Our room was stylish enough, but the carpet had visible stains, the bathroom fan rattled all night, and the air conditioning never cooled the room properly. We also found used glasses left on the desk, which made me question how thoroughly the room had been cleaned. The hallway was noisy until well after midnight, with doors slamming and guests talking loudly. Breakfast was overpriced for lukewarm eggs, dry pastries, and slow service. Staff were polite when approached, but nobody seemed particularly interested in fixing anything. For the price, I expected much better maintenance and attention to detail.

Great hotel in a wonderful location. I stayed in this hotel last weekend for one night before coming home and I loved it. I couldn't recommend it highly enough. Evidently popular and busy, the staff were still helpful. The rooms were lovely and spacious and clean. Bathrooms were clean, bright and spacious also. I'd definitely recommend this hotel too, it's close to the magnificant mile.

After some deliberation I booked the Sofitel Water Tower Place for a 3 night stop-over in June. This was my first visit to Chicago and it turned out that we had a really great time. We loved our rooms, which were just the basic type on the lower floors but they were very well appointed. The decor is modern and personally I liked it a lot. The rooms were pleasant and airy and the bed extremely comfortable. The hotel location is just perfect, close to the shops on Michagan Avenue, and the beach at Oak Street. Lovely restaurants close by and nightlife in Rush Street is just steps away. The area although bustling was peaceful and quiet. We could walk to most places and I would not hesitate to stay here again. The hotel staff very helpful, always smiling and ready to help; from the doormen to the helpful lady at Conceriage. I would not hesitate at all to stay at Sofitel Water Tower Place next time I'm in Chicago; in fact I look forward to my next visit.

The room was very spacious with very nice, colorful decorating. The beds felt like lying on a cloud, and there were four pillows on each bed, two fiberfill and two down so you could choose which you like better. The bathroom was very nice also. Overall, I was very pleased with the stay. You had to show your room key to get in after ten p.m. I thought that was a good security issue. It has a great location too, close to downtown. I would recommend it. The decorations were very classy. Most hotels have two of the same framed art, boring bedspreads and lumpy pillows. The Hyatt Regency was just the opposite.

I really wanted to love Hotel Talbott, given the charming facade and prime location, but our stay was a letdown from arrival. The front desk staff were courteous but overwhelmed, leaving us waiting over twenty minutes past check-in time while our room was 'still being prepared.' When we finally got in, the room itself was cramped and tired. The paint was chipped near the windowsill, the carpet had an odd, musty smell, and the air conditioning unit rattled loudly all night, interrupting what little sleep we could get. The advertised 'boutique' feel just translated to outdated decor and worn furniture. Breakfast was a chaotic, overpriced buffet with lukewarm eggs and stale pastries. For the nightly rate, I honestly expected far better. The location is the only reason this gets two stars instead of one, but we left feeling we'd overpaid for a mediocre, noisy experience that didn't live up to the photos.

The Knickerbocker was an excellent base for a few days in New York. Being right by Times Square made it incredibly convenient for Broadway shows, the subway, and walking to Bryant Park and Fifth Avenue, yet the hotel itself felt surprisingly removed from the crowds. Our room was quiet at night, with little street noise even on a busy weekend. The decor is polished and fresh, mixing modern touches with a classic luxury feel rather than seeming dated. Wi-Fi worked reliably throughout our stay, including when I needed to join a video call from the room. Staff were warm and efficient, and the rooftop was a memorable bonus. I'd happily stay here again.

Despite the prime location, I regret paying these rates. The bathroom had questionable stains, and street noise seeped through the walls all night, making sleep nearly impossible--definitely not worth the premium.

I booked the Omni expecting the polished, upscale vibe the photos promised, but the reality was a frayed version of that. The front desk staff were painfully indifferent, barely looking up from their screens to hand over the key card, and every request for extra towels or a late checkout was met with a curt 'we'll see.' The wifi was a joke--it dropped constantly in the room, forcing me to camp in the lobby just to send a simple email, which hardly feels acceptable at these rates. Honestly, the price tag felt absurd for what I got. The bathroom was the worst part: a cracked tile near the tub, a showerhead that sprayed sideways, and a lingering musty odor no amount of fan noise could fix. I've had better stays at mid-range chains for half the cost. This was a disappointing, overpriced miss.

Stayed for a weekend getaway and the Omni exceeded expectations. The pool area was relaxing, and the staff remembered our names each morning. Room was spotless, bed super comfy. We'll definitely be back.

We wanted a nice place to stay the night after dinner, theater, and my daughter's 21st birthday. This place certainly fit the bill. It was convenient to everything including the SouthShore Railroad station. The staff were all friendly. Their was a small wine reception in the lobby in the evening and Starbucks coffee in the morning. Ryan, the concierge, ordered flowers for my daughter and had a nice bowl of Hershey Kisses waiting for us when we arrived. We were upgraded to a suite and although they forgot to make up the sofa bed, they came promptly to get it set up when we called later. The window seats were beautiful as well and I enjoyed drinking my coffee in the morning and reading a book.

The buffet was sparse and the scrambled eggs turned cold fast, so paying top dollar felt like a mistake. WiFi dropped constantly in the room, and while the bed was made, dusty corners and a stained carpet made the whole stay feel neglected.

I really expected more from the Fairmont, honestly. We paid for a room with a view and got one mostly facing another building, plus the air conditioning rattled so loudly the first night that I barely slept. Called the front desk twice and someone said they'd send engineering up, but nobody ever showed. The room itself felt tired, worn carpet edges, a bathroom door that wouldn't close properly, and housekeeping skipped our room entirely one day. I will say the lobby is beautiful and the doormen were lovely, but the actual guest experience didn't match the price tag at all. Breakfast in the restaurant ran us nearly $90 for two people and the eggs were cold. For what this hotel charges, the attention to detail just isn't there. Not sure we'd come back.
Swissotel was a really comfortable stay, with a spotless room, helpful staff, and a great city view. The location made getting around easy, and breakfast was better than expected.

I had a very enjoyable stay at The Knickerbocker. The location is exceptionally convenient, right by Times Square and close to subway lines, Broadway theaters, and plenty of restaurants, yet the hotel itself felt more polished and relaxed than the busy streets outside. My room was stylish and fresh, with modern furnishings, comfortable bedding, and thoughtful lighting; nothing felt dated or worn. Wi-Fi worked reliably throughout my stay, including for video calls and streaming. Despite being in such a lively part of Manhattan, the room was surprisingly quiet at night, with only occasional city noise. The staff were welcoming and efficient, and check-in was quick. The rooftop bar was an added highlight, offering memorable views. It is not the least expensive option, but the comfort and location made it feel worthwhile.

Wish I could have stayed longer than two nights; the city panorama from the 18th floor was postcard-perfect. Fast, reliable Wi-Fi kept me connected, and despite central location, my room was impressively silent--a truly restorative sleep.

The Hyatt exceeded my expectations--the bed was impossibly comfortable and the staff remembered my name by day two. Breakfast had great variety, and the location made exploring effortless. I'd happily book again.

This hotel does not live up to the reviews. The room was larger than I expected. However, the decor was a bit dated. The bedding was ripped, carpet was stained, and the shower door was broken. There was a long wait to the elevators, and if you're on floors 2-6 you need to take a second elevator to get to the roof bar and gym. The main issue I had was the attitude I received from the staff. There was literally only ONE nice person at the front desk. There are no ice machines in this building, so you have to request it from the front desk. One day I requested it by going down to the desk and asking in person. 20 minutes later I made a follow up call because I did not receive my ice. I was nastily told that ice takes 10 minutes and I should just wait. I finally got the ice 10 minutes later. Two days later I requested ice again. Waited 30 minutes and just gave up. While I was leaving, I mentioned this to the woman at the front desk and she just said 'I didn't get a call for ice.' Well I obviously wasn't making it up, lady! I called and spoke with someone. She didn't even apologize or offer me anything. Overall, I would not recommend this hotel. There are so many hotels in the Chicago area. Choose a different one.

After a long travel day, I was frankly dreading a mediocre hotel bed. Instead, I slept like a rock--the mattress was firm but yielding, and the blackout curtains made the room a perfect cave. The cleanliness was impeccable, from the streak-free mirrors to the crisp, fresh-smelling linens. The staff felt genuinely attentive without hovering; the front desk remembered my name and the valet had great local tips. My corner room's view was the real reward, though: a sweeping, glittering panorama of the city skyline at dusk that made me pull up a chair and just sit there. Minor quibble: the shower pressure was slightly weak, but that's a small price for such a peaceful, well-run stay. I'd happily return.
Disappointing stay. AC rattled all night, and the bathroom had a lingering musty smell. Staff were polite but shrugged off the noise complaint. Not worth the boutique price.

I had a very pleasant stay at the Fairmont and would happily return. My room was comfortable and thoughtfully laid out, with a large window overlooking the city skyline and a glimpse of the river. The view was especially lovely in the evening when the lights came on. Breakfast offered plenty of choice, including fresh fruit, pastries, eggs made to order, and good coffee, though the restaurant became busy later in the morning. The location was extremely convenient, with restaurants, shops, and public transportation all within an easy walk, while the hotel itself remained quiet and welcoming. The bed was excellent, and I slept soundly every night. Service was professional and friendly throughout, making the whole experience feel smooth and relaxing.

After reading the reviews & getting an excellent rate through travelzoo, I decided to give this hotel a try. I must say it was a great choice! The location is perfect, just off from N Michigan Ave, walking distance from everything. The staff was very helpful and friendly, and the room was excellent. They gave us a corner room w/a great view. As many have posted, the bed & pillows were very comfortable (I am very picky about that). I slept well every night! The renovation is almost done & did not bother us one bit. I highly recommend this hotel.

The Conrad exceeded my expectations from start to finish. I booked a standard king, and the room was genuinely spacious with a gorgeous view of the river--the floor-to-ceiling windows made the whole space feel even bigger. The bed was incredibly comfortable, and the blackout curtains actually worked, which I can't always say. The staff at the front desk were warm and efficient, and they proactively arranged a late checkout without me even asking. The bathroom had a rain shower and lovely Aesop toiletries, which was a nice touch. We had drinks at the lobby bar one evening, and the cocktails were well made, though pricier than I'd normally go for. The fitness center was compact but had everything I needed. Location-wise, it's a short walk to the riverwalk and plenty of restaurants. I'd happily return.

Our stay at Hotel Ambassador was disappointing overall. The room faced a busy road, and the constant traffic, late-night conversations in the hallway, and doors slamming made it difficult to sleep, even with the windows closed. The bed was comfortable enough, but the room felt dated and needed better cleaning around the bathroom fixtures. Staff were polite when approached, though check-in was slow and no one seemed particularly interested in solving our concerns. We stayed two nights, which felt longer than necessary because the hotel offered little atmosphere or comfort beyond the basic essentials. Considering the price, I expected a quieter room, more attentive service, and better-maintained facilities. It was not a terrible experience, but it certainly did not feel worth what we paid.

I wasn't expecting much beyond a place to crash, but the Ambassador genuinely surprised me. The lobby has this warm, classic feel without being stuffy, and the front desk clerk actually remembered my name the next morning, which was a nice touch. My room was incredibly quiet--I slept like a log even though I was facing the main street. The bed was firm but comfortable, and the blackout curtains did their job perfectly. Breakfast was included and it wasn't the usual sad continental spread; they had made-to-order omelets and really good coffee. The only minor hiccup was the elevator being slow during the morning rush, but honestly, it gave me time to check my emails. For the price, especially in this neighborhood, I felt like I got way more than I paid for. I'd definitely book here again for a weekend getaway.

Great, awesome service. Seriously, the people are amazing. That, and the nice bartender who serves after last call (at least, that's what I was told - I of course don't drink) save this place from one star. But seriously blah, small, non-luxury rooms with beds that are just really uncomfortable - and for a card rate of $725/night, even in a major city, the rooms better be awesome. I've had waaaay better rooms in NYC for $350/night. (Good thing I had a corporate rate.) And my room was not especially big, despite what the below reviews say. But here's the main problem. Even on the 10th floor, the guy blowing the whistle to summon cabs downstairs woke me up at 6, and 6:15, and 6:30, and 6:45, and 6:50, and 6:55, and...and, well, I finally got up and said screw it, let's greet the day. Maybe everyone else was already up, but somehow I doubt it. Am now safely ensconced in the Four Seasons.

I'd heard the Intercontinental name carries weight, so I expected more than what I got. The room faced the inner courtyard, which was eerily quiet at night--until 6 a.m., when housekeeping carts rumbled down the corridor like a freight train. I slept in fits, never reaching that deep rest you hope for when traveling. The WiFi was a joke: patched into the lobby network, it dropped every time I turned my phone, and the in-room 'high-speed' option required a login that expired hourly. For the price, I felt cheated. The stay felt agonizingly long, not because I wanted to leave, but because each minute dragged with broken promises--stained carpet, lukewarm shower water, and a mini-bar that was mostly empty. Two nights stretched into an eternity. I'd rather have slept in the airport lounge.
Really enjoyed my stay at Hotel Palmer--the room was comfortable, staff genuinely friendly, and the location made it easy to explore everything nearby. I'd happily book here again.

We stayed at the Fairmont for three nights to celebrate our anniversary, and honestly it exceeded what we were hoping for. Check-in was smooth despite us arriving early, and they upgraded our room without us even asking, which was a lovely surprise. The room itself was spacious with a huge marble bathroom and a view of the city lights that we couldn't stop staring at. Housekeeping was attentive but never intrusive. We had breakfast downstairs twice, and the salmon eggs benedict was genuinely one of the best meals I've had in a while, though be warned it fills up fast after 9am. The concierge arranged dinner reservations for us and even remembered our anniversary when we returned that evening. Only tiny gripe was slow elevator waits during peak hours, but that's nitpicking. Would absolutely return.

went to chicago for a week in may, decided to be good to ourselves and stay in the hilton, we were not disapointed. perhaps it was becuse there were quite a few conventions going on and a lot of people were only staying 1 or 2 nights but we got upgraged to exceutive level. we had 2 double beds with a bathroom each. they beds and pillows were too die for, so so comfy ant the end of a day when we seemed to have walked for miles. all the staff were very helpful. a lot of guests seemed to ignore the staff especially the chamber maids who they seemed to think they were in their way so perhaps that why some people felt these people were rude or unhelpful. about 2 blocks away on Harrison is a cafe called 'Orange' which you have to make the only place you will have breakfast, the cafe and the staff are suberb. expect a 15 min wait on a sat & sun morning.

The Good LOCATION Views Decor Room Service Friendly Staff The Bad Shower curtain in replacement room was too short and leaked Bed was just Ok The Ugly Had to pack our bags again and change rooms after loud noises from the elevator kept us up. I am a heavy sleeper but even with my white noise app cranked on the hotel's iPod dock it was still loud enough to keep me up. Also our toilet leaked into a puddle by the shower. The staff did however provide a replacement room although not immediately. Also, they mentioned that they had AREADY been aware of the noise problem with that room from past customers.

The Palmer's location is the strongest part of the stay: it's convenient to downtown attractions, restaurants, and public transportation, so I could walk almost everywhere. Unfortunately, the room itself was a letdown. The carpet looked tired, there were noticeable smudges around the desk and nightstand, and the air conditioner rattled through the night. The bathroom was especially disappointing for a hotel at this level; the fixtures felt dated, the water pressure was weak, and the grout around the tub could use a serious cleaning. Staff members were polite, but service felt slow when I called about the noise and requested extra towels. With the high nightly rate plus additional fees, the Palmer did not feel worth the price. The convenient address helped, but I expected much better upkeep and comfort.

I usually stay at the Hotel Monaco but stayed at the Allegro because most the Monaco was booked. While the Allegro is similar to the Monaco in it's decor (less traditional and more funky interior) it is not nearly as nice. The linens are not as high quality as the Monaco and the rooms are not decorated as nice. The rooms are also smaller. The main reason I would not recommend the hotel though, is the bathroom. It has an old tiled floor, with an old sink, and old toilet. It reminds me of something you would find in a men's locker room. Although the Allegro has installed a nice mirror, it does not make up for the limited counter space and dingy apperance. Also, the layout of the bathroom is terrible. The toilet is so close to the wall that the toilet paper sits in your lap as you sit on the toilet. Also, the room is not very clean as well. The floor in my room was dirty and I found crumbs in the drawers. I would recommend staying at the Monaco, Hard Rock, or Soffitel for a hotel that is a little less traditional but still nice.

Loved the rooftop pool and the bar downstairs, and the bed was honestly one of the comfiest I've slept in at any hotel. Staff remembered my name by day two. Perfect location too -- would happily stay again.

We stayed at the Monaco for three nights in early October and I'm still thinking about it. I'd read some mixed comments about noise before booking, so I requested a room away from the street, and the front desk looked after us without any fuss. It turned out to be genuinely quiet the whole stay, which honestly made the trip. The location is hard to beat if you're on foot: grab a coffee and you're at the waterfront in ten minutes, museums and restaurants just a short walk in the other direction. Our room had the quirks you'd expect from a boutique property, but everything worked, including the wifi, which stayed fast even when the place filled up for a conference midweek. The bathroom was bigger than we needed, with good water pressure and decent toiletries. Staff remembered our names by day two. Would return without hesitation.

Bathroom had hair on the floor and the shower pressure was dismal. Walls were paper-thin, with guests stomping until midnight. Location is decent for metro access, but the dated room and poor cleanliness made this stay far from the InterContinental standard.

My friend book this hotel for us for a girls weekend in Chicago. Lets just say we were thankful we didn't have to spend much time in the room. The carpet was so stained it looked like it was suppose to be that way. The furniture was worn and outdated. The place was gross and just wasn't worth the money we spent on it. The only redeeming quality was the door man, we was very nice and helpful.

This hotel is totally overrated. Yes, the location is awesome, but there are plenty of other nearby hotel options. The customer service, or lack thereof, was particularly disappointing. Why are they paying anywhere from 2 - 8 doormen yet none of them can ever actually open the door for a lady? Even when her hands are full. The housekeeping staff couldn't figure out our preferences even after we left them a daily note explicitly stating such along with a tip -every day. Why ask what newspaper we want with our morning room service when you don't bring it anyway. As stated previously, the location is great. Location, however, does not make up for the complete lack of customer service and inattentiveness from staff. I would not stay here again.
Staff were warm and efficient, the decor felt fresh rather than tired, and breakfast had plenty of choice. Despite the central location, our room stayed pleasantly quiet at night.

My three-night stay at the Hilton was exactly what I needed, and honestly, I could have used a fourth day to fully unwind. The room was spotless, with crisp white linens and a bathroom that gleamed like it had just been sanitized. I was a bit worried about street noise given the central location, but the double-glazed windows kept everything wonderfully hushed; I slept like a log. The highlight was the view--a sweeping panorama of the city skyline that shifted from glittering lights at dusk to soft, hazy gold at sunrise. I never felt rushed, though the time flew by. The housekeeping staff were discreet and efficient, refreshing towels daily without ever intruding. It's rare to find a hotel that balances comfort, quiet, and convenience so seamlessly. I'm already checking dates for my return visit.

My stay at the Hyatt was disappointing, especially considering the price. I expected a polished, comfortable experience, but the room felt dated and lacked the careful maintenance I associate with this brand. Although the sheets and towels were clean, there was dust along the window ledge and a questionable stain on the desk chair. The Wi-Fi was another frustration: it connected briefly, then repeatedly dropped during work calls, even after I restarted my device. Breakfast had plenty of options, but most of the hot food was lukewarm, the coffee tasted weak, and the dining area was crowded and poorly cleared. Staff were polite when approached, but not especially attentive. Overall, the stay did not feel worth the money, and I would choose a less expensive hotel next time.
Breakfast was fresh and varied, the staff genuinely welcoming, and our room overlooked the city skyline. For the comfortable stay and central location, Hotel James felt well worth the price.

Omni made our weekend feel easy from the moment we checked in. The front desk team was warm, efficient, and happy to suggest a nearby restaurant without sounding rehearsed. Our room was spotless and surprisingly quiet, with a broad view of the skyline and the park below; sunset from the window was a real highlight. The decor has a classic, slightly traditional feel, but it looked well maintained rather than dated, and the bed was exceptionally comfortable. We also appreciated the prompt response when we asked for extra towels. Between the comfortable room, friendly service, and convenient location, the stay went by far too quickly. We would gladly return.

You can't beat the location for exploring downtown, which was the only saving grace. Unfortunately, the stay felt about two nights too long once the issues piled up. Breakfast was a chaotic zoo--the scrambled eggs were watery, the coffee urn ran dry twice, and the 'hot' oatmeal was lukewarm by the time I found a table. Sleep was nearly impossible: the AC unit clanked all night, and the walls were so thin I heard every toilet flush from the adjacent room. The bed sagged in the middle, and the pillows were flat as pancakes. I checked out a day early, honestly. For the price, I expected basic comfort. Instead, I left exhausted and disappointed. A convenient spot wasted on a rundown property. I won't be back.

I'll keep it short. My wife, daughter and I stayed at this hotel for 3 nights. We go on several vacations a year and this was a great hotel. Location: It is located in the center of the Magnificent Mile (Michigan Ave.), so it is near or easily accessible to everything you might want to do. Hotel: The hotel itself is very clean, as were the rooms. Maid service was excellent, including 2x daily cleaning and turndown service (I think they missed a night). Service: Every staff member we encountered was super friendly and kind. They always have someone at the lobby door greeting you with a smile. Every night we had milk and cookies waiting in our room (sometimes chocolates on our pillows). They always pushed the elevator button for you if they were near it. There was no shortage of people to ask things. My only conplaint was that the congierge was tough to get. They shouuld have more than one, or longer hours. Other: We had breakfast in the 676 Restaurant and it was very good, and well attended, appointed. They even carried my wifes plate to the table from the buffet. The pool was a nice addition and a hit with the kids. It was nice to go for a swim after a long day of walking. Pool and changing areas were spotless. Room: Clean, sunny and spacious. Probably over 400 sq. ft. - 2 TVs, couch, desk, chairs - all in perfect shape. The windows open for some fresh air. Pillows were pretty comfortable. With all aspects considered, I think this was an unbeatable value! I would not hesitate to stay again or recommend it to a friend. I truly have nothing negative to say about the hotel. It was a wonderful stay and we will miss being there. Omni has hit the right formula to make a guest feel like a welcomed person as opposed to just a nuisance or a number. The airlines have cornered the market on that.

I stayed here for 2 nights in May 2008. I have to say the hotel was exceptionally clean and very modern and funky. They had a free wine tasting each evening! The restaurant served very good breakfasts and the staff were lovely and helpful throughout the stay. The hotel is located within walking distance to the metro system and also close to shopping / restaurants and sights! Rooms were lovely, althou the bathroom was slightly on the compact side. Will be back.

We booked the Affinia expecting a lot more for the price. The 'suite' we got was just a standard room with a couch jammed in, and the AC unit sounded like a lawnmower all night. We asked for a quiet floor at check-in and got put right next to the elevator, which dinged constantly. The hallways smell strongly of old carpet and disinfectant. On the second day, housekeeping didn't come until 5 PM, and when they did, they just dropped off fresh towels and didn't make the bed. The gym is a closet with two broken treadmills, and the 'complimentary coffee' in the lobby is lukewarm dishwater. Location is decent for walking, but honestly, for what we paid, you're better off at a standard chain two blocks away. I left feeling like this place banks entirely on its address and forgot about basic comfort. We won't be back.

Booked the Affinia based on photos promising a chic, cozy boutique vibe. What I got was a shoebox with a view of a brick wall and a radiator that clanked like a haunted boiler all night. The 'modern' bathroom had a shower head that dribbled and a fogged-up mirror I couldn't see myself in. The staff were polite but useless--asked for extra towels twice, they never arrived. The lobby smelled like stale coffee and Febreze, and the so-called 'complimentary' wifi dropped every ten minutes. Honestly, for the price, I could've stayed at a Motel 6 and gotten better sleep. The location saved it from a one-star review, but I will not be returning. Save your money.

I expected a glamorous room and I walked into a disappointment. Housekeeping and Management must not be concerned with attention to detail at this hotel. If you like staying somewhere that the air in the rooms doesn't go down past 74, the closet is 24' wide, all old/dirty brass fixtures, beds that are a little bigger than a twin, showerheads that barely put out water, then this is your hotel. I might be spoiled by staying in Marriott's, but I stay in hotels 1/3 of the year and was severly disappionted. No free breakfasts or a room change will get me to stay here again.

We had a reservation for 3 rooms with 5 adults and 2 kids, got only 2 rooms on arrival. 2 of the corner rooms with an extra room. During the night it was very cold and we were not able to change the a.c., even though we switched it off, it went on cooling, strange! At night it was very loud from the street. In the morning they uploaded something infront of our window and I stood vertically in the bed, not what you need, if you only spend 1 night in a hotel. We came here a few years ago and had it better in mind. The area is in good walking distance to all famous shopping places, very good. Clean and fancy. Sorry, but next time we`ll be looking for a more quiet hotel in Chicago.
The Hard Rock looked exciting online, but my room felt tired, the hallway was noisy all night, and staff seemed uninterested when I asked for help. Disappointing stay.

Me, My sister and my best friend all went to stay here in the summer of 2004...they said there all spacious suites...yeah right...our room you could barely walk in...and they said theres 2 double beds...yeah well one was a pull out couch...and the bathroom...tiny tiny tiny...and it took forever and a day to check in and the people blamed us for throwing a book out the window and somehow someone knew exactly where it fell from and which room...yeah...i wouldnt stay here again

The Hyatt felt like a solid value--staff were genuinely attentive without hovering, and our room stayed blissfully quiet despite a full house. The decor leans classic rather than cutting-edge, but it's well-maintained and comfortable, making the rate feel justified.

Hotel Knickerbocker's central location made exploring easy, and the staff were warmly attentive. Our bathroom was spotless and spacious, while the room stayed surprisingly quiet despite the busy area.
Booked a city view but got a parking lot; AC sounded like a jet engine and the hallways smelled like old fries. Staff were polite but the whole stay felt rundown and overpriced for what we got.

I had a very comfortable two-night stay at the Hyatt while in town for meetings. The lobby and guest room both felt current without trying too hard--warm lighting, clean furniture, and no tired patterned carpets or dated artwork. My room was quiet despite facing a busy street, and the bed, pillows, and blackout shades helped me sleep through the night better than I usually do in hotels. The bathroom was spotless, with a roomy walk-in shower, strong water pressure, plenty of counter space, and good lighting around the mirror. Staff were pleasant and quick when I needed an extra towel. It was not the cheapest option nearby, but the location, reliable service, and overall comfort made the rate feel fair. I would happily stay here again.

I stayed at the Hilton for three nights while visiting for a conference and came away very pleased. The location made getting around easy, with restaurants and public transportation only a short walk away. My room was quiet, comfortable, and larger than expected, with a good desk, plenty of outlets, and a bed that was genuinely hard to leave in the morning. Everything was clean, although the bathroom showed a little wear around the fixtures. Check-in was quick, and the front desk staff were friendly whenever I had a question. I also appreciated the well-equipped fitness room and the coffee shop downstairs for an early start. Wi-Fi worked reliably throughout my stay. It is not the most distinctive hotel I have visited, but it was dependable, comfortable, and well managed.

this is my letter to the management..... Sir or Madam: I am writing to give feedback about our recent stay the Amalfi. We were a guest from 11/20 to 11/23. During our stay we used the 'Valet' Service operated through Standard Parking. Our vehicle was returned with stolen items from the glove compartments. Much to my chagrin, $44/day valet service did not include proper security/monitoring, despite the premium over 'self park'. I understand that these parking services are sub-contracted by the hotel, but I would think that any worthy hotel would remedy the situation. This was not the case. I hope that your staff will be able to take measures to rectify the situation for future guests

took a weekend trip with my wife. got a great rate with valet included, paid a couple extra bucks for the larger room. staff was nice, workout facility was great. room has current decor, but was starting to show some wear. watch the concierge, she suggested a pretty bad restaurant to us.

I have stayed at many hotels traveling for both business and pleasure and I can honestly stay that The James is tops. The service at the hotel is first class. The rooms are modern and very comfortable. The location is perfect within walking distance to all of the great sights and restaurants. Highly recommend to both business travellers and couples.

My stay at the Sheraton was a disappointing experience overall. The room looked presentable at first, but it was not as clean as expected: there was dust along the desk, a sticky spot on the nightstand, and the carpet clearly needed a deeper vacuum. The bathroom was especially underwhelming, with worn grout, water marks on the fixtures, and weak water pressure in the shower. I also slept poorly because the mattress was too firm and hallway noise continued late into the night. Although I stayed for two nights, it felt too long rather than too short because the hotel offered little comfort or atmosphere to make the visit enjoyable. The staff were polite enough, but that did not compensate for the condition of the room.

Hotel Allegro looked promising online, but the stay was frustrating from the start. The lobby has some charm, yet the rooms feel tired, with scuffed furniture, worn carpeting, and decor that seems untouched for years. My room faced the street, and between traffic, hallway noise, and a rattling air conditioner, I barely slept either night. Breakfast was disappointing: lukewarm eggs, stale pastries, weak coffee, and very little replenished once the dining room got busy. The staff at reception were polite enough, but seemed distracted and offered no real help when I mentioned the noise. For the rate, I expected a cleaner, more comfortable experience and at least a decent night's rest.

Under the gloss of a nice building, friendly staff, and a wild set of items in the minibar, this is somewhat below-average hotel. In particular, the bed and chairs were some of the least comfortable I ever encountered. After two nights, my wife and I were practically cripped by bed pain. We complained to the staff and were immediately offered the chance to switch to a different room, but the other room was furnished identically. The owners of the Omni need to stop spending money on bath salts for the rooms and invest in the basic comforts. I should not be lying on the floor, trying to unkink my back, thinking longingly of the last Red Roof Inn I visited.

I'd heard Sheraton was a solid, reliable choice, but my stay here was anything but. The room smelled musty, like the AC filter hadn't been changed in months, and the carpet had suspicious stains near the window. Housekeeping skipped our room entirely on day two--we had to call twice just to get fresh towels. Breakfast was a chaotic free-for-all with empty chafing dishes and lukewarm coffee that tasted burnt. The pool was closed for 'maintenance' without any prior notice, which was a letdown since we booked specifically for the kids. To top it off, the front desk agent seemed annoyed when I asked for a late checkout, offering a curt 'not possible' before turning away. For the price, I expected basic competence, but this felt more like a run-down roadside motel. I won't be back.

I am usually a big fan of Kimpton Hotels, but this place is awful !!! I would rate it poor from the moment we arrived to the moment we left. It is an old, dark and damp hotel that they slapped a coat of paint on to make it look more 'botique' . The carpets are dirty, and tattered; patrons are walking around the lobby in their barefeet. yuck!!! The bathrooms are tiny, and the floors look like they have a layer of flith on them. When we called down to the desk to ask for them to be cleaned, we were brushed off and told they were made to look that way. We woke up on the first morning to find multiple wads of gum on the lobby table. We told the front desk, called housekeeping, and then called the front desk again..finally after several hours someone came and cleaned the gum. The elevators are slow, and often only one is working at any given time. I did not find the staff to be friendly at all, except for one waiter @ breakfast. What a disappointment :(
Homewood felt fresh and welcoming rather than dated, with a clean, well-kept bathroom and a convenient location near restaurants. I only wish our stay had been a little longer.

Move beyond the rock theme and it's an average hotel with a good location. Room was unbearably hot and the controls on the wall did nothing. Thank goodness the window opened or we'd have been cooked alive. That of course let in all the noise from Michigan Ave. This combined with our neighbors door slamming against their thrown door lock every 30 seconds made for a lively setting. Room was stuffy too. Burn marks on carpet lead me to believe nasty smokers had occupied room on many occasions. Wife happy w/ Aveda in bath. Base bar was good with great service and well made drinks tho pricey.
For the price, the room felt tired and cramped, with street noise well past midnight. Staff were polite but slow to respond, and the bathroom wasn't as clean as it should have been.

Hotel Monaco was a great base for a long weekend downtown. The lobby has a fun, slightly quirky style without feeling overdone, and the front desk team was genuinely warm when we arrived early and needed somewhere to leave our bags. Our room was quiet, very clean, and had surprisingly comfortable pillows; I slept better than I usually do in hotels. We also appreciated the little touches, like the evening wine hour and coffee available in the morning. The location made it easy to walk to restaurants, museums, and the river, so we barely used a cab. The bathroom was a bit compact, but the water pressure was excellent and everything worked well. I'd happily stay here again.

Be prepared the hotel is old. It is on the historic list. The is updating to be done no doubt.. So just be forewarned. It is clean and the staff is phenomenal. Having said that, you can not beat the location. Right in the heart of the Gold coast. Take a train from O'hare right into the city. It drops you off only 4 blocks from the hotel. One block from the beach and public transportation is right there. Incredible area to explore. I highly recommend the Ambassador East

Stayed here for a conference and was genuinely impressed. The bed was ridiculously comfortable, and the staff remembered my name each morning. Great location too--easy walk to the waterfront. Would happily book again.
Great location near Oak Street shops and the beach. Rooms are cozy and quiet, and the staff couldn't have been friendlier. A solid choice if you want a boutique feel in Lincoln Park.

We booked thru hotwire which we have a high percentage of positive outcomes. I was very happy when we saw that we would be staying at The Knickerbocker-as I had stayed when I was younger. We reserved a King Non-Smoker. Upon arriving we were told that they did not have that and we only had the choice of a Smoking room. When argued they stated 'well you booked thru hotwire so you do not have priority'. As we entered the room I noticed the bathroom door was off track and the bathroom light did not turn on. We called the front desk and they fixed the door but not the light. Later that eveing as I took a shower the seal around the shower was so poor water got all over the floor and towels. Also, I must add the room reaked of smoke. The next day when we checked the front desk clerk asked how our stay was and when we told him the problems, he told us the total and had not concern of our issues. We also checked in our bags for the day, and the bellmen came quickly and made very rude comments about us hurrying up so he could get on with his day. We realized a bit later that we forgot something in one of the bags and was told they would not get them back out. STAY AWAY-even if you get a good deal!!

I booked two rooms four months in advance at the Talbott. We were placed on the top floor next to the elevators, which are used all night long. When speaking to the front desk, I was told that they were simply honoring my request for an upper floor, which I had requested for a better view. I am looking at a brick wall, and getting no sleep. He also told me that they had received complaints before from guests on the 16th floor, and were aware of the noise problem. Why then did they place us on this floor when the hotel is not totally booked? A request for an upper floor does not constitute placing someone on the TOP floor and using that request to justify this. If you decide to stay here, request a room on a lower floor and away from the elevator! I spoke at length when booking my two rooms about my preferences. This is simply poor treatment of a guest whom they believed would not complain.
Hardrock looked great online, but our room was noisy, the AC barely worked, and service at check-in felt rushed. For the price, I expected much better.

The location was great, but that's about all this place has going for it. Our room smelled musty, the AC rattled all night, and the staff acted like we were bothering them. For these prices, I expected a lot more.

I would not recommend this hotel. Although it is in a good area, the room was very small and is getting rather dated. The room had extensive damage. The paint on the bathroom ceiling was peeling. The wallpaper in the bathroom was peeling. The wood work in the bathroom looked like it had been chewed on. There was mold and stains on the bathroom tile. The room was very small. There was not room for a sofa. Just a small faded chair and ottoman. The carpet had stains on it. Also, the bed was comfortable, but there was not a top sheet, just the bottom sheet and a comforter. Overall I was not satisfied with the hotel for the price that was charged. I have stayed in other hotels in the area that provided much more space, cleanliness, and value for the money paid.

When I called to edit my existing reservation, I was placed on hold for 30 minutes! Finally someone came on the phone and said, 'Ill have to transfer you', so I was put on hold for another 5 minutes. When I finally did get to speak to someone, as I was going through my changes, I asked her to send me a revised copy of the reservation to which she huffed and acted very put off. Before she was able to disconnect with me, I said 'I have one more question' to which she replied 'I'm working at the front desk and I have customers waiting!' I thought, so am I not your customer? pathetic and rude. Hotel better find some better employees for their guests to truly enjoy their stay.
Really enjoyed our stay at Hotel Palmer--room was clean and comfy, and the front desk staff went out of their way to help when our flight got delayed. Breakfast was basic but fresh. Would stay again.

We stayed in the IC chicago for 6 nights from 26th Dec after reading the reviews on Trip Advisor. We werent disappointed. We had 2 rooms opposite each other in the Historic tower. The rooms were spacious and very clean with good views towards the river and tribune building. We got a good rate on the rooms but did not have breakfast in the hotel as it was very expensive as was the Wifi at $17 per day. As the hotel is on the Magnificent mile there are plenty of place to eat including for breakfast. The starbucks in the lobby was a hit with the kids - very handy. I would definitely recommend the hotel.
Really enjoyed my stay at the Hyatt -- the front desk staff were genuinely friendly and my room was spotless with a super comfy bed. Location was walkable to everything. Would definitely book again.

Our stay at the Fairmont was a very pleasant surprise. The lobby felt polished without being stuffy, and check-in was quick even though we arrived earlier than expected. Our room was quiet, comfortable, and larger than it looked online, with a genuinely comfortable bed and plenty of space for our luggage. Housekeeping did a careful job, and the small evening turndown was a nice touch. We had breakfast at the hotel one morning; it was a little expensive, but the coffee was excellent and everything arrived quickly. What stood out most was the staff. Everyone we dealt with, from the front desk to the restaurant, was friendly and patient when we needed directions and a late checkout. It is not the cheapest option, but the service and overall ease made it feel worthwhile.

My stay at the Sheraton was disappointing from the start. The room looked dated and only superficially cleaned; there were crumbs beside the chair, dust on the nightstand, and a stain on the carpet near the bed. The bathroom was especially underwhelming, with mildew around the tub seal, weak water pressure, and towels that felt rough and worn. I barely slept because the air-conditioning rattled every few minutes and hallway noise carried straight through the door. Even though I was only there for one night, it felt much longer than it should have. Staff were polite at check-in, but that did not make up for the uncomfortable, poorly maintained room.

I arrived at the Sofitel for a joint leisure and business. It is a fantastic hotel and made the trip very memorable. The rooms are spacious, great beds, pillows and linen. The bathroom has a great shower and bath. WiFi works really well and the desk is large. The staff are wonderful. The location is great for shopping, spa's, Starbucks and hairdressers. I loved every minute of it and would not hesitate to stay there again or recommend it.

I had a very pleasant stay at Homewood and would gladly return. The room was spotless when I arrived, with clean linens, a fresh bathroom, and no signs of dust or wear in the corners. It was also surprisingly quiet, which made it easy to relax after a long day. Every staff member I encountered was friendly and professional, from check-in to the morning departure, and they were happy to answer questions without being overly formal. The decor is not especially modern, but it felt well maintained and comfortable rather than genuinely dated. The bed was supportive, and having a little extra space made the room feel less cramped. Considering the cleanliness, service, and overall comfort, the price felt fair and well worth it.

We also just returned from a frigid weekend in Chicago. I booked the Ambassador East because of its great rate, $89.00 with my AAA card and we were delighted. Yes, the rooms show some signs of wear, but the warmth and charm far make up for it. This was such a pleasant change from the sleek, modern look of many other chain and boutique hotels. We became members of the I preferred program and were therefore eligible for an upgrade which we automatically got upon check in. We had a lovely suite with lots of sitting room and a comfortable bedroom and bathroom. We had wonderful food at the Pump Room which is classic. Our oatmeal there was so tastefully served, I'd love to have some right now! The location was great. Had it been normal winter weather, we could have easily walked to Michigan Avenue for shopping, but due to the minus 20 degree windchills, we opted for a cab which was less than a $5.00 fare. We also enjoyed a glass of wine around the fireplace in the lobby and found it so welcoming and cozy and not overcrowed at all. We would definitely stay here again!

The Fairmont's grandeur fades fast--our room was tired, with a view of an air shaft and a bathroom that smelled musty all weekend. Staff were polite but stretched thin, making us wait 20 minutes for a simple ice refill. For the price, this felt like a letdown.

The breakfast buffet had everything from fresh pastries to made-to-order omelets, and the staff were genuinely warm and efficient. Waking up to a sweeping city view from the 22nd floor made the price feel completely justified.

My fiance and I traveled to Chicago for the first time this December and we were not happy with this hotel. The friendliest people on the staff were the bell boys. They greeted us with a smile and gave us lots of great advice throughout our stay. The rest of the staff however was terrible. When we first checked in, I was instantly discouraged. The front desk person was not in a good mood and I couldn't wait to leave the lobby. Having not traveled here before we were looking for exciting places to eat and to go sightseeing. We asked multiple staff members at the front desk of places to go and see and never got any good recommendations. We felt as if we were an inconvenience to the staff. At one point, the front desk person was on the phone while we were waiting to talk to her, as she was on the phone a family of four came up behind us waiting to talk to her as well. Even though she saw us standing there, after she finished with the phone call she ignored us and helped the family first. Yes, we are in our mid 20's, but we are still paying guests and there is no reason to be treated like we are invisible. For how much money we paid for each night, I would have rather stayed somewhere else. We decided to go with this hotel because of the location and the great reviews, but we did not experience any of this during our stay. The rooms were alright, but nothing special. I would not stay in this hotel again.

My company booked our group for a Conference and Sales Meeting. The service was friendly, helpful and the property was beautiful. The hotel was clean and filled with history. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay and the rate was reasonable as well.

I booked the Conrad expecting the usual Hilton luxury, but this stay fell embarrassingly short. The check-in process was a mess--two agents arguing about my room type while I stood there, then a 'surprise' that they'd given away my suite and bumped me to a standard room with a view of the air conditioning units. Housekeeping never came until 5pm, and even then, they forgot fresh towels twice. The bathroom had a persistent mildew smell, and the shower pressure was pathetic. I tried the lounge, but it was packed with noisy conference attendees and the food was lukewarm, clearly sitting out for hours. The bed was decent, I'll give them that, but for nearly $400 a night, I expect working elevators and staff who actually care. Honestly, I've had better experiences at a Courtyard. I won't be back.

October 3rd, 2007 My wife and I stayed at The Sofitel toward the end of September 2007. The hotel is VERY modern. The room was immaculate, but the furiture looked as though it came from IKEA. It was chipped in many places. The light switches were difficult to find, and the HVAC made noise. However, the bed was wonderful. The bathroom was large and well maintained.
