Housekeeping brought us as many towels as we wanted. The restaurant was small. You can eat for less at a 24 hour restaurant around the corner called Tempo. If you want a truly great breakfast try The Peninsula Hotel. However, after dining there you might not want to return to The Sofitel. Prior to checking in we had paid for everything in full. When we checked in, we were asked to leave a credit card for incidentals. Upon returning home, we discovered that although the credit card had not been used the Sofitel had an authorization placed on it. This reduced the line of credit, and it took several days to be removed from the card. Great location! Reasonable value. If you have a Privilege Card they allow you to check out at 4pm as opposed to 12 in the afternoon.

Ambassador East is an awesome hotel!!! Understand that this hotel is full of history and is a boutique hotel. My family stayed at the Ambassador for two nights in a suite. Very clean room with great space. The best part of the Ambassador is not the rooms though. The staff was extremely courteous, especially the concierge. If you stay here you have to go to the Pump Room. The restaurant is full of nostalgia, the staff is great, and the food is excellent. Great atmosphere and music.

Hotel Monaco is in a really great location, only a block away from the Miracle mile and a couple of blocks from Millenium Park. Sears Tower is also well within walking distance and if you don't mind walking you won't have a problem walking to Greek Town and Lincoln Park (we did). The daily, complimentary, wine hour is a really nice touch that we unfortunately were only around once to try out. If you can, leave your car behind, you won't need it and the parking is quite pricey, which is not very surprising considering the location. Everything was clean, fresh and modern and the staff very helpful. The only bad thing was that the noise from the elevated train around 'the loop' was quite loud and that our room happened to be next to the maid's supply room so it was quite busy in the morning.

My stay at the Swissotel was more disappointing than I expected for a property with such a strong reputation. The room was reasonably spacious, but the decor felt tired rather than fresh, with scuffed furniture, faded carpet, and a generally dated atmosphere. I had requested a quiet room, yet I could hear doors slamming and conversations in the hallway late into the night, followed by traffic noise early in the morning. The view was another letdown: mostly nearby buildings and service areas, with only a narrow glimpse of the city. The bathroom was clean enough, but the fixtures looked worn, water pressure was inconsistent, and there was very little counter space. Nothing was especially terrible, but the price suggested a more polished and comfortable experience than this hotel delivered.

I wanted to like the Knickerbocker, especially given the price and reputation, but the stay was more frustrating than enjoyable. Our room looked stylish in photos, yet it felt cramped and showed wear around the furniture. The bed was comfortable enough, but hallway noise and doors slamming late at night kept waking us, so neither of us slept well. Breakfast was another disappointment: the buffet was limited, lukewarm, and slow to be replenished, with coffee that tasted stale. The bathroom was clean but surprisingly small, with weak water pressure and almost no counter space for toiletries. We were also promised a city view, but our window faced a nearby wall and a collection of rooftop machinery. Staff were polite when approached, though service felt impersonal. For this rate, I expected a considerably better experience.

We arrived at 10:30 am on a Friday, and they had a room ready for us by 11:30 am, mind you check in is not until 3:00pm. We got our room on Priceline for $65.00 per night and stayed 3 nights. We were upgraded - for free - to a suite. I think I was so blown away by that, that I forgot to thank them at check-in! Our room was fantastic. It also had a wet bar and a fridge. The bathroom was quite large and had a nice sized closet with many hangers. I knew from previous reviews to not touch the mini-bar. The bed and pillows were very comfortable. The room was very clean. Every employee there went out of their way to be friendly and helpful. We stayed on the 25th floor of the east tower and had a quiet room. Yes, you could hear people in the hallways, but only because they were rude and were yelling. These were not children, they were adults. I don't know why everyone complains about $48 for parking. This is Chicago and every other hotel we saw charged just as much, some without in/out privledges. We didn't use any of the restaurants or the health club. We tried to eat at the Corner Bakery but it was too crowded. Breakfast at nearby Houlihan's had a buffet for $9.99 per person. Also the grocery store behind the hotel is great. There is a 7-11 not too far away. I don't know why there are so many bad reviews on this hotel. Yes, it's a big hotel. If you don't want a busy lobby, don't stay in a 2,000 plus room hotel!! I loved the Hotel and would recommend it to anyone. Not one problem. Wasn't too busy for me. Would stay here again in a heartbeat.

I stayed at the Hyatt for a quick weekend in town and came away pleasantly impressed. The lobby was busy when I arrived, but the front desk handled the line efficiently and even pointed me toward a nearby coffee shop while my room was being finalized. My room was on a higher floor, quiet at night, with a comfortable bed, useful desk, and plenty of outlets for charging everything. The bathroom was spotless and the water pressure was better than expected. Breakfast downstairs was not cheap, but the buffet had enough fresh options to make it convenient. I also appreciated that the elevators were quick, which sounds minor until you are rushing out for a meeting. Staff throughout the hotel were friendly without being overly formal. I would happily book here again.
Service was indifferent and the room felt dated, with a broken AC that took hours to fix. The noise from the bar below made rest impossible, and I left feeling ripped off for the price.

Great stay at the Sheraton overall. The bed was incredibly comfortable and the club lounge breakfast saved me time every morning. Staff at the front desk remembered my name by day two, which was a nice touch. Would happily return.

This is a great hotel but there is no way that I would recommend it until the construction around it is complete. The elevator is the alley starts for the construction site behind at 5:30am and goes on into the night. Dumpster filling and emptying also seems to go on 24/7. Worst of all, the restaurant is open to the sidewalk cafe here and the rats go scampering from the construction next door to street to grating. Ugh!

I wanted to like the Hard Rock, but the stay was more frustrating than fun. The lobby was crowded and loud at all hours, and check-in took nearly 40 minutes even though I had already completed everything online. Our room looked worn, with scuffed furniture, a slow-draining shower, and a window that faced a noisy service area. Housekeeping skipped our room one day and only brought towels after I called twice. The music theme is entertaining in the public areas, but it also means you should expect noise late into the night; earplugs barely helped. Staff members were polite when reached, yet nobody seemed eager to solve problems. For the price, I expected a cleaner room and smoother service. The location was convenient, but I would choose another hotel next time.

I really wanted to love The Knickerbocker, especially given the location and the price, but the stay was more disappointing than impressive. Check-in took far too long, and the room wasn't ready until well after the advertised time. When I finally got in, the room looked stylish but felt surprisingly cramped, with scuffed furniture and a bathroom that needed better cleaning. The air-conditioning was noisy throughout the night, and the pillows were uncomfortably flat. Staff were polite, though not particularly attentive when I called about the issue. The rooftop bar has a great view, but the drinks were overpriced and service was slow even when it wasn't busy. For a luxury hotel, I expected much more attention to detail. Great location, but the experience didn't justify the cost.

The room felt dated and the air conditioning rattled all night, making sleep impossible. Breakfast was a chaotic stampede with lukewarm food, and the front desk seemed annoyed by every request--hardly the standard you'd expect from this name.

Excellent Hotel ! Rooms and service were great. A great value ! I have been to places that are not as good for nearly twice the price. Good location. Close to the L and short walk to rental car service. Restaurants in the area a bit of a disappointment, but the shopping was great. Area recommendations Great theatre, restaurants, museums and shopping.

I had a really pleasant stay at Hotel Monaco. The location was ideal for walking around downtown, with restaurants, shops, and the main attractions all close by, yet my room was surprisingly quiet at night. The decor has a playful, boutique feel without sacrificing comfort, and the bed was excellent after long days exploring. Everything was clean and well maintained, and the front desk staff were genuinely friendly and quick to help with directions and dinner suggestions. I also appreciated the little thoughtful touches, including the complimentary coffee in the morning and the relaxed atmosphere in the lobby. The only minor issue was that the bathroom felt a bit tight, but it was spotless and functional. Overall, the hotel offered great service, character, and a very convenient stay.

We stayed at the Ambassador for three nights in early October and were thoroughly impressed. Our room on the sixth floor was spotless when we checked in, not a dust mote or stray hair anywhere, and housekeeping kept it that way throughout our visit. The bathroom was surprisingly roomy, with a deep tub, strong water pressure, and fluffy towels replaced daily without our even having to ask. I was a little worried the decor might feel tired given the hotel's age, but the recent renovation shows: fresh paint, updated light fixtures, and a nice mix of classic and contemporary touches. Best of all, the beds are genuinely comfortable with firm mattresses and quality pillows, so I slept better than I do at home. Location near the park was a bonus. Would happily return.

I stayed here for about a week during a conference and the service was excellent. In addition to the excellent service the location was great. With quick access to Michigan Ave.. The bars and Shula's restaurant were excellent. You must have the rib-eye steak...very well done.

We stayed at the Intercontinental for our anniversary weekend and it honestly exceeded what we expected. Check-in was quick and the front desk agent noticed the occasion from our booking notes and sent up a plate of chocolates with a handwritten card, which was a lovely touch. Our room on a higher floor had a gorgeous view of the harbor, and the bed was probably the most comfortable I've slept in at any hotel, pillows included. Housekeeping was discreet and thorough, turndown service every evening. We used the concierge twice for dinner reservations and both spots were excellent. Breakfast buffet had a huge spread, though it does get busy around nine so go early. Only minor gripe was the wait for the elevator one morning, but that's hardly a complaint. Would absolutely return.

The hotel Palmer is seriously tired--our room had scuffed walls and a broken desk lamp, while the breakfast buffet featured congealed eggs and lukewarm coffee. For these rates, I'd expect fresh towels daily, not a worn-out stay.

We stayed at the Homewood for three nights, and honestly, it delivered far more than I expected for the rate we paid. Our room on the seventh floor had a killer view of the skyline, especially at dusk when the lights started popping on--it felt like a free show every evening. The staff were the real highlight though; from the front desk to housekeeping, everyone seemed genuinely invested in making our stay smooth, even remembering our names by day two. The Wi-Fi was rock solid, too--I ran a few video calls without a single drop, which is rare for a hotel this size. Breakfast was standard but fresh, and the location made it easy to walk to dinner spots. I'd absolutely book again next time I'm in town. Minor nitpick: the hallway carpets looked a bit tired, but that didn't dull an otherwise great stay.

Stayed at the Chicago Hilton for three nights and from the minute we walked through the door I was very impressed. Check-in was quick, easy and I was very glad that we were able to check in despite being earlier than the advertised check-in time. We were given a twin room with two bathrooms which was brilliant. It made getting ready to go out much quicker! The hotel location is great opposite the park, which is a must see. Although located on South Michigan Ave it is easily within walking distance of all the shops and sights of the whole of Michigan Ave. Would also recommend the street one block back from Michigan Ave for good shopping. For breakfast I would recommend grabbing a muffin, croissant or bagel from the bar just past reception rather than going for the more expensive breakfast in the restaurant. For evening entertainment Kitty O'Sheas is a must. Typical Irish bar with good drinks and live music. Finally the bed at Hilton Chicago is the most comfortable bed ever. I would have taken it home if I could! Definately made for a good nights sleep.
Swissotel delivered a comfortable stay: reliable Wi‐Fi, genuinely friendly staff, and a bright city view from my room. The price felt fair for the location and overall service.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly couldn't have picked a better spot. The location is unbeatable--steps from the riverfront and a short stroll to all the good restaurants, but the street itself stays quiet at night, which I appreciated. Check-in was smooth, and they even let us into our room early since we'd arrived before the standard time. The room itself was stylish without feeling stuffy, and the bed was genuinely comfortable; I slept like a log both nights. Bathroom had great water pressure and those little toiletries that actually smell nice. The bar downstairs is worth a visit even if you're not a guest--the bartender mixed a killer Old Fashioned. Only tiny gripe: the hallway ice machine was out on our floor, but the front desk sent someone up with a bucket within minutes. Would gladly book again.

I stayed here August 20 through 23rd with my sixteen year old son and we thoroughly enjoyed this hotel. The price was very reasonable for a hotel located right on Michigan Avenue. The front desk and concierge service was excellent and enhanced our stay by making it easy for us to plan fun activities. The John Entwistle theme on our floor was a nice touch. Any of you single fathers out there can appreciate how difficult it can be to take a fun affordable vacation with your children and The Hard Rock Hotel in Chicago really helped me accomplish just that!

I loved this hotel - reasonable for downtown Chicago, an older hotel with a great reno (a bit over-the-top design, but still very lovely and charming), clean rooms, and very friendly staff. They're also amazingly pet-friendly - they welcomed our 130lb Mastiff cross with a gift bag (treats and directions to an off-leash area), and even had a cute blackboard with visiting dog's names on it.

Was really expecting more from the Intercontinental. The room was passably clean but the decor felt straight out of the 90s, my 'view' was a brick wall, and the bathroom tile was grimy around the edges. Disappointing for the price.

I had a very pleasant stay at Hotel Amalfi. The room was spotless and a good size, with a comfortable bed and surprisingly quiet nights; I slept better than expected despite being in a busy part of town. The location was especially convenient for walking to restaurants, shops, and nearby attractions, and taxis were easy to find when I needed one. The lobby and guest rooms have a warm, classic style rather than a completely modern look. Some furniture shows a little age, but everything is well maintained, and the decor feels charming instead of dated. Staff members were friendly and quick to help with directions and dinner suggestions. I only stayed two nights, which felt too short, since the hotel was an easy and comfortable base for exploring.

We stayed at the Sofitel for three nights and honestly wished it had been a week. The bed was wonderful -- the mattress had that perfect balance of firmness and softness, and with the blackout curtains I slept straight through every night without waking once, which almost never happens for me. Even better, the room was remarkably quiet despite the hotel being fully booked; we heard no hallway noise or street traffic at all, just the distant hum of the air conditioning. The wifi was fast and reliable throughout, easily handling video calls and streaming in the evenings without a single drop. Staff were warm and attentive from check-in to checkout, and the breakfast spread was excellent. Highly recommend and we'll definitely be back.

Wow. Here is a place to NEVER hold an event. First, no one smiles, including the bartenders. Doesn't anyone here know they are in the HOSPITALITY business? The bartender was 54 years old. Why do I know that? Because, she stated to another employee that 'when you get to be 54 years old, you tell it like it is.' Very specifically, she was referring to the fact that she could tell her employers how they should run things. Wow. The room was set up the wrong way for the event. The food was just plain bad. $9 at a Ponderosa would have been as good. However, this is the Swisshotel. Oh, let's go back to the bartender telling us, unsolicited, about all the problems with the hotel. Man, you just have to wonder how a place like this stays in business. $50 for valet. Ouch. Anyone asking you if you need something, like help? No. Does management make excuses? You bet. Do you ever want to hold an event here? Big no.
Disappointing Hyatt stay: my room overlooked a noisy loading area, so sleep was restless. Staff were polite but distant, and the promised city view felt bleak.

Location is excellent, but don't valet your car there,(53.00 a day). Bed was to soft, pillows were flat, we couldn't open up the mini bar cabinet because the bed was in the way. All in all not what you'd expect from a hotel in that area.

I expected much more from Swissotel given the rate and the name. The lobby looks polished, but the experience fell apart quickly. Check-in took nearly 25 minutes because only one desk was staffed, and nobody acknowledged the line. My room had a nice view but felt tired: scuffed furniture, a stained chair, and an air conditioner that rattled all night. The bathroom fan did not work, so it stayed damp after a shower. I called twice about extra towels and they arrived the following afternoon, after I had already gone out. Breakfast was crowded, lukewarm, and oddly understocked. Location was convenient, but that alone did not justify the price. I left feeling like I had paid for appearances rather than service.

Stayed at the Sheraton for a conference and was pleasantly surprised by how comfortable everything felt. The staff were genuinely friendly, the bed was amazing, and the lobby bar had great cocktails after a long day. Solid choice overall.
Hotel Palmer was a pleasant surprise--our room was spotless and quiet, the bed incredibly comfortable, and the staff genuinely welcoming. The location also made it easy to explore everything nearby.
The 'bay view' was a muddy rooftop, and our bathroom smelled of stale bleach. Slept poorly on a lumpy mattress, and for this price, it felt like a wasted weekend getaway.

The Hilton exceeded my expectations--room was spotless with a great view, and the front desk even remembered my coffee order by day two. Location made sightseeing a breeze, and I'd happily book here again for the price.

After checking out of the Sofitel Chicago Water Tower the other day, I left the hotel, crossed the street and started to walk EB on Chestnut while looking for a cab. I was still within sight of a Sofitel doorman when I sighted a cab approximately one block away and attempted to hail same. After doing so, I immediately heard a Sofitel doorman yelling for me to stop and then heard the sound of his whistle. As the cab slowed to pick me up, the doorman continued to yell at me and blow his whistle as he started to run in my direction. When the cab stopped, I quickly entered cab and locked the door for fear of being physically attacked by the Sofitel doorman. After locking the door, the doorman attempted to open the door as he continued to accost me from outside of the cab. After claiming that he had hotel customers waiting for cabs, he suggested that I had no right to hail a cab in the vicinity of the hotel and then called me a 'jerk' before allowing the cab driver to depart to my destination. Consequently, unless you enjoy being accosted by hotel doormen, please don't attempt to hail a cab anywhere near the hotel under any circumstances without first securing the permission of a doorman. Lastly, as for the rest of my stay, you will enjoy this hotel if you seek a highly pretentious staff who prefer to speak to guests in French instead of English. While I have nothing against the French or French language, I much prefer communicating in English when visiting one of the best cities in the best country in the world. Viva la USA!

Our stay at the Fairmont was exactly what we needed after a long travel day. The lobby feels grand without being stuffy, and the check-in process was smooth and welcoming, even with a small line. Our room overlooked the city and was genuinely quiet, which made for an excellent sleep. The bed was plush without being too soft, and the blackout curtains did their job perfectly. I particularly appreciated the little touches--the turn-down service left a small card with the next day's weather, and the bathroom amenities smelled lovely. We had breakfast at the hotel restaurant and the service was attentive but not hovering. The location made walking to most sights easy, though we did use the valet once and it was quick. Overall, a comfortable, polished stay that met all expectations, and we would definitely return.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly, I'm still thinking about the bed. That mattress was pure cloud--slept like a log all three nights, which never happens in hotels. Location is unbeatable: two blocks from the river, easy walk to all the good coffee spots, and quiet enough at night. The front desk guy, Marcus, remembered our names and had great tips for a hidden speakeasy we'd have never found. Room was compact but smartly laid out, with a rainfall shower that had serious pressure. Breakfast was simple--pastries, fruit, decent espresso--but the fresh orange juice was a lovely touch. Only tiny gripe: the hallway ice machine was out of order one afternoon. Minor. Would absolutely book again for the location and that heavenly bed.
Hotel Allegro was disappointing: the bathroom was cramped and dated, and the room had dust in the corners. For the price, I expected better; my window faced a brick wall.

Stayed here for a business trip and was pleasantly surprised by how smoothly everything went. The location is unbeatable--right next to the metro and a short stroll to the waterfront, which made getting around a breeze after my meetings. Wi-Fi was strong and reliable in both the room and the lobby, no dropped connections during video calls, which is rare in my experience. The staff genuinely stood out; from the cheerful front desk who upgraded me to a higher floor to the housekeeper who remembered my late checkout request without being reminded. Considering the service and the comfy bed, I'd say it was worth every penny, even though it's not the cheapest option. Room was quiet, the breakfast buffet had solid variety, and I left feeling refreshed. Would happily book again.
Sofitel made our weekend in the city wonderfully easy, with a quiet, comfortable room, polished service, and a surprisingly good breakfast. I'd happily stay here again.

The harbor view was nice enough, but that's where the praise ends. Paper-thin walls meant hearing every neighbor all night, I barely slept, and the disinterested staff couldn't have cared less. Expected far more from Conrad.

Despite the prime location, my stay was a letdown. The room felt dusty and worn, and the street noise kept me tossing all night with a view of a brick wall. Staff seemed indifferent when I complained, and I left more tired than I arrived.
Hard Rock delivered a fun, comfortable stay; the fresh breakfast buffet had plenty of options, Wi-Fi worked flawlessly, and the price felt fair. Our weekend was over far too soon.

Any traveler who is loyal to a favorite hotel has experienced this sad truth: eventually the lodging deteriorates. But you do not expect the price to double and triple at the same time! I have been staying at the Talbott for several decades. Yes, changes have been made, like the updated heating and cooling systems and the front entrance, most recently. But other things have gone downhill. For the last several stays I have experienced very dirty carpets and slow service. Rates have skyrocketed and now they are asking for 3 night minimum stays on many occasions. This is the kind of rate structure one might expect from the 5 star hotels within spitting distance of The Talbott, but not this less-than-maintained lodging. I, personally, am shopping for a new home away from home.

The rooms are stunning, but the staff seemed overwhelmed and indifferent during our entire stay. We waited over an hour for luggage delivery, and the pool was inexplicably closed for a private event without notice. Expected far more for the price.
Slept wonderfully on the plush bed and loved waking up to the city view from our window. Spacious, spotless bathroom too -- felt totally worth the price for a Midtown stay.

Booked a weekend here expecting the usual Hilton polish--walked away genuinely underwhelmed. Check-in took nearly twenty minutes despite arriving at 4 PM, and the front desk agent seemed more interested in her phone than acknowledging the queue. The room itself was clean, sure, but the AC rattled all night like a trapped wasp, and the 'city view' was basically a brick wall and a ventilation shaft. Breakfast was the real letdown: lukewarm scrambled eggs, stale pastries, and coffee that tasted burnt, all for $28 per person. On top of that, housekeeping never replaced our towels after the first day, and when I called down about it, I got transferred three times and eventually gave up. The lobby bar was packed with conference attendees and the bartender openly ignored me for ten minutes. Honestly, for the price, the Hampton down the street would've been a better bet. Save your money.
Hotel Monaco looked stylish, but the room was noisy all night and housekeeping missed basic cleaning. For the price, the worn furniture and slow front desk service were disappointing.
The James was a comfortable base for our Chicago weekend--the room was quiet, the bed was excellent, and the staff were genuinely helpful. Its location made exploring easy.

My wife and I booked a last-minute weekend getaway and landed at Allegro, and honestly, it was a happy accident. The room was compact but spotless, and the bed was surprisingly comfy--I slept better here than at home. The real standout was the staff. From the front desk who let us check in early to the bartender who remembered our drink order on night two, everyone seemed genuinely happy to help. The rooftop pool is small but perfect for a lazy afternoon, and the included breakfast hit the spot every morning, especially the fresh-baked pastries. Location-wise, it's a quick walk to the tram and a few great local spots we found. The walls are a tad thin, and the shower pressure could be stronger, but for the price, this place overdelivers. We've already mentioned coming back.

The view of the Chicago skyline from my room was stunning, and the location made it effortless to walk everywhere I wanted. The decor felt classic without being dated, though I genuinely wished I had one more night to soak it all in.
The room was spotless, with a lovely city view, and our two-night stay felt far too short. Omni's central location made restaurants and attractions wonderfully convenient.

The hallways smelled like stale cigarette smoke, and housekeeping ignored our request for extra towels twice. Honestly, for these prices, the threadbare carpets and lukewarm shower were a total letdown. We left feeling ripped off.
The Hyatt was surprisingly noisy at night, and my room faced a bland parking structure. For the steep rate, unreliable Wi‐Fi and worn furnishings made the stay feel disappointing.

From checkin to departure a poorly run hotel. It took 30 minutes in line to check in because only one clerk was on duty. Another person, perhaps the manager, was in the back room but never came out to help the check in clerk even as the line grew. The hotels elevators are small resulting in 10 minute waits to get up and down floors,especially when 1 of the 3 breaks, as seems to be frequent occurence. After specifically asking for a room away from the elevators, I was assigned to a room directly across from them, necessitating another 20 minute wait in line. The room smelled of mildew and water dripped from the ceiling the first night. I requested a news paper be delivered to my room - it appeared on the morning and never again. Basically, the hotel is understaffed and poorly trained. Never again !

The location is fine, but the room was noisy all night and the AC barely worked. Staff seemed overwhelmed and forgot our wake-up call. For these prices, I expected way more polish. Left feeling pretty let down overall.

Stayed at the Hard Rock over a long weekend and honestly didn't want to leave. The whole vibe hits you the moment you walk in--music playing, guitars on the walls, just a cool energy without feeling gimmicky. Room was quiet, bed super comfy, and the blackout curtains actually worked, which is rare. I loved that they had a real record player in the room with a small vinyl collection; that was a fun touch we didn't expect. Staff were down-to-earth and quick with dinner spots that weren't tourist traps. Pool area gets busy but the service there kept things flowing. Only minor gripe was the elevator wait during checkout, but that's it. We've already booked our next stay. Solid pick for a fun, comfortable trip.
Expected more from a Hilton: the room smelled stale, the AC rattled all night, and front desk staff barely acknowledged us when we mentioned it.

Bathroom had a clogged drain and chipped tiles, and the hallway decor felt stuck in the 1980s. The location was central, which helped, but even a two-night stay dragged on far too long given the dated, run-down feel.

The Conrad's location is unbeatable for exploring, but what really stuck with me was how quiet and comfortable the room felt after long days out. Staff were genuinely warm, and the little touches--like the evening turndown--made it feel special.

The room had a stale smell and crumbs near the nightstand, and the so-called city view was just a brick wall. Street noise bled through the windows all night, while the front desk shrugged off my complaints with a dismissive 'we'll look into it.'

Outmoded and worn furnishings combine with some poor original design choices to produce a drab place to stay. This hotel's five-star rating needs a downgrade! When I visited this hotel 14 years ago, The Fairmont was among the classiest brands. No more. My 29th floor room was expansive, but dark -- only one small window and one light was not working. The upholstery was frayed, the bathtub faucet produced only a trickle of water, and the room's door didn't close unless you pulled on it in a certain way. Worse, the management has filled the room with price lists and displays of things to sell you, with one set of snacks even in a large tacky plastic case on the dresser. It was like sleeping in an old vending machine, but when I looked for a pen to take a phone message, there was none to be found. Other reviewers remarked that this hotel 'needs updating,' but I think some of the original design choices are also to blame. For instance, someone decided to place a series of heavy doors in strange configurations. I couldn't sit on the toilet without leaving the door to the toilet cubby open -- the space wouldn't accommodate my legs. (I am not unusually tall.) There are so many great hotels in Chicago that deserve five stars, that the Fairmont shouldn't be able to compete. See my profile for better ideas. Niftyc

I booked the Hard Rock hoping for a fun, rock-and-roll vibe, but what I got was a tired, overpriced room that felt like a generic budget hotel with a guitar decal slapped on the wall. The bathroom was the worst part: the shower head dripped constantly, the grout was stained dark in the corners, and the tiny mirror was fogged up for a full hour after any hot water ran. Honestly, at over $300 a night, this was a total rip-off. The room itself had crumbs on the carpet near the mini-fridge and a suspicious sticky patch by the desk that housekeeping clearly missed. As for noise, forget sleeping in--the hallway thumped with bass from a party until 3 AM, and the ice machine on our floor rattled like a broken snare drum all night. The only thing 'hard' about this stay was the bed, which felt like a concrete slab. Save your money and pick somewhere else.

Booked a suite at Affinia and walked into a dated room that smelled faintly of old carpet. AC rattled all night, and housekeeping never replenished the tiny shampoo bottles. For the price, the staff were polite but overwhelmed--truly underwhelming stay.

Sadly disappointing stay at Hotel James. Walls were paper-thin--I heard every hallway conversation all night, making my two days feel endless. WiFi constantly dropped, and the location was far from anything worth visiting.

Breakfast was overcooked eggs and stale pastries, the window looked onto a brick wall, and the wifi dropped constantly. Staff seemed annoyed by every question, making me feel like an inconvenience rather than a guest.

Loved my stay at Hotel Palmer -- the balcony view of the harbor was stunning, and restaurants were just a short walk away. Rooms feel freshly updated, and the quiet hallways meant I slept soundly both nights.

I haven't stayed all that much with Hyatt and I'm not sure if I will be going back anytime soon. The staff was very professional and helpful. Our room was close to being 4 stars; however, fell a little short. It really is time for a remodel of the bathroom. The toilet was of an older and flawed design where you had to close the lid to flush. I'm not a germ freak or anything; however, I really don't want to have to constantly have to touch anything on a toilet if I don't have to. The hotel was fully booked with a teen convention (FCCLA) and unfortunately for anyone else we all suffered for it. The noise at night from every direction. The only way to describe it was as if every room around us was having a slumber party. Coming back from dinner one night it took twenty minutes for us to get to our room due to the traffic. With little to no supervision the kids would cut in line to get on the elevators or they would jump floors not to mention having teens going floor to floor to visit with one another, absolutely ridiculous. The lobby of the Hyatt at night was a complete Zoo. During our second night I finally had enough and called to complain only to be told the Hotel was fully aware of the situation and that there really wasn't anything they could do. ...read more

Overview: --Overrated hotel in a premium location. The Great: --Location - walking distance or cheap cab ride to a ton of great restaurants, bars, and sights. The Good: --Inviting lobby, pleasant staff though a few were a bit snobby, in particular the night deskman. --Nice bathroom, comfortable bed and desk chair. The Mediocre: --Room (excluding bathroom) was underwhelming in design. --No kitchen or bar though they have limited room service from Harry Caray's across the street. --Free cocktails 5-7pm in 'lounge' is right idea with wrong execution; tiny little room packed with people and a line extending out the door. --Hot water (or lack thereof) - almost every morning my shower water temperature would waver between comfortably hot to lukewarm. Pressure is pretty low. --View - mine wasn't great but apparently some of the rooms are horrible. The Bad: --Free wi-fi / ethernet has inconstant speeds and required multiple logins every day, even when my computer wasn't moved - really aggravating. Same deal for my iPhone. I also got numerous vulnerability threat warnings from my Norton Anti-virus that makes me wonder how secure it is. --No blackout curtains! I had a corner room with a huge wrap-around window and awoke to bright sunlight every morning (not to mention a near total lack of privacy at night). Never had this issue in any hotel or motel I've ever stayed at. --Noise! - the hotel is sandwiched between a few different bars and the late night cacophony of yelling, bar music, trucks, car horns, and sirens is hugely distracting well into the early hours of the morning. I had to wear ear plugs despite being on the 5th floor. --TV had crappy HD signal with out of sync audio on every channel. And the remote was useless. --In room bar had standard inflated prices but the $7 bottle of Fiji water bedside was insulting. Don't even think of opening it; there's a 7-Eleven around the corner that sells exact same bottle for a fraction of the cost. Summary: --Not recommended. Looks much nicer in the website photos than it is. Rating on Yelp is bloated by at a least a star.
The dated decor and constant hallway noise made our two-night stay feel twice as long. I barely slept on the lumpy mattress, and the thin walls meant every slamming door jolted me awake.
Disappointing for the price. The room had dust on every surface, the bathroom smelled musty with a slow drain, and the 'view' was a brick wall. Not coming back.

The lobby of the Homewood is right down the hall from the kitchen and dining room(actually more of a grade school cafeteria type set up). The odors from the kitchen were disgusting, and indeed reminded my of that of a institutional kitchen(I.e. hospital). The free breakfast and free dinner were not at all palatable. I suppose that if you are traveling with a young family as many guests were, that makes this hotel a good value. But i would not stay here again.

Stayed here for two days while attending Lollopalooza music festival. One of the best locations in Chicago, on Michigan Ave near the Tribune and Sun-Times buildings. An easy walk or bus ride to many attractions. The King sized room was very nice, not large, but with a generous bathroom. Service was excellent throughout. Check out the awesome swimming pool, straight out of twenties.

I stayed at the Hotel Palmer for three nights in early October and was genuinely impressed. The lobby and rooms have been recently renovated, so everything felt fresh and modern rather than the tired, dated look you sometimes get at this price point. My room on the sixth floor faced an interior courtyard, which kept things remarkably quiet despite the busy street outside--I slept better there than I do at home, honestly. The front desk staff were warm without being overbearing; when I asked about a late checkout they arranged it in under a minute, no fuss. Breakfast was included and better than expected: fresh fruit, decent pastries, eggs cooked to order, and good coffee that someone actually refilled promptly. Only minor quibble was slow elevator service at peak times. Would gladly return.

We stayed at the Hard Rock for four nights over a long weekend and honestly it exceeded what I expected. The music theme could easily feel gimmicky but it's done well, memorabilia everywhere without being over the top. Our room was quiet despite being right off the main drag, the bed was genuinely comfortable, and the shower had great water pressure. Staff were consistently friendly, the front desk got us into a late checkout no problem, and the bartender down in the lobby bar made a killer old fashioned while a live acoustic set played. Location is solid too, walkable to a bunch of restaurants and nightlife. Only small gripe was slow elevator waits at peak times and valet taking a bit long one evening. Still, I'd book it again without hesitation. Great value for what we paid.

I had high hopes for Hotel Amalfi, but honestly, the experience left a sour taste. The room itself was passable at first glance, but the carpet had a sticky patch near the mini-fridge, and there was a suspicious, damp smell that lingered the entire time. Our one-night stay ended up feeling interminable, mostly because the air conditioning unit rattled like a coffee grinder all night, making sleep nearly impossible.

The staff were polite enough at check-in, but whenever we called down for extra towels or a wake-up call, we were met with a dismissive tone and long holds. The bathroom was the worst offender: the showerhead sprayed in a weak, erratic pattern, and the grouting had gone a worrying shade of black. Plus, the exhaust fan didn't work, leaving the room steamy and muggy. For the price, I expected far more, and I cannot recommend this place.

I wanted to like the Talbott because the location is excellent, but the stay was more frustrating than relaxing. Check-in took nearly half an hour even though the desk did not seem especially busy, and the employee helping us was distracted and offered little information. Our room looked tired, with scuffed furniture, a slow-draining sink, and a window that let in constant street noise. Housekeeping also skipped our room one day, and when we called for fresh towels, they arrived much later than promised. The bed was comfortable enough, but that was about the only thing that felt dependable. For the price, I expected a more polished experience and better attention to basic service. The Talbott has a convenient address, yet I would choose another hotel next time.

The recently remodeled Affina was amazing - from the 6 choice pillow menu to the stocked 'pantry and refrigerator' to the brand name bathroom ammenities. Within walking distance to just about everything you could possibly need, the Affina is a great hotel. The staff was pleasant and seemed to enjoy their jobs. Having never stayed in downtown Chicago before, the Affina over and above exceeded our expectations. Although our trip to Chicago was only for one night, we will consider staying at the Affina again for a future visit.

I had a very pleasant stay at Swissotel and would happily return. The room was spotless, with fresh linens, a tidy bathroom, and no dust or overlooked corners. Everything felt well maintained, and the bed was especially comfortable. I slept deeply both nights, helped by the quiet surroundings and effective blackout curtains. My only complaint is that the stay felt too short; I wish I had booked an extra night to enjoy the facilities and explore more of the area. Breakfast was another highlight, offering a generous selection of fresh fruit, pastries, eggs made to order, cereals, and both local and international options. The dining area was bright, and the staff kept everything replenished without being intrusive. Overall, the service was friendly, efficient, and consistently welcoming.

My stay at the Hilton was disappointing, especially given the price. The room was reasonably clean overall, but the carpet looked tired, there was dust along the desk, and the bathroom grout clearly needed attention. The decor felt dated rather than fresh, with worn furniture and a slightly musty smell that never fully disappeared. Noise was another problem: I could hear doors slamming in the hallway and conversations from neighboring rooms late into the night, making it difficult to sleep. The bed was comfortable enough, and the staff at reception were polite, but those positives did not justify the expensive nightly rate. I expected a more polished and relaxing experience from a Hilton, yet the hotel felt overdue for renovation. It was clean enough to manage, but not worth the money.
The room was spotless, and the modern bathroom had a great shower and plenty of space. Our stay felt far too short, but the attentive service made the price well worth it.

My family has dubbed the Omni in Chicago 'Fawlty Towers' because there always seems to be something wrong. This time our room was right above the kitchen and the odor of cooking grease wafted through our bedroom all night long. It smelled like a greasy spoon restaurant and it permeated all of our clothing. The bedroom window was bolted shut, so we couldn't get any fresh air into the room. With the amount that the Omni is charging for a room, they should have a much better ventilation system.

The view was a drab parking garage, and the hallway noise made sleep impossible until after midnight. The bathroom had a cracked tile and weak water pressure, yet somehow the stay felt far too long for what it offered.

Sitting on the terrace with our morning espresso, watching the sun climb over the water, I almost forgot we had to leave. The rooms are simple but spotless, and the staff treated us like old friends rather than tourists.

I had a very pleasant stay at Hotel Allegro and would happily return. My room overlooked the quieter side of the neighborhood, with a lovely view of the rooftops and a little greenery rather than a busy street. Everything was spotless, from the freshly made bed to the bathroom corners, and the room smelled clean without feeling overly scented. The mattress was comfortable, the curtains blocked out the morning light, and I slept deeply both nights. The staff were consistently warm and professional, greeting me with a smile and quickly helping when I needed directions and an extra towel. Check-in was smooth, and the relaxed atmosphere made the hotel feel welcoming without being noisy or crowded. Overall, it offered comfort, cleanliness, and genuinely thoughtful service at a reasonable price.

I had a very pleasant stay at the Sofitel, although two nights felt far too short to enjoy everything properly. The room was spotless on arrival, with crisp linens, a comfortable bed, and a well-maintained bathroom. I especially appreciated how quiet it was at night despite the hotel's central setting. Breakfast offered a generous selection, including fresh fruit, pastries, eggs made to order, and good coffee; the service was attentive without being intrusive. The location was extremely convenient, with restaurants, shops, and public transport all within an easy walk, which saved us a lot of time. Staff throughout the hotel were welcoming and professional, quickly helping with directions and a late checkout request. I would happily return, preferably for a longer stay next time.

Here are my experiences: - Had three rooms reserved, when checked in we were charged 2 different rates for the rooms - screwed up initial room assignments, gave us a room that was not even cleaned yet when we checked in - Could not get us new keys to a different room without great difficulty (we had to go to the front desk because bell staff went to the wrong room to give us new keys) - In room guide says pool in on the 8th floor and signs say it is on the 7th - could not get to the pool from the 14th floor without going all the way down to the lobby and then had to go to the 7th floor and take the stairs to the 8th - When we checked in we had the front desk staff go over which credit cards were assigned to which room. - When we received our bills, the credit card assignments were still wrong. I stay at 'economy' hotels a lot and I have not even come close to having this many problems with a hotel until this one. This hotel should do Chicago a service and just close its doors. Due to this experience, I will never stay downtown again to deal with overpriced hotels with poor service and surrounding business that are just as bad.

The Hotel Allegro turned out to be a great pick for our long weekend downtown. I'll admit I booked it mostly for the location near the theater district, but the whole experience was a pleasant surprise. The lobby has this old-school, slightly theatrical vibe that's fun without trying too hard, and check-in was quick even with a line forming behind us. Our room wasn't huge, but it was smartly laid out, spotless, and the bed was genuinely comfortable--I slept like a rock. The staff stood out the most; every single person we passed in the hallways or at the front desk offered a smile and a helpful tip. We didn't try the restaurant much beyond a quick breakfast, but what we had was solid. If you're looking for swanky luxury, this isn't it, but for a friendly, clean, and wonderfully central stay, I'd happily return.

We stayed at the Monaco for three nights over a long weekend and it honestly exceeded what I was expecting. The location is fantastic, walkable to tons of restaurants and the waterfront, and the staff went out of their way to make us feel welcome, right down to remembering our names by the second day. Our room was on the smaller side but cleverly laid out, with a super comfortable bed and that quirky, colorful decor the brand does so well. Free wine hour in the evening was a nice touch we took advantage of twice. The only hiccup was a slow elevator situation on Saturday, but honestly with the vibe here I can't complain much. Housekeeping was thorough and quick. Would absolutely come back next time we're in town.

I was expecting much more from the Ambassador, especially given the price and its reputation. Check-in took nearly half an hour, and the front desk seemed distracted rather than welcoming. Our room looked tired, with scuffed furniture, a stained carpet near the window, and a bathroom fan that rattled loudly whenever the light was on. The bed was comfortable enough, but the walls were so thin that we could hear conversations and doors slamming well past midnight. Housekeeping also skipped our room on the second day, even though we had left the sign out and asked about it later. The location is convenient, and one employee did apologize, but those positives didn't make up for the general lack of upkeep. I left feeling the stay was overpriced and disappointing.
Hyatt made a busy overnight easy: quick check-in, a quiet room with a great bed, and friendly staff who pointed me toward a solid late-night dinner nearby.
Great stay overall--room was spotless and the bed incredibly comfortable. Front desk staff went out of their way to help with a late checkout. Solid location too, would happily come back.

Disappointing stay at the Amalfi. Staff seemed bothered whenever we asked for anything, the lobby decor felt straight out of the 90s, and our bathroom had mold around the tub. Honestly, even two nights felt too long.

We stayed at the Omni for three nights over a long weekend, and honestly, it exceeded what I expected for the price. Yes, it's not the cheapest option in the city, but between the location, the service, and the quality of the room, I felt like we got real value. Our room had been recently refurbished, so the decor felt fresh and modern, nothing dated or tired like some photos suggested. The bed was genuinely comfortable, and the housekeeping staff kept everything spotless. Breakfast was a highlight: a hot buffet with made-to-order omelets, fresh fruit, and really good coffee, served in a bright, pleasant dining room. One small gripe: the wifi was spotty in the corner of our room near the window, though it worked fine everywhere else. Would happily return.

I booked this hotel for $75 on Hotwire with mid-level expectations for one night. Totally blown away. Arrived on a Sunday night. Gave car to valet ($51/night). Lobby was a social people watching scene with swank music. Check-in was smooth and easy. I asked for an upgrade and was told no free upgrades to 3rd party bookings. Upgrade to suite was available at a cost. I passed since only 1 night stay. I asked for a nice, quiet room away from noisy housekeeping and ice machine. Received room 10-120. Room was huge with 2 beds. Felt like 400 square feet. Newly renovated last year. Bell hop told me some rooms are very small so I totally lucked out! Service from start to finish was top notch. Everyone had a smile on their face. Always spoke with great respect and made us feel welcome. Ordered room service at 10:45 PM. Arrived in 1/2 hour. food was so-so. Had pancakes in Lockwood for breakfast. Very good food and very good service. Strong coffee. Hotel is right on State Street shopping. FYI - Rooms on floors 15 and below were renovated last year. Rest were done 5 years ago. For the price, it was a great bargain! Only complaint is bathroom is small.

The grand lobby promised luxury, but our room smelled of damp carpet and the AC rattled all night. Breakfast was chaos, and staff seemed annoyed by basic requests. Not the Sofitel standard I remember.

Booked the Palmer expecting old-world charm; got a lesson in disappointment. The so-called city view from our room was mostly a brick wall and a sliver of a neighboring rooftop, with the actual skyline teased just out of frame. Breakfast was a sad affair--cold scrambled eggs, stale pastries, and coffee that tasted burnt and bitter. At over $300 a night, I felt completely fleeced; the worn carpets and chipped bathroom tiles only added insult. Sleep was the worst part: the mattress sagged in the middle, and the street noise filtered through the thin windows all night. I woke up more tired than when I arrived. Unless you enjoy overpaying for a mediocre stay, look elsewhere. This place has traded its former reputation for penny-pinching and neglect.
Expected so much more from an InterContinental. Room was dusty, AC barely worked, and staff took hours to fix it. Overpriced for this level of service--won't be returning.

Stayed here for a weekend getaway and was pleasantly surprised by the spacious room and comfy bed. The rooftop bar has killer views, and the staff were genuinely friendly. Would definitely book again.

We have stayed at several high end places in Chicago and this is still our favorite. Location is superb, staff are particularly gracious and welcoming without being cloying. Cornell, at the front desk, is unfailingly helpful as is the concierge. We love the extra room that a suite provides and if you join the frequent guest program, high speed internet is gratis, as is a breakfast beverage delivered along with the newspaper each morning at the time of your choosing. Bedding is of excellent quality and they offer truly amazing blackout curtains! We have never had a bad stay at this hotel.

Booked a 'renovated' room and honestly, it felt like a coat of paint on a very tired building. The AC unit sounded like a lawnmower with a sinus infection, and the bed was so lumpy that I woke up more tired than when I checked in. Housekeeping did show up, but only after I called twice on the second day, and they seemed to have missed the 'do not disturb' sign hanging on my door. The bar downstairs was understaffed, so I waited 20 minutes for a lukewarm cocktail that cost $18. The elevator--one of three working--had a distinct post-jogger aroma. Look, the staff at the front desk were polite enough, but that's about the only positive. For this price, you're paying for the name and the location, not for comfort. I've stayed in roadside motels with better towels and quieter plumbing. Disappointed is an understatement. Wouldn't come back.
Breakfast was lukewarm and limited, and the dated decor made the hotel feel tired. My room was clean enough, but street noise and a lumpy mattress made sleeping difficult.

My stay at the Sheraton was more frustrating than relaxing. The room looked tired, with scuffed furniture, thin towels, and a view of the parking structure that hardly justified the rate. Wi-Fi was unreliable throughout the visit; it kept dropping during a work call, and the paid high-speed option was no better. The front desk staff were polite enough, but check-in felt rushed and nobody offered much help when I reported the internet problem. Even the elevators were painfully slow during peak hours. I had booked two nights, yet the stay felt strangely long because there was little comfort to enjoy after a busy day. For the price, I expected a cleaner, better-maintained room and more attentive service. I would only consider returning if the rates dropped substantially.

I was a bit wary booking the Sheraton, given its size, but my stay exceeded expectations. The room was surprisingly quiet, with solid soundproofing that let me sleep in despite a full house. The Wi-Fi was fast and stable for both streaming and video calls, which I really appreciated. Decor-wise, it's not cutting-edge, but the classic, warm tones and updated bedding kept it feeling fresh rather than dated. Breakfast was a highlight: a generous buffet with made-to-order omelets, fresh pastries, and decent coffee--definitely above the usual hotel standard. Staff were efficient, and the location made exploring easy. It's not a boutique experience, but for comfort and reliability, I'd happily return.

Homewood felt worth the price for the spacious room and friendly service. The bathroom was spotless with good water pressure, Wi‐Fi worked reliably, and breakfast had plenty of fresh, filling options.

The decor felt refreshingly modern, and the location put us steps from everything we wanted. The bathroom was spotless with great water pressure; our only regret was that our stay felt far too short to enjoy it all.

The 'luxury' felt like a facade--our room smelled musty, the AC rattled all night, and housekeeping never replaced towels. Staff were polite but useless when we asked for a late checkout. For this price, utter disappointment.

The front desk team at Affinia was wonderfully warm and efficient, making check-in a breeze. Our room felt refreshingly modern, not dated, and breakfast offered a solid variety of fresh pastries and hot options.

I booked the James expecting a trendy, upscale stay, but left feeling thoroughly let down. The breakfast buffet was a sad affair--scrambled eggs that were watery and cold, stale pastries, and coffee that tasted burnt, all for an exorbitant supplemental charge. The bathroom was my biggest frustration: the showerhead dribbled with uneven pressure, and the drain clogged halfway through my second morning, leaving a puddle on the tile that housekeeping never fully addressed. My room's window faced a brick wall, so the 'city view' was nonexistent unless I leaned out awkwardly to glimpse a sliver of the next building. Given the nightly rate, this felt like a rip-off. The lobby is stylish, sure, but that doesn't compensate for the worn mattress springs and the constant hallway noise from neighboring guests. I'd rather have paid half the price for a functional chain hotel. Disappointing, overpriced, and not worth the hype.
The Affinia staff were warm and quick to help, while the decor felt fresh rather than dated. Breakfast had plenty of choices, and our room stayed pleasantly quiet despite the central location.

The bathroom was spotless with excellent water pressure, and the bed was so comfortable I slept straight through till morning. Staff were attentive yet never intrusive, and the room itself was immaculate throughout.

My initial thought of the hotel was, this place is just ok, I didnt look up any reviews as I was staying there with 2 other friends. I was truly impressed from ceiling to floor with the room. Views were good, its just the surrounding buildings unless your towards the front where the river is located. I'm crazy about huge bathrooms and this one is HUGE. I love all the space they have. Flat tv, traditional seating and I admired the fabric-based headboards. Those are very nice! Walking distance to restaurants were convenient. I'm a highly frequent traveler to Chicago almost 20 years now and always stay with relatives. In any event, I'd recommend staying at the Monaco again!

Stayed at Hotel Allegro for a quick getaway and was genuinely impressed--the vibe is stylish without being stuffy, and the front desk folks were incredibly warm. The room was comfy and quiet, and the location made it easy to walk everywhere. Would absolutely book again.

I decided to book at the Amalfi after cancelling a reservation for a different hotel after reading their reviews on TA. I was blown away by the reviews for the Amalfi on TA and decided to check it out. I was able to secure a great price on the hotel room and I was not disappointed. I asked to be put in a quiet room because I was having an interview the next day. The room was very quiet and in a great location, but my only complaint was that it was right next to the fitness center and I could hear people running on the treadmill during the day. However, it quieted down at night and I could not hear anything. The rooms were enormous for Chicago and I was pleased!!! The hotel provided free breakfast which was good, free internet, and free gym access. The hotel is only a few blocks from the Magnificient Mile and I walked there everyday to do shopping. I have to say that the doorman is truly a gem and is very friendly. I wish that their front desk staff were as friendly as he was. All in all, I plan to stay at the Amalfi anytime I visit Chicago in the future.
Really pleasant stay at the Hotel Allegro -- comfy bed, quiet room despite being downtown, and the breakfast spread was better than expected. Staff were genuinely friendly. Would happily come back.

We had a great experience at this hotel. The hotel is Huge! The rooms were very clean, well appointed, and our room was very roomy with a great view of the snow covered park. The Staff was so nice and very helpfull. Donald, at the the Concierge desk scored us tickets to WICKED the day of the performance, and on a Holiday weekend too. They were great seats and a reasonable price. He worked very hard for us to see that show. They truely topped off what was a Fun New Years Celebration. This will be my first pick when I return in the spring.

Despite its unbeatable location, my stay felt far too brief and overpriced for what was offered; the staff seemed indifferent and overwhelmed, making an already disappointing experience feel longer than it was.
Expected much more from InterContinental: the room smelled musty, check-in took forever, and the air conditioning barely worked all night.

We loved our stay at the Talbott--the staff remembered our names and the room was spotless. That chic lobby bar with the late-night jazz was the perfect wind-down after exploring. Can't wait to return!

I really wanted to like this place, but the whole stay felt off from the moment we arrived. We booked a suite specifically for the separate bedroom and were given a room that smelled strongly of damp carpet and old cigarette smoke, despite the '100% non-smoking' sign on the door. The front desk clerk barely looked up when we asked to switch, and said nothing was available even though I saw open rooms on their booking site later that night. The air conditioning unit rattled all night, and the hallway was so noisy we could hear every door slam until 2 a.m. The breakfast was lukewarm and the scrambled eggs were basically watery mush. On the positive side, the beds were comfortable and housekeeping did a decent job, but that doesn't make up for the lack of care or the feeling that nobody actually paid attention to the details. For the price, I'd honestly find somewhere else next time.

I wanted to like the Talbott, especially given its location and the nightly rate, but the stay was more disappointing than relaxing. My room looked tired, with scuffed furniture and thin walls that let hallway conversations and doors closing carry straight through. I slept poorly both nights; the bed was comfortable enough, but the noise and an overly warm room made it difficult to stay asleep. The front-desk staff were polite, though not especially welcoming, and my request for extra towels took nearly an hour. For what I paid, I expected better maintenance and more attentive service. Two nights felt longer than they should have because of the restless sleep, yet I still left feeling I had not received reasonable value. The location is convenient, but it does not make up for the shortcomings.

I was in Chicago for a convention and stayed at the Sheraton towers. I had a negative experience because I got about one dozen very painful bites by bed bugs on my torso. It made attending the conference uncomfortable. The staff changed the sheets but could not move me to another room, as the conference had booked the whole hotel. After the sheets were changed, I got no more bites, thankfully. Despite this, I managed to enjoy the stay. I liked the location next to the river, and the fact that it was easy to walk to Magnificent Mile.

We stayed at the Hotel Palmer for three nights and honestly couldn't have asked for a better stay. The front desk staff went out of their way on arrival, offering us a room on a higher floor after I mentioned being a light sleeper, and it made a real difference. The bed was genuinely comfortable, and the shower had strong water pressure, which matters more to me than most hotel luxuries. Breakfast was simple but fresh--good coffee, pastries, and eggs that weren't sitting under a heat lamp forever. Location was a huge plus, walkable to the metro and a bunch of restaurants within a few blocks. Only tiny gripe: hallways could get a bit noisy around 10pm, but nothing earplugs wouldn't fix. Would happily book again next trip.

The Hotel Talbott felt like a hidden gem--the staff remembered my name by day two, and that cozy library nook was perfect for morning coffee. Room was quiet, bed incredibly plush, and the location made exploring the city effortlessly easy. I'd happily return.
The room looked worn and the shower barely warmed up. For the price, I expected better service too; calls to the front desk went unanswered twice.
The room's balcony view of the sea was spectacular, and the staff went out of their way to make our anniversary special. Breakfast was fresh and plentiful. Just wish we could have stayed longer.

I was looking for a fun, contemporary hotel and it didn't deliver. The lobby was nice, and the rooms were mostly clean, but it really wasn't special. Service time was slow for room requests, I found empty water bottles under the chair, and the a

My stay at Hotel Allegro was disappointing, especially considering the price. The room looked tired, with scuffed furniture and a view directly onto a service alley and overflowing bins rather than anything pleasant. Breakfast was another letdown: the selection was limited, the pastries seemed stale, and the coffee from the machine was barely drinkable. I also slept poorly. The mattress was too firm, and noise from the hallway continued late into the night, followed by delivery trucks and staff activity early in the morning. The windows did little to block the street sounds. Staff were polite enough, but they seemed rushed and offered no useful solution when I mentioned the noise. The location may be convenient, but the room quality and lack of rest made this stay poor value.

My stay at the Sofitel was much more disappointing than expected for a hotel at this price. The room looked tidy at first glance, but closer inspection found dust along the skirting boards and a few marks on the bathroom grout. The bed was comfortable enough, yet I slept poorly because the walls seemed paper-thin; conversations in the corridor, doors slamming, and traffic noise carried on well past midnight. The decor also feels tired rather than elegant, with scuffed furniture, faded carpet, and lighting that made the room seem gloomy. Staff were polite, but the service was slow when I reported the noise and requested extra towels. The location may be convenient, but the overall experience did not feel luxurious or worth the expense.
Our room overlooked lively city streets, and the updated decor felt bright rather than dated. Staff were warm and quick to help, while the central location made exploring wonderfully easy.

Booked the Allegro for a weekend getaway and left pretty let down. The lobby looks great in photos but the room was worn out, the AC rattled all night, and the front desk barely acknowledged us. Not worth the price, honestly. Won't be back.

Was one of the worst travel experiences of quite some time.... 1. Arrived to construction or renovation to main lobby... no warning. not on the website... 'thanks for letting me make the choice to stay in hotel with construction site' 2. Lengthy line to wait at makeshift reception area (25 min wait).. check in..ACHE conference-- be prepared for the influx of people for the convention. 3. Double book room.... go back to check in... told to get back in line... and we will review when it is your turn... told them I just waited 25 mins.. Curt service worker said wait your turn. 4. Second room... dirty dishes from room service in front of door at our check in at 3PM. 5. Internet kept dropping and slower than dial up network.... 6. Second day and Third day stay... No hot Water to start the day off with cold shower.... 7. Check out... overcharge on bogus fees.... Travel to Chicago stay at the Palmer House or Fairmont.

beautiful place with European charm. No complaints, great location, (never like parking in Chicago, though). It was $35 a night next door. Large beautiful lobby, a touch of class. Fantastic location for downtown, Navy Pier, and the great Grant Park(Millenium Park, too)...Loved it.

We just returned from a weekend at the Palmer House. We normally stay north on the Mag Mile but wanted to be closer to Soldier's Stadium and the Art Insitiute this time. We were able to upgrade to a suite upon arrival at half the price that we paid for a regular room at the Four Seasons two weeks earlier. What a suite!! It was huge. The basic living room, dining room and kitchen/wet bar area was one large room. Up to three additional bedrooms can be added by the use of connecting doors. All rooms were spotlessly clean. They even smelled good. Lovely soaps, robes, etc. Lots of large closets. The bathrooms were older but well maintained. Much better than the ones at the Four Seasons. The furniture was nice but worn in some spots. The beds and linens were excellent. Room service was fast. The food and service were great. The pool and workout areas were clean and well maintained. We had one small problem with a burned out lightbulb in one of the lamps. Maintaince arrived quickly with a new bulb. They wouldn't allow me to tip them!! Check-in was somewhat slow as the hotel has been sold out for several weeks. This is a very large hotel, so they have to move a lot of people and rooms. Also, the hotel does not have views as it is configured like an 'E'. All in all, the Palmer House is a good value for the money.
The Palmer's location was convenient, but the room felt tired and the walls were paper-thin. Housekeeping missed basics, and the price didn't come close to matching the experience.

I stayed at the Allegro for several days in August 2004 and I would defintely stay again. I had a very large room with a huge bathroom, although the property is a converted theater so the rooms may vary in size and layout. The lobby is comfortable with big sofas and chaise lounges, a nice place to enjoy the simple (2 choices, no munchies) but pleasant wine reception. At night, there is not much going on in the immediate vicinity, other than theater traffic, but it's a short cab ride to Michigan Avenue shopping and River North restaurants.

Loved our stay at Hotel Monaco. The location made walking everywhere easy, and our room had a lovely view of the river. Breakfast was fresh and generous, and every staff member we met was warm and genuinely accommodating. Would happily return!

Stayed three nights for a conference and left genuinely puzzled by the hype. The lobby is slick, sure, but that's where the polish ends. Our room faced the inner courtyard, which meant zero natural light and a constant hum from the HVAC that never let up. The bed was comfortable enough, but the pillows were flat and lumpy. Housekeeping skipped our turndown twice without notice, and when I called for extra towels, they arrived after a 40-minute wait. The bar downstairs is overpriced--$19 for a small gin and tonic that was mostly ice. Also, the gym has two treadmills, one of which was broken the whole stay. For what they charge per night, I expected far more attention to detail. It's not terrible, just a mid-tier experience with a boutique price tag. I'd book elsewhere next time.

I read the reviews on Trip Advisor for this property which had it ranked as #1 in Chicago. I got a king room overlooking Michigan Ave. The view was beautiful. The room was also impeccable. Nice and bright, very fresh and modern. I find it very hard to fault any Sofitel's. The service, attentiveness of staff, cleanliness and luxury are always top notch. Location was great, head left from the lobby and you reach a bunch of european style cafe's and restaurants. Straight ahead of the hotel on Michigan Ave is a shoppers paradise. A great place to stay, and much better value than Park Hyatt. I do find some of the charges in luxury hotels to be a bit crazy, such as for the internet. When you are paying top dollar, a few inclusions would be nice.

I was disappointed by my stay at the Omni. The room looked worn rather than upscale, with scuffed furniture and a faint musty smell that never quite disappeared. The bathroom was clean enough, but cramped, with poor lighting, chipped grout, and water pressure that dropped whenever someone else in the building showered. My window faced a rooftop crowded with vents and machinery, so there was no pleasant city view, just constant humming and an unattractive wall. The Wi-Fi was especially frustrating: it connected briefly, then slowed to a crawl or disconnected whenever I tried to work. I only booked two nights, and although I was ready to leave, the stay still felt longer than it should have because of these small problems. For the price, I expected a much more comfortable and polished experience.

For a Hilton hotel I was very unimpressed, the rooms are incredibly small, there are no refrigirator or coffee machine for coffee or tea. Wifi costs an arm. Plus side there is a Starbucks at the bottom, but only limited opening hours, the lobby is very nice. Location is decent.

The chandeliers looked tired, and the carpet in our hallway felt thirty years old. I barely slept with the street noise, and at $600 a night, it was impossible to justify--though hopping to the waterfront for dinner was undeniably easy.

I'm genuinely puzzled by the high ratings for this Intercontinental. The lobby's grand chandeliers can't hide the fact that the carpet in my hallway was stained and frayed, and the furniture in the room felt like a time capsule from the early 2000s--scratched wood, a remote that barely worked, and a bed that sagged in the middle. My bathroom was the lowlight: the 'rain' showerhead sputtered unevenly, and the grout was discolored with mildew in the corners. The staff weren't rude, but they were distractingly indifferent--I had to ask twice for extra towels, and the front desk barely looked up when I checked in. For nearly $400 a night, this felt like a mid-tier business hotel, not a luxury flagship. I left disappointed and won't return. There are far better options nearby for far less.

Sometimes you just can't find fault with a hotel, even if you tried. Such was the case with Sofitel, where we'd never stayed before. It's a sleek, modern, sophisticated hotel with European touches. We spent three days there on a leisure weekend, we had a 29th floor king room looking directly at the Hancock Building, at a total cost including taxes and lugs of about $165 a night. The room was average sized, well-appointed, everything in it worked, and it had a fabulous view of the Chicago high-rise jungle, including snippets of the lake. The public areas were wonderfully decorated. The restaurant served a good breakfast at, for Chicago, reasonable prices. The staff was excellent. My wife broke her ankle several weeks before we visited and was on crutches. The staff loaned us a wheelchair and was very helpful in assisting her.

I really wanted to like this Hilton, especially given the brand name, but the experience fell flat from the moment I walked in. Check-in took nearly twenty minutes because there was only one person at the desk, and she seemed completely overwhelmed by a line of guests. The room itself was worn down--carpet had stains, the AC rattled all night, and the bathroom had a lingering musty smell despite the towels being fresh. I got no sleep and barely any hot water in the morning shower. The WiFi kept dropping, and when I called the front desk about it, I was put on hold for ages. The only bright spot was the location, but honestly, for the price I paid, I expected far better maintenance and service. Disappointed is putting it mildly.

I would NOT recommend staying at the Swissotel in Chicago. I was travelling with a friend and we arrived at different times. She had booked the hotel but had added my name to the reservation since I would be arriving first. The 'night manager' at the hotel was extremely rude and told me I could not check in since they could not find the note about my name being on the reservation. (this was THEIR mistake) They told me I could sit in the lobby for 4 hours until my friend arrived. They did nothing to try and help me until I stood there and complained for twenty minutes. I can't believe that a 'manager' would treat a customer this way. There are other great hotels in Chicago. This hotel is not worth the aggravation!

I really wanted to like Hotel Monaco, given the hype, but our stay was a letdown from start to finish. The check-in process was painfully slow, with only one person at the desk despite a long line. When we finally got our room, the AC was on the fritz and the room smelled musty, like old carpet. The bed was hard as a rock, and the pillows were flat lumps. The bathroom had a lingering odor of mildew, and the water pressure in the shower was a pathetic trickle. To make matters worse, the 'complimentary' Wi-Fi kept disconnecting, so I couldn't even stream a movie. For the price we paid, I expected a lot more. The location is decent, right in the heart of things, but that's about the only positive I can dredge up. I won't be coming back. Save your money and book elsewhere.
Really enjoyed my stay at The Knickerbocker--the room was comfortable and quiet, the staff genuinely welcoming, and the rooftop bar made an easygoing evening after exploring the city.

My only regret is not booking another night--the Palmer was that good. Despite being downtown, the room was blissfully quiet, and I slept like a log. Everything sparkled, from the crisp linens to the pristine bathroom.
