Our stay at Sofitel was genuinely lovely from check-in onward. The lobby felt elegant without being stiff, and the receptionist welcomed us warmly after a long flight. Our room was spotless, quiet, and had a wonderfully comfortable bed with crisp linens; the city view at night was a bonus. Breakfast offered plenty of fresh options, especially the pastries and made-to-order eggs. We also appreciated how attentive the concierge was when arranging a restaurant reservation at short notice. The pool area got busy in the afternoon, but there were still enough loungers and staff came by regularly with towels. It is not the cheapest option, but the service, location, and little touches made it feel worthwhile.

The Talbott felt like a hidden gem--our room was spotless, the Wi-Fi never lagged, and being steps from the river made exploring effortless. For the thoughtful touches and prime spot, the price honestly felt like a steal.

We recently celebrated our 20th anniversary in Chicago and stayed at the Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers. Having looked at a gizillion places I chose this one because of its location to Navy Pier. (We were going on a dinner cruise-The Odyssey at Navy Pier) The hotel is a short walk...unless you are wearing heels:) to Navy Pier. We found out on the way home only a $5 cab ride:) worth $20 to your blisters!! Its also only a short walk to Michigan Ave shopping...for comfortable shoes perhaps?? I chose this hotel because of location, but the views are also terrific. This time we had a lake view of Navy Pier, but our previous trip we had a river and lake view. both very nice. The hotel is very nice. Several restaurants, although we haven't tried them. The burger place downstairs sure smelled good though:) We ended up at Bubba Gumps at Navy Pier. GOOD! The rooms were very spacious and CLEAN!! I am kind of a germaphobe! so clean is important for my sanity:) The bottom level has doors that leads right out to the riverwalk, and a cool water fountain. :) I obviously highly recommend this hotel:) I <3 CHICAGO

Just returned from 2 nights at the Ambassador and I have to say that I am very happy that I chose this hotel. It is true that this is an older hotel. But it is well kept and it does not lack in style and grandeur. (think of the hotel from the Shining, minus the elevator of blood and creepy twins.) From the check-in desk to the surprise turn down service from the maids, I was made to feel like royalty. A special acknowledgment goes out to the doormen who helped me with all my tourist questions. Also the location of the hotel is great. Close to all the action, but on a quite residential street with beautiful old mansions. I also got a sweet $89 per night room by booking on travelzoo. That was just an added bonus however. Even if I paid $200 per night, my impression of the Ambassador would not change. Highly, highly recommended.
Despite the prime downtown location, the Hilton felt like a letdown. Staff were curt at check-in, the bathroom had a stubborn clog, and our room's view was mostly a brick wall and a busy rooftop.

I really wanted to love this place, given the history and the location right on Michigan Avenue, but our stay was a letdown from start to finish. The lobby is stunning, I'll give them that, but the charm stops at the elevator doors. Our room was shockingly small for the price, with a view of a brick wall and an air conditioning unit that rattled all night. Housekeeping knocked at 8:30 AM on our first morning, and when I asked for more coffee pods, they just never showed up. The 'vintage' vibe quickly felt dated, with worn carpet and a bathroom that desperately needed a regrout. Check-in took over 20 minutes because they somehow lost our reservation, even though I had the confirmation email. The one saving grace was the bar downstairs, but honestly, the whole experience felt like a cash grab on the name. For what we paid, we could have had a much fresher, less stressful stay a few blocks away. I won't be back.
The Knickerbocker was a comfortable base for exploring Midtown, with a quiet, well-kept room and genuinely friendly staff. The rooftop views at sunset were a lovely bonus, too.

I was a bit nervous booking Hotel Allegro, given the mixed-age reviews, but it genuinely exceeded expectations. The location is unbeatable for exploring the Loop, and honestly, the price felt fair for what you get--the room was spotless, with a surprisingly plush bed and a quiet corner that made me forget I was in the middle of a city. The wifi was flawless; I streamed videos and joined a work call without a single drop. My window faced west, and catching the sunset over the rooftops was a lovely, unplanned perk. Breakfast was the highlight each morning: a solid spread of fresh pastries, made-to-order eggs, and proper coffee, served with no rush. The staff even remembered my room number by day two. Minor wear in the hallway carpet, but nothing that mattered. I'd happily rebook next time I'm in town.

Stayed at the Conrad for a long weekend and honestly, it exceeded expectations. The location is perfect for exploring, but the real standout was the service--front desk remembered our names and the concierge booked us a last-minute river cruise without any fuss. Room was quiet, bed was genuinely comfortable, and I appreciated the Nespresso machine and the little touches like complimentary shoe shine service. Breakfast was solid, though a bit pricey; the omelet station made up for it. Only minor gripe was the gym being slightly warm in the morning, but equipment was top-notch. Valet was quick both times. Would happily return for a business trip or another getaway--it's that rare hotel that feels polished without feeling stuffy.

Hard Rock was a fun, comfortable base: breakfast offered plenty of choice, the bathroom was spotless with strong water pressure, and the central location was ideal. I only wish our stay had been longer.

The king room we booked looked nothing like the photos. The carpet had a suspicious sticky patch near the minibar, and the 'city view' was mostly a brick wall and a sliver of the next building. I get that hotels age, but this felt neglected. Housekeeping was inconsistent--one day we got fresh towels, the next we had to call twice for toilet paper. The AC unit rattled all night like a trapped wasp, and the blackout curtains didn't fully close, so the hallway light bled in. The lobby bar was overpriced, and the bartender seemed annoyed we asked for a wine list that didn't exist. Honestly, the only bright spot was the location--walkable to a few decent spots. But for what we paid, I'd expect basic upkeep and a proper night's sleep. Won't be back, and I wouldn't recommend it unless you're desperate.
Disappointing stay at the Omni--our room looked worn, the air-conditioning barely cooled, and housekeeping skipped us until late afternoon. For the price, I expected far better upkeep and service.

Was slated for two nights in Chicago, June 12 - 14, 2007. I could onyl get the Intercon for both nights. I booked a handicapped room since that was they had left. After reading other reviews of the property, I decided to move it from two nights to one, and stay the second night at the Hotel Monaco. Of course, upon check-in, I was given a suite. Nice room, great linens, clean bathroom, and very quiet. Parking is really high ($48). I understand some peopel saying the rooms need to be updated, but everything was clean and worked well. At ,ost, the rooms were a bit dark. I had a late night drink at the bar, which was reasonably priced. i did not eat there, but the menu seemed pretty good, albeit with the typical hotel mark-ups to be expected. In all, I thought the place was everything I needed, and was very happy with the room, the staff, the linens, and the housekeeping. Much better than others have indicated.

I stayed at Hotel James for three nights and honestly slept better than I do at home. The bed was plush without being too soft, and despite being right in the city center, my room on the fifth floor facing the courtyard was remarkably quiet -- no street noise, no hallway commotion, even on a Friday night. Breakfast exceeded my expectations: fresh pastries, proper coffee, eggs cooked to order, and enough variety that I never got bored. Location-wise, it's hard to beat, just a five-minute walk to the main square with restaurants and the tram stop practically at the doorstep. Staff were warm and helpful with directions whenever I asked. Small imperfections like a slow bathroom drain aside, I'd happily return and recommend it to anyone visiting.

I had a very comfortable stay at the Sheraton and would happily return. The lobby was busy when I arrived, but the front desk team kept things moving and even pointed me toward a quieter elevator bank. My room was clean, well laid out, and had a surprisingly comfortable bed; I slept better than I usually do in hotels. The workspace was useful for catching up on emails, and the shower had great water pressure. Breakfast downstairs was fresh and had enough variety for a couple of mornings without getting boring. I also appreciated that housekeeping was attentive without knocking at inconvenient times. The location made it easy to get around, whether I was heading to meetings or looking for dinner nearby. It is a polished, dependable hotel with genuinely friendly service.

We stayed at the Swissotel for a long weekend and left genuinely impressed. Breakfast was a standout--the made-to-order omelet station was a nice touch, and the fresh pastries and proper cappuccino made a great start to the day. The lobby and our room felt modern and clean, not at all dated, with sleek wood accents and soft, warm lighting that made it cozy. I slept like a log on the firm-but-comfortable bed, and the blackout curtains were a lifesaver for sleeping in. The wifi was surprisingly solid; I streamed a movie without a single buffer, which is rare for a hotel. The location was perfect for exploring, and the staff were friendly without being overbearing. Only minor gripe: the bathroom could use a bit more counter space. Otherwise, we'd absolutely book again.

The Hard Rock delivered solid value for the money--the location put us steps from the Strip action, and breakfast was surprisingly hearty. The decor leans a bit flashy but feels current, not tired. I'd happily return.

We picked Homewood because we needed a kitchen for a week-long stay, and honestly, it exceeded what we expected. The suite was genuinely spacious--our two kids had their own sleeping nook, and the full-size fridge meant we actually cooked dinner three nights instead of eating out. Breakfast had real variety, not just the sad scrambled eggs you see at some places; the oatmeal bar and make-your-own waffles were a hit. The pool was warm and clean, though it's on the smaller side, so we went at off-hours. Staff at the front desk remembered our room number by day two, which felt personal. Only minor gripe: the hallway ice machine was on our floor but out of order, and they directed us to the next floor. Not a big deal. For the price, especially with the included evening social on weekdays, this is a solid, comfortable pick for families or anyone wanting more than a basic hotel room. We've already booked our next stay.

I stayed at the Fairmont for a few nights and found the whole experience excellent. I was given a very large room with great views of the city; the breakfast was extremely good; and the location was as central as I could have wished for. The pool was not large but felt luxurious and was great for early morning swims. In the evening I spent some time in the hotel bar with friends and that was excellent too. Highly recommended as a base for exploring Chicago.
The Fairmont exceeded expectations. From the stunning lobby to the impeccably clean room with a killer view, every detail felt thoughtful. Staff were genuinely warm, and the service was flawless.
Hotel Allegro made for an easy weekend downtown--the room was comfortable, staff genuinely friendly, and the lobby had a fun old-school Chicago feel. I'd happily return.

I stayed at the hotel during the Dave Matthews Caravan tour and would come home each night rather dusty/dirty from being at an outdoor concert with 200,000 of my closest friends. I used half a bottle of shampoo the first night. The second night, the staff had not refreshed my bar soap or shampoo. I informed the front desk who made apologies and said they would take care of it immediately. I got home that night with a tiny tiny bar of soap (hand soap) for the bath/shower and they had replaced the shampoo in its original place, nicely displayed, but with the EXACT SAME bottle of shampoo that was now 1/8 full. Yeah!! The hotel is in a great location to Navy Pier and Michigan Ave....I'll grant them that....but that's where their 'pros' end. I'd rather stay at a Hampton Inn. I would not recommend this hotel to anyone.

Checked in at 4pm and was told our room wouldn't be ready until 5:30. The front desk agent shrugged and said 'we're running behind' without any offer to store bags or give a drink voucher. When we finally got the keys, the room smelled like stale cigarette smoke, even though it was a non-smoking floor. The air conditioning rattled loudly all night, and the bathroom had a cracked tile and a hair in the sink drain. Housekeeping never came the next morning despite the do-not-disturb sign being off. I called twice and was put on hold for ten minutes. The location is convenient, but the hallway carpets are worn, the elevator is painfully slow, and the mini-bar was stocked with expired snacks. For the price, I expected far better. Not worth it.

The room's worn furniture and flickering bathroom light set the tone. Staff seemed overwhelmed, and the AC rattled all night. Honestly expected far more polish from a Sheraton--left frustrated and disappointed.
Disappointing stay at Hotel Palmer: Wi-Fi barely worked, the room overlooked a grimy alley, hallway noise carried all night, and the bathroom clearly needed a deeper clean.

Spent three nights at the hotel for a girls weekend. The staff was wonderful, room was beautiful and location great. You can take the train directly from Midway and walk one block to the hotel. Very close to museums and restaurants. I have stayed here before and it always proves to be a great choice for a trip to Chicago.

My parents booked five nights at The James for its location and good reviews. They had a terrible first night with defective air conditioning and not much sympathy from the management staff. They sent engineers three times to repair the unit, and they insisted that it was getting cooler when it wasn't, under the rationale that the summer temperature is high and the filter was dirty. At my parents' request, the hotel staff moved them to a lower floor with a queen instead of a king and with neither a rate discount nor an effort to compensate them for the inconvenience and discomfort. The hotel insisted they were fully booked and reluctantly gave them that room. Don't book this hotel in the summer. And by the way, there is no view at all from any of the rooms - except for the windows of other buildings.

Hotel Amalfi was a lovely base for our weekend in Rome. The building has plenty of character, but the room felt fresh, spotless, and surprisingly quiet once the windows were closed. We had a small balcony overlooking the street, which was perfect for a coffee before heading out each morning. Breakfast was simple but well stocked, with good pastries, fruit, eggs, and staff who kept everything moving without hovering. The front desk team was especially kind when our train arrived late; they checked us in quickly and marked a few nearby trattorias on a map. The location made it easy to walk to the Colosseum and Monti, while the metro was close enough for longer trips. Our only minor note is that the elevator is tiny, but that is part of staying in an older central building. We would happily return.

On our visit to Chicago, we chose the Hyatt due to its location in downtown, within walking distance to most major attractions, such as Sears Tower, Magnificent Mile, Grant/Millenium Parks, etc. Subway & bus stops very close by to travel to other locations in the city . Overall the hotel was very nice, clean, and at a great location. Was in a safe area. Went to beautiful Wrigley Field and Soldier Field and saw both teams play. I love Chicago and would defenitely stay here again!
Disappointing stay at Homewood: the bed was uncomfortable, the bathroom felt cramped and dated, and the Wi-Fi kept dropping. I was glad the short visit ended quickly.

The bathroom was spotless with great water pressure, and the room itself felt freshly cleaned. Location made exploring effortless, and the Wi-Fi never dropped once during my stay. Overall, a comfortable and dependable choice.

The decor felt refreshingly modern without being sterile, and the spotless bathroom had excellent water pressure. Steps from the metro, the staff were genuinely warm--offering a free upgrade and great local tips that made my trip effortless.

We had a wonderful long weekend at the Sofitel. The check-in was incredibly smooth, and we were greeted with a lovely welcome drink which set a warm tone. Our room was spacious and impeccably clean, with the classic French elegance you'd expect, but the bed was the real highlight - I slept like a log every night. The staff throughout the hotel were attentive without being intrusive; the concierge arranged a fantastic last-minute dinner reservation for us. Breakfast offered a great mix of pastries and hot dishes, and the coffee was top-notch. The only hiccup was a slightly slow elevator during a busy morning, but it was a minor issue. Location is perfect for exploring, yet the hotel feels like a peaceful sanctuary. We left feeling genuinely rested and would absolutely return.

My wife and I brought our daughter downtown for a blowout 'American Girl' Weekend and chose the Monaco because of it's glowing reviews. We arrived late and maybe that's when they put out their second-stringers, but we felt unwelcome by the desk staff--like we were an intrusion. I'll never understand this--they're in the hospitality business and they're inhospitable! (This is getting picky, but the reception desk which is cleverly designed to look like a vintage Louis Vuitton trunk needs some maintenance. The repeated 'HM' initials are peeling off--looks like they used rub-downs where they should have silk screened for durability). When we got to our room we found the maid's ratty work shoes at the foot of the bed (yuck!). I'm still trying to figure out that scenario. There were no ashes--so I've ruled out spontaneous combustion. Also, to the disappointment of my daughter, the much-advertised goldfish was MIA. The bellhop (who apologized for the shoes) explained that they take away the fish when they turn down the bed '...is that OK?' he said. I think the proper response at a hotel like this would have been to bring up a stinking 35C/ fish to make a tired 5-year-old happy. On the up side, the rooms are nice and have an over-the-top decoration that my daughter loved ('I'd like to live here!' she said). The bed is VERY comfortable--my wife wants the same brand now. The bathroom is nicely appointed with quality materials and good strong shower--except for the cheap fall-apart-while-you're-using-it toilet paper. Come on Kimpton! How much can a decent roll cost? The view towards the river is great (try to get one) and my daughter loved the upholstered wide ledge by the window--she closed the curtains and was in her own 'club house' watching the world go by from from high above the city. In short: very nice hotel--desk staff at night could be nicer (wouldn't cost anything and would have made up for the maid's shoes!)

Checked in to a dark, cramped room that smelled like old carpet, and the A/C rattled nonstop. Staff was polite but shrugged off every request. For the price, this felt more like a motel than a boutique hotel.
Disappointing stay at Hotel Allegro: the room was only passably clean, the bathroom felt dated and cramped, and the supposedly convenient location came with a dull view of traffic.

I stayed at the Fairmont during a professional conference. While I have to say that for a conference, some of the meeting rooms were too small, in terms of traveler's comfort the hotel is exceptional! I can't think of a single thing about my room that wasn't perfect. The accommodations were luxurious and the hotel is conveniently situated within walking distance of many Chicago attractions.

Booked the Hyatt for a weekend getaway and left pretty deflated. The room was tired, with scuffed furniture and a bathroom that smelled musty. Staff seemed overwhelmed at check-in, and the breakfast buffet was cold and overpriced--definitely not worth the hype.

When you're standing in a craptastic excuse for a shower buttnaked and cold with soap in your hair because the water from the shower head has gone from a weak spray to a dribble to nothing coming out at all, nothing in the world will ever convince you to stay here again. The worst part is that the hotel knows this is a problem (they told me that it happens to the upper floors, and I wasn't even staying on the highest floor!) as if that makes it ok. I can look past the 'rustic' decor of the room and take it for what it is - an inexpensive place to crash, but c'mon, a girl's gotta shower.

Stayed here for one night in June, but have stayed here before when on business in Chicago. Great location for business/shopping/sightseeing. In between Michigan Avenue's Magnificent Mile and the Loop and next to the Chicago River. Rooms very spacious and clean. Gym has a wonderful view, as it is situated on the top of the hotel. Bar next to lobby, very busy with good atmosphere. Cannot fault the hotel. Prefer it to the Westin - my previous address when in Chicago.

i stayed at this hotel for a week with my family this hotel is huge so clean has comfy beds foods great staff couldn,t of being any nicer. stayed here for thanksgiving it was fabulous second time in chicago and still want to go back again ... the hotel is within walkin distance to both state street and michicgan avenue.There,s taxis right outside the hotel and the concierge can also ring for mini buses if your travelling with a big crowd.there,s also a cinema 2 mins away opposite the hotel . Perfect Hotel for a great get away ...

Affinia was a fantastic surprise--the staff genuinely cared, the blackout curtains made for perfect sleep, and the location couldn't be beaten. My only wish is that I booked a longer stay. Will definitely return next trip.

I was disappointed with my stay at Affinia. The location was convenient, but the room felt tired and not especially clean, with scuffed walls, dusty corners, and a bathroom that clearly needed better maintenance. The bed was comfortable enough, although the sheets had a worn feel. Check-in took far too long, and the front desk staff seemed overwhelmed rather than welcoming. My room was also surprisingly noisy at night, with hallway conversations and doors slamming until well after midnight. Wi-Fi was unreliable, which made working difficult, and the extra fees were not explained clearly when I booked. I expected a more polished experience for the price. It wasn't a complete disaster, but the service and upkeep fell well below what I consider acceptable.

Not worth the price, even a little bit. A week prior to scheduled check-in, receiving an email for a room upgrade and accepting, of course, upon arrival, nobody knows about it. Typical. After nobody was doing anything about it, I notified them of this stay's review will be posted on the newly-developing TheChicagoCritic . Com, all of a sudden they figured out the problem and even offered an early check-in. Too little, Too late. Very small room with 2 queens instead of the 'Select King' I was supposed to have. Windows didnt open, TV took forever to change channels and the bathroom fan was not controllable. The faboulous Lodge Net system that every hotel in the world uses for ease of checkout for guests, well there was no check out feature. This shit hole couldn't hold a candle to the Las Vegas Hard Rock!

Just putting in a good word for the Hard Rock Hotel in Chicago. The reviews I read before going were mixed so we were not sure what to expect. The location was perfect. The hotel was beautiful. Our view was awesome. The room was large enough and very clean. The bed was very comfy. The staff were helpful - especially the concierge, Jared. I couldn't find anything negative to say. If you want to stay in downtown Chicago - you can't go wrong with this cool hotel.

I expected more from Hotel Allegro given the photos and rate. Our room faced a narrow inner courtyard, so the 'view' was basically air-conditioning units, stained walls, and other guests' windows a few metres away. Breakfast was disappointing too: lukewarm eggs, dry pastries, weak coffee, and several empty trays that were not refilled promptly. Sleeping was difficult because the walls seemed very thin; we heard conversations, doors slamming, and plumbing from neighbouring rooms well past midnight. Street noise started again early in the morning, despite the windows being closed. The staff were polite when asked for help, but the overall stay felt tired and poorly managed.

Our stay at Sofitel felt far too short; we would happily have added another night. The room was spotless on arrival, with crisp linens, a beautifully maintained bathroom, and housekeeping that refreshed everything unobtrusively each day. Breakfast was a real highlight, offering fresh pastries, fruit, hot dishes, and excellent coffee, with staff keeping the buffet tidy and well stocked even during the busy morning period. The location was especially convenient, close enough to walk to major sights, restaurants, and public transport without needing taxis. Service throughout was warm and polished, making the hotel feel both luxurious and genuinely welcoming.

The best service!!! The staff here was incredible. You never had to lift a finger. The room was huge as hotel rooms go. The view was phenomenal. Location great. What a great weekend. We did stop for a drink at the Palm Restaurant and unfortunately, it closes at 11 p.m. Too bad!!! The Lobby Lounge is open later but drinks costs twice as much as the bar at the Palm.

I had high hopes for the Conrad given the price point, but this stay left me genuinely frustrated. Check-in took nearly forty minutes because apparently they couldn't find my reservation, and nobody offered an apology so much as a shrug. The room itself looked nice at first glance, but the air conditioning rattled all night and the shower went lukewarm by day two. Housekeeping skipped our floor entirely one afternoon and we had to call twice to get fresh towels. The concierge recommended a restaurant that turned out to be closed for renovations, which tells you how current their information is. For a hotel charging this much, the service felt careless at every turn. The location is convenient, I'll give it that, but I won't be returning and can't recommend it to anyone expecting the luxury experience they advertise.

I had a really pleasant stay at the Talbott. The location was perfect for walking around the neighborhood, with plenty of restaurants, shops, and coffee nearby, yet the hotel itself felt quiet once we were back in the room. Our room was clean, comfortable, and surprisingly spacious, with a great bed and thoughtful little touches that made it feel more polished than a typical city hotel. Everyone at the front desk was warm and helpful, especially when we asked for dinner recommendations. The lobby has a classic, welcoming feel without being stuffy. Valet was convenient, although a little pricey, which is probably expected for the area. Overall, it was an easy, comfortable experience and I would happily stay again.

We stayed at the Allegro for three nights in mid-June and honestly didn't want to leave. Our room on the fifth floor looked out over the harbor, and watching the boats come in with morning coffee became the highlight of each day. The decor is fresh and modern, warm wood tones and soft lighting rather than the tired floral drapes you still get in so many places. Breakfast exceeded expectations: fresh pastries, made-to-order eggs, good coffee, and plenty of fruit and yogurt options. What really stood out, though, was the staff. The front desk remembered our names by the second day, and when I asked for a late checkout they arranged it without any fuss. Friendly without being pushy, attentive without hovering. We'll definitely be back next year.

I had a very comfortable three-night stay at the James. The location was a major plus--just a short walk to Michigan Avenue, restaurants, and the lake, while still feeling fairly quiet at night. My room was bright, thoughtfully laid out, and exceptionally clean, with no dust or lingering odors anywhere. The bathroom was a good size and well maintained, with strong water pressure, plenty of towels, and nice toiletries; the only minor drawback was limited counter space around the sink. Every staff member I encountered was welcoming and genuinely helpful, from check-in to arranging a car and suggesting nearby places for breakfast. Service felt polished without being stiff. The room could have used a little more natural light, but overall the hotel offered a relaxed, convenient base, and I would happily return.

I arrived here at about 8pm after a flight from California. I didn't know about the renovation when I made the reservations, but that didn't bother me very much. I was helped by a man at the front desk named Ben, who was friendly enough, but literally just handed me my room key and told me to have a nice stay. He gave me NO information about anything. I had no idea where breakfast was served, or even if there WAS breakfast. There was also an EXTREMELY unpleasant woman working behind the desk(she wasn't wearing a name tag but was African American, slim with short hair) who seemed to be actually radiating hostility. It made me very uncomfortable and needless to say, made me feel unwelcome. I actually felt like I was putting her out by staying in the hotel. I encountered her again the next morning when I had to go downstairs to ask a question and again tried to smile at her a bit, and again was met with utter disdain and rudeness. I also watched her interact with another guest and saw her act with the same rudeness and bad manners. No matter what may be going on in one's life, when you work in customer service you need to leave whatever is happening at the door and put on a smile. I was appalled by her demeanor. My room was alright, there was no clock which I found very odd. Since I came from a different time zone my computer and phone had 2 different times and I was constantly confused as to which one was correct, especially upon waking up in the morning. It would have been nice to have a clock. There was also no literature on local sites, maps, restaurant menus, or even anything with the hotel's name and address in the room. Also, the mattress was the absolute worst mattress I've ever slept on in my life. I woke up every morning with a sore back and neck. I've had better sleep on a hard, lumpy futon. It was absurd. Like another person posted, my tub did not drain either, and I was also shocked that there were no soda machines or ice machines to be found. Maybe they were around somewhere, but I wasn't made aware of it at check-in, and I didn't want to go downstairs and ask for fear of being treated like I was a burden to the employees. The hotel is in a good location and the rooms look nice upon first glance, but I absolutely would not stay here again. I've had more pleasant stays at a cheap chain hotel, which was a bummer because it was my first visit to Chicago and I had pretty high expectations.

Room: I stayed in the 16thz floor. 2 double bed room. The room has a decent size. Equipment is state of the art. The Furniture are stylish. Room Size was very nice. I could have left my big suitcase opened throughout the stay (which rarely happens in most hotels ;)) 42' LCD Screen Complimentary WiFi in the room The bed and pillows are of extrodinary quality which provided an excellent deep sleep to me. Location Located quite central. Shopping streets are in reach of 5 minutes by feet. Midway Airport is in reach by cab within 30 minutes (~30 USD). Service - Spa and Fitness exists - though I did not use. - Restuarant (not used) - Business Center - Very friendly and helpful staff. (even printed our boarding passes at the reception) I do travel frquently, and do recommend this hotel for a business stay, as also for an overnight with friends going shopping, partying whatever in the city center of Chicago. Pricing was very moderate for teh standard being provided at a downtown hotel.

We stayed at the Sofitel for three nights and it was honestly one of the better hotel experiences we've had in ages. The location is great, quiet street but still walkable to everything we wanted, and the moment you step into the lobby there's this calm, understated elegance that sets the tone. Our room on the ninth floor was spotless, the bed is genuinely one of the most comfortable I've slept in at any hotel, and the French touches like the bath products and the little welcome note made it feel special. Front desk staff remembered our names by day two, which was a nice surprise. Room service arrived faster than promised and the food was actually hot. Only tiny gripe would be slow elevator waits at peak times, but that's minor. Would absolutely return.

The Fairmont's reputation clearly precedes it, but our stay felt trapped in a bygone era. The lobby's grand chandeliers are impressive, yet the room's decor was tired--worn floral drapes and dark, scuffed furniture that screamed 1990s. Our 'city view' was mostly a brick wall and a sliver of the rooftop AC units. The bathroom was the low point: a cracked tile floor, a showerhead with uneven pressure, and a grimy caulk line around the tub that made me want to skip bathing entirely. Breakfast was a cafeteria-style disappointment. The scrambled eggs were watery, the bacon flabby, and the coffee tasted burnt. For the nightly rate, I expected polish, not peeling wallpaper and frostbitten service at the front desk. I've had better stays at a mid-range chain. This felt like a grand dame who's forgotten how to care for her guests. Save your money.

We attended a Bachorette Party in Chicago in Aug 2005. There were 10 girls total. We had 5 rooms ... and I did not hear one complaint from anyone during our entire extended weekend. Never been to Chi-town before, I booked our hotel based on reviews from TA. And we were not disappointed. The staff is wonderful, the happy hour was just fabulous. The room was nice and clean, with a great double headed shower and Aveda products was an extra bonus! Then you also get free internet in your room! The hotel was chic and hip without the pretentiousness. We still talk about what a wonderful time we had ... and we all agree that if we ever go back to Chicago we will be staying at the Amalfi again. Trust me the pics don't do it justice!

While I had stayed in the Hotel Monaco before, this was my husband's first trip to Chicago and I insisted we stay here as I loved it the first time. Well the second stay was even better -- we had one of the corner suites on the river -- the service was excellent and staff was very friendly and helpful. The warm cookies in the afternoon is a nice touch after a day of sightseeing. Unfortunately we missed the wine hour. One thing that realy impressed me is that b/c of flight delays we got to Chicago a day late -- Hotel Monaco manager waived the cost of the first night on our room even though it was a guaranteed reservation.

My stay at The James was disappointing, especially given the price. The location is convenient for Michigan Avenue, restaurants, and the train, but the central setting could not make up for the problems inside. The room looked tidy at first glance, yet there was dust along the baseboards and a used tissue behind the nightstand. The bathroom was cramped, with water collecting around the sink and grout that clearly needed attention. Staff interactions were inconsistent: one receptionist was polite and helpful, while another seemed irritated when I asked for fresh towels and offered little information. Noise from the hallway continued late into the night, and the bed was less comfortable than expected. I wanted to like this hotel, but the overall lack of care made it poor value.

The Hotel Talbot exceeded my expectations--it felt like a steal for the location and service. Yes, the lobby decor leans traditional, but the rooms are freshly updated with crisp linens and modern touches that avoid the dated cliche. I slept like a log on the plush king bed, with blackout curtains that actually block the street light. The bathroom was a real highlight: a spotless walk-in rain shower with excellent water pressure and plush towels. It's rare to find that level of polish at this price point. The only minor quibble was the hallway noise in the morning, but it didn't ruin the overall experience. I'd gladly pay again.

Booked via Priceline.com for a weekend getaway and got the room for $75 per night. When we arrived via Midway we took the Orange Line to within a block of the hotel for just $2. Hotel easy to find. Never felt uncomfortable with the neighborhood/area. Saw very few homeless or panhandlers. Walked all over the place. Great location and hotel is about a $5-$6 cab ride from most major attractions/shopping/restaurants. Hotel is almost gawdy with colors/decor, but it's not that different from a cruise ship decor. It was not annoying decor by any means. Check in was painless and the service was great! Heard NO noise whatsoever...the reports of 'thin walls' are greatly exaggerated. The walls are all concrete and thick...we heard NOTHING both nights we were there! Highly recommend this hotel! Rooms are small but not crowded for two people...they are old style hotel rooms..very classic

The Hyatt was a solid choice for our anniversary getaway. The bathroom felt like a small spa retreat, with excellent water pressure in the rainfall shower and thick, fluffy towels that actually wrapped around you. I was pleasantly surprised by how quiet our room was, despite the hotel being fully booked; we never heard hallway chatter or street noise. Our corner room faced the river, and watching the city lights flicker at dusk was a real treat. The housekeeping team clearly took pride in their work--the carpet looked vacuumed, the glass surfaces were streak-free, and the sheets smelled fresh without being overpowering. Everything felt crisply maintained, from the bedside lamps to the minibar. It wasn't flashy, but it was exactly what we needed for a restful weekend, and the front desk even surprised us with a small dessert for our anniversary. We'd happily book here again.

Stayed at the Amalfi hotel in Chicago this month with good expectations. And what a disappointment! Paid just under $200 for a 'deluxe king', and what we got was a 2nd floor view of construction, a dirty, badly 'rehabbed' bathroom, itchy sheets, no down comforter!! (just sheets and the gross old hotel blanket thing) , previously opened bottles in our mini bar, and plenty of rude, inexperienced staff members & managers (def. not a 3 or 4 star staffing!!) I do live in Chicago, and have stayed at a wide range of places. I know that for $200 in February, you can expect a great hotel. As there were many available the weekend we stayed at Amalfi, choosing it over say, the Palmer House Hilton, Hotel Sax, Sutton Place, Hotel 71, was a huge waste. Definitely keep looking and book elsewhere. Not worth the price at all, don't let their pictures fool you. Also, I wouldn't say that our experience was just a rare mishap, the hotel looks like an old Days Inn that had undergone a slight renvation, i.e., new lamps.

This hotel is a shambles-furniture literally falling apart and a staff that is both rude and uninformed, nevermind the lack of security and the absence of the so-called amenities. The 'fitness center' is an oversized closet! We were appalled during our stay! Truly anticipated 'warm, Irish hospitality' and short of a barman, no one was Irish, warm or hospitable! Manager was unresponsive to our needs and front desk attendent was incredibly rude when we made a simple request. Her manager (?) refused to come out of the office when she called to ask them to speak with us. Room was pretty at first glance but when dresser drawers fell out and the major construction of the hospital next door began at 7:30am it is not the kind of experience anyone could tolerate. To call this a Red Roof Inn would be an insult to RRI! The manager that finally called us back was soooo fake and insincere that we would have prefered no call at all. The only thing they have going for them is the location but its not worth the trade-off.
Hotel Monaco was not worth the steep rate: street noise and thin walls kept me awake, and the dismissive front desk staff offered little help when I complained.

We enjoyed the Hotel Monaco. Great location for walking and beautiful rooms. The staff was so friendly and we especially enjoyed the wine reception and getting to meet other guests. Will definitely stay there again!

I had a very enjoyable two-night stay at The Knickerbocker. The location is wonderfully convenient for Times Square and the subway, yet my room was surprisingly quiet once the door closed; I barely noticed the city noise at night. I was on a higher floor and had a great view of the surrounding Midtown rooftops and bright signs, especially after dark. The room itself was stylish without feeling impractical, with a comfortable bed, plenty of outlets, and a spotless bathroom. Housekeeping kept everything fresh and neatly arranged throughout my stay. Every staff member I encountered was warm and professional, from the quick check-in to the concierge who gave me useful restaurant suggestions. The rooftop atmosphere was a highlight as well. It is a busy hotel, but the service and comfort made it feel easy to relax.

We got this hotel by chance since we decided the spur of the moment to spend a nite in Chicago on 7/24/09. We went thru Priceline and was lucky to get a room at this hotel for only $69 (normal rate was around $200). The room was superb on the 29th floor with a nice king bed. Hotel is only about 1.5 blocks to Michigan Ave so the location is very convenient. Parking is very expensive at $50 a nite but we parked right next door at a selfpark for just $30. We decided to have breakfast at the hotel restaurant to save us from walking elsewhere. We ordered the buckwheat pan cakes and egg benedict. They were absolutely delicious which stunned us since we didn't expect this type of experience from a hotel restaurant especially for breakfast. Glad we didn't pick their breakfast buffet since the special menu is much better. I highly recommend this beautiful and cozy hotel for your Chicago visit.

Homewood ended up being exactly the kind of stay I didn't know I needed. The room was spotless and quiet, with a kitchenette that actually had decent cookware--I made breakfast twice instead of eating out. The bed was firm but comfortable, and the blackout curtains did their job perfectly. What really stood out, though, was the front desk team. I had a minor billing mix-up and they sorted it in under five minutes, no hassle, plus they remembered my name the next day and asked about my hike. The free evening reception was a nice bonus, and the pool was warm and uncrowded. Parking was easy and right by the entrance. For the price, I genuinely can't complain. I'd happily book here again for a longer trip.

I really wanted to like this place, but it just missed the mark from the second I walked in. The 'modern luxury' vibe they push in the photos is gone--the hallways feel tired and the carpet is badly stained. My room smelled damp and stale, like no one had actually aired it out after the last guest. Housekeeping didn't really clean it; I found a used water bottle under the desk on day two. The staff was polite but totally apathetic, especially at check-in when I waited over twenty minutes with only one person at the desk while three others stood around talking. The bed was lumpy and the pillows were flat. Even the coffee maker looked grimy, so I skipped it. Honestly, not worth the money they're charging. I'd skip it unless you're truly desperate for a room.

Had a week long stay at the Hilton on south Michigan while attending a meeting. The hotel has some elegance in the lobby, meeting rooms and lounges - the hotel rooms could definitely use updating. I would definitely say that for the price of a room here - the rooms should be top notch. My car was misplaced during valet parking, our reservations were messed up, hotel staff showed up repeatedly throughout the week at our door with items (room service, a new coffee pot, laundry) that wasn't ours. I would not stay at this property again. There are much better places for the money in close proximity to Michigan Ave. It is a very big hotel and at times it felt like we were staying at Faulty Towers.

Guys trip to Chicago, scored this hotel on Priceline for $100 a night. Had a little confusion over the bed situation at first. They said they only had kings available even after I had called and requested 2 doubles. After a 30 minute ordeal at the front desk they put us in a room with 2 doubles. The room was nice, nothing specacular, a little on the small side but nice. The lobby was beautiful to look at but that's about it. Hotel is within walking distance to Soldier Field, Sears Tower, ESPN Zone, and lots of bars and restaurants. Great location that and the price we got the room for made our trip. Would definately try and stay at this hotel again.

Me and my husband stayed in the Allegro Hotel Chicago for 4 days 3 nights recently. We got a room with a king size bed.. Although the room is small, we got no problems with that as there was enough space for our luggages & all. However, we felt that the bed is not exactly comfortable, the bed sheets kinda feel rough to us. The walls are really thin and we could hear our neighbours talking and occasionally the flushing sound. 1 of the days, our room was not cleaned till afternoon and so we went to check with the front desk and was told that we got to request for our room to be cleaned which was a shock to us as we thought that like all hotels, rooms are cleaned except when you put on the no disturb sign. The worst is upon returning to the hotel at night, we found a bag of our garbage in the room and it was right next to our luggage. The housekeeping people must have forgotten to take it out after cleaning our bins. This is unacceptable to us. The hotel is in the theatre district and it is rather quiet at night. Although it is near the CTA trains, i would rec one to stay somewhere close to the magnificent mile where its lively at night or hotels near the chicago river so that you can get a great view. Am staying again at a Kimpton hotel in San Fran next month and i am contemplating if i should change! Overall, not a good experience and i wouldnt choose this hotel again if i were to head to Chicago again!
Our room overlooked the river and old rooftops, and the blackout curtains made for an excellent night's sleep. Breakfast was fresh and varied, making Hotel Allegro feel well worth the price.

My wife and I just returned from a 3 night stay at the Amalfi Hotel in Chicago and enjoyed everything about the Hotel. Most importantly our room was perfect with plenty of space, great jazz CD's in the room, wonderful bathroom and one of the most comfortable beds I've ever slept in. The staff was very helpful with every request. The Amalfi offers a great continential breakfast on every floor each morning with good coffee and a great selection of pastry's, fruit's and jucie's. We also enjoyed the managers receptions one evening where they offer a great choice of complementary cocktails and antipasta's for their guests. Would highly recommend this hotel.
The Palmer looked charming online, but our room was tired, the bathroom wasn't properly cleaned, and street noise kept us awake most of the night. Definitely not worth the price.

I had such high hopes for this Hyatt based on the price, but honestly the stay fell flat in almost every way. Check-in took nearly half an hour because apparently they were short-staffed, and nobody apologized or even acknowledged the wait. My room overlooked the loading dock, so I was woken up at 5:30 every morning by beeping trucks. The air conditioning rattled so loudly I had to shut it off the second night and just sweat it out. Housekeeping skipped my floor one day entirely, and when I called the front desk about fresh towels, they never came. The breakfast buffet was soggy and lukewarm both mornings, not at all what you'd expect at these rates. The location was fine, I'll give it that, but that's about the only thing going for it. I won't be returning, even though I usually stay loyal to this brand.

Intercontinental gave us a seamless check-in and a room that was quiet, spotless, and surprisingly spacious for downtown. Staff remembered our names and offered great local tips--rare touch. We'll happily return for the location and genuine warmth.

This is my second time here in two months; both stays were great. The rooms are very nice and very clean. The staff is terrific and always attentive. My only concern would be there never seems to be anyone at the concierge desk.

This was my first time in Chicago and wanted a hotel that was in a good location. This definitely fit the bill. I could walk to all the places I wanted to see - very close to Michigan Ave and the Magnificent Mile. About a 15 minute walk to the Art Institute. The hotel staff was very friendly and went out of their way to be helpful. There was coffee in the lobby every morning, that was very welcome. The room was comfortable and clean and fairly quiet. I could hear the train and some traffic from the street (considering the location, this wasn't bad and didn't affect my ability to sleep or relax). I would definitely recommend this hotel - a gem!!

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly, I was impressed by how smooth everything went. The front desk crew was quick and genuinely friendly, not the usual scripted hospitality. Our room overlooked the pool area, which was a nice surprise, and the bed was seriously comfortable--I slept better than I do at home. The little touches like the complimentary coffee station in the lobby and the way they refreshed the room discreetly while we were out made it feel like they actually care. We ate at the on-site restaurant for breakfast one morning, and the avocado toast was solid, though a bit pricey. Location-wise, it's a short walk to a few decent bars and a convenience store, which came in handy. Would happily book here again for another city trip.

I stayed at The James for a long weekend and was pleasantly surprised by how relaxed the whole experience felt, especially given the downtown location. The room was quiet, thoughtfully laid out, and had a very comfortable bed, with plenty of space for luggage and a small work area. I liked the simple, contemporary design more than the overly decorated style some hotels go for. Everyone at the front desk was friendly and quick to help with directions, restaurant suggestions, and a late checkout request. The location made it easy to walk to shops, restaurants, and the river, while taxis were easy to find when the weather turned. Housekeeping kept everything spotless without being intrusive. It is not the cheapest option, but the service and convenience made it feel worthwhile.
My weekend at Hotel Allegro went by far too quickly. The room was spotless, I slept deeply in the quiet bed, and the bright bathroom had a generous shower and plenty of counter space.
Affinia was a great find--quiet room, genuinely friendly front desk, and an easy walk to restaurants and the subway. The bed was especially comfortable after a long day out.
The weekend flew by, and for that price, the cramped room wasn't worth it. The bland, lukewarm breakfast was a letdown, though the location was a saving grace for exploring.

Stayed at the Hotel Palmer for a long weekend and was genuinely impressed. The front desk upgraded our room on arrival, the mattress was incredibly comfy, and the breakfast spot next door they recommended became our favorite of the trip. Would happily return.
Our stay at the Conrad felt too short, but the spotless room, polished bathroom, and genuinely warm staff made it easy to leave impressed and eager to return.
The bathroom was cramped and poorly cleaned, and street noise kept me awake most of the night. Staff seemed indifferent when I complained, making the steep rate feel especially unjustified.
Disappointing stay at Swissotel: the city view was mostly blocked by nearby buildings, the dated decor felt tired, and constant hallway noise made even our short visit feel exhausting.

We spent three nights at the Knickerbocker and honestly wish it had been a week. The room was spotless when we arrived, housekeeping kept it that way throughout, and the bed was genuinely comfortable after long days of walking around the city. Location is hard to beat, tucked right off Times Square yet surprisingly quiet once the door closes, with the subway a couple minutes away. Breakfast in the restaurant was a highlight each morning, fresh pastries, excellent coffee, and eggs cooked to order rather than the usual buffet tray. Staff were warm without hovering. Would happily return.

Great location right in the thick of it all, and the rooftop bar was a perfect spot for sunset cocktails. Rooms were quiet and comfy, though the gym could use a few more dumbbells. Would definitely book again.

The Knickerbocker looks impressive online, but my stay was far less polished than expected. The location near Times Square is convenient, although the surrounding noise and crowds made it hard to feel relaxed. Check-in took nearly half an hour, and the front desk seemed overwhelmed rather than welcoming. My room was stylish but surprisingly cramped, with barely enough space to open a suitcase, and the bathroom had scuffed fixtures and weak water pressure. Housekeeping also skipped replacing the coffee supplies one day. I had hoped the rooftop bar would make up for it, but the prices were excessive and service was slow. For what I paid, the experience felt more like an expensive address than a comfortable luxury hotel. I expected much better attention to detail.

Our suite at the Knickerbocker are quite nice, but the behavior and attitude of the staff is beyond abysmal. First, a member of the staff entered our room mid-day unannounced only to apologize after realizing that he failed to verify that we were present. Not a tremendous problem, but when the young woman at the front desk replied 'What do you want me to do about it' with the tone of a flippant teenager, I began to suspect that a severe deficiency in manners may have been evident in the staff. Fast forward to this evening. Following a lovely meal off the premises, we chose to turn in a bit early at 11:30 pm only to discover that despite our best intentions, the bass from a party downstairs was more than audible in our room. Acting prudently and with restraint, we decided to phone the front desk to inquire as to why our room had been inadvertently annexed into the party downstairs, but yet again we were met with a curt and quite rude response. Sean at the front desk informed us that the party was a greater priority for the hotel, and that the family dictated that the music was to be set at a certain volume. On one hand I appreciated his honesty, but on the other, I truly would have preferred that he at least pretended to care about the guests who chose to stay at his property. Since we're out of options for the evening, we've decided to stay up and try to watch TV for the time being, but given the circumstances, the staff could have easily made up for the negative situations that arose in quick succession. Also, I was alarmed to learn that while I slept the prior night, a possible gang-related shooting took place mere blocks from the property. This wouldn't have been a concern if like nearby hotels, the Knickerbocker chose to enlist any type of security measures within their lobby. Would I stay here again? Maybe on a dare, or if someone else was footing the bill. Yet I've had better experiences in road side motels, and the employee training regimen could use a serious revamping to better serve the interests of the guests, and more importantly simple common sense.

Stayed at the Chicago Affinia Dec 10 thru Dec 12 and was very impressed with the staff, the room, and the location. Close to shopping and the pizza place next door was great. Of course, there were many other restaraunts nearby as well. I had a little trouble figuring out the heat, but it was fine once I learned how to set it. They were working on the hotel, so we got a great rate. But the work never bothered us. The room was great, with the walk-in shower in the spacious bathroom a wonderful surprise. I would definately stay here again and would recommend to others.

Great beds, clean rooms, amazing bathroom, nifty view, wonderful service, expensive parking ($40, but it's Chicago), speedy in and out. Very European in sensibility and amenities, but with air conditioning!

I try to stay at the James every time I happen to be in Chicago. There are other good choices in town, but nobody has what the James offers: superior service - aka class meets efficiency -, metropolitan design and comfort with an attention to details I found only at the W in Seoul, and what always plays a role meaning a convenient location ... Then they get to you with small unexpected touches that make the difference ie: I was about to take off and drive North, it was a hot July day...one of the staff members handed me a bottle of water. A small gesture. Unexpected and appreciated. The management AND the staff understand what we expect and more importantly, what we need. AND they consistenly execute against that.

Our Sheraton stay felt far too brief--the room was spotless, the bed heavenly, and despite full occupancy, we heard barely a whisper all night. I woke rested and genuinely wished we had one more morning here.
The room was spotless, and the marble bathroom felt spacious with great water pressure. I slept wonderfully in the quiet bed, while every staff member was warm, attentive, and professional.

This morning, I checked out and left behind one of the worst hotel experiences I've ever had: Hard Rock Hotel, Chicago. I am in disbelief that this hotel is part of the 'Preferred Hotels' group. Upon checking in, I was 'greeted' by a front desk staff that had better things to be doing and let it show. My room was poorly lit and dirty. The desk/desk chair was covered in sticky, dried soda pop (or something else?) which I had to clean myself so I could work. The 'sound system' was put to shame by my 10-year-old daughter's boombox. No one, rock star or otherwise, wants to reach more than an arm's length for toilet paper. Everything is possible. This includes hiring professional and courteous staff to answer customer calls that are directed to the 'everything is possible' line. Great marketing fails with no follow through. The in-room mini-bar policy ranks in my personal top-five most ridiculous business practices of all time. Do you charge Steven Tyler $7.81 for opening his in-room 'fridge? Looking back, I would have much preferred enjoying cocktails in my dirty room rather than the dirty, drafty, overpriced bar (with a horrendous wine list) With the exception of the fact that I was leaving, check-out was no better than checking in. I wasn't even asked about my stay! The young woman who provided me with a copy of my bill could not have been more unpleasant. I, for one, will not bring my business back to that location. Next time I'm in Chicago, I'm staying at the Hyatt. Rock on, TripStarr

For nearly $600 a night I expected far more than a dated bathroom with a dripping shower and walls so thin I heard every hallway conversation. Great location downtown, but definitely not worth the price.

Hotel Amalfi was a great base for a long weekend in the city. The location made everything easy: we walked to restaurants, shops, and the river, and taxis were always quick to find when we went farther afield. Our room was quiet despite being so central, and I slept remarkably well on the comfortable bed with the blackout curtains drawn. The decor has a slightly classic, older feel rather than a trendy boutique look, but it was well maintained and gave the room some character. Staff at the desk were warm and efficient, especially when we asked for dinner suggestions. We only stayed two nights, which felt far too short; I would happily return and allow more time to enjoy the neighborhood.

We stayed at the Hotel Amalfi for four nights in early September and it genuinely exceeded what I expected for the price. I was a little worried the area would be noisy at night, but the windows block out almost everything, and we slept quietly the whole stay. The room itself was spotless, honestly one of the cleanest I've seen, housekeeping even arranged our toiletries neatly each day. Wifi was fast and stable, my husband worked from the room two mornings with video calls and never had a lag issue. Breakfast surprised us: fresh pastries, decent espresso, eggs, fruit, and they happily made adjustments when I asked. The rooftop views weren't the selling point I thought they'd be, but the staff made up for it with warm, unhurried service. We'd happily come back next trip.

This was a great hotel right in the heart of the Chicago Loop. Within walking distance to the downtown attractions. Parking is expensive ($50 p/nt) so we parked at a free remote location (recreation drive) since we weren't planning on driving once we checked in. The staff was friendly and helpful. The rooms are large and clean.

Perfectly located within walking distance of everything, with genuinely friendly staff who remembered our names. The bathroom was spotless and modern, and despite being downtown, the room stayed wonderfully quiet at night.
Great Michigan Avenue location, and our suite was quiet, roomy, and spotless. The front desk got us checked in quickly and even pointed us toward a terrific late-night pizza spot.

Disappointed with the Knickerbocker. Paid a fortune for a room that felt dated, and the AC rattled all night. Location is fine, but at these rates I expected far better service and much quieter rooms. Won't be back.
Solid stay at the Ambassador -- front desk was friendly at midnight check-in, room was quiet and the bed seriously comfy. Location near the parks is a steal. Would book again without hesitation.
The James was a great base for our Chicago weekend--quiet, comfortable room, quick check-in, and staff who were genuinely helpful when we needed dinner recommendations. I'd happily stay here again.

I had a very pleasant stay at Hotel Palmer and would happily return. The location was ideal for getting around town, with restaurants and shops within an easy walk, yet my room was surprisingly quiet at night. Everything felt clean and well cared for, from the comfortable bed and fresh linens to the spotless bathroom. The front desk staff were warm, efficient, and genuinely helpful when I asked for local recommendations. I also appreciated the small touches, like the good coffee in the morning and the easy check-in process after a long journey. The room was a little compact, and the Wi-Fi slowed down briefly in the evening, but neither issue affected my stay. Overall, it was welcoming, convenient, and very good value.
The decor felt tired rather than rock-and-roll fresh, and hallway noise kept us up. Even for one night, the stay dragged, while staff seemed indifferent to our complaints.

Our stay at the Omni felt too short--three days just flew by. The location was perfect for walking to downtown sights, the beds were incredibly comfortable, and breakfast offered fresh pastries and strong coffee every morning.

I really wanted to like the Sheraton, but the stay fell short in too many ways. The room smelled faintly of smoke despite being a non-smoking floor, and the carpet looked like it hadn't been replaced in years. Housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely, and when I called the front desk twice about it, nobody followed up. The elevator wait times were brutal in the mornings, sometimes ten minutes, with conference crowds crammed in. Breakfast at the restaurant cost $28 per person and both the food and service were mediocre at best. On the plus side, the location is convenient and the bed itself was reasonably comfortable. Still, for a hotel charging these rates, I expect far better attention to basics. I won't be returning.

I had a very pleasant three-night stay at Hotel Ambassador. The lobby and room decor lean a little classic rather than ultra-modern, but everything felt well cared for, clean, and comfortable, not tired or neglected. My room faced a quieter side street, and with the blackout curtains drawn I slept exceptionally well; the bed and pillows were better than expected. Breakfast was simple but satisfying, with fresh fruit, pastries, eggs, and good coffee, and the staff kept refilling items even near the end of service. Wi-Fi worked reliably in both my room and the lounge, which made catching up on emails easy. Everyone at the front desk was friendly without being overly formal. I would gladly return for the location, restful rooms, and consistently helpful service.

Stayed at the Sofitel Chicago Water Tower for 3 nights in early April 2007. Very convenient location just a block from all of the shopping on the Golden Mile. Good restaurant at the hotel serving a la carte breakfast different from the usual fare and with a nice French twist. Dinner at the restaurant was also good. Prices are reasonable. Room is comfortable, only problem was with a card access door lock that usually required several swipes before opening. Excellent service from the bellmen to the concierge and front desk staff. Would definitely stay here again if visiting Chicago. Concierge recommended a small van tour, which was excellent. However early April is too early to visit Chicago as popular activities such as the boat tour of the architecture of Chicago was not operating yet.

Awesome hotel, our room overlooked Michigan Ave and we could see the river. Very stylish, trendy room and hotel. Lacked a bit in amenities (pool, etc) but more than made up for it with the location and quality of the hotel. Booked it thought Hotwire for $99 which was awesome value.

We barely wanted to check out--our two nights at Hotel Allegro flew by. I slept deeply in the plush bed, the bathroom's rainfall shower was perfect, and the spotless room made every moment feel fresh and welcoming.

I'm genuinely disappointed with my stay at the Omni. The wifi was a constant struggle, dropping out every few minutes, which made it impossible to get any work done in the room. The staff, while polite at check-in, became nearly impossible to reach afterward--housekeeping ignored our 'do not disturb' sign and we had to call twice just to get extra towels. Our 'city view' was essentially a brick wall and the air conditioning unit's hum was louder than the traffic below. Considering the nightly rate, this felt like a highway motel price tag with none of the perks. The lobby is nice, but that doesn't make up for a dated room, spotty connectivity, and service that vanished when we actually needed help. I'd think hard about paying this much again.

Lovely stay at the Hotel Ambassador--fresh, modern decor throughout and a spotless bathroom with great water pressure. The location couldn't be more convenient for exploring the city, and honestly the weekend flew by far too quickly.
Had a great stay at the Hard Rock Hotel--our room was comfortable, the staff were upbeat and helpful, and the live music downstairs made the whole weekend feel fun without being overwhelming.

I had a really enjoyable stay at the Hard Rock Hotel and felt the price was justified, especially considering the lively atmosphere, comfortable room, and central location. The room was stylish and clean, with a surprisingly comfortable bed and plenty of space for two people. Breakfast had a good range of choices, including fresh fruit, pastries, eggs, bacon, and decent coffee, though the buffet became busy after 9 a.m. Despite the hotel's energetic music and busy lobby, our room was quiet at night, with only occasional hallway noise. I slept very well and appreciated the blackout curtains and excellent pillows. The staff were friendly and quick to help when we needed extra towels. Overall, it offered a fun experience without sacrificing comfort, and I would happily stay here again.

Staff were warm and genuinely attentive, making check-in effortless. I slept deeply in the plush bed, and the central location made exploring a breeze. Mornings started perfectly with a delicious breakfast spread that had something for everyone.

Overall I had a VERY Bad experience when hosting a meeting for company, but when my parents came in from out of town and wanted to stay at the Swissotel, I thought we should give them another try. Turns out my first impression was correct, this is the LEAST friendly hotel I've ever been in! Even the concierge was rude and disagreeable. I could go on and on, but instead I'll just say GO SOMEWHERE ELSE!

This small boutique hotel is tucked away in a perfect location between the Loop and the Miracle Mile. Two blocks west of the Wrigley Building and so convenient to restaurants, etc. The staff, from doormen to desk folks are extra nice and accommodating. The delicious breakfast on each floor is ultra-convenient, the evening happy hour is more than generous, and the morning paper is welcome. Bedding is so comfortable. This is our second stay, and certainly not our last. We love Chicago, and this hotel is one of the reasons why.

We went to Chicago for my 2nd wedding anniversary and stayed at Homewood. My first impression was great, very helpful valet employees and VERY nice. That is one perk of my stay here. Otherwise, we had no problems checking in other than the hotel has 19 floors and when we booked the room we asked that we have the highest room avalible due to the fact that it was my husband first time there and the higher up, the more beautiful the view is. So we got the 9th floor. Not what I call 'high up' when the rooms started on floor 6. Then the following morning, we went to breakfast of which was ok, nothing great. My husband and I went down in jeans and a sweatshirt but had not really thought about shoes as we thought it would just be a few bagles, some fruit, and that was it. So, we got our food and sat down. After getting stared at for the first 15-20 minutes, an employee came and told us that we wernt allowed to eat breakfast without our shoes on. Remind you, it was about 15-20 minutes after we had even entered the room. So she asked that we go get shoes while sitting down and eating our breakfast. Pretty pointless AFTER we already had gotten our food. I am sure it is because very few employees could speak understandable english that it took so long. Last but not least, dont come with a clean car. I had washed my car one day prior to arriving there and when it was returned, it was filthy dirty.

Not worth the price. We almost stayed at a hotel for $110 a night, but instead choose the Hard Rock for $180 (a special). We were located on the 'newly renovated' Beatles floor. The carpets in the hallways looked like they needed to be replaced. Upon entering our room we found some cool Beatles artwork along with a 3x4 foot Marilyn Manson portrait. I think they were halfway done re theming the room. At checkout they tried to charge us $11 for using the mini-bar which we didn't even open. They removed the charge right away but I wonder if they try to get unsuspecting people with that charge. Nothing special here. If you want to pay a bunch extra for some light theming then this is the place for you.

Perfect location for sightseeing--steps from the station yet whisper-quiet. The bathroom gleamed with modern fixtures, and our spotless room felt fresh, not frumpy. A truly effortless, comfortable stay.

The room was stiflingly hot and the constant street noise meant I barely slept, a real shame given the lovely terrace view. Staff were aloof and unresponsive to my complaints, making the whole stay feel more like a chore than a getaway.

Stunning lake view from the 28th floor, but that's where the wow ended. The bed sagged, I woke up stiff, and crumbs under the desk made it feel neglected. At $400 a night, this was a letdown I won't repeat.
Really enjoyed my stay at Affinia--the room was spacious and quiet, the bed comfortable, and the staff genuinely welcoming. The location made getting around the city wonderfully easy.

We chose the Allegro based on the photos and the location, but the stay fell short of expectations almost immediately. Our room overlooked the alley, so the 'view' was a brick wall, dumpsters, and constant deliveries starting before 6 a.m. The bathroom was cramped and dated, with peeling wallpaper, a showerhead that barely had pressure, and a drain that seemed permanently slow. The room itself wasn't much better; there were stains on the carpet, smudges on the mirror, and what looked like old hair behind the nightstand, which made me question how thoroughly the housekeeping staff cleans between guests. As for the front desk, they were indifferent at best. When we mentioned the noise, we were told the hotel was full and given nothing in the way of an apology or adjustment. For the price, I expected far more and won't be returning.

The staff were fantastic from check-in to checkout, and the breakfast buffet had everything we craved. Our room was spotless with a killer view. The pool was a bonus. We left feeling completely refreshed.

I stayed at the InterContinental for three nights and honestly wish it had been a week. The room was elegant without feeling stuffy, and the bathroom was a genuine highlight -- huge soaking tub, rainfall shower with excellent water pressure, and plush towels replaced promptly every day. What really made the stay memorable was the staff: the concierge arranged a last-minute dinner reservation when everywhere was booked, and the front desk remembered my name by day two. Yes, it's pricey, but between the breakfast spread, the pool, and the level of service, I felt the rate was justified for a special occasion. Checkout was smooth and they held our bags courteously. Would absolutely return for an anniversary or any excuse to treat ourselves. Highly recommended.
The Sheraton felt polished and welcoming, with a comfortable room, great city views, and staff who handled a late check-in smoothly. Breakfast was fresh and well worth adding.

Stayed with a group for a bachelorette party, and was disappointed. The hotel is beautiful, the staff was all rather friendly. The main problem was the room/sleeping situation. We had booked rooms with 2 queen beds several weeks before, but received an email a few days before our visit stating they were sold out (how that happens I don't know!!) so they 'upgraded' us to two 'suites' with a king and a pull out. First, this meant our party was split up and on different floors. Second, that meant two of us were stuck on a pull out couch. :( I'm not a picky, unreasonable person, but that was the WORST 'bed' I've ever slept on! It was sunken in the middle so we literally rolled into each other unless we balanced ourselves on the very edge of the bed. Then there were the springs poking into our backs ALL night! Just awful! For the amount of money we spent I expected to be comfortable! I would not stay here again after this experience.

Stayed here for a long weekend and was genuinely impressed. The location is a huge win--we walked to the Louvre and the Seine in under ten minutes, and the metro was practically on the doorstep. The wifi was flawless throughout, even in the hallways, which was a pleasant surprise. Our room faced the inner courtyard, so it was wonderfully quiet, especially at night; I barely heard a peep. The decor felt more classic than cutting-edge, but it was tasteful and well-maintained, with plush carpets and elegant touches that didn't seem tired. The staff were attentive without being fussy. Breakfast was a lovely spread of pastries and fresh fruit. All in all, a very relaxing and convenient base, and I wouldn't hesitate to book here again.

I was attending a conference at the Mariott. They were booked up and I shared a room at the Hard Rock for a week by default. What a lucky break. This is a beautiful hotel. I am not a fan of all that black/grey vibe and find it a little cheesy. What I loved was the way the Hard Rock left the beautiful old hotel features intact, and decorated around the basic stucture. My room was CLEAN, CLEAN, CLEAN. I want to comment on the staff. What an upbeat group of people. This included the doormen, the front desk, the consierge. They were wonderful! Every morning one of the bell men would find my TV morning news show for me in the bar, while I drank their courtesy coffee. They brought us a refrigerator, IPOD dock, and extra suitcase stand within minutes of check-in. I had a hard time contacting the airport transport. The consierge took care of it for me. While I was waiting for the 4:50 am airport shuttle, one of the bell men found me a cup of coffee in the back. I just couldn't get over how nice and friendly everyone was....great place to stay. I hope to go back with my husband.
Hyatt's central location made getting around effortless, and our weekend felt far too short. The staff were warmly attentive, while the room was spotless and comfortably maintained throughout.
Hotel Allegro looked tired, the room was noisy all night, and the front desk seemed indifferent when I mentioned the broken air conditioning. Not worth the price.

Negative points: 1. I guess they gave me the worst room. It's small room with a king size bed even though I'd requested a room with two queen beds. 2. No roll away bed was available so I had to sleep on the floor. 3. The tub in the bathroom would not drain. 4. No exhaust fan in the bathroom. 5. broken furniture. Plus point: 1. Convenient location.

We chose to stay at a small hotel because we did were looking for a hotel with less crowds. We anticipated we would get better service in a smaller hotel, than some of the other larger high rise hotels. We did not experience very good service at the Talbott Hotel. When we checked Irena seemed very robotic and aloof. The front desk clerks were neither welcoming nor gracious. The lobby is small and the front desk is just a few feet from the front door. Each time we came into the hotel we were never greeted nor even received a smile from the staff, just a blank stare and gaze. The front desk staff was chilly and stiff, no greetings, no smiles and no personality. They had difficulty answering simple questions or requests. On the other hand the bellman Perry was great.
